INTRODUCTION
For me, this book is long overdue. Too often, training-related materials are
solely focused on frameworks or methods that are impractical for those who
work in a team setting. Some incredible resources guide us on why, how, and
what to do with training, but those of us working with teams are left to infer
how to apply methods or protocols designed for one-on-one environments.
I can recall several times leaving a conference or reading a book or article
and being beyond excited to implement a concept I had just learned. I was
always met with the reality that the practical application of the concept or
method was impossible. The ingenuity required to apply something novel to
more than one person is an underrated skill. Again and again, I would
eventually throw out the concept entirely and stick with what was time tested
and proven.
My stance on education has been constructed by going down the lessbeaten path. I always like to stray away from what everyone else is doing in
strength and conditioning. I am not saying I try to be a maverick or an
anarchist within strength and conditioning. But I knew that going to a
conference where I knew no one or where I was completely out of my depth
in terms of knowledge would only make me better. The willingness to break
away is what eventually became incredibly valuable.
I attended conferences where I was exposed to novel nutrition protocols,
different training methods, and unique exercise techniques that I had never
encountered before. This could create a certain level of resistance or
skepticism. But if everyone could do what I could, how would I be able to
differentiate myself in a crowded profession? Getting past any fear or
skepticism became a necessity to further my career. The difference between
where I was and where I wanted to be was first being exposed to something
new. The hard part was learning how to apply it.
The most anxiety I had was after a conference, as I considered how I was

介绍
对我来说，这本书姗姗来迟。 很多时候，与培训相关的材料只关注对
于在团队环境中工作的人来说不切实际的框架或方法。一些令人难以置
信的资源指导我们为什么、如何以及如何进行培训，但我们这些与团队
合作的人只能推断如何应用为一对一环境设计的方法或协议。
我记得有几次离开会议或阅读一本书或一篇文章时，我对实施我刚刚
学到的概念感到非常兴奋。 我总是遇到这样的现实：概念或方法的实
际应用是不可能的。 将新颖的东西应用于多个人所需的聪明才智是一
项被低估的技能。 一次又一次，我最终会完全抛弃这个概念，并坚持
那些经过时间考验和证明的东西。
我对教育的立场是通过走少有人走的路而建立的。我总是喜欢偏离其
他人在力量和体能方面所做的事情。 我并不是说我试图在力量和体能
方面成为一个特立独行者或无政府主义者。 但我知道，去参加一个我
不认识的人或者我完全超出我知识范围的会议只会让我变得更好。脱离
的意愿最终变得非常有价值。
我参加了一些会议，在那里我接触到了我以前从未遇到过的新颖的营
养方案、不同的训练方法和独特的运动技巧。 这可能会产生一定程度
的抵制或怀疑。 但如果每个人都可以做我能做的事情，我如何才能在
拥挤的职业中脱颖而出呢？ 克服任何恐惧或怀疑成为我职业生涯发展
的必要条件。 我现在的位置和我想要的位置之间的区别在于首先接触
到新的东西。困难的部分是学习如何应用它。
我最焦虑的是会议结束后，因为我考虑了自己的情况

going to implement these new ideas with my teams. For instance, at a
conference, I went through a protocol of 6, 12, 25 and was floored by how
challenging it was. We paired heels-elevated safety squats for 6 reps,
pendulum squats for 12 reps, and leg presses for 25 reps. We rested for 3 min
and repeated two more times. Feeling floored by this protocol both physically
and mentally, I needed to understand how to implement it with my team in
some way.
Returning to my weight room, I was faced with the dilemma of not having
either a pendulum squat or a leg press; my example of how to implement was
irrelevant. Most of us who work in a team setting more than likely have
access only to free weights with barbells, dumbbells, and kettlebells. This
creates a fundamental question with any protocols: Can we replicate
complicated methods within a team setting? Adding to this question, can we
replicate equipment designed for a team setting?
I could easily say the same for a particular conference focusing on a
particular skill. Going through a protocol with kettlebells, Olympic lifting,
speed training, flexibility, mobility, or movement ability is important for
strength coaches. We can leave these seminars empowered. We have learned
a new skill, which gives us the potential to do more. This is all well and good
unless we have some idea of how to incorporate this with a team. Does this
take the place of something else? Does this mean what I was doing before
was less than?
The burden of knowledge is not the easiest path. Knowledge of methods,
protocols, and techniques without the ability to implement them is torturous
to a coach who cares. Being entrenched within a system without knowledge
of what else is out there is unequivocally the easier path for a coach. But
easier is not the answer. The best interest of the athlete is the harder, more
arduous path. All we need is a resource that unpacks what is true and how to
apply methods that were not designed for large groups.
We are all creatures of habit. What I see a lot is not a fear of change; it is a
fear of something not working. Research is a fundamental aspect of strength
and conditioning. The curiosity to explore something new regarding training
is the fuel to keep the flame burning. A huge roadblock, however, is the
inability to apply something that makes sense in concept but not in practical

将与我的团队一起实施这些新想法。 例如，在一次会议上，我经历了 6
、12、25 项协议，并对它的挑战性感到震惊。 我们将脚后跟抬高安全
深蹲进行 6 次，摆式深蹲进行 12 次，腿举进行 25 次。我们休息了 3 分
钟，然后又重复了两次。我在身体和精神上都对这个协议感到困惑，我
需要了解如何以某种方式与我的团队一起实施它。
回到举重室后，我面临着既没有摆式深蹲也没有腿举的困境；我的如
何实施的例子是无关紧要的。 我们大多数在团队环境中工作的人很可
能只能使用杠铃、哑铃和壶铃进行自由重量训练。 这对任何协议都会
产生一个基本问题：我们可以在团队环境中复制复杂的方法吗？除了这
个问题之外，我们可以复制为团队环境设计的设备吗？
对于专注于特定技能的特定会议，我可以轻松地说出同样的话。 对
于力量教练来说，完成壶铃、奥林匹克举重、速度训练、灵活性、灵活
性或运动能力的协议非常重要。我们可以让这些研讨会充满力量。我们
学到了一项新技能，这使我们有潜力做得更多。这一切都很好，除非我
们知道如何将其与团队结合起来。 这会取代其他东西吗？ 这是否意味
着我之前所做的事情少于？
知识的负担并不是最简单的道路。 对于关心的教练来说，了解方法
、协议和技术而没有能力实施它们是一种折磨。 对于教练来说，在不
了解其他系统的情况下扎根于一个系统中无疑是更容易的道路。 但更
简单并不是答案。 运动员的最大利益是走更艰难、更艰巨的道路。我
们所需要的只是一种资源，能够揭示什么是真实的，以及如何应用并非
为大型群体设计的方法。
我们都是习惯的生物。我经常看到的并不是对改变的恐惧；而是对改
变的恐惧。这是对某些事情不起作用的恐惧。研究是力量和体能训练的
一个基本方面。探索训练新事物的好奇心是保持火焰燃烧的燃料。 然
而，一个巨大的障碍是无法应用一些在概念上有意义但在实践中没有意
义的东西

application. I have seen too many sound concepts not get implemented due to
a lack of understanding of how to execute them within a group. Application
or logistics should not be the determining factor in learning something.
Training principles are the foundation of a program; there is no change
(figure 1). Principles reflect a consensus about what is true and require
creative implementation, regardless of the group’s size. From one person to
100 people, principles are nonnegotiable. They need to be in place no matter
how large or small the group is. Principles are the foundation for
programming regardless of any variable or context that the program is set to
serve.

FIGURE 1 Training principles.
The other aspect we need to explore is the human influence on training
decisions. We are all ruled by personal biases and preferences. The art and
science of programming are something that we should appreciate as one of
the most enjoyable aspects of our profession. It is also the area where we are
most vulnerable to making irrational decisions that could lead to diminished

应用。我见过太多合理的概念由于缺乏对如何在团队中执行它们的理解
而未能实现。 应用或逻辑不应该成为学习某样东西的决定因素。
培训原则是计划的基础； 没有变化（图 1）。 原则反映了对真实情
况的共识，并且需要创造性地实施，无论团体规模如何。 从一个人到
一百个人，原则是不容谈判的。无论团队规模大小，他们都需要就位。
无论程序要服务的变量或上下文如何，原则都是编程的基础。

图 1 训练原则。
我们需要探索的另一个方面是人类对培训决策的影响。 我们都受到
个人偏见和偏好的支配。 编程的艺术和科学是我们职业中最令人愉快
的方面之一，我们应该欣赏它。这也是我们最容易做出非理性决定的领
域，这些决定可能会导致我们的能力下降。

performance while simultaneously increasing risk.
This is why we need rules (figure 2). Just as sports have rules, we need
rules to make decisions. This is systems-based thinking. Systems are merely a
sequence of decisions to garner a predictable outcome. Within this system,
we have constraints that can be perceived as limits to what we can do. Within
these constraints, there are limiting factors or bottlenecks, such as equipment
or quality control. These bottlenecks are where we create rules to avoid
inconsistent or unpredictable outcomes. Rules allow us to bridge the gap
between what is good on paper and what we can practically apply.
Principles and rules are the foundation of this book. Creating structure
with programming is the concept we need to explore. A training program is
not art. It is not art because its value is not determined by its novelty,
scarcity, or demand. Instead, a training program’s value is determined by its
effectiveness. Does the program consistently deliver high-level results? We
may be successful from time to time with a randomized approach, but this is
not a strategy we can employ when working with larger groups. Everything is
multiplied when we work with groups. A small problem becomes a big
problem with larger samples. We will get exposed to larger samples if we do
not develop a system based on principles and rules.
It is not good enough to say something is good because we want it to be. A
mechanic is unlikely to say they did a good job without fixing the problem
they faced. Their perception of value is tied to actually completing the job.
An artist with incredible talent and skill can get away with a lack of systems
because the perception of value is based on less definable outcomes. Coaches
are more like mechanics than artists. We have to have clearly defined rules
and objectives and base everything we do on principles. Our outcomes cannot
be at the mercy of perceived value; they have to be tangible.

绩效的同时增加了风险。
这就是我们需要规则的原因（图 2）。 正如体育运动有规则一样，
我们也需要规则来做出决定。这是基于系统的思维。系统只是一系列获
得可预测结果的决策。 在这个系统中，我们有一些约束，这些约束可
以被视为对我们能做的事情的限制。在这些限制内，存在限制因素或瓶
颈，例如设备或质量控制。 这些瓶颈是我们创建规则以避免不一致或
不可预测的结果的地方。 规则使我们能够弥合纸上的美好与实际应用
之间的差距。
原则和规则是本书的基础。 用编程创建结构是我们需要探索的概念
。 培训计划不是艺术。 它不是艺术，因为它的价值不是由它的新颖性
、稀缺性或需求决定的。 相反，培训计划的价值取决于其有效性。 该
计划是否始终如一地提供高水平的结果？ 我们有时可能会通过随机方
法取得成功，但这不是我们与较大群体合作时可以采用的策略。当我们
与团队合作时，一切都会成倍增加。 样本越大，小问题就会变成大问
题。如果我们不开发一个基于原则和规则的系统，我们就会接触到更大
的样本。
仅仅因为我们希望某件事是好的而说它是好是不够的。如果没有解决
所面临的问题，机械师不太可能说他们做得很好。 他们对价值的看法
与实际完成工作息息相关。具有令人难以置信的天赋和技能的艺术家可
以摆脱缺乏系统的影响，因为对价值的感知是基于难以定义的结果。教
练更像是机械师而不是艺术家。 我们必须有明确的规则和目标，并以
原则为基础。我们的结果不能受感知价值的支配；它们必须是有形的。

FIGURE 2 Training rules.
We, as coaches, need to write effective programs that solve the problems
athletes are facing in competition. This is not doing something different for
the sake of doing something different. It is also not avoiding implementing a
program because we are not creative enough to apply it. It is relying on what
we know to be true and avoiding our human instincts to do something
irrational. Principles and rules are our best chance to write programs that
can consistently make a meaningful difference.
We could say cliché things like “there is no such thing as a bad exercise”
or “there is no such thing as a bad program.” But there are bad exercises for
certain people, and therefore, there are bad programs for certain situations.
It’s lazy and misleading to give people a pass on choosing contradictory
exercises or poorly implemented and executed training programs. Rules help
us avoid this. Rules give constraints that we must work within. If we go
outside of those constraints, we get unpredictable and undesirable outcomes.
If a program does not abide by the principles of training, it is a bad
program. Not implementing progression, progressive overload, specificity,
individuality, diminishing returns, and reversibility makes a program bad.
The issue is that this is not an easy thing to do with larger group sizes.
Acknowledging something is challenging is not an excuse to ignore it.
Principles govern us as coaches; we simply cannot omit something because it

我们编写能够持续产生有意义的变化的程序的最佳机会。
我们可以说一些陈词滥调，比如“没有糟糕的练习”或“没有糟糕的

，也有一些不好的计划。让人们选择相互矛盾的练习或实施和执行不力

给出了我们必须在其中工作的约束。 如果我们超出这些限制，我们就
会得到不可预测和不良的结果。
如果一个程序不遵守训练的原则，那么它就是一个糟糕的程序。 不
实施渐进性、渐进式超负荷、特异性、个性化、收益递减和可逆性会使
计划变得糟糕。问题是，对于规模较大的团体来说，这并不是一件容易
的事。承认某件事具有挑战性并不是忽视它的借口。作为教练，我们必
须遵循原则；我们根本不能省略某些东西，因为它

is hard to implement.
Omitting principles of training should not be tolerated. We do not tolerate
that in other professions, so why should we in ours?
“Sorry, I don’t have time to wash my hands.
Where am I cutting?”
Not something we would tolerate from our
surgeons.
“Yeah, I don’t know how to incorporate
progressive overload in training, so we’re not
going to do it. Just go and get tired.”
Not something we should tolerate from our
strength and conditioning coaches.
We can challenge a diagnosis by getting a second opinion from another
doctor. Their estimation of diagnosis is based on their educated perspective
while looking at a list of symptoms. With strength and conditioning
programs, we can question anything outside of principles; this is healthy and
constructive. Rules are context dependent. For each circumstance, rules may
change, which creates important discussion on how to execute a program.
Research overwhelmingly shows that when we institute rules or checklists in
complex environments, performance goes up exponentially (Gawande, 2009;
Grant, 2021). Rules allow us to create repeatable steps within larger groups.
In other words, we remove inconsistencies with training that serve as noise.
All rules do is allow us to be more consistent.
To save time and provide something tangible for coaches, this book builds
rules for team training. This list of rules could theoretically go on forever.
But as a whole, regarding programming for groups, I’ve decided that the
following are most important: biomechanical rules through structural balance
and physiological rules through periodized program design. This way, we
have the foundation of a checklist combined with executable strategies to

institute the rules.
Creating rules in training eliminates noise for us as coaches. Noise is
an unwanted variance in a system. Rules are not principles because they are
not true. They are important to reduce variance in expected results from
training. One thing we need to appreciate about working with various group
sizes rather than just with one person is that we are hoping for the best
possible results for the majority of the group. This is different from working
with one person, where we can customize and cater to the individual. We
have to expect that there will be unwanted logistic and situational aspects
when working with larger groups.
Systems thinking is a big step for any coach. We are process-oriented
people. We intrinsically know and value the day-to-day, commonly referred
to as the grind. However, an important question remains: If you were to take
a day off or a leave of absence, would the training take a huge step back? A
good system is antifragile; it is designed to handle variance. An antifragile
system assumes that the universe is moving to a disorganized state and
preemptively controls what we can control to slow or limit that progression
(Taleb, 2014).
Routines and systems are very different things. A routine is something we
do every day that becomes routine through repetition. A system is a sequence
of things that we can easily interchange and evolve yet remains consistent
and reliable. Doing a very redundant warm-up is a lot different from doing a
movement preparation block in your training plan. Generically raising body
temperature and stretching with a choreographed clapping sequence is
extremely fragile if the team captain is out or the coach does not blow the
whistle on time. A logical sequence of movement preparation that is based on
biomechanical and physiological rules is malleable to its environment and
much more robust in terms of adaptability from one person to another.
A system means we can change exercises or methods based on an everincreasing knowledge base. If we have rules and respect the rules, we can
change anything whenever we want. As more information becomes available,
we can seek out that new information without fear of not being able to
implement it. Establishing rules and a rationale to follow organically creates a
system. A system empowers us to find better solutions to existing problems.

制定规则。
在训练中制定规则可以消除我们作为教练的噪音。 噪声是系统中不
需要的变化。 规则不是原则，因为它们不真实。 它们对于减少培训预
期结果的差异非常重要。 在与不同规模的团体合作而不仅仅是与一个
人合作时，我们需要欣赏的一件事是，我们希望为团体中的大多数人带
来尽可能好的结果。这与与一个人合作不同，在后者中我们可以定制并
迎合个人的需求。 我们必须预料到，与较大的团体合作时，会出现不
必要的后勤和情境方面的问题。
系统思考对于任何教练来说都是一大进步。 我们是注重过程的人。
我们本质上了解并重视日常生活，通常称为磨砺。然而，一个重要的问
题仍然存在：如果你请一天假或请假，训练是否会大幅倒退？一个好的
系统是具有反脆弱性的；它旨在处理差异。反脆弱系统假设宇宙正在走
向无组织的状态，并先发制人地控制我们可以控制的事物，以减缓或限
制这一进程（Taleb，2014）。
例程和系统是非常不同的东西。例行公事是我们每天都会做的事情，
通过重复而成为例行公事。系统是一系列事物，我们可以轻松地互换和
发展，但仍保持一致和可靠。进行非常多余的热身与训练计划中的运动
准备块有很大不同。 如果队长不在或教练没有按时吹哨，那么通过精
心设计的拍手顺序来提高体温和伸展运动是极其脆弱的。基于生物力学
和生理规则的运动准备的逻辑顺序可以适应其环境，并且在一个人对另
一个人的适应性方面更加稳健。

系统意味着我们可以根据不断增加的知识库来改变练习或方法。 如
果我们有规则并尊重规则，我们就可以随时改变任何事情。随着更多信
息的出现，我们可以寻找新信息，而不必担心无法实施它。建立规则和
遵循的基本原理有机地创建了一个系统。系统使我们能够为现有问题找
到更好的解决方案。

The order in a workout may stay the same, but the individual parts within that
order can easily change or progress. We can be empowered to learn and grow
without fear of being unable to apply change.
Again, this could easily be met with resistance—sticking to what is
already known is the path of least resistance. Sticking with the proven aspects
of a program is important but not at the expense of progress. It would be a lie
to say that hubris is not a factor when it comes to taking credit for designing a
training program. It helps when you have staff who know that the ultimate
goal of any program is to facilitate the highest level of performance. Yielding
personal pride to a system that is better at handling a larger and more
complex environment is our only choice. Athletes and coaches need to be on
the same page in knowing the goal, the principles, and the rules. From there,
you can collectively make the necessary changes to build a program that
produces constant and consistent improvement.
Revisiting the structure, reinstituting our plan, and debating what we can
do and what is worth our time take a lot of effort. I distinctly remember
spending hours of prep time rehearsing how to implement pillar prep before
movement prep. Do we break into stations? Do we have enough equipment to
do this as a team? Do we lose time but gain value from structuring in this
manner? The burden of knowing what is out there made our job considerably
harder relative to just sticking to what we know.
It is liberating to have a more adaptive system based on rules and
principles. I can honestly evaluate what I do and ask what is best for
improving our athletes. I can easily and without hesitation get rid of
unnecessary things. If something is logistically more challenging but can
bring more value, then we have to do it. Being faced with a potentially better
version of something you are creating is where validation comes from, not
from making someone arbitrarily tired. Validation should be based on making
the largest systemic impact possible on the entire team.
Murphy’s Law states that anything that can go wrong will go wrong. Talk
to any veteran coach, and you will get a laundry list of what not to do with a
team. They have seen everything that could go wrong, and they have
developed wisdom through years of experience training athletes. They may
come off as rigid, but what they have in fact formed is a set of rules that

锻炼中的顺序可能保持不变，但该顺序中的各个部分可以轻松更改或进
步。我们可以被赋予学习和成长的能力，而不必担心无法应用变革。
同样，这很容易遇到阻力——坚持已知的阻力最小的道路。坚持计划
中经过验证的方面很重要，但不能以牺牲进展为代价。如果说在设计培
训计划时傲慢不是一个因素，那就是谎言。 当您的员工知道任何计划
的最终目标都是促进最高水平的绩效时，这会有所帮助。将个人自豪感
交给能够更好地处理更大、更复杂环境的系统是我们唯一的选择。运动
员和教练员需要在了解目标、原则和规则方面达成共识。从那里，您可
以共同进行必要的更改，以构建一个能够产生持续和一致改进的计划。

重新审视结构、重新制定计划、讨论我们能做什么以及什么值得我们
花时间需要付出很多努力。 我清楚地记得在准备动作之前花了几个小
时的准备时间排练如何实施支柱准备。我们闯入车站吗？我们有足够的
设备来团队合作吗？ 以这种方式构建我们是否会浪费时间但获得价值
？相对于仅仅坚持我们所知道的事情，了解外面的事情的负担使我们的
工作变得更加困难。
拥有一个基于规则和原则的更具适应性的系统是一种解放。 我可以
诚实地评估我所做的事情，并询问什么最有利于提高我们的运动员。
我可以轻松、毫不犹豫地摆脱不必要的东西。 如果某件事在逻辑上更
具挑战性，但可以带来更多价值，那么我们就必须这样做。面对你正在
创建的东西的一个可能更好的版本是验证的来源，而不是让某人任意疲
劳。验证应基于对整个团队产生最大的系统影响。
墨菲定律指出，任何可能出错的事情就一定会出错。与任何一位经验
丰富的教练交谈，你都会得到一份关于球队不应该做的事情的详细清单
。 他们已经看到了一切可能出错的地方，并且通过多年训练运动员的
经验积累了智慧。 它们可能看起来很僵化，但实际上它们形成的是一
套规则，

evolved from trial and error. Rules allow us to perceive what has a higher
probability of going wrong and then reduce or eliminate that risk.
Rules are in place because we know that people struggle to make decisions
without bias or preference. We all have things we like and prefer; these
preferences shape our decisions more than we like to admit. Rules eliminate
our biases and create structures. Debates will proliferate about what form of
periodization or what exercise is best. What these debates do not do is give
guidance for a coach to make consistently correct decisions about training.
Rules need to be put in place to ensure that we create positive outcomes
for most of the people with whom we work. If we have 100 people, the
chance of creating a perfect solution for each person is small. Adding rules to
the system increases the odds of creating positive outcomes for more people.
The result is that we are governed not by emotion but by logic and reason.
We, as coaches, need to understand human fallibility and turn to rules to
shape our decisions.
This book would be incomplete without discussing the nuances of training
a team. The logistics and mechanics that shape a weight room and influence a
program’s implementation are critical. Setting up a weight room, getting the
correct equipment, using technology and analytics, creating flow, and
optimizing the coach-to-athlete ratio are paramount to success. We either
create a program based on the weight room we inherit, or we create a
weight room for the program we dream of implementing.
The logistics of training are critical in a team environment. Traditionally,
we learn this through mistake after mistake, because we rarely have total
control over logistics. Yet we should still think critically about how to
optimize our setup. Giving solutions, not problems, is a crucial aspect of
working for someone. Taking an existing setup and tweaking its organization
to increase flow and productivity is a product of feedback and collaboration.
A good staff communicates when something can be better; communication is
the fuel of any great system. The best chance of creating a great program is
collaboration among staff, athletes, and anyone else capable of interpreting
mistakes for the sake of improvement.

population after 14 years of working in a team setting. I knew a lot about

从尝试和错误中演变而来。 规则使我们能够感知哪些地方出错的可能
性更高，然后减少或消除该风险。
制定规则是因为我们知道人们很难在没有偏见或偏好的情况下做出决
定。 我们都有自己喜欢和喜欢的东西； 这些偏好对我们决策的影响比
我们愿意承认的还要大。 规则消除了我们的偏见并创造了结构。 关于
哪种形式的周期划分或哪种运动最好的争论将会激增。 这些辩论并没
有为教练提供指导，使其在训练方面做出一致正确的决定。
需要制定规则，以确保我们为大多数与我们一起工作的人创造积极的
成果。 如果我们有 100 个人，为每个人创建完美解决方案的机会很小
。在系统中添加规则可以增加为更多人创造积极成果的可能性。结果是
我们不再受情感支配，而是受逻辑和理性支配。作为教练，我们需要了
解人类的错误，并根据规则来制定我们的决策。
如果不讨论团队培训的细微差别，这本书就不完整。塑造举重室并影
响计划实施的后勤和机制至关重要。 建立举重室、获得正确的设备、
使用技术和分析、创造流程以及优化教练与运动员的比例对于成功至关
重要。 我们要么根据我们继承的举重室创建一个计划，要么为我们梦
想实施的计划创建一个举重室。
培训的后勤工作在团队环境中至关重要。 传统上，我们通过一次又
一次的错误来认识到这一点，因为我们很少能够完全控制物流。 然而
我们仍然应该批判性地思考如何优化我们的设置。 为某人工作的一个
重要方面是提供解决方案，而不是问题。采用现有的设置并调整其组织
以提高流程和生产力是反馈和协作的产物。当事情可以变得更好时，优
秀的员工会进行沟通；沟通是任何伟大系统的燃料。 创建一个伟大项
目的最佳机会是工作人员、运动员和任何其他有能力解释错误以进行改
进的人之间的合作。
在团队工作了 14 年之后，我开始拥有自己的企业并与大众一起工作
。 我知道很多关于

working with groups; I did not know how much I would have to evolve in my
approach. I am not talking about training principles. I’m talking about
understanding the power of scale and the importance of decision-making in
incredibly large groups. I had to think larger: If my program grew to 50 times
its size, would the system support that scale? Evolving meant adjusting my
original thought process while still upholding principles and rules.
The concentric circle: The consequences of making a bad decision when
training one person are small. The concentric circle of making a bad decision
with athletes who have a small bandwidth to handle stress is extremely small.
Working with larger groups, regardless of their resiliency, gives a coach an
extremely high margin of error; mistakes compound when we work with
large groups. I needed to figure out what would have the highest residual
impact with the least possible risk, not in the context of one person with a
small margin of error, but in the context of hundreds of people, possibly
thousands.
This new scale forced me to revisit the idea of what brings more from less.
Time is finite, and the older one gets, the more one values one’s time. As we
visit the central theme of training, we need to connect the methods we are
using with our desired goals. Working with teams makes training decisions
easy based on a singular goal: Win more games. With a general population, it
is much less clear. Goals fall into the general categories of wanting to lose
weight, gain weight, or just feel better. Less specificity means less
accountability to any particular thing. A training program can lose value
when expectations are not clear. The presence of goals facilitates a clearer
understanding of how to manage time. If we understand why we are doing
something, we can better allocate time toward whatever it is we want.
What moved the needle regarding accomplishing any one of those three
goals became the priority. I needed to figure out how to get more from less.
The primary means of getting more from less is figuring out how to
maximize the time we have. I ended up focusing on the best means to do so
—improving range of motion. If the client does not have a clearly defined
goal, we can avoid one of the biggest limiting factors: injuries. Time is
relative, but how we use that time is not. We can control what and how we do
something to optimize our time.

与团体合作；我不知道我的方法需要改进多少。 我不是在谈论训练原
则。 我说的是理解规模的力量以及在极其庞大的群体中决策的重要性
。我必须考虑更大的问题：如果我的程序增长到其大小的 50 倍，系统
会支持这种规模吗？进化意味着调整我原来的思维过程，同时仍然坚持
原则和规则。
同心圆：培训一个人时做出错误决定的后果很小。与那些处理压力的
带宽较小的运动员一起做出错误决定的同心圆非常小。与更大的团队合
作，无论他们的弹性如何，都会给教练带来极高的错误率； 当我们与
大型团体合作时，错误会更加复杂。 我需要弄清楚什么会以最小的风
险产生最大的残余影响，不是在一个人的误差范围很小的情况下，而是
在数百人，可能是数千人的情况下。

这个新的尺度迫使我重新审视“少而多”的想法。时间是有限的，年
纪越大，越珍惜时间。当我们探讨培训的中心主题时，我们需要将我们
正在使用的方法与我们期望的目标联系起来。 与团队合作可以根据单
一目标轻松做出训练决策：赢得更多比赛。对于一般人群来说，情况就
不太清楚了。 目标分为想要减肥、增加体重或只是感觉更好的一般类
别。 较少的特异性意味着对任何特定事物的责任较少。 当期望不明确
时，培训计划可能会失去价值。 目标的存在有助于更清楚地了解如何
管理时间。 如果我们明白为什么要做某事，我们就可以更好地将时间
分配给我们想做的事情。
推动实现这三个目标中任何一个目标的因素成为首要任务。 我需要
弄清楚如何从更少中获得更多。事半功倍的主要方法是弄清楚如何最大
限度地利用我们所拥有的时间。我最终把注意力集中在最好的方法上—
—改善运动范围。 如果客户没有明确的目标，我们可以避免最大的限
制因素之一：受伤。 时间是相对的，但我们如何利用时间却不是。我
们可以控制做什么以及如何做某事来优化我们的时间。

Where in the workout can we create the necessary change? And how do
we compel someone to do that when they are paying to be there? By having a
system for each part of the workout, it became clear that we had to focus on
the movement prep. If it was a speed session where we were doing
plyometrics and sprinting, our warm-up needed to be specific to that. If it was
a training session with much less central nervous system fatigue and potential
risk, we could easily adjust the movement prep to accommodate more
flexibility and mobility work. We are the product of what we repeatedly do,
so we had better do things that are relevant to the goal. Time becomes more
valuable if you understand how to leverage it more effectively.
The true test of fragility is not what we changed but when we changed.
Two years into our business, with existing customers who had grown
accustomed to their routine, we made a wholesale change with our movement
prep. After going to a conference that was better than my current system of
developing flexibility, I decided to adjust our entire movement prep system.
Because we had a system, we could make this change without collapsing. We
could have easily stayed with what we were doing and not changed at all. But
the overwhelming feeling of knowing that there was something better than
what we were doing made the need to change clear.
The change was met with resistance. It was met with the challenge of
training staff, organizing the session, purchasing new equipment, and
educating clients. The work was immense but felt necessary. The result of the
change was that people ended up training longer with us and achieving better
results. They broke down slower, recovered faster, and could train through a
fuller range of motion; this opened our exercise selection and made our
program more capable of helping. The burden of knowledge meant not being
limited by logistics or commitment to something we had always done.
Organization is a fundamental aspect of creating a great training program.
Having an identity and purpose with what you do makes that organization
hold weight.
The final part of this book centers on coaching in a group setting. The art
of conversation is a fundamental part of coaching. The science of
communication is more important than ever when working with groups.
Getting multiple people to repeatedly execute something with precision

我们可以在训练中的哪些地方做出必要的改变？ 当人们付费去那里
时，我们如何强迫他们这样做呢？通过为锻炼的每个部分建立一个系统
，很明显我们必须专注于运动准备。 如果这是我们进行增强式训练和
冲刺的速度训练，我们的热身就需要针对这一点。如果这是一次中枢神
经系统疲劳和潜在风险较少的训练课程，我们可以轻松调整运动准备以
适应更多的灵活性和流动性工作。 我们是反复做事的产物，所以我们
最好做与目标相关的事情。如果您了解如何更有效地利用时间，时间就
会变得更有价值。
对脆弱性的真正考验不是我们改变了什么，而是我们何时改变。我们
开展业务两年后，现有客户已经习惯了他们的日常生活，我们对运动准
备进行了大规模的改变。 在参加了一次比我目前的灵活性发展系统更
好的会议后，我决定调整我们的整个运动准备系统。因为我们有一个系
统，所以我们可以在不崩溃的情况下进行这种改变。我们本可以轻松地
坚持我们正在做的事情，根本不改变。但当我们知道还有比我们正在做
的事情更好的事情时，这种压倒性的感觉让我们明确了改变的必要性。
这一改变遭到了阻力。 它面临着培训员工、组织会议、购买新设备
和教育客户的挑战。这项工作虽然艰巨，但又是必要的。改变的结果是
人们最终与我们一起训练了更长时间并取得了更好的成绩。他们崩溃得
更慢，恢复得更快，并且可以进行更全面的运动范围训练； 这开放了
我们的练习选择，并使我们的计划更有能力提供帮助。知识的负担意味
着不受物流或对我们一直在做的事情的承诺的限制。组织是创建优秀培
训计划的一个基本方面。对你所做的事情有一个认同感和目标，会让这
个组织举足轻重。

本书的最后部分集中讨论小组环境中的辅导。谈话的艺术是教练的基
本组成部分。 在与团队合作时，沟通科学比以往任何时候都更加重要
。让多人重复精确地执行某件事

toward a threshold is the goal. Talking is important, but communicating is
what separates good from great. Effective communication is the foundation
for delivering a program that can adapt to ever-changing environments with
large groups.
The hope for this book is to give you, the coach, a new perspective on
what you can do in a team setting. Ideally, this will be a powerful resource
for you to proactively look back at programs or frameworks in a new light. In
turn, reading the book will lead to revisiting those programs with a new
perspective on practical application. Some methods or exercises that were
once thought to be a nice idea but impractical can be practically applied with
a high level of quality. How much better an experience would that be for both
the coach and the athlete?
This book aims to give you something unique in that we will create
archetypes of training. On one end, when we have a slow or low responder,
we will call them slow. On the other end, when we have a fast or high
responder, we will call them fast. These archetypes will give context for how
a person may respond to training when discussing principles and rules. They
may be fast-twitch versus slow-twitch athletes or novice versus advanced
athletes. These are the real problems we face in a team setting. Variance
among the team is simply an opportunity to create better rules.
Case study examples, appearing throughout the book, will shed light on
the most important dynamic we need to consider when training a team:
variance. Everyone responds differently to training: some good, some bad,
some net neutral. The goal is to make training as positive for as many people
as possible. Giving fast or slow reactions to different training will provide a
proxy for incorporating principles and rules. These high and low responders
create a standard distribution of results with any program (figure 3); it is our
job to make our lower responders the equivalent of our competitors’ high
responders.

达到一个门槛就是目标。 说话很重要，但沟通才是好与坏的区别。 有
效的沟通是交付能够适应大型团体不断变化的环境的计划的基础。
这本书的希望是为教练提供一个新的视角，让你了解在团队环境中可
以做什么。理想情况下，这将成为您以新的眼光主动回顾程序或框架的
强大资源。反过来，阅读这本书将导致以新的视角重新审视这些程序的
实际应用。 一些曾经被认为是好主意但不切实际的方法或练习可以高
质量地实际应用。对于教练和运动员来说，这会是一种更好的体验吗？

本书旨在为您提供一些独特的东西，我们将创建培训原型。 一方面
，当我们有一个缓慢或低响应者时，我们将称它们为 slow。 另一方面
，当我们有一个快速或高响应者时，我们将称他们为fast。这些原型将
为人们在讨论原则和规则时如何应对培训提供背景。他们可能是快肌运
动员与慢肌运动员，或者新手与高级运动员。 这些是我们在团队环境
中面临的真正问题。 团队之间的差异只是创建更好规则的机会。
整本书中出现的案例研究示例将阐明我们在培训团队时需要考虑的最
重要的动态：方差。 每个人对训练的反应都不同：有些是好的，有些
是坏的，有些是网络中立的。目标是让尽可能多的人受益于培训。对不

应者和低响应者创建了任何计划的标准结果分布（图 3）；我们的工作

FIGURE 3 Standard distribution of results.
This book could easily throw a list of things to do at you without any
consideration of the nuance that comes with weight rooms and staff. That
approach does not consistently help create an effective program within a team
environment. Our fast-to-slow continuum is a foundational piece to the
programming puzzle for a team environment. At the same time, you will need
to program to the lowest and highest common denominator. If you do not
account for variance in your execution, your program will struggle. The
continuum forces you to think of how your best and worst athletes will
respond to the program. Hint: We create rules.
A program’s effectiveness should not be limited exclusively to practical
application. If the program has a good foundation, is based on principles, and
respects the rules of training, then you can find a means to implement it. The
shame of it is that we often choose programs that are easily implemented out
of fear of change. Or worse, we choose a program that does not use rules or
principles. This leads to increased risk and diminished performance for the
majority of participants.
Writing an effective program should be our first priority with every

PART I
PRINCIPLES

第一部分
原则

1
FIRST-PRINCIPLES THINKING
The most important aspect of principles is that they are true. We can place a
principle in any situation, and it will always be true. This is by far the most
valuable tool we have as coaches working within a team setting. Our work is
complex; eliminating ambiguity is our best tool for consistently writing
effective programs.
Time is the most important variable we need to manage. As we look at
gaining a competitive advantage over other teams, those that are managing
their time more effectively will be at an advantage. First principles are not a
time management strategy. First principles are where we should be spending
most of our time. Principles save us time because we do not need to spend
time debating what is known as true. Principles are true and need to be
accepted as part of any training program. If a program lacks principles, it will
not be an effective program over multiple periods with increased group sizes.

How Should We Approach Training?
First principles require that we accept principles MUST come first. They are
first because they are true in every situation. We use that as a foundation for
all subsequent decisions. Working with open systems, systems that need to
obtain energy from the outside world, makes it harder to predict the outcome
of any decision we make. That element is combined with living in a world
that is moving constantly toward chaos. Principles give some clarity and

1
第一性原理思维
原则最重要的方面是它们是真实的。我们可以在任何情况下制定一条原
则，并且它永远是正确的。 这是迄今为止我们作为教练在团队环境中
工作的最有价值的工具。我们的工作很复杂； 消除歧义是我们持续编
写有效程序的最佳工具。
时间是我们需要管理的最重要的变量。 当我们考虑获得相对于其他
团队的竞争优势时，那些更有效地管理时间的团队将处于优势。第一原
则不是时间管理策略。首要原则是我们应该花费大部分时间的地方。
原则可以节省我们的时间，因为我们不需要花时间争论所谓的真理。
原则是真实的，需要被接受为任何培训计划的一部分。如果一个计划缺
乏原则，那么它就不会成为一个在多个时期以及增加小组规模的情况下
有效的计划。

我们应该如何进行培训？
首要原则要求我们接受原则必须放在第一位。它们是第一，因为它们在
任何情况下都是真实的。我们以此作为所有后续决策的基础。 使用开
放系统（需要从外部世界获取能量的系统）使得预测我们所做的任何决
策的结果变得更加困难。 这一元素与生活在一个不断走向混乱的世界
相结合。 原则给出了一些清晰度和

predictability of what will happen. All systems are moving to a disorganized
state; this is a law of nature. Principles give some predictability within that
uncertainty.
Traditionally, coaches insert their specialty or preference into all situations
they are placed in. It is the equivalent of saying, “I am only bringing a
hammer regardless of what needs fixing”—the hammer-and-nail complex—
without even thinking about what needs to be built or fixed. We have the
exercises or protocols we prefer. We are specialists in something based on
those preferences. When faced with a certain problem, we naturally apply a
preconceived solution based on that preference and bias. The problem is we
do not know the problem and therefore cannot predict the solution.
Unpredictable situations and systems moving to uncertainty matched with the
rigid application of programming create a more chaotic environment, which
takes away the ability to achieve success with the largest number of people
over multiple exposures.

Hammer-and-Nail Complex
As coaches, we can take on a hammer-and-nail complex (figure 1.1). We
force solutions before we even know what the problem is. We have programs
written out before we even know what the limiting factors are for our
athletes. We have philosophies before we even know what equipment we
have in our weight rooms. We commit to organizational structures before we
have an idea of how many coaches we will have and what their skill sets are.
Not everything is a nail, and we have more tools than a hammer. Solutions
are what we decide after we understand the problem and what the intended
outcome is.
A team setting makes this problem almost insurmountable to solve with
complex open systems. We cannot approach problems with what we prefer.
We solve problems first by how we frame the problem. We have to
understand that we do not know the answer to a problem, which does not
diminish experience; we should trade experience for wisdom. The wiser we
get, the better we are at framing a problem as unique and finding the best
solution more rapidly. We metaphorically put down the hammer and grab the
screwdriver for the screw.

对将要发生的事情的可预测性。所有系统都在走向无序状态； 这是自
然法则。 原则在这种不确定性中提供了一些可预测性。
传统上，教练将他们的专长或偏好融入到他们所处的所有情况中。这
相当于说，“我只带一把锤子，不管什么需要修复”——锤子和钉子的
情结——甚至没有考虑需要建造或修复什么。 我们有我们喜欢的练习
或方案。 我们是基于这些偏好的专家。 当面对某个问题时，我们自然
会根据偏好和偏见应用先入为主的解决方案。 问题是我们不知道问题
所在，因此无法预测解决方案。不可预测的情况和系统走向不确定性，
与严格的编程应用相匹配，创造了一个更加混乱的环境，这剥夺了以最
大数量的人在多次暴露中取得成功的能力。

锤子和钉子复合体
作为教练，我们可以承担锤子和钉子的复杂任务（图 1.1）。 在我们还
不知道问题是什么之前，我们就强制提出解决方案。在我们知道运动员
的限制因素是什么之前，我们就已经制定了计划。 在我们知道举重室
里有什么设备之前，我们就已经有了哲学。在我们了解我们将拥有多少
教练以及他们的技能组合之前，我们就对组织结构做出了承诺。并非所
有东西都是钉子，我们拥有的工具比锤子还多。 解决方案是我们在了
解问题和预期结果后决定的。
团队设置使得这个问题几乎无法用复杂的开放系统来解决。 我们不
能用我们喜欢的方式来解决问题。我们首先通过如何构建问题来解决问
题。 我们必须明白，我们不知道问题的答案，但这不会减少经验； 我
们应该用经验换取智慧。 我们越聪明，我们就越能将问题视为独特的
，并更快地找到最佳解决方案。比喻我们放下锤子，拿起螺丝刀来拧螺
丝。

FIGURE 1.1 Hammer-and-nail complex.

Handling Complexity
We encounter surface-level complicated problems every day. For example, I
know where my home is, and when I leave work, I need to determine the best
route home. Ultimately, I will get home if I take a scenic route or the
highway, but it may take a lot longer if I choose incorrectly. We have several
dynamics that are complicated and that we need to work through
programming. We know how long a training session, a microcycle, a
mesocycle, and a macrocycle will last. This is where we apply complicated
problem-solving in training. We get to the outcome more linearly if we
understand the logical sequence of steps that need to be taken.
We encounter hidden complex problems all the time. For example, you get
a cold and have to decide whether you will go to work. On the one hand, you
will miss work and get behind, especially if it is an important time of the
year. On the other hand, you could easily get others sick and set the entire
organization back. You could overexert yourself and get the flu or
pneumonia. This is what programming for a team is. It is understood that
there is no direct path in complex situations. Everything we do creates a
concentric circle that is sometimes positive or negative and sometimes big or
small.
The primary difference is that we understand that we do not know the

图 1.1 锤子和钉子复合体。

处理复杂性
我们每天都会遇到表面复杂的问题。例如，我知道我的家在哪里，当我
下班时，我需要确定回家的最佳路线。 最终，如果我走风景优美的路
线或高速公路，我会回家，但如果我选择错误，可能会花更长的时间。
我们有一些复杂的动态，需要通过编程来解决。 我们知道一次训练、
一个微周期、一个中周期和一个宏观周期会持续多长时间。 这就是我
们在培训中应用复杂问题解决的地方。 如果我们了解需要采取的步骤
的逻辑顺序，我们就能更线性地获得结果。
我们总是遇到隐藏的复杂问题。例如，您感冒了，必须决定是否去上
班。一方面，你会错过工作并落后，尤其是在一年中的重要时刻。 另
一方面，你很容易让其他人生病并让整个组织陷入困境。 您可能会过
度劳累而患上流感或肺炎。 这就是团队编程。 据了解，复杂情况下没
有直接路径。 我们所做的一切都会形成一个同心圆，有时正，有时负
，有时大，有时小。

主要区别在于我们知道我们不知道

outcome of complex problems. We always need to have intention with our
program, which means that we appreciate that each problem has its unique
solution requiring a novel sequence of variables relative to that problem. We
have to approach training programs with first principles because they will be
true regardless of whether we know the outcome.
A thread that can emerge is that, with complexity, there is no point in
planning. We cannot predict the future, so why bother with planning? This is
the worst possible strategy. Without some structure, we fall into the oblivion
of chaos. This will lead us to fall victim to making decisions based on
agenda, emotion, and bias. Without principles, every decision we make will
be based on what we feel as opposed to applying logic. Principles give us
structure. The idea is not to get overwhelmed by complexity and quit but to
find what is true and work outward from there.
We know that humans are fallible and incapable of making rational
decisions consistently well over time. When faced with complex problems,
this is not the time to throw your hands up and say “What’s the point?” A
complex problem is the opportunity to use logic and reason to systematically
solve problems we do not yet know how to solve. Logic and reason are based
on principles, which make principles the key factor in addressing complex
problems.
A program is a system. A system is a set of things that are structured
strategically to get a predictable outcome. Complexity means we need to have
a system in place to control the environment. A system is built upon
appreciating what we cannot change and finding what we can change. With
principles being true, we build our system—our program—around them. The
application of principles is open for debate, but their use is not, which gives a
framework for a system to work within and creates a structure within
complexity.
Dan John, an all-American discus thrower and world-class Olympic
weightlifter, said, “Programming is like Mexican food; often it is a
combination of meat, rice, beans, and tortillas.” Programs are some
combination of exercises, sets, reps, tempo, rest, and frequency. The
organization of the ingredients is what makes the difference in how
something tastes. It is the same with programming: We are not changing the

复杂问题的结果。 我们总是需要对我们的程序有意图，这意味着我们
认识到每个问题都有其独特的解决方案，需要与该问题相关的新颖的变
量序列。我们必须以首要原则对待培训计划，因为无论我们是否知道结
果，它们都是真实的。
可能出现的一个线索是，由于复杂性，规划是没有意义的。我们无法
预测未来，那为什么还要费心去计划呢？这是最糟糕的策略。如果没有
某种结构，我们就会陷入混乱的遗忘之中。 这将导致我们成为基于议
程、情绪和偏见做出决策的受害者。 如果没有原则，我们做出的每一
个决定都将基于我们的感受，而不是应用逻辑。 原则为我们提供了结
构。 我们的想法不是被复杂性压垮而放弃，而是找到真实的东西并从
那里向外努力。
我们知道，随着时间的推移，人类容易犯错，并且无法始终如一地做
出理性决策。 当面对复杂的问题时，现在不是举手说“有什么意义？
”的时候。 复杂的问题是使用逻辑和推理系统地解决我们尚不知道如
何解决的问题的机会。逻辑和推理是基于原则的，这使得原则成为解决
复杂问题的关键因素。
程序就是一个系统。 系统是一组经过战略性构建以获得可预测结果
的事物。复杂性意味着我们需要有一个适当的系统来控制环境。 系统
建立在认识我们无法改变的事物和发现我们可以改变的事物的基础上。
有了正确的原则，我们就围绕这些原则构建我们的系统——我们的计划
。原则的应用是有争议的，但它们的使用则不然，它为系统提供了一个
工作框架，并在复杂性中创建了一个结构。
美国铁饼运动员、世界级奥运会举重运动员丹·约翰 (Dan John) 表示
：“编程就像墨西哥食物；通常是肉、大米、豆类和玉米饼的组合。”
计划是练习、组数、重复次数、节奏、休息和频率的组合。 成分的组
织决定了食物味道的不同。编程也是一样：我们不会改变

variables; we are merely organizing them in a manner that is relative to the
goal. A variable’s outcome is controlled by principles and how we organize
them during training.
Having principles in place is important so that we can avoid discussing
things that we cannot change. Instead, we can explore how we layer and
organize the variables in a manner that best suits the outcome. As a
profession, we tend to be overly preoccupied with details that are quite
frankly irrelevant. Therefore, we need a structure for programming.
Discussing which exercise is best is less important than discussing how we
are going to use the principle of progressive overload with the exercises we
choose.

First-Principles Thinking Is Foundational for
Science
One key attribute of science is the foundation of logic and
reason. Science is the systematic study of the structure and
behavior of the physical and natural world through observation
and experiment. The big question is, do we consider strength
and conditioning a science?
There can easily be a typecasting of strength and conditioning
coaches as either scientists or motivators (figure 1.2). The
phrase “knowledge on ice or passion on fire” should resonate
with those who have been placed in this black-and-white picture
of coaching. This binary categorization is dangerous because it
threatens the desire to adhere to first principles. It becomes our
insignia, and it is difficult to break a certain typecast.
Regardless of how you view our role as strength and
conditioning coaches, we need to appreciate what we do within
science. Your appreciation, or lack thereof, does not change the
fact that we are attempting to change someone’s physiology
through the intentional use of stress. Understanding true things
is a prerequisite to applying stress safely and effectively.

变量； 我们只是以与目标相关的方式组织它们。 变量的结果由原则以
及我们在训练期间组织它们的方式控制。
制定原则很重要，这样我们就可以避免讨论我们无法改变的事情。
相反，我们可以探索如何以最适合结果的方式分层和组织变量。 作为
一个职业，我们往往过于关注那些坦率地说无关紧要的细节。 因此，
我们需要一个编程结构。讨论哪种运动最好并不重要，重要的是讨论我
们将如何在我们选择的运动中运用渐进超负荷的原则。

第一性原理思维是科学的基础
科学的一个关键属性是逻辑和理性的基础。 科学是通过观察和实
验对物理和自然世界的结构和行为进行系统研究。 最大的问题是
，我们是否认为力量和体能训练是一门科学？
体能教练很容易被归类为科学家或激励者（图 1.2）。 “冰上
的知识或火上的激情”这句话应该会引起那些处于黑白教练画面
中的人的共鸣。 这种二元分类是危险的，因为它威胁到遵守首要
原则的愿望。 它成为我们的标志，很难打破某种类型。

无论您如何看待我们作为体能教练的角色，我们都需要欣赏我
们在科学领域所做的工作。您的欣赏或缺乏欣赏，都不会改变我
们试图通过有意使用压力来改变某人的生理机能的事实。 了解真
实的事物是安全有效地施加压力的先决条件。

FIGURE 1.2 Strength and conditioning typecasts.
All scientific disciplines have gone through a maturation
process. Physics, chemistry, and biology at one point or another
have dealt with human biases and perspectives that were not
based on logic and reason. As these sciences matured, the
evolution of thought shifted from opinion to fact. Arguing whether
gravity exists on this planet is not something physicists spend a
lot of time on daily.
As we evolve as a science, principles (figure 1.3) will become
more foundational and will need to be discussed less. Innovation
at this stage of our profession is more novelty than improvement.
Innovation in more mature sciences is based on standardizing
procedures, which improves efficiency. We lack consistency with
our nomenclature. In more mature sciences, there are
standardized units of measurement and classification to
communicate clearly. We have an extremely low barrier to entry
for coaches. Professions associated with mature sciences have
standardized curricula and accreditation requirements to meet

图 1.2 力量和体能类型转换。
所有科学学科都经历了成熟的过程。物理学、化学和生物学都
曾在某种程度上处理过人类的偏见和观点，这些偏见和观点并非
基于逻辑和理性。 随着这些科学的成熟，思想的演变从观点转向
事实。争论这个星球上是否存在引力并不是物理学家每天花费大
量时间的事情。
随着我们作为一门科学的发展，原则（图 1.3）将变得更加基础
，并且需要讨论的更少。在我们这个行业的这个阶段，创新更多
的是新颖性，而不是改进。更成熟的科学领域的创新基于标准化
程序，从而提高了效率。我们的命名法缺乏一致性。 在更成熟的
科学中，有标准化的测量单位和分类来清晰地沟通。我们对教练
的准入门槛极低。 与成熟科学相关的专业有标准化的课程和认证
要求，以满足

for employment. We have made so much progress yet have so
far to go to be considered a legitimate science.
First principles of physics or principles of training are true
regardless of whether we accept them or not. Maturing into a
science will take first accepting that we are a science. Modern
medicine was once not as regarded as it is today. There are
downsides to increased regulation, but that should not slow
down our maturity. At the moment, we have coaches who do not
appreciate the harm they may be inflicting on their athletes.
Good intent does not outweigh bad outcomes. Skipping
principles is inexcusable; they need to be embedded into every
program.

Confirmation Bias
What is confirmation bias? It is a tendency to prematurely select

为了就业。 我们已经取得了如此大的进步，但距离被认为是一门
合法的科学还有很长的路要走。
无论我们是否接受，物理学第一原理或训练原理都是正确的。
要成为一门科学，首先要接受我们是一门科学。 现代医学曾经不
像今天这样受到重视。 加强监管有负面影响，但这不应减缓我们
的成熟度。目前，我们的教练并没有意识到他们可能对运动员造
成的伤害。良好的意图并不能胜过不良的结果。 忽视原则是不可
原谅的； 它们需要嵌入到每个程序中。

图 1.3 训练原则。

确认偏差
什么是确认偏差？这是一种过早选择的倾向

information that substantiates your beliefs. To the point of
efficiency, it is flat-out faster to come to a conclusion we already
believe is true. Because we have always done it that way, or this
is what (insert person you admire) does. It’s faster to make
decisions this way than to sit down and process information from
all sides that supports or negates something we have already
concluded.
Confirmation bias is not all bad. Leveraging experience early
in your career is not a bad thing. Team training is complex; we
need to rely on our instincts. Having bias based on previous
experience is potentially a good starting point. We can include
bias from other people’s experiences, and that is probably a
better starting point.
Relying on previous experience is a strategy that can lead to
less-than-ideal outcomes.
Confirmation bias can be reinforced by a concept called
availability bias. In our process of logically making decisions, we
can reinforce shared beliefs by associating with and absorbing
reinforced information. Our learning process begins with what we
are exposed to from our first bosses and mentors. If the program
we choose is not reevaluated relative to the environment and the
needs of the athletes, that is where availability bias leads us
astray. We need to appreciate the lessons we learned, but not
rely exclusively on what we have been exposed to.
This is a crossroads where we need to expose ourselves to
different points of view—to opposing perspectives to make
unbiased decisions effectively. The reality of bias is inevitable;
it’s just more efficient to rely on things that are true. We are the
products of availability bias when learning an individual system.
Unfortunately, we need to be able to detach from that bias in the
first available moment to remove confirmation bias. If we are only
exposed to what we know repeatedly, we will assuredly become
biased.
While looking for all the potential efficiencies we can use, we

证实您信念的信息。 就效率而言，得出我们已经相信是正确的结
论的速度要快得多。因为我们一直都是这样做的，或者这就是（
插入你钦佩的人）所做的。 以这种方式做出决定比坐下来处理来
自各方支持或否定我们已经得出的结论的信息要快。

确认偏差并不都是坏事。 在职业生涯早期利用经验并不是一件
坏事。 团队训练复杂； 我们需要依靠我们的直觉。 基于以往经
验的偏见可能是一个很好的起点。 我们可以纳入其他人经历中的
偏见，这可能是一个更好的起点。
依赖以前的经验是一种可能导致不太理想结果的策略。
确认偏差可以通过称为 availability bias 的概念得到加强。在我
们做出逻辑决策的过程中，我们可以通过关联和吸收强化信息来
强化共同信念。我们的学习过程始于我们从第一任老板和导师那
里接触到的东西。如果我们选择的计划没有根据环境和运动员的
需求进行重新评估，那么 availability bias 就会让我们误入歧途。
我们需要珍惜所吸取的教训，但不能仅仅依赖我们所经历的事情
。
这是一个十字路口，我们需要让自己接触不同的观点——相反
的观点，以便有效地做出公正的决定。 现实中的偏见是不可避免
的；依赖真实的事情只会更有效率。 在学习单个系统时，我们是
可用性偏差的产物。不幸的是，我们需要能够在第一时间摆脱这
种偏见，以消除确认偏见。如果我们只是反复接触我们所知道的
东西，我们肯定会产生偏见。

在寻找我们可以利用的所有潜在效率的同时，我们

become vulnerable. Making rash decisions with incomplete
information can lead to harmful or, at best, less effective
outcomes. Looking at every problem through a preconceived
bias is dangerous and perpetuates itself by omitting
nonsupporting evidence. It closes you off to contrary opinions,
which leads to becoming hostile and dismissive of others’
successes.
The more success you have had in one area, the more
convinced you become. Not everyone can be as successful as
you have been, which can lead to being dismissive of other
opinions. You focus on the solution instead of looking at the
problem or the desired outcome. The ability to evaluate your
rationale for thinking about a complex problem and to see the
entire picture and frame it as one solution is limited.
Programming with a narrowed focus on select aspects, rather than on
principles, we lose sight of what is important, which leads to a less-thanoptimal training program. The idea that there is no such thing as a bad
program, regardless of the effort, is simply wrong. If the program does not
have principles, it is flat out denying something that we know is true. If
something can be good, then by default, something can be bad. Shifting focus
away from principles is the foundation of bad programming.
This is an important concept to discuss because we can shield ourselves
from subjectivity. Art is an entity that is based on interpretation. Someone
decides something is beautiful or awful based on what they feel. We cannot
say whether programming is art based on subjectivity. Strength coaches do
not have the same latitude of perceived value as artists. When we start
arbitrarily deciding something is good based on an undetermined set of
criteria, there can be irreparable damage. Principles are our criteria to
determine what is effective and what is not.

What Is a Good Program?
The entire point of training is to garner an outcome that is better than if we

变得脆弱。 在信息不完整的情况下做出鲁莽的决定可能会导致有
害的结果，或者充其量是效果较差的结果。 通过先入为主的偏见
来看待每个问题是危险的，并且会因为忽略非支持性证据而长期
存在。 它让你无法接受相反的意见，从而导致你对他人的成功充
满敌意和轻视。
你在某一领域取得的成功越多，你就越有信心。 并不是每个人
都能像您一样成功，这可能会导致对其他观点不屑一顾。 您专注
于解决方案，而不是关注问题或期望的结果。 评估思考复杂问题
的基本原理、纵览全貌并将其构建为一个解决方案的能力是有限
的。

如果编程只关注选定的方面而不是原则，我们就会忽视重要的事情，
从而导致培训计划不太理想。 无论付出多少努力，都不存在坏程序的
想法是完全错误的。 如果该程序没有原则，那么它就完全否认了我们
所知道的事实。 如果某件事可能是好的，那么默认情况下，某事可能
是坏的。将焦点从原则上转移是糟糕编程的基础。
这是一个需要讨论的重要概念，因为我们可以保护自己免受主观性的
影响。 艺术是一个基于解释的实体。 有人根据他们的感受来决定某件
事是美丽的还是可怕的。 我们不能说编程是否是基于主观性的艺术。
力量教练没有与艺术家相同的感知价值自由度。 当我们开始根据一组
不确定的标准武断地决定某件事是好的时，可能会造成无法弥补的损害
。 原则是我们判断什么是有效、什么是无效的标准。

什么是好程序？
训练的全部目的是获得比我们直接训练更好的结果

did not train at all (figure 1.4). Without progressive overload in the form of
volume, intensity, or density, we have no direct link to positive adaptation or
no adaptation at all. If there is no progression from light to heavy, slow to
fast, stable to unstable, or planned to unplanned, we cannot assess why
something worked or not. First-principles thinking gives us a direct link to
why something worked or did not work. We can track adaptation and
therefore validate our program.

FIGURE 1.4 Good programming.

Priority 1: Does the Program Have Training Principles?
A program devoid of any progressive overload is a bad program, plain and
simple. Make any excuse you want, but the biggest reason is a lack of
discipline or focus on programming. From one week to the next, there needs
to be a series of checks and balances. Lack of progression from one week to
the next screams lack of system. The natural evolution of a person adapting
to a stimulus is predicated on the actual thought process that the imposed
stress needs to be increased.
Principles should feel as though they are second nature when writing a

根本没有训练（图1.4）。 如果没有体积、强度或密度形式的渐进性超
负荷，我们就与积极适应没有直接联系，或者根本没有适应。 如果没
有从轻到重、从慢到快、从稳定到不稳定、或有计划到无计划的进展，
我们就无法评估为什么某件事有效或无效。 第一性原理思维使我们能
够直接了解为什么某件事有效或无效。 我们可以跟踪适应情况，从而
验证我们的计划。

图 1.4 良好的编程。

优先事项 1：该计划是否有培训原则？
一个没有任何渐进式过载的程序是一个糟糕的程序，简单明了。 你可
以找任何借口，但最大的原因是缺乏纪律或对编程的关注。从一周到下
一周，需要进行一系列的制衡。从一周到下一周缺乏进展尖叫着缺乏系
统。 一个人适应刺激的自然进化取决于需要增加施加的压力的实际思
维过程。
在编写文档时，原则应该感觉像是第二天性

program. If you cannot progress, overload, specify, individualize, consider
diminishing returns, or avoid reversibility, step back and revisit the program.
Before choosing exercises or sets and reps, we need to establish the
framework for integrating principles within training. How are you going to
explain progressive overload to your team from one week to the next?

Priority 2: Can You Explain Principles to Your
Athletes?
Reversibility is one principle that is often taken for granted. But when
reversibility comes up, people struggle to answer why we need to
continuously train. Adaptation takes time; there’s no cramming or fasttracking in physiology. Changing some aspect of the nervous system or
muscular system involves breakdown and subsequent repair, followed by
increasing the stimulus and then repeating over and over. The result is
something better than when you started. If you end the exposure to stress, the
body will naturally return to a state of baseline or homeostasis.
This state of homeostasis may be higher than when one started, but it will
still be a regression to some mean. Reversibility is relative; time invested in
exposing athletes to stress is proportional to their level of adaptation. If we
spend more time training, the rate of decline is lengthened. Ending the
exposure will result in a gradual decline to baseline; this is the reason we
have an off-season training program. It is arguably the reason we have a
profession. Yet when the conversation comes up regarding skipping training
days, not training during the season, or taking time off, it diminishes the
value we can bring. But can you hold yourself and the athletes accountable
for that?

Priority 3: Do You Hold Yourself and the Athletes
Accountable for Applying Principles?
Without understanding the principle of reversibility (use it or lose it), we lose
the argument of why we need to train. There is a delicate balance between
when and where we should push to have time with our athletes. If we are too
passive about asking for any training time, we are going against the principle
of reversibility in training. Reversibility is the reason to justify year-round

程序。 如果你无法进步、超载、指定、个性化、考虑收益递减或避免
可逆性，请退一步并重新审视该计划。在选择练习或组数和次数之前，
我们需要建立将原则整合到训练中的框架。 您将如何向您的团队解释
从一周到下一周的渐进性超负荷？

优先事项 2：你能向你的运动员解释原则吗？
可逆性是一项常常被认为是理所当然的原则。 但当可逆性出现时，人
们很难回答为什么我们需要持续训练。 适应需要时间； 生理学中没有
临时抱佛脚或快速跟踪。 改变神经系统或肌肉系统的某些方面涉及崩
溃和随后的修复，然后增加刺激，然后一遍又一遍地重复。 结果比刚
开始时要好。如果您结束压力，身体会自然恢复到基线或体内平衡状态
。
这种稳态可能比开始时更高，但它仍然会回归到某种平均值。 可逆
性是相对的； 运动员承受压力所花费的时间与他们的适应水平成正比
。 如果我们花更多的时间训练，下降的速度就会延长。 结束暴露将导
致逐渐下降至基线； 这就是我们有淡季训练计划的原因。 这可以说是
我们拥有职业的原因。 然而，当谈论跳过训练日、赛季期间不训练或
休假时，我们可以带来的价值就会减少。 但你能让自己和运动员为此
负责吗？

优先事项 3：您是否要求自己和运动员对应用原
则负责？
如果不理解可逆性原理（使用它或失去它），我们就失去了为什么需要
训练的论据。 我们应该在何时何地与运动员共度时光之间存在着微妙
的平衡。如果我们过于被动地要求任何训练时间，我们就违背了训练的
可逆性原则。 可逆性是全年合理的理由

training.
Experience with coaching and programming can be a tremendous asset.
We gain perspective and wisdom from what we do, which is invaluable.
Seeing the bigger picture gives context to something as being either
inconsequential or important. It creates patience and confidence in our
decision-making. It allows us to filter out irrelevance and focus on what is
meaningful. What experience teaches us is that we do not know what will
happen, and we appreciate more so what is true: principles.
Specificity is a principle that can be an Achilles’ heel of an experienced
programmer. Finding a system is one thing. Having a dynamic sense of
where people are supposed to be and what they are supposed to be doing
consistently is a powerful driver of efficiency. If that system is rigid and only
prioritizes efficiency over principles, the system is now counterproductive.
Finding the balance between general and specific within training is a critical
aspect of programming for a team.

Priority 4: Can We Integrate Principles Into a System
to Make It Efficient?
Specificity can be misconstrued as loaded movement patterns done during
competition. There can certainly be a specific physical preparation block
where we are trying to replicate the movement patterns, energy systems, and
physiological aspects of their sport. This can be a polarizing topic for some,
and it may be difficult for many coaches to truly appreciate how much we
might limit potential by being overly specialized. In exchange, we become
overly focused on developing general abilities at the expense of specific
abilities.
Specificity does not necessarily have to be exclusive to throwing weighted
baseballs in the winter or doing conditioning with football pads in the
summer. Specificity can be something much simpler during a sport’s inseason or off-season. Specificity could be training for resiliency in those
areas with the highest risk of injury during competition. Specificity could be
understanding and preparing the appropriate energy system needed during
competition. The point is, a program should have relevance to the actual sport
the athlete participates in but does not have to be the sport itself done in the

训练。
辅导和编程方面的经验可能是一笔巨大的财富。我们从所做的事情中
获得了无价的视角和智慧。看到更大的图景可以为某件事提供背景，无
论它是无关紧要的还是重要的。 它为我们的决策创造了耐心和信心。
它使我们能够过滤掉不相关的内容并专注于有意义的事情。 经验告诉
我们，我们不知道会发生什么，因此我们更欣赏真理：原则。
特异性是一个原则，可能成为经验丰富的程序员的致命弱点。 找到
一个系统是一回事。 对人们应该在哪里以及他们应该做什么保持动态
的认识是提高效率的强大推动力。如果这个体系是僵化的，只注重效率
而不是原则，那么这个体系现在就会适得其反。在培训中找到一般性和
具体性之间的平衡是团队规划的一个关键方面。

优先事项 4：我们能否将原则整合到系统中以使其高
效？
特异性可能会被误解为比赛期间进行的负荷运动模式。 当然可以有一
个特定的身体准备模块，我们试图复制他们运动的运动模式、能量系统
和生理方面。 对于一些人来说，这可能是一个两极分化的话题，许多
教练可能很难真正理解我们因过于专业化而可能在多大程度上限制我们
的潜力。 作为交换，我们变得过于专注于发展一般能力，而牺牲了特
定能力。
特异性不一定只限于在冬天投掷负重棒球或在夏天用足球垫进行体能
训练。 在一项运动的赛季内或休赛期，特殊性可能要简单得多。 具体
可以是在比赛期间受伤风险最高的区域进行弹性训练。特殊性可以是理
解并准备比赛期间所需的适当能源系统。要点是，计划应该与运动员参
加的实际运动相关，但不一定是运动本身

weight room.
Individuality is a principle that should not be very hard to understand
based on our explanation of humans as open systems. We all respond to the
same stress uniquely; this is a given. But the issue is determining ahead of
time what constraints someone might have with exposure to certain stressors.
We can easily overlook someone’s poor adaptation as a product of working
in a group environment, and we cannot reach peak adaptation with everyone.
This relates to the concept of standard distribution. There is always a
spectrum of how people will respond to a stressor. If we have no inventory
for unique responses to training, we have no impetus to apply individuality.
We just keep creating blanket solutions to every problem and going with the
guise that what we do works based on the time served.
Much like specificity, we may need to be creative in how we approach
individuality. It could mean having a custom program for everyone that we
train. It could be hard to standardize execution and technique with a large
team, but that is the point of systems. It could be making a set of criteria
based on screening to determine the best version of a program someone could
do. The need for a reliable or replicable screen that is valid is a challenge in
itself, which is where our rules will come in. Having a diagnostic process to
determine what things we should avoid is individualization and its objective.

Priority 5: Can We Evaluate Principles Objectively?
The final principle we need to consider is diminishing returns. At what point
is what we are doing no longer effective? In a group setting, this is paramount
to safety and performance. Predicting how one person will perform in
response to a given set of variables is not possible; now multiply that by how
many are on a given team, and your odds become exponentially less. A
system of contingency needs to be in place to know when to stop training
across multiple athletes at a given time.
The stipulation of diminishing returns is having a purpose in what you are
doing in the first place. If there are no criteria for what the training plan
should accomplish, how do you determine it is no longer effective? Pushing
through when something is counterproductive is based on understanding what
that is relative to. If the program is not based on any criteria, there is no

举重室。
根据我们对人类作为开放系统的解释，个性是一个不难理解的原则。
我们对同样的压力都有独特的反应； 这是既定的。 但问题是提前确定
某人在接触某些压力源时可能会受到哪些限制。我们很容易忽视某人因
在团队环境中工作而表现出的不良适应能力，并且我们无法与每个人都
达到最佳适应水平。
这涉及到标准分布的概念。 人们对压力源的反应总是多种多样。 如
果我们没有对培训的独特反应的库存，我们就没有动力去运用个性。我
们只是不断为每个问题创建一揽子解决方案，并以我们所做的工作基于
所服务的时间为幌子。
就像特异性一样，我们可能需要在处理个性方面具有创造性。 这可
能意味着为我们培训的每个人制定一个定制计划。 对于一个大团队来
说，标准化执行和技术可能很困难，但这就是系统的要点。 它可以根
据筛选制定一组标准，以确定某人可以执行的程序的最佳版本。对可靠
或有效的可复制筛选的需求本身就是一个挑战，这就是我们的规则的用
武之地。通过诊断过程来确定我们应该避免哪些事情是个性化及其目标
。

优先事项 5：我们能否客观地评估原则？
我们需要考虑的最后一个原则是收益递减。什么时候我们所做的事情不
再有效？在团体环境中，这对于安全和性能至关重要。 预测一个人对
一组给定变量的反应如何是不可能的；现在，将其乘以给定团队的人数
，您的几率就会呈指数级下降。 需要建立一个应急系统，以了解在给
定时间何时停止多名运动员的训练。
收益递减的规定首先是你所做的事情有一个目的。 如果没有关于培
训计划应达到的目标的标准，您如何确定它不再有效？ 当某件事适得
其反时，坚持下去的基础是理解它的相关性。 如果该计划不基于任何
标准，则没有

indication of whether it is effective or ineffective.
Programming variables and then stopping because they are not doing what
you intended will take confidence in your plan. That confidence is based on
understanding what is wanted from the training program. If we want to
increase someone’s speed and they are not able to reach a certain level of
velocity, we are no longer effective. If we are trying to get stronger and
missing reps or altering the range of motion, we are not getting stronger; we
are developing a movement pattern that allows us to lift more weights. This is
the downside of overly prioritizing the general. We want these general
patterns to translate to specific qualities. Diminishing returns is an assurance
we do.
The idea behind first principles is that principles are in place so a program
can consistently be assessed as effective or ineffective. It is the foundation to
determine whether it is a good program. I talk with coaches a lot about the
difference between negligence and ignorance. The difference comes down to
understanding and applying principles. If a person does not know and does
something wrong, that is ignorance. If a person knows and does something
wrong, that is negligence. This creates a paradox within our profession: Do
we not understand it, or do we not abide by it?
People will claim that strength and conditioning is a simple construct. Lift
weights, run, and repeat; how hard could it be? In the world of competitive
athletics, the difference between good and bad is potentially extremely
lucrative. If it were such a simple construct of lift, run, and repeat, then we
would see a lot less parity at the highest levels. Not all things are created
equal, and organizations that get more from the same time constraints are the
ones that are consistently more successful.
Performance aside, the risk is certainly increased with improperly
designed programs. Bad programs are, quite frankly, a liability for elite
athletes. Poor programming and bad application leave athletes
disenfranchised with strength and conditioning. It could be argued that no
athlete is better than a bad program. Consistently, when a professional sports
league takes a hiatus due to a strike, the following year shows an increased
rate and severity of injuries. This can be traced almost exclusively to a lack of
structured strength and conditioning in the off-season. If our athletes at the

表明它是有效还是无效。
对变量进行编程，然后因为它们没有按照您的预期进行而停止，这会
让您对您的计划充满信心。 这种信心基于对培训计划的需求的理解。
如果我们想提高某人的速度，但他们无法达到一定的速度水平，我们就
不再有效。 如果我们试图变得更强壮，却缺少重复次数或改变运动范
围，那么我们并没有变得更强壮；相反，我们并没有变得更强壮。我们
正在开发一种运动模式，使我们能够举起更多的重量。这是过度优先考
虑一般性的缺点。 我们希望这些一般模式能够转化为特定的品质。收
益递减是我们所做的保证。
首要原则背后的想法是，原则已经到位，因此可以一致地评估计划是
否有效。它是判断一个程序是否优秀的基础。 我和教练们经常讨论疏
忽和无知之间的区别。差异归结于理解和应用原则。 如果一个人不知
道而做错事，那就是无知。 如果一个人知道并做了错误的事情，那就
是疏忽。 这在我们的职业中造成了一个悖论：我们是不理解它，还是
不遵守它？
人们会声称力量和体能训练是一个简单的概念。举重、跑步，然后重
复； 这有多难？ 在竞技体育的世界里，好与坏的区别可能是极其有利
可图的。 如果这是一个简单的举重、跑步和重复的结构，那么我们在
最高水平上看到的平价就会少很多。 并非所有事物都是生而平等的，
能够从相同的时间限制中获得更多收益的组织往往会更加成功。
除了性能之外，设计不当的程序肯定会增加风险。 坦率地说，糟糕
的计划是精英运动员的责任。 糟糕的编程和糟糕的应用让运动员被剥
夺了力量和体能训练的权利。 可以说，没有一个运动员比一个糟糕的
项目更好。一贯地，当职业体育联盟因罢工而中断时，接下来的一年受
伤率和严重程度都会增加。这几乎完全可以追溯到休赛期缺乏结构化的
力量和体能训练。 如果我们的运动员

peak of their earning potential in their careers are struggling to find a reason
to train, something has to give.
What if we extrapolate that into multiple off-seasons? Are bad strength
and conditioning programs consistently placing their athletes at risk?
Programs that demonstrate a lack of clear purpose and avoid using principles
are a definitive risk factor for athletes in the upcoming season. Organizations
that understand how to best leverage principles in training have a huge
competitive advantage. This is especially true in less-than-perfect situations.
In turn, it becomes a competitive disadvantage for organizations that cannot
or will not apply principles to their training.
The teams that can most effectively apply
principles to complex situations are the ones that
will be more successful.
The question of ignorance or negligence (figures 1.5 and 1.6) comes back
to why certain teams do not use principles in training. We have all seen
someone fall into a strength and conditioning role with no formal training.
The football coach becomes a strength coach between jobs for some time.
The football coach who takes over the program to develop the things he
wants happens more often than it should. There is a possibility that the
happenstance coach goes out and learns principles of training and applies
them to his team, but that is unlikely. This would be an example of
ignorance: They do not know, so they don’t apply.
However, there are plenty of circumstances when a coach has a master’s
degree in exercise physiology and has coached for several years and still does
not apply principles. It becomes a burden to apply something that they know
is true because it is more work than they want to do. This could be a matter of
that person not thinking principles were that important in the first place. It
could simply be not understanding how to apply principles in training. Either
way, this would be an example of negligence: They know, but they still don’t
apply.
Which is better or worse? It does not matter. The result will be the same.

他们在职业生涯收入潜力的顶峰时期正在努力寻找培训的理由，必须放
弃一些东西。
如果我们将其推断为多个休赛期会怎样？ 糟糕的体能训练计划是否
一直让运动员处于危险之中？缺乏明确目的并避免使用原则的计划是运
动员在即将到来的赛季中的一个明确的风险因素。了解如何在培训中最
好地利用原则的组织拥有巨大的竞争优势。 在不太完美的情况下尤其
如此。反过来，对于不能或不愿将原则应用于培训的组织来说，这会成
为竞争劣势。

能够最有效地将原则应用于复杂情况的团队将会更加成
功。

无知或疏忽的问题（图 1.5 和 1.6）又回到了为什么某些团队在训练
中不使用原则的问题。 我们都见过有人在没有经过正规训练的情况下
就陷入了力量和体能训练的角色。足球教练在工作间隙会担任一段时间
的力量教练。足球教练接管该计划以开发他想要的东西，这种情况发生
的次数比应有的次数多。 偶然教练有可能出去学习训练原则并将其应
用到他的团队中，但这不太可能。 这是一个无知的例子：他们不知道
，所以他们不适用。
然而，很多情况下，教练拥有运动生理学硕士学位，执教多年，仍然
不讲原则。应用他们知道正确的东西会成为一种负担，因为这比他们想
做的要多。这可能是因为这个人一开始就不认为原则那么重要。 可能
只是不了解如何在培训中应用原则。不管怎样，这都是一个疏忽的例子
：他们知道，但他们仍然不适用。

哪个更好或更差？不要紧。结果是一样的。

There are circumstances where someone can be successful without applying
principles of training. Probably the most important question we can ask
ourselves as strength and conditioning coaches is, are we successful because
of or despite our contribution? We do not want to be successful despite
ourselves; we want to be part of the reason for success.

在某些情况下，某人无需应用培训原则即可取得成功。 作为体能教练

图 1.5 无知。

FIGURE 1.6 Negligence.
Are we successful because of our contribution, or
are we successful in spite of it?
Determining whether success is in spite of or because of our efforts is not
difficult. We inventory what we are doing as objective and true no matter the
context. Applying principles to training gives us a platform of objectivity. It
is objective because principles are true in all situations. The absence of
principles automatically classifies our contribution as in spite of.
There is no place for ambiguity in what we do. This is a science, and yes,
there is a degree of art and skill in it. Art needs structure. This is where we
create rules for what to do going forward. Without principles, variance is
viewed as random or noise. Random variance is viewed as a fluke and not
conducive to further inquiry. Without principles, we essentially have to view
everything as noise in the system and not our problem.
Isaac Newton viewed science as a means to remove randomness from the
world. Before Newton, phenomena in nature were viewed as God’s will. The
narrative was that some omnipotent being chose things for us with some
higher or deeper meaning, and we should accept it as true without question.
Training outcomes are not some divine intervention of great genetics
combined with luck. If we approach training as anything other than a science,
we are destined to fail. With principles, we remove randomness and create a
better understanding. We move further away from hope and more toward
predictability.
No one is going to say applying principles to training is easy, which is
essentially the point of this book: making the complex practical. The
challenge comes from appreciating that we have a nonnegotiable set of
variables to apply. The reward comes from understanding there is no simple
manner to do this yet finding a way. This is the heart of complex problemsolving—having no preconceived expectations of what you are going to do
with something unknown. The essence of science is that we are problem
solvers, not solution validators.

FIGURE 1.6 Negligence.
我们的成功是因为我们的贡献，还是尽管我们做出了贡
献？
确定成功是因为我们的努力还是因为我们的努力并不困难。无论背景
如何，我们都会将我们正在做的事情视为客观和真实。 将原则应用于
培训为我们提供了一个客观的平台。 它是客观的，因为原则在所有情
况下都是正确的。 如果缺乏原则，我们的贡献就会自动归类为“尽管
如此”。
我们所做的事情没有任何含糊之处。这是一门科学，是的，其中有一
定程度的艺术和技巧。 艺术需要结构。 这是我们为未来的行动制定规
则的地方。 如果没有原则，方差就会被视为随机或噪声。 随机方差被
视为侥幸，不利于进一步探究。如果没有原则，我们本质上必须将一切
视为系统中的噪音，而不是我们的问题。
艾萨克·牛顿将科学视为消除世界随机性的一种手段。在牛顿之前，
自然界的现象被视为上帝的意志。叙述是，某个全能的存在为我们选择
了具有更高或更深刻意义的事物，我们应该毫无疑问地接受它。训练的
结果并不是伟大的基因与运气相结合的神圣干预。如果我们将培训视为
一门科学之外的任何东西，我们注定会失败。有了原则，我们就能消除
随机性并建立更好的理解。 我们离希望越来越远，越来越走向可预测
性。
没有人会说将原则应用于培训是一件容易的事，这就是本书的要点：
让复杂的事情变得实用。 挑战来自于认识到我们有一组不可协商的变
量可供应用。 回报来自于理解没有简单的方法可以做到这一点，但找
到了一种方法。 这是解决复杂问题的核心——对你将要如何处理未知
的事物没有先入为主的期望。 科学的本质是我们是问题解决者，而不
是解决方案验证者。

We do this by distilling down to what is true because there are so many
factors to consider. All these factors are continuously changing and evolving.
Training programs are a blank canvas each time. What we create is largely up
to our imagination and what we consider the best possible solution to the
problem we are facing. We make this easier by saying that, no matter what,
we will account for individuality, specificity, progression, progressive
overload, diminishing returns, and reversibility in all training programs.
The organization of those principles (part I), along with sticking to the
rules (part II) of training, can consistently create programs that garner
success. The teams you work with will achieve success because of your
contribution, not in spite of it. Foundations need to be laid down to develop
the best programs.

Take Home
First principles are the foundation of any successful training program.
Without principles (individuality, specificity, progression, progressive
overload, diminishing returns, reversibility), we have nothing concrete to
determine our contribution to success. Principles are true and therefore allow
us to create programs that we can objectively review to determine their
effectiveness. The impact of a program will lead to success as a team or
organization because of our contribution, instead of in spite of it.

我们通过提炼出真实的情况来做到这一点，因为需要考虑的因素太多
了。所有这些因素都在不断变化和发展。每次培训计划都是一张空白的
画布。我们创造的东西很大程度上取决于我们的想象力以及我们认为解
决我们所面临问题的最佳解决方案。 为了让这件事变得更容易，我们
会说，无论如何，我们都会在所有培训计划中考虑个性、特异性、进步
、渐进超负荷、收益递减和可逆性。
组织这些原则（第一部分），并遵守培训规则（第二部分），可以持
续创建获得成功的计划。 与您合作的团队将因您的贡献而取得成功，
而不是忽视您的贡献。 需要奠定基础来开发最好的项目。

带回家
首要原则是任何成功培训计划的基础。如果没有原则（个性、特异性、
进步、渐进超负荷、收益递减、可逆性），我们就没有任何具体的东西
来确定我们对成功的贡献。原则是正确的，因此使我们能够创建可以客
观审查以确定其有效性的计划。 项目的影响将导致团队或组织的成功
，因为我们的贡献，而不是无视我们的贡献。

INDIVIDUALITY
Individuality is a principle because it is a guarantee that we all respond
differently to all stressors. This chapter explores why we respond to stress
differently and what we can do about it.
Individuality means that everyone
differently to the same training stress.

responds

This chapter is very important for our archetypes of fast and slow
responders. The challenge of writing a program that is challenging for the
fast responder yet not too challenging for the slow responder is daunting.
Think what a traditional Westernized school system would do in this
situation. If someone is excelling with the curriculum, they either move up a
grade or to a higher-level class, such as going from algebra to calculus. The
slower-developing student will stay in more basic classes, get special
instruction, or be left behind altogether. With strength and conditioning
(S&C) we have to accommodate individuals who respond extremely well and
those who respond poorly within the same group (figure 2.1). The question
will eventually become, do we have to do the same thing with both?
It is a well-known fact that humans are open systems, meaning we procure
energy from the outside world. Unlike closed systems, we cannot produce
energy to support life internally. This dependence on energy from the outside
