个性
个性是一项原则，因为它保证我们对所有压力源都有不同的反应。 本
章探讨了为什么我们对压力的反应不同，以及我们可以采取什么措施。

Individuality意味着每个人对相同的训练压力的反应不
同。
本章对于我们的 fast 和 slow responders 原型非常重要。 编写一个对
快速响应者具有挑战性但对慢速响应者来说不太具有挑战性的程序是令
人畏惧的。想想传统的西方化学校系统在这种情况下会做什么。如果某
人在课程上表现出色，他们要么升一级，要么进入更高级别的课程，例
如从代数转到微积分。 发展较慢的学生将留在更基础的课程中，接受
特殊指导，或者完全被抛在后面。 对于体能训练 (S&C)，我们必须适
应同一组中反应非常好的人和反应较差的人（图 2.1）。 问题最终会变
成，我们是否必须对两者做同样的事情？

众所周知，人类是开放系统，这意味着我们从外部世界获取能量。
与封闭系统不同，我们无法在内部产生能量来维持生命。这种对外部能
源的依赖

world makes the rate of change more rapid. Closed systems are much more
efficient out of necessity. We function on the natural ebb and flow of energy
available to us, combined with expenditure to find more energy.
Energy is expressed in terms of heat. As we break down energy and create
heat, we create change. The net change is either positive or negative in terms
of cellular size (hypertrophy or atrophy) or number (fusion or fission). When
we replace that lost heat with energy from the outside world, we create
another ripple in the system’s concentric circle. In his book Scale, West
(2017) describes the three key reasons people live longer: fewer heartbeats,
lower body temperature, and less caloric intake. These reasons are a key
feature of how we manage energy gain or loss and why we respond in such
unique ways to stress, which is important because all these lifespan correlates
correspond with less heat exchange overall and therefore less change in the
system.

FIGURE 2.1 Standard distribution of results.
Humans live longer by having fewer heartbeats,
lower body temperature, and less caloric intake.

世界使得变化的速度更加迅速。 出于必要，封闭系统的效率要高得多
。我们依靠可用能量的自然潮起和流动以及寻找更多能量的支出来运作
。
能量以热量表示。当我们分解能量并产生热量时，我们就创造了变化
。就细胞大小（肥大或萎缩）或数量（融合或裂变）而言，净变化要么
是正的，要么是负的。当我们用外部世界的能量替代损失的热量时，我
们会在系统的同心圆中产生另一个涟漪。 West (2017) 在他的著作 Scale
中描述了人们长寿的三个关键原因：心跳减少、体温降低和热量摄入减
少。 这些原因是我们如何管理能量增益或损失以及为什么我们以如此
独特的方式应对压力的一个关键特征，这一点很重要，因为所有这些寿
命都与整体热交换较少相关，因此系统变化较小。

图 2.1 结果的标准分布。
人类通过减少心跳、降低体温和减少热量摄入来延长寿
命。

Performance is about increasing heart rate,
increasing body temperature, and burning more
calories (West, 2017).
If we invert keys to living longer, we can look at them with individuality.
The Catch-22 of performance is that we need to increase heart rate, increase
body temperature, and increase caloric intake to create the necessary
adaptations. Performance does not run contrary to longer lifespans directly,
or at least intentionally. Performance tries to increase the rate of change
within an open system. Raising heart rates, increasing body temperatures, and
increasing caloric exchange are the costs of doing business in performance
training.
The constant exchange of heat lost and energy gained creates more net
change. Some key factors associated with physiology amplify this change,
including fast and slow responders. A person’s response rate is either
amplified or reduced based on certain key factors. The combination of these
factors, along with the biological need to gain energy from the outside world,
makes individuality a principle we need to understand.
We need to appreciate that fast responders are more adept at handling
stress. This could be genetic, natural, or just a better training plan—that is,
nurture. Nakamura and colleagues (2016) discuss that higher degrees of
variance in response to stress, such as intense training sessions, are better
handled by more fit athletes. This means that if we apply a certain threshold
of stress to two athletes, the more fit one will handle that stress better. The
fast responder will respond better to stress because they are better at
managing that stress. Slow responders could be less fit or simply less
equipped from a genetic perspective to handle the same level of stress.

Rack Assignments
Something team settings inherently understand is the idea of
hierarchy. Hierarchy comes in all shapes and sizes, such as
head football coach and support staff or seniors and freshmen.
In the weight room, an organic hierarchy develops with rack

表现在于提高心率、提高体温和燃烧更多卡路里（West
，2017）。

如果我们颠倒长寿的关键，我们就能以个性化的眼光看待它们。表现
的第 22 条军规是我们需要提高心率、提高体温和增加热量摄入，以创
造必要的适应。 性能并不直接（或至少有意）与更长的使用寿命背道
而驰。 性能试图提高开放系统内的变化率。提高心率、升高体温和增
加热量交换是进行性能训练的成本。

损失的热量和获得的能量的不断交换会产生更多的净变化。 一些与
生理相关的关键因素放大了这种变化，包括快速反应者和缓慢反应者。
根据某些关键因素，一个人的反应率要么被放大，要么被降低。 这些
因素的结合，加上从外界获取能量的生物需要，使个性成为我们需要理
解的原则。
我们需要认识到，快速反应者更善于应对压力。 这可能是遗传的、
自然的，或者只是一个更好的训练计划——即后天培养。 Nakamura 及
其同事 (2016) 讨论了更健康的运动员可以更好地应对压力反应的更大程
度的差异，例如高强度训练。这意味着，如果我们对两名运动员施加一
定的压力阈值，那么身体越健康的运动员就能更好地应对这种压力。
快速反应者会对压力做出更好的反应，因为他们更善于管理压力。 从
遗传角度来看，反应迟缓的人可能不太适合或根本没有能力应对相同水
平的压力。

机架分配
团队设置本质上理解的就是层次结构的概念。 等级制度有各种形
式和规模，例如足球主教练和后勤人员，或者高年级学生和新生
。在举重室中，通过架子形成了有机的层次结构

assignments.
It could be deliberate, such as a coach assigning racks to their
athletes, or the opposite, with position groups working out
together. A question to ask is, what do we gain from having
partitioned subgroups within a group? A central piece of this is
having racks, or stations, that we build the workout around. We
build the workout even further around certain exercises and
certain pieces of equipment. What determines where someone
works out in a group is their acumen with certain exercises.
Think about how we organize all other aspects of physical
development, from skills to working outside; nothing replicates
assigning racks. Assigning racks is the only thing we organize by
someone’s ability at a certain exercise. Position work is by
position groups. Linear speed or multidirectional speed work is
probably by position group as well. But in the weight room, that
organizational aspect is abandoned.
There is an elephant in the room when it comes to this
hierarchy. The best lifters migrate to certain areas, and the worst
lifters migrate to the opposite end of the room. What does this
mean in terms of the ability to respond to stress? The better
lifters are probably better at adapting to the stress. In a
somewhat random way, this weight room hierarchy has
partitioned fast and slow responders. The athletes who were
able to improve faster are those who are most capable of
responding to stress.
The model of organizing a weight room is a perfect example of
the logistics, whether it was well thought out or not, of how the
S&C community has managed individuality. We have the uphill
battle of creating a program that accommodates such drastically
different needs simultaneously. We have models that have
evolved and can aid us in our ability to manage this seemingly
impossible task effectively.
In research, there is a key component in terms of designing an experiment:

作业。
这可能是故意的，例如教练为运动员分配训练架，或者相反，
让不同的位置组一起训练。 要问的一个问题是，通过在组内划分
子组我们可以获得什么好处？ 其中的核心部分是拥有我们围绕其
进行锻炼的架子或站。 我们围绕某些练习和某些设备进一步构建
锻炼。 决定一个人在团体中锻炼的位置的是他们对某些练习的敏
锐度。
想想我们如何组织身体发展的所有其他方面，从技能到户外工
作； 没有什么可以复制分配机架。分配架子是我们根据某人在某
项练习中的能力来组织的唯一事情。 职位工作是按职位组进行的
。 线性速度或多向速度工作也可能按位置组进行。 但在举重室
里，组织方面就被放弃了。
当谈到这种等级制度时，房间里有一头大象。最好的举重运动
员会迁移到某些区域，最差的举重运动员会迁移到房间的另一端
。 这对于应对压力的能力意味着什么？ 更好的举重运动员可能
更善于适应压力。 以一种有点随机的方式，这个健身房的层次结
构划分了快速反应者和慢速反应者。 能够更快进步的运动员是那
些最有能力应对压力的人。

无论是否经过深思熟虑，组织健身房的模式都是施恩禧社区如
何管理个性的完美后勤例子。 创建一个能够同时满足如此截然不
同的需求的程序是一场艰苦的战斗。 我们拥有不断发展的模型，
可以帮助我们有效地管理这项看似不可能的任务。

在研究中，设计实验有一个关键组成部分：

sample size. Sample size gives a certain amount of credibility or ambiguity to
the research results. The same is true for a training program. If we get great
results with one person, we could assume that it will be true on a larger scale.
However, in research, this would not be a big enough sample size to say
those results are proven. They may be promising, but saying more than that
would be presumptuous. The general idea of sample size is important to
appreciate when comparing potentially anecdotal results to a larger group;
results may vary.
Research is a jumping-off point for understanding how to approach
individuality within a team setting. A method or protocol can get great results
within a one-on-one environment. These results may not scale up. They could
just be random. The sample size in research is referred to as N, which would
make these great results N = 1. When you see N = 1, assume that the results
will vary in larger sample sizes. A larger sample size will always result in
variance. The amount of variance determines the efficacy of the intervention.
A good comparison with certain small sample results is with gambling. If
we bet on the number two on the roulette table and we win, what does this
mean going forward? If we put in a bunch of chips and we win a bunch of
money in return, would this influence our decision? With gambling, we
appreciate that it is a game of chance, that there are no patterns, just random
occurrences. If we applied a program to a professional athlete that showed
tremendous results, do we take the same approach with larger groups?
Chances are that the results from that program would be more closely tied to
the level of athletes adhering to the program. Chances are that the level of
athlete you work with at scale would not compare to a professional athlete.
The same logic applies to winning big on a certain number. We
understand there are too many variables to account for to say that it will
translate to larger groups with different response rates, but we double down
and do the same program regardless of it potentially being an anomaly. We
have to look at the sample size just as we look at probabilities. We know that
principles are true. We know there is a natural regression to the mean. We
know that larger groups have natural tendencies to respond differently. The
point is not to state the obvious but to compare, applying probabilities to
gambling, just as when programming for large groups; our odds improve if

划也是如此。 如果我们在一个人身上取得了很好的成果，我们就可以
假设在更大的范围内也会如此。然而，在研究中，样本量不够大，不足
以证明这些结果得到证实。 他们或许很有希望，但说得更多就显得自
以为是了。 在将潜在的轶事结果与更大的群体进行比较时，理解样本
量的总体概念很重要；结果可能会有所不同。
研究是了解如何在团队环境中实现个性的起点。一种方法或协议可以
在一对一的环境中获得很好的结果。这些结果可能无法扩大规模。它们
可能只是随机的。研究中的样本量称为 N，这将使这些出色的结果 N =
1。当您看到 N = 1 时，假设结果会因样本量较大而有所不同。 较大的
样本量总是会导致方差。方差的大小决定了干预的效果。
与某些小样本结果的一个很好的比较是赌博。如果我们押注轮盘赌桌
上的第二号并且我们赢了，这意味着什么？ 如果我们投入大量筹码并

业运动员应用了一个项目并取得了巨大的成果，那么我们是否会对更大
的群体采取同样的方法？该计划的结果很可能与遵守该计划的运动员的

动员相比。

要考虑，无法说它会转化为具有不同响应率的更大群体，但我们加倍努
力并执行相同的计划，无论它可能是异常情况。 我们必须像查看概率
一样查看样本量。我们知道原则是正确的。 我们知道均值存在自然回
归。 我们知道，较大的群体自然倾向于做出不同的反应。 重点不是陈
述显而易见的事实，而是进行比较，将概率应用于赌博，就像为大型群
体编程一样； 如果

Training Age
The biggest reason people vary in terms of high or low responders is their
training age. Training age (figure 2.3) is defined as the amount of time
someone has trained. Lemmer and colleagues (2000) showed that experience
plays a large role in response to resistance training in the development of
strength, giving the first overreaction to the effectiveness of training:
Success with novice trainees does not scale to large groups.
Athletes with limited training experience will respond favorably to any
new stimulus, which creates a problem with long-term programming. Early
success does not predict long-term success. We won our first hand, which has
no impact on future hands. Because a novel stressor showed promising
results, that does not mean it will be effective with a larger and more diverse
sample size. Experienced athletes will not respond as greatly to a familiar
training program because they already have adapted to that stress. The more
times or the longer a person does a certain program, the fewer results they
will get from it.

FIGURE 2.3 Training age.
Accommodating training age within a team is all about understanding that
anything will work with novices, while a lot less will work with advanced

训练年龄
人们反应高或低的最大原因是他们的训练年龄。 Training age（图 2.3
）被定义为某人训练的时间量。 Lemmer 及其同事（2000）表明，经验
在力量发展中对阻力训练的反应中起着重要作用，这首先对训练的有效
性做出了过度反应：新手受训者的成功并不能扩展到大群体。
训练经验有限的运动员会对任何新的刺激做出积极的反应，这会给长
期规划带来问题。 早期的成功并不能预示长期的成功。我们赢了第一
手牌，这对以后的手牌没有影响。 因为一种新的压力源显示出有希望
的结果，但这并不意味着它在更大、更多样化的样本量下会有效。 经
验丰富的运动员不会对熟悉的训练计划做出太大反应，因为他们已经适
应了这种压力。 一个人执行某个程序的次数越多或时间越长，他们从
中获得的结果就越少。

图 2.3 训练年龄。
适应团队中的培训年龄就是要理解任何东西都适合新手，而少得多的
东西适合高级人员

athletes. What this means for you, the programmer, is that what is done with
advanced athletes needs to be more well thought out. Mukherjee (2015) said,
“Normals teach us rules; outliers teach us laws.” There always needs to be an
appreciation that one thing does not mean everything, and everything does
not mean one thing. Novice athletes create an overreaction to training, a
response that simply is not universally true, especially for advanced athletes.

Novice Athletes
With novice athletes, anything will work, so keep it simple. These are fast
responders, which means earlier in the progression, you use simple, stable,
slow, and low thresholds and reduced progressions in terms of progressive
overload, single progressions, intensity, or volume by reps. Keep in mind that
adding complicated variables to the training program will make it harder to
determine where the progress came from. Anything will work, but that does
not permit you to do just anything. This also means that the rate of
progression is slow to allow for adequate time to adapt to the new stimulus.

Advanced Athletes
With advanced athletes, we need to be more strategic. They have already
responded to the stimulus we applied when they were novices. These are fast
responders, which means further progressions in complex, unstable, fast and
heavy, and higher thresholds. In terms of the number of progressions and
threshold of progressive overload, double and triple progressions, intensity or
volume by reps, and volume by sets, a more advanced athlete will need a
faster rate of progression because they are more familiar with the stimulus.
With advanced athletes, the evaluation of how quickly they reach critical
drop-off (principle) is more important. When internal metrics start to
accumulate, they will need to change. Their motor development will allow
for much more nuanced exercise selection. Their strengths and weaknesses
are more transparent and will require more direct input to accommodate their
overall profile. Compared to novice athletes who are learning and adapting
simultaneously, the shift to too much training is much less violent, which
creates more subtle changes.

运动员。对于程序员来说，这意味着对高级运动员所做的事情需要经过
深思熟虑。 Mukherjee (2015) 说：“常态教会我们规则；异常值教会我
们法律。”始终需要认识到一件事并不意味着一切，一切也不意味着一
件事。 新手运动员会对训练产生过度反应，这种反应并不普遍适用，
尤其是对于高级运动员而言。

新手运动员
对于新手运动员来说，任何事情都会有效，所以要保持简单。 这些是
快速反应者，这意味着在进展的早期，您可以使用简单、稳定、缓慢和
低的阈值，并在渐进超负荷、单次进展、强度或重复次数方面减少进展
。请记住，在培训计划中添加复杂的变量将使确定进度来自何处变得更
加困难。 任何事情都会起作用，但这并不意味着你可以做任何事情。
这也意味着进展速度缓慢，以便有足够的时间来适应新的刺激。

高级运动员
对于先进的运动员，我们需要更具战略性。 当他们还是新手时，他们
已经对我们施加的刺激做出了反应。这些是快速反应者，这意味着复杂
、不稳定、快速和沉重以及更高的阈值的进一步进展。 就渐进超负荷
的级数和阈值、双级和三级级数、重复次数的强度或容量以及组数而言
，更高级的运动员将需要更快的级数速度，因为他们更熟悉刺激。
对于高级运动员来说，评估他们达到临界下降（原则）的速度更为重
要。 当内部指标开始积累时，它们将需要改变。 他们的运动发育将允
许更细致的运动选择。 他们的优势和劣势更加透明，需要更直接的投
入来适应他们的整体形象。 与同时学习和适应的新手运动员相比，过
度训练的转变要温和得多，这会产生更微妙的变化。

Novice athletes—anything works, keep it simple.
Advanced athletes—fewer things work, make it
specific.

Biological Age
The athlete’s biological age (figure 2.4) needs to be considered as much as, if
not more than, their training age. The bottom line is that younger athletes are
naturally fast responders, and older athletes are naturally slow responders.
The simple fact is that older athletes are not given the same latitude as
younger athletes. If you are in a situation where there is a significant age gap,
this will have a profound effect on programming.
This may appear to be contradictory in that training and biological age are
inverted regarding fast and slow responders. Novice athletes are not always
young, and advanced athletes are not always old. It takes time to appreciate
the nuance in these seemingly similar attributes. Experience with a particular
entity, such as training, does not run on a parallel timeline with someone’s
age.

新手运动员——一切都有效，保持简单。
高级运动员——有效的事情较少，要具体化。

生物年龄
运动员的生物学年龄（图 2.4）需要与他们的训练年龄同等程度地考虑
（如果不是超过的话）。最重要的是，年轻的运动员天生反应快，而年
长的运动员天生反应慢。一个简单的事实是，老年运动员没有得到与年
轻运动员相同的自由度。如果你处于年龄差距很大的情况，这将对编程
产生深远的影响。
这似乎是矛盾的，因为对于快速反应者和慢反应者来说，训练和生物
年龄是相反的。 新手运动员并不总是年轻，高级运动员并不总是老.需
要时间来欣赏这些看似相似的属性的细微差别。特定实体的经验（例如
培训）并不与某人的年龄平行。

图 2.4 生物年龄。
最大的过度反应——老年运动员需要

same stimulus to reach peak performance as
when they were younger. This creates the
counterreaction of younger athletes who are
impervious to high stress, leading to a training
paradox that is hard to overcome, especially
within a group dynamic.
As coaches, we need to receive validation from what we decide to do with
our athletes. Our athletes need to be assured that they are given the absolute
best experience in each training session. Gone is the concept of minimal
effective dose when the group increases in size. The smaller the group, the
easier it is to convey to the athlete that less is more. As the group expands,
both the coach and athlete become less confident that they are doing enough.
When the sample size has increased, we lose the benefit of the doubt. This
organically creates an increased training intensity and volume, and possibly
duration, which becomes the standard to reach adaptation and has longerterm consequences. We become reliant on more, more, and more to
accommodate our lack of confidence in whether we are doing enough.
An athlete’s biological age affects their recovery through various
pathways, primarily immune function. Ahtiainen and colleagues (2016)
discuss that the athlete’s immune function predicted the recovery rates seen
when introducing a strength program that looked at increasing lean muscle
mass. The older we get, the more our immune system declines. Remember,
we are open systems that have gone through thousands of cycles of energy in
and heat out, and that takes its toll.
The impact of training places a demand on all bodily systems. The concept
of training stress working within an isolated aspect is a huge misconception.
Hautala and colleagues (2001) showed that the impact of high-intensity
training had greater systemic effects on the autonomic nervous system if the
person’s fitness was worse. Older athletes have more exchanges of heat in
and out of the body, which makes the response to training more impactful.
Older athletes’ immune systems are rate-limiting factors in their ability to
handle higher stress from training because they are already stressed.

与年轻时一样达到巅峰表现的刺激。 这会导致年轻运
动员对高压力不敏感，从而产生反作用，从而导致难以
克服的训练悖论，尤其是在团体动态中。

作为教练，我们需要从我们对运动员所做的决定中获得认可。我们的
运动员需要确保他们在每次训练中都能获得绝对最佳的体验。 当群体
规模增加时，最小有效剂量的概念就消失了。 团体越小，就越容易向
运动员传达“少即是多”的信息。 随着团队规模的扩大，教练和运动
员都会对自己做得不够有信心。当样本量增加时，我们就失去了怀疑的
好处。 这有机地增加了训练强度和训练量，甚至可能持续时间，这成
为达到适应的标准并产生长期影响。 我们变得越来越依赖，以适应我
们对自己是否做得足够缺乏信心的情况。

运动员的生物年龄通过多种途径影响他们的恢复，主要是免疫功能。
Ahtiainen 及其同事 (2016) 讨论了运动员的免疫功能预测了在引入旨在
增加瘦肌肉质量的力量计划时所看到的恢复率。 我们年纪越大，我们
的免疫系统就越衰退。 请记住，我们是开放系统，已经经历了数千次
能量输入和热量输出循环，这会造成损失。
训练的影响对所有身体系统提出了要求。在孤立的方面进行训练压力
的概念是一个巨大的误解。 Hautala 及其同事（2001）表明，如果人的
健康状况较差，高强度训练对自主神经系统的系统性影响更大。 年长
的运动员体内和体外的热量交换更多，这使得对训练的反应更有影响力
。老年运动员的免疫系统是他们处理训练中更高压力的能力的限制因素
，因为他们已经承受了压力。

Toward the end of an athlete’s playing career, we need to appreciate that
we are not working with highly resilient athletes. A strategy on what is
necessary from a stress standpoint is critical. It is critical to create and
understand the prerequisite adaptation to ensure we do what is necessary. We
simply do not have the same latitude as we would with a younger athlete due
to their lessened resilience. Having a target on a given day in terms of volume
or intensity with specific correlated lifts is essential to preserving
performance for the older athlete.
If we go back to West’s (2017) determinants of longer life of heartbeats,
body temperature, and calories ingested, we can create a fractal relationship
with an athlete’s lifespan. Fractals are simple rules repeated. The athlete’s
career has a fractal relationship with their overall lifespan. This creates a
correlation between lifespan determinants and playing-career determinants.
The athlete has a certain number of heartbeats, body temperature, and
calories within their playing career. As we approach the apex of that ability,
we need to appreciate the limited resources left for performance. Training
needs to be respectful of that decline in resources.

Older Athletes
What this translates to is an inverted relationship between an athlete’s
biological age and how much volume, frequency, and session length one can
handle. The older the athlete, the greater the need to get more from less. The
good news is that they are more experienced, probably more mature, and
more capable of getting more from less. The amount of exposure to training
and intensity has a more linear relationship to the biological age. The older
the athlete, the more you will need to rely on higher-intensity training. This
could be conveyed as reaching the rep max threshold during a set or pushing
to the failure threshold during a set. Older athletes are spending less time
overall with training, so they will need to get more from less.

Younger Athletes
Alternatively, this means younger athletes will benefit more from volume,
time, and frequency to absorb the nuances and adapt to training stimuli. With
younger athletes, much like with the novice training age, we do not need as

适应的运动员合作。 从压力的角度来看，制定必要的策略至关重要。
创建和理解先决条件适应至关重要，以确保我们做必要的事情。由于年
轻运动员的适应能力较差，我们根本没有与年轻运动员相同的自由度。
在特定的一天设定一个具体的相关举重训练量或强度目标对于保持老年
运动员的表现至关重要。
如果我们回到 West (2017) 的心跳、体温和摄入卡路里等长寿的决定
因素，我们可以创建与运动员寿命的分形关系。 分形是简单规则的重

年长运动员
这意味着运动员的生物年龄与一个人可以处理的训练量、频率和训练时
长之间存在一种倒数关系。运动员年龄越大，就越需要少花钱多办事。
好消息是，他们更有经验，可能更成熟，并且更有能力事半功倍。 接
受训练的量和强度与生物年龄具有更线性的关系。 运动员年龄越大，
就越需要依赖更高强度的训练。 这可以表示为在一组期间达到最大次
数阈值或在一组期间达到力竭阈值。 年龄较大的运动员总体上花在训
练上的时间较少，因此他们需要事半功倍。

年轻运动员
或者，这意味着年轻的运动员将从训练量、时间和频率中受益更多，以
吸收细微差别并适应训练刺激。对于年轻的运动员，就像新手训练年龄
一样，我们不需要

much high-intensity training. Relatively speaking, for session duration
combined with time spent at a threshold, the older athlete will spend more
time at higher intensities. The younger athlete will be fine at moderate
intensity and letting adaptation take its course.
This means that we should be careful with stress with someone who has a
higher bandwidth to handle stress. To quote a coach I worked with, “More is
not better; better is better.” If we can achieve certain results with less stress,
we should prioritize that. Having clear expectations from training helps us
dictate what is enough. The point is not to do more work; the point is to get
more from the work we do. Clear expectations give confidence when we
reach a critical drop-off in training to stop or alter if needed. As coaches
within a group setting, when something is no longer effective, we can
confidently manage overall stress to have better and longer results. We
reached the upper limits of stress that one can handle in a training session,
and we stopped.
Older athletes—less resilient, get more from less.
Younger athletes—more resilient, be strategic
with stress.

Sex
The most obvious but most difficult to discuss concerning individuality is
sex. This is such a difficult topic to address in a team training setting. For the
record, stating that men and women are different regarding the allocation of
training stress does not mean one is better than the other. It just means that
men and women respond differently to the same program.
The obvious reason is that men are more androgen dominant, specifically
testosterone, and women are more estrogen dominant. One is not better than
the other; simply, men’s and women’s biology creates different responses to
specific stress, specifically with resistance training. Hubal and colleagues
(2005) demonstrated that differences associated with response to strength

多高强度训练。 相对而言，就训练持续时间和达到阈值的时间而言，
年长的运动员会花更多的时间进行更高的强度。 年轻的运动员在中等
强度下会很好，让适应自然进行。
这意味着我们应该小心对待那些拥有更高带宽来处理压力的人的压力
。引用我共事过的一位教练的话：“更多并不是更好，更好才是更好。
”如果我们能够以更少的压力取得某些成果，我们应该优先考虑这一点
。 对培训有明确的期望有助于我们决定什么是足够的。重点不是做更
多的工作；而是做更多的工作。重点是从我们所做的工作中获得更多。
当我们在训练中达到严重下降以在需要时停止或改变时，明确的期望会
给我们信心。 作为团体环境中的教练，当某些事情不再有效时，我们
可以自信地管理整体压力，以获得更好、更长久的结果。 我们达到了
训练中可以承受的压力上限，然后我们就停下来了。

年长的运动员——恢复能力较差，可以少花钱多办事。
年轻的运动员——更有弹性，对压力有策略。

性别
关于个性，最明显但最难讨论的是性。在团队训练环境中这是一个很难
解决的话题。郑重声明，男性和女性在训练压力分配方面存在差异并不
意味着其中一方比另一方更好。 这只是意味着男性和女性对同一项目
的反应不同。
明显的原因是男性的雄激素占主导地位，特别是睾丸激素，而女性的
雌激素占主导地位。一个并不比另一个更好；简而言之，男性和女性的
生物学特性对特定压力（特别是阻力训练）产生不同的反应。 Hubal 及
其同事 (2005) 证明，差异与对力量的反应相关

training were mainly attributed to hormonal differences. This is an important
distinction because most training outcomes are related to increases in crosssectional muscle area (CSA). Increases in CSA are aided by more androgenic
pathways, which may not be optimal for female athletes.

Female Athletes
Charinga (2012) discusses the discrepancy: Higher volume at higher
intensities was better tolerated by female weightlifters compared to male
lifters. One of the primary reasons behind this was that women were more
efficient biomechanically during movement and could use more passive
energy during snatch, clean, and jerk. Men, who are more androgenic, rely on
more mechanical energy from increased muscle mass during lifts and
therefore cannot accumulate as much volume in a training session. Women,
who are more estrogenic, cannot create as much CSA and need a different
strategy to increase performance. This also translates to less heat exchange
for women compared to men.
The biggest overreaction to sex differences—
women need to do the same program as men in
terms of volume and intensity.
Anyone who has ever coached a female team understands this intuitively.
Taking the same program used for a male-female counterpart sport (track and
field, basketball, soccer, or volleyball) and applying the same program, the
female team will be done in a fraction of the time. Women’s faster finish is
usually accounted for by their not needing the same rest periods due to not
training at as high an intensity as men. This is speculative at best; there is no
clear diagnostic of the absolute load to prove that claim. Relatively lighter
body masses change the absolute weight lifted to a lighter absolute load,
which makes the intensity the same relative to body mass for men and
women. Women finishing quicker could be associated with increased fitness
levels or less energy expended from having smaller body masses, but more
than likely, it is simply due to being more efficient.

训练主要归因于荷尔蒙差异。这是一个重要的区别，因为大多数训练结
果都与横截面肌肉面积（CSA）的增加有关。 CSA 的增加需要更多雄
激素途径的帮助，这对于女性运动员来说可能不是最佳选择。

女运动员
Charinga（2012）讨论了这种差异：与男性举重运动员相比，女性举重
运动员对更高强度的更高训练量的耐受性更好。 其背后的主要原因之
一是女性在运动过程中的生物力学效率更高，并且可以在抓举、挺举和
挺举中使用更多的被动能量。男性的雄激素水平较高，在举重时依赖更
多来自增加的肌肉质量的机械能，因此无法在训练中积累那么多的训练
量。 雌激素水平较高的女性无法产生那么多的 CSA，因此需要不同的
策略来提高表现。 这也意味着与男性相比，女性的热交换更少。

对性别差异最大的过度反应是，女性需要在训练量和强
度上与男性进行相同的训练。

任何曾经执教过女队的人都直观地理解这一点。采用与男女对应运动
项目（田径、篮球、足球或排球）相同的程序并应用相同的程序，女队
将在很短的时间内完成比赛。 女性完成速度更快通常是因为她们不需
要与男性相同的休息时间，因为她们的训练强度不像男性那么高。这充
其量只是推测而已。没有明确的绝对负载诊断来证明这一说法。 相对
较轻的体重会将举起的绝对重量改变为较轻的绝对负荷，这使得男性和
女性相对于体重的强度相同。女性完成得更快可能与健身水平的提高或
体重较小所消耗的能量减少有关，但更可能的是，这仅仅是因为效率更
高。

In reality, estrogens make passive energy more accessible. Chidi-Ogbolu
and Baar (2019) discussed that while estrogens are effective for increasing
lean muscle mass, they make tendons and ligaments more malleable to stress.
The higher prevalence of estrogens lowers joint stiffness. Certain standards of
movements through various range of motion criteria require less mechanical
energy than their male counterparts. When women perform the same program
in terms of exercise selection, volume, and intensity, they will use less
mechanical energy to accomplish the task.
The biggest underreaction to sex difference—
women are less susceptible to overtraining due to
a higher potential for volume in training.
It becomes incredibly easy to overload a female athlete due to the simple
need to fill time. When men and women use the same program, there
becomes a void of time that needs to be filled for women who finish faster.
This can easily be filled with more “stuff,” which could further dampen their
central nervous system or immune system. As a coach, programming to
accommodate women’s efficiency is critical to preserving higher quality
throughout training.

Male Athletes
With male athletes, we need to be conscious about how to maximize
recovery. We can build density in a training session by shrinking rest
between primary and secondary exercise sets. Or we can be creative with
workout flow by incorporating various things that are needed during intrarest
periods or primary and secondary sets. If the philosophy is one exercise at a
time, this could drastically reduce the total volume in a training session and
possibly should be revisited. Supersetting, or pairing exercises to increase
density, can be reversed; therefore, supersetting is not a principle. It is not a
principle because there are definitive exceptions.
Exercise order rules require us to place higher central nervous system,
higher threshold exercises first in a workout. Before that, there will be some

事实上，雌激素使被动能量更容易获得。 Chidi-Ogbolu 和 Baar (2019
) 讨论道，虽然雌激素可以有效增加瘦肌肉质量，但它们会使肌腱和韧
带更容易承受压力。雌激素的使用率较高会降低关节僵硬。通过各种运
动标准的某些运动标准比男性同行需要更少的机械能。当女性在运动选
择、运动量和强度方面执行相同的计划时，她们会使用更少的机械能来
完成任务。

对性别差异最大的反应不足是，由于女性的训练量潜力
更大，因此不太容易受到过度训练的影响。

由于简单地需要打发时间，女运动员很容易超负荷。 当男性和女性
使用相同的程序时，就会出现时间空白，需要由完成速度更快的女性来
填补。这很容易被更多的“东西”填充，这可能会进一步削弱他们的中

于在整个训练过程中保持更高的质量至关重要。

男运动员
对于男性运动员，我们需要意识到如何最大限度地恢复。 我们可以通
过减少主要和次要练习组之间的休息时间来提高训练密度。 或者，我
们可以通过整合休息期间或主要和次要组期间所需的各种内容来创造性
地设计锻炼流程。如果这一理念是一次一项练习，那么这可能会大大减
少训练课程的总量，并且可能应该重新审视。 超级组或配对练习以增
加密度，可以逆转； 因此，超集并不是一个原则。 这不是一个原则，
因为有明确的例外。
锻炼顺序规则要求我们在锻炼中首先进行中枢神经系统较高、阈值较
高的锻炼。在此之前，还会有一些

movement preparatory exercises. Soft tissue, flexibility exercises, mobility
exercises, and corrective exercises will all have a residual impact on
performance during the earlier exercises in a workout. This creates silos of
time that we need to account for and which could, by default, reduce density
within a training session. In response to this, we can reduce things we do
before primary exercises or splice in between sets. We can unlearn or relearn
how to manage our time to best meet the individual needs of athletes.
One thing in training is that the more complicated the exercise, such as the
increased number of joints used, increased intensity, velocity, or volume and
duration, the more difficult it is to manage. The more return on investment
(ROI) an exercise may have, the more we need to prioritize it, and that may
mean isolating that exercise during a training session. But the problem with
this is that team sports need a variety of planes and vectors to best prepare for
competition. Team sports need a wider range of exercises to best prepare for
the unpredictable environments of competition. If we isolate exercises within
a training session, this could come at the expense of the range of exercises
needed to best prepare that athlete. A narrowed focus on one thing can limit
the potential of developing the male athlete.
With male athletes, we need to accommodate their use of more mechanical
energy in training and figure out creative solutions to manage that output. It
could mean supersetting primaries or pushing and pulling exercises. It could
mean placing a pillar exercise in between sets of a primary exercise. It could
mean we need to better accommodate mechanical advantage and leverage
safely loading joints during an exercise. No matter the solution, with male
athletes, we need to appreciate that they cannot hit the same densities as
women in a training session. The lack of efficiency among men creates a
fundamental need for more creative solutions during training.
The nuance between men and women is enough to consider when
programming. The ability to manage variables to serve your athletes is the
secret to the game. Holding on to arbitrary things like particular programs or
conditional dependencies limits what we can do and runs contrary to the
principle of individuality.

动作准备练习。 软组织、灵活性练习、灵活性练习和矫正练习都会对
锻炼中早期练习的表现产生残余影响。 这会产生我们需要考虑的时间
孤岛，并且默认情况下，这可能会降低训练课程中的密度。 针对这一
点，我们可以减少主要练习之前或组间拼接之前所做的事情。我们可以
忘记或重新学习如何管理我们的时间，以最好地满足运动员的个人需求
。
训练中的一件事是，练习越复杂，例如使用的关节数量增加，强度、
速度或体积和持续时间增加，管理起来就越困难。 一项练习的投资回
报 (ROI) 越高，我们就越需要优先考虑它，这可能意味着在训练期间隔
离该练习。 但问题是团队运动需要各种飞机和载体来为比赛做好最好
的准备。团队运动需要更广泛的练习，以便为不可预测的比赛环境做好
最好的准备。如果我们在一次训练中单独进行练习，这可能会以牺牲运
动员最佳准备所需的练习范围为代价。只专注于一件事可能会限制男性
运动员的发展潜力。

对于男性运动员，我们需要适应他们在训练中使用更多的机械能，并
找出创造性的解决方案来管理这种输出。 这可能意味着超组初选或推
拉练习。这可能意味着在几组主要练习之间放置一个支柱练习。这可能
意味着我们需要更好地适应机械优势并在锻炼过程中安全地利用加载关
节。 无论采取何种解决方案，对于男性运动员来说，我们都需要认识
到，他们在训练中无法达到与女性相同的密度。 由于男性缺乏效率，
因此在训练期间迫切需要更具创造性的解决方案。
编程时，男性和女性之间的细微差别就足以考虑。 管理变量来为运
动员服务的能力是这项运动的秘诀。坚持任意的东西，比如特定的程序
或条件依赖，限制了我们能做的事情，并且违背了个性原则。

Female athletes—more efficient, manage volume
at high intensity.
Male athletes—less efficient, require creative
workout design.

Muscle Fiber Type
The other big consideration for individuality is muscle fiber type. For the
most part, sports are aligned by muscle fiber type. Fast-twitch fibers have fast
fatigue rates, are primarily anaerobic, and can generate higher force and
velocity. Whereas slow-twitch fibers have slow fatigue rates, are primarily
aerobic, and can accomplish large amounts of work. Team sports and various
individual sports, such as sprinting and jumping, are primarily fast-twitch
oriented. Whereas individual sports that focus on distance or duration are
slow-twitch oriented.
Fiber type influences training to a great degree. The key attribute that
distinguishes individual muscle fiber types is their rate of fatigue. Increasing
capacity helps overcome fatigue from central to increasing thresholds in
training.
The biggest overreaction to muscle fiber type—fast-twitch fibers will
convert to slow-twitch fibers if we train for a longer duration.

Fast-Twitch Athletes
Fast responders are fast-twitch athletes. This should feel intuitive, and it is
nice when that plays out. It makes the concept of who will respond faster to
stress easier to remember. A word of caution here: Fast responders generally
are more susceptible to burnout or overtraining. Fast-twitch athletes are fast
responders because they use faster energy-yielding fuel substrates.
Phosphagen systems use a combination of ATP and phosphocreatine along
with greater use of glycolysis, which creates more rapid energy but also more
waste products. They will respond faster, but that comes with an equal risk of
being overworked.

女运动员——效率更高，在高强度下控制训练量。
男性运动员效率较低，需要创造性的锻炼设计。

肌纤维类型
个性的另一个重要考虑因素是肌肉纤维类型。 在大多数情况下，运动
是根据肌纤维类型进行调整的。快肌纤维具有快速的疲劳率，主要是厌
氧的，并且可以产生更高的力和速度。 而慢肌纤维的疲劳率较低，主
要是有氧的，可以完成大量的工作。团队运动和各种个人运动，例如短
跑和跳跃，主要以快肌为导向。 而注重距离或持续时间的个人运动则
以慢肌纤维为导向。
纤维类型在很大程度上影响训练。 区分各个肌纤维类型的关键属性
是它们的疲劳率。能力的提高有助于克服训练中从中心到增加阈值的疲
劳。
对肌纤维类型最大的过度反应是，如果我们训练时间较长，快肌纤维
将转化为慢肌纤维。

快肌运动员
快速反应者是快肌运动员。 这应该感觉很直观，而且当它发挥出来时
感觉很好。 它使谁对压力反应更快的概念更容易记住。这里需要注意
的是：快速反应者通常更容易出现倦怠或过度训练。 快肌运动员反应
速度很快，因为他们使用产生能量更快的燃料基质。磷酸原系统结合使
用 ATP 和磷酸肌酸，并更多地使用糖酵解，从而产生更快速的能量，
但也产生更多废物。他们的反应速度会更快，但这也会带来同样的过度
劳累的风险。

The biggest consideration we have to make with muscle fiber types is how
much density (work in a given period) we can safely accrue. Athletes with a
higher distribution of fast-twitch fibers will fatigue faster and need longer
recovery, thus decreasing density. Fast-twitch fibers will exert more (rate
coding, motor unit recruitment, neurotransmitter usage) per repetition at the
same intensity compared to slow-twitch muscle fibers. You will see their rep
max chart play out differently relative to a slow-twitch athlete.
Accommodating someone with a higher distribution of muscle fibers who
cannot hit a number at a given intensity relative to a slow-twitch athlete
greatly affects programming (Ahtiainen, 2015). If we prescribe a certain
intensity to the fast-twitch athletes, they will not be as capable of hitting as
many reps as the slow-twitch athletes. The fast-twitch athlete will have a
higher perceived intensity, or rating of perceived exertion.
The biggest underreaction to muscle fiber type—
aerobic development is devalued for fast-twitch
fibers.
The trickiest part of all this is the management of density within a team
setting. Ahtiainen and colleagues (2015) describe the prevalence of certain
muscle fiber types as a key feature of why some athletes adapt differently to
the same training protocol. Again, training within the team setting with a
singular program makes variance more of an issue.
A significant aspect of exercise physiology is the understanding that all
energy systems are working concurrently (Plisk, 1991). We understand
energy systems by reducing them to three primary systems: phosphagen,
glycolysis, and oxidation (see chapter 3 for more information). Because we
break them up to understand them does not mean they work in isolation. We
have understood for some time that developing anaerobic systems is
predicated on aerobic-driven pathways. Our fast-twitch athletes will be
limited by how well they can recover between anaerobic bouts of exercise.
The recovery between anaerobic bouts is accomplished aerobically (Plisk,
1991). Being limited by how much we can do in a training session by limited

对于肌肉纤维类型，我们必须考虑的最大因素是我们可以安全地增加
多少密度（在给定时间内做功）。快肌纤维分布较多的运动员会更快疲
劳，需要更长的恢复时间，从而降低密度。 与慢肌纤维相比，在相同
强度下，快肌纤维每次重复会发挥更多作用（速率编码、运动单位募集

现有所不同。与慢肌纤维运动员相比，肌肉纤维分布较多但无法在给定

其同事（2015）将某些肌纤维类型的普遍存在描述为为什么一些运动员
对相同训练方案的适应不同的一个关键特征。 同样，在团队环境中使
用单一计划进行培训会使差异成为一个更大的问题。
运动生理学的一个重要方面是理解所有能量系统同时工作（Plisk，19
91）。 我们通过将能量系统简化为三个主要系统来理解它们：磷酸原
、糖酵解和氧化（有关更多信息，请参阅第 3 章）。 因为我们将它们
分解以理解它们并不意味着它们是孤立工作的。一段时间以来，我们已
经了解到无氧系统的发展是以有氧驱动的途径为基础的。 我们的快肌
运动员将受到无氧运动之间恢复程度的限制。无氧运动之间的恢复是通
过有氧运动完成的（Plisk，1991）。受限于我们在一次训练中能做的事
情

oxidative capacity is a key determinant of how high our ceiling can be for
fast-twitch athletes.
The athletes we have to accommodate the most during training will always
be the most anaerobically adapted. The response to this is to adjust to a lower
density of work to accommodate their lack of recovery, which could come at
a cost to development for fast-twitch athletes (figure 2.5).

Slow-Twitch Athletes
In the case of this example of relative intensity for slow-twitch athletes, we
need to encourage challenging rep-intensity selection. Having a slow-twitch
athlete execute the same repetitions at a given intensity as a fast-twitch
athlete will not be difficult for the slow-twitch athlete. Encouraging athletes
who are more fatigue resistant to push their intensity to a higher level to
accommodate their greater endurance is as important as managing perceived
effort for fast-twitch athletes.
Slow-twitch athletes generally have a higher capacity at a given rep
bracket. Said differently, they can do more reps at a certain intensity relative
to a fast-twitch athlete. We need to address this by accommodating them with
a higher number of reps at a given intensity. Slow-twitch fibers have more
mitochondria present, which allows for expedited recovery between sets. We
accommodate them by using shorter rest periods between sets. Athletes with
higher distributions of slow-twitch fibers will fatigue more slowly and need
less recovery, thus increasing density. The impact on volume, density, and
even frequency is immense based on fiber type distribution.

氧化能力是快肌运动员的上限的关键决定因素。
我们在训练期间最需要适应的运动员总是最适应无氧运动的。对此的
应对措施是调整到较低的训练密度，以适应他们缺乏恢复的情况，这可
能会损害快肌运动员的发展（图 2.5）。

慢肌纤维运动员
在这个慢肌运动员相对强度的例子中，我们需要鼓励具有挑战性的重复
强度选择。 让慢肌运动员在给定强度下执行与快肌运动员相同的重复
动作对于慢肌运动员来说并不困难。 鼓励更抗疲劳的运动员将强度提
高到更高水平以适应更大的耐力，与管理快肌运动员的感知努力同样重
要。
慢肌运动员通常在给定的次数范围内具有更高的能力。换句话说，相
对于快肌运动员，他们可以在一定强度下做更多次数。我们需要通过在
给定强度下为他们提供更多次数来解决这个问题。 慢肌纤维含有更多
线粒体，可以加快组间恢复。我们通过缩短组间休息时间来适应他们。
慢肌纤维分布较高的运动员疲劳速度会更慢，并且需要较少的恢复，从
而增加密度。 根据纤维类型分布，对体积、密度甚至频率的影响是巨
大的。

FIGURE 2.5 Muscle fiber rep max.
We can limit our focus to one aspect of training, such as anaerobic output,
and lose sight of what is going on daily. If you take the macro view of
someone who is not stimulated enough due to not enough volume, it becomes
a huge problem. The discrepancies that Ahtiainen and colleagues (2015) saw
in training are not from one training session; they are the aggregate of several
training sessions over multiple weeks. If the more aerobically developed
athlete is accruing more reps during a training session simply by being able to
recover faster, the difference would be immense over a week, a block, a
mesocycle, and an entire training program.
Considering muscle fiber type during training sessions is extremely
difficult. Sex, training age, and biological age are easier to classify. When it
comes to nuanced areas like muscle fiber type, which is harder to quantify
directly, making changes during training becomes increasingly difficult.
Therefore, it becomes increasingly important to track and monitor during
training blocks to assess rates of progress or lack thereof.
Fast-twitch athletes—less fatigue resistant,
develop anaerobic capacity through oxidative
pathways.
Slow-twitch athletes—more fatigue resistant,
increase intensity at a given rep bracket.

我们可以将注意力限制在训练的某一方面，例如无氧输出，而忽略了
每天发生的事情。 如果宏观来看一个人因为量不够而刺激不够，那就
是一个大问题了。 Ahtiainen 及其同事（2015）在培训中看到的差异并
非来自一次培训；而是来自一次培训。它们是数周内多次培训课程的总
和。 如果有氧运动能力更强的运动员在训练期间仅仅通过恢复得更快
而获得更多次数，那么在一周、一个训练组、一个中周期和整个训练计
划中，差异将是巨大的。
在训练过程中考虑肌肉纤维类型是非常困难的。性别、训练年龄和生
物学年龄更容易分类。当涉及到肌纤维类型等微妙领域时，很难直接量
化，因此在训练期间做出改变变得越来越困难。因此，在训练期间进行
跟踪和监控以评估进展或缺乏进展的速度变得越来越重要。

Athlete Tracking and Monitoring
We are in a renaissance of sports science. Reading through Science &
Practice or Supertraining, you can romanticize proletariat ideologies, treating
athletes as if they were high-priced experiments pushing the boundaries of
human potential. You may have read those seminal books on performance
training. You probably were invigorated by the thought of incorporating more
advanced methods with your team. We’re going to track this, implement that,
examine and debrief on all that can be examined … then you get in front of
25 14-year-olds who cannot pay attention even if you paid them to. In turn,
you throw out everything you learned and rely on time-tested, proven
methodologies. This is all too often a series of events for a strength coach.
With advancements in technology and innovation in the daily practice of
athlete monitoring, we have made great strides in making this a reality. We
can implement daily tracking on a low budget: sleep, wellness, rating of
perceived exertion, and basic performance tracking. On a high budget, we
can implement wearables, global positioning system (GPS), velocity-based
training (VBT), blood, urine, saliva, and data analytics software. Whatever
your budget, you can implement tracking and monitoring. The ability to
implement a high-level program within a team setting has never been more
attainable.
Tracking and monitoring, regardless of how big or small the scale is, gives
insight into rates of change per individual. Neupert and colleagues (2019)
made an excellent case that periodization in general needs to evolve as a
construct entirely. Instead of being a predetermined aspect of training
programs, it needs to be a living, breathing entity that becomes a new
iteration as we get more information. Periodization is the initial construct
behind the methodology, which then shifts to meet the level of adaptations
based on what monitoring tells us. It takes the proverbial baton from the
original concept of periodization and planning and runs with it into the
future; its central piece is individuality.
There are countless other variables that we need to consider for
individuality in team training. Height is one; pairing people at the same rack

运动员跟踪和监控
我们正处于运动科学的复兴之中。 阅读Science & Practice或
Supertraining，您可以将无产阶级意识形态浪漫化，将运动员视为推动
人类潜力极限的高价实验品。 您可能已经阅读过那些关于表现训练的
开创性书籍。您可能因将更先进的方法与您的团队结合起来而感到振奋
。我们将跟踪这个，实施那个，检查并汇报所有可以检查的事情……然
后你就会站在 25 个 14 岁的孩子面前，即使你付钱给他们，他们也无法
集中注意力。 反过来，你会抛弃你所学到的一切，并依赖经过时间考
验、经过验证的方法。对于力量教练来说，这往往是一系列的事件。
随着运动员监测日常实践中技术的进步和创新，我们在实现这一目标
方面取得了长足的进步。 我们可以以较低的预算实现日常跟踪：睡眠
、健康、感知劳累评级以及基本表现跟踪。 在高预算的情况下，我们
可以实施可穿戴设备、全球定位系统 (GPS)、基于速度的训练 (VBT)、
血液、尿液、唾液和数据分析软件。 无论您的预算如何，您都可以实
施跟踪和监控。 在团队环境中实施高水平计划的能力从未如此容易实
现。
跟踪和监控，无论规模有多大或多小，都可以深入了解每个人的变化
率。 Neupert 及其同事（2019）提出了一个很好的案例，即周期化总体
上需要作为一种结构完全发展。 它不是训练计划的预定方面，而是需
要成为一个活生生的、会呼吸的实体，当我们获得更多信息时，它会成
为新的迭代。 周期化是该方法背后的初始构造，然后根据监测结果进
行调整以满足适应水平。 它从最初的分期和规划概念中接过众所周知
的接力棒，并带着它走向未来；它的核心是个性。

对于团队训练中的个性化，我们还需要考虑无数其他变量。身高为一
；将同一机架上的人员配对

who are drastically different heights is not something we can be successful
with. What you say in that situation is, “Tall person, it is easier for you to go
down than for the short person to go up.” Bodyweight is another factor that
we need to account for. Imagine doing a bodyweight exercise and
programming a higher rep count for an athlete under 200 lb (91 kg) than for
an athlete over 300 lb (136 kg). Relative strength exercises, such as pull-ups,
push-ups, single squats, or leg curls, are drastically different for a person who
is under 200 lb (91 kg) than for one who is 300 lb (136 kg).
A key aspect of this is understanding that group dynamics affect the
psychological development of athletes. The law of averages dictates that we
will fall into some sort of mean; this is also called regression to the mean
(figure 2.6). Meaning that if we do something long enough or with enough
people, eventually a level of variance will settle. Remember that Mukherjee
(2015) states, “Outliers create the rules.” We can build off that comment by
creating rules or constraints to help us control the level of differences. This
phenomenon can help us with the task of creating a program that
accommodates individuality while still having some semblance of quality
control.
One aspect that comes up with child development is the concept of nature
versus nurture. If we have biological twins that are as close as two humans
could be, growing up in separate environments, what will be the impact?
Harris (2021) discusses that an adolescent’s peers have a greater influence on
their development and socialization than their parents. This point is a
foundational piece to understanding how to reduce noise or variance within a
team of individuals. As coaches, we only have so much impact on an
individual relative to the level of impact the rest of the team has. The
question is, how do we manage the team?

身高相差悬殊的人并不是我们能够成功的对象。在这种情况下你会说：
“高个子，你下去比矮个子上去容易。” 体重是我们需要考虑的另一
个因素。 想象一下，在进行自重锻炼时，体重低于 200 磅（91 公斤）
的运动员比体重超过 300 磅（136 公斤）的运动员计划的重复次数更高
。相对力量练习，例如引体向上、俯卧撑、单蹲或腿弯举，对于体重低
于 200 磅（91 公斤）的人与体重 300 磅（136 公斤）的人来说有很大不
同。
其中一个关键方面是了解群体动态会影响运动员的心理发展。 平均
法则规定我们会陷入某种平均状态； 这也称为regression to the mean (
图 2.6)。 这意味着，如果我们做某件事足够长的时间或有足够多的人
参与，最终一定程度的差异将会得到解决。 请记住 Mukherjee (2015) 指
出，“异常值创造了规则。” 我们可以通过创建规则或约束来建立该
评论，以帮助我们控制差异程度。 这种现象可以帮助我们创建一个既
能适应个性，又能保持一定质量控制的程序。

儿童发展的一个方面是先天与后天的概念。 如果我们有像两个人一
样亲密的生物双胞胎，在不同的环境中长大，会产生什么影响？ Harris
(2021) 讨论了青少年的同龄人对他们的发展和社会化的影响比他们的父
母更大。 这一点是理解如何减少团队中的噪音或差异的基础。 作为教
练，我们对个人的影响力相对于团队其他成员的影响力来说是有限的。
那么问题来了，我们如何管理团队呢？

FIGURE 2.6 Regression to the mean.
We can run multiple programs within a large group of people and see the
effect of training relative to one another. Understanding that the nurture
component of large groups will reduce noise in results, we can bank on that
positively affecting results. Having more specific recommendations based on
training age, biological age, sex, or muscle fiber type can create more
positive adaptations across the group. The distribution becomes skewed,
potentially from moderately high to high.
The response to training from multiple programs could swing violently the
other way if we do not place controls on the environment. Research helps
determine the environment. We can do this in multiple ways: assigning group
times based on programs, assigning racks or groups within the group based
on specific characteristics, and organizing the training facility to allow for a
clearer flow from exercise to exercise based on a specific program.
Further controls are based on tracking and monitoring, creating workflows
that control volume and intensity based on rates of adaptation. Outside
stressors affect intratraining a great deal. A bad night’s sleep, dehydration,
lack of nutrition, immunocompromised periods like finals or travel, and
personal affairs all affect performance. Having an account for subsequent
contingencies is a fundamental step in creating controls on the volume or
intensity reached during a training session.

均值回归。

我们可以在一大群人中运行多个项目，并查看相对于彼此的培训效果
。 了解大群体的培育成分会减少结果中的噪音，我们可以指望这会对
结果产生积极影响。根据训练年龄、生物年龄、性别或肌纤维类型提供
更具体的建议可以在整个群体中创造更积极的适应。 分布变得倾斜，
可能从中高到高。
如果我们不对环境进行控制，对多个项目的培训的反应可能会剧烈地
向另一个方向摇摆。 研究有助于确定环境。我们可以通过多种方式做
到这一点：根据计划分配小组时间，根据具体特征在小组内分配训练架
或小组，以及根据特定计划组织训练设施，以实现从一个练习到另一个
练习的更清晰的流程。
进一步的控制基于跟踪和监控，创建根据适应率控制音量和强度的工
作流程。 外部压力源对内部训练影响很大。 晚上睡眠不好、脱水、缺
乏营养、期末考试或旅行等免疫功能低下的时期以及个人事务都会影响
表现。 考虑到后续的突发事件是控制训练期间达到的训练量或强度的
一个基本步骤。

The unenviable task of designing a program that will enhance everyone is
our responsibility to figure out. We must first understand that this is
inevitable, appreciate the differences in response to training from various
individuals, and place them in systems of controls and monitoring to best
adjust training. Individuality is a principle that is easily taken for granted, and
this is a huge mistake. We can get lucky with one-off programs and fast
responders, but does this translate to larger groups? Focus on what is
different, then make the necessary adjustments. Lean on the group dynamics
that help, monitor and adjust again, and continue until the team is ready for
the season.

Multiple Programs
Having multiple programs occurring at the same time with a
singular team will test your ability to manage a team during
training. A common discussion among S&C practitioners is
whether we are better served by performing one program that is
easy to manage or multiple programs that are difficult to
manage.
This is not to say that a singular program cannot have
specifications for the individual. We can accommodate intensity
relatively easily and go heavier or lighter based on the execution.
We can accommodate lateralizations and regressions by finding
an exercise that does not hurt or that the athlete can be
successful with. We can create customized “necessary” work for
individuals to do on top of the program.
Alternatively, we can make a customized program for each
person on the team. There are situations where we can do this,
and there is a case that if we can, we should. Having one team
of 15 athletes makes it manageable to create a customized
program for each individual. Exercise selection based on
biomechanics and periodization based on physiology from an indepth screen sounds like a dream.
An analogy in business that we can pull from is vertical versus

设计一个能够增强每个人的计划这一艰巨的任务是我们有责任弄清楚
的。 我们必须首先明白这是不可避免的，了解不同个体对训练反应的
差异，并将它们置于控制和监控系统中，以最好地调整训练。个性是一
个很容易被视为理所当然的原则，这是一个巨大的错误。 我们可以幸
运地获得一次性计划和快速响应者，但这是否会转化为更大的群体？
关注不同之处，然后进行必要的调整。依靠团队的动力来帮助、监控和
调整，并继续下去，直到球队为赛季做好准备。

多个程序
在一个团队中同时进行多个项目将考验您在培训期间管理团队的
能力。 S&C 从业者之间的一个常见讨论是，执行一个易于管理的
计划还是执行多个难以管理的计划是否可以为我们提供更好的服
务。
这并不是说单个程序不能为个人提供规范。 我们可以相对轻松
地调节强度，并根据执行情况增加或减少重量。我们可以通过找
到一种不会造成伤害或运动员可以成功的练习来适应偏侧化和回
归。我们可以为个人在该计划的基础上创建定制的“必要”工作
。
或者，我们可以为团队中的每个人制定定制计划。 在某些情况
下我们可以这样做，在某些情况下如果我们可以，我们就应该这
样做。 一支由 15 名运动员组成的团队可以轻松地为每个人制定
定制计划。 基于生物力学的运动选择和基于生理学的周期化从深
度屏幕听起来就像一个梦想。
我们可以从商业中得出一个类比：垂直与

horizontal integration. On the one hand, if we want to focus on a
singular product by acquiring supply chains to make a product,
that would be vertical integration. On the other hand, we may
want to buy a business that is not directly related but would be a
good revenue stream to add to a portfolio, which would be
horizontal integration. Both have their pros and cons. If we focus
on vertical integration only, we can become fragile to changes in
the popularity of that item. We incur high costs, which affect our
profit margins for a single product. If we focus on buying
nonrelated products, that could distract us from our primary
revenue stream.
With multiple programs versus a single program, you have to
decide what is most effective to reach the desired outcome. Are
you going to vertically integrate by having a single program and
putting all resources there? Or are you going to horizontally
integrate by having multiple programs going on simultaneously?
Both have their strengths and weaknesses. As a coach, you
have to decide whether one helps more than the other.
Peer impact gives us a tool to build a foundational concept:
Large groups will reduce variance organically. Group settings
reduce variance with social aspects of training, which can omit
variables that make it hard to determine where progress came
from. We can approach this one way: Make an extremely simple
and universal program that everyone has to do. This happens
quite a bit in team training. Not accommodating individual
differences creates more variance in results.
The individual factors are summarized as follows:
Training Age
Biggest overreaction: Success with novice trainees does not scale out
to large groups.
Biggest underreaction: Advanced trainees have already adapted to the
stimulus.

横向一体化。一方面，如果我们想通过收购供应链来制造产品来
专注于单一产品，那就是垂直整合。 另一方面，我们可能想购买
一个不直接相关的业务，但会是一个很好的收入来源，可以添加
到投资组合中，这将是横向整合。两者都有各自的优点和缺点。
如果我们只关注垂直整合，我们可能会对该产品受欢迎程度的变
化变得脆弱。 我们的成本很高，这影响了我们单一产品的利润率
。 如果我们专注于购买不相关的产品，这可能会分散我们对主要
收入来源的注意力。

对于多个计划与单个计划，您必须决定什么最有效地达到预期
结果。 您是否打算通过单一程序并将所有资源放在那里来进行垂
直整合？ 或者您打算通过同时运行多个程序来进行横向整合？两
者都有各自的优点和缺点。 作为一名教练，你必须决定一个人是
否比另一个人更有帮助。
同伴影响为我们提供了构建基本概念的工具：大群体将有机地
减少差异。 小组设置减少了培训中社交方面的差异，这可能会忽
略一些变量，从而难以确定进步来自何处。我们可以用一种方法
来解决这个问题：制作一个非常简单且通用的程序，每个人都必
须这样做。 这种情况在团队训练中经常发生。 不适应个体差异
会导致结果出现更大的差异。

个别因素总结如下：
训练年龄
Biggest overreaction:新手学员的成功并不会扩展到大型团体。
Biggest underreaction:高级学员已经适应了这种刺激。

Biological Age
Biggest overreaction: Older athletes need the same stimulus to reach
peak performance as when they were younger.
Biggest underreaction: Younger athletes can handle unlimited stress.
Sex
Biggest overreaction: Women need to do the same program as men in
volume and intensity.
Biggest underreaction: Women are less susceptible to overtraining due
to a higher potential for volume in training.
Muscle Fiber Type
Biggest overreaction: Fast-twitch muscle fibers will convert to slowtwitch fibers if we train for longer durations.
Biggest underreaction: Aerobic development is devalued for fasttwitch athletes.

Take Home
Individuality is a principle that we as coaches need to understand. Seeing and
doing nothing based on training age, biological age, sex, or muscle fiber type
is a huge missed opportunity. It is an opportunity to find better methods of
tracking and monitoring. It is an opportunity to create controls and systems
that create better practices to manage differences between one athlete and
another.

生物年龄
Biggest overreaction:年长的运动员需要与年轻时相同的刺激才能
达到最佳表现。 Biggest underreaction:年轻运动员可以承受无限的
压力。
性别
Biggest overreaction:女性需要在数量和强度上与男性进行相同的计
划。 Biggest underreaction: 由于训练量的潜力更大，女性不太容易
受到过度训练的影响。
肌纤维类型
Biggest overreaction:如果我们训练时间较长，快肌纤维将转化为慢
肌纤维。 Biggest underreaction: 对于快肌运动员来说，有氧运动
的发展被低估了。

带回家
个性是我们作为教练需要理解的原则。根据训练年龄、生物年龄、性别
或肌肉纤维类型来观察和采取任何行动是一个巨大的错失机会。 这是
寻找更好的跟踪和监控方法的机会。 这是一个创建控制和系统的机会
，可以创建更好的实践来管理运动员与另一名运动员之间的差异。

SPECIFICITY
What specificity is is not as important as what it represents. Specificity is
simply that we become better at what we repeat. Hawley (2008) defined it
as “training responses—adaptations are tightly coupled to the mode,
frequency, and duration of the exercise performed.” The question we have to
answer in this chapter is whether repeating something over and over creates a
beneficial outcome. Specificity represents the intent behind what we do as
much as what we do.
Michael Yessis (2008) coined the term specific physical preparation
(SPP). This runs counter to general physical preparation (GPP). This simple
distinction served the functional purpose of athletes developing general
qualities that were supposed to indirectly increase their specific capabilities.
GPP’s main goal was to increase the potential of SPP’s effect on the athlete’s
peak performance. The higher one could raise someone’s GPP, the higher the
potential for SPP.
In a sense, this classification created a siloed approach to performance.
GPP became the responsibility of the S&C coach before the season, and SPP
became the role of the sports coach during the season. A house divided
became the result of GPP and SPP in North American sports.
Bondarchuk, discussed in Brearley and Bishop (2019), broke down
specificity into exercise selections: general preparatory exercises, specific
preparatory exercises, specialized developmental exercises, and finally,
competitive exercises. Similar to Yessis (2008), it created distinctions with

3
特异性
特异性是什么并不重要，重要的是它所代表的内容。 特异性就是让我
们在重复的事情上变得更好。 Hawley（2008）将其定义为“训练反应
——适应与所进行的练习的模式、频率和持续时间紧密相关。”本章中
我们必须回答的问题是一遍又一遍地重复某件事是否会产生有益的结果
。 特异性代表了我们所做的事情背后的意图。
Michael Yessis (2008) 创造了术语 specific physical preparation (SPP)
。这与 general physical preparation (GPP) 背道而驰。这种简单的区别服
务于运动员发展一般素质的功能目的，这些素质应该间接提高他们的特
定能力。 GPP 的主要目标是提高 SPP 对运动员最佳表现的影响潜力。
可以提高某人的 GPP 越高，SPP 的潜力就越大。
从某种意义上说，这种分类创建了一种孤立的绩效方法。 GPP在赛
季前成为S&C教练的职责，SPP在赛季中成为体育教练的角色。 一场分
裂成为了北美体育界GPP和SPP的结果。
Bondarchuk 在 Brearley 和 Bishop（2019）中讨论过，将特异性分解
为练习选择：一般准备练习、特定准备练习、专门发展练习，最后是竞
争性练习。 与 Yessis (2008) 类似，它与

specific inputs but in a way that closed the gap between GPP and SPP silos. It
was less seasonal and more a function of the inputs we chose to do with
athletes. What is true is that a more European model of performance, where
everything is unified, needs classifications of general versus specific. This
classification was due to the overlap and connectivity between sports
coaches, S&C coaches, psychology, and sports medicine.
James Smith (2015) discussed the concept of a unified theory of sport, in
which he dove into a completely integrated model of sports performance. The
original intent of Yessis (2008) and Bondarchuk (in Brearley & Bishop,
2019) was not to create separate entities or divisions of the year based on an
athlete’s development. Smith’s interpretation was to integrate all facets of an
athlete’s development into a singular framework within the North American
sports system, tying together, as he put it in his book, Governing Dynamics
(2015): cultural, psychological, analytical, technical, tactical, biomotor,
biodynamic, bioenergetic, and medical. Each role within an athletic
department functions as a singular entity toward creating a more capable and
resilient athlete (figure 3.1).

Remove Bias
Continuing with the theme of obvious statements: Anything we
repeat will eventually improve. Let’s take this familiar principle
and look at it in a new light to gain a greater perspective. To
appreciate the relative impact of specificity, we need to evaluate
where we often go wrong.
“You are the product of what you repeatedly do, so excellence
is not an act; it is a habit.”
—Aristotle
The concept of bias is real. Bias is a preference toward
something regardless of logic or reason. It does not mean that
no logic or reason is used, but all logic is directed toward
validating a preconceived belief. Bias is based on several
factors, most notably ego and pride. We all want to be
recognized as coaches. We find that the best way to be

特定的投入，但以某种方式缩小了 GPP 和 SPP 孤岛之间的差距。它的
季节性较少，更多的是我们选择对运动员进行的投入的函数。 事实是
，一个更加欧洲化的绩效模型，其中一切都是统一的，需要一般与特定
的分类。 这种分类是由于运动教练、体能教练、心理学和运动医学之
间的重叠和联系。
詹姆斯·史密斯（James Smith，2015）讨论了运动统一理论的概念，
其中他深入研究了运动表现的完全集成模型。 Yessis（2008）和 Bondar
chuk（Brearley & Bishop，2019）的初衷并不是根据运动员的发展情况
创建单独的年度实体或部门。史密斯的解释是将运动员发展的各个方面
整合到北美体育体系的一个单一框架中，正如他在《
Governing Dynamics (2015)》一书中所说：文化、心理、分析、技术、
战术、生物运动、生物动力、生物能量和医学。 体育部门内的每个角
色都作为一个单一的实体发挥作用，旨在培养更有能力、更有韧性的运
动员（图 3.1）。

消除偏见
继续显而易见的主题：我们重复的任何事情最终都会有所改善。
让我们以新的眼光来看待这个熟悉的原则，以获得更广阔的视角
。 为了了解特异性的相对影响，我们需要评估我们经常出错的地
方。
“你是你反复做事的产物，所以卓越不是一种行为，而是一种
习惯。”
——亚里士多德
偏见的概念是真实存在的。 偏见是对某事的偏好，无论逻辑或
理由如何。 这并不意味着不使用逻辑或推理，而是所有逻辑都旨
在验证先入为主的信念。 偏见是基于几个因素，最明显的是自我
和骄傲。 我们都希望被认可为教练。 我们发现最好的方式是

recognized is to stand out in a particular area. If we excel in one
aspect of performance, we can, in turn, be more readily identified
as an expert or as unique. What eventually starts to unfold is an
affinity toward the thing that makes us an expert, and thus, the
development of a bias. There are other reasons a bias develops,
such as success, community, a mentor, or just preference. What
makes this complex is that we are constantly faced with
problems outside the scope of our biased method or protocol.
Often, someone with exceptional skill in one area uses that
skill exclusively with anyone they may train.
A weightlifter teaches weightlifting, a powerlifter teaches
powerlifting, a bodybuilder teaches bodybuilding, and the list
goes on and on. What we see is that they get better at what they
are asking their athletes to do. With specificity as a principle, it is
expected that everyone improves in what they do repeatedly.
What we do not know is if they are closer to an outcome they
desire or need. The association of improvement without
considering whether improvements were made toward a specific
goal is flawed logic.
In a sense, S&C has been regulated to GPP over SPP. Early
on in our profession, this was out of necessity. Many of us were
working other jobs while also running a weight room. Over time,
we made S&C into a full-time profession that was performed at
practices and meetings, which created a crossover to the SPP
side of the world. Ritual and tradition are associated with the
idea that we are GPP specialists, not sports coaches. The
question is, is that the best angle for our athletes?
GPP develops the big three (biomotor, biomechanical, and
bioenergetic systems) without context. Just getting stronger,
faster, and better conditioned is wonderful. Without context, it
can run flat relative to someone extremely skilled in their sport.
We see this example all the time, and it is significantly more
important with sports that require a high degree of skill, such as
baseball, relative to football. Football benefits are greater than

被认可就是在某个特定领域脱颖而出。如果我们在某一方面表现
出色，我们就会更容易被认为是专家或独特的人。最终开始显现
的是对使我们成为专家的事物的亲和力，从而形成了偏见。偏见
的形成还有其他原因，例如成功、社区、导师或仅仅是偏好。使
事情变得复杂的是，我们不断面临着我们有偏见的方法或协议范
围之外的问题。
通常，在某一领域具有特殊技能的人会专门将这种技能用于他
们可能训练的任何人。
举重运动员教举重，举重运动员教举重，健美运动员教健美，
这样的例子不胜枚举。我们看到的是，他们在要求运动员做的事
情上做得更好了。以针对性为原则，期望每个人都能在重复做的

关联起来是有缺陷的逻辑。

从某种意义上说，S&C 受到 GPP 而非 SPP 的监管。在我们职
业的早期，这是出于必要。我们中的许多人一边做其他工作，一

职业，在练习和会议中进行，这创造了与 SPP 世界的交叉。 仪式
和传统与我们是 GPP 专家而不是体育教练的理念相关。 问题是，
这对我们运动员来说是最好的角度吗？
GPP 在没有背景的情况下开发了三大系统（生物运动、生物力
学和生物能量系统）。 变得更强、更快、状态更好就很棒了。
如果没有上下文，它可能会相对于在其运动中非常熟练的人来说
平淡无奇。我们经常看到这个例子，对于需要高水平技能的运动

好处大于

baseball if all we focused on was GPP. The issue with that
approach is that it only works for so long and with so many

Reframing to a singular focus where all divisions are aligned gives

have an appreciation of how improving general qualities applies to specific
circumstances (figure 3.2). The sports coach should have an understanding of
how general training inputs affect specific qualities. The idea is that if we
were to do something redundantly to make a change, all parties—coaches and
athletes—should agree that it is beneficial.

图 3.1 特异性框架。
重新构建一个单一的焦点，让所有部门保持一致，为我们从特异性中
获得的结果提供了动力。体能教练应该了解如何在特定情况下提高综合
素质（图 3.2）。体育教练应该了解一般训练投入如何影响特定素质。

教练和运动员——都应该同意这是有益的。

FIGURE 3.2 General to specific.
Imagine a dynamic where all parties involved with an athlete’s
performance understood specificity as Mang (2022) describes it:
“Physiological adaptations to exercise reflect the specific stimuli applied
during an exercise training program.” The choice to choose an exercise that is
more appropriate within a specific period of the year or based on that
athlete’s development would not be a bad thing. The development of
irrelevant variables is an ineffective approach to training. It may manifest in
improvement not directly relevant to the athlete’s needs or the demands they
have during competition.
The direction of the training we choose should be more thought out and
focused on a unified approach. A concept called dynamic correspondence
(Brearley & Bishop, 2019), which is the perceived effect from general to
specific qualities. It is a concentric circle created from a decision made
regarding training. Dynamic correspondence refers to the interconnectedness
of general training inputs with more specific training inputs.
Verkhoshansky (2011) broke down general training inputs into three
separate categories: bioenergetic, biomotor, and biomechanical systems. In
reality, these categories are interconnected and are facilitative of each other.
These three separate but connected entities are what we can leverage to have
an impact on performance. Influencing someone’s ability to create and use
energy efficiently (bioenergetics), the rate, length, or amount of force they
can create (biomotor ability), and their ability to move efficiently and
effectively (biomechanics). What we do repeatedly will be funneled into
three subcategories.

Bioenergetics
Bioenergetics is how someone procures energy and then uses that energy; this
is called an energy system. The three primary energy systems are
phosphagen, glycolytic, and oxidative (figure 3.3). The energy systems are
further broken down into two categories, termed power (maximal exertion)
and capacity (maximal duration or volume). To further delineate how to best
leverage these three energy systems, each energy system can be classified as

图 3.2 一般到具体。
想象一下这样一种动态，参与运动员表现的所有各方都理解特异性，
正如 Mang (2022) 所描述的那样：“运动的生理适应反映了运动训练计
划期间施加的特定刺激。”选择在一年中的特定时期或根据运动员的发
展情况选择更合适的运动并不是一件坏事。 开发不相关的变量是一种
无效的培训方法。 它可能表现为与运动员的需求或他们在比赛中的要
求不直接相关的改进。

我们选择的培训方向应该经过深思熟虑，并集中在统一的方法上。
一个称为 dynamic correspondence (Brearley & Bishop, 2019) 的概念，它
是从一般品质到特定品质的感知效果。 它是根据培训决策创建的同心
圆。 Dynamic correspondence 指的是一般训练输入与更具体训练输入的
互连性。
Verkhoshansky（2011）将一般训练输入分为三个不同的类别：生物
能量系统、生物运动系统和生物力学系统。 事实上，这些类别是相互
关联的并且互相促进的。我们可以利用这三个独立但相互关联的实体来
影响性能。 影响某人有效地创造和使用能量的能力（生物能量学），
他们可以创造的力量的速度、长度或大小（生物运动能力），以及他们
高效和有效地移动的能力（生物力学）。 我们反复做的事情将分为三
个子类别。

生物能量学
生物能量学是指人们如何获取能量然后使用该能量；这称为
energy system。 三个主要能量系统是磷酸原、糖酵解和氧化（图 3.3）
。 能量系统进一步分为两类，称为power（最大努力）和capacity（最
大持续时间或体积）。为了进一步描述如何最好地利用这三个能源系统
，每个能源系统可以分为：

either power or capacity:
Phosphagen power or phosphagen capacity: 0 to 10 sec
Glycolytic power or glycolytic capacity: 30 to 60 sec
Oxidative power or oxidative capacity: 30 to 180 sec

Phosphagen System
The first occurring energy system is the phosphagen system that uses
primarily ATP and phosphocreatine (PCr). This is the briefest of the energy
systems but has the highest potential to create force or velocity. The
phosphagen system uses the ATP-PCr cycle to create energy and runs for
under 10 s. The more readily available energy is the central reason behind the
phosphagen system’s force or velocity output being what it is. The same
reason it has the highest force and velocity output also makes it the fastest
expended energy system. For most team-based sports, the phosphagen system
is the determinant of success.
The biggest overreaction with bioenergetics: train
slow—be slow.
The truth is, the pendulum has swung away from the original intent of
S&C, which is to assist with sports performance. The fight against long, slow
distance in athletic development was a huge fight for the performance coach.
Athletes would often use long-distance running for training to such a degree
that it ran contrary to improving force or velocity. The result of this was a
huge overreaction to avoid anything that would be considered extended
cardiorespiratory work.

power 或 capacity：
Phosphagen power or phosphagen capacity:0 至 10 秒
Glycolytic power or glycolytic capacity: 30 至 60 秒
Oxidative power or oxidative capacity: 30 至 180 秒

磷酸原系统
第一个出现的能量系统是主要使用 ATP 和磷酸肌酸 (PCr) 的磷酸原系统
。 这是最简单的能量系统，但具有最大的产生力或速度的潜力。 磷酸
原系统利用 ATP-PCr 循环产生能量，运行时间不到 10 秒。更容易获得
的能量是磷酸原系统的力或速度输出背后的核心原因。 同样的原因，
它具有最高的力和速度输出，也使其成为消耗最快的能量系统。对于大
多数团队运动来说，磷酸原系统是成功的决定因素。

对生物能量学最大的过度反应是：缓慢训练——慢慢来
。
事实上，钟摆已经偏离了S&C协助运动表现的初衷。对于运动表现教
练来说，与长距离、慢距离的运动发展作斗争是一场巨大的斗争。运动
员经常使用长跑进行训练，以至于与提高力量或速度背道而驰。 其结
果是一种巨大的过度反应，以避免任何被认为是长时间的心肺工作的事
情。

FIGURE 3.3 Bioenergetic system.
Avoiding extended cardiorespiratory work is a challenging concept to
explore because it runs contrary to what team sports’ perceived needs are.
The concept of specificity is that if we do something repeatedly, we will be
better at it. However, the concept of dynamic correspondence makes the need
for only phosphagen power not directly true. Team sports need to specifically
develop phosphagen power more toward the power capacity end of the
spectrum. Complete abandonment of any extended cardiorespiratory or
slower, longer activities leads to limiting the capacity of any energy system.
We restrict potential by training phosphagen work volume or density intraand intertraining. If we cannot recover between reps, we have to lower the
volume of work. We recover aerobically with anaerobic work.
Bennett (2006) discusses this with a review of sport-specific conditioning
for football. The overwhelming majority of S&C coaches focus on agility or
change of direction work for their football-specific conditioning. The key is
to repeat agility drills for multiple reps within a period, replicating gamelike
situations. The capacity of the phosphagen system is what determines

图 3.3 生物能系统。
避免长时间的心肺工作是一个具有挑战性的概念，因为它与团队运动
的感知需求背道而驰。特异性的概念是，如果我们重复做某件事，我们
就会做得更好。然而，动态对应的概念使得仅需要磷酸原功率的需求并
不直接成立。团队运动需要专门开发磷酸原的力量，使其更接近功率谱
的末端。 完全放弃任何扩展的心肺活动或更慢、更长的活动会导致任
何能量系统的能力受到限制。我们通过训练内和训练间的磷酸原工作量
或密度来限制潜力。 如果我们无法在重复次数之间恢复，我们就必须
减少工作量。我们通过无氧运动进行有氧恢复。

Bennett (2006) 通过回顾足球运动的具体训练来讨论这个问题。绝大
多数 S&C 教练都专注于针对足球特定训练的敏捷性或方向改变工作。
关键是在一段时间内重复进行多次敏捷训练，复制类似游戏的情况。
磷酸原系统的容量决定了

transfer, not the power. The ability to repeat is the difference.

Glycolytic System
The next energy system is the glycolytic energy system, which primarily uses
glucose and glycogen (stored glucose). The primary mechanism to procure
energy comes from glycolysis. The sports that use the glycolytic energy
system are hockey and 400 m sprinters. Which gives you a picture of the
timeline: 30 to 60 s. The other part of this is that the glycolytic system is the
most visceral or noticeable. Going through a bout of maximal anaerobic work
for 30 to 60 s will elicit a higher rating of perceived exertion (see chapter 4
for more details).
One byproduct of glycolysis is the excess production of hydrogen. This
hydrogen saturation of the cell results from the inability of pyruvate, one of
the end products of glycolysis, to enter the mitochondria as rapidly as the
energy needed can support. The result is that lactate dehydrogenase reduces
pyruvate to lactate using NADH. This is a reaction to a change in pH in the
cytosol that the cell needs to expel excess hydrogen ions. The change in
cellular pH, along with excess phosphates from the phosphagen system
circulating, creates this systemic outcome of fatigue.
The biggest misconception with bioenergetics is
that excess fatigue is the only means of
improving.
The fatigue driven by the change in pH becomes a validator of training
effectiveness. One key feature of specificity is that we get better at what we
repeatedly do. What we do repeatedly can be diminished by what we cannot
recover from. Stress and fatigue are a means to an end. Stress and fatigue are
not the end. The problem with specificity and the glycolytic system is the
perception of value based on being constantly tired. Residual fatigue is a
specific outcome of developing the glycolytic system and can lead to
diminished performance if it is overprioritized.
Not that glycolytic training does not have value in certain situations. It is

转移，而不是权力。重复的能力就是区别。

糖酵解系统
下一个能量系统是糖酵解能量系统，它主要使用葡萄糖和糖原（储存的
葡萄糖）。 获取能量的主要机制来自糖酵解。 使用糖酵解能量系统的
运动有曲棍球和 400 m 短跑运动员。 这为您提供了时间线的图片：30
到 60 秒。另一方面是糖酵解系统是最内在的或最引人注目的。进行 30
至 60 秒的最大无氧运动将获得更高的感知用力等级（更多详细信息，
请参阅第 4 章）。
糖酵解的副产品之一是过量产生氢气。 细胞的氢饱和是由于丙酮酸
（糖酵解的最终产物之一）无法以所需能量支持的速度快速进入线粒体
所致。 结果是乳酸脱氢酶利用 NADH 将丙酮酸还原为乳酸。 这是对
细胞质中 pH 值变化的反应，细胞需要排出多余的氢离子。 细胞 pH 值
的变化，以及磷酸原系统循环中过量的磷酸盐，造成了这种全身性的疲
劳结果。

对生物能量学最大的误解是过度疲劳是改善的唯一方法
。

pH 值变化引起的疲劳成为训练效果的验证因素。 专一性的一个关键
特征是我们能够在重复做的事情上做得更好。我们反复做的事情可能会
因为我们无法恢复的事情而被削弱。压力和疲劳是达到目的的手段。压
力和疲劳并不是终点。 特异性和糖酵解系统的问题是基于持续疲劳的
价值感知。 残余疲劳是糖酵解系统发育的一个特定结果，如果过度重
视它，可能会导致性能下降。
并不是说糖酵解训练在某些情况下没有价值。 这是

specific to certain energy systems used by certain sports. However, the
primary problem becomes being too tempted to only use that energy system
because it will result in acute exhaustion. The issue with excess glycolytic
work is that it requires a longer recovery time and disrupts a microcycle. It
also diminishes the levels of both phosphagen and oxidative systems
(Francis, 2013). It becomes a matter of whether there are better things we can
do redundantly.

Oxidative System
The final system to dive into in bioenergetics is the oxidative system. The
oxidative system works in the presence of oxygen, which derives its fuel
primarily from fat and protein. This system is primarily in effect after 60 s, or
after the phosphagen and glycolytic systems. The primary effect that the
oxidative system provides is to increase the capacity of both the phosphagen
and glycolytic systems.
Regardless of where we derive energy from or how long a bout lasts, we
recover oxidatively. Depleting immediate energy reserves for the phosphagen
or glycolytic system is the rate-limiting factor of the capacity of these
systems. We need ATP following a short, violent burst of activity, and we
need glucose following intense but longer bursts of activity. This happens
oxidatively, which allows for the capacity of these systems. The faster we
replenish substrates related to their energy system, the greater the capacity of
the system.
Fast responders are usually oriented more toward fast-twitch muscle fiber,
which would lead to increased ability within the phosphagen system. As we
discuss what we do with fast-twitch athletes, we need to appreciate that, by
nature, they will respond faster to something they already have a
physiological adaptation to. With these athletes, accounting for more rest
intraworkout, intramicrocycle, and intramesocycle is critical. Less volume or
time under tension per set, more rest between high-intensity training sessions,
and more rapid rates of change with programs are all strategies we need to
use with fast responders. But this comes at a cost of less density within those
periods.
Faster-twitch athletes will benefit greatly from increased capacity to

特定于某些运动使用的某些能量系统。 然而，主要的问题是太想只使
用该能量系统，因为这会导致严重的疲惫。 糖酵解工作过多的问题是
它需要更长的恢复时间并扰乱微循环。 它还降低磷酸原和氧化系统的
水平（Francis，2013）。问题在于我们是否可以多余地做更好的事情。

氧化系统
生物能学中最后一个要深入研究的系统是氧化系统。 氧化系统在氧气
存在的情况下工作，氧气的燃料主要来自脂肪和蛋白质。该系统主要在
60 秒后或在磷酸原和糖酵解系统之后起作用。 氧化系统提供的主要作
用是增加磷酸原和糖酵解系统的能力。
无论我们从哪里获取能量或比赛持续多长时间，我们都会通过氧化恢
复。耗尽磷酸原或糖酵解系统的直接能量储备是这些系统容量的速率限
制因素。 在短暂、剧烈的活动爆发后，我们需要 ATP，而在剧烈但较
长的活动爆发后，我们需要葡萄糖。 这是通过氧化发生的，从而发挥
了这些系统的能力。 我们补充与其能量系统相关的底物的速度越快，
系统的容量就越大。
快速反应者通常更倾向于快肌纤维，这将导致磷酸原系统内的能力增
强。 当我们讨论如何对待快肌运动员时，我们需要认识到，从本质上
讲，他们会对他们已经有生理适应的事物做出更快的反应。 对于这些
运动员来说，在训练中、微周期内和中周期内进行更多的休息至关重要
。减少每组的训练量或紧张时间，在高强度训练之间增加休息时间，以
及更快地改变计划，这些都是我们需要与快速反应者一起使用的策略。
但这是以这些时期密度降低为代价的。

快速肌动运动员将因能力的提高而受益匪浅

facilitate the increased density of a training session. The recovery
mechanisms from any anaerobic bout are limited by oxidative pathways.
Fast-twitch athletes, by definition, have fewer slow-twitch and oxidative
fibers, which limit the potential for recovery. Fatigue byproducts and their
removal rate limit subsequent sets anaerobically. Lowered mitochondria-rich
oxidative muscle fibers increase fatigue byproducts. We can expedite fatigue
byproduct removal if our oxidative pathways are developed, which in turn
can increase the density of anaerobic work in intratraining sessions.
Alternatively, slow responders are typically more slow-twitch muscle fiber
oriented, which leads to an increased ability to handle higher volumes and
durations due to having a greater distribution from the oxidative system. The
management of training sessions, microcycles, and mesocycles is less
difficult because they recover faster. Their development is typically slower
because they have fewer fast-twitch muscle fibers. This needs to be
accounted for by increasing intensity from microcycle to microcycle
consistently over a longer period. Essentially, this means we have to go
longer with our mesocycles with slow responders.
