Biomotor Abilities
Biomotor abilities can be broken down into three major funnels. With
specificity, we eventually focus on velocity, force, or work for any exercise
after developing the pattern (figure 3.4). Taking a developed movement
pattern toward some threshold of speed, load, or duration is the best means to
maximize transfer from that exercise. Reaching the threshold of one or all is

促进培训课程密度的增加。 任何无氧运动的恢复机制都受到氧化途径
的限制。根据定义，快肌运动员的慢肌纤维和氧化纤维较少，这限制了
恢复的潜力。 疲劳副产物及其去除率限制了后续的厌氧装置。富含线
粒体的氧化肌纤维减少会增加疲劳副产物。如果我们的氧化途径得到发
展，我们就可以加速消除疲劳副产品，这反过来又可以增加训练中无氧
运动的密度。
或者，慢反应者通常更倾向于慢肌纤维，这导致处理更大容量和持续
时间的能力增强，因为氧化系统的分布更大。训练课程、微循环和中循
环的管理不太困难，因为它们恢复得更快。 他们的发育通常较慢，因
为他们的快肌纤维较少。 这需要通过在较长时期内持续增加微循环到
微循环的强度来解释。 从本质上讲，这意味着我们必须在反应缓慢的
情况下延长中周期。

磷酸原系统——大多数团队运动； 发展能力胜过权力
糖酵解系统——仅限于磷酸原和氧化；战略性与使用性
氧化系统——发展所有系统的能力；促进康复

生物运动能力
生物运动能力可以分为三个主要漏斗。 在制定模式后，我们最终会具
体关注任何练习的速度、力量或功（图 3.4）。 将已开发的运动模式朝
着速度、负荷或持续时间的某个阈值发展，是最大化该运动转移的最佳
方法。达到其中一项或全部的阈值

relative to the specificity of the primary sport.
With dynamic correspondence, the threshold comes into play most
deliberately. Primarily, when we look at these variables in isolation, they do
not connect very directly. Doing an exercise for a long period, with a heavy
external load or at a higher speed, is not a one-to-one connection to
performance in a sport. In a general sense, we need to demonstrate velocity,
force, and work with all athletes regardless of sport. A needs analysis based
on sport can easily become just a focus on all three. However, this strategy
might lead to diminished performance.
Applying specificity based on the athlete’s needs or the sport’s
requirements without considering the prerequisite ability is a mistake. A
needs analysis is based on a twofold approach: the end goal and baseline
ability. We need the relative context of what the sport’s functional needs are
from a biomotor perspective. However, the results could be amplified if we
understand where the athlete is deficient before the onset of training.
Understanding where we are starting from, as well as where we want to go, is
a foundational piece of training.

相对于主要运动的特殊性。
对于动态对应，阈值最有意地发挥作用。 首先，当我们孤立地看待
这些变量时，它们并没有非常直接的联系。 长时间、外部负荷较大或
速度较高的锻炼与运动表现并不是一一对应的。 一般来说，我们需要
展示速度、力量，并与所有运动员合作，无论从事什么运动。 基于运
动的需求分析很容易成为对这三个方面的关注。 然而，这种策略可能
会导致性能下降。
根据运动员的需求或运动的要求来应用特异性而不考虑先决能力是错
误的。 需求分析基于双重方法：最终目标和基线能力。我们需要从生
物运动的角度了解这项运动的功能需求的相对背景。 然而，如果我们
在训练开始前了解运动员的不足之处，结果可能会放大。了解我们从哪
里开始以及我们想要去哪里，是培训的基础部分。

FIGURE 3.4 Force, velocity, work.
Organically, we should see an inverse relationship with all three. Force
and velocity are inversely proportional, force and work are inversely
proportional, and velocity and work are inversely proportional. Without any
training influence, this occurs naturally. High force and velocity exertions can
only last for a brief period. High work can only be accomplished at a lowered
force and velocity. The primary aspect to understand is the ability to increase
the level relative to the baseline and end goal. Because specificity leads to
improvement, it just needs to be based on what is needed.

Force
Developing force comes down to moving an increasing mass, regardless of
time. Force is mass multiplied by acceleration (change in velocity divided by
change in time). Force is such a tempting attribute to train because it is the

图 3.4 力、速度、功。
从有机角度来看，我们应该看到这三者之间存在反比关系。 力和速
度成反比，力和功成反比，速度和功成反比。 在没有任何训练影响的
情况下，这是自然发生的。高力量和高速度的施加只能持续很短的一段
时间。高强度工作只能以较低的力和速度完成。要理解的主要方面是提
高相对于基线和最终目标的水平的能力。 因为具体才能改进，所以只
需要根据需要而定。

力量
发展力量归根结底就是移动不断增加的质量，无论时间如何。力是质量
乘以加速度（速度变化除以时间变化）。 力量是一种很容易训练的属
性，因为它是

most easily changed. With velocity, we cannot change the time or distance as
readily. If we rearrange the equations a little, we can potentially say that to
increase velocity, we have to increase the potential force we can create. This
is not relative to baseline information; it is a blanket statement that could lead
to less than net development.
The biggest overreaction: strength is always the
most important quality.

Velocity
Developing velocity ultimately comes down to increasing the rate of force
development. Since velocity is inversely proportional to force, this will mean
lowered mass. Velocity is a change in displacement divided by a change in
time. The farther we go in less time, the more velocity we will have. We can
focus on this by trying to go farther at a specific rate or a specific distance in
less time or go farther in less time. Gamble (2006) demonstrated that the rate
of force development is easily one of the most important factors someone can
focus on, and it is accentuated by increased external load.
The difficult part of increasing velocity is choosing what to focus on. We
can readily decrease the time if we can decrease the mass. Having to exert
less overall force (mass multiplied by acceleration) will decrease the effort to
move a certain distance and the potential for velocity, which is not the easiest
thing to do while moving our body weight. We have to establish that there is
a point of diminishing returns going so light, while at the same time not
getting preoccupied with only increasing force. Force is something to
appreciate, can be a misleading indicator, and is too often leveraged as a
means to improve both velocity and work.

Work
We can easily say the same for work relative to increasing force. Work is
force multiplied by displacement. We may not need or want to go farther or
create more displacement, but it does not diminish the value of work. If we

最容易改变。对于速度，我们无法轻易改变时间或距离。 如果我们稍
微重新排列一下方程，我们可以说，为了增加速度，我们必须增加我们
可以产生的潜在力。这与基线信息无关；这是一个笼统的声明，可能会
导致低于净发展。

最大的过度反应：实力永远是最重要的品质。

速度
发展速度最终归结为增加力量发展的速度。由于速度与力成反比，这意
味着质量降低。 速度是位移的变化除以时间的变化。我们在更短的时
间内走得越远，我们的速度就越快。我们可以通过尝试在更短的时间内
以特定的速度或特定的距离走得更远或在更短的时间内走得更远来专注
于这一点。 Gamble（2006）证明，力量发展的速度很容易成为人们可
以关注的最重要因素之一，并且随着外部负荷的增加而加剧。
提高速度的困难部分是选择关注点。如果我们可以减少质量，我们就
可以轻松地减少时间。 必须施加较小的总力（质量乘以加速度）会减
少移动一定距离的努力和速度的潜力，这在移动我们的体重时并不是最
容易做的事情。我们必须确定，存在一个收益递减点，但同时不要只专
注于增加力量。 力量是值得欣赏的东西，可能是一个误导性的指标，
并且经常被用作提高速度和工作的手段。

工作
对于与增加力量相关的功，我们可以很容易地得出同样的结论。 功是
力乘以位移。 我们可能不需要或不想走得更远或造成更多的流离失所
，但这并不会降低工作的价值。 如果我们

increase the force, we can readily increase the amount of work done, which
gives a natural bias toward just increasing an athlete’s force without
considering the actual need for it in the first place.
With all biomotor variables, it is so important to understand an athlete’s
starting point relative to the goal. As we start to develop a focus on increasing
force, velocity, or work, it is important to understand the best use of time
toward a goal. If the athlete is underdeveloped in creating force, there will be
value in increasing strength relative to improving speed or capacity. Making
that assumption is a common misconception. We often assume that strength
is the lacking quality, but that is only an assumption. If the needs of the
athlete only require a certain amount of force to be produced, then strength
may be adequate. This is the same for any biomotor focus with no relative
context to the baseline.
However, there could easily be a developed athlete who is spending an
unnecessary amount of time on increasing strength. The athlete who is strong
and needs to improve speed or capacity could make increasing force
counterproductive. Body mass can potentially increase when we improve the
force. A large part of strength improvement comes from neurological
improvement, but the rest comes from increasing cross-sectional area. If the
goal is to go longer or faster and the athlete is solely focused on force, they
could derail their progress by increasing their body mass.
In most cases, increasing body mass is not a bad thing; it is celebrated
within team sports. The problem is that it is true until it’s not. Unnecessary
body mass is counterproductive to athletes who need to go for longer
durations or, as we discussed, go at higher velocities. It is counterproductive
unless we know that increased body mass is a good thing. There are countless
examples of increased body mass being a good thing, but that does not make
it universally good for everyone.
Missing the mark on one of these variables is commonly the case when we
associate bias with decisions. A common model used in decision-making is
Occam’s razor: The most obvious solution is the best solution. If the athlete
needs to improve speed, the most logical thing would be to focus on highervelocity activities. In turn, we inject our logic, which is influenced by our
preferences or biases. Instead of focusing on speed, we increase body mass or

增加力量，我们可以很容易地增加完成的工作量，这自然地倾向于只增
加运动员的力量，而不首先考虑其实际需要。
对于所有生物运动变量，了解运动员相对于目标的起点非常重要。当
我们开始关注增加力量、速度或工作时，了解如何最好地利用时间来实
现目标非常重要。如果运动员在创造力量方面不够发达，那么相对于提
高速度或能力而言，增加力量将更有价值。做出这种假设是一种常见的
误解。 我们常常认为力量是缺乏的品质，但这只是一个假设。 如果运
动员的需要只需要产生一定量的力量，那么力量可能就足够了。 这对
于任何与基线没有相关背景的生物运动焦点都是一样的。

然而，很容易有一个发达的运动员花费不必要的时间来增加力量。身
体强壮且需要提高速度或能力的运动员可能会使增加力量适得其反。当
我们提高力量时，体重可能会增加。 力量的提高很大一部分来自于神
经系统的改善，但其余的则来自于横截面积的增加。 如果目标是走得
更远或更快，而运动员只专注于力量，那么他们可能会因增加体重而偏
离进度。
在大多数情况下，增加体重并不是一件坏事。 它在团队运动中得到
庆祝。 问题是，在事实并非如此之前，它都是真实的。 不必要的体重
对于需要更长持续时间或如我们所讨论的更高速度的运动员来说会适得
其反。除非我们知道体重增加是一件好事，否则它会适得其反。有无数
的例子表明体重增加是一件好事，但这并不意味着它对每个人都有好处
。
当我们将偏见与决策联系起来时，通常会出现漏掉其中一个变量的情
况。 决策中常用的模型是奥卡姆剃刀：最明显的解决方案就是最佳解
决方案。 如果运动员需要提高速度，最合乎逻辑的做法就是专注于更
高速度的活动。 反过来，我们注入了我们的逻辑，这受到我们的偏好
或偏见的影响。我们不关注速度，而是增加体重或

strength, which can be counterproductive. We will be good at what we
repeatedly do—so we better be doing the right thing.
The fast responder will respond more rapidly to any of these variables
when assigned. Velocity and force are more neurological in development, so
a faster responder will simply adapt faster. The slow responder will take more
time to develop due to a variety of reasons stemming from lower amounts of
fast-twitch muscle fibers. Slow-twitch muscle fibers have a less adept
nervous system and take longer to develop force or velocity. However, work
is typically faster developing, and there is a faster decline in both fast and
slow responders. What this means for training is that we need to allocate as
much time as possible to developing force and velocity while appreciating
that we can develop work quickly.
The biggest misconception: work (capacity) does
not matter.
This is a huge problem because it undermines the idea that fitness is
irrelevant if we simply increase strength. Since we recover oxidatively, we
need high capacity to push to larger thresholds anaerobically. This is an effect
a training paradox: we need capacity to force and velocity, but we do not
have enough time to develop capacity. It undermines the idea that fitness is
less important to increase strength. In fact, it is a critical factor to increasing
strength. As discussed with bioenergetics, the capacity of an energy system is
a greater determinant than the power of that system. Work is the ability to go
longer or farther. Devaluing work leaves athletes in a vulnerable position
when they have to execute repeat intervals relative to those during
competition.

快速响应者在分配时将对这些变量中的任何一个做出更快的响应。速
度和力量在发育过程中更具神经性，因此反应速度更快的人会适应得更
快。由于快肌纤维数量较少等多种原因，慢反应者需要更多时间才能发
育。 慢肌纤维的神经系统不太熟练，需要更长的时间才能产生力量或
速度。然而，工作通常发展得更快，而快速响应者和慢速响应者的下降
速度也更快。 这对于训练来说意味着我们需要分配尽可能多的时间来
发展力量和速度，同时意识到我们可以快速开展工作。

最大的误解：工作（能力）并不重要。

这是一个大问题，因为它破坏了“如果我们只是增加力量，健身就无
关紧要”的观念。 由于我们通过氧化进行恢复，因此我们需要高能力
以无氧方式达到更高的阈值。这是一个训练悖论的结果：我们需要力量
和速度的能力，但我们没有足够的时间来发展能力。 它破坏了“健身
对于增加力量来说不太重要”的观点。事实上，它是增强实力的关键因
素。正如生物能量学所讨论的，能量系统的容量比该系统的功率更具有
决定性。工作是走得更远或更远的能力。 当运动员必须执行相对于比
赛期间的重复间隔时，贬低工作的价值会使运动员处于弱势地位。

The Simplest Solution is the Most Correct
As we set up a training program, we need to narrow our focus
and see our target more clearly. At some level, all performance
goals boil down to adjusting the time spent improving force,
velocity, and capacity. It may seem overly simplistic to say we
need to focus our attention and emphasize moving something
heavy, moving something quickly, or moving something for
longer durations. We work with complex open systems; the more
we do, the more we will need to simplify things. There are far too
many variables to consider with all athletes to presume it is as
simple as only getting stronger, faster, or better conditioned. As
coaches we want to distill down our solutions to easily
understood objectives, while at the same time remembering that
nothing is ever simple.
Simply looking at basic equations can help to establish a lot
about what we need to do with our athletes and clients:
Force = Mass × Acceleration
Work = Force × Displacement
Power = Work ÷ Change in Time
We can narrow down any goal into being tied to some degree
of wanting to become stronger (force), move faster (velocity), or
go longer (work). These equations connect to training focuses as
strength–force, power–velocity, and capacity–work. The ability to

最简单的解决方案是最正确的
当我们制定培训计划时，我们需要缩小重点，更清楚地看到我们
的目标。 在某种程度上，所有的表现目标都归结为调整提高力量
、速度和能力所花费的时间。 说我们需要集中注意力并强调移动
重物、快速移动某物或长时间移动某物似乎过于简单化。我们使
用复杂的开放系统；我们做得越多，就越需要简化事情。所有运
动员都需要考虑太多的变量，不能认为这只是变得更强、更快或
更好的状态那么简单。 作为教练，我们希望将我们的解决方案提
炼为易于理解的目标，同时记住没有什么是简单的。

简单地查看基本方程可以帮助我们确定我们需要与运动员和客
户做什么：
Force = Mass × Acceleration
Work = Force × Displacement
Power = Work ÷ Change in Time
我们可以将任何目标缩小范围，将其与某种程度的想要变得更
强（力量）、移动得更快（速度）或走得更远（工作）联系起来
。这些方程与力量-力量、功率-速度和能力-功等训练重点相关。
有能力

leverage these equations within training toward any desired
outcome makes all the difference in reaching an outcome in any
timeline. The big question is, which of these variables holds the
most weight? The answer is whichever variable makes the most
changes toward the desired outcome.
The target is moving; we need to zero in on the variables that
matter most to slow the target down so we can hit it effectively
every time. Knowing the target we are shooting at before we
shoot is logical. Instead, we often go in the opposite direction
and choose what we are going to do with someone before we
know what we want to accomplish. Establishing a system that
allows us to interpret the most direct path to reach a goal through
the proper selection of how we prescribe training stimulus should
be the standard. We can focus our efforts on what is familiar, but
that may not be what the person we are training needs. We can
associate increased force as all-encompassing, but it may be
just accentuating an already developed area. If someone wants
to lose weight, they need to do more work, which could simply be
accomplished by increasing displacement. If someone wants to
run faster, they may need to move at a higher velocity. If
someone wants to increase strength, they need to use heavier
weights during training.
Occam’s razor states that the simplest explanation is more
often the correct explanation. Focus on what is necessary over
what is convenient or preferred.

Biomechanics
The final piece of specificity is biomechanics. This is an important quality to
understand because it considers both exercise selection and how we perform
the exercise, or execute it. The way we do it matters as much as, if not more
than, how much, how fast, or how long we do it.
Biomechanics considers the structure, function, and motion of the
mechanical aspects of biological systems. Key aspects behind biomechanics

在训练中利用这些方程来实现任何期望的结果，对于在任何时间
线内达到结果都有很大的不同。 最大的问题是，这些变量中哪个
最重要？答案是哪个变量对期望结果的改变最大。
目标在移动；我们需要将最重要的变量归零以减慢目标速度，
这样我们每次都能有效地实现目标。 在射击之前知道我们要射击
的目标是合乎逻辑的。 相反，我们经常走相反的方向，在知道我
们想要完成什么之前就选择我们要与某人一起做什么。 标准应该
是建立一个系统，让我们能够通过正确选择如何制定训练刺激来
解释实现目标的最直接路径。我们可以将精力集中在熟悉的事情

的事情，而不是方便或偏好的事情。

生物力学
最后一个特殊性是生物力学。这是一个需要理解的重要品质，因为它考
虑了练习选择以及我们如何进行练习或执行它。我们做事的方式与我们
做事的数量、速度或时间一样重要，甚至更重要。
生物力学考虑生物系统机械方面的结构、功能和运动。 生物力学背
后的关键方面

are the relationship between the skeletal system, the muscular system, and the
associated connective tissue (fascia, tendons, ligaments). Mechanically, the
skeletal system is moved by the muscular system, and the connective tissue
supports, transmits, and facilitates movement.
Simplistically, we can say that the body is a series of levers and pulleys
that create locomotion. The problem with this rationale is that it only
considers two dimensions, which makes the idea of levers only partly true in
terms of biomechanics. It is nice to say that, acting as a lever, the muscle
shortens (concentrically), pulls on the connective tissue, and then moves an
attached bone. This is the approach of traditional anatomy and physiology—
reduce the body down to its most stripped parts and understand what is
happening. But this is incomplete because the human body does not live on a
two-dimensional sheet of paper. The human body lives in a three-dimensional
world.
With functional anatomy, we have to shift our line of thinking to the body
living and moving in a three-dimensional space. On top of that, there is a
universal law that everything is moving toward chaos, or entropy. What we
see on a sheet of paper is not true because the version we are seeing is only
within two dimensions of its perfect state. The two-dimensional
representation does not translate because it has a predictable outcome of
flexion and extension, abduction and adduction, and internal and external
rotation. The pure or perfect function of a joint does not translate as linearly
as we want. Three-dimensional views have to look at more variables
simultaneously.
A fundamental aspect of understanding biomechanics is that movement
needs to be challenged in all planes of motion and vectors, moved through a
full range of motion (ROM), and focused on all contraction types. Team
sports are played in chaotic environments. There is an infinite number of
movements and sequences of movements that will occur during competition.
Exercises need to be diverse in their selection and in how we load them to
prepare the athlete to meet the demands of an unpredictable environment.
Taking a traditional approach based on traditional anatomy and
physiology’s two-dimensional view of movement limits transfer to sport. The
same reductionism is applied to exercise selection, prematurely thrusting

是骨骼系统、肌肉系统和相关结缔组织（筋膜、肌腱、韧带）之间的关
系。 从机械角度来说，骨骼系统由肌肉系统移动，而结缔组织则支持
、传递并促进运动。
简单地说，我们可以说身体是一系列产生运动的杠杆和滑轮。 这个
原理的问题在于它只考虑两个维度，这使得杠杆的想法在生物力学方面
仅部分正确。 可以说，作为杠杆，肌肉缩短（同心），拉动结缔组织
，然后移动附着的骨头。这是传统解剖学和生理学的方法——将身体缩
小到最精简的部分，并了解正在发生的事情。但这是不完整的，因为人
体并不是生活在一张二维纸上。人体生活在三维世界中。

通过功能解剖学，我们必须将思路转移到在三维空间中生活和运动的
身体。 最重要的是，有一个普遍规律：一切都在走向混乱，或者说熵
。 我们在一张纸上看到的并不真实，因为我们看到的版本仅在其完美
状态的二维范围内。 二维表示不会平移，因为它具有可预测的屈曲和
伸展、外展和内收以及内部和外部旋转的结果。关节的纯粹或完美功能
并不像我们想要的那样线性转换。 三维视图必须同时观察更多变量。

理解生物力学的一个基本方面是，运动需要在所有运动平面和矢量上
受到挑战，通过全方位的运动 (ROM) 进行移动，并关注所有收缩类型
。 团队运动是在混乱的环境中进行的。 比赛期间会出现无数的动作和
动作序列。练习的选择和负荷方式需要多样化，以使运动员做好准备，
满足不可预测的环境的要求。
采用基于传统解剖学和生理学的二维运动视图的传统方法限制了向运
动的转移。同样的还原论也适用于运动选择，过早地推进

athletes into singular exercises and overvaluing variables of force, velocity,
or work. These variables are important, but not if they diminish the ability to
train in multiple planes through a full ROM and all three contraction types. A
limited approach could net us less from exercises for our athletes. Twodimensional approaches combined with a myopic focus on specific biomotor
abilities lack the prerequisite depth to best prepare athletes.

Cardinal Planes of Motion
We have three planes of motion: sagittal, frontal, and transverse. The
orientation of movement is traditionally based on the direction of movement.
This can become more nuanced as we look at multijoint exercises that include
joints that articulate in multiple directions. Cardinal planes (figure 3.5) are
the lock and key for understanding the difference between two-dimensional
and text-based anatomy and three-dimensional and functional anatomy.
Understanding how we accommodate all three planes in training directly or
indirectly ensures that we are best prepared for an unpredictable environment.
In reality, movements do not fit conveniently within a single classification.
For instance, we can classify a forward lunge as sagittal plane movement, but
what if the athlete is holding a single dumbbell in a fixed position? Is it a
frontal plane movement because the load is offset? What if we exchange the
dumbbell for a medicine ball, and we rotate over the front leg? Is that now a
transverse movement? The exercise has a direct classification compared to
the indirect movement, which can help with exercise prescription a great
deal. Our traditional loaded movement patterns can move or resist movement
in all three planes of motion at any given time.

运动员进行单一的练习并高估力量、速度或功的变量。这些变量很重要
，但如果它们削弱了通过完整的 ROM 和所有三种收缩类型在多个平面
上进行训练的能力，那么它们就不再重要了。有限的方法可能会减少我
们运动员的锻炼量。 二维方法与对特定生物运动能力的短视关注相结
合，缺乏为运动员做好最佳准备的先决深度。

运动的基本平面
我们有三个运动平面：矢状面、额状面和横向面。 运动方向传统上基
于运动方向。当我们研究包括多个方向关节的多关节练习时，这一点可
能会变得更加微妙。 基面（图 3.5）是理解二维和基于文本的解剖学与
三维和功能解剖学之间差异的锁和钥匙。了解我们如何直接或间接地在
训练中适应所有三架飞机，可以确保我们为不可预测的环境做好最好的
准备。
事实上，运动并不能方便地归入单一分类。例如，我们可以将前弓步
归类为矢状面运动，但如果运动员在固定位置握住单个哑铃怎么办？
是因为负载偏移而导致额面运动吗？如果我们把哑铃换成药球，然后在
前腿上旋转会怎么样？现在是横向运动吗？ 与间接运动相比，该运动
具有直接分类，这对运动处方有很大帮助。我们传统的负载运动模式可
以在任何给定时间在所有三个运动平面上移动或抵抗运动。

At the same time, the reality is that these semantics make it difficult to
assess if we are getting enough focus in all three planes of motion. There are
some consistently trainable movement patterns: squat, lunge, hinge, kneedominant posterior chain, horizontal and vertical upper body push, and
horizontal and vertical upper body pull. Trainable means that we can most
readily progress and progressively overload. The problem is that these
movements are mostly oriented and loaded with the sagittal plane. We need
to appreciate that these sagittal-oriented movements are best transferred by
having a more three-dimensional approach. Understanding what is most
trainable and what is most transferable is the means of incorporating
functional movement within a team setting.
The biggest overreaction: a movement that is
more easily quantified is more valuable than
movements that are not as quantifiable.

与此同时，现实情况是，这些语义使得我们很难评估我们是否在所有
三个运动平面上获得了足够的关注。有一些可持续训练的运动模式：深
蹲、弓步、铰链、膝主导的后链、水平和垂直上身推、以及水平和垂直
上身拉。 可训练意味着我们最容易进步并逐渐超负荷。 问题是这些运
动大多是在矢状面定向和加载的。 我们需要认识到，这些矢状方向的
运动最好通过更加三维的方法来转移。 了解什么是最可训练的以及什
么是最可转移的是将功能性运动融入团队环境中的方法。

最大的过度反应是：更容易量化的运动比不可量化的运
动更有价值。

A simple inspection of muscle fiber orientation, whether parallel or
pennate, reveals that fascial lines and connective tissue mostly run obliquely.
The obvious function of the body is that it is designed to move in all three
planes of motion, or three dimensions. The issue is that loading or pushing to
a biomotor outcome is hard to quantify in the frontal and transverse planes.
Structural balance is a rule that we will leverage with exercise selection.
Simply balancing pushing and pulling exercises creates a structurally stable
joint that is more resilient than a structurally imbalanced joint. This same
logic applies to stressing the joint in all three planes of motion. For every
sagittal plane movement, we will need to load in the frontal and transverse
planes at least. Pulling equal to pushing combined with being strong and
capable in all dimensions is the basis for structural balance.
Attuning to lines of tension along all fascia and connective tissues will
maintain the spacing of the joints to function properly. In Anatomy Trains,
Thomas Meyers (2020) developed the concept of tensegrity, in relation to the
human body. Tensegrity is the interplay of fascia and the body, or the
interplay of tension and compression. Compression is the space maker, and
tension is the space retainer. This concept is called compressional
discontinuity: the maintenance of lines of tension and specific compression
that allows our body to move and function in all three planes of motion.
Biomechanics would not be complete without discussing force and length
(figure 3.6). Force is the amount of tension a muscle cell can create, and
length is how long that muscle cell is. The relationship between force and
length is not completely inverse, but it is weaker when a muscle is in a
shortened and lengthened position and stronger when it is at the midpoint of
ROM.
Force and length, in terms of specificity, are about increasing force at
increased lengths, which is best accomplished by training through as large a
ROM as possible. The function of a joint makes a significant difference in
degrees of freedom in various planes. The degrees of freedom with certain
movements are specific and important to train through full ROM. But first,
we need to understand the common joints’ primary functions.
Hinge Joint
Knees and elbows

对肌纤维方向的简单检查，无论是平行的还是羽状的，都会发现筋膜
线和结缔组织大多是倾斜的。身体的明显功能是它被设计为在所有三个
运动平面或三个维度上移动。问题是加载或推动生物运动结果很难在额
状面和横向面上量化。
Structural balance是我们在选择练习时将利用的规则。简单地平衡推
和拉练习可以创建结构稳定的关节，该关节比结构不平衡的关节更有弹
性。 同样的逻辑适用于在所有三个运动平面上对关节施加压力。 对于
每个矢状面运动，我们至少需要在额状面和横状面加载。 拉力等于推
力，再加上在各个方面都保持强大和能力，这是结构平衡的基础。
调整所有筋膜和结缔组织的张力线将保持关节的间距以正常运作。
在 Anatomy Trains 中，Thomas Meyers (2020) 提出了
tensegrity, in relation to the human body 的概念。 张拉整体是筋膜和身
体的相互作用，或者说张力和压力的相互作用。 压缩是空间制造者，
张力是空间保持者。 这个概念称为 compressional discontinuity：维持张
力线和特定压缩线，使我们的身体能够在所有三个运动平面上移动和发
挥作用。
如果不讨论力和长度，生物力学就不完整（图 3.6）。 力是肌肉细胞
可以产生的张力的大小，长度是肌肉细胞的长度。 力和长度之间的关
系并不完全相反，但当肌肉处于缩短和拉长位置时，力和长度之间的关
系较弱，而当肌肉处于 ROM 的中点时，力和长度之间的关系较强。
就特异性而言，力量和长度是指在增加长度的情况下增加力量，这最
好通过尽可能大的活动范围进行训练来实现。 关节的功能使不同平面
的自由度产生显着差异。 某些动作的自由度是特定的，对于通过完整
的 ROM 进行训练非常重要。 但首先，我们需要了解常见关节的主要功
能。

The development of strength through a larger degree of freedom is easily
one of the most valuable focal points for an athlete. Everything is moving to a
state of entropy, or chaos. The maintenance and possible development of
force through a larger degree of freedom decreases the rate of chaos. Range
of motion gives the potential to create a force that allows athletes to handle
variance in a chaotic world. Increasing force through a greater degree of
variance decreases the risk in that position.

Range of Motion
This biggest misconception: Force development’s
value is relative to the ROM it is demonstrated
within.
Much like planes of motion, we typically prioritize ROMs within which we
can exert more force. It is easier to add force to length than length to force.
The athlete who has developed high levels of strength at a reduced ROM will
have a harder time increasing length than the athlete with developed length
and added strength.
Specificity means that we will be better at what we repeatedly do. If we
prioritize strength regardless of ROM, we will be better at that smaller
window of ROM. When discussing every aspect of specificity between
bioenergetic, biomotor, and biomechanical systems, there can easily be a
myopic focus on the end. Prioritizing what the athlete is relative to and
developing them from their baseline toward the goal makes all the difference.
Without a doubt, if the athlete has a full degree of freedom of all joints
(flexibility) and control at that ROM (mobility), we can develop the athlete
more completely.

The final component of biomechanics is contraction types (figure 3.7). The
muscle cell goes through three phases of contraction: eccentric (lengthening),
concentric (shortening), and isometric (static). The three phases of

切都在走向熵或混乱的状态。 通过更大的自由度维持和可能发展力量
可以降低混乱率。 运动范围有可能产生一种力量，使运动员能够应对
混乱世界中的变化。 通过更大程度的变化来增加力量可以降低该位置

就像运动平面一样，我们通常会优先考虑可以施加更多力量的 ROM。
将力加到长度比将长度加到力更容易。在减少活动范围的情况下发展出
高强度力量的运动员将比发展长度和增加力量的运动员更难增加长度。
特异性意味着我们会在重复做的事情上做得更好。 如果我们优先考
虑力量而不考虑ROM，那么我们会在较小的ROM窗口中表现得更好。
当讨论生物能量、生物运动和生物力学系统之间特异性的各个方面时，

线向目标发展它们，这一切都会有所不同。毫无疑问，如果运动员的所
有关节都具有充分的自由度（灵活性）并在ROM（活动性）上进行控制
，我们就可以更全面地发展运动员。

收缩类型
生物力学的最后一个组成部分是收缩类型（图 3.7）。 肌肉细胞经历三
个收缩阶段：偏心（延长）、向心（缩短）和等长（静态）。 三个阶
段

contraction all occur in every movement, sometimes initiated eccentrically
and sometimes concentrically.
What you will find relatively quickly is that most movements are
governed by what the athlete can do concentrically. In terms of natural
strength, concentric is the weakest, which is why movements are governed by
concentric ability. On the other end of the spectrum, eccentric contraction is
the strongest, and isometric contraction is right in the middle. This creates a
prioritization of concentric strength because it is the rate-limiting step in all
exercises, which limits the stimulation of the eccentric and isometric strength
levels of the muscle cell.
Without any direct focus on eccentric or isometric strength, which can be
broken into yielding or overcoming, it becomes underdeveloped. We have a
naturally higher level of strength during these contraction types; therefore,
they become less of a priority to focus on. Depending on the sport or the
position within the sport, there may be a direct need to develop eccentric or
concentric ability. If there are only exercises that prioritize concentric ability,
we risk underdeveloping the needs of certain athletes.
Zatsiorsky and colleagues (2020) mentioned that the distribution of the
three contraction types should be 70% concentric, 20% eccentric, and 10%
isometric, which is a good jumping-off point for where to focus specificity of
contraction types (figure 3.8). Without knowing the goals or baseline levels,
we can easily adjust this distribution to have a more eccentric focus. An
eccentric focus would be 60% eccentric, 30% concentric, and 10% isometric.
Training should include all three planes of motion;
structural balance needs to include balance with
all planes of motion.

The result of specificity is that we are better at something than when we
started. The fundamental question is, what is that relative to? Developing
something should have some relevance to a desired outcome. At the same

be specific, and we must be accurate with that focal point.

Take Home
Specificity is about being conscious of the beginning and end points at all
times. The power to influence performance is based on how accurately we
select what inputs we repeatedly do. If the input is not based on the needs of
the sport, we will diminish performance. If the input is not based on baseline
performance, we will run the risk of not reaching the performance goal.
Choose the right inputs relevant to the goal and context from which the
athlete is starting.

ROM 在其中进行了演示。

带回家
特异性是指始终意识到起点和终点。 影响绩效的力量取决于我们选择
重复执行的输入的准确程度。如果投入不是基于运动的需要，我们就会
降低表现。如果输入不是基于基线绩效，我们将面临达不到绩效目标的
风险。选择与运动员开始的目标和背景相关的正确输入。

4
PROGRESSIVE OVERLOAD
Of all the principles, progressive overload is by far the most identifiable
aspect of a strength training program. If we were to zero in on any aspect of a
training program, it would be the progression of increased stress from one
microcycle to the next (figure 4.1). However, the most recognizable aspect of
a program is often the most taken-for-granted aspect of a training program.
Tracing the origins of progressive overload goes back to Greek mythology
and the fable of Milo lifting the baby calf until it became a full-grown bull,
supported from a physiological standpoint with general adaptation syndrome
created by Hans Selye. The premise is extremely simple: Apply some amount
of stress, let the body adapt, and progress until a goal is reached.

4
渐进式超负荷
在所有原则中，渐进式超负荷是力量训练计划中最明显的方面。如果我
们将训练计划的任何方面归零，那么压力就会从一个微周期到下一个微
周期逐渐增加（图 4.1）。然而，项目中最容易识别的方面往往是培训
项目中最被认为理所当然的方面。
追溯渐进性超负荷的起源可以追溯到希腊神话和米洛举起小牛直到它
变成一头成年公牛的寓言，从生理学的角度来看，汉斯·塞利创造了一般
适应综合症。前提非常简单：施加一定的压力，让身体适应并进步，直
到达到目标。

FIGURE 4.1 Adaptation.
Perhaps simplicity is what makes progressive overload so easy to
overlook. It becomes a matter of stating the obvious regarding the premise of
the program. Anthony Ditillo (1982), in his book Development of Physical
Strength, paints the clearest picture imaginable with single, double, and triple
progressions from week to week, highlighting the benefits of tracking
progressions weekly. Ditillo also said, “More work is not better than hard
work.”
This is where the fundamental problem with progressive overload
becomes apparent. Is it so bad if we work as hard as we can and do not see
any quantifiable improvement? The glorification of hard work without the
context of improvement is a missed opportunity to be strategic with stress.
Mentzer (2003) discusses that the central tenet of any training program is the
rate and amount at which one can progress from one training session to the
next. Progressive overload-based training is not without hard work, but hard
work can occur without progressive overload. The difference is critical for
performance.
Hard work is necessary to accomplish a greater amount from one week to
the next. However, if that hard work yields nothing, it was for nothing other
than to validate being tired. Progressive overload is a series of checks and
balances to justify the hard work. Mentzer (2003) suggests not working again
until you can improve in intensity, volume, or density. This could occur

图 4.1

适应。

也许简单性使得渐进式超载如此容易被忽视。这变成了陈述有关程序
前提的显而易见的问题。 Anthony Ditillo (1982) 在他的书
Development of Physical Strength 中，描绘了每周一次、两次和三次进展
的最清晰的画面，强调了每周跟踪进展的好处。 迪蒂洛还表示，“更
多的工作并不比努力工作更好。”
这就是渐进性超负荷的根本问题变得显而易见的地方。 如果我们尽
了最大的努力却看不到任何可量化的改进，这难道就很糟糕吗？ 在没
有改进的情况下赞美辛勤工作是错失应对压力的战略机会。 Mentzer (20
03) 讨论了任何培训计划的中心原则是一个人从一个培训课程进展到下
一个培训课程的速度和数量。 基于渐进式超负荷的训练并非没有艰苦
的训练，但艰苦的训练可以在没有渐进式超负荷的情况下进行。 这种
差异对于性能至关重要。
为了从一周到下一周完成更多的工作，必须付出艰苦的努力。然而，
如果努力没有任何成果，那也只是为了证明自己已经累了。 渐进式超
负荷是一系列的制衡，以证明努力工作的合理性。 Mentzer（2003）建
议，在强度、体积或密度得到改善之前，不要再进行训练。 这可能会
发生

anywhere from a few days to over a week before hitting the same body part
or movement pattern.
The three forms of progressive overload (figure 4.2) are the most
important variables we should use to determine a program’s success. The
entire pretense of periodization is that we can make progress from one
training session to the next, one microcycle to the next, and one mesocycle to
the next. If we cannot progress the entire periodization framework, it is, in a
sense, destined to fail.
Rates of improvement are based on the person’s training age, overall
stress, and residual fatigue. A person with a lower training age will be able to
make larger week-to-week changes and do that over a longer time frame.
This is inverted for someone with a higher training age, who will make
smaller week-to-week jumps over a shorter time frame. Stress through
training or in general will negatively affect the amount and rate of
progressive overload. Fatigue, being the natural byproduct of stress, increases
the period and amount we can progress from training session to training
session.

FIGURE 4.2 Forms of progressive overload.

在接触相同的身体部位或运动模式之前，可能需要几天到一周以上的时
间。
渐进式超载的三种形式（图 4.2）是我们应该用来确定程序成功的最
重要变量。 周期化的全部目的是，我们可以从一个训练课程到下一个
训练课程、从一个微周期到下一个训练周期、从一个中周期到下一个训
练周期取得进展。如果我们不能推进整个分期框架，从某种意义上说，
它注定会失败。
改善率取决于个人的训练年龄、整体压力和残余疲劳。训练年龄较低
的人将能够每周做出更大的改变，并在更长的时间内做到这一点。对于
训练年龄较高的人来说，情况正好相反，他们会在较短的时间内进行较
小的每周跳跃。 训练带来的压力或一般情况下的压力会对渐进性超负
荷的数量和速度产生负面影响。疲劳是压力的自然副产品，它会增加我
们每次训练的时间和次数。

图 4.2 渐进式超负荷的形式。

FIGURE 4.3 Kaizen-based progressive overload.
Poliquin (2013) discusses the concept of the Kaizen Method regarding
progressive overload (figure 4.3). The Kaizen Method is “constant and neverending improvement.” This approach promotes process over outcome. The
idea is to commit to sustainable and consistent progress as the goal. The
context is inverted from reaching an arbitrary goal to pushing to something
better over a set period. Poliquin references a potential 1% increase with
more experience, 3% for intermediate experience, and 5% for novices in
terms of training age.
This method is also relative to the length of the mesocycle (cluster of
microcycles) and how long we have to progressively overload. Shorter
mesocycles, which are the preferred length for more advanced lifters, will
require larger and faster rates of progressive overload. Alternatively, longer
mesocycles for more novice lifters will require smaller and slower rates of
progressive overload. The idea we can learn from Poliquin’s (2013) Kaizen
Method is that we are seeking constant improvement with a strategy that is
congruent with the length of the mesocycle, the athlete’s training age (figure
4.4), and even the athlete’s muscle fiber.
As we explore the forms of progressive overload, we need to view them as
a separate entity from key performance indicators. We want to drive toward

图 4.3 基于 Kaizen 的渐进式超载。
Poliquin (2013) 讨论了关于渐进性超负荷的 Kaizen 方法的概念（图 4.
3）。 Kaizen 方法是“持续、永无止境的改进”。 这种方法注重过程
而非结果。 这个想法是以致力于可持续和持续进步为目标。 背景从实
现任意目标转变为在设定的时间内推动更好的事情。 Poliquin 提到，就
训练年龄而言，随着经验的增加，可能会增加 1%，中级经验会增加 3%
，新手会增加 5%。
这种方法也与中循环（微循环簇）的长度以及我们必须逐渐超载的时
间有关。 较短的中周期是更高级举重运动员的首选长度，需要更大更
快的渐进超负荷率。 另外，对于更多的新手举重运动员来说，更长的
中周期将需要更小、更慢的渐进超负荷率。 我们可以从 Poliquin (2013)
的 Kaizen 方法中学到的想法是，我们正在通过与中周期长度、运动员
的训练年龄（图 4.4）甚至运动员的肌肉纤维相一致的策略来寻求持续
改进。
当我们探索渐进式超负荷的形式时，我们需要将它们视为独立于关键
绩效指标的实体。 我们想要驶向

things that transfer to performance, but we want to avoid being pulled faster
in the wrong direction. Judging a program by steady progress should not be a
paradigm shift; it should be the standard. The result should manifest in
overall performance improvement through increased key performance
indicators.

Intensity
Intensity is the means to progressively overload the quantity of effort.
External load is simply adding load to the bar. This is the most intuitive. With
advancements in technology, we can now use progressive overload intensity
with velocity. We can increase intensity by adjusting the speed at which we
lift.

FIGURE 4.4 Progressive overload based on training age.

External Load
The first form of progressive overload has to be external load. This is the
most common and simplest to understand, and therefore, easiest to
implement. The typical form is to increase the external load in terms of
external weight from one workout to the next. Athletes readily understand the
objective of increasing weight for a particular exercise week to week.
Understanding the form of progressive overload is critical for the novice

这些事情会转化为绩效，但我们希望避免被更快地拉向错误的方向。以
稳步进展来判断一个项目不应该是一种范式转变； 它应该是标准。 结
果应体现在通过增加关键绩效指标来提高整体绩效。

强度
强度是逐渐超负荷努力的方法。外部负载只是将负载添加到杆上。这是
最直观的。随着技术的进步，我们现在可以使用渐进的超载强度和速度
。 我们可以通过调整举重的速度来增加强度。

图 4.4 基于训练年龄的渐进超负荷。

外部负载
渐进式超负荷的第一种形式必须是外部负载。 这是最常见、最容易理
解的，因此也最容易实现。 典型的形式是从一次锻炼到下一次锻炼增
加外部重量（外部重量）。运动员很容易理解每周增加特定运动的体重
的目标。
了解渐进性超负荷的形式对于新手来说至关重要

athlete. The aspect of overload is so easily overshadowed by the prospect of
what others can do. The hierarchy structure we lean so heavily into with
record boards or leaderboards can easily manipulate someone to prioritize
what they haven’t attained over the process of getting somewhere. This is
such a vulnerable period where we are battling to create lasting effects on the
athlete.
The biggest overreaction—nervous system
adaptations permit making larger week-to-week
external load jumps.
When someone is exposed to a new stimulus, the adaptation is mostly
neural. This rapid change reflects the nervous system’s improved efficiency
in recruiting more motor units, synchronizing them, and increasing the action
potential firing rate (Sale, 1988). The ability to increase performance is
mostly due to the nervous system being more efficient. This can embolden a
coach to consistently make larger increases than we should.
Coaches need to be pragmatists with how we encourage progression from
one week to the next. Recall from Poliquin (2013) that we need to make a 1%
to 5% (novice 5%, advanced athletes 1%) increase from one week to the next.
The more experience that person gets, the smaller the increase we can make
week to week. We have to learn how to be strategic with progression. The
adaptation from a nervous system standpoint allows the novice to make a 5%
jump in external load. Advanced lifters have less direct change from the
nervous system. Less change is due to the movement pattern and nervous
system being more developed. This decreases the rate of intensity increase to
a 1% jump in external load.
The confidence gained in making a jump from one week to the next is
validating for the athlete. The feeling of making substantial progress can be
euphoric, and we want to encourage that. You, as the coach, need to see the
bigger picture and think about sustainable progress. Yes, we need to tell our
athletes to train hard. Channeling that energy into the execution of the
movement and set, rep, and tempo scheme, each training session is followed

FIGURE 4.5 Relative % rep max.
The concept of a rep max intensity chart gives a relative intensity with a
certain rep number (figure 4.5). Traditionally, this is viewed as a 100% rep
max (RM); for example, 1 RM would be 100% load (figure 4.6). This is used
to determine the intensity and relative intensity to work from. This way, we
can systematically organize progression based on the potential perceived
100% rep max after a mesocycle. A traditional cycle would take an approach
of progressing someone’s rep max 10% per week: 70%, 80%, 90%, and
100% relative intensity. We take our 100% rep max and multiply it by the
relative intensity of the week to determine the working max for that week.
For example, a 100 kg (220 lb) 1 RM at 70% relative intensity would be 70
kg (154 lb), 80% relative intensity would be 80 kg (176 lb), and 90% relative
intensity would be 90 kg (198 lb).

根据执行级别增加。

重复最大强度图的概念给出了特定重复次数的相对强度（图 4.5）。
传统上，这被视为 100% 最大重复次数 (RM)；例如，1 RM 表示 100%
负载（图 4.6）。这用于确定工作强度和相对强度。 这样，我们就可以
根据中周期后潜在感知的 100% 最大次数来系统地组织进展。传统的周
期会采取每周将某人的代表次数提高 10% 的方法：70%、80%、90% 和
100% 相对强度。 我们将 100% 最大重复次数乘以一周的相对强度，以
确定该周的最高工作量。例如，100 千克（220 磅）1 RM 在 70% 相对
强度下将为 70 千克（154 磅），在 80% 相对强度下将为 80 千克（176
磅），在 90% 相对强度下将为 90 千克（198 磅）。

FIGURE 4.6 Traditional cycle.
We can look at relative intensity as setting someone’s rep max to a
specific external load, as we did in the previous example, with reserve reps
(figure 4.7). In place of working off a lowered intensity, we view them as
reps in reserve. Lowered relative intensity would mean we have more reps in
reserve. For example, 70% relative intensity would have 12 reps in reserve,
80% relative intensity would have eight reps in reserve, and 90% relative
intensity would have four reps in reserve.
As we break down how to progress from week to week, creating a system
that works for you as the coach is most important. Have a clear plan of attack
to progress intensity from week to week. Relative intensity, reserve reps, or
simply making small intensity increases week to week are foundational to
tracking and accounting for continued improvement.
An aspect of the rep max chart (see figure 2.5 on page 29) that we need to
account for is that muscle fiber type will have an impact on reps at a given
intensity. Someone with a higher distribution of fast-twitch muscle fibers will
perform fewer reps relative to an athlete with a higher distribution of slowtwitch muscle fibers at the same intensity. This is the product of more
fatigue-resistant pathways, which equates to slower-twitch athletes being able

Within the team setting, some camps within the S&C community
vigorously support the rep max intensity-based approach. External load
through increasing intensity week to week is the only way to ensure value is
obtained from training, which can be an Achilles’ heel as well. A narrowed
focus on only intensity-based progressions can lead to diminished impact
from training. Intensity can easily be too little stimulus for the athlete. It can
lower the relative effect on training if we were to progress volume or density
instead.

using intensity based on the rep max chart with progressive overload. It is
impossible to predict how athletes who are complex open systems will adapt.
An approach from Verkhoshansky (2009) called cybernetic training bases the
external load on the athlete’s level of recovery from the previous workout.

The problem with this approach is that humans fluctuate with emotion and
motivation. One could argue that a drop in motivation would indicate an
overreached state, but it may not be an actual physiologically overreached
state. A subjective appraisal should have an impact on what cannot be done,
but not at the expense of an objective appraisal saying what can be done.
The biggest misconception with intensity-based
progressive overload—we cannot predict what an
athlete will do next week, so why prescribe
weight?
Mann and colleagues (2010) demonstrated that a more autoregulatory
approach was superior to prescribed intensity based on 1 RM, termed APRE
(autoregulatory progressive resistance exercise). This was an important
finding, but there is a twist. The athlete chooses a weight based on the
preplanned difficulty within a training block, which is inadvertently a form of
intensity-based progression. The progression is framed in a way that
hopefully considers different levels of adaptation. Higher APREs work
toward a higher external load. A predetermined APRE is similar to having a
prescribed external load. No matter how you frame it, there is a systematic
increase in intensity from one week to the next.

Tonnage Increase With Intensity
Tonnage, volume multiplied by intensity, is a metric used to
systematically reach certain levels of performance. The theory is
that if someone can accumulate certain tonnages over some
time, it should manifest into higher levels of performance.
Takano (2012) discusses this theory in his book, describing
training programs as a means to accumulate as much tonnage
within a training cycle as possible. More accumulated tonnage
equates to higher levels of performance with the Olympic lifts.
One of the central aspects of accumulated tonnage is what

这种方法的问题在于，人类会随着情绪和动机而波动。 有人可能会说
，动机下降表明存在一种过度的状态，但这可能不是一种真正的生理上
的过度状态。主观评估应该对不能做的事情产生影响，但不能以牺牲可
以做什么的客观评估为代价。

对基于强度的渐进式超负荷的最大误解是——我们无法
预测运动员下周会做什么，那么为什么要规定体重呢？

Mann 及其同事 (2010) 证明，一种更加自我调节的方法优于基于 1 R
M 的规定强度，称为APRE (自动调节渐进抗阻运动)。 这是一个重要的
发现，但有一个转折。 运动员根据训练块内预先计划的难度选择重量
，这无意中是一种基于强度的渐进形式。 进展的框架方式有望考虑不
同程度的适应。 APRE 越高，外部负载就越高。预定的 APRE 类似于
具有规定的外部负载。 无论你如何设计，强度从一周到下一周都会有
系统地增加。

吨位随强度增加
吨位（体积乘以强度）是用于系统地达到一定性能水平的指标。
该理论认为，如果某人能够在一段时间内积累一定的吨位，那么
它应该体现为更高水平的绩效。 Takano（2012）在他的书中讨论
了这一理论，将培训计划描述为在培训周期内积累尽可能多吨位
的一种手段。 更多的累积吨位相当于奥林匹克举重机的更高水平
的性能。
累积吨位的核心问题之一是

holds more weight week to week in terms of progressive
overload. For context, an increase in weight of 1 to 2 kg (2-4 lb)
will have a relatively small effect on tonnage. If we were looking
for huge spikes in tonnage, we would have to look elsewhere
than intensity, or intensity as a single progression (table 4.1).
This is where you see coaches use multiple progressions at
once. If we add volume in the form of sets or reps, plus increase
intensity, we will make exponentially larger spikes from one week
to the next (table 4.2). It is simple arithmetic: Making a 1 to 2 kg
(2-4 lb) improvement at the same volume will be a pittance
compared to adding a rep each week.

即使不增加强度，您也可以对吨位产生巨大影响。每周看似微
小的变化可能会让作为教练的你觉得需要更积极地进步。我们讨
论的关于新手的一个领域是，每周的相对增加可以更快，这可能
允许教练在吨位上进行更大的增加。这是一个错误，原因如下：

我们不知道什么时候会出现收益递减点

occur, especially with someone we know little about. Taking into
account that there will be an abrupt point at which a novice can
no longer execute with more violent increases in tonnage. It is
better to focus on the minimal effective dose and stick with
intensity until you know the athlete can make more rapid
increases in tonnage. As we have seen, simply increasing a rep
each week can have significant effects on tonnage, and we can
easily do too much.

Velocity
With fast responders, a higher intensity will create more damage relative to
slower-responding athletes. The reason is largely based on the distribution of
fast-twitch muscle fibers. Faster-twitch athletes will make more rapid
neuromuscular adaptations and be able to make a faster and larger
progression from week to week. Considering that the faster responders will
recruit more muscle fibers and motor units at the same relative intensity
compared to the slower-twitch muscle fibers, intensity-based progressions
can be used as a means to slow down fast responders and speed up slow
responders.
This plays out with the velocity of the lift. The greater motor unit
recruitment from fast-twitch athletes is associated with the speed of a lift.
Speed, therefore, can be used to track intensity. We can look at the velocity
zones that range from under 0.50 m/s to above 1.30 m/s as a means to
determine how hard a set was. For instance, if an athlete working within the
absolute strength zone of under 0.50 m/s performs set one at an average
velocity of 0.55 m/s, we can say that the weight was too light. The suggestion
then is to go up in intensity the following week.
Rates of progression can be determined by how high the RPE (rating of
perceived exertion) was from the previous session. Asking the athlete how
hard or how long it took to recover following the previous workout can make
an impact on the next workout. Higher RPEs mean smaller progressions
week to week (figure 4.8), which is why it is so important to track load and
how the athlete felt using that load. Giving a diagnostic assessment to

发生，尤其是对于我们知之甚少的人。考虑到会出现一个突然点
，新手将无法再以更猛烈的吨位增加来执行。 最好专注于最小有
效剂量并坚持强度，直到您知道运动员可以更快地增加吨位。正
如我们所看到的，每周简单地增加一次次数就会对吨位产生重大
影响，而且我们很容易做得太多。

速度
对于反应速度快的运动员来说，相对于反应速度较慢的运动员来说，较
高的强度会造成更大的伤害。原因很大程度上是基于快肌纤维的分布。
快速抽动的运动员将做出更快速的神经肌肉适应，并且能够每周取得更
快更大的进步。 考虑到与慢速肌纤维相比，快速反应者会在相同的相
对强度下募集更多的肌肉纤维和运动单位，基于强度的进展可以用作减
慢快速反应者速度和加速慢反应者速度的手段。

这与升力的速度有关。 快肌运动员募集更多的运动单位与举重的速
度有关。因此，速度可以用来跟踪强度。 我们可以查看从低于 0.50 m/s
到高于 1.30 m/s 的速度区域，以此来确定一组的难度。例如，如果一名
运动员在绝对力量区低于0.50 m/s的情况下以0.55 m/s的平均速度进行第
一组训练，我们可以说重量太轻了。建议下周加强强度。

进展率可以通过前一疗程的 RPE（感知用力等级）的高低来确定。
询问运动员在上一次锻炼后恢复的难度或时间可以对下一次锻炼产生影
响。 RPE 越高意味着每周的进步越小（图 4.8），这就是为什么跟踪负
荷以及运动员使用该负荷的感受如此重要的原因。 进行诊断评估

progress from one week to the next helps immensely. This is how to best
leverage subjective appraisal with a systematic progressive overload scheme.
It relies on psychological assessment to determine the rate of physiological
adaptation.
There should be synchronization between how fast a lift was or wasn’t and
the level of RPE. Consider a way of fact-checking the RPE. Similar to Mann
and colleagues’ (2010) APRE, velocity drop from the first and last rep within
a set can determine the difficulty of that set. This can be extrapolated from set
to set and help you determine what intensity to use for that exercise. This can
further be extrapolated to weekly progressive overload.
Hearing things such as “I could barely walk the next day” means we have
smaller windows we can work within in terms of intensity progressive
overload. You do not need to track RPE to determine that. You can simply
look at the velocity of the set. Having multiple reps in a row below the
targeted velocity zone will translate to unwanted outcomes. However, hearing
someone say the workout was extremely easy means we can make larger
intensity jumps week to week. Again, we do not need RPE to determine that.
If someone is well above their targeted velocity zone, you need to intervene
and suggest a higher intensity. However, if we do not have a means to
determine progress, we fall victim to random application of stress. With RPE,
we can account for steady increases in weight from week to week. Debriefing
from a training session and asking how hard something was can give a clear
picture of what to do in the next training session.

从一周到下一周的进步有很大帮助。 这就是如何通过系统的渐进式超
载方案最好地利用主观评价。它依靠心理评估来确定生理适应率。
升降机的速度和 RPE 水平之间应该同步。考虑一种对 RPE 进行事实
核查的方法。与 Mann 及其同事（2010）的 APRE 类似，一组中第一次
和最后一次的速度下降可以决定该组的难度。这可以从一组到另一组进
行推断，并帮助您确定该练习的强度。这可以进一步推断为每周渐进性
超负荷。
听到诸如“第二天我几乎无法行走”之类的话意味着我们可以在强度
渐进超负荷方面工作的窗口较小。 您无需跟踪 RPE 即可确定这一点。
您可以简单地查看该组的速度。 在目标速度区域以下连续进行多次重
复将会导致不良结果。然而，听到有人说锻炼非常简单意味着我们可以
每周进行更大的强度跳跃。同样，我们不需要 RPE 来确定这一点。如
果某人远高于目标速度区，您需要进行干预并建议更高的强度。 然而
，如果我们没有办法确定进展，我们就会成为随机施加压力的受害者。
通过 RPE，我们可以计算出每周体重的稳定增加。总结培训课程并询问
某件事有多难可以清楚地了解下一次培训课程要做什么。

Volume
Volume-based progressive overload is traditionally important with relative
strength exercises such as pull-ups, push-ups, dips, inverted rows,
bodyweight leg curls, and bodyweight single-leg squats. Volume is also a
useful strategy when the coach does not have access to a lot of external load
options. You will also see that volume progressions are an excellent
alternative to intensity-based progressions from time to time.
As we discussed with intensity-based progressions, volume-based
progressions can have a significant impact on tonnage. More importantly, it is
very difficult to continuously progress for an extended period. If you think
about volume progressions, you are potentially asking someone to increase
upward to a 100% load from one week to the next. Think about asking
someone who can only do one pull-up to do double that in the next training
session. Having to do two pull-ups is a 100% increase. This would be an
impossible task for the athlete, depending on their level of strength.
There are three primary methods of progressing volume: repetition, time
under tension, and sets. Each one has its own merits and subsequent
negatives; your job as the coach is to leverage this depending on the goal. We
can look at increasing one of these as a potential alternative to increasing
intensity or a potentially situation-dependent progression that can create
significant advantages.

Reps
As mentioned previously, adding reps from one week to the next can be a tall
order for relative strength exercises like pull-ups, push-ups, or dips. We can
leverage a goal of setting a new rep max at body weight or with additional
weight by strategically adding repetitions each week (figure 4.9). This can

规定的强度基于运动员对之前训练的反应：
RPE>4，增加1%至2%； RPE < 3，增加2%至5%。

体积
传统上，基于容量的渐进式超负荷对于引体向上、俯卧撑、臂屈伸、倒
立划船、自重腿弯举和自重单腿深蹲等相对力量练习非常重要。 当教
练无法使用大量外部负荷选项时，训练量也是一个有用的策略。 您还
会发现，时常训练量渐进是基于强度渐进的绝佳替代方案。
正如我们讨论的基于强度的级数，基于体积的级数可以对吨位产生重
大影响。更重要的是，想要长期持续进步是非常困难的。 如果您考虑
训练量的进展，您可能会要求某人从一周到下一周将负荷增加到 100%
。 考虑要求一个只能做一个引体向上的人在下一次训练中做两倍的引
体向上。 做两次引体向上就增加了100%。 对于运动员来说，这将是
一项不可能完成的任务，具体取决于他们的力量水平。
提高音量的主要方法有三种：重复、紧张时间和组数。 每一种都有
其自身的优点和缺点；作为教练，你的工作就是根据目标利用这一点。
我们可以将增加其中一项视为增加强度的潜在替代方案，或可以创造显
着优势的潜在视情况而定的进展。

代表
如前所述，对于引体向上、俯卧撑或臂屈伸等相对力量训练，每周增加
次数可能是一项艰巨的任务。 我们可以通过策略性地每周增加重复次
数来利用根据体重或额外重量设定新的最大重复次数的目标（图 4.9）
。 这个可以

build in recovery for the athlete before they attempt to reach higher levels in
terms of a rep max at body weight. We need to be conscious of how
challenging this would be with little ability to manipulate one’s body mass.
Another method for adding reps is to use a fixed intensity and progress
reps week to week. Taking the rep max intensity chart mentioned in intensitybased progression (see figure 2.5 on page 29), we can use lower reps at
certain intensity levels and progress week to week. For example, with 5 RM,
we should be able to hit 90% of our 1 RM. This would be a tough weight to
hit five reps for without some progression. We can build confidence at a
certain weight by adding repetitions each week.
The biggest overreaction with volume—the only
way to prepare for rep max loads is intensitybased progressions.
It is quite common for athletes during competitive periods to be skittish
with maximal load. Athletes have a connection to what will feel heavy, which
can create a certain amount of apprehension, especially during competitive
periods. This can be a matter of framing. Reframing progressions to volume
can help with approaching maximal loads.
Having an alternate strategy to accomplish the same task can be catalytic
for certain athletes during the year. The strategy here would be that if we are
not making improvements with only intensity progressions and can
accomplish the task by using repetition progressions instead, we should do
that. In the end, if the athlete is stronger, that is all that matters.

在运动员尝试达到更高的体重最大重复次数水平之前，帮助他们进行恢
复。 我们需要意识到，如果没有能力操纵一个人的体重，这将是多么
具有挑战性。

运动员在比赛期间在最大负荷下感到不安是很常见的。运动员对感觉
沉重的事物有一种联系，这可能会产生一定程度的恐惧，尤其是在比赛
期间。 这可能是一个框架问题。 重新调整训练量的进展有助于接近最
大负荷。
制定替代策略来完成相同的任务可能会在这一年中对某些运动员产生
催化作用。这里的策略是，如果我们不只通过强度级数进行改进，并且
可以通过使用重复级数来完成任务，那么我们应该这样做。最后，如果
运动员更强，那才是最重要的。

Time Under Tension
The next, and often overlooked, volume progression is time under tension
(TUT). For most relative strength repetitions, progressions will be tough.
Asking someone to increase their 1 RM pull-up to 2 RM in the next training
session is not realistic for most athletes. However, asking someone to
increase the duration of the set is very doable, and this is based on varying
strength during different portions of the rep.
One aspect of a rep that is often overlooked is that its concentric portion
dictates the external load used. Concentric strength is the weakest of the three
contraction types. Eccentric is the strongest, and isometric is the second
strongest (see figure 3.7 on page 51).
The biggest misconception with volume—
concentric max is not the maximum amount the
muscle or movement pattern can handle.

图 4.9 基于重复的进展。

紧张的时间
下一个经常被忽视的容量进展是紧张时间（TUT）。 对于大多数相对
力量重复来说，进步会很困难。对于大多数运动员来说，要求某人在下
一次训练中将 1 RM 引体向上增加到 2 RM 是不现实的。 然而，要求某
人增加一组的持续时间是非常可行的，这是基于在代表的不同部分期间
不同的强度。
重复动作中经常被忽视的一个方面是，其同心部分决定了所使用的外
部负载。同心力量是三种收缩类型中最弱的。 偏心最强，等距次强（
参见第 51 页图 3.7）。

对体积的最大误解是同心最大并不是肌肉或运动模式可
以处理的最大量。

What this means for progressing TUT is that whatever we can do
concentrically, we can do more eccentrically or isometrically. Within a set,
we are first limited by what we can do concentrically, and this is far from the
limit of eccentric or isometric max force. Progressions from one week to the
next will be predicated on the rate-limiting step, which is concentric ability.
We still have more ability if we focus on the eccentric or isometric portions
of that exercise—this could mean more rapid or larger progressions from one
training session to the next.

The critical aspect here is that eccentric or isometric contractions are
traditionally maladapted. Most training is centered on the concentric portion
of the lift, leaving the eccentric and isometric portions underdeveloped. If we
asked someone to focus progressions on eccentric or isometric portions, we
would have a hard time predicting what the threshold is due to a lack of
exposure or focus. A common aspect of TUT-focused progressions that
leverage eccentric or isometric contractions is larger jumps from week to
week. The lack of exposure makes selecting an introductory weight more
challenging.
We can progress TUT by placing more focus on total TUT within a set.
We accomplish this by altering the time spent eccentrically, isometrically, or
concentrically. Since our eccentric and isometric contractions are stronger,
we can always go longer during a set than we can concentrically.
On the one hand, we can always add to a concentric max during either
eccentric or isometric contractions. The example of performing a rep max
number of pull-ups or dips is concentrically based. Instead of adding a rep the
following week, which is not always possible, we can add more TUT during
the eccentric or isometric portion (table 4.3).

这对于 TUT 的进步意味着，无论我们能做同心的事情，我们都可以
做更多的偏心或等距的事情。 在一组内，我们首先受到同心力所能做
的限制，这远非偏心或等距最大力的限制。从一周到下一周的进展将取
决于速率限制步骤，即同心能力。如果我们专注于该练习的偏心或等长
部分，我们仍然拥有更多能力 - 这可能意味着从一个训练课程到下一个
训练课程的进步更快或更大。

Because this is such an underused aspect of training, we see more rapid
adaptations. Taking a relative strength exercise and adding a rep week to

thought when progressing with TUT. The most crucial aspect about
leveraging TUT with progressive overload is to have a smaller progression.
Adding a rep may mean increasing 100%, adding a second eccentrically or
isometrically more attainable from a progressive overload standpoint.

Sets
The final means of volume-based progression is an increased number of sets
from one training session to the next. A word of caution here: Increasing the
number of sets will have the most direct impact on tonnage. Increasing sets, if
not carefully managed, can easily lead to overtraining.
A fundamental aspect of training is that volume in a session is inversely
proportional to intensity. There is a fractal element to this (simple rules
repeated) to the number of sets and volume per set, which are also inversely
proportional. Higher intensity means we use a higher number of sets and a
lower number of repetitions. Lower intensity means we use a lower number
of sets and a higher number of repetitions. This relationship between volume,
intensity, and sets creates the framework for progression (figure 4.10).
This relationship should feel intuitive about a training session. We can
only fit so much within a single session. If we use higher repetitions, we have
to do fewer sets. If we use lower repetitions, we should perform more sets.

另一方面，我们可以通过关注强项（偏心和等长）并以弱点（同心）
结束（表 4.4）来实现更快的适应速度。早期，我们将尽可能多的注意
力放在动作的偏心或等长部分上，让适应有机地发生。因为这是训练中
未被充分利用的方面，所以我们看到了更快速的适应。 在进行 TUT 训
练时，进行相对力量练习并通过在离心或等长部分花时间每周增加一次
重复次数是相反的想法。 利用渐进超负荷的 TUT 最重要的一点是渐进
性较小。增加一次次数可能意味着增加 100%，从渐进式超负荷的角度
来看，增加第二次偏心或等长训练更容易实现。

套
基于训练量的渐进的最后一种方法是从一个训练课程到下一个训练课程
增加组数。这里需要注意的是：增加组数将对吨位产生最直接的影响。
如果不小心管理，增加组数很容易导致过度训练。
训练的一个基本方面是训练量与强度成反比。 组数和每组的体积有
一个分形元素（重复简单的规则），它们也成反比。 更高的强度意味
着我们使用更多的组数和更少的重复次数。 较低的强度意味着我们使
用较少的组数和较高的重复次数。训练量、强度和组数之间的这种关系
创建了渐进的框架（图 4.10）。
这种关系在培训课程中应该是直观的。 我们在一次会议中只能容纳
这么多内容。如果我们使用更高的重复次数，我们就必须做更少的组数
。 如果我们使用较低的重复次数，我们应该执行更多的组数。

This applies to progression in that we need to know when and where we can
perform more sets from week to week with higher intensity and lower
repetitions per set. We simply run out of time within a single training session
when we use higher repetition sets.

FIGURE 4.10 Reps-to-set relationship.
As discussed in the example of relative strength exercises, asking someone
to increase their 1 RM by two reps from one training session to the next is not
always possible. However, we can increase the total number of repetitions in
a training session by increasing the sets if we keep the reps the same. From
one training session to the next, we accrue more total volume at higher
intensities by adding a set for each training session. We are not asking for
reps in a set; we are instead asking for more reps overall.
In actuality, if we could hit 1 RM for 10 sets in a training session, we
probably would have increased our 1 RM. The point being that if an athlete
can hit the 1 RM multiple times, they are stronger. We could use the same
logic of taking a rep max intensity and trying to hit more sets at a lower rep

Density
The final progression is density. Density is something that we can use for a
small window of time due to taking volume and intensity to threshold each
session. With that said, it is also very autoregulated. Your readiness for
training will dictate how much volume you can hit at a certain intensity
within a set period or training session.
Density is broken down into two categories: compression and expansion.
Compression density progressions are doing the same volume and intensity in
less time (table 4.5). We have to decrease the time in intra- (not always
possible) and inter- (always possible) sets. Expansion is doing more volume
and intensity at the same time (table 4.6). Again, we have decreased time
during or in between sets. If you think about it, density-based progressions
are based on decreasing rest intervals.

每周的数量和进度集。
相对力量练习的次数进展是困难的：
通过使用次最大重复次数并逐渐达到最大次数来获得
更好的表现。
对于大多数运动员来说，TUT 是更合理的训练量级数
：
早期利用较强的收缩、偏心和等长收缩，稍后利用较
弱的向心收缩。
渐进组数对相对于次数或 TUT 渐进的吨位有巨大影响
：
进步组包括高强度和低容量组。

密度
最后的进展是密度。 密度是我们可以在一小段时间内使用的东西，因
为每次训练都以训练量和强度为阈值。 话虽如此，它也是非常自我调
节的。 您对训练的准备情况将决定您在设定的时间段或训练课程中可
以达到一定强度的训练量。
密度分为两类：压缩和膨胀。压缩密度级数是在更短的时间内完成相
同的体积和强度（表 4.5）。 我们必须减少组内（并不总是可能）和组
间（总是可能）的时间。 扩展是同时增加训练量和强度（表 4.6）。
再次，我们减少了组间或组间的时间。 如果你仔细想想，基于密度的
渐进是基于减少休息间隔。

Compression
The most important aspect of density-based progressions is that the person’s
state of readiness will dictate the rate and amount of progression one can
make. We want steady and consistent progress from one week to the next.
We can only do that for a small window of time when we are pushing to the
absolute threshold, or failure, each week. We want to select the length of time
we can progress a training stimulus through our periodization plan, or
mesocycle length. One of the more important aspects of mesocycle length is
muscle fiber type and experience. Faster-twitch athletes and more
experienced lifters need shorter mesocycles. Density-based progressions will
have a more systemic effect on fast-twitch athletes because they do not have
the recovery mechanisms of slower-twitch athletes. This could equate to a
faster point of diminishing returns and, subsequently, shorter mesocycles.
The same is true for high-volume and high-intensity training programs.
We can view compression as we would progress sets in a volume-based
progression. It will have a significant systemic impact if not managed
properly—the person will break down and become overtrained. The most
logical answer is to limit the length of our progress, which creates a large
systemic stress.

压缩
基于密度的进展最重要的方面是，人的准备状态将决定一个人可以进行
的进展速度和数量。 我们希望从一周到下一周都能取得稳定、持续的
进展。当我们每周达到绝对阈值或失败时，我们只能在一小段时间内这
样做。我们想要选择通过分期计划进行训练刺激的时间长度，或中周期
长度。中周期长度更重要的方面之一是肌纤维类型和经验。 快速抽动
运动员和更有经验的举重运动员需要更短的中周期。基于密度的渐进将
对快肌纤维运动员产生更系统的影响，因为他们不具备慢肌纤维运动员
的恢复机制。 这可能相当于更快的收益递减点，以及随后更短的中周
期。

大容量、高强度的训练计划也是如此。我们可以将压缩视为基于体积
的进展中的进展组。 如果管理不当，它将产生重大的系统性影响——
人会崩溃并训练过度。 最合乎逻辑的答案是限制我们进步的时间，这
会造成巨大的系统性压力。

Compressing training volume from one week to the next is a great strategy
for athletes who struggle to find motivation for training. It incentivizes them
to push harder each week to be done faster. The trick is setting a fixed
intensity that targets the appropriate quality being developed. Muscle fiber
type and relative fitness levels will have a huge impact on the relative time to
completion. A faster-twitch athlete will require much longer rest periods,
which elongate the time to completion. As the athlete adapts to the training
stimulus, they will see big week-to-week improvements in time.
One aspect you will find with density-based progression is the visceral
nature of this training. Density in a training session creates a ton of fatigue
and acidity. This means that people will feel incredibly tired. A unique aspect
of this is that people reason with themselves, which is a missing aspect in
their training. As a result, those making steady progress week to week will
feel extreme exhaustion very infrequently (figure 4.11).
The biggest overreaction with density-based
progressions—progression is not exclusive to
exhaustion in every training session.
The idea is to be better, not tired. Confusing activity with accomplishment
is a huge aspect that a coach needs to illustrate to their athletes as faulty logic.
The effectiveness of training is not how much fatigue you accrue, but how
much better you can be. As we will discuss with the diminishing returns
principle (chapter 7), training has a point where it is no longer effective. You,
as the coach, have to help the athlete avoid this with every training session.
Therefore, it is very important to understand the limits of certain
progressions, such as density. The athlete who constantly overreaches will
have to find a strategy to meet the demands asked of them.

Quality Control
If you think about progressive overload, we are essentially
testing a hypothesis. We know what we want, such as running

对于那些难以找到训练动力的运动员来说，将训练量从一周压缩到下
一周是一个很好的策略。它激励他们每周更加努力，以更快地完成工作
。 诀窍是设定一个固定的强度，以培养适当的质量为目标。 肌纤维类
型和相对健康水平将对相对完成时间产生巨大影响。 快速抽动的运动
员需要更长的休息时间，从而延长完成比赛的时间。 当运动员适应训
练刺激时，他们会及时看到每周的巨大进步。
您会发现基于密度的渐进训练的一个方面是这种训练的本能本质。
训练的密度会产生大量的疲劳和酸度。这意味着人们会感到非常疲倦。
其中一个独特的方面是人们会自我推理，这是他们的训练中缺失的一个
方面。 因此，那些每周稳步进步的人很少会感到极度疲惫（图 4.11）
。

对基于密度的渐进的最大过度反应是，渐进并不意味着
每次训练中都会出现精疲力尽的情况。

我们的想法是变得更好，而不是累。将活动与成就混为一谈是教练需
要向运动员说明的一个重要方面，这是错误的逻辑。训练的有效性不在
于你累积了多少疲劳，而在于你能变得更好多少。 正如我们将讨论收
益递减原理（第 7 章），培训有一个不再有效的点。作为教练，你必须
帮助运动员在每次训练中避免这种情况。因此，了解某些级数（例如密
度）的限制非常重要。 不断超越的运动员必须找到一种策略来满足他
们的要求。

质量控制
如果你考虑渐进式超负荷，我们本质上是在检验一个假设。 我们
知道自己想要什么，比如跑步

faster or farther. We form a hypothesis to get us there, come up
with an intervention to get us to that goal, test that intervention,
and see the results. Progressive overload is the intervention to
get us to an outcome. Test outcomes are predicated on how well
thought out the hypothesis was and how well the intervention
was run.
Anthony Ditillo (1982) talks about how there can be more than
one progression at any given time, but you should avoid doing
so. We can layer in an intensity-based progression with a
volume-based progression. Ditillo refers to this as a double
progression. We could do an intensity-based, volume-based, and
density-based progression simultaneously. Ditillo refers to this as
triple progression. The problem with double and triple
progressions is that if something is not working properly, we
have a hard time tracing back to what went wrong.
Good programming or good research design is built on a very
simple premise: Can we maintain quality control of the
intervention during the experiment? If we have many different
things we are testing or implementing, we will have an
exponentially harder time tracking what caused or led to
something working or not. Reducing the inputs we use creates a
narrowed focus on what we are doing. That narrowed focus
allows us to spend time and energy on how well we are doing
something. We know definitively what the cause of something
not working or working is because it eliminates potential noise.
Single progressions of intensity, volume, or density may not
appear to be the most aggressive strategy. The idea that we can
progress multiple things at once may seem tempting. But before
jumping into the progression deep end, ask yourself, could you
predict where success came from if you used a double or triple
progression? If the technique was bad, the coach was not
motivating, you did not have the right equipment, or training was
scheduled at the wrong time, it would be hard to determine the
cause when so many other variables are at play.

更快或更远。我们提出一个假设来实现这一目标，提出一种干预
措施来帮助我们实现该目标，测试该干预措施并查看结果。 渐进
式超负荷是让我们达到结果的干预措施。测试结果取决于假设的
深思熟虑程度以及干预的实施情况。
Anthony Ditillo (1982) 讨论了如何在任何给定时间存在多个级数
，但您应该避免这样做。 我们可以将基于强度的进展与基于容量
的进展分层。 Ditillo 将此称为 double progression。我们可以同
时进行基于强度、基于体积和基于密度的进展。 Ditillo 将此称为
triple progression。 双级和三级级数的问题在于，如果某些东
西不能正常工作，我们就很难追溯到哪里出了问题。

好的编程或好的研究设计建立在一个非常简单的前提之上：我
们能否在实验过程中保持干预的质量控制？ 如果我们正在测试或
实施许多不同的东西，那么我们将更加难以追踪导致或导致某些
东西起作用或不起作用的原因。减少我们使用的投入会缩小我们
对正在做的事情的关注范围。 这种缩小的关注范围使我们能够将
时间和精力花在我们做某事的效果上。 我们明确地知道某些东西
不工作或不工作的原因是什么，因为它消除了潜在的噪音。

强度、体积或密度的单一渐进可能看起来不是最激进的策略。
我们可以同时取得多项进展的想法似乎很诱人。但在进入渐进深
度之前，问问自己，如果你使用双重或三重渐进，你能预测成功
来自哪里吗？ 如果技术不好，教练没有激励，你没有合适的装备
，或者训练安排在错误的时间，当有这么多其他变量在起作用时
，很难确定原因。

All systems move to a more disorganized state: entropy. We
can accelerate by adding more variables. The physical
representation of chaos in the human system is injury or illness.
Environmental demand surpassed the system’s capacity, and
injury or disease occurred. In terms of development, we increase
the demand by adding more than the system can handle at one
point. We want to do this systematically so the body can adapt
and become more resilient. We want to avoid adding too much
with multiple progressions to avoid either injury or diminished
performance.

FIGURE 4.11 Activity versus accomplishment.
The biggest misconception about density-based
progressions—altering technique, range of
motion, or body position to achieve more is not
positively adapting from one training session to
the next.

所有系统都会进入一种更加无组织的状态：熵。 我们可以通过
添加更多变量来加速。 人类系统中混乱的物理表征是伤害或疾病
。环境需求超出了系统的容量，导致伤害或疾病发生。在开发方
面，我们通过添加超出系统在某一点可以处理的数量来增加需求
。 我们希望系统地做到这一点，以便身体能够适应并变得更有弹
性。 我们希望避免在多个级数中添加太多，以避免受伤或性能下
降。

图 4.11 活动与成就。
关于基于密度的渐进（改变技术、运动范围或身体位置
以实现更多目标）的最大误解不是积极地从一个训练课
程适应到下一个训练课程。

Expansion
Changing the means of doing an exercise to accomplish more is
compromising the point of stress in the first place. The best regression if
someone cannot do something is to lower the weight. By that logic, if
someone cannot do something, we should never allow an athlete to adjust
their technique to meet the task.
Expanding training volume within a fixed amount of time is the alternative
option with density-based progressive overload. This is the correct option
within a team setting because it controls the group more effectively. Having a
definitive start and end time is important for leveraging the psychological
aspect of training. There will be a regression to the mean, with most athletes
hovering in the middle of the pack, with a select few either pulling the group
forward or holding the group back. The trick is not overreacting to high or
low volume but encouraging individual progressive overload week to week.
Integrity with both the rep and the set is a hard rule that we need to uphold
in training. As we progress, regardless of form, the way we do something
matters. Standards of movements, predetermined range of motion, or
predicted intensity, volume, and rest all need to be upheld. If we lose the
integrity of the rep and the set, the progression is meaningless. We did not
progress; we found a short-term solution to the problem. The athlete was not
physiologically more prepared, so they adjusted the strategy.
Optimal output is predicated on optimal input. You get out what you put
in, no matter how good the plan was. Priority should be based first on quality
and then on quantity. Too often, it is lost that the most important aspect of
anything is the way we do something. A bad program executed well will
probably be more effective than a good program executed poorly. Strive to
have both great execution and effective programming.
Density progressions are invaluable for several reasons. It is autoregulated
and phenomenal for developing capacity. It can be a tremendous tool for
creating metabolic stress or simply challenging your athletes. Taking an
approach of density progressions is only as good as the execution of the
training block.

扩张
改变锻炼方式以实现更多目标首先会损害压力点。 如果某人不能做某
事，最好的回归就是减轻体重。 按照这个逻辑，如果有人不能做某事
，我们就不应该允许运动员调整他们的技术来完成任务。
在固定时间内扩大训练量是基于密度的渐进超负荷的替代选择。 这
是团队环境中的正确选择，因为它可以更有效地控制团队。确定明确的
开始和结束时间对于利用培训的心理方面非常重要。将会出现均值回归
，大多数运动员徘徊在群体的中间，少数人要么拉动群体前进，要么阻
碍群体前进。 诀窍不是对高或低的训练量反应过度，而是鼓励个人每
周进行渐进式超负荷训练。
代表和团队的诚信是我们在训练中需要遵守的硬性规则。 随着我们
的进步，无论形式如何，我们做事的方式都很重要。 运动标准、预定
的运动范围或预测的强度、体积和休息都需要得到遵守。 如果我们失
去了重复次数和动作组的完整性，那么进步就毫无意义。 我们没有进
步；我们找到了问题的短期解决方案。运动员在生理上并没有做好更多
准备，因此他们调整了策略。
最优输出取决于最优输入。 无论计划有多好，你都会得到你投入的
东西。优先级应首先基于质量，然后基于数量。 人们常常忘记，任何
事情最重要的方面就是我们做事的方式。 执行得好的坏程序可能比执
行得不好的好程序更有效。 努力同时拥有出色的执行力和有效的编程
。
由于多种原因，密度级数是无价的。它是自动调节的并且对于发展能
力来说是惊人的。 它可以成为创造代谢压力或简单地挑战运动员的强
大工具。 采用密度渐进的方法仅与训练块的执行一样好。

Compression is the same work in less time;
expansion is more work in the same time,
ultimately progressing with less rest.
Faster-twitch athletes need shorter mesocycles:
Slow-twitch athletes 3 to 4 weeks; fast-twitch
athletes 2 to 3 weeks.
Less is more; exhaustion is not the goal; progress
over feeling tired.
The progressive overload factors are summarized as follows:
Intensity
Biggest overreaction: Nervous system adaptations permit making
larger week-to-week intensity jumps.
Biggest misconception: We cannot predict what an athlete will do next
week, so why prescribe weight?
Volume
Biggest overreaction: The only way to prepare for rep max loads is
intensity-based progressions.
Biggest misconception: Concentric max is not the maximum amount
the muscle or movement pattern can handle.
Density
Biggest overreaction: Progression is not exclusive to exhaustion every
training session.
Biggest misconception: Altering technique, range of motion, or body
position to achieve more is not positively adapting from one training
session to the next.

带回家
渐进性超负荷分为三类：强度、容量和

density. There is a time and a place for each. Most progressions will be based
on intensity. There will be a time and place for volume, such as relative
strength exercises or reframing for the athlete to break a plateau. There will
be a time and a place for density, with caution to limit exposure due to the
system stress one may experience. The most important aspect to remember is
that execution combined with progression is what creates positive outcomes.
One cannot exist without the other.

密度。每个人都有时间和地点。大多数进展将基于强度。 会有一定的
时间和地点进行训练量，例如相对力量练习或运动员打破平台期的重构
。 密度会有一定的时间和地点，但要小心限制暴露，因为人们可能会
经历系统压力。要记住的最重要的一点是，执行力与进步相结合才能创
造积极的结果。两者缺一不可。
