PROGRESSION
The biggest paradox of progression is whether to develop weaknesses into
strengths or accentuate strengths to peak. Are we fixing problems or reverse
engineering solutions? Progression becomes a matter of perspective on what
is needed versus what is necessary, which becomes compounded when we
interject our agenda and bias into our training preferences. The goal of any
progression is to apply logic and reason to improve relative to not doing
anything at all.
We are, in effect, deciding whether we are going to run from weaknesses
or run toward our strengths. The decision to improve a weakness or peak for
strength is difficult and probably not an effective use of time. In truth, you
are always doing both. Choosing an arbitrary camp to stay in is not beneficial
to yourself or your athletes. This is not a polarizing pick-a-side topic, but it is
worth thinking about. What is the basis for your progression?
The basis for a progression is evident in the way one programs. It becomes
obvious that certain camps screen and assess to determine where to start and
ultimately where to go (figure 5.1). Others follow a sequence to engineer a
certain outcome. In the team setting, you will face difficult decisions between
elaborate screening and predetermined progressions. The volume of people
and the amount of unknown, even with a screen before training, is immense.
Having a diagnostic to determine who should do what is possible and will
take ingenuity, which we will discuss in part II.
To achieve the desired training adaptations from a certain activity or

5
进展
进步的最大悖论是，是把弱点发展成优势，还是把优势发挥到顶峰。
我们是在解决问题还是逆向工程解决方案？进步变成了对需要什么和必
要什么的看法问题，当我们将我们的议程和偏见插入到我们的培训偏好
中时，这种情况就会变得更加复杂。 任何进展的目标都是应用逻辑和
推理来改进（相对于什么都不做）。
实际上，我们正在决定是要摆脱弱点还是发挥自己的优势。决定改善
弱点还是提高力量峰值是很困难的，而且可能不是有效利用时间的方法
。 事实上，你总是同时做这两件事。随意选择一个营地住宿对你自己
或你的运动员都没有好处。这不是一个两极分化的话题，但却值得思考
。你进步的基础是什么？
进步的基础在一个人的编程方式中是显而易见的。很明显，某些营地
会进行筛选和评估，以确定从哪里开始以及最终去哪里（图 5.1）。 其
他人则遵循一定的顺序来设计特定的结果。在团队环境中，您将面临精
心筛选和预定进展之间的艰难决定。 即使在训练前有屏幕，人员数量
和未知数量也是巨大的。进行诊断以确定谁应该做可能的事情并且需要
独创性，我们将在第二部分中讨论。
为了从某项活动中获得所需的训练适应或

stimulus, training must gradually and constantly evolve. This implies that
there is an optimal time frame for the adaptation to occur. If overload
increases too quickly, it may result in poor technique, improper muscle firing
patterns, or injury. If overload progresses too slowly, improvements will be
minimal or nonexistent. Progression is not the same as progressive overload;
it is often confused and hence overlooked. The idea of progression relative to
progressive overload is the optimal development of biomotor, bioenergetic,
or biomechanical qualities. Progressive overload is the driver (sets, reps,
tempo, rest, frequency), and progression is the vehicle (exercise selection,
exercise order) for adaptation.
Progression aims to create an optimal path to ensure we can reach an
outcome that is perceived as elite. It is a logical sequence from one step to the
next that ensures success. To do something complex, we first need to
demonstrate that we can do simple things. There is no elite without going
through the appropriate steps.

FIGURE 5.1 Direction.
If we can understand the most fundamental parts, we can sequence these
parts in such a way that will ensure success more consistently. Progression
cannot be discussed without including fractals because they are such a
universal aspect of nature. The patterns in nature that repeat themselves, such
as the shoreline or a snowflake, represent a larger and more universal truth.
This truth represents that certain things are simply the sum of their parts. This

刺激、训练必须逐步、不断发展。 这意味着适应发生有一个最佳时间
范围。 如果超负荷增加得太快，可能会导致技术不佳、肌肉放电模式
不正确或受伤。 如果超载进展太慢，改进将很小或根本不存在。进展
并不等同于进行性超负荷；它经常被混淆并因此被忽视。相对于渐进性
超负荷的渐进理念是生物运动、生物能量或生物力学品质的最佳发展。
渐进式超负荷是驱动因素（组数、次数、节奏、休息、频率），渐进式
是适应的载体（运动选择、运动顺序）。

进步旨在创造一条最佳路径，以确保我们能够达到被视为精英的结果
。这是确保成功的从一步到下一步的逻辑顺序。 为了做复杂的事情，
我们首先需要证明我们可以做简单的事情。 没有经过适当的步骤就没
有精英。

图 5.1 方向。
如果我们能够理解最基本的部分，我们就可以以确保更一致地成功的
方式对这些部分进行排序。 如果不包括分形，就不能讨论渐进，因为
它们是自然的普遍方面。自然界中不断重复的图案，例如海岸线或雪花
，代表了一个更大、更普遍的真理。这个真理表明某些事物只是其各部
分的总和。这

invites the question: What are the parts? Training is complex, which makes
the need to find true things that much more important (figure 5.2).

FIGURE 5.2 Complicated versus complex training.
The most fitting starting point here is to simplify before it gets
complicated or complex. We need to establish what is complicated before we
can demonstrate what is simple. Complicated is a lot of individual parts that
are sequentially ordered in a way that can be replicated. A puzzle can be
complicated. Having more or fewer pieces can make a puzzle simpler or
more complicated. If someone has never done a puzzle before and wants to
enjoy doing puzzles, start with a simpler one with fewer pieces and sharp,
contrasting color patterns. Over time, with repetition, you will improve and
enjoy more blended color schemes and higher-piece puzzles.
Complexity is not determined by order. It is a blank canvas, which is how
we should approach programming. The human body and sport are more
complex than complicated, which makes it harder to predict what
progressions will be effective. Regardless of whether the problems are
complicated or complex, a coach needs to distill what is true. The key aspect
of both is that they are fractals. They have similar elements within the macro

提出一个问题：有哪些部分？ 培训很复杂，这使得寻找真实事物的需

图 5.2 复杂与复杂训练。

复杂性不是由顺序决定的。它是一块空白的画布，这就是我们应该如
何进行编程。 人体和运动比复杂更复杂，这使得预测哪些进展会有效
变得更加困难。 无论问题复杂还是复杂，教练都需要提炼出真实的东
西。两者的关键在于它们都是分形。它们在宏中具有相似的元素

and micro perspectives. The difference is that complicated problems have
continuity from one to another. Complexity lacks continuity from one
problem to another.
With exercise selection, we want to add layers sequentially to reach a
more complicated, or perhaps a complex, version. If someone is limited in
experience, the most logical strategy for ensuring success is to start simply
and remove complications. More moving parts, such as joints, types of
resistance, planes of motion, or vectors, can make something more
complicated. More random environments are more complex. When we start
with something simple or predictable, it is easier to see potential limitations.
The more complicated or complex things are, the more there is to sort
through the mystery to find a solution.
Continuous improvement is based on the timing of setbacks. Setbacks are
natural and a great reminder of just how complex the training process is. The
difference between complicated and complex training is that complex
training has no repeatable sequence that we can follow. The body responds in
an infinite number of ways to any stressor placed on it. The more complex
something is, the less complicated the strategy we can use.
We use progressions because we want a better way to assess the quality of
our plan. For instance, a single-joint exercise failing before a multijoint
exercise is a win because it provides a clearer perspective of where the lack
of success came from. The fractal relationship is understanding the simplest
aspect of a problem and how it will manifest itself as a larger, more systemic
problem.
Find out the problem early by starting simply to
find the best plan.
The most obvious progression is lighter before heavier. We can easily say
this interchangeably: slower before faster or less intense before more intense.
Something heavier, faster, or more intense is simply more complicated and
will have a smaller margin of error. If the load is less, the speed is slower, or
if the intensity is lower, the margin for error becomes significantly larger. A

和微观视角。 不同之处在于，复杂的问题从一个问题到另一个问题具
有连续性。 复杂性缺乏从一个问题到另一个问题的连续性。
通过练习选择，我们希望依次添加层以达到更复杂的版本。 如果某
人的经验有限，那么确保成功的最合乎逻辑的策略就是从简单开始并消
除复杂性。 更多的运动部件，例如关节、阻力类型、运动平面或矢量
，会使事情变得更加复杂。 随机环境越复杂。 当我们从简单或可预测
的事情开始时，更容易看到潜在的局限性。事情越复杂，就越需要解开
谜团才能找到解决方案。

持续改进是基于挫折的时机。挫折是很自然的，并且很好地提醒我们
训练过程是多么复杂。复杂训练和复合训练之间的区别在于，复杂训练
没有我们可以遵循的可重复序列。身体会以无数种方式对施加在其上的
任何压力做出反应。 事情越复杂，我们可以使用的策略就越简单。
我们使用级数是因为我们想要一种更好的方法来评估计划的质量。
例如，在多关节练习之前失败的单关节练习是一种胜利，因为它提供了
一个更清晰的视角来了解失败的根源。 分形关系是理解问题最简单的
方面，以及它如何表现为一个更大、更系统的问题。

通过简单地开始寻找最佳计划来尽早发现问题。

最明显的进展是先轻后重。我们可以很容易地互换地说：先慢后快，
或者先不那么强烈，然后更强烈。更重、更快或更强烈的东西只会更复
杂，并且误差幅度也会更小。如果负载较小，速度较慢，或者强度较低
，则误差幅度会明显增大。一个

mistake made within a simpler context will lead to a much less dire
consequence. We are placing constraints on our programming by using
simpler or more attainable solutions to develop a clearer path. As we learn
more about the athletes, we place fewer constraints on them and increase
their tolerance and bandwidth to stress.
A simpler context is less risky and easier to interpret any mishaps. The
reason slow motion exists is to make the unseeable seeable. A race car
driving at 10 mph (16 km/hr) before reaching the start line and blowing a
gasket has a much simpler fix and less catastrophic outcome than a race car
driving at 200 mph (322 km/hr) coming around a turn with 30 other cars
jockeying for the same spot and then blowing a gasket. We need to ensure
success for the athlete. First, we need to ensure our plan is the correct one by
ruling out any simple faults as fast as possible.
Imagine a great engineer as a child getting an alarm clock or transistor
radio and taking it apart to learn how it works. Every child takes the radio
apart; it is the engineer who puts it back together. The key to putting
something back together is to see how the parts interact with one another.
What we know from fractals is that, mathematically, we can see smaller parts
within any complicated structure more clearly. What we do not know is
exactly how they form the larger entity within a complex process, but we will
be much closer to understanding. This is why we need to start simply.
We can take the smallest fractal representation in a progression to
understand those smaller pieces and then piece them together step by step.
When there is a setback, which there will be, handling it will be easier
because these setbacks are so transparent and more readily fixed. Simple
before complex, slow before fast, light before heavy, or stable before
unstable are all necessary to consistently handle inevitable problems well as
they come up. We can fix problems with larger groups more readily when we
are slow, light, and stable than when we are fast, heavy, and unstable.

在更简单的环境中犯下的错误将导致不那么可怕的后果。 我们通过使

程。 随着我们对运动员的了解越来越多，我们对他们的限制就会越来
越少，他们对压力的耐受力和带宽也会增加。

除任何简单的错误，以确保我们的计划是正确的。
想象一下，一位伟大的工程师小时候得到了一个闹钟或晶体管收音机
，并将其拆开以了解其工作原理。 每个孩子都会拆开收音机； 工程师

看到任何复杂结构中的较小部分。 我们不知道的是它们如何在复杂的

简单地开始。
我们可以采用级数中最小的分形表示来理解这些较小的部分，然后将
它们逐步拼凑在一起。当出现挫折时（确实会出现），处理它会更容易
，因为这些挫折是如此透明并且更容易解决。 先简单后复杂、先慢后
快、轻后重、稳定前不稳定，这些都是在不可避免的问题出现时始终如
一地处理好的必要条件。当我们缓慢、轻便和稳定时，我们可以比快速
、沉重和不稳定时更容易地解决较大群体的问题。

FIGURE 5.3 Top down and bottom up.
A complicated problem occurs when we backtrack over several steps to
zero in on the source of the problem. When looking forward to this
complicated outcome, we can go about it in one of two ways: top down or
bottom up (figure 5.3). Top down is reverse engineering from the desired
end, starting at the end and refining as needed, while bottom up starts with
individual pieces and forms them into a complicated result. Bottom up
develops early weakness into later strength. It is an approach that teaches
individual parts, such as how to read music, learn the instrument, hear notes,
et cetera.
A great example of this would be Olympic lifting (snatch, clean, and jerk).
The classic Russian teaching style is bottom-up pedagogy, teaching the
individual parts of front squats, pulls, power catch variations, and then full
snatch, clean, and jerk. Alternatively, the Bulgarian approach is a top-down
method that starts with the snatch, clean, and jerk and chooses accessory
exercises based on deficiencies observed during the lift. This difference in
training approach is not exclusive to weightlifting; it is a debate in any
complicated skill development, such as math or music. In music playing, a
top-down approach would be to teach the entire song and let a student
replicate it. In math, a bottom-up approach would be teaching basic

当期待这个复杂的结果时，我们可以采用以下两种方式之一：自上而下
或自下而上（图 5.3）。 自上而下是从所需的末端开始进行逆向工程，
从末端开始并根据需要进行改进，而自下而上则从各个部分开始并将它
们形成一个复杂的结果。 自下而上将早期的弱势发展为后来的强势。
这是一种教授各个部分的方法，例如如何阅读乐谱、学习乐器、听音符
等等。
一个很好的例子就是奥林匹克举重（抓举、挺举）。经典的俄罗斯教
学风格是自下而上的教学法，教授前蹲、拉体、力量接球变式的各个部
分，然后是完整的抓举、挺举和挺举。 另外，保加利亚方法是一种自

缺陷选择辅助练习。 这种训练方法的差异并非举重所独有。 这是任何

方法是教授整首歌曲并让学生复制它。 在数学中，自下而上的方法将
教授基础知识

arithmetic before basic problem-solving.
With either method, we are trying to progress to reach the highest absolute
level of development. Everyone being able to reach an absolute peak would
be ideal. With training being a complex problem, our best outcome is hitting
the largest number of positive development outcomes possible within the
group. The more people we can have move toward a positive outcome, the
better. Positive results are more indicative of the quality of the choice in our
progressions. Within our progressions, we can fall easily into a trap of
subjectivity. Technique can sometimes fall into the same category as “beauty
is in the eye of the beholder.” With bad technique, people get hurt. Therein
lies the way we quantify technique or biomechanics. Injury reduction through
good biomechanics turns a qualitative marker into a quantitative one.
Techniques leading to positive results and reduced rates of injury become the
focus of how to evaluate the strength of a progression.
We want to look at progressions as a means to maximize performance by
minimizing inefficiencies. Someone getting injured during training is
extremely significant. In terms of statistics, when it comes to injuries
during training, only one metric is attributed to a successful plan: zero.
If people get hurt, all interventions are obsolete. In math, anything
multiplied by zero is always zero. Any protocol or method multiplied by an
injury is always injured. “Those who survive will be champions” is a flat-out
counterproductive approach. The idea of loading someone with the highest
threshold version of exercises early in a progression may appear to be a good
strategy to fast-track results. However, the more complicated something is
when combined with poor technique, the greater the risk. Moving faster
through progressions without proper vetting, therefore, potentially comes at a
cost.
A bottom-up approach is the central tenet of progression. Taking
individual pieces and adding them to make an integrated, complicated
movement or program is key. A good training program ensures success for
the majority. A top-down approach would be a program that focuses on the
success of the minority. Bottom up, we can see where everyone is succeeding
or failing and make amendments to improve the outcome for the majority.
We can also see if a progression is moving too quickly and leading to

increased rates of injuries. The bottom-up approach takes a sequential
approach to ensure both safety and success simultaneously. We want our
athletes to succeed because of, not in spite of, our programs.
Progression is about minimizing risk while simultaneously optimizing
performance through programming. The concept of starting simple or easy
before complicated or complex is to set everyone up for success. Easy before
difficult matters greatly when it comes to safety. The performance gain from
someone in a poorly designed program who makes it through that program
will always be greater than the one in which someone gets hurt. Looking at
the bottom line is important: We are in the improvement business. A bottomup approach is the framework of progression to ensure success and safety.
That, above all else, is our purpose. Yes, there will always be an aggressive
play, but that is reserved for when there is an absolute certainty that it will
work. In the meantime, we choose proven winners. The best chance of
success is the strategy that is the least risky, which is why progression exists
in the first place.
As we think about progression, consider that we are building a base to
have a higher ceiling. Progression is how we organize and sequence training
to have the highest peak possible form of training. A huge aspect of
biomechanics, bioenergetics, and biomotor abilities is not just the maximal
expression of power but the repeatability capacity of certain velocities or
intensities. It is the capacity of each of those abilities that creates not only a
higher potential for power but also more resilience when exposed to
randomness or a high degree of variance. We can say that capacity is the
same thing as variability.
Narrowing the focus leads to diminished time for other aspects of
development. Peaking is prioritizing what is needed to accelerate during
competition. With peaking, we diminish time spent on other areas, and this
potentially makes us vulnerable to novel stimuli or randomness. Developing
variability, or a wide base, gives us a larger bandwidth to handle whatever
comes in complex environments. Power is the natural funnel of training; the
question then becomes, are we more vulnerable to outside stressors through
direct power training too early? As we push to a threshold, we need to
acknowledge the response to high-constraint, simple stressors. As we move

Biomechanics
Progression is about ordering training to achieve the best possible outcome.
We are starting with biomechanics to establish a foundation with
progressions. This is important because it lays the foundation with technique,
or the ability to do something as a priority. Limiting injury risk by
standardizing optimal biomechanics is a priority. It is our best way to
quantify the quality of a progression.
The most important progression is range of motion (ROM). As a whole,
we want to establish full ROM, or the highest attainable range of movement,
with every exercise first. This means that we only want to reduce ROM when
we cannot move through a certain ROM or a specific performance outcome.
Unless there is a specific reason, there is no need not to go through a full
ROM.

Full ROM Before Partial ROM
An important aspect of any progression is giving as much variability to the
system as possible. The variability of a system is the determinant of
resiliency. A system that can handle a higher degree of variance in the form
of stress will be more capable of responding to more stress later. Too often,
we lose variability through reduced ROM exercises. The result is that we see
injuries and decreased performance. With biomechanics, we want to create a
foundation of full ROM to provide the most resilience possible.
One of the biggest misconceptions about
biomechanics is that increased external load with
reduced ROM is more beneficial than reduced
load with increased ROM.
We will discuss force, velocity, and work with biomotor progressions, but
the idea that we can increase force with increased external load is not as

更快、更重或更长，我们可以更好地理解潜在的反应。

生物力学
进步是指安排培训以实现最佳结果。我们从生物力学开始，为渐进奠定
基础。这很重要，因为它为技术奠定了基础，或者说优先做某事的能力
。 通过标准化最佳生物力学来限制受伤风险是当务之急。 这是我们量
化进展质量的最佳方法。
最重要的进展是运动范围 (ROM)。 总的来说，我们希望在每次练习
中首先建立完整的 ROM，即可达到的最高运动范围。这意味着，只有
当我们无法通过某个 ROM 或特定的性能结果时，我们才想减少 ROM
。除非有特殊原因，没有必要不经过完整的ROM。

完整 ROM 先于部分 ROM
任何进展的一个重要方面是为系统提供尽可能多的可变性。 系统的可
变性是弹性的决定因素。 一个能够处理更高程度的压力变化的系统将
更有能力在以后应对更大的压力。 很多时候，我们会因为减少活动范
围练习而失去可变性。结果是我们看到受伤和表现下降。通过生物力学
，我们希望创建完整 ROM 的基础，以提供尽可能大的弹性。

关于生物力学的最大误解之一是，通过减少 ROM 来增
加外部负荷比通过增加 ROM 来减少负荷更有利。

我们将讨论力、速度以及生物运动进展的工作，但是我们可以通过增
加外部负载来增加力的想法并不像

direct a connection to performance improvement as one would hope. In all
actuality, that increased force is only specific to that exercise at that ROM
and not universally transferable. When we reduce ROM, we also reduce the
amount of work we do. We may use a heavier external load, but that does not
mean we have increased transfer or something valuable. It will, however,
come with more risk. This creates a risk-reward aspect that we need to
consider. Remember, we want to make training as simple as possible; less
ROM is clearly a cause of risk.
We can always add an external load by reducing the ROM. That will
always be true, but that would result in less work being done. With that said,
since it will always be there, we should strive to move through a full ROM
for as long as possible, or at least until we no longer need to. When the
opportunity arises, such as trying to use partials or inertial work, a reduced
ROM to use heavier loads or create more power will always be an option.
However, it is like cooking: We can always add ingredients, but it is hard to
subtract them. We can always take ROM away, but we cannot always add it.
You will become good at what you repeatedly do: specificity. If we prioritize
training through a full ROM, it will be ingrained.
As discussed in chapter 3, Specificity, movement patterns need to go in
order toward specificity, whether it is general or specific to the task.
Developing general before specific can give a higher potential ceiling to tasks
during sports, like running faster, jumping higher, or being able to go longer
distances. The reverse would be specific training all the time, which may not
allow the development of general qualities. This is the concept of bottom up,
which is general to specific. Said differently, let’s be able to do the full thing
before we ask to do part of the thing with a stipulation, such as heavier or
faster.
The idea of an early specialist, as discussed in books like Sports Gene,
Range, or Outliers, shows the need to prioritize a more deliberate approach.
The important aspect to digest here is that success is multivariate. There is no
clearly laid-out path. For some, developing general qualities is incredibly
beneficial. For others, more focus on specific qualities is the best choice.
What is important is that we create a diagnostic approach to this. We could
easily say that always doing general before specific is a similar thought to

正如人们所希望的那样，直接与绩效改进联系起来。 事实上，增加的
力量只是特定于该 ROM 的练习，而不是普遍可转移的。 当我们减少 R
OM 时，我们也会减少我们所做的工作量。我们可能会使用更重的外部
负载，但这并不意味着我们增加了传输或有价值的东西。 然而，这将
带来更大的风险。 这产生了我们需要考虑的风险回报方面。 请记住，
我们希望使培训尽可能简单； 较少的 ROM 显然是造成风险的一个原因
。
我们总是可以通过减少 ROM 来添加外部负载。 这永远都是事实，
但这会导致所做的工作减少。话虽如此，由于它永远存在，我们应该努
力尽可能长时间地使用完整的 ROM，或者至少直到我们不再需要为止
。 当机会出现时，例如尝试使用部分功或惯性功，减少 ROM 以使用更
重的负载或产生更多功率将始终是一种选择。然而，这就像烹饪一样：
我们总是可以添加配料，但很难减少它们。我们总是可以删除 ROM，
但我们不能总是添加它。你会变得擅长你反复做的事情：特异性。如果
我们优先考虑通过完整的 ROM 进行训练，它就会根深蒂固。
正如第 3 章“特异性”中所讨论的，运动模式需要走向特异性，无论
是一般任务还是特定任务。先发展一般性，后发展具体性可以为运动中
的任务提供更高的潜在上限，例如跑得更快、跳得更高或能够走更远的
距离。反之就是一直进行专门的训练，这可能不允许一般素质的发展。
这就是自下而上的概念，从一般到具体。换句话说，在我们要求按照规
定（例如更重或更快）做部分事情之前，让我们能够完成全部事情。

正如 Sports Gene、Range 或 Outliers 等书籍中所讨论的，
early specialist 的想法表明需要优先考虑一种更审慎的方法。这里需要
消化的一个重要方面是成功是多因素的。没有明确的路径。 对于某些
人来说，培养一般素质是非常有益的。 对于其他人来说，更多地关注
特定品质是最好的选择。重要的是我们为此创建了一种诊断方法。 我
们可以很容易地说，总是在具体之前先做一般性的想法与

ROM and variability. This simply is not true. There are too many exceptions
to that thought to make it an absolute truth. If we are doing specific training
incorrectly all the time, we may be going in the wrong direction faster and
possibly be injured more often.
We need diagnostic criteria to begin trying to answer this question. If the
person is not skilled but very powerful, strong, fast, or greatly conditioned,
more specific work is needed. If the person is extremely skilled but not very
powerful, strong, fast, or greatly conditioned, more general work is needed.
Having conversations with the coach or the athlete is the best place to start. If
they are not very skilled or developed, the best bet probably is to develop
specific qualities. There are simply too many examples of specialization or
generalization to say that there is one size that fits all. But if we can apply
logic and meet the athletes where they are, we can increase our chances of
success. When in doubt, it’s probably best to go from general to specific, or
bottom up.
Poor sports skills—work specific
Poor general development—work general
Poor sports skills and poor general development
—work from general to specific
The final progression to discuss is going from predictable to
unpredictable. This is the fundamental difference between training and
competition. The primary question we need to answer is how many
constraints we need to place on the athlete for them to be successful based on
their current level of development.
Novice athletes need many constraints within training. They have yet to
master the baseline fundamentals of movement to add uncertainty. Taking an
unprepared athlete and having them perform in a chaotic environment would
be a mistake. As the off-season progresses, we want to remove constraints
and expose the athlete to more unpredictability.

ROM 和可变性。这根本不是真的。这种想法有太多例外，无法使其成
为绝对真理。如果我们一直错误地进行特定训练，我们可能会更快地走
向错误的方向，并且可能会更频繁地受伤。
我们需要诊断标准来开始尝试回答这个问题。如果这个人不熟练，但
非常强大、强壮、快速或条件很好，则需要更具体的工作。如果这个人
技术非常好，但不是很强大、强壮、快速或条件很好，则需要进行更一
般的工作。与教练或运动员交谈是最好的开始。如果他们不是很熟练或
不发达，最好的选择可能是培养特定的素质。 专业化或泛化的例子太
多了，无法说有一种方法适合所有人。 但如果我们能够运用逻辑并与
运动员见面，我们就可以增加成功的机会。 如有疑问，最好从一般到
具体，或自下而上。

运动技能差——具体工作
整体发展不佳——工作一般
运动技能差和整体发展差——从一般到具体的工作

最后要讨论的进展是从可预测到不可预测。 这是训练和比赛的根本
区别。 我们需要回答的主要问题是，根据运动员目前的发展水平，我
们需要对他们施加多少限制才能取得成功。
新手运动员在训练中需要很多限制。 他们尚未掌握运动的基本原理
，从而增加了不确定性。让一个毫无准备的运动员在混乱的环境中表演
将是一个错误。 随着休赛期的进行，我们希望消除限制，让运动员面
临更多的不可预测性。

The biggest overreaction with biomechanics:
Everything needs to have a definite beginning and
end to be effective.
We know that small-sided games have a much more definitive impact on
increasing V̇O2max (Hadiana, 2019). The benefits of random environments
toward general fitness are profound. This again comes down to what the
athlete can handle; if they are not prepared for the random environment, they
could be at higher risk. This serves as a crucial point of conditioning tests,
where preparation for them might hinder the development of the actual thing
we want to accomplish.
Predictability is a high-constraint environment. Unpredictability is a lowconstraint environment. In between is about taking away constraints. Some
examples of constraints are predictability, time, space, tasks, joints, stability,
speed, or intensity. Each of these constraints can be expanded to be more
challenging or less challenging. Your job as a coach is not only to add or
subtract constraints but to increase or decrease the level of those constraints
(figure 5.4).
If you remember from the discussion of progressive overload (chapter 4),
we want to be strategic with the variables we progress at one time. We are
trying to move to a potentially more random environment to prepare for
competition, but we cannot progress all variables simultaneously all the time.
We need to consider the bandwidth of movements during competition to help
us with this. Although we are moving to a complex environment, we need to
try to distill simple explanations as to why something worked or not.

对生物力学最大的过度反应是：一切都需要有明确的开
始和结束才能有效。

我们知道，小场比赛对增加 V̇O2max 具有更明确的影响（Hadiana，2
019）。 随机环境对总体健康的好处是深远的。 这又取决于运动员的
处理能力；如果他们没有为随机环境做好准备，他们可能会面临更高的
风险。 这是条件测试的一个关键点，为它们做准备可能会阻碍我们想
要完成的实际事情的发展。
可预测性是一个高约束环境。 不可预测性是一个低约束环境。 介于
两者之间的是消除限制。 约束的一些例子是可预测性、时间、空间、
任务、关节、稳定性、速度或强度。 这些限制中的每一个都可以扩展
到更具挑战性或更少挑战性。 作为教练，你的工作不仅是增加或减少
限制，还要增加或减少这些限制的水平（图 5.4）。
如果你还记得渐进超载的讨论（第 4 章），我们希望对我们一次性进
展的变量采取战略性的态度。 我们正在尝试进入一个可能更加随机的
环境来为竞争做准备，但我们无法始终同时推进所有变量。我们需要考
虑比赛期间运动的带宽来帮助我们解决这个问题。尽管我们正在进入一
个复杂的环境，但我们需要尝试提炼出简单的解释来解释为什么某些东
西有效或无效。

Cyclic Sports Versus Acyclic Sports
A key factor to consider is that cyclic sports (repeated movement actions, like
running straight ahead) have a much smaller need for a random or broad
spectrum of progressions. A 100 m sprinter or cyclist will need structural
balance, ROM, and stability in all three planes, but primarily in the sagittal
plane, to reduce risk from training. However, the exercise inventory does not
need to be extensive. In a sense, we are increasing constraints to prioritize
peaking and performance in correlated exercises.

Acyclic or team sports have an infinite number of movements, orders, or
demands that are placed on the athlete during competition. Their exercise
inventory and progression to more unpredictable environments become more
necessary. Predictable movement needs to be performed in all three planes of
motion, with full ROM and a focus on structural balance to better prepare the
athlete. This creates a larger exercise inventory and a more direct connection
to unpredictable environments. It is a foundation for unpredictable
environments due to its capability for a larger degree of variance. We want to
reduce the constraints as we progress through training from start to finish.
This will translate more adequately to competition than the reverse.

When we think about biomechanical progression, having a clear
perspective on the intended outcome is paramount for success. In a team
setting, you know that the demands from sport to sport are different. We
know that the general development of traditional movement patterns is the
standard, but that is not extensive enough. Relying on obvious observations
and knowledge of the environment being open or closed is critical to making
correct progressions.

Biomotor Abilities
Force, velocity, and work are the biomotor abilities we will discuss. Said
differently, how heavy can we go, how fast can we go, or how long can we
go? Distilling this into key funnels and deciding to focus on one area versus
another results from taking an inventory of how well someone performs.

弹力
非循环或团队运动在比赛期间对运动员有无限数量的动作、命令或要
求。 他们的练习清单和进入更不可预测的环境变得更加必要。可预测
的运动需要在所有三个运动平面上进行，具有完整的活动范围并注重结
构平衡，以便运动员更好地做好准备。这会创建更大的练习清单，并与
不可预测的环境建立更直接的联系。 由于它能够承受更大程度的变化
，因此它成为不可预测环境的基础。我们希望在训练从开始到结束的过
程中减少限制。这将比相反更充分地转化为竞争。

非循环运动
比赛中的大动作模式范围 高约束到低约束训练 大运动量 对不可预
测环境的高需求 特定于随机，从可预测进展到不可预测 在三个运
动平面上进行训练，确保结构平衡和不可预测训练环境的 ROM。

当我们考虑生物力学进展时，对预期结果有清晰的认识对于成功至关
重要。 在团队环境中，您知道不同运动项目的要求是不同的。 我们知
道，传统动作模式的普遍发展是标准，但还不够广泛。 依靠对开放或
封闭环境的明显观察和了解对于取得正确的进展至关重要。

生物运动能力
力、速度和功是我们将讨论的生物运动能力。 换句话说，我们可以走
多重，可以走多快，或者可以走多长时间？通过盘点某人的表现，将其
提炼成关键渠道并决定专注于一个领域而不是另一个领域。

Cyclic Sports Versus Acyclic Sports
As described with cyclic versus acyclic sports, there is a pretty clear outcome
from a biomechanical perspective. The same could be said for biomotor
abilities. We know that a cyclic endurance sport needs work as its primary
input. We know that for cyclic sprinters, velocity and possibly force (relative
to one’s body weight) are critical. This is not as easy to say about acyclic
sports.
How do we determine where to start? The easiest way is to determine
what is needed. This goes into the foundation of progressions: Are we
developing weaknesses into strengths or moving toward a sports-specific
outlet? With cyclic sports, it’s pretty straightforward to develop a plan that
focuses directly on sports specificity. However, with acyclic sports,
developing a plan for fixing weaknesses may be more necessary.
Cyclic sports—biomotor progression to sportspecific outcomes
Acyclic sports—biomotor progression working
from weakness to strength
Charles Poliquin (2013) said that if you want to know where to start, focus
on strength ratios, for instance, a ratio of snatch to clean in weightlifting. If
the athlete’s snatch is less than 85% of their clean max, they need to work on
speed. If their snatch is greater than 85% of their clean max, they need to
work on strength (figure 5.5). The point is to determine where they are less
developed and create a plan that accommodates that inherent weakness. The
weakness or strength is determined by comparing relatively common
movement patterns that require a more direct biomotor ability, such as force
or velocity.
The dynamic strength index is a metric that compares countermovement
jump to isometric mid-thigh pull to determine training needs. It uses a model
that looks at how much force an athlete produces and the rate of peak force to
determine whether to focus on developing maximal strength or ballistic

循环运动与非循环运动
正如循环运动与非循环运动所描述的那样，从生物力学的角度来看，有
一个非常明显的结果。 对于生物运动能力来说也是如此。 我们知道循
环耐力运动需要工作作为其主要投入。我们知道，对于循环短跑运动员
来说，速度和可能的力量（相对于体重）至关重要。 对于非循环运动
来说，这并不容易说。
我们如何确定从哪里开始？ 最简单的方法是确定需要什么。 这涉及
到进步的基础：我们是将弱点转化为优势还是朝着特定运动的方向发展
？ 对于循环运动，制定直接关注运动专项性的计划非常简单。 然而，
对于非循环运动，制定解决弱点的计划可能更为必要。

循环运动——生物运动进展到运动特定结果
非循环运动——从弱到强的生物运动进展

Charles Poliquin（2013）表示，如果你想知道从哪里开始，请关注力
量比，例如举重中抓举与翻举的比例。 如果运动员的抓举成绩低于其
翻举最大值的 85%，他们就需要提高速度。 如果他们的抓举超过其翻
举最大值的 85%，他们就需要加强力量训练（图 5.5）。 关键是要确定
它们在哪些方面欠发达，并制定一个计划来弥补这些固有的弱点。 通
过比较需要更直接的生物运动能力（例如力或速度）的相对常见的运动
模式来确定弱点或力量。
动态力量指数是一种将反向运动跳跃与等长大腿中部拉力进行比较以
确定训练需求的指标。它使用一个模型来观察运动员产生的力量和峰值
力量的速率，以确定是否专注于发展最大力量或弹道

strength (Suchomel et al., 2020). If the athlete is at a certain ratio that
demonstrates they are not producing enough force, increase focus on
maximal strength. If the athlete demonstrates they are not producing force at
a fast enough rate, focus on ballistic strength.
The goal of DSI is to compare how much force an athlete can make
compared to the rate of force created in two tests. One test is more ballistic
(countermovement jump), the other static. From that, we can create a forcevelocity profile. A ratio below 0.6 would mean that the athlete is not as
effective ballistically and needs more plyometric and a high rate of forcedevelopment exercises (Suchomel et al., 2020). A ratio above 0.8 would
mean the athlete is not as good at producing force in general and needs to
focus more on relative strength (Suchomel, 2020).

This breakdown consists of three key biomotor progressions: simple
before complicated and complex, light before heavy, and slow before fast.
That’s it! As you look at your program, with this projection from start to
finish, developing it is relatively straightforward in logic. The challenge is
how to implement it.

强度（Suchomel 等人，2020）。 如果运动员的某个比例表明他们没有

以足够快的速度产生力量，请关注弹道力量。
DSI 的目标是比较运动员可以产生的力量与两次测试中产生的力量的

Novice Versus Advanced Athletes
One area we haven’t discussed regarding biomechanics is novice versus
advanced athletes, which is not very relevant to the form of progression we
have discussed. It is, however, very relevant to biomotor abilities. Novice
athletes develop faster but need slower progressions. Advanced athletes
develop more slowly but need faster progressions. This may sound
counterintuitive, but as you will see, it matters a great deal for organizing
training.
Novice athlete—faster
progressions

development,

slower

Advanced athlete—slower development, faster
progressions
As you break down your training, you will need to evaluate your
mesocycle length based on the training age. The mesocycle organization is by
far the most important variable for changing biomotor abilities. Novice
trainees can respond positively to similar stimuli for an extended period of 6
to 8 weeks. Advanced trainees respond positively to similar stimuli for a
shortened period of 2 to 4 weeks.
With novice trainees (figure 5.6), it is not as imperative to reach these
outlets of progressions of fast or low constraint. It is important to reach
heavy, relative to their start, within a training cycle. As they are developing
training habits, intent during exercise, and motor learning, the need to rush to
an outlet of speed or low constraint is not as important as reaching heavier
loads.
The biggest overreaction: You constantly need to
work toward some outcome regardless of the
situation.

新手与高级运动员
关于生物力学，我们还没有讨论的一个领域是新手与高级运动员，这与
我们讨论的进展形式不太相关。 然而，它与生物运动能力非常相关。
新手运动员发展得更快，但需要更慢的进步。 高级运动员的发展速度
较慢，但需要更快的进步。 这听起来可能违反直觉，但正如您将看到
的，这对于组织培训非常重要。

新手运动员——发展更快，进步更慢
高级运动员——发展较慢，进步较快

当您分解训练时，您需要根据训练年龄评估中周期长度。中周期组织
是迄今为止改变生物运动能力的最重要变量。 新手学员可以在 6 至 8
周的较长时间内对类似刺激做出积极反应。 高级学员在 2 至 4 周的较
短时间内对类似刺激做出积极反应。
对于新手学员（图 5.6），到达这些快速或低约束进展的出口并不是
那么必要。 在一个训练周期内达到相对于起始重量的重量非常重要。
当他们正在养成训练习惯、锻炼时的意图和运动学习时，冲向速度或低
约束的出口的需要并不像达到更重的负荷那么重要。

最大的过度反应：无论情况如何，你都需要不断地努力
争取某个结果。

Team sports are complex environments. Ego, validation, and camaraderie
are factors that determine the value the athlete feels from their training. Early
on, as they are assimilating into a new environment, like school or joining a
professional organization, they will lack confidence. Getting small wins is
huge. Quite frankly, it is easier to get stronger early in training. It is better to
place your athletes in situations with high velocity, low constraint, or both. It
is easier and more necessary to develop force with novices. Getting small
wins is imperative to building long-term connections with your athletes.
It is also very connected to the development of other qualities. The idea
that strength is the mother of qualities is situationally dependent but holds
weight early with novice trainees. Developing force for someone with little
exposure to training will have huge value from increasing both velocity and
work without even focusing directly on it (see figure 3.4 on page 42). There
will be a point of diminishing returns, but that’s when to progress to the
advanced training stage.
With advanced trainees (figure 5.7), we have to progress faster and get to
high-velocity (or power) or low-constraint environments. This is where
having shorter mesocycles comes in. We progress from one mesocycle to the
next, focusing on developing baseline qualities and getting to the most
specific outlet possible. They have more experience, and we have a greater
understanding of their strengths and weaknesses. Developing weakness into
strength with acyclic sports manifests in sports performance.

团队运动是复杂的环境。自我、认可和友情是决定运动员从训练中感
受到的价值的因素。早期，当他们融入新环境，如学校或加入专业组织
时，他们会缺乏信心。 获得小胜利是巨大的。坦白说，在训练初期更
容易变得更强。最好将运动员置于高速、低约束或两者兼而有之的环境
中。和新手一起发力更容易，也更有必要。 获得小胜利对于与运动员
建立长期联系至关重要。
它也与其他品质的发展密切相关。 力量是素质之母的观点取决于具
体情况，但很早就对新手学员产生了影响。 对于很少接受训练的人来
说，通过提高速度和工作量来发展力量将具有巨大的价值，甚至无需直
接关注它（参见第 42 页的图 3.4）。 会有一个收益递减点，但那就是
进入高级训练阶段的时候。
对于高级学员（图 5.7），我们必须进步得更快，并进入高速（或功
率）或低约束环境。 这就是较短的中周期的用武之地。我们从一个中
周期进展到下一个中周期，专注于开发基线质量并尽可能达到最具体的
出路。 他们有更多的经验，我们也更了解他们的优势和劣势。 通过非
循环运动将弱点转化为力量体现在运动表现上。

Advanced training age allows for faster progressions because there is a
built-in motor pattern, more awareness of training loads, and better training
habits. We can spend less time on particular things because we adapt faster.
We exchange slower rates of progression with faster changes in mesocycles.
The biggest misconception: Having a single
program in a group is the only way to be
successful.

multiple programs going on simultaneously, but if you can figure out the
logistics, you can create a more robust program for each of your athletes. We
always program to the lowest common denominator, which is the novice
trainee. We can create a program that is too much for them, or we can create
a program that is too little for the advanced athletes.
As we are developing force, velocity, or work, we need to consider what it
is relative to. Acyclic sports make it a lot harder to determine what is needed.

We tend to overly apply what is needed for cyclic sports, with their linear
vector to a specific outcome, to acyclic training. We can infer this from the
relative impact of track and field, weightlifting, and powerlifting on training.
Recall that with biomechanical progressions, we go from general to specific,
where general could be directly developing an undeveloped need or building
capacity to perform more specific work.

Screening for Multilevel Programs in a Team
Environment
I think a multilevel program within a singular team is a must.
There is simply too much variance between rookies or freshmen
and veterans or seniors not to have multiple programs going on
simultaneously. With that said, it is not an easy process. I have
attempted this at multiple schools and in multiple settings, and
you have an uphill battle ahead of you. The more important
component is that you have the benefit of logic and reason, so
you need to use it.
The first thing you will learn is you are unintentionally making
silos within your program. Having a certain group of people doing
one program and another group doing a separate program will
create a feeling that one group is getting the good program, and
the other is not. The perception will always be that one is better
than the other. This is not unlike a control group versus a
placebo group in research.
Combating that feeling always comes down to clear and
objective criteria for determining programming. Human nature in
both the coach and the athlete will result in their feeling that
subjectivity is involved with decision-making regarding who goes
in what group. Your job as a coach is to create an environment
where people understand and agree that the decisions are in the
best interest of the athlete’s development and safety. Having a
dialed-in screen makes all the difference for this to happen.
We are essentially creating rules for a game. Biomechanics

我们倾向于过度地将循环运动所需的东西（其线性向量与特定结果）应
用于非循环训练。 我们可以从田径、举重和举重对训练的相对影响来
推断这一点。回想一下，随着生物力学的进步，我们从一般到具体，一
般可以直接开发未开发的需求或建立执行更具体工作的能力。

在团队环境中筛选多层次计划
我认为单一团队内的多层次计划是必须的。菜鸟或新生与退伍军
人或高年级学生之间的差异太大，不能同时进行多个项目。 话虽
如此，这并不是一个容易的过程。 我已经在多所学校和多种环境
中尝试过这一点，而你面前有一场艰苦的战斗。 更重要的是你有
逻辑和推理的好处，所以你需要使用它。

您将学到的第一件事是您无意中在程序中造成了孤岛。让某一
组人执行一个程序，另一组人执行另一个程序，会产生一种感觉
，即一组人得到了好的程序，而另一组则没有。 人们总是认为一
个人比另一个人更好。 这与研究中的对照组与安慰剂组没有什么
不同。
与这种感觉作斗争总是归结为确定编程的明确和客观的标准。
教练和运动员的人性都会导致他们感觉主观性参与了关于谁进入
哪个组的决策。 作为教练，你的工作是创造一个环境，让人们理
解并同意所做的决定符合运动员的发展和安全的最佳利益。 拥有
拨入屏幕使这一切的发生变得不同。

我们本质上是在为游戏制定规则。 生物力学

and physiology are the primary diagnostic criteria for determining
what program is best. Your goal is to rely on objective criteria,
and your best way to do that is to remove human error as much
as possible. This is where hardware and software come into
play. You need to have as much data not influenced by humans
as possible. How much force on a force plate, how fast in a
timing gate, how much strength on a dynamometer, how much
body fat on a DEXA … are all better than “I think you are ready.”
It is a good goal to have a comprehensive program that
serves several ages and abilities simultaneously. It can be a
difference maker if you are good at executing this. However, you
can destroy morale and compliance if you do not have clear
criteria for establishing who is in what program and why they are
in that program.
Logistics aside, if you can figure out how to implement multiple programs
simultaneously, it will help you tremendously. Trust and autonomy with
athletes are hard for strength coaches. This is not meant to be critical, just a
matter of where a coach feels they can bring the most value. Having a
program that looks like chaos in the weight room is not great for your
perceived value from your superiors.
However, having multiple programs going on simultaneously is not a dayone venture. When you start a program with a new team, you have to
perceive everyone as a novice. This program will be a slower, progressionbased, 6-to-8-week program. From a training expectations standpoint, it is
better to be successful at limited things as opposed to multiple things. As you
progress with your team, you expand and increase the bandwidth of your
program.

Bioenergetics
We are in a golden era of progressing bioenergetics in the team setting. We
have more peer-reviewed objective and subjective data than we have ever had
in our profession. We have options with little to no budget and options with

这就是硬件和软件发挥作用的地方。您需要拥有尽可能多的不受

生物能量学
我们正处于团队环境中生物能量学进步的黄金时代。 我们拥有的经过
同行评审的客观和主观数据比我们行业中任何时候都多。 我们有几乎
没有预算的选择，也有

unlimited budgets. If you ever wanted to create a plan to increase
bioenergetic output, there is no better time to do so.
Let’s start again with cyclic versus acyclic sports. What is nice about
cyclic sports is that we know how long someone needs to go beforehand.
From this, we can develop a reverse-engineered plan to reach that outcome
most efficiently. There has been some controversy in the past 50 years about
“developing a base” versus “train slow, be slow.” As we have learned, it is
not this binary classification of sprinters only sprinting and distance runners
only going super long. The limiting factor might not be how long or how fast,
but how we allocate stress that is stimulated through training to run faster or
longer.
Compare that to football and collect GPS reports. We know that practice
planning can result in thousands of yards accumulated over a practice. I’ve
experienced athletes accumulating 7,000 to 8,000 yd (6,401-7,315 m) during
practice. As we break down training to prepare for that, we have to be honest:
They are distance athletes as much as they are sprint athletes, by that logic.
The only difference between them and distance athletes is that they
sometimes have to run fast. We have seen this in all sports, with the
distribution of walking, jogging, running, and sprinting during soccer or
lacrosse being heavily skewed toward walking, jogging, and running with
limited sprinting. If you look at the bioenergetic prescriptions for football
versus soccer, which surprisingly share many similarities, they look
drastically different.

Quality Development
So what does this mean for preparation? We have to develop whatever
energy system the sport is primarily driven by to improve absolute ability or
power. We want to express how long they need to go during a play or
sequence as fast as possible. If they need to go 5 yd (4.6 m) or 50 yd (46 m),
it will need to be done as fast as possible. However, they need to recover
rapidly to repeat that speed. Again, how do we prepare for that?
As we break down cyclic versus acyclic sports, we have to appreciate the
fact that power versus capacity holds drastically different values per sport.
The nice thing about athletes in cyclic sports is that we can reach absolute

品质发展
那么这对于准备来说意味着什么呢？ 我们必须开发这项运动主要驱动
的能量系统，以提高绝对能力或力量。 我们想要尽可能快地表达他们
在一场比赛或一场比赛中需要花多长时间。如果他们需要移动 5 码（4.6
m）或 50 码（46 m），则需要尽快完成。 然而，他们需要迅速恢复才
能重复这个速度。再说一遍，我们如何为此做好准备？
当我们分解循环运动和非循环运动时，我们必须认识到这样一个事实
：每种运动的力量与能力有着截然不同的价值。循环运动中运动员的好
处是我们可以达到绝对的水平

power with them to perform at the highest level. It is pretty simple to develop
power when we know they need to run 100 m versus 5,000 m.
Comparatively, acyclic sports athletes need power in multiple distances and
directions to perform at their highest levels. The unpredictability of acyclic
sports makes energy system prescription much more difficult. We do know
one thing: Regardless of the distance or direction, the ability to recover
between bouts is what ultimately determines success.
The ability to repeat efforts is more important than a single maximal effort
for team sports. Not that we do not want to be able to produce high amounts
of velocity, power, or force in a single effort, we just need to be able to repeat
that frequently. Alternatively, with cyclic activities, we need to accumulate
more volume throughout training, which will be the product of that athlete’s
capacity. The rate-limiting step to developing power is how much volume,
distance, or duration at maximal intensity an athlete can accrue. If the
capacity of their energy system limits them, it will limit total volume,
distance, or duration, and subsequently, power.
How do we do this? To progress most efficiently, we can explore two
models: mesocycle and microcycle periodization schemes (figure 5.8).
Starting with mesocycles, we can look at an undulating block versus a
conjugate block orientation. With an undulating block, we saturate that
mesocycle with a specific quality, such as force, velocity, or work. With a
conjugate block, we mix training throughout each training session to
accommodate each quality of force, velocity, and work.
In terms of microcycle organization, a large part of that is determined by
the mesocycle approach. The undulating block approach can only
accommodate a certain number of high-threshold or high central nervous
system (CNS) intensive days within a microcycle. We therefore need to
accommodate that frequency with a lower threshold or low CNS days.
Alternatively, with the conjugate block (figure 5.9), we have a mixed
approach every day and need to adjust exercise selection to fit within a
microcycle. For example, using an upper-lower split to fit within a weekly
format.

与他们一起发挥最高水平的力量。当我们知道他们需要跑 100 m 与 5,00
0 m 时，开发动力就非常简单了。相比之下，非周期性运动运动员需要
在多个距离和方向上提供力量才能发挥最高水平。 非循环运动的不可
预测性使得能量系统的处方变得更加困难。 我们确实知道一件事：无
论距离或方向如何，在比赛之间恢复的能力才是最终决定成功的因素。
对于团队运动来说，重复努力的能力比单次最大努力更重要。并不是
说我们不希望能够在一次努力中产生很高的速度、功率或力量，我们只

训练过程中积累更多的训练量，这将是运动员能力的产物。 发展力量
的速率限制步骤是运动员在最大强度下可以积累多少体积、距离或持续
时间。 如果他们的能量系统的容量限制了他们，就会限制总体积、距

应不同的力量、速度和做功质量。

A classic example used within both cyclic and acyclic sports is the highlow approach developed by Charlie Francis (2008). With this setup, we
simultaneously develop power and capacity. The idea is that we use capacity
to provide a lower CNS day following a high CNS day, where we work on
power. The interplay of both allows for higher quality and increased levels
toward the preseason. The most important aspect is that you build the yardage

For cyclic sports, the high-low approach allows for higher attainable levels
during the high days. As we are peaking with highly correlated exercises or
sport-specific activities, we build in low days to allow for recovery so we do
not overreach and burn out. We build capacity through the off-season to aid
in recovery during these periods.

Acute-to-Chronic Workloads
If you think about it, we are developing the capacity for singular efforts or to
reach higher levels of power, as well as increasing capacity, or repeatability,
for the specific energy system. With both cyclic and acyclic sports, we aim to
establish the capacity to reach higher levels. The general method to determine
whether we are prescribing the appropriate volume should be through acute
versus chronic workloads.

运动员将在季前赛期间进行低强度的积累，同时在高强度的日子里发展
速度、力量和力量的品质。

图 5.9 高-低与共轭周期化。
对于循环运动，高低方法可以在高强度的日子里达到更高的水平。
当我们通过高度相关的锻炼或特定运动活动达到顶峰时，我们会在低强
度的日子里进行锻炼，以便恢复，这样我们就不会过度劳累和精疲力尽
。 我们在淡季期间建立能力，以帮助这些时期的恢复。

急性至慢性工作负荷
如果你想一想，我们正在开发单一努力或达到更高功率水平的能力，以
及增加特定能源系统的容量或可重复性。通过循环和非循环运动，我们
的目标是建立达到更高水平的能力。确定我们是否规定了适当的训练量
的一般方法应该是通过急性与慢性工作负荷。

Fitness Development
No matter what the goal, no one will ever regret having better
fitness. Fitness is a loaded term, but simply put, it is the ability to
go faster for longer. Fitness can be classified as the ability to
deliver oxygen to peripheral tissues to perform tasks. Those
tasks are not exclusive to playing in a game; it is more
appropriate to discuss making it through practice, which is
traditionally longer, harder, and more taxing than games for the
collective team.
Oxygen and lactate are always present at the local muscular
level. We can manage this, which determines our ability to
execute certain tasks at certain durations or intensities. Ideally,
we want to go longer and faster for practice, which comes down
to managing our cardiorespiratory system.
Starting at the heart, we pump blood out of the left ventricle to
the arterial system. This oxygen-rich blood travels to the capillary
system to diffuse into the muscular tissue. As we perform more
work, our heart rate increases. This results in lower levels of
oxygen being delivered from the heart to the arterial system and
subsequently to the capillary system. The venous system returns
carbon dioxide, the byproduct of diffused oxygen, away from the
muscle to the heart. Oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange rates
have huge implications for the capacity of the system.
When we have less oxygen being delivered, we begin to
accumulate fatigue substrates. Hydrogen accumulates in the
cytosol of a cell, which leads to end products of glycolysis
converting glucose into lactic acid instead of acetyl-CoA. Less
acetyl-CoA means less ATP production from glucose due to not
being able to enter the mitochondria. Another fatigue byproduct
is circulating phosphates that have been cleaved from ATP to
produce ADP and AMP. Circulating phosphates are a valuable
indicator of fatigue and diminished capacity.
This means that we have to slow down to manage the fatigue

健身发展
无论目标是什么，没有人会后悔拥有更好的健康状况。健身是一
个内涵丰富的术语，但简单地说，它是跑得更快、跑得更远的能
力。 健康可以归类为向周围组织输送氧气以执行任务的能力。
这些任务并不只限于玩游戏。 讨论如何通过练习来实现这一目标
更为合适，传统上，练习比集体团队的比赛更长、更难、更费力
。
氧气和乳酸始终存在于局部肌肉水平。 我们可以对此进行管理
，这决定了我们在特定持续时间或强度下执行特定任务的能力。
理想情况下，我们希望练习时间更长、更快，这归根结底是管理
我们的心肺系统。
从心脏开始，我们将血液从左心室泵入动脉系统。这种富含氧
气的血液流向毛细血管系统并扩散到肌肉组织中。 当我们做更多
的工作时，我们的心率就会增加。 这导致从心脏输送到动脉系统
并随后输送到毛细血管系统的氧气水平较低。静脉系统将二氧化
碳（扩散氧气的副产品）从肌肉返回心脏。氧气和二氧化碳的交
换率对系统的容量有巨大的影响。

当输送的氧气较少时，我们就开始积累疲劳基质。 氢在细胞的
细胞质中积聚，导致糖酵解的终产物将葡萄糖转化为乳酸而不是
乙酰辅酶A。 由于无法进入线粒体，乙酰辅酶 A 较少意味着从葡
萄糖产生的 ATP 较少。 另一种疲劳副产品是循环磷酸盐，它们从
ATP 中裂解产生 ADP 和 AMP。 循环磷酸盐是疲劳和能力下降的
重要指标。

这意味着我们必须放慢速度来管理疲劳

substrates being built up. This, in turn, lowers our overall output.
The ability to repeat higher-intensity efforts will be the product of
our fitness levels, the ability to manage fatigue at a local level, or
the ability to deliver oxygen efficiently. This gives more and more
credence to markers such as V̇O2max, which is the maximum
rate of oxygen consumption attainable. This is the fundamental
aspect of repeated efforts; our fitness levels provide the
foundation for increased volumes of high-intensity efforts, which
has a significant effect on overall performance.
Athletes with higher V̇O2 max levels are more equipped to
handle higher volumes and higher frequencies of intensity
training for practice. This does not mean they will be faster, but
they will have more potential from training. That training will raise
the potential to benefit from practice. They can recover faster
intrarep, interrep, and from practice sessions. An athlete with
better fitness can withstand higher volumes during a practice
session. They will also be able to handle a higher frequency of
higher-intensity practices. This will ultimately translate to better
reaching higher specific performances or the ability to repeat
higher intensities during practice or competition.
Acute-to-chronic ratios are determined by a fractal of the rating of
perceived exertion (RPE) (see figure 4.8 on page 64) multiplied by minutes
of activity. For example, taking an RPE of 6 reported from a practice or lift of
90 min would be 540 AU (arbitrary units). This is a meaningless number
unless it is compared to something and evaluated concerning a general goal.
We are constantly moving toward increasing capacity for practice with
off-season training. For team sports, the highest workloads will be achieved
during the season. It is the longest, most intense, and most concentrated
practice plan throughout the entire year. We have to reverse-engineer
workloads from preseason through the off-season. This means we
systematically increase our acute workloads through the off-season to raise
our chronic workloads (figure 5.10) going into the season.

正在建造基板。这反过来又降低了我们的总体产出。重复更高强
度训练的能力将取决于我们的健康水平、局部疲劳管理能力或有
效输送氧气的能力。这使得 V̇O2max（可达到的最大耗氧率）等标
记越来越可信。 这是反复努力的根本； 我们的健身水平为增加
高强度训练量奠定了基础，这对整体表现有重大影响。

的练习强度训练。 这并不意味着他们会更快，但他们会从训练中

非将其与某些事物进行比较并根据总体目标进行评估。
我们正在不断努力通过休赛期训练来提高训练能力。 对于团队运动

Acute workloads are the sum of individual practice or lift workloads
during a microcycle or week. For example, taking a week of preseason, it
would be 6 × 120 min (720 AU) for 5 to 6 days of preseason practice, which
would make 3,600 to 4,320 AU. Reverse engineering the off-season would
need a systemic increase in acute workload each week until we hit that
number. Matching the time to preseason practice is the most challenging
aspect. This alters the workload from RPE, which is not multiplied by 120
min of practice but by 60 to 90 min of training. For example, this would be
what a summer program preparing for 4,000 AU could look like.
This is where we have an acute-to-chronic window of workloads to
determine whether we are progressing too fast or too slow. It is simply a 0.8
to 1.3 acute-to-chronic ratio (Gabbett, 2016). To simplify even further, we
can look at a chronic workload of 1,000 AU, and when we have an acute

training week of 2,000 AU, that would be two times too much on the system.
Alternatively, we could be at 500 AU of acute workload, and that would be
too little stimulus. We want to stay roughly between 800 and 1,300 AU of
acute workload to ensure we are stressing enough to prepare for the season
(figure 5.11).
The biggest overreactions with bioenergetics is
that we have to go at maximal speed to get faster.
Once you see how much training volume you will need, you will have a
new appreciation of capacity development. Nowhere in any prescription for
developing fitness is it dictated that you will give submaximal effort. Too
often, slow days or slowed-down repetitions are perceived as a waste of time.
The reality is that intent is a lot more important than the actual speed of the
movement.
We always want the most intensity, regardless of the speed, load, or
duration of any exercise. Intent comes in many forms. It could be great focus,
it could be maximal concentric speed, it could be staying engaged longer, or
it could be anything as long as we base it toward a larger goal, like preparing
for the season. The intent determines the intensity.
The biggest misconception with bioenergetics is
that if you train slowly, you will become slow.

可以保持更长时间的参与，或者它可以是任何东西，只要我们将其建立

适应窗口。

To the point of working on what is needed, we can readily shift focus from
velocity to force to work. Our movement rate based on external load or
duration will be significantly altered. The absolute speed at which we can
work is drastically different when we have to focus on other areas. This is
why intent is so much more important than absolute speed. It shifts the focus
toward quality and understanding of the assignment over any measurement.
Regardless of whether it’s a cyclic or acyclic activity, we want to increase
the relevant speed toward the activity, which can lead to the notion of just
always going fast. Obvious aspects aside, this is not the only determining
factor of success. The elephant in the room is that training will not adequately
prepare for preseason due to the length and frequency of practices compared
to training. We want to improve relevant speed, but not at the expense of
increasing risk during the highest workloads during the calendar year. Again,
this is where simply applying more intent to what you are doing can close the
gap in time and frequency between preseason and training.
In any system, there is always a bottleneck or an impediment to the system
being able to complete its task. For bioenergetics, developing power or
capacity is determined by the resilience and variability of the system. We can
only train as hard as we can recover from. Lack of variability or being able to
create energy from multiple sources is a bottleneck. Having increased risk
from not being able to adequately recover during or in between a set or
training session is a bottleneck. To develop speed, we will need to have the
resilience and the variability to work with larger workloads.
We need to acknowledge that high-constraint environments may be good
for more raw output but may not prepare athletes as effectively as lowconstraint environments. When we can more readily account for yardage or
change of directions from the predictability of the task, we can quantify the
impact on bioenergetic development. However, if we evaluate acute
workloads or even heart rate during activity, we can better evaluate the
amount of stress we are imposing. This is why it is so important to adopt
more measurements; it prevents us from arbitrarily using a certain method or
exercise due to having more control. We have to prepare for the needs of the
athlete or sport, not what we can say we control.

任务的可预测性来解释码数或方向的变化时，我们就可以量化对生物能
量发展的影响。 然而，如果我们评估活动期间的剧烈工作负荷甚至心
率，我们就可以更好地评估我们施加的压力大小。 这就是为什么采用
更多测量如此重要的原因；它可以防止我们因为拥有更多的控制权而随
意使用某种方法或练习。我们必须为运动员或运动项目的需求做好准备
，而不是我们可以说我们可以控制的东西。
随着生物能量的进步，我们需要为季前赛做好准备。我们

will need to systematically increase workloads from the beginning of the offseason to best prepare for the season. Power is the product of higher levels of
capacity. This is not the same as building a base but is building capacity
while developing power. Progression is a matter of increasing acute
workloads to reach the specific chronic workloads. Nothing in that
progression means not focusing on force or velocity; it is more of a matter of
increasing overall fitness and performance throughout the off-season.
The progression factors are summarized as follows:
Biomechanics
Biggest overreaction: Everything needs to have a definite beginning
and end to be effective.
Biggest misconception: Increased external load with reduced ROM is
more beneficial than reduced load with increased ROM.
Biomotor Abilities
Biggest overreaction: You constantly need to work toward some
outcome regardless of the situation.
Biggest misconception: Having a single program in a group is the only
way to be successful.
Bioenergetics
Biggest overreaction: We have to go at maximal speed to get faster.
Biggest misconception: If you train slowly, you will become slow.

Take Home
Progression is foundational to what we do as a profession. It could be as
simple as progressing from simple to complex. Or it could be as intricate as
progressing workloads within a specific window each week. Having a
mindset of progression with everything you do is paramount to off-season
success. Biomechanical, biomotor, and bioenergetic progressions are the keys
to preparing adequately during the year and from one year to the next.

从淡季开始就需要系统地增加工作量，为赛季做好最好的准备。力量是
更高水平能力的产物。 这与建设基地不同，而是在发展实力的同时建
设能力。 进展是增加急性工作负荷以达到特定的长期工作负荷的问题
。 在这个过程中，没有什么意味着不关注力或速度；这更重要的是在
整个休赛期提高整体健康和表现。

带回家
进步是我们职业的基础。 它可以像从简单到复杂一样简单。 或者它可
能像每周在特定窗口内处理工作负载一样复杂。 对所做的一切保持进
步的心态对于休赛期的成功至关重要。生物力学、生物运动和生物能量
进展是在这一年和下一年做好充分准备的关键。

REVERSIBILITY
When we think of the profession of strength and conditioning, we have to
appreciate that without the principle of reversibility, we would not exist.
There are a couple of moments that we can refer to in our chronology as to
how we established ourselves as a viable component to athlete development:
Bill Starr with the Colts and University of Hawaii, Boyd Epley with the
University of Nebraska, Arthur Jones and Kim Wood and high-intensity
training with several Big Ten and National Football League teams. These
inflection points of our industry made our profession what it is today: a yearround process that requires a full-time staff to oversee. There are more names
on this list, but we should at least know these in particular because they have
largely shaped how S&C professionals operate today.
Reversibility is the foundation of strength and
conditioning’s existence.
You have to imagine that at one point, training a football team in January
was not considered an option. The team was off until spring practice and then
off again until preseason. A massively misunderstood aspect of the yearround football schedule is that mat drills served as a preconditioning before
spring practice. It was assumed the team did very little before spring practice,
so establishing a period of conditioning going into spring practice was

6
可逆性
当我们想到体能训练这一职业时，我们必须认识到，如果没有可逆性原
则，我们就不会存在。在我们如何将自己打造为运动员发展的可行组成
部分方面，我们可以在年表中参考几个时刻：比尔·斯塔尔与小马队和夏
威夷大学的合作、博伊德·埃普利与内布拉斯加大学的合作、阿瑟·琼斯
和金·伍德的合作，以及与几支十大联盟球队和国家橄榄球联盟球队的高
强度训练。 我们行业的这些拐点造就了我们今天的职业：一个需要全
职员工监督的全年流程。这个名单上还有更多的名字，但我们至少应该
特别了解这些名字，因为他们在很大程度上塑造了施恩禧专业人士今天
的运作方式。

可逆性是力量和体能存在的基础。

你必须想象一下，在一月份训练一支足球队曾一度被认为是不可行的
。球队休息到春季训练，然后又休息到季前赛。 全年足球赛程中一个
被严重误解的方面是垫上训练是春季训练前的准备工作。人们认为球队
在春季训练前几乎没有做任何事情，因此在春季训练前安排一段时间的
训练是

necessary. The fact that mat drills still exist today is a symbol of how
relatively new our profession is.
Spring mat drills should be considered an antiquated approach to yearlong
development, but they precede most S&C departments, which is why they
still exist despite 6 to 8 weeks of winter training preceding mat drills. It took
a lot of convincing to say we need to have access to a football team in
January to get them prepared for August. We take for granted that having a
weight room, a staff, and huge amounts of resources are all recent evolutions
within the team setting. The reason this exists is because of easily understood
concepts, such as it is better to stay in shape than get in shape, or easy come,
easy go, or hard earned—hard lost. Reversibility is a principle that everyone
should readily understand and appreciate as the backbone of why we can do
what we do.
Principle of Reversibility: When a training stimulus is taken away from an
athlete for an extended period, they will not be able to maintain a certain
level of performance. Over time, the adaptations that were achieved will
return to the original level. (Sands et al., 2012, p. 9)

Do You Want to Train Every Day?
That was the question I got from a football coach during the
preseason, and I was a bit taken aback by the question. To be
honest, I was not expecting that at all and was not sure what to
say. So I said, “Absolutely.” Then the reality of that set in: What
the hell am I going to do with an entire team training 6 days a
week with 1 day off for an entire preseason?
It’s a crazy thought to have your team in every day for 28 to
32 days in the weight room. It almost feels like you are an
Eastern Bloc country at the peak of Communism fighting for
Olympic superiority. The hardest part is knowing what to do with
that time. My answer is to start at the end and work backward.
What do you want in the season? Can we get stronger? Can
we put on lean muscle mass? Can we preserve movement
quality or technique throughout the season? These are questions

必要的。 垫上练习至今仍然存在，这一事实象征着我们的职业相对较
新。
春季垫上训练应该被认为是一种过时的全年发展方法，但它们先于大
多数 S&C 部门，这就是为什么尽管垫上训练之前有 6 到 8 周的冬季训
练，但它们仍然存在。我们花了很多说服力才说我们需要在一月份接触
一支足球队，让他们为八月份做好准备。 我们理所当然地认为，拥有
举重室、员工和大量资源都是团队环境中最近的演变。存在这种情况的
原因是因为易于理解的概念，例如
it is better to stay in shape than get in shape、easy come,、easy go 或
hard earned—hard lost。可逆性是每个人都应该容易理解和欣赏的原则
，它是我们能够做我们所做的事情的支柱。

可逆性原理：当运动员长时间失去训练刺激时，他们将无法保持一定的表
现水平。 随着时间的推移，所实现的适应将恢复到原来的水平。 （Sand
s 等人，2012 年，第 9 页）

你想每天训练吗？
这是我在季前赛期间从一位足球教练那里得到的问题，这个问题
让我有点吃惊。 说实话，我根本没想到会这样，也不知道该说什
么。 所以我说：“当然。” 然后现实就出现了：整个球队每周
训练 6 天，整个季前赛休息 1 天，我到底该怎么办？
让你的团队每天都在举重室呆 28 到 32 天，这是一个疯狂的想
法。 几乎感觉就像是一个处于共产主义顶峰的东欧集团国家，正
在为奥运会的优势而战。最困难的部分是知道如何利用这段时间
。我的答案是从最后开始并向后推算。
这个季节你想要什么？ 我们能变得更强吗？ 我们可以增加瘦
肌肉质量吗？ 我们能否在整个赛季保持运动质量或技术？这些都
是问题

you ask going into a competitive season. All these questions will
have a significant impact on the direct performance during the
season and in the subsequent off-season. Those questions hold
the answer to what you do with 4 weeks straight of training every
day.
Starting at the end means thinking about certain movement
patterns, such as squat, hinge, lunge, push, and pull. If we can
preserve the pattern longer throughout the season, we can
increase outputs such as force, velocity, or power longer. It is
easier to get the output when we have more options, more
directly from our inputs. When we have access to higher
threshold strategies, our job becomes easier. Preserving barbell
movements, even at extremely low intensities, is a priority with
training every day.
Time spent in the weight room builds positive habits with
movement prep, periworkout nutrition, movement execution, and
variables (sets, reps, tempos, intensity), as well as being present
in the moment. We lose that with the loss of frequency. You do
not realize that when you do not have access to your athletes for
the entire preseason. That first lift after 4 weeks off is awful, and
it feels like you have lost everything you built in the off-season.
Maintaining these habits and creating mental conditioning to do
everything in the best possible way are imperative.
The rotation we used was lower 1, upper 1, lower 2, upper 2,
and regeneration. Each day had a primary pattern broken down
into lower 1: squat, upper 1: vertical pull, lower 2: hinge, and
upper 2: horizontal push. We opened every day with soft tissue,
flexibility, mobility, and corrective exercises, and empty barbell
patterning. We finished the day with supplemental work focused
on structural balance throughout the preseason. Regeneration
was soft tissue, flexibility, mobility, corrective exercises, lowintensity cardiorespiratory work, and breath work. Yes, we did
daily breath work with the football team!
We work backward from scrimmages by placing regeneration

work the day after. This would place a CNS (central nervous
system) day either on the day of or the day before to stress test
potentiation strategies around games. We often take for granted
that doing potentiation work feels counterintuitive to athletes.
Their default is to rest and mentally prepare. Doing velocity- and
power-based work on game day is not something you can just
do. Preseason daily workouts are a great way to stress test their
reaction to something like this.
I was fortunate enough to have training every day during
preseason for eight seasons. It became second nature over time.
Athletes, coaches, sports medicine, and strength coaches all
came to realize the residuals in the season were worth it alone.
The bigger play was that it was a great way to reset and
recalibrate for the day throughout camp. Athletes hydrate earlier,
move more, recover faster, lock in more during meetings, and
perform better for longer during practice.
What we have to establish in the team setting is that year-round
commitment to training, from early postseason through the entire competitive
season, is better than not training. Anyone who works with Olympic sports in
the college setting appreciates that it is not a guarantee that you will be able
to train your athletes throughout the year. Coaches will look at the weight
room as an impediment to the practice or skill work one could be doing. They
will gladly sacrifice time in the weight room to get them to rest, recuperate,
put time toward film review, practice more—pretty much anything but lift.
Your job as an S&C coach in that situation is to establish that reversibility is
a principle and needs to be acknowledged, or there will be performance and
resiliency issues.
We can leverage the fitness–fatigue model (covered in more detail in
chapter 11; of note, see figure 11.2 on page 182) and the general adaptation
syndrome right here. There are an incredible number of factors at play in
adaptation. The reverse of adaptation would be de-adaptation. The obvious
statement here is that if we want the outcomes from training, such as
increased force, velocity, or work, we need to train over a long time to get

年致力于训练，总比不训练好。任何在大学环境中从事奥林匹克运动工
作的人都会明白，这并不能保证你能够全年训练你的运动员。 教练会
将举重室视为练习或技能训练的障碍。他们会很乐意牺牲在举重室的时
间来休息、恢复体力、花时间复习电影、进行更多练习——几乎除了举

可逆性是一项原则，需要得到承认，否则就会出现性能和弹性问题。

我们可以在这里利用健身-疲劳模型（第 11 章中有更详细的介绍；值
得注意的是，请参见第 182 页的图 11.2）和一般适应综合症。 影响适
应的因素数量多得令人难以置信。 适应的逆过程是de-adaptation。 这
里显而易见的说法是，如果我们想要训练的结果，例如增加力量、速度
或做功，我们需要进行很长时间的训练才能获得

them. We cannot get the effects of training without prioritizing training. The
stress imposed on the system corresponds directly with adaptations gained
from that stress. What is most important is that there is only so much stress
one can incur at a given time, and we need to spread that out over a longer
period to accrue more. Cramming stress into a short period will not create
large residual effects. The concentric circle of ability will be small and will
rapidly diminish once we stop.
Looking down the road for the training effect, not only toward a goal but
also for the residual effect, we can prevent the rapid decay of training (figure
6.1). Greater levels reached in adaptation over a longer period result in
longer-lasting residual effects (Verkhoshansky, 2009). The entire premise of
saying to a coach or an athlete that we need to train as much as possible
between now and the start of the season is to have a longer residual and less
decay during the season. We want to follow up by saying that we want to
establish an in-season training regimen to decrease the decay and maintain or
possibly develop the qualities we worked so hard to obtain in the off-season.
Training adaptations are the capital we earn from the time spent during the
off-season. We work all off-season in the hope that we positively change
things when it matters: competition. We build both our progression and
progressive overload on the central theme of preparing for the season. Our
preparedness is based on the quality of progression and progressive overload
we have before a competition. But after that, what? Preseason is a stressor
that will have a large systemic impact on force, velocity, or work levels
obtained during the season. If our functional levels are not as developed as
they could have been prior to the season, we are at a larger deficit than if we
trained more or started earlier in the off-season.

训练适应是我们从休赛期花费的时间中赚取的资本。 我们整个休赛
期都在努力工作，希望能够在重要的时候积极改变事情：竞争。 我们
以备战赛季为中心主题，构建进步和渐进超负荷。 我们的准备工作基
于比赛前的进展质量和渐进超负荷。 但在那之后呢？ 季前赛是一种压
力源，会对赛季期间获得的力量、速度或工作水平产生巨大的系统性影
响。 如果我们的功能水平没有像赛季前那样发达，那么我们的赤字比
我们在休赛期进行更多训练或更早开始时要大。

Reversibility plays out in the preseason, changes in schedules, coaches not
believing in training, athletes skipping training, or injuries. These
interruptions in training are where the principle of reversibility becomes
important. During the season, we need to take a hiatus from training and still
capitalize on the qualities we have developed during the off-season. We want
to build a plan to handle an inevitable break in training. We can look at it as
cushioning for training interruptions. At its core, the long-term training
approach is preparation to handle the inevitable decreased commitment to
training.
As discussed with the progression principle, we worked hard over the offseason to develop a higher chronic workload capacity. That is our overall
adaptive response to stress incurred during the off-season. Whether we want
it or not, the preseason workload will be what it is, which is higher than we
can probably prepare for. But that is our job, and we have to prepare for it as
much as possible. Our ability to build up functional workloads toward that
goal is central to handling the stress of the season, but more importantly, the
ability to preserve that capacity as long as possible during the season. In-

在赛季期间，我们需要暂停训练，并继续利用我们在休赛期培养的素质

season is where training adaptations count.
We know that when athletes participate in off-season training, they react
better to future stressors in season (Chou et al., 2021). Stress is stress,
whether it is in the form of training, technique, tactics, or psychology. A
long-term approach to training helps prepare our athletes to handle higher
stress periods more effectively. Preseason, in-season, and postseason are all
higher-stress environments. We can make this assertion by the inflection
point of stress and adaptation levels through rates of acute illness or injury.
Both are the intersection of stress imposed and the adaptation level’s ability
to handle it (figure 6.2).

Rating of Perceived Exertion and Progressive
Overload
I have found that the rating of perceived exertion (RPE) is a
great mechanism to regulate progressive overload. Traditionally,
RPE is used for establishing workloads from training sessions’
microcycles, but it also establishes context for weekly changes in
intensity.
We have all faced this question, “What weight should I use?”
Early in a mesocycle, it is an educated guess. In the following
weeks, we should have a much more dialed-in answer for weight
to use. A more accurate weight selection is based on gathering
information from previous experience.
When an athlete asks that question, my first response is,
“How hard was last week?” This will be met with “I don’t
remember,” which creates a teachable moment with your athlete.
Your athletes should be engaged with what they are doing each
week. Having an understanding of how hard the last workout
was is the first and most important aspect of what we can do in
the future.
Depending on how hard the last training session was, the
jump from one week to the next can be smaller or larger. It
should make sense to make a larger jump if the workout was

我们知道，当运动员参加休赛期训练时，他们对赛季中未来的压力源
的反应会更好（Chou et al., 2021）。 压力就是压力，无论是训练、技
术、战术还是心理方面的压力。 长期的训练方法有助于我们的运动员
做好准备，更有效地应对更高的压力时期。 季前赛、赛季中和季后赛
都是压力较大的环境。 我们可以通过急性疾病或伤害发生率的压力和
适应水平的拐点来做出这一断言。两者都是施加的压力和适应水平处理
压力的能力的交集（图 6.2）。

感知用力和渐进性超负荷的评级
我发现感知用力等级（RPE）是调节渐进性超负荷的一个很好的机
制。传统上，RPE 用于根据培训课程的微周期确定工作量，但它
也为每周强度变化建立背景。
我们都曾面临过这样的问题：“我应该使用什么重量？”在中
周期早期，这是一个有根据的猜测。 在接下来的几周内，我们应
该会对使用的重量有一个更加明确的答案。 更准确的重量选择基
于从以前的经验中收集信息。
当运动员问这个问题时，我的第一反应是：“上周有多难？”
这会遇到“我不记得了”，这为你的运动员创造了一个受教的时
刻。您的运动员应该专注于他们每周所做的事情。 了解上次锻炼
的难度是我们未来可以做的第一个也是最重要的方面。

根据上一次训练的难度，从一周到下一周的跳跃可能会更小或
更大。 如果锻炼是这样的话，进行更大的跳跃应该是有意义的

easy or there was limited fatigue or delayed onset muscle
soreness in the following days. Harder training sessions, barring
all reps being hit, require a smaller jump. Missing reps would
mean we have to go at a lighter weight to hit all reps and build
from that going forward.
Basing your next week’s training intensity on RPE will create
more meaning for RPE. Asking an athlete to fill out a posttraining
session RPE can be challenging over time. If the athlete can
instinctually see the benefit of keeping track of how hard a
training session was, it makes a huge difference in tracking.
A model that we can reference to understand the timing of training stress
with scheduled breaks toward adaptation is tapering. The tapering model
suggests that rest is the key to unlocking the value of previously done work.
This model focuses on how much stress is needed to be expressed through
aggregates of total distance, various intensity distances and durations, weight
room volume, weight room tonnage (volume × intensity), or general and
specific preparation. Based on the focal point of development toward these
aggregates, there will need to be a corresponding drop in volume or intensity,
or both, to allow for supercompensation.
Tapers come in all shapes and sizes (figure 6.3). There are global tapers of
dropping volume and intensity to peak. Some tapers just focus on a singular
quality of dropping volume or intensity. There is a step taper where we
alternate drops in volume and intensity. There is the classic “take a week off”
taper before preseason (Mujika, 2009). A wide range of variables influences
why a certain taper may be more useful than others. Another method would
be intramesocycle tapers, referred to as deload microcycles. Deload weeks
also drop volume or intensity, or both, to allow for continued progress during
a macrocycle.

在接下来的几天里，很容易出现疲劳，或者出现有限的疲劳或延
迟出现的肌肉酸痛。更艰苦的训练，除非所有次数都被击中，需
要较小的跳跃。 缺少次数意味着我们必须以更轻的重量来完成所
有次数，并以此为基础继续前进。
将下周的训练强度基于 RPE 将为 RPE 创造更多意义。随着时间
的推移，要求运动员填写训练后 RPE 可能会具有挑战性。 如果运
动员能够本能地看到跟踪训练的难度的好处，那么跟踪就会产生
巨大的差异。

我们可以参考一个模型来了解训练压力的时间安排以及为适应而安排
的休息时间，该模型正在逐渐减少。 逐渐减少模型表明，休息是释放
之前完成的工作价值的关键。该模型重点关注需要通过总距离、各种强
度距离和持续时间、举重室体积、举重室吨位（体积×强度）或一般和
特定准备的聚合来表达多少压力。 根据这些总量的发展重点，需要在
数量或强度或两者上有相应的下降，以实现超级补偿。

锥体有各种形状和尺寸（图 6.3）。全球范围内，交易量和强度都在
逐渐下降至峰值。 有些锥度训练只专注于降低音量或强度的单一品质
。 有一个渐进的过程，我们交替降低音量和强度。季前赛前有一个经
典的“休息一周”的方法（Mujika，2009）。 多种变量会影响为什么
某种锥度可能比其他锥度更有用。 另一种方法是中周期内渐缩，称为
deload microcycles。 减负荷周还会降低训练量或强度，或两者兼而有
之，以允许在宏观周期期间持续取得进展。

FIGURE 6.2 Adaptation percent.
We often see deload weeks play out with off-season work in the team
setting by scheduling time off. In college athletics, there are scheduled
discretionary weeks when nonvoluntary preparation is turned into voluntary,
and athletes cannot be coached directly. Some athletes opt to do nothing;
others may do something. The rate and amount of training decay during these
periods are predicated on the preceding volume and intensity during training.
If the levels were intentionally overreaching or exceeding the athletes’ ability
to directly recover during the mesocycle, it may be beneficial to take the
week off entirely. If the athlete was working submaximally in volume and
intensity, taking the week off could actually be counterproductive. In this
situation, prescribing reduced intensity or volume would be useful during
discretionary periods.
