于之前训练期间的训练量和强度。如果这些水平故意超出或超过运动员
在中周期期间直接恢复的能力，那么完全休息一周可能是有益的。 如
果运动员的训练量和强度都低于最大水平，那么休息一周实际上可能会
适得其反。 在这种情况下，在酌情期间减少强度或训练量会很有用。

训练停止后的一段时间应该得到积极的适应。 它

should make no difference if there was an abrupt stoppage or a gradual taper.
When training stops, there should be an uptick in adaptations from stressed
qualities such as force, velocity, or work. What does it say when you do not
improve? It most certainly does not say that a training program was effective
in preparing for the inevitable stoppage. It more than likely means that the
program was either too much or too little stress. We can refer back to the
acute-to-chronic window of 0.8 to 1.3 workload progression week to week
(Gabbett, 2016). If we work well above 1.3 for the preceding microcycles, we
should see an immediate improvement from resting. If we work from 1.0 to
1.3, we should still see improvement from the stoppage in training. If the
workloads were below 1.0 for the preceding microcycles, it may lead to an
uptick in performance and a drop in force, velocity, or work.

FIGURE 6.3 Tapering.
Depending on the length of the off-season, there should have been some
indications as to when the stoppage occurred, which are either positive or
negative. We see this impact during deload weeks as microtapering tests. At
the end of a deload microcycle, we should see the supercompensation effect
occur (Verkhoshansky, 2009). If not, we go back to the drawing board. We
get better at selecting more appropriate volumes and intensities to maximize

、速度或工作等压力品质的适应应该会有所增加。当你没有进步时，它

逐渐变细。

根据休赛期的长度，应该有一些关于何时发生停赛的迹象，这些迹象
要么是积极的，要么是消极的。我们将减载周期间的这种影响视为微锥
化测试。在减载微循环结束时，我们应该看到超级补偿效应发生（Verk
hoshansky，2009）。 如果没有，我们就回到绘图板。 我们能够更好地
选择更合适的训练量和强度来最大化

return as well as endure anything, including stoppages, that may come. If we
do not see improvement following a taper, that probably means we did not
accumulate enough stress during the preceding training.
Longer training periods garner longer residuals (Verkhoshansky, 2009).
There will be a longer window to work within if the training period is longer.
This is a central tenet of an off-season training program having longer
residuals during a competitive season. With that said, we can more clearly see
the effectiveness of the plan. Short off-seasons are inevitable and usually
require more aggressive tactics. More aggressive tactics on abbreviated
timelines leave less time to evaluate whether the training stoppage will lead
to a positive adaptation. It will also not show that if the stoppage were to
continue, there would be enough adaptation to make it through (figure 6.4).
What we can control regardless of off-season length are training variables:
frequency, volume, intensity, density, and quality. What we have to look at is
the functional level of the athlete entering preseason, which is the aggregate
of all stress imposed before whatever happens next: stoppage, preseason, inseason, or postseason. This could be the aggregate of a long off-season with
high frequency, volume, intensity, density, and quality. Or it could be the
complete opposite: a short off-season with low frequency, volume, intensity,
density, and quality. The residuals, or the ability to handle future stress, will
be much higher from long off-seasons with high frequency than from short
off-seasons with low frequency.
Adjusting the variables affects the training residuals for force, velocity,
and work. Each of these qualities will respond differently to adjusting those
variables. We need to account for that based on the time allotted in the offseason and the future time we will have in the season. We have to look at
reversibility through the lens of in-season training, which is the period with
the highest potential for decay of force, velocity, or work.

返回并忍受可能发生的任何事情，包括停工。如果我们在逐渐减量后没
有看到改善，这可能意味着我们在之前的训练中没有积累足够的压力。
训练时间越长，残差就越长（Verkhoshansky，2009）。如果培训时
间较长，工作窗口就会更长。这是休赛期训练计划的核心原则，在竞技
赛季中具有更长的剩余时间。至此，我们可以更清楚地看到该计划的有
效性。 短暂的休赛期是不可避免的，通常需要更具侵略性的战术。 在
缩短的时间内采取更激进的策略，会导致评估停止训练是否会带来积极
适应的时间更少。 它也不会表明，如果停工继续下去，将有足够的适
应来完成（图 6.4）。
无论淡季时间长短，我们可以控制的是训练变量：频率、训练量、强
度、密度和质量。我们必须关注的是进入季前赛的运动员的功能水平，
这是在接下来发生的事情之前施加的所有压力的总和：停赛、季前赛、
赛季中或季后赛。 这可能是一个长期休赛期的高频率、高数量、高强
度、高密度和高质量的总和。 或者情况可能完全相反：短暂的淡季，
频率、数量、强度、密度和质量都较低。长休赛期、高频率的残差或处
理未来压力的能力将比短休赛期、低频率的要高得多。

调整变量会影响力、速度和功的训练残差。 这些品质中的每一个都
会对调整这些变量做出不同的反应。 我们需要根据休赛期分配的时间
和赛季中未来的时间来考虑这一点。 我们必须从赛季中训练的角度来
看待可逆性，这是力量、速度或做功衰减可能性最大的时期。

FIGURE 6.4 Percentile change.
Let’s break down force, velocity, and work regarding the principle of
reversibility.

Force
Strength is the mother of all qualities. You may have heard this before; it is
a great thought. It makes the world around us easier to understand.
Unfortunately, the human body is a lot more complex than that. When
combined with performance within chaotic environments, saying something
as convenient as exclusively getting someone strong is hard to justify.
Looking back over progression and progressive overload, we do want to
get stronger. That is a given. But stronger is a context-dependent term.
Stronger means positively adapting to said stress. Stronger is relative to what
we choose from a programming perspective. Stronger means better.
Improving force is on the short list you want to start with when looking to
develop an athlete, but keep in mind that the list is more robust than just one
quality.

图 6.4 百分位变化。
让我们根据可逆性原理来分解力、速度和功。

力量
力量是一切品质之母。你可能以前听过这个；这是一个伟大的想法。
它使我们周围的世界更容易理解。不幸的是，人体比这复杂得多。 当
与混乱环境中的表现结合起来时，说像专门让某人变得强大这样方便的
话很难证明是合理的。
回顾进步和渐进式超负荷，我们确实希望变得更强。 这是既定的。
但 stronger 是一个依赖于上下文的术语。更强意味着积极适应所述压力
。更强是相对于我们从编程角度选择的。 更强意味着更好。当你寻求
培养一名运动员时，提高力量是你想要开始的候选清单中的一个，但请
记住，这个清单不仅仅是一种品质。

Increased force comes from a multitude of sources. Motor unit
coordination is a big one. The simple act of being able to recruit the right
muscle fibers from better motor unit coordination is valuable toward
increasing force. The rate and amount of motor unit recruitment are clear
factors behind improving force. Speeding up the recruitment of type II
muscle fibers to meet the task’s demands more effectively is strongly
correlated with increasing force. Force comes mainly from increasing the
neural aspect of a contraction.
Although it could be considered an outcome, increased cross-sectional
muscle area (CSA) is extremely important to increasing force. The bottom
line is that increased CSA means we have the machinery and contractile
tissue to generate force. More muscle, more sarcomeres, and increased force.
This is a critical aspect because a loss of CSA means we lose forcegenerating capacity. With this in mind, we have to consider the decay rate
and amount and the reversibility of muscle mass in relation to force.

In-Season Force Decay
We have to understand how to increase force before we can understand how
to preserve it. Increasing force is a product of practice and repetition; it is
therefore a skill. Like any skill, preserving it, just as increasing it, is the
product of practice and repetition. If you were looking for any reason to
continue with strength training during the preseason, in-season, and
postseason, it is because strength is a skill. A large part of that is connected to
neural aspects of contraction. That neural aspect is skill, and skill is
maintained by continued practice and repetition.
Cross-sectional muscle area is a diagnostic tool to assess if we are losing
one connection to maintain force during periods when we cannot maintain as
much frequency or use as much volume. Loss of muscle mass in the season
clearly indicates force production loss. We can use that as a diagnostic at all
parts of the year to assess both the level of development and the potential loss
of that development. More so than a more neurally demanding test, such as
rep max (RM) or a 1 RM, due to the associated risk. Decreased exposure to
training in the season negatively affects not only the skill but also the
preservation of muscle mass. If we lose muscle mass due to a lack of

有价值的。 运动单位募集的速度和数量是提高力量的明显因素。 加速

量主要来自于增加收缩的神经方面。

季节内力衰减
我们必须先了解如何增强武力，然后才能了解如何保存武力。 力量的
增强是练习和重复的结果； 因此，它是一种技能。 与任何技能一样，
保留它和增强它一样，都是练习和重复的产物。 如果您在季前赛、赛
季中和季后赛期间寻找继续进行力量训练的理由，那是因为力量是一项
技能。其中很大一部分与收缩的神经方面有关。 神经方面就是技能，
而技能是通过不断的练习和重复来维持的。
横截面肌肉面积是一种诊断工具，用于评估当我们无法保持尽可能多
的频率或使用尽可能多的训练量时，我们是否失去了维持力量的连接。
赛季中肌肉质量的损失清楚地表明了力量产生的损失。我们可以用它作
为一年中所有时间的诊断来评估发展水平和发展的潜在损失。 由于相
关风险，比对神经要求更高的测试（例如最大重复次数 (RM) 或 1 RM）
更重要。 在赛季中减少训练不仅会对技能产生负面影响，还会对肌肉
质量的保存产生负面影响。 如果我们由于缺乏肌肉而失去肌肉质量

exposure to training, we can infer that we have lost the skill as well. There is
a compounding effect of loss of muscle mass with dwindled neuromuscular
ability to decrease the amount and rate of force loss.
One of the biggest misconceptions about inseason training—it will have a negative impact on
recovery.
The concept of hormesis suggests that the body’s response to stress can
have a minimal effective dose. What is the bare minimum we need to give or
do to get the targeted outcome? If we can get to the same outcome with a
fraction of the effort, should we at least consider that option?
Minimal effective dose is a fundamental aspect behind effective
competitive period training. One of the more important aspects of off-season
training is developing the foundational components behind creating force.
Once we reach a period of having a certain level of force potential, we have a
much easier time maintaining it. By starting early in the off-season and
training through the entire competitive year, we can more readily maintain
with less effort longer during the season and beyond.
Reaching higher functional levels through early off-season adoption of
strength training focused on increasing force makes it more accessible longer
with fewer inputs later. We see this with advanced trainees; they reach higher
levels faster with a protocol, or a specific set, rep, tempo, rest, and intensity
scheme. They have a greater ability to adapt to methods and exercises faster
from being more familiar and therefore more capable quicker, which is a big
reason we need shorter mesocycles with advanced trainees during the offseason. The same can be said for the competitive season; we need less
exposure to something to get what we want.
We can use a fractal relationship with in-season training by adjusting
shorter periods of training. Instead of shorter mesocycles, we can use shorter
training sessions in the season. Shorter training sessions can be achieved by
using fewer sets. We can use fewer reps per time under tension. We can
adjust the time dedicated to strength training to compensate for the additional

神经肌肉能力的减弱会产生复合效应，从而降低力量损失的数量和速度
。
关于赛季中训练的最大误解之一是它会对恢复产生负面

hormesis的概念表明，身体对压力的反应可以有一个最小的有效剂量
。为了达到目标结果，我们至少需要付出或做些什么？ 如果我们只需
付出一小部分努力就能获得相同的结果，我们至少应该考虑这个选择吗
？
最小有效剂量是有效竞技期训练的一个基本方面。休赛期训练更重要
的方面之一是培养创造力量背后的基础要素。一旦我们达到了具有一定
水平的力量潜力的时期，我们就更容易维持它。 通过在休赛期尽早开
始并在整个比赛年度进行训练，我们可以在赛季及以后更轻松地以更少
的努力保持更长的时间。
通过在休赛期早期采用以增加力量为重点的力量训练来达到更高的功
能水平，可以在以后以更少的投入更长时间地进行训练。我们在高级学
员身上看到了这一点；通过协议或特定的组数、次数、节奏、休息和强
度方案，他们可以更快地达到更高的水平。他们通过更加熟悉而有更强
的能力更快地适应方法和练习，因此更快地更有能力，这是我们在休赛
期需要与高级学员进行更短的中间周期的一个重要原因。 对于竞技赛
季来说也是如此。 我们需要更少地接触某些东西才能得到我们想要的
东西。
我们可以通过调整较短的训练时间来利用分形关系与季内训练。我们
可以在赛季中使用较短的训练课程，而不是较短的中周期。 通过使用
更少的组数可以实现更短的训练课程。 在紧张状态下，我们每次可以
使用更少的次数。 我们可以调整专门用于力量训练的时间来补偿额外
的时间

time dedicated to technique (practice) and tactics (strategy) required in
season. In doing so, we maintain the skill of strength and the ability to
produce force.
Decay of force during competitive periods from not being able to train as
frequently or with as much volume is only a problem if the preceding training
was inadequate. We need to accumulate as much training as possible before
preparing for the drop in both frequency and volume from in-season demand.
The more we do in the off-season, the easier it is to get more from less with
frequency, shorter training sessions, less volume, and less intensity.

Off-Season Force Development
Training, therefore, needs to start as early as possible, which means
immediately following the postseason. Emotionally, following a season,
athletes are pretty susceptible to burnout. Reading the room is critical.
Having a feel for how an athlete is rejuvenated with new opportunities or
harboring a lot of frustration from the last season heading into the start of a
new off-season is an experience game. The more off-seasons as a coach you
can accrue, the better you can interpret an athlete’s messaging, both verbal
and nonverbal. A significant factor in this is that if the off-season training is
the polar opposite of what we did just weeks before during the season, the
transition will be much more difficult. Meaning, if we are doing zero in
season, we will create too much stress and burnout during the following offseason. Therefore, we must train in the season with at least a minimal
frequency or volume, or both, with adequate intensity and intent.
Because starting training as early as possible is foundational, we optimize
training in the off-season by accumulating as much stress as possible to focus
on frequency. In the season, frequency is minimal, 2 to 3 days per week. In
the off-season, we see some sports accumulate 3 to 4 days per week. With
both the in-season and the off-season, the lift format and schedule are based
on what we are doing from a practice or running schedule. Practice, speed, or
change of direction work is all logistics.
Logistics are a significant reason we prioritize running in the off-season. It
takes more planning to accommodate running, especially if you have a
facility in a cold-weather environment. We plan strength training around

专门用于赛季所需的技术（练习）和战术（策略）的时间。 通过这样
做，我们保持了力量的技巧和产生力量的能力。
如果之前的训练不充分，那么在比赛期间，由于无法经常进行训练或
进行大量训练而导致的力量衰减只会成为一个问题。 我们需要积累尽
可能多的培训，才能为旺季需求带来的频率和数量下降做好准备。我们
在休赛期做的越多，就越容易以更少的频率、更短的训练时间、更少的
训练量和更少的强度获得更多的成果。

淡季部队发展
因此，训练需要尽早开始，这意味着季后赛结束后立即开始。 从情感
上来说，一个赛季结束后，运动员很容易出现倦怠。 阅读房间至关重
要。感受运动员如何通过新的机会重新焕发活力，或者在上个赛季进入
新的休赛期开始时承受很多挫败感，都是一种体验游戏。作为一名教练
，你获得的休赛期越多，你就越能更好地解读运动员的口头和非口头信
息。其中一个重要因素是，如果休赛期的训练与我们几周前在赛季中所
做的截然相反，那么过渡将会困难得多。 这意味着，如果我们在赛季
中做到零，我们将在接下来的淡季中造成太多压力和倦怠。 因此，我
们必须在赛季中进行至少最低限度的训练频率或训练量，或两者兼而有
之，并具有足够的强度和意图。
因为尽早开始训练是基础，所以我们在休赛期通过积累尽可能多的压
力来重点关注频率来优化训练。 在旺季，频率很少，每周 2 至 3 天。
在淡季，我们看到一些运动每周累积 3 到 4 天。 无论是赛季内还是淡
季，举重形式和时间表都基于我们在练习或跑步时间表中所做的事情。
练习、速度或改变方向的工作都是后勤工作。
物流是我们优先考虑淡季跑步的一个重要原因。需要更多的计划来适
应跑步，特别是如果您的设施位于寒冷的天气环境中。 我们围绕以下
内容计划力量训练

when and where we can run. This is relevant because we have to make a
considerable impact on the ability to increase someone’s force during the offseason. Either we lift weights after running, when fatigued, or we fit it in on
days between runs, again, when fatigued.
This is problematic from the stance we are trying to reach, which is as
high a functional level as possible, while developing speed through running.
Consider for a second that we will need to prioritize either sprinting or lifting
at certain points of the year, one over the other. We may need to revisit how
we organize lifting over running within a microcycle based on either the
demand or the risk. It’s not binary in terms of training from a philosophical
standpoint. It is binary due to most of our setups having a designated place to
run versus lift. Both have their upsides and downsides, the end goal being to
reach as high a functional level as possible relative to when we started. We
can easily use body composition to assess muscle mass development and see
the developed force, or at least the potential, from our decisions. In the offseason, we can use periodic tracking of sprinting to determine progress. In
the end, results are all that matter.
For all biomotor abilities, it is either a mesocycle focus or a microcycle
focus. With a mesocycle focus, we layer training from one block to the next
to prioritize developing force, velocity, or work. We concentrate on one
quality to develop to a higher level. With a microcycle focus, we adjust the
frequency with methods such as high-low or multiple training sessions a day
to reach the highest levels possible.
The point is that we need to organize training to reach a higher overall
level of force to have a greater reserve and longer residuals during the
competitive season. Force will decay faster and more quickly if we do not
accumulate enough training stress directly related to producing force in the
off-season. Logistics will dictate much of this, but we need to organize
training to accomplish it.
Novices will obtain more improvement in the off-season (figure 6.5), but
they will decay more and faster in the season than advanced trainees. This
means that we will need greater frequency and volume in season, if possible,
for novice athletes. Alternatively, we will reach less relative improvement in
force during the off-season for advanced training-age athletes. They will need

我们可以在何时何地跑步。 这是相关的，因为我们必须对休赛期增加
某人力量的能力产生相当大的影响。我们要么在跑步后疲劳时举重，要
么在跑步之间的几天进行举重，同样是在疲劳时。
从我们试图达到的立场来看，这是有问题的，即尽可能高的功能水平
，同时通过跑步提高速度。考虑一下，我们需要在一年中的某些时间点
优先考虑短跑或举重，一个优先。我们可能需要重新审视如何根据需求
或风险在微循环内组织举重而不是跑步。 从哲学的角度来看，训练并
不是二元的。这是二元的，因为我们的大多数设置都有指定的跑步和举
重地点。两者都有其优点和缺点，最终目标是相对于我们开始时达到尽
可能高的功能水平。 我们可以轻松地利用身体成分来评估肌肉质量的
发展，并从我们的决定中看到所发展的力量，或者至少是潜力。 在淡
季，我们可以使用定期跟踪冲刺来确定进度。 最后，结果才是最重要
的。
对于所有生物运动能力，它要么是中循环焦点，要么是微循环焦点。
以中循环为重点，我们将训练从一个模块分层到下一个模块，以优先考
虑发展力量、速度或功。 我们专注于一种品质，以向更高的水平发展
。 以微循环为重点，我们通过高低或每天多次训练等方法调整频率，
以达到尽可能高的水平。
关键是我们要组织训练，达到更高的整体力量水平，在赛季中有更多
的储备和更长的剩余时间。 如果我们在休赛期没有积累足够的与产生
力量直接相关的训练压力，力量就会越来越快地衰减。 后勤将决定这
一切，但我们需要组织培训来完成它。
新手在休赛期会获得更多的进步（图6.5），但在赛季中他们会比高
级练习生衰退得更多、更快。 这意味着，如果可能的话，对于新手运
动员，我们将需要在赛季中增加训练频率和训练量。或者，我们将在休
赛期为高级训练年龄的运动员实现相对较小的力量改善。他们将需要

less frequency and volume in season to maintain their development. The
inverted response to volume and frequency for both advanced and novice
athletes, in-season or off-season, is why it is so hard just to say it is all about
getting stronger. It is too complex a problem to say something is that simple.
One of the biggest overreactions in training—we
need to have a uniform program year round.
I have worked enough in the off-season to see that veteran athletes can
reach higher functional levels faster than rookie athletes. They can also tap
into that reserve faster during competition. This means that we need to vary
the stimulus based on the potential for not only development but also the rate
of decay. Veterans, more advanced athletes, need less exposure and less
volume to reach as high a level, which is again more of a logistics problem.

FIGURE 6.5 Novice versus advanced athletes.
Organizing by mesocycle versus microcycle is equally as important as
programming based on training age. Since we can reach higher functional

当季减少频率和数量以维持其发育。 无论是赛季内还是休赛期，高级
运动员和新手运动员对训练量和频率的反应都是相反的，这就是为什么
很难说这一切都是为了变得更强。问题太复杂了，说起来就这么简单。

训练中最大的过度反应之一是我们需要全年制定统一的
计划。
我在休赛期做了足够的工作，发现经验丰富的运动员可以比新秀运动
员更快地达到更高的功能水平。 他们还可以在比赛中更快地利用这一
储备。 这意味着我们不仅需要根据发展潜力，还要根据衰退速度来改
变刺激措施。 退伍军人、更高级的运动员需要更少的接触和更少的训

为我们可以达到更高的功能

levels faster with more advanced training-age athletes, they decay less and
slower. We need to adjust for that off-season by increasing the frequency and
volume for novice athletes during the season and decreasing the frequency
and volume for advanced athletes during the season. By this time, we are
transitioning our focus to other areas, the technical and tactical aspects. When
in doubt, check muscle mass and make a connection to the level of training
with practice, games, and game planning for both novice and advanced
athletes.
Force does not decay as much during the season as one might think.
Training intensity, intent, and general organization all have profound effects
on limiting decay. Most importantly, this is a way to perform at the highest
level in the season. It pays homage to all the hard work we did before. All the
effort and hard training sessions would be for nothing if we just packed it in
during the season. Force does not have to decay; we can maintain it in the
season by working equally hard but with more strategy to preserve and build
what we worked so hard to get.

Velocity
Different from creating force, velocity has a very clear point of diminishing
returns (figure 6.6). One thing that makes training such a difficult problem is
that it is hard to remove certain associations from the things we choose to do
with our athletes. We look at something like velocity as the product of other
things, rather than focusing on the act of doing velocity. We associate success
there with doing something else, like force. Instead of using the simple logic
of doing something at a faster rate, even at the expense of external load, it
seems counterintuitive when it should be extremely intuitive.

训练年龄越高的运动员水平越高，他们的衰退就越少、越慢。我们需要
针对休赛期进行调整，增加赛季中新手运动员的频率和训练量，并减少
赛季中高级运动员的频率和训练量。 此时，我们正在将重点转移到其
他领域，即技术和战术方面。如有疑问，请检查肌肉质量，并将新手和
高级运动员的训练水平与练习、比赛和比赛计划联系起来。

力量在赛季中的衰减并不像人们想象的那么严重。训练强度、意图和
总体组织都对限制衰退有深远的影响。 最重要的是，这是在赛季中发
挥最高水平的一种方式。这是对我们之前所做的所有辛勤工作的致敬。
如果我们只是在赛季中完成所有的努力和艰苦的训练，那一切都将毫无
意义。 力量不必衰减； 我们可以通过同样努力工作，但采取更多策略
来保护和建设我们辛辛苦苦获得的东西，从而在本赛季保持这种状态。

速度
与创造力不同，速度有一个非常明显的收益递减点（图 6.6）。使训练
成为如此困难的问题的一件事是，很难从我们选择与运动员一起做的事
情中消除某些关联。我们将速度之类的东西视为其他事物的产物，而不
是关注速度的行为。我们将成功与做其他事情联系起来，比如武力。与
其使用以更快的速度做某事的简单逻辑，即使以外部负载为代价，这似
乎是违反直觉的，而它应该是非常直观的。

FIGURE 6.6 Velocity brackets.
Another method we can use is velocity ranges within a velocity target. For
the most part, with force-related training inputs, we use the absolute strength
zone. Absolute strength is 0.3 to 0.5 m/s velocity. Typically, when reps fall
below 0.3 m/s, there is a significant drop-off in technique for multiple reps in
a row. Similar to rep ranges, the athlete needs to stay within that zone. Below
0.3 m/s means the weight is too heavy, and we have hit the critical drop-off.
Above 0.5 m/s means the weight is too light, and we need to increase the
intensity. The nice thing about velocity-based training is that we can be more
objective in assessing critical drop-off.
Velocity is a skill much like force is, maybe even more so. Practice and
deliberate effort are critical to developing velocity. The neural aspects of

我们可以使用的另一种方法是速度目标内的速度范围。在大多数情况
下，对于与力量相关的训练输入，我们使用绝对力量区。 绝对强度为 0
.3 至 0.5 m/s 的速度。 通常，当次数低于 0.3 m/s 时，连续多次重复的
技术会显着下降。与次数范围类似，运动员需要保持在该区域内。低于
0.3 m/s 意味着重量太重，我们已经达到了临界下降。超过0.5m/s说明重
量太轻，需要加大强度。基于速度的训练的好处是我们可以更客观地评
估关键下降。
速度是一种技能，就像力量一样，甚至更是如此。 练习和刻意的努
力对于提高速度至关重要。 神经方面

contraction are much more critical to velocity than to force. In this situation,
CSA does not contribute as much to velocity, which leaves velocity more
neural than muscular. When we omit direct work on velocity for periods, we
begin to decay not only from a physiological perspective but also from a skill
perspective. Unlike force, velocity cannot be maintained with heavier loads
or higher volumes; we need to make a concerted effort to move as fast as
possible. However, there is a workaround; we can improve the rate of
something from the intent with which we move. If we are giving as much
effort as possible on each rep, it is equivalent to moving with more velocity
without having to move at a faster rate.
Here’s a quick recap from physics on velocity before we go over decay.
Velocity is the product of displacement, how much we move, over time. Said
differently, velocity is how far we go relative to how long it takes. To be
blunt, lighter things go farther in less time. Power is work (force ×
displacement) over time. The mass of something has a larger influence on
power, which is important. Mass does not have the same impact on velocity.
Power is the true north of most S&C programs, which is why we so easily
associate force-generating ability with an athlete’s performance. Force is
mass multiplied by acceleration, so if we can move more mass, we can have
more power. Velocity is a much fickler entity. We cannot simply add weight
and say we are producing more velocity. Our only three options are to go
farther at the same time, go the same distance in less time, or go farther in
less time. That is not as easy to do as simply adding some weight to increase
force and, subsequently, power.
Therefore, intent is important for velocity. The effort, the focus, and the
execution all influence velocity. Effort is a huge contributing factor to all
biomotor abilities, but the thought that we need something external, such as
weight on the bar, to get it is misguided. If we move something with maximal
intent, we can get the same outcome as if it were heavier but with a lighter
weight. This is important because velocity is more associated with moving
lighter things faster.
One of the biggest misconceptions about velocity

收缩对速度的影响比对力的影响要重要得多。在这种情况下，CSA 对速
度的贡献不大，这使得速度更多地是神经性的而不是肌肉性的。当我们
在一段时间内忽略对速度的直接研究时，我们不仅从生理角度而且从技
能角度开始衰退。 与力不同，较重的负载或较大的体积无法维持速度
； 我们需要齐心协力，尽快采取行动。 不过，有一个解决方法； 我
们可以根据我们移动的意图来提高某件事的速度。 如果我们在每次重
复中付出尽可能多的努力，就相当于以更快的速度移动，而不必以更快
的速度移动。
在我们讨论衰变之前，这是对速度的物理学的快速回顾。速度是位移
的乘积，即我们随时间移动的距离。换句话说，速度是我们走多远相对
于花费多长时间。 坦率地说，更轻的东西在更短的时间内走得更远。
功率是随时间变化的功（力×位移）。 物体的质量对功率的影响更大，
这一点很重要。质量对速度没有同样的影响。
力量是大多数体能训练项目的真正核心，这就是为什么我们如此容易
地将力量产生能力与运动员的表现联系起来。 力是质量乘以加速度，
所以如果我们可以移动更多的质量，我们就能拥有更多的功率。速度是
一个变化无常的实体。我们不能简单地增加重量并说我们正在产生更高
的速度。 我们唯一的三个选择是同时走得更远，用更少的时间走同样
的距离，或者用更短的时间走得更远。这并不像简单地增加一些重量来
增加力量和随后的功率那么容易。
因此，意图对于速度很重要。 努力、专注和执行都会影响速度。 努
力是所有生物运动能力的一个重要因素，但认为我们需要外部因素（例
如杠上的重量）来获得它的想法是错误的。如果我们以最大的意图移动
某物，我们可以获得与较重但重量较轻相同的结果。 这很重要，因为
速度与更快地移动较轻的物体更相关。

One of the biggest misconceptions about velocity

and speed—external load is the only way to create
more effort.
Warm-up sets are a great example of this. We can readily increase velocity
during warm-up sets because the external load is lessened. But we rarely
adopt this strategy. We can use intent during this period to increase the
technical aspects of the lift, which is important. We can use intent to increase
the rate at which we perform something, which is equally important. We see
this with accommodating resistance (bands or chains). It is lighter, but the
weight increases based on the natural strength curve. We can increase intent
in response to the increasing weight, but it is lighter at a certain point of the
lift and leads to increased speeds.
I say this because when we implement a year-round training program, we
need to condition our athletes to give their best within the time we have
allotted. Off-season warm-up sets seem like a burden when we are going to
increase the percentage of our RM by 25% to 50%, but they are not.
Velocity-based training (figure 6.7) gives the target bar speed for us to work
based on the quality we are looking for. There is an inverse relationship
between the speed we can go and the weight we can use; this is a critical
factor.
Off-season and in-season will always have warm-up sets; that is a
guarantee. What is not a guarantee are things like plyometric exercises,
medicine ball throws and tosses, Olympic lifts, and starting strength-based
lifts all year. We will, with absolute certainty, warm up for anything we do,
which is a great opportunity to practice the skill of velocity. This is a
trainable quality: practicing velocity by demonstrating maximal intent with
every rep we do.

和速度——外部负荷是产生更多努力的唯一方法。

热身组就是一个很好的例子。由于外部负荷减少，我们可以在热身组
期间轻松提高速度。 但我们很少采用这种策略。 我们可以利用这段时
间的意图来增加技术方面的提升，这一点很重要。我们可以利用意图来
提高执行某件事的速度，这同样重要。我们通过调节阻力（带或链）看
到了这一点。 它更轻，但重量根据自然强度曲线而增加。 我们可以随
着重量的增加而增加意图，但在举升的某个点上重量会更轻，从而导致
速度增加。
我这样说是因为当我们实施全年训练计划时，我们需要让我们的运动

比增加 25% 至 50% 时，淡季热身赛似乎是一种负担，但事实并非如此
。基于速度的训练（图 6.7）为我们提供了目标杆速度，以便我们根据
我们正在寻找的质量进行工作。 我们可以行驶的速度和我们可以使用
的重量之间存在反比关系； 这是一个关键因素。
淡季和旺季总会有热身组； 这是一个保证。 不能保证的是增强式训
练、健身球投掷和投掷、奥林匹克举重以及全年开始的力量举重等。
我们绝对会为我们所做的任何事情热身，这是练习速度技能的绝佳机会
。 这是一个可训练的品质：通过在我们所做的每一次重复中表现出最
大的意图来练习速度。

FIGURE 6.7 Velocity-based training.
Force-velocity relationships will inevitably control how heavy or fast we
move something. We have established that we will be overly influenced by
the need to create power from training, which will be more readily changed
by increasing force, making it natural to prioritize increasing strength over
velocity. If we are playing the law of averages game, a larger number of
people will increase their power by increasing their strength. But that is true
until it isn’t. There will always be outliers, but there is a simpler logic here:
The best way to get faster is to go faster.
There is another reason focusing on force is preferred: It is easier to
interpret as a coach. Perceived effort is a lot more transparent with increasing
mass on a bar than having someone move the same distance 0.01 s faster.
Telling someone to go heavier to increase intent is externally focused. Telling
someone to go faster to increase intent is internally focused. We can only rely
so much on external driving of intent. For instance, in the season or
postseason, there is a limit to how much weight one can use. There could be a
situation where the athlete is elite in terms of strength and needs to focus on
the rate of force over the amount of force. Therefore, we need to focus on

图 6.7 基于速度的训练。
力-速度关系将不可避免地控制我们移动物体的重量或速度。 我们已
经确定，我们会受到训练中产生力量的需求的过度影响，而通过增加力
量更容易改变这一点，因此自然会优先考虑增加力量而不是速度。 如
果我们玩的是平均法则游戏，更多的人会通过增加实力来增加他们的力
量。 但事实并非如此。 总会有异常值，但这里有一个更简单的逻辑：
加快速度的最佳方法就是走得更快。
优先关注力量还有另一个原因：它更容易被理解为教练。随着杆上质
量的增加，感知的努力比某人以 0.01 秒的速度更快地移动相同距离要透
明得多。告诉某人增加重量以增加意图是外在的。告诉某人走得更快以
增加意图是内部关注的。我们只能非常依赖外部意图的驱动。 例如，
在赛季或季后赛中，一个人可以使用的重量是有限制的。可能存在这样

量的大小。 因此，我们需要重点关注

intent, internally, from velocity. It gives us more options.
A critical aspect of the force-velocity relationship is inventorying how
much you move something heavy and slow versus how much you move
something light and fast (figure 6.8). We are the product of what we
repeatedly do—specificity—so if we want to reach higher levels of velocity,
we need to have a certain amount of time allocated to it. Although we may be
more apt to leverage force to increase power, the highest power output is at
lighter external loads (30% of 1 RM). We must commit to moving light
things fast, year round, to enhance the neural aspects of the skill.
The biggest overreaction regarding velocity—we
get enough from practice or games in season.

意图，内部，来自速度。它给了我们更多的选择。
力-速度关系的一个关键方面是盘点您移动重且慢的物体的量与移动
轻且快的物体的量（图 6.8）。 我们是我们反复做的事情（特异性）的
产物，所以如果我们想达到更高的速度水平，我们需要分配一定的时间
。尽管我们可能更倾向于利用力来增加功率，但最高功率输出是在较轻
的外部负载（1 RM 的 30%）下。 我们必须致力于全年快速移动轻物，
以增强神经方面的技能。

关于速度的最大过度反应是我们从赛季中的训练或比赛
中得到了足够的东西。

图 6.8 1 RM 力-速度曲线的百分比。
请记住，练习和比赛都有技术和战术的重点；

training is more general. Practice and games are low-constraint environments,
which have an impact on how fast we can go. The fewer the constraints, the
more we have to process, which will slow you down. Training increases the
number of constraints to movement and provides the potential to produce
higher velocities. We need dedicated time in the weight room to do highvelocity work throughout the year.
Force is strongly correlated with muscle mass; we have to find something
that we can connect to velocity. The easiest measurement of this is the
countermovement jump (CMJ). The ability to propel your body vertically is a
clear indicator of velocity. No external load and high speed, relatively
noninvasive, and connection to performance make CMJ valuable. We can use
CMJ as a proxy year round to assess velocity potential. Higher CMJ heights
mean we are providing adequate velocity stimulus.
Of note, when you are working with athletes in the off-season, you will
see an increase in body mass. Total activity levels are down without having
to practice for multiple hours a day. A large amount of the focus will be on
strength training, which will correspond to an increase in body mass. This
body mass increase will negatively impact the ability to produce high
velocity. If the athlete can jump the same height at increased body mass, they
have increased power. This may not mean an increase in velocity.
Alternatively, athletes in the season can lose weight and maintain or increase
their jump height. This could be considered an increased velocity but could
simply mean a lesser need to produce force. There are layers to every metric,
but jumping higher is always going to be a net positive, regardless of how it
happened.
Velocity decay is a natural byproduct of a lack of exposure. One could
easily avoid training with high velocity during exercises for whatever reason.
Prioritizing slow and heavy to develop strength can be diminished with the
use of plyometrics or simply time commitment. In-season focus on injury
reduction can lead to avoiding high-velocity work. A commitment to moving
light things fast, from direct programming, such as plyometric or light
medicine ball exercises, or indirect programming, such as moving with more
intent during warm-up sets, is the only way to prevent decay. Direct velocitybased training is often underused and is a potential edge if you can find

培训内容比较笼统。练习和比赛是低约束环境，这会影响我们的速度。
限制越少，我们需要处理的就越多，这会减慢你的速度。 训练增加了
运动的限制，并提供了产生更高速度的潜力。 我们需要在健身房里投
入专门的时间来全年进行高速训练。
力量与肌肉质量密切相关；我们必须找到可以与速度联系起来的东西
。 最简单的测量方法是反向运动跳跃 (CMJ)。垂直推动身体的能力是
速度的明确指标。 无外部负载、高速、相对无创以及与性能的联系使
CMJ 有价值。我们可以全年使用 CMJ 作为代理来评估速度潜力。较高
的 CMJ 高度意味着我们提供足够的速度刺激。
值得注意的是，当您在休赛期与运动员一起工作时，您会发现体重有
所增加。 无需每天练习多个小时，总活动水平就会下降。 大部分注意
力将集中在力量训练上，这将对应于体重的增加。 这种体重增加将对
产生高速的能力产生负面影响。如果运动员能够在体重增加的情况下跳
相同的高度，那么他们的力量就会增加。 这可能并不意味着速度的增
加。或者，本赛季的运动员可以减轻体重并保持或增加跳跃高度。 这
可以被认为是速度增加，但可能仅仅意味着产生力的需要减少。每个指
标都有层次，但跳得更高总是会带来净积极影响，无论它是如何发生的
。

速度衰减是缺乏暴露的自然副产品。 无论出于何种原因，人们都可
以轻松地避免在练习过程中进行高速训练。通过使用增强式训练或仅仅
投入时间，可以减少优先考虑缓慢和大重量来发展力量的情况。 赛季
中注重减少伤害可以避免高速工作。致力于快速移动轻量物体，通过直
接编程（例如增强式或轻型实心球练习）或间接编程（例如在热身组中
更加专注地移动）是防止衰退的唯一方法。基于速度的直接训练通常未
得到充分利用，如果您能找到

creative ways to implement it. Simply encouraging greater intent through
velocity-based training is a powerful velocity antidecay strategy.

Work
Unlike force or velocity, we get the necessary amount of work in the season.
We see this with potential spikes in workloads during practice. What we need
to evaluate relatively is the impact of work when we are focused elsewhere:
the off-season.
This brings up an interesting aspect of S&C: We are responsible for
balancing the equation when our counterparts, sports coaches, make things
unbalanced. In the off-season, we are the ones creating asymmetry from
technique and tactics toward general performance. But we also create
asymmetry by focusing on certain qualities such as force, velocity, or work,
depending on the time of year or the goal of a training block. When we
transition back into the season, we need to provide balance to high amounts
of work done during practice, which usually comes in the form of force and
velocity. This creates a large distribution of our time focused on force and
velocity, but not as much on work.
One of the biggest misconceptions about work—
power is more important than capacity.
All energy systems are broken down into a maximal effort for a single rep:
power, or for repeat submaximal efforts: capacity. We often see that when an
athlete expresses a single effort without the ability to repeat it, their
performance suffers. We want as much force or velocity as possible, but that
is relative to being able to repeat that effort. We recover between anaerobic
activities aerobically. We therefore need to consider work and capacity as a
means of going further, through higher volume or density in a session and
microcycle.

Focused Energy System Work for Sport or Position

创造性的方法来实施它。 通过基于速度的训练来鼓励更大的意图是一
种强大的速度抗衰策略。

工作
与力量或速度不同，我们在赛季中得到了必要的工作量。我们在练习过
程中看到了工作量可能出现峰值的情况。我们需要相对评估的是当我们
把注意力集中在其他地方：淡季时，工作的影响。
这就提出了 S&C 的一个有趣的方面：当我们的同行（体育教练）使
事情变得不平衡时，我们有责任平衡方程式。 在休赛期，我们是造成
技战术和整体表现不对称的人。 但我们也会通过关注某些品质（例如
力量、速度或功）来创造不对称性，具体取决于一年中的时间或训练组
的目标。 当我们回到赛季时，我们需要为练习期间所做的大量工作提
供平衡，这些工作通常以力量和速度的形式出现。 这使得我们的大部
分时间都集中在力量和速度上，而不是花在工作上。

关于工作的最大误解之一是权力比能力更重要。

所有能量系统都分为单次最大努力：功率，或重复次最大努力：容量
。我们经常看到，当一名运动员表现出单一的努力而无法重复时，他们
的表现就会受到影响。我们想要尽可能多的力或速度，但这与能够重复
该努力有关。 我们在无氧活动之间通过有氧活动进行恢复。 因此，我
们需要考虑将工作和能力作为进一步发展的手段，通过在会议和微周期
中提高容量或密度。

专注于运动或职位的能量系统工作

Work in the off-season is an afterthought because of the singular focus on
developing exclusively force and velocity. The rate-limiting step for both
force and velocity is being able to hit an adequate volume within a certain
period, or density. If we lack capacity, we will have to compensate for having
to rest more. Resting more leads to being unable to hit a certain volume
during a session. We could try to offset this by increasing frequency, but this
is not a reliable option in a team setting. The best option to raise the upper
limits of density we can hit in a session is to increase capacity.
Having higher capacity means we can hit a higher density because we will
recover faster interset. This is not an insignificant aspect of off-season
training. We can more readily adjust volume than we can adjust frequency
with athletes’ schedules. This makes the capacity to withstand certain
volumes at a threshold intensity, potentially reaching higher functional levels
of force and velocity, the most important quality to develop. For us to reach
levels of running faster or jumping higher, the capacity to recover will be the
ultimate deciding factor.
Capacity will help us withstand not only off-season stress but also inseason stress. Not only that, it allows us to lessen and slow the rate of decay
of force or velocity during the competitive season from our increased
tolerance to stress. Handling higher acute workloads better is a greater
indicator of an athlete’s capacity. Poor response to acute spikes above 1.3
chronic workloads means we did not have the fitness to handle that stress
(Gabbett, 2016). This will lead to a negative response to training the
following week. If we are going to reach elite levels of performance, we will
need to handle higher stress more efficiently, which is determined by
capacity.
We have metrics we can use to assess capacity. Wellness is an excellent
proxy for response to stress and adaptation. We can look at internal metrics,
such as resting heart rate, heart rate variability, or heart rate recovery
intratraining, to assess adaptations to work. These metrics are an assessment
relative to the impact on the ability to perform certain volumes, at certain
intensities, with certain amounts of density. If we can do more volume at
higher intensity within the same or even a shortened period, we have
developed fitness. We see higher wellness, lower resting heart rate, higher

Power’s Effect on Capacity
What goes up must come down. Having a countermeasure to CNS load is
necessary. Developing more performance qualities that the athlete can handle
while expediting recovery is the edge in training. We can always train low
CNS activity; however, we cannot say the same about high CNS activity.
This may not be a principle, but it is a hard rule. During both the off-season
and in-season, we can adopt this model of using low CNS activity and
working capacity following high CNS days. Following a sprint session, we
can work on lower-intensity tempo runs. Following a game, we can use a
lower-intensity, higher-volume session. These diagnostics are the body’s
indicators that it cannot sustain as much as it is without some
countermeasure.
The main focus is to develop capacity by prioritizing work to allow us to
reach higher levels of force and velocity. Work gives us a strategy to focus on
while we are working hard to develop and maintain those qualities. Work is
not an afterthought. Work is foundational to both force and velocity to obtain
adequate volume at higher intensities; it can’t be secondary. We are the
product of what we repeatedly do. The product is therefore based on what we
can repeat—capacity.
The biggest misconception about work—it is
secondary to the other qualities.
Work is listed as one of the big three biomotor abilities because of its
impact on everything. The entire off-season, as well as the in-season, is based
on our ability to repeat something. The rate of decay of work, much like force
or velocity, is based on how much focus we place on it. In the season, we
have so much work with practice and games. In the off-season, we need to

The reversibility factors are summarized as follows:
Force
Biggest overreaction: Training needs to be uniform for all athletes year
round.
Biggest misconception: Strength training during competition does not
hurt performance if executed properly.
Velocity
Biggest overreaction: We get enough direct velocity work from
practice and games in the season.
Biggest misconceptions: External load is the only way to create more
effort.
Work
Biggest overreaction: Work is secondary to other qualities.
Biggest misconception: Power is more important than capacity.

Take Home
We are the product of what we repeatedly do. If we do not do something, we
lose it. The rate of that loss is based on how much and how well we do
something during periods of lessened focus. The amount of that loss is based
on how much we built up during periods of increased focus. Reversibility is
about understanding our ability to not only build in the off-season but also
manage the season.

指了解我们不仅在休赛期建设的能力，而且还管理赛季的能力。

DIMINISHING RETURNS AND
CRITICAL DROP-OFF
Diminishing returns only matter if you are training hard enough at threshold
intensity and duration to reach the point of diminishing returns. I look at
diminishing returns as acute overtraining. It is the body’s fail-safe when you
are pushing to a threshold. If we surpass the body’s capacity to handle the
level of stress being imposed on it, the body will respond by limiting its
output. The caveat, and this is the point, is that there needs to be at least an
adequate amount of acute stress for the body to respond with diminishing
returns. We need to push the razor’s edge of high-level stress constantly. The
only way we can do this safely is if we have a fail-safe in case it’s too much.
Principle of Diminishing Returns: Performance gains are related to the
level of training (training age) of each individual. Athletes who have never
participated in a training program before can see huge initial performance
gains in their program. On the other hand, athletes who have been lifting
for several years will see smaller gains over longer periods. As an athlete
nears their genetic potential, the gains in performance will be much harder
to obtain. The key is to continue to show progress in the areas in which
they have weaknesses. For example, when an athlete first starts a training
program as a freshman in college, the athlete’s vertical jump may improve
from 22 in. to 30 in. in the first year. As the athlete continues to train
through the next three years, their vertical jump performance may
increase from 30 in. to 38 in. Achieving the eight-inch improvement in the

收益递减才有意义。 我将收益递减视为严重的过度训练。当您达到阈
值时，它是身体的自动防故障装置。 如果我们超出了身体处理施加在
其上的压力水平的能力，身体就会通过限制其输出来做出反应。 需要
注意的是，这也是重点，身体至少需要足够的急性压力才能做出收益递
减的反应。我们需要不断地突破高水平压力的剃刀边缘。我们能够安全
地做到这一点的唯一方法是如果我们有一个故障安全装置，以防它太多
。
收益递减原理：绩效收益与每个人的训练水平（训练年龄）有关。以前从
未参加过训练计划的运动员可以在他们的计划中看到巨大的初始表现提升
。另一方面，已经进行了数年举重训练的运动员在较长时间内会看到较小
的收益。 当运动员接近其遗传潜力时，表现的提高将变得更加困难。 关
键是要继续在自己薄弱的领域取得进步。例如，当一名运动员作为大学一
年级新生首次开始训练计划时，该运动员的垂直弹跳可能会在第一年从 2

垂直弹跳能力可能会从 30 英寸提高到 38 英寸。实现垂直弹跳能力提高 8
英寸

final three years is much more significant and difficult than the eight-inch
in the first year. (Sands et al., 2012, p. 9)

The law of diminishing returns is the one principle that forces us to
adjust our plan after the preliminary planning. All the other principles are
before training: individuality, specificity, progressive overload, progression,
and reversibility. We have to respond to critical drop-off, not prepare for it.
The preparation for diminishing returns is developing contingency plans.
This is a unique aspect of diminishing returns that we need to understand
because it is the ultimate litmus test of a great program. The problem of
diminishing returns is a microcosm of adaptation—a complex problem that
requires establishing alternative routes for an infinite number of possibilities.
The trick is picking the best alternate route to our goal when we meet these
training inflection points.
The hardest part of diminishing returns is that we have to train hard
enough to reach them. This is not necessarily a given. It feels counterintuitive
to a degree that we need to think about how to motivate and ensure amazing
effort but, at the same time, have a backup plan for when that goes too far. As
with any venture into the great unknown, we have to have a plan to handle
both what we think will happen and what we do not know will happen.
This creates a paradox for the coach, especially in the group environment.
On the front end, you have to organize and align a collective group of S&C
coaches, sports coaches, sports medicine professionals, and athletes within a
program. This takes conviction and skill. At the same time, you as the leader
need to convey that this is our plan—until it’s not. Saying that this plan we
worked so hard to create will at any moment be deemed ineffective is hard to
process as a coach. This takes not only conviction in your ability to plan but
also confidence that your plan is only as effective as what one can recover
from.
We have established how principles are foundational to programming.
Now we have to establish what to do when our program is no longer doing
what it was designed to do. Our aim is to develop the biomotor abilities of
force, velocity, or work, and we need biomechanics to get there, although our
bioenergetic capacity will limit us. In a sense, we are pushing the biomotor

收益递减法则是迫使我们在初步规划后调整计划的一个原则。所有其
他原则都在训练之前：个体性、特异性、渐进性超负荷、渐进性和可逆
性。 我们必须应对严重的下降，而不是为此做好准备。应对收益递减
的准备工作是制定应急计划。这是我们需要理解的收益递减的一个独特
方面，因为它是一个伟大项目的最终试金石。 收益递减问题是适应的
一个缩影，这是一个复杂的问题，需要为无限种可能性建立替代路线。
诀窍是当我们遇到这些训练拐点时，选择实现目标的最佳替代路线。

收益递减最困难的部分是我们必须足够努力地训练才能达到它们。这
不一定是给定的。我们需要考虑如何激励和确保做出惊人的努力，但同
时还要制定一个备用计划，以应对走得太远的情况，这在某种程度上感
觉违反直觉。与任何探索未知世界的冒险一样，我们必须制定计划来处
理我们认为会发生的事情和我们不知道会发生的事情。
这给教练带来了一个悖论，尤其是在团队环境中。在前端，您必须在
一个计划中组织和协调由体能教练、运动教练、运动医学专业人员和运
动员组成的集体小组。这需要信念和技巧。与此同时，作为领导者，你
需要传达这是我们的计划——直到事实并非如此。 作为一名教练，如
果说我们辛辛苦苦制定的这个计划随时都会被认为是无效的，那是很难
接受的。这不仅需要对你的计划能力有信心，还需要相信你的计划只有
在人们能够从中恢复的情况下才有效。
我们已经确定了原则如何成为编程的基础。现在我们必须确定当我们
的程序不再执行其设计目的时该怎么办。 我们的目标是发展力量、速
度或做功的生物运动能力，我们需要生物力学来实现这一目标，尽管我
们的生物能量能力会限制我们。 从某种意义上说，我们正在推动生物
马达

ability to the threshold and using biomechanics and bioenergetics to
determine if that threshold is too far. If it looks like something we do not
want from a biomechanical perspective, we need to adjust. If we no longer
have the energy to perform the task, we need to adjust our plan.
A great coach sees all angles and all potential outcomes of actions before
they even happen. Critical drop-off is the point where we reach technical and
physiological limits. There is always a moment of perfection when a program
is put from our mind to paper and is ready to enter an athlete’s life. It is at
that moment that we think the program is the best it will ever be. It is perfect
until it interacts with the human for whom it was created. These complex,
adaptive, open systems will respond in a variety of ways, none of which we
can anticipate. That is why we need an alternative plan when our perfect plan
is no longer effective.
Writing down something to do is only a fraction of what a program is. It is
the ability to handle the unpredictability that makes the program complete.
The value of the training program is the ability to pivot and adapt to how the
athlete is responding. The value of a program in a group environment
conveys the larger fundamental goal of enlisting trust with autonomy. The
ends are the product of the quality of the means.
A great program will build in fail-safes. After writing a program, we have
to evaluate the interaction between every entity and predict what may go
wrong. A coach needs to simultaneously have fail-safes and be willing to
pivot or ditch a plan when necessary. A coach needs to plan to bail on a
program before it leads to catastrophic results. There is a point to doubling
down and pushing, but that will have to be built off a plan of when to
redirect.
A plan has an objective. There should be as much time spent on when and
where the plan can go wrong as on the actual plan itself. What is an
appropriate fail-safe for a training plan? Before we can answer that question,
we have to establish what the plan intends to accomplish: improving
performance. If there is no intent, there will be no acceptable deviation from
the plan. When we understand the true purpose of the plan, we establish a
tolerable deviation from it. A massive deviation is hard to evaluate without
understanding how far off course we have gone from the objective. Without

伟大的教练在行动发生之前就能看到行动的各个角度和所有潜在结果

写下要做的事情只是程序的一小部分。正是处理不可预测性的能力使
程序变得完整。训练计划的价值在于能够调整和适应运动员的反应方式
。 团体环境中的程序的价值传达了更大的基本目标，即通过自主来赢
得信任。 目的是手段质量的产物。
一个伟大的计划将内置故障保险。编写程序后，我们必须评估每个实
体之间的交互并预测可能出现的问题。 教练需要同时具备故障保险，
并愿意在必要时改变或放弃计划。 教练需要在计划导致灾难性结果之
前计划好放弃计划。 加倍努力和推动是有道理的，但这必须建立在何
时重新调整方向的计划之上。
计划有目标。花在计划何时何地可能出错的时间应该与花在实际计划
本身上的时间一样多。 培训计划的适当故障保护是什么？在回答这个
问题之前，我们必须确定该计划想要实现的目标：提高绩效。如果没有
意图，就不会出现可接受的偏离计划的情况。 当我们了解计划的真正
目的时，我们就可以确定与计划的偏差是可以容忍的。 如果不了解我
们离目标有多远，就很难评估巨大的偏差。 没有

an objective, there is no direction and therefore no boundaries to stay within.
Statistics has a term for the process: standard deviation. This is the
deviation from the group as a whole, in this case, from the original plan.
Standard deviation goes both ways: in one direction, you can do too much; in
another direction, you can do too little. For critical drop-off, the standard
deviation is the range we need to work within to be successful in any plan we
have set. Looking at the intended outcome as point B, standard deviation
creates parameters that we have to reroute along the way to point B. Ideally,
we want as many people to get to point B as efficiently and safely as
possible. So we need to know when someone is not capable of executing the
predetermined plan and what tolerable deviation from the plan allows them to
stay on course.
We need to make consistently good decisions within a specific time frame.
If we know our intended outcome, we can make natural variances in training
person-to-person, which gives us confidence to break from the plan. We are
still moving forward. Training is about delayed gratification; we have to wait
for the outcome. The things we do in training are based on its premise; it is a
means to an end. Training is not an end in itself. Training only matters in
context to something else; with that said, a deviation from a plan for the
greater good, therefore, becomes a priority if it is moving us closer to the
objective.
We have to build in ranges, much like the acute-to-chronic ratio, 0.8 to
1.3, to work within. On one end of the spectrum, we have a minimal effective
dose, and on the other end, we have a maximal effective dose. This creates
the range to work within. On the maximum end, the range would evaluate
fail-safe procedures: If the athlete is no longer producing x force or x
velocity, we shut down operations. This is the point of critical drop-off. It has
a built-in mechanism to determine objectively that this protocol is no longer
effective. On the low end, we have established velocity and intensity brackets
and rep ranges to work with. In this way, we have a high and low range to
ensure we are doing enough but not too much.
Next is to have a debrief about why the operation had to stop or be altered.
This goes back to what the actual purpose of training is. Without a clear
understanding of the goal of training, we cannot make acceptable ranges to

没有目标，没有方向，因此没有界限。
统计中有一个术语来描述该过程：standard deviation。 这是与整个
团队的偏差，在本例中是与原始计划的偏差。标准差是双向的：在一个
方向上，你可以做得太多；在另一个方向上，你可以做得太多。从另一
个方向来说，你能做的太少了。 对于临界下降，标准差是我们在制定
的任何计划中取得成功所需的工作范围。 将预期结果视为 B 点，标准
偏差创建了我们必须沿到达 B 点的路线重新路由的参数。理想情况下，
我们希望尽可能多的人尽可能高效、安全地到达 B 点。因此，我们需要
知道某人何时无法执行预定计划，以及在多大程度上可以容忍偏离计划
才能让他们保持正轨。
我们需要在特定的时间范围内做出始终如一的正确决策。如果我们知
道我们的预期结果，我们就可以在人与人之间的训练中做出自然的变化
，这让我们有信心打破计划。 我们仍在前进。培训是关于延迟满足的
；我们必须等待结果。我们在训练中所做的事情都是基于它的前提；这
是达到目的的手段。 培训本身并不是目的。 培训只在与其他事物相关
的情况下才重要； 话虽如此，如果偏离更大利益的计划能够使我们更
接近目标，那么它就成为优先事项。
我们必须建立一个范围，就像急性与慢性的比率一样，0.8 到 1.3，以
便在其中工作。在该范围的一端，我们有最小有效剂量，在另一端，我
们有最大有效剂量。 这创造了工作范围。 在最大范围内，该范围将评
估故障安全程序：如果运动员不再产生 x 力或 x 速度，我们将关闭操作
。这是临界下降点。它有一个内置机制来客观地确定该协议不再有效。
在低端，我们建立了速度和强度范围以及重复范围。 这样，我们就有
了一个高低范围，以确保我们做得足够但又不过分。

接下来是汇报为什么必须停止或改变行动。这又回到了训练的真正目
的是什么。 如果没有清楚地了解培训目标，我们就无法制定可接受的
范围

work within. We can only fix something after we find out what was wrong.
We cannot make the call on cutting a set, going lighter, or getting more rest if
we do not know the athlete understood what or why they were doing
something. We also do not know what the athlete is walking in with before
training; this will have a profound effect on the training threshold. We have
to justify our decisions with an objective. Understanding that wellness scores
were down is better than just feeling like they were off. We can see the
impact of seeing a number and adjusting it more clearly.
Having access to tools helps. A good velocity-based training monitor,
force plates, GPS, heart rate monitor, or whatever is out there makes this
process of toggling variables more objective. The three outcomes will be to
drop intensity, cut volume, or decrease density. That adjustment can be
random and not vetted properly. Hardware detaches the human element from
the appearance of arbitrarily saying, stop, rest more, or go lighter. It makes
the response to critical drop-off more objective. Having a target speed for
each rep makes it easier to say to the athlete, “Your bar speed is down; do we
need to go lighter or get more rest?” We cannot objectively eyeball these
things over time.

Rep Brackets
The ability to progress from one week to the next is largely
based on when a critical drop-off might occur. Before we decide
how much we should progress, we need to evaluate what the
acceptable standard deviation is from the set. This is referred to
as set integrity, the ability to perform each rep within a set with
optimal technique and at a stimulating intensity.
Set integrity determines what a good set is and establishes
criteria to hold that standard. The criteria to determine what is
good are based on understanding the movement pattern and
what constitutes good technique. Intensity has a significant
impact on set integrity and the ability to sustain good technique.
The most important aspect of set integrity is that we hit all the
reps within the set that we were supposed to. If the set calls for a

代表括号
从一周到下一周的进步能力很大程度上取决于何时可能发生严重
下降。在我们决定应该进步多少之前，我们需要评估可接受的标
准偏差是多少。这被称为 set integrity，即以最佳技术和刺激强度
执行一组内每次重复的能力。
集合完整性决定了什么是好的集合，并建立了保持该标准的标
准。 确定什么是好的标准是基于理解运动模式和什么是好的技术
。 强度对设定的完整性和维持良好技术的能力有重大影响。整组
完整性最重要的方面是我们完成了整组中我们应该做的所有次数
。如果集合需要一个

specific number of reps, our ability to hit all those reps with great
technique at a specific intensity determines the outcome. Using a
certain number of reps or TUT (time under tension) is intended
for a specific outcome (see chapter 17). If we lose technique due
to the high intensity, we alter the outcome. Set integrity ensures
we get what we want from our training programs.
One area we have to be realistic with is that when pushing to
the threshold, we may not always be perfect. The entire premise
of pushing something to maximal and possibly supramaximal
levels is that we have to adapt to stress greater than we are
accustomed to. Ideally, we choose sustainable progressions that
we can maintain set integrity at all times. While still creating an
optimal amount of adaptation. This, however, is not always the
case.
Critical drop-off is how we determine what constitutes an
acceptable deviation from perfect set integrity. We want to stay
within a certain standard deviation to ensure we are still working
on what we intended to work on. This gives us a range to work
within and to determine the rate and amount of progression in
the next training session. With volume, we accomplish this with
rep brackets. This gives us a high (optimal) and low (bottom of
acceptable deviation) to work within. If the athlete can hit more
reps than the high end of the rep bracket, they should go up in
the next training session. If they miss the low end of the range of
the rep bracket, they need to either stay the same weight or
possibly go down in weight in the next training session.
Rep brackets give points of context for the athlete to work
within. Focus fluctuates from the beginning to the end of a
training session. A missed rep could be caused by the athlete
not adapting enough to handle that level of stress, or it could be
that they lost focus during a set. An important consideration for
coaching rep brackets is reengaging the athlete to encourage
them to hit all their reps during a set to maintain rep integrity or
simply understanding that the athlete is not present physically or

Rep brackets go from smaller ranges with lower rep sets to
larger ranges with higher rep sets (figure 7.1). With more reps in
a set, more can go wrong. We need larger brackets with higher
rep sets for all the variables that could happen during a set that
lasts longer. However, lowered rep sets are matched with higher
intensity. With higher external load or faster speeds, the margin
for error is smaller, so the bracket is reduced. Rep brackets
adjust to when and where set integrity is most vulnerable to
being compromised.

First, ask yourself, does the athlete know what the target range is? Not
knowing happens quite a lot. It can easily get lost in the list of things, from
movement prep to exercise demonstrations, sets and reps, tempo, rest,
exercise order, schedule changes, cool down, and finally, an epic team break
in a program. Important details can be easily forgotten or overlooked. Next,

what was prescribed, this could be considered a good thing but could easily
turn into a very bad thing. It could be ego, or it could be a simple
misunderstanding, but either way, if the bar is slow and not in line with the
goal, the countermeasure is to ensure they make the necessary changes to
move faster. The point of a coach during a training session is to keep athletes
on track and lifting with good technique to ensure safety. It also involves
understanding the objective and keeping the athletes on track to achieve it
(figure 7.5).

Force
Force is the biomotor ability that we need to be most conscious of regarding
biomechanics. The quality being trained is absolute strength, relative
strength, or functional hypertrophy. These are all slower contractions,
therefore making it easier to see the critical drop-off than other qualities.
Because it is slower, we can more readily interpret a drop in set integrity.

When in Doubt, Lower Intensity
Force is usually associated with heavier external loads, so if technique is not
looking the way we want, decreasing the thing that caused it to go wrong in
the first place is the most logical solution. Decreasing external load is the
simplest and most logical way to improve technique from the coach to the
athlete. Generally, athletes and coaches can readily come to a consensus on
external load causing aberrant motion and agree that lowering weight is the

图 7.5 设置完整性。

力量
力是我们在生物力学方面最需要意识到的生物运动能力。 所训练的素
质是绝对力量、相对力量或功能性肥大。 这些都是较慢的收缩，因此
比其他质量更容易看到临界下降。因为它速度较慢，所以我们可以更容
易地解释集合完整性的下降。

当有疑问时，降低强度
力通常与较重的外部负载相关，因此，如果技术没有达到我们想要的方
式，首先减少导致其出错的因素是最合乎逻辑的解决方案。 从教练到
运动员，减少外部负荷是提高技术最简单、最合理的方法。 一般来说
，运动员和教练员很容易就外部负荷导致异常运动达成共识，并同意减
轻体重是解决问题的方法。

fastest and most direct way to fix the problem.
The most obvious indicator would be reduced ROM (range of motion).
Several reasons contribute to reduced ROM, but the most obvious is
uncertainty about being able to complete the lift at a larger ROM. The
elephant in the room is, what is that reduced ROM relative to? Full ROM
strategies mean many things. The biomechanics of the big three joint types in
most compound movements, including the shoulder and hip (ball and socket),
elbow and knee (hinge), and wrist and ankle (saddle) joints, all have
directional capacity. Ball-and-socket joints flex and extend, internally and
externally rotate, and abduct and adduct; hinge joints flex and extend
(primarily); and saddle joints flex and extend (primarily). The joint’s function
allows for a certain amount of ROM.
Each of those joints, in theory, is only limited by skeletal structures around
the joint. For instance, knee flexion is limited by the femur making contact
with the tibia and fibula. The premise of each movement pattern taken to its
joint’s natural limits is the foundation for whatever constitutes full ROM.
Once we get into the movement pattern, some aspects affect reaching each
joint’s limits. We do have other tissues, such as connective tissue, fascia, and
muscle tissue, that may affect or obstruct movement. There could be motor
pattern development reasons that we reduce ROM. The most important
variable is that ROM during training is pretty relative to the environment.
Intensity should not be the deciding factor for full ROM.

Leveraging Intent
The biggest misconceptions about force is that
we do not need a large external load to create
force.
Intent is the most important factor in creating force. We focus on the task; we
give our best effort to engage with the rep, and the external load becomes
obsolete. This is proven during our intent’s effect on force during isokinetic
or isometric contractions. We create peak tension based on our desire to

解决问题的最快、最直接的方法。
最明显的指标是 ROM（运动范围）的减少。导致ROM减少的原因有
很多，但最明显的是能否以更大的ROM完成举重的不确定性。 房间里
的大象是，减少的 ROM 相对于什么？ 完整的 ROM 策略意味着很多事
情。大多数复合运动中的三大关节类型的生物力学，包括肩部和髋部（
球窝）、肘部和膝部（铰链）以及腕部和踝部（鞍形）关节，都具有定
向能力。 球窝关节可弯曲和伸展、内旋和外旋、外展和内收； 铰链关
节弯曲和伸展（主要）；和鞍状关节弯曲和伸展（主要）。关节的功能
允许一定量的 ROM。

理论上，这些关节中的每一个仅受关节周围的骨骼结构的限制。 例
如，膝盖弯曲受到与胫骨和腓骨接触的股骨的限制。每个运动模式达到
其关节自然极限的前提是构成完整 ROM 的基础。一旦我们进入运动模
式，某些方面就会影响每个关节的极限。我们确实有其他组织，例如结
缔组织、筋膜和肌肉组织，可能会影响或阻碍运动。 我们减少 ROM 可
能是由于运动模式发展的原因。 最重要的变量是训练期间的 ROM 与环
境密切相关。强度不应该成为完整ROM的决定因素。

利用意图
关于力的最大误解是我们不需要很大的外部载荷来产生
力。

意图是创造力量的最重要因素。我们专注于任务；我们尽最大努力与销
售代表互动，外部负载就变得过时了。 这在等速或等长收缩期间我们
的意图对力的影响中得到了证明。 我们根据我们的愿望创造峰值张力

recruit a muscle, not on how heavy something is. The result of training is that
we get better without load from the development of patterns. When the load
is increased, we have the pattern and contractile tissue to accomplish the task.
We can use heavier loads after we understand how to leverage intent.
Regardless of the reduced ROM coming from full ROM or partial ROM,
when an athlete adopts reduced ROM, the best option is to respond by
lowering intensity. Reducing ROM is not the best option because it lowers
work. When the athlete has to adopt a strategy to accommodate the external
load, and they reduce ROM, they decrease total distance, resulting in a
reduction in total work. It is the coach’s job to ensure that there is a standard
of execution for each movement based on full ROM. Changes in strategies
are only noticeable if there is a consistent pattern to begin with. A coach’s job
is to emphasize the standard, so when the athlete reaches a threshold, we have
a better understanding of what is no longer effective. When the athlete can no
longer uphold the standard, we need to change the strategy.
Traditionally, reduced ROM is associated with an altered position. The
other aspect of joints is how they affect movement when they are not moving.
This comes with the joints that are attempting to stabilize during movement.
Stabilization of body segments through positional control ensures localized
tension. When we can no longer maintain that tension, we adopt a strategy to
find a more mechanically advantageous position and divert that tension
elsewhere. Shifting the center of mass or trying to gain a mechanical
advantage, we lower the stress in the targeted area. If we look at ROM as a
component of work, we can look at stabilization as a component of localized,
targeted work.
Reduced ROM affects the mechanical advantage of going through a ROM
that uses the contractile tissues with the highest distribution of sarcomeres.
We also see this by shifting the center of mass forward and back to
accommodate the length–tension relationships. You see this all the time:
squats where the torso drops or hinges where the knees come forward. This is
the body reacting to the length (ROM) it was placed in, combined with the
external load placed on it. If the capacity of contractile tissue is surpassed, we
adopt a strategy of altered position to find contractile tissue that can complete
the movement.

锻炼肌肉，而不是根据某物的重量。训练的结果是我们在没有模式开发
负担的情况下变得更好。 当负荷增加时，我们就有了完成任务的模式
和收缩组织。在了解如何利用意图后，我们可以使用更重的负载。
无论减少的活动范围是来自完整的活动范围还是部分的活动范围，当
运动员采用减少的活动范围时，最好的选择是通过降低强度来应对。
减少 ROM 并不是最好的选择，因为它会减少工作量。 当运动员必须采
取适应外部负荷的策略时，他们会减少活动范围，从而减少总距离，从
而减少总做功。教练的工作是确保每个动作都有一个基于完整ROM的执
行标准。 只有一开始就存在一致的模式，策略的变化才会引人注目。
教练的工作是强调标准，因此当运动员达到阈值时，我们可以更好地了
解什么不再有效。当运动员无法再坚持标准时，我们就需要改变策略。

传统上，活动范围的减少与位置的改变有关。 关节的另一个方面是
它们在不移动时如何影响运动。这与在运动过程中试图稳定的关节有关
。通过位置控制稳定身体各部分，确保局部张力。当我们无法再维持这
种紧张时，我们会采取一种策略来寻找机械上更有利的位置，并将这种
紧张转移到其他地方。 通过转移质心或试图获得机械优势，我们可以
降低目标区域的应力。 如果我们将 ROM 视为工作的一个组成部分，那
么我们就可以将稳定性视为本地化、有针对性的工作的一个组成部分。

ROM 减少会影响使用肌节分布最高的收缩组织的 ROM 的机械优势
。我们还通过前后移动质心以适应长度-张力关系来看到这一点。 你经
常会看到这样的情况：在躯干下降的地方深蹲，或者在膝盖向前的地方
铰链。这是物体对其所处长度 (ROM) 以及施加在其上的外部负载的反
应。如果超过收缩组织的能力，我们采取改变位置的策略来寻找可以完
成运动的收缩组织。

This is problematic for several reasons. Injury risk is assuredly increased.
It does not take a veteran coach to see that compromised positions under load
can increase risk. Another reason is the long-term effect of becoming
structurally imbalanced. When we adopt a strategy of altered position to
accommodate the external load, we shift our body’s levers to accommodate
the tension, creating an imbalance over time that disrupts the premise of
structural balance, which allocates tension evenly. We want progressive
overload, not excessive loading, leading to reduced ROM or altered positions.
Therefore, lowering the intensity of the exercise is a really important strategy
when we reach the critical drop-off.
The big three of critical drop-off are missing reps,
missed velocity, and missed intensity.
The previously established standard of movement is the basis for the
success of the task. Hitting the full rep scheme with an altered position or
reduced ROM is a missed rep. Reducing ROM at a certain external load to hit
a certain velocity or intensity is a missed rep. Missing reps lose set integrity,
and we lose the potential impact.
The biggest overreaction with force and critical
drop-off is the perception that effort is more
valuable than the accomplishment of the task.
Confusing activity with accomplishment is a problem with fitness. Trying
and failing is not the goal. The goal is to have a plan and push yourself within
that plan. You will fail, but you are more the product of your training
accomplishments, or completed reps. I could put any weight on the bar at any
given moment and fail. It is much harder to continuously hit your reps each
set, training session, week, month, and year, but it will lead to longer-term
success.
Aside from the technical aspect, we need to use rep ranges to

由于多种原因，这是有问题的。受伤风险肯定会增加。不需要经验丰
富的教练就能看出，在负荷下妥协的位置会增加风险。 另一个原因是
结构失衡的长期影响。 当我们采取改变体位的策略来适应外部负荷时
，我们会改变身体的杠杆来适应张力，随着时间的推移会产生不平衡，
从而破坏结构平衡的前提，而结构平衡是均匀分配张力的。 我们希望
渐进式超负荷，而不是过度负荷，从而导致活动范围减少或位置改变。
因此，当我们达到临界下降时，降低运动强度是一个非常重要的策略。

严重下降的三大因素是缺少重复次数、缺少速度和缺少
强度。
先前建立的运动标准是任务成功的基础。 改变位置或减少活动范围
来完成完整的代表计划是一次错过的代表。在一定的外部负载下减少 R
OM 以达到一定的速度或强度是一个错过的代表。缺少代表会失去设定
的完整性，我们也会失去潜在的影响。

对武力和严重下降的最大过度反应是认为努力比完成任
务更有价值。

将活动与成就混为一谈是健身的一个问题。尝试和失败并不是目标。
目标是制定一个计划并推动自己遵守该计划。 你会失败，但你更多的
是你的训练成就或完成的代表的产物。我可以在任何特定时刻将任何重
量放在杠上，但都会失败。 连续完成每组、每节训练、每周、每月和
每年的重复次数要困难得多，但它将带来长期的成功。
除了技术方面之外，我们还需要使用代表范围来

accommodate “mulligan” reps and sets. Focus during a lift goes in waves.
Focus during various parts of the year wavers. Playing the law of averages,
large groups, tons of training sessions, and a potentially poor coach-to-athlete
ratio will lead to diminished quality control. Having the ability as a coach to
ask if the athlete missed the rep because they lost track of what they were
doing is an opportunity to avoid an unnecessary pivot.
It is worth discussing rep ranges (brackets), at least from the context of
explaining them to your athletes. Rep ranges are the most available method,
barring athletes knowing what a missed rep looks like, to explain critical
drop-off. It is the tolerable limit to assess if the intensity is too much or too
little. If the athlete misses a rep or if there is a large discrepancy between reps
completed with rep integrity and reps prescribed, it is too heavy. If the athlete
hits all the reps in the set with rep integrity and there are still several extra
reps in reserve that the athlete can hit, it is too light. We want to hit that sweet
spot of training intensity by using a load that hits the second, or larger,
number in that range. We want to hit the larger number but cannot go way
past that. If they are within range, we won’t have to use a contingency plan
and can progress the following week.
Critical drop-off with force will be more obvious than with velocity due to
the speed at which the movement is executed. The issue with something like
force is that there will be an impulse to encourage the athlete to rise to the
occasion. Due to the slower nature, coaches will have a greater inclination to
try to motivate the athlete to execute the movement. Context matters. If it is
the end of the off-season or mesocycle, the net impact from a coach’s
motivation tactics might be marginal at best. Earlier in the off-season or
mesocycle might mean we need to push our athletes to rise to the challenge.
Relying on objective aspects makes it easier for the coach to avoid
subjectively resorting to tactics that push athletes past their adaptive
potential, which can be the difference between good and bad programs.

What Is Adaptation?
What is the point of all this? Why train or organize training with
such detail? We do it very simply to adapt positively. The hope is

适应“调度”次数和组数。 升降机过程中的注意力会呈波浪状。一年
中不同时期的焦点会发生波动。 遵循平均法则、大团体、大量的训练
课程以及可能较差的教练与运动员比例将导致质量控制下降。作为教练
，有能力询问运动员是否因为忘记自己在做什么而错过了代表，这是避
免不必要的转变的机会。
值得讨论次数范围（括号），至少从向运动员解释它们的角度来看是
这样。 次数范围是最可用的方法，除非运动员知道错过的次数是什么
样子，才能解释严重的下降。 这是评估强度是否过多或过少的可容忍
限度。如果运动员错过了一次，或者按照完整次数完成的次数与规定次
数之间存在较大差异，则说明重量过重。如果运动员以完整的次数完成
了该组中的所有次数，并且仍然有一些额外的次数可供运动员完成，那
么它就太轻了。我们希望通过使用达到该范围内第二个或更大数字的负
荷来达到训练强度的最佳点。 我们想要达到更大的数字，但不能超越
这个数字。 如果它们在范围内，我们就不必使用应急计划，并且可以
在下周取得进展。
由于执行运动的速度，力的临界下降比速度的临界下降更明显。像力
量这样的东西的问题在于，会产生鼓励运动员应对这种情况的冲动。由
于速度较慢，教练会更倾向于尝试激励运动员执行动作。 背景很重要
。 如果是在休赛期或中周期结束时，教练激励策略的净影响最多可能
是微乎其微的。 在休赛期或中周期的早期可能意味着我们需要推动我
们的运动员迎接挑战。依靠客观方面可以让教练更容易避免主观地采取
使运动员超越其适应潜力的策略，这可能是好项目和坏项目之间的区别
。

什么是适应？
这一切有什么意义呢？ 为什么要进行如此详细的培训或组织培训
？我们这样做很简单，就是为了积极适应。希望是

that the adaptation manifests into something better. If not, then
spending a second on organizing training is pointless.
The single most important determinant of adaptation is
progressive overload. Aside from the rate of adaptation or the
amount of adaptation, if we can make some progress from one
week to the next, we are adapting. It does not matter whether we
go up in reps, intensity, or do more work; if we are going up, we
are adapting.
Therefore, it is so important to have a point of diminishing
returns to ensure we are positively going up each week. We will
set a goal that exceeds the previous week’s, but we will not know
if it will happen until we start training. If it becomes apparent that
we cannot go up, we will need to find an alternative solution.
Think of diminishing returns as the intersection of adaptation
and lifestyle. If the athlete is not adequately prepared for the
day’s plan, our contingency plan will allow for future adaptation.
If we overshoot with training expectations, our contingency plan
will allow for future adaptation. These principles provide the
foundation for adaptation to our training.
Principles are the key to creating outcomes. The secret is to
find out how to adapt them in complex situations such as large
groups or large outside stressors.
This is the reality of diminishing returns; we need to fight the notion that
the psychological aspect of training will always be there. We cannot repeat
whatever button we pressed to inspire athletes, but we can look at when the
program’s performance is trailing off. Reduced ROM, altered positions,
missed reps, and decreased velocity are all more objective measures than a
coach’s ability to motivate an athlete. Autonomy for the athlete, combined
with objective evaluation of execution, should build trust that we are doing
the best we can to reach the ultimate objective.

Velocity

适应会转化为更好的东西。 如果不是，那么花时间组织培训是毫
无意义的。
适应的最重要的决定因素是渐进性超负荷。 除了适应速度或适
应量之外，如果我们能够从一周到下一周取得一些进展，我们就
正在适应。无论我们增加次数、强度还是做更多的工作，这并不
重要。如果我们要向上，我们就在适应。
因此，有一个收益递减点非常重要，以确保我们每周都积极上
涨。我们会设定一个超过前一周的目标，但直到开始训练我们才
会知道它是否会发生。如果我们明显无法上升，我们将需要找到
替代解决方案。
将收益递减视为适应与生活方式的交叉点。 如果运动员没有为
当天的计划做好充分准备，我们的应急计划将为未来的调整做好
准备。如果我们超出了培训预期，我们的应急计划将允许未来进
行调整。 这些原则为适应我们的培训奠定了基础。
原则是创造成果的关键。 秘诀在于找出如何使它们适应复杂的
情况，例如大群体或巨大的外部压力。

这就是收益递减的现实；我们需要与这样一种观念作斗争，即训练的
心理方面永远存在。 我们不能重复按下任何按钮来激励运动员，但我
们可以看看该计划的表现何时开始下降。 活动范围减少、位置改变、
重复次数减少和速度下降都是比教练激励运动员的能力更客观的衡量标
准。 运动员的自主权与对执行力的客观评估相结合，应该建立起我们
正在尽最大努力实现最终目标的信任。

速度

Velocity-focused training is a lot faster than force-focused training, so seeing
technical aspects is a lot harder. We have to rely on more objectivity for
critical drop-off. The technique is critical, especially since moving at a higher
rate with technical flaws increases risk.

When in Doubt, Rest More
More than likely, velocity critical drop-off is a density issue. We are simply
not resting enough in between reps. Moving at high rates requires more than
just effort; it requires a significant amount from the central nervous system
(CNS). The CNS takes considerably longer than the muscular system to
recover from activity. Estimates can be as high as 6 to 10 times longer
(Poliquin, 2013). This creates a logistics problem.
When working with college or even professional athletes, attention spans
can be limited. Adding the element of multiple people training at the same
time can amplify decreased attention. The combination of short attention
spans and large groups with coaches who have a certain expectation of
training being fun and engaging can lead to rapidly declining rest periods. I
am not saying that we cannot find creative ways to get 3 to 5 min of rest
between maximal sprints; I am saying it is not as easy as you say, and they
do. There is a tradeoff between quality and decreasing rest periods. There is
also a tradeoff between standing around for 300 s waiting for your next sprint
and staying focused. Critical drop-off is a better proxy for determining how
short is too short for rest periods.
This leads to a problem with density management. In short, we rush rest
periods because we have to in large groups. We can overjustify this by saying
we need adequate tissue temperature or a certain heart rate recovery between
reps. The bottom line is that if performance is going down, it was probably
not enough rest. Physiologically, you will see this manifest with longer
ground contact times during sprints or jumps. Biomechanically, you will see
this by adopting altered positions to either create more momentum or gain
mechanical advantage. Pushing hips back when attempting to jump vertically
or standing up when attempting to accelerate are all clear signs of diminished
quality, which will affect the performance. If you are looking for a metric on
a force plate, you may see impulse (time × force) stay the same or go up, but

以速度为中心的训练比以力量为中心的训练要快得多，因此了解技术方
面要困难得多。 对于关键的下降，我们必须更加客观。该技术至关重
要，特别是因为技术缺陷导致的高速移动会增加风险。

当有疑问时，多休息
速度临界下降很可能是一个密度问题。 我们在代表之间休息得不够。
高速前进需要的不仅仅是努力；还需要努力。 它需要中枢神经系统（C
NS）提供大量的能量。 中枢神经系统从活动中恢复所需的时间比肌肉
系统长得多。 估计时间可能会延长 6 至 10 倍（Poliquin，2013 年）。
这就产生了物流问题。
当与大学甚至职业运动员一起工作时，注意力的持续时间可能会受到
限制。 添加多人同时训练的元素可以放大注意力下降的情况。 注意力
持续时间短、团体人数多、教练期望训练有趣、有吸引力，这两者结合
在一起可能会导致休息时间迅速缩短。 我并不是说我们无法找到创造
性的方法来在最大冲刺之间获得 3 到 5 分钟的休息时间； 我是说这并
不像你说的那么容易，而他们却做到了。 在质量和减少休息时间之间
需要权衡。 在等待下一个冲刺 300 秒和保持专注之间也需要权衡。 临
界下降是确定休息时间多短是否太短的更好指标。

这导致了密度管理的问题。 简而言之，我们会匆忙休息，因为我们
必须成群结队。我们可以通过说我们需要足够的组织温度或重复次数之
间一定的心率恢复来夸大这一点。 最重要的是，如果表现下降，可能
是休息不够。 从生理上讲，您会在冲刺或跳跃期间较长的接触地面时
间中看到这一点。从生物力学角度来看，你会通过改变姿势来创造更多
动力或获得机械优势来看到这一点。尝试垂直跳跃时向后推臀部或尝试
加速时站立都是质量下降的明显迹象，这会影响表现。如果您正在寻找
测力台上的指标，您可能会看到冲量（时间 × 力）保持不变或上升，但
是

the reactive strength index (time on a plate versus time in the air) goes down.
If we are looking to improve the rate of force development, we need faster
movements to facilitate that.
The biggest overreaction with velocity is that
moving in general is the goal.
Speed versus quickness is a hot-button issue in S&C. It really should not
be. Quickness may or may not involve displacement. Speed always involves
displacement. There is a skill associated with moving quickly without much
displacement, which is facilitated by repetition. Creating a greater
displacement at a faster speed produces something more objective. Moving in
general is a great way to produce work, but if that is not the goal, then
velocity is not the goal. Getting somewhere that is usually farther away at a
faster rate is the primary reason we need to train velocity.
A primary issue with decreased rest intervals is that we do not care until it
is too late. The point of no return with a high rate of force development
activity is injury. We cannot turn back the clock and say we wish we rested
more or cut the set sooner when someone gets hurt (figure 7.6). We need to
be objective and probably be overly cautious with velocity because the risk is
flat-out higher. It is higher because we are in an environment that does not
want long rest periods. Team settings always want to go, go, and go some
more. Managing CNS in a group environment is easily the most challenging
aspect of an S&C coach’s job.

反应强度指数（在盘子上的时间与在空气中的时间）下降。如果我们希
望提高部队发展速度，我们需要更快的行动来实现这一目标。

对速度最大的过度反应是总体上移动是目标。

速度与速度是施恩禧的一个热点问题。 确实不应该。速度可能涉及
也可能不涉及位移。速度总是涉及位移。 有一种技巧可以快速移动而
不会产生太大的位移，而重复可以促进这种技巧的实现。 以更快的速
度创造更大的位移会产生更客观的结果。一般来说，移动是一种产生工
作的好方法，但如果这不是目标，那么速度就不是目标。 通常以更快
的速度到达更远的地方是我们需要训练速度的主要原因。
减少休息时间的一个主要问题是我们不关心，直到为时已晚。 高发
力活动率的不归路就是受伤。 当有人受伤时，我们不能倒转过去，说
我们希望多休息或早点结束比赛（图 7.6）。 我们需要保持客观，并且
可能对速度过于谨慎，因为风险明显更高。 它更高是因为我们所处的
环境不需要长时间的休息。 团队设置总是想走、走、再走。在团队环
境中管理 CNS 无疑是 S&C 教练工作中最具挑战性的方面。

FIGURE 7.6 Increasing rest tactics.
Your appraisal of the situation is critical to preventing unwanted injuries.
The best predictor of a future injury is a previous injury. You are wearing
white gloves with athletes who have an injury history during higher-rate force
development activities. We are in a situation where we are working with
larger groups with low attention spans, and the probability of mistakes is
amplified. We need to appraise the relative risk for everyone participating,
and the previous injury means a higher risk. Their critical drop-off is faster
and more volume based overall. Your ability to stop something entirely as
soon as it becomes something you do not want is necessary for the greater
good.

overall intensities; lighter things move faster. This is a much more sensitive
zone to rest than absolute strength. A great example of this is dynamic effort
