FIGURE 7.7 Velocity zones.
In this example, we are rolling! When we get to set 8, we are dangerously
close to being out of our velocity zone. It could be training monotony and
athletes losing focus. Fatigue has accumulated, and the velocity potential has
dropped. We could do what we do with force and drop the weight, but the
weight is already at 35% of rep max. That would be a poor decision based on
using a lowered weight, because we are at such a low weight to begin with.
This leaves us with resting more or cutting the set entirely.
Resting more, in my opinion, is the best strategy. Group dynamics matter.
When you have three people rolling through 10 sets and one cannot keep up,
it is difficult for the athlete to feel like they are the weakest link. It is more
than likely that the athletes got ahead of themselves and rushed between sets.
That strategy was not a problem until it became a problem later in the
protocol. You could cut the set entirely, and this is not a bad decision. But
what if the athlete was working at a weight heavier than they should but did
not want to slow the group? Or what if the athlete did back-to-back lifts
because they had an event to be at over the weekend that they could not miss?
Context is really important in group dynamics. Having contingencies that
don’t necessarily alienate your athlete but still reach the target is superior
every time. In my experience, applying the rest tactics is the best strategy in a
situation like this. Give them more recovery and see what happens.
In the situation where the form breaks down entirely, you should cut the
set. You will see a form breakdown much earlier than a velocity drop. In part,
we are adjusting the form to meet the demand. We reduce ROM, we alter
position, or we flat-out improvise to hit the target. At that point, the more
important aspect is establishing that quality is more important than finishing a
protocol. What would be the point of finishing with substandard execution?
Are we fast with bad technique?

少活动范围，改变位置，或者全力以赴地即兴发挥以击中目标。 在这
一点上，更重要的方面是确定质量比完成协议更重要。 以不合格的执
行结束有何意义？我们技术差但速度快吗？

保持质量
The biggest misconception about velocity is that
finishing something with poor quality is a better

alternative than just stopping altogether.
The issue again is associated with increased risk. Not only is it a much more
refined skill to move with higher speeds, but we also have less margin to do
things wrong and get away with it. We have to acknowledge that increasing
someone’s rate of movement is much more challenging than increasing the
amount they can move. Moving fast with bad quality will lead to poorly
developed motor patterns. High rates of force amplify the impact.
Velocity critical drop-off is probably of more importance than force with
critical drop-off due to the potentially increased risk. You can simply get
away with more if it is slower, not so much when it is faster. The harder part
is that it is a lot less clear when to stop something. Chances are, you just need
to rest more in between sets. Microcycle setup (see chapter 18) matters a
great deal here as well.

Work
Work is what we call conditioning in the team settings. We intentionally
move more during a training session or go longer during a set to elicit a
stimulus for both the bioenergetic and cardiorespiratory systems. It is also the
area that has the biggest impact on microcycle and mesocycle fatigue rates
and levels. I’ll explain more about this later. At any given time, it will be the
most important thing you do and at the same time, the biggest afterthought.

When in Doubt, Cut Volume
Work is important; I hope we have established that. But in the team setting,
we have to account for the lowest and highest common denominators
simultaneously. Chances are that we are conditioning the least fit and giving
an easy day to the most fit during the same session. The coach will have to
choose whether to program up to the best-fit athlete or down to the worst-fit
athlete. This creates a paradox.
If we program up to the best-fit athlete, we place a large risk on the less fit
athlete. It is a combination of both the velocity and capacity of the more fit
athlete that places the less fit athlete in such a compromised state. The less fit

alternative than just stopping altogether.
这个问题又与风险增加有关。以更高的速度移动不仅是一项更加精细的
技能，而且我们做错事并侥幸逃脱的余地也更小。 我们必须承认，增
加某人的移动速度比增加他们的移动量更具挑战性。 质量差的快速移
动会导致运动模式发育不良。高比率的武力会放大影响。
由于潜在的风险增加，速度临界下降可能比临界下降的力更重要。
如果速度较慢，您可以简单地逃脱更多，但如果速度较快，则不会那么
多。更困难的部分是，何时停止某些事情还不太清楚。很可能，你只需
要在组间休息更多。 微循环设置（参见第 18 章）在这里也很重要。

工作
工作就是我们在团队设置中所说的conditioning。 我们故意在训练过程
中移动更多，或者在一组训练中走得更久，以刺激生物能量和心肺系统
。这也是对微循环和中循环疲劳率和水平影响最大的区域。稍后我将对
此进行更多解释。在任何特定时间，这都将是您所做的最重要的事情，
同时也是最重要的事后想法。

如有疑问，请减少音量
工作很重要； 我希望我们已经确定了这一点。 但在团队环境中，我们
必须同时考虑最低和最高公分母。很可能我们会在同一训练期间对最不
健康的人进行训练，并让最健康的人度过轻松的一天。 教练必须选择
是针对最适合的运动员还是针对最差的运动员进行训练。这就产生了一
个悖论。
如果我们为最健康的运动员制定计划，那么我们就会给不太健康的运
动员带来很大的风险。 正是健康状况较好的运动员的速度和能力的结
合，使健康状况较差的运动员处于如此妥协的状态。越不适合

athlete has to work harder to keep up and lacks the fitness to recover between
reps and sets. Group dynamics are tough with someone who is the proverbial
slow person. It places a lot of pressure on the coach to either motivate them to
push past their level or slow the rest of the group to accommodate their lack
of ability. Often, our best option is to motivate the least fit to try to keep up
and not slow down the group. Chances are, the weaker link for the athlete
slowing down the group is fitness, and that is the best strategy to employ. We
live in an imperfect world with team training, and we have to find the best
solution for the situation.
If we program down to the worst-fit athlete’s level, we are essentially
wasting the time of the best-fit athlete. Or so we think. Having a session
programmed for someone with poorer fitness levels to accommodate
recovery can be extremely slow and sometimes boring for the best-fit athlete.
We increase the rest periods organically through staging rest tactics. It is the
smarter play. We lower the risk associated with work in a group setting for
the faster-twitch athlete. We also avoid overexerting that athlete, leading to
better performance in the next training session.
Work is the core of the microcycle. We are the product of what we can do
during a training session and a training week. To increase the capacity during
either a training session or a microcycle, we will need higher fitness levels.
Therefore, we need to develop chronic workloads. We need to ensure that we
allow for adequate rest in between high CNS training sessions. We expedite
the need for rest by having increased chronic workload levels (fitness). The
idea of being able to make sessions denser because we can recover faster
leads to higher ceilings of performance. The other aspect allows us to develop
concurrently multiple qualities without derailing progress to the end of a
macrocycle.
Having capacity training sessions during a microcycle allows for rest from
more power training sessions. If we do too much following a power or high
CNS day, we will risk increasing residual fatigue that will affect the next high
CNS day. High CNS days will have a larger systemic impact on the more
advanced athletes. These athletes exert more and tax the CNS more than
novice athletes. Therefore, it is so important to take a conservative approach
to work; it protects the athletes. We can protect our faster-twitch athletes by

Central Nervous System Impact
The biggest misconception about work is the
impact of higher CNS days on fitness.
We improve fitness during high CNS days, not to the extent of a lowerintensity, longer-duration volume day, but fitness adaptations are occurring.
With that said, we should look at critical drop-off as a means to assess the
level of fitness. If we are reaching critical drop-off earlier than we should
during anaerobic phosphagen work, we have lost the recoverability between
bouts and sets (figure 7.8). Our recovery rates are based on fitness, which is
oxidative capacity. If we are struggling to recover between sets of anaerobic
phosphagen work, it comes down to not resting enough between sets, built-in
residual fatigue, or poor oxidative fitness.
Missed opportunities from high CNS days, from being overly fatigued
from previous sessions, or from having low aerobic fitness are a huge
problem. We only have so many high CNS days in an off-season; if even one
of them is of a lower quality, we are at a significant disadvantage going into
the season. Work is important; it becomes the primary facilitator to avoid a
critical drop-off in velocity or force. The better our capacity is, the more
power work we can do.

更加注重微循环内的能力建设，并在培训课程中应用有机休息策略。

对中枢神经系统的影响
关于工作的最大误解是较高的中枢神经系统天数对健身
的影响。
我们在中枢神经系统高强度的日子里改善了体能，但没有达到低强度、
持续时间较长的训练日的程度，但体能适应正在发生。话虽如此，我们
应该将临界下降视为评估健康水平的一种手段。 如果我们在无氧磷酸
原训练期间比应有的时间更早地达到临界下降，我们就失去了比赛和组
数之间的可恢复性（图 7.8）。我们的恢复率基于健康状况，即氧化能
力。如果我们在无氧磷酸原训练之间难以恢复，则可以归结为组间休息
不足、内在的残余疲劳或氧化适应性差。
错过中枢神经系统高强度日、之前训练过度疲劳或有氧运动水平低的
机会都是一个大问题。淡季我们只有这么多 CNS 高的日子；如果其中
一个质量较低，我们在进入赛季时就会处于明显的劣势。 工作很重要
； 它成为避免速度或力量严重下降的主要促进者。 我们的能力越好，
我们能做的功就越多。

FIGURE 7.8 Training session pacing.
Stopping a running session or cutting sets will not be received the same
way as stopping something related to force or velocity. There are strategies
we can use to stop or cut the volume of a session without it appearing as
though we are just randomly stopping.
One of the biggest overreactions to work is the
idea that stopping is a failure.
Stopping, when strategically planned and objectively evaluated, is by far
the most important thing you can do regarding work in the off-season.
Having a fail-safe for the worst-conditioned athletes places everyone,
including the coach, in a much better spot to get value from the training
session. Stopping for the more advanced, probably faster-twitch athletes is
the best thing to ensure less fatigue going into the next high CNS day. Being

图 7.8 训练课程节奏。
停止跑步或切割组的接收方式与停止与力或速度相关的操作不同。
我们可以使用一些策略来停止或减少会话的音量，而不会显得我们只是
随机停止。

对工作最大的过度反应之一就是认为停止就是失败。

经过战略性规划和客观评估后，停下来是迄今为止您在淡季工作中可
以做的最重要的事情。为状态最差的运动员提供故障保护，可以让包括
教练在内的每个人都能更好地从训练中获得价值。 对于更高级、可能
是抽搐更快的运动员来说，停下来是确保在下一个中枢神经系统高强度
日减少疲劳的最佳方法。存在

unprepared or reactive is unprofessional. When you stop things based on an
irrational emotional response to something that triggers you, it will reduce
motivation. Looking at trends from wellness, workloads, and session
performance to adjust plans is smart.
Work, velocity, and force will be our focal points during the off-season.
The message regarding diminishing returns is that we should be married to
outcomes, not solutions. We need to understand that training is a means to an
end. The end is higher performance and more resilience. Lowering intensity,
cutting volume, and stopping a session are all justifiable actions to
accommodate the means. In reality, if we sacrifice short-term overreaching at
the expense of long-term adaptations, we compromise the entire premise of
training.
The diminishing return factors are summarized as follows:
Force
Biggest overreaction: Perception of effort is of more value than the
accomplishment of the task.
Biggest misconception: We do not need a large external load to create
force.
Velocity
Biggest overreaction: Moving, in general, is the goal.
Biggest misconceptions: Finishing something with poor quality is a
better alternative than just stopping altogether.
Work
Biggest overreaction: Stopping is failure.
Biggest misconception: Work has a high impact on CNS days due to
fitness.

Take Home
Because of diminishing returns, you must accept that at certain points, there
will be a crossroads for developing physical qualities and what is effective.
Physiology will reach a stopping point when we overreach for weeks and
months on end. Having a contingency that is readily available and easy to

没有准备或反应是不专业的。 当你基于对触发你的事情的非理性情绪
反应而停止事情时，就会降低动力。 查看健康状况、工作负载和训练
表现的趋势来调整计划是明智的做法。
训练、速度和力量将是休赛期我们的焦点。关于收益递减的信息是，
我们应该关注结果，而不是解决方案。我们需要明白，培训是达到目的
的一种手段。最终是更高的性能和更强的弹性。降低强度、减少训练量
和停止训练都是适应这些手段的合理行动。事实上，如果我们以牺牲长
期适应为代价来牺牲短期的过度扩张，那么我们就会损害训练的整个前
提。
收益递减因素总结如下：
力量
Biggest overreaction:对努力的感知比任务的完成更有价值。
Biggest misconception:我们不需要很大的外部负载来产生力。

速度
Biggest overreaction:一般来说，移动是目标。
Biggest misconceptions: 完成质量较差的事情是比完全停止更好的
选择。
工作
Biggest overreaction:停止就是失败。 Biggest misconception: 由于健
身，工作对 CNS 天数有很大影响。

带回家
由于收益递减，你必须接受这样的事实：在某些时候，发展身体素质和
什么是有效的将会有一个十字路口。当我们连续数周或数月过度活动时
，生理学将达到一个停止点。 拥有现成且易于处理的意外事件

implement, based on objective criteria that you can re-create, is paramount to
long-term success and safety. Critical drop-off point is that point where you,
the coach, are forced to make a decision on what to do when the original plan
is no longer effective.

基于您可以重新创建的客观标准来实施对于长期成功和安全至关重要。
关键的下降点是当最初的计划不再有效时，你作为教练被迫做出决定该
怎么做的点。

ELIMINATING NOISE
Judges make their most inaccurate sentencing decisions before lunch when
they are hungriest (Kahneman et al., 2021). If you think about that for a
second, this could be the most extreme example of poor decisions one could
make in the world. The fact that judges are people, probably the people we
need to make the best decisions, and can make mistakes simply because they
are hungry. What does that say for us strength and conditioning coaches?
Where are we most vulnerable to making bad training choices, and what
contingencies do we have to protect ourselves from making bad decisions?

Establishing Rules
Before we dive into rules and our contingencies, let’s examine their
relationship to principles. Remember, principles are true without context.
Therefore, principles are the foundation of your program because they are not
context dependent.

True Without Context
Show me a program without principles, and I will show you a bad program.
Show me a program without rules, and I will have to ask, “What context was
this written for?” How do you evaluate someone’s program? You start with
the principles of training. But as we know, that is not the only thing that
determines a good program. How do we evaluate the rest? We are going to go

事实上，法官也是人，可能是我们做出最佳决定所需要的人，并且可能
仅仅因为饥饿而犯错误。 这对我们体能教练来说意味着什么？我们在

制定规则

关系。 请记住，原则在没有上下文的情况下都是正确的。因此，原则

真实无上下文
给我一个没有原则的程序，我就会给你一个糟糕的程序。向我展示一个
没有规则的程序，我将不得不问，“这是为什么背景编写的？” 你如

through simple and agreed-upon rules, but the difference between rules and
principles is that we can strategically omit or break rules but not principles.
One of the best things about S&C is that so much is open for
interpretation. It is truly an amazing aspect that we have so much freedom
with the decisions we make when training someone. It demonstrates that
S&C is as much an art as it is a science. But there have to be some constraints
when creating a training program. Otherwise, we would have this complete
mismatch of training inputs and random, unexpected outputs. Without actual
constraints to training, outside of principles, we are potentially subject to a
significant disconnect from becoming a respected science. It becomes
exclusively subjective as to what is good or bad, and that is not repeatable
over time or with large groups.

Not Knowing and Not Doing Versus Knowing
and Not Doing
Ignorance is not knowing something. If you chose to do
something when it was wrong and you did not know it was
dangerous, are you really to blame if someone gets hurt?
Negligence is knowing the right answer but choosing to do
something else. Even if you thought it was dangerous, you still
went through with it. This is usually responded to with, “It was not
my call; I was just following orders.” This is a real problem. As
strength coaches, we need to understand the consequences of
making poor decisions and understand when we are at fault with
our teams.
Ignorance would be if a strength coach chooses not to
research something properly before administering it. Or you were
allowed to do something without the appropriate training. In
some ways, this is the fundamental problem with such a low
barrier to entry into our profession. We can let people bypass the
phase of developing competency and even common sense.
They instead focus on first-order consequences and do not
understand that second-order consequences will be negative.

通过简单且商定的规则，但规则和原则的区别在于，我们可以战略性地
省略或打破规则，但不能战略性地省略或打破原则。
S&C 最好的事情之一就是有很多可供解释的地方。 我们在培训某人
时做出的决定有如此大的自由度，这确实是一个令人惊奇的方面。 它
表明 S&C 既是一门艺术，也是一门科学。但制定培训计划时必须有一
些限制。 否则，我们的训练输入和随机的、意外的输出就会完全不匹
配。如果没有对训练的实际限制，在原则之外，我们可能会与成为受人
尊敬的科学产生重大脱节。 至于什么是好是坏，它变得完全主观，而
且随着时间的推移或在大群体中，这种情况是不可重复的。

不知道而不做与知道而不做
无知就是不知道某事。 如果你选择做某件事，而你不知道这件事
是错误的，而且你不知道这件事很危险，那么如果有人受伤，你
真的要为此负责吗？疏忽是知道正确答案却选择做其他事情。 即
使你认为这很危险，你还是坚持了下来。人们通常会这样回应：
“这不是我的决定；我只是执行命令。” 这是一个真正的问题。
作为力量教练，我们需要了解做出错误决定的后果，并了解我们
何时对团队犯错。

如果力量教练选择在进行某件事之前不进行适当的研究，那就
是无知。或者你被允许在没有经过适当培训的情况下做某事。 从
某些方面来说，这是进入我们行业的门槛如此之低的根本问题。
我们可以让人们绕过发展能力甚至常识的阶段。相反，他们关注
一阶后果，不明白二阶后果将是负面的。

The answer here? We need more education to explain what
we do not know. We need more training to reinforce and
reemphasize what we do know.
Negligence is that I was told to do something I knew was
wrong, and I was not in a position of authority to override that
decision or that I knew I was wrong; however, under the
circumstances, I chose to do it anyway. This is where it becomes
tough. We inherently understand that both answers are
unacceptable, but it is as simple as saying you should never do
something. Sometimes we do not have the luxury of best
practice. Rapid decisions are made all the time. You could be in
the middle of a conditioning session, and you need to pivot and
engage your team and choose a contraindicated drill, but this
decision may increase risk. The issue is that what you are doing
is not working, and you have to redirect the program. Decisions
are not binary. We can increase risk, but that could be offset by
increased performance. No decision is 100% good or bad; it’s
always some degree of both.
We need more education, more training, and higher
standards. Ignorance is completely avoidable, and there are
simply no excuses. Negligence is avoidable too; we need more
authority on how we make our decisions. We are responsible for
all our actions; they define us as people. The choice is effectively
up to us to hold ourselves accountable. Having respect for
yourself and placing safety above everything is how we avoid
negligence.

Need for Larger Groups
To fully appreciate the value of rules, we need to review two principles:
specificity and individuality. Specificity means that we are the product of
what we repeatedly do. Individuality is that we all respond differently to the
same stress. These two principles have to be included in the conversation
about rules because they can create a paradox with our decisions. If we repeat

需要更大的团体
要充分认识规则的价值，我们需要审视两个原则：特殊性和个性化。
Specificity 意味着我们是我们反复做的事情的产物。 Individuality 是我们
对相同压力的反应不同。 这两个原则必须包含在有关规则的对话中，
因为它们可能会与我们的决策产生悖论。如果我们重复

what we do, we will get a predictable outcome. If we repeat what we do with
two different people, we will get different outcomes. How do we train people
in larger groups with these two principles running at odds with each other?
Principles have to be true. That does not mean they fit perfectly into
training decisions. If you were to ask me what the point of this book is, it
would be trying to answer this question: How can I apply principles within
training all the time? So many coaches abandon principles within their plans
because managing all of them is simply too challenging, especially if they
lead to unpredictable outcomes. However, if we simply omit them from our
program, we decrease our odds of having a predictable outcome from
training.
Principles are true without context; the context
makes applying principles hard.
The worst types of data are a “noisy” dataset (figure 8.1). We see scatter
plots, and we hope they create a clear pattern of cause-and-effect
relationships between training inputs and predicted outputs. Seeing a noisy
dataset can give the impression of a completely screwed-up training plan. The
truth is, without rules, all training plans, regardless of whether they include
principles, can look like this. We need rules to omit noise from training.

我们所做的，将会得到可预测的结果。如果我们对两个不同的人重复我
们所做的事情，我们会得到不同的结果。当这两个原则相互矛盾时，我
们如何在更大的群体中培训人们呢？
原则必须是真实的。 这并不意味着它们完全适合培训决策。 如果你

I can attest to the feeling of presenting off-season testing results to both
athletes and coaches and having to build defenses for why something did not
work out. The data were always noisy. It’s disheartening and humiliating to
know that something you put so much effort into has a significant
discrepancy in results among the athletes in your training. This is where the
convergence of specificity and individuality presents itself. It is impossible to
peak everyone at a singular event. We may be preparing for that specific
event, but everyone will peak at different times. Not only that, but if you are
customizing aspects of a program throughout the training process, you are no
longer preparing for a specific event. According to diminishing returns, we
will always have a functional need to alter the plan. Any customization,

This is training; it’s messy and chaotic. It’s filled with decisions that have
to be made that include gray areas. We have to accommodate so many needs
and outcomes simultaneously. It becomes a matter of choosing what is the
best option at the moment. This will always be part of the equation with
training, which creates a more direct need for actual rules of engagement. We
need constraints to unburden ourselves from making impossible decisions
about what to do next. If not, we end up being ruled by bias, and that leads to
random, unpredictable outcomes that may be unwanted. Are we making
people better because of our programs or in spite of them?
We have rules everywhere in life. Rules of driving are a great example of
organizing chaotic environments. The fact that we do not always have traffic
accidents happening is a testament to how effective rules are in controlling
inputs and outputs.
You can see the connection between rules and outcomes. A question
would be, what if I break these rules? When we are at a four-way stop with
no one around and roll through a stop sign, does it matter? The answer
depends 100% on the context. We can lift with a subpar technique when the
intensity is incredibly low because the risk is minimal. There will always be
situations where the risk is simply not there, and we can casually omit the
rules. However, if you are driving on a five-lane highway with thousands of
cars, you better hope that everyone driving understands the rules and is
upholding them. The same could be said when you are running a maximal
sprint; you better be adequately prepared from a rest and movement prep
standpoint, otherwise the risk is monumental. The risk involved has a
considerable influence on the need and application of rules.
One way to evaluate the consequences of not adhering to rules is insurance
rates. Someone who is a historically bad driver with a high number of
documented accidents or citations will have higher insurance rates than
someone who has the opposite driving record. Driving has numerous
constraints placed on drivers to protect the greater good. People choose not to
acknowledge the rules all the time because they are unaware of or
unconcerned with the risk; for instance, texting while driving. One could say

偏差、修正等会产生连锁反应，进一步加剧训练产生的噪音结果。
这是训练；很混乱。它充满了必须做出的决策，其中包括灰色区域。
我们必须同时满足如此多的需求和结果。 这变成了选择目前最好的选
择的问题。 这始终是培训等式的一部分，这对实际的交战规则产生了
更直接的需求。我们需要约束来减轻自己对下一步该做什么做出不可能
的决定的负担。如果不是，我们最终会受到偏见的统治，这会导致随机
的、不可预测的结果，而这些结果可能是不受欢迎的。 我们是因为我
们的计划而让人们变得更好，还是不顾这些计划？
我们生活中处处都有规则。驾驶规则是组织混乱环境的一个很好的例
子。我们并不总是发生交通事故，这一事实证明了规则在控制输入和输
出方面的有效性。
您可以看到规则和结果之间的联系。 问题是，如果我违反这些规则
怎么办？ 当我们在四向停车处周围没有人并穿过停车标志时，这有关
系吗？ 答案 100% 取决于上下文。当强度极低时，我们可以使用低于
标准的技术举重，因为风险很小。 总会有一些情况，风险根本不存在
，我们可以随意忽略规则。然而，如果您在拥有数千辆汽车的五车道高
速公路上行驶，您最好希望每个开车的人都了解并遵守规则。 当你进
行最大冲刺时，情况也是如此。 您最好从休息和运动准备的角度做好
充分的准备，否则风险是巨大的。 所涉及的风险对规则的需要和应用
有相当大的影响。

评估不遵守规则后果的一种方法是保险费率。 历史上驾驶不良且有
大量事故记录或罚单的人的保险费率将高于具有相反驾驶记录的人。
为了保护更大的利益，驾驶对驾驶员施加了许多限制。人们总是选择不
承认规则，因为他们不知道或不关心风险；例如，开车时发短信。可以
说

they have been in a lot of traffic accidents due to bad luck, but that will not
change your insurance rate. Bad driving, or breaking rules, is a liability for
yourself and others, so it, therefore, costs more to insure you.
Driving is a strategic metaphor due to the redundancy in which we drive;
the same is true with training. Anything we do repetitively will have a
lessened level of focus. It is human nature to take for granted the relative risk
of things we do repetitively. Your first thought of repetitive training might be
really strong people picking up dumbbells; it is never done with the same
focus as maximal lifts. Where risk comes in is with technique while pushing
to a threshold; without a solid foundation of technique, risk is amplified.
Another example of athletes being extremely vulnerable to injury is at the end
of a training session when lifting with suboptimal technique. We organically
found solutions based on understanding the upper limit or inefficiency of
doing something. We started with zero rules for driving until we found a
direct need. The more we drive or the faster the car, the more rules matter.
The more we train and the better we get, the more rules we need to follow to
ensure certain outcomes without injury.
Strength and conditioning is loaded with rule breakers. Some are even
classified as trailblazers. This makes this industry so interesting. Compared to
driving, we have an innumerable number of coaches who have been driving
without a license without much consequence. We have people respecting the
rules of driving, driving alongside those that are not. To amplify the problems
associated with driving without a license and not respecting the rules, we are
driving buses with a bunch of people on board. We have created a world
where coaches are not accredited, doing whatever they want, with a bunch of
people following our lead. Abandonment of principles, combined with the
application of rules, has made it impossible to determine what is good or bad
training.
Rules can be perceived in different ways. Rules are simply boundaries to
ensure the safety and performance of our programs. That statement could
easily be construed as restrictive to creativity. However, the best athletes in
the world play sports with rules. Their ability to express themselves within a
constrained environment is built on the foundation of rules. Without rules,
these athletes would be random, impressive feats of athleticism. Think of a

他们因为运气不好而发生过很多交通事故，但这不会改变你的保险费率
。 不良驾驶或违反规则是对您自己和他人的责任，因此，为您投保需
要花费更多费用。
由于我们驾驶的冗余性，驾驶是一个战略隐喻；培训也是如此。 我
们重复做的任何事情都会降低注意力。将我们重复做的事情的相对风险
视为理所当然是人的本性。你对重复训练的第一个想法可能是非常强壮
的人拿起哑铃； 它从来没有像最大举升一样专注于完成。当技术达到
某个阈值时，风险就出现了。 如果没有扎实的技术基础，风险就会被
放大。运动员极易受伤的另一个例子是在训练结束时使用次优技术举重
时。我们基于了解做某事的上限或低效率有机地找到了解决方案。 我
们从零驾驶规则开始，直到我们发现直接需求。 我们开得越多或者车
开得越快，规则就越重要。我们训练得越多，训练得越好，我们需要遵
循的规则就越多，以确保取得特定结果而不受伤。

力量和体能训练充满了规则破坏者。 有些甚至被列为开拓者。这使
得这个行业如此有趣。与开车相比，我们有无数的教练无证驾驶而没有
造成太大后果。我们有人尊重驾驶规则，有人与不遵守规则的人并肩驾
驶。为了放大与无证驾驶和不遵守规则相关的问题，我们正在驾驶载有
一群人的公共汽车。 我们创造了一个教练不受认可、为所欲为、而一
群人追随我们的世界。 原则的放弃，加上规则的运用，已经让人无法
判断训练的好坏。

规则可以通过不同的方式来理解。 规则只是确保我们程序的安全和
性能的边界。 这种说法很容易被理解为对创造力的限制。 然而，世界
上最优秀的运动员都是按照规则进行体育运动的。他们在受限环境中表
达自己的能力建立在规则的基础上。 如果没有规则，这些运动员将是
随机的、令人印象深刻的运动壮举。 想一个

live stream of parkour compared to the Super Bowl. Random feats are
impressive but lack the context to understand what is good. Applying rules
while performing amazing feats of athleticism gives merit to what we are
seeing by allowing for context.
The secret to successful rules is that they have to be simple and intuitive.
If rules are too hard to remember, they will not be upheld. Rules can be built
up over time, but they have to start with something incredibly easy to
understand for them to be effective. As we expand upon anything, we have to
have a very clear understanding of why those rules were in place to begin
with. If we have too many or they are difficult to understand, the feeling of
restriction becomes the dominant force. Taking away someone’s freedom to
express themselves through selecting exercises or managing variables is not
the reason behind the rules. Most coaches do not understand that not adhering
to rules is a problem until long after they come up short with their training
plans.
One of the best thought experiments for rules is scaling your sample size.
People are always most critical of the coaches who work with the most
athletes. The truth is that coaches working with larger samples are governed
by a different set of rules. Their mistakes are exponentially larger. One bad
training decision could result in a 10% injury rate among a sample size. The
coach who works one-on-one with only 10 people does not have the same
perspective as the coach working with 1,000 people. Both can make the same
mistake, but the 10-person roster compared to the 1,000-person roster could
be one versus 100 in terms of injury. Training larger groups repeatedly
exposes any flaws in decisions a coach is making.
Rules are more necessary when the group sizes
are larger.
If you are working with people in a one-on-one environment and have
aspirations to work in a team setting, you will have the hardest adjustment
adhering to rules-based programming. You will lose the luxury of
customizing for customization’s sake. You will lose the luxury of being

跑酷直播与超级碗比赛相比。 随机的壮举令人印象深刻，但缺乏背景
来理解什么是好的。 在表现出令人惊叹的运动能力的同时应用规则，
通过考虑到背景，可以为我们所看到的事情带来价值。
成功规则的秘诀在于它们必须简单且直观。如果规则太难记住，它们
就不会被遵守。规则可以随着时间的推移而建立，但它们必须从非常容
易理解的东西开始才能有效。当我们扩展任何事物时，我们必须非常清
楚地了解为什么要制定这些规则。 如果太多或者难以理解，限制感就
会成为主导力量。 通过选择练习或管理变量来剥夺某人表达自己的自
由并不是规则背后的原因。大多数教练直到他们没有达到训练计划很久
之后才明白不遵守规则是一个问题。

规则的最佳思想实验之一是扩大样本量。人们总是对与最多运动员一
起工作的教练最挑剔。 事实是，处理更大样本的教练受到一套不同的
规则的约束。 他们的错误成倍地扩大。 一项错误的训练决策可能会导
致样本量中受伤率达到 10%。只与 10 人一对一工作的教练与与 1,000
人一起工作的教练的观点不同。两者都可能犯同样的错误，但 10 人名
单与 1000 人名单相比，在伤病方面可能是 1 比 100。 训练更大的团队
会反复暴露教练决策中的任何缺陷。

当团体规模较大时，规则就更加必要。

如果您在一对一的环境中与人合作，并且渴望在团队环境中工作，那
么您将在遵守基于规则的编程方面进行最困难的调整。 你将失去为了
定制而定制的奢侈。 你将失去存在的奢侈

spontaneous with changes on the fly. Having an extremely detailed program
is noble, but it is a luxury for those working in a one-on-one setting. Scaling
up group sizes forces the coach to focus on what is necessary. A large part of
that is ruling out what you cannot do. Every coach who works with a larger
group comes to this realization sooner or later, but the truth is that larger
numbers are a force multiplier for enforcing rules on yourself with
programming.
As a coach, I started with group training. I was conditioned to focus only
on programs that serve multiple athletes simultaneously. In many ways,
programming became about applying more constraints to control the
environment. Progressing as a coach can take a bunch of funny turns if you
are not paying attention. I could easily see a very rigid structure to training
based on the guise that it is better to focus on uniformity to ensure
predictability. This was the natural reaction to my feeling inadequate and
reacting to overly controlled environments.

Little Control and Prediction
The feeling of losing control and having less predictability was something I
was not ready to accept. Control is an illusion with training. A great example
of this is working with someone regarding nutrition. It is so abstract because
we are entrusting the person to execute their intervention on their own.
Comparatively, with a program, I control 100% of what we do, how we do it,
and when we do it in the weight room. But that program is probably 3 to 4 h
of their entire week. How much do you control? When we compare the time
spent controlling something to the time spent not controlling something, we
can see we have very little control at all. What we think we are controlling is
more under the control of everything else in our athletes’ lives.
Having a more predictable outcome based on the illusion of control is not
the answer either. We have very little control over what will happen. Entropy,
chaos, complexity … what will happen is impossible to predict. Think about
the number of bad National Football League draft picks or bad coaching
hires. There are millions of dollars at stake, and people screw that up all the
time. Do you mean to tell me a program you are writing for literally hundreds
of people on a Sunday evening, on the only day off you had in weeks, is more

自发的、动态的变化。 拥有极其详细的计划是高尚的，但对于那些在
一对一环境中工作的人来说却是一种奢侈。扩大小组规模迫使教练专注
于必要的事情。其中很大一部分是排除你不能做的事情。 每个与较大
团队一起工作的教练迟早都会意识到这一点，但事实是，较大的数量是
通过编程对自己执行规则的力量倍增器。
作为一名教练，我从团体训练开始。我习惯于只关注同时为多名运动
员服务的项目。 在许多方面，编程变成了应用更多的约束来控制环境
。 如果你不注意的话，作为一名教练的进步可能会发生很多有趣的转
变。 我可以很容易地看到一种非常严格的培训结构，其幌子是最好注
重一致性以确保可预测性。 这是我感觉自己能力不足以及对过度控制
的环境做出的自然反应。

控制和预测很少
失去控制和缺乏可预测性的感觉是我不愿意接受的。控制是训练的幻觉
。一个很好的例子就是与营养方面的人合作。它是如此抽象，因为我们
委托该人自己执行干预。相比之下，通过计划，我可以 100% 控制我们
做什么、如何做以及何时在举重室做。但这个计划可能占他们一周的 3
到 4 个小时。你控制多少？当我们将控制某事所花费的时间与不控制某
事所花费的时间进行比较时，我们会发现我们根本无法控制。我们认为
我们正在控制的东西更多地受到运动员生活中其他一切的控制。

基于控制幻觉而获得更可预测的结果也不是答案。我们几乎无法控制
将会发生的事情。熵、混乱、复杂性……将发生的事情是无法预测的。
想想有多少糟糕的国家橄榄球联盟选秀或糟糕的教练聘用。这涉及数百
万美元，但人们总是把事情搞砸。你是想告诉我，你在周日晚上为数百
人编写的一个程序，这是你几周来唯一的休息日，是吗？

well thought out than a National Football League general manager whose job
and organization are 100% contingent on their making a good choice? No
one can predict what will happen, nor do we have control over what we think
we are controlling.
We have little control with little ability to predict
what will happen.
I am not trying to be morbid. Think of the judge who mistakenly
sentenced someone to life without parole because they were hungry. We can
say that when stakes are increased, such as making a diagnosis and
intervention, sentencing someone to prison, having huge financial
implications, or working with extremely large groups, biases and agendas
become more of a crutch, which is why we need rules. We need to account
for our inability to make decisions, and we need a fractal approach, with
simple rules repeated, in our thinking to ask a fundamental question: If I
increase the scale of what I am doing, would my decisions still be effective or
true?

Reduce Constraints
One thing we are responsible for is increasing performance. As
strength coaches, we can lock in on programming or technique,
but that might be the equivalent of treading water.
We need to spend an equal amount of time trying to find
constraints for our program. Constraints are bottlenecks of
efficiency. We want to increase performance, but constraints
place an artificial ceiling upon what we can accomplish with the
time we have.
Our focal point for creating a great program will be to apply
principles through the creation and application of rules. The
application of rules will face constraints throughout the program.
Finding them and reducing their impact increases our output.

比一个国家橄榄球联盟总经理深思熟虑，他的工作和组织100%取决于
他们做出正确的选择吗？ 没有人能够预测将会发生什么，我们也无法
控制我们认为我们正在控制的事情。

我们几乎无法控制，也几乎没有能力预测将会发生什么
。
我并不是想变得病态。 想想那位法官，因为某人饥饿而错误地判处
他终身不得假释。我们可以说，当风险增加时，例如进行诊断和干预、
将某人判入狱、产生巨大的财务影响或与极其庞大的群体合作，偏见和
议程就变得更像是拐杖，这就是我们需要规则的原因。 我们需要考虑
到我们无法做出决策，我们需要一种分形方法，重复简单的规则，在我
们的思维中提出一个基本问题：如果我扩大我正在做的事情的规模，我
的决定仍然有效或真实吗？

减少限制
我们负责的一件事是提高绩效。 作为力量教练，我们可以锁定编
程或技术，但这可能相当于原地踏步。
我们需要花费同样多的时间来尝试寻找我们的程序的限制。 约
束是效率的瓶颈。 我们希望提高绩效，但限制因素给我们在有限
的时间内所能完成的任务设置了人为的上限。
我们创建出色计划的重点是通过创建和应用规则来应用原则。
规则的应用将在整个计划中面临限制。找到它们并减少它们的影
响会增加我们的产出。

There are a couple of models we can leverage here to better
spot constraints. The first model is inversion. Start at the end and
work backward through the program. Much like reversing a
motor pattern can reveal movement compensations, we can see
much more clearly constraints to our program. Where we are
getting less execution or efficiency is hard to spot when we are
plowing through the program with business as usual.
The second model is changing perspectives. Switching roles
with staff can reveal how hard certain jobs are and potentially
reveal how necessary they are. A head coach setting up a lift
can bring clarity to what is necessary. Do we need this many
hurdles?—a question only asked by the person setting up the
hurdles. The same goes for an assistant being responsible for
making large-scale decisions. The classification of right or wrong
is a lot more blurred when you are at the top. Young coaches will
struggle to understand how certain decisions are made without
being placed in the position to make those decisions.
The most obvious thing with finding constraints is being
aware. More often than not, inefficiencies are obvious, just not
seen as easily as they should be, based on perspective.
Reversing the order of things or changing the vantage point can
make the obvious more obvious.
But as you can see from my experience, you can easily let rules go too far
by being overly strict. This can be restrictive to finding creative and elegant
solutions to complex problems. We need rules to be simple and
understandable. Simple and understandable is more agreeable to everyone.
This is important because if rules become overly complicated, you will lose
the support of those who have to uphold them. We cannot control or predict
what will happen, but we can control what we cannot do, which will reduce
noisy outcomes. Like anything, there will be a balancing act to apply
constraints to any system. Too much or too complicated, and you will lose
the group. Too little or too random, and you will lose the group.
Understanding the outcome and what you do not want to happen organically

。从最后开始并逆向执行该程序。 就像逆转运动模式可以揭示运

们像往常一样努力完成该计划时，很难发现执行力或效率较低的
地方。
第二种模式是改变观点。 与员工互换角色可以揭示某些工作的

，这将减少噪音结果。 与任何事情一样，对任何系统施加约束都需要
平衡。 太多或太复杂，你就会失去群体。 太少或太随机，你就会失去
这个群体。了解结果以及您不希望发生的事情

presents the rules for you.
When I was forced to switch from working with large groups to working
with small groups or even working one-on-one, I had to revisit what rules
were universal. Scaling up means you need to place more constraints on your
training with more rigid rules. That does not necessarily mean we have to
remove those constraints when scaled down. As we have talked about with
driving, it is a matter of context regarding how much we have to uphold those
rules. We may have more latitude with breaking the rules as we scale down.
Handling feedback or opposition to doing a program is drastically
different when working one-on-one versus working in a team setting.
Someone being insubordinate in a large group is typically met with a punitive
response. I’m not trying to cast a militaristic nature on group training but
rather an understanding of group dynamics. How much conviction you have
in what you are doing is ultimately decided by those doing it when you face
opposition. In a one-on-one setting, you have less ability to assert your
authority due to the intimacy of the situation. You would look like a drill
sergeant if you just started making someone do up downs in a private training
session for missing a rep during a set. In a group setting, you get what you
emphasize. If you demand high integrity with each rep, set, and training
session, you will get a more predictable outcome. Therefore, we need a more
assertive approach that ensures this outcome when dealing with larger
groups.
Context matters a great deal with rules. Going 70 mph (113 km/h) in a 65
mph (105 km/h) zone but going with the flow and pace of traffic is a clear
rule violation but will not be perceived as such. The cliché of rules are meant
to be broken is misunderstood. Rules are not inherently meant to be broken
but to be understood and applied in context, with logic guiding whether to
adhere to them. Upholding rules that do not apply to the situation is a
mistake. I do not need to punish my 75-year-old private training client for
showing up 5 min late and paying me for the session. Alternatively, there are
significant consequences for coaches who are perceived as pushovers if they
do not take action for a freshman showing up late to a team training session.
Group dynamics will supersede your authority and limit your ability to coach
your team if you avoid conflict.

为您呈现规则。
当我被迫从与大型团体合作转向与小组合作甚至一对一合作时，我不
得不重新审视哪些规则是通用的。扩大规模意味着您需要通过更严格的
规则对训练施加更多限制。 这并不一定意味着我们必须在缩小规模时
消除这些限制。 正如我们所讨论的驾驶问题，我们必须在多大程度上
遵守这些规则，这取决于具体情况。随着规模的缩小，我们可能有更多
的自由来打破规则。
一对一工作与团队工作相比，处理项目的反馈或反对意见是截然不同
的。在一大群人中不服从命令的人通常会受到惩罚性反应。 我并不是
想在团体训练中赋予军国主义性质，而是对团体动态的理解。 当你面
临反对时，你对自己所做的事情有多少信心最终取决于那些做这件事的
人。 在一对一的环境中，由于情况的亲密性，你很难维护自己的权威
。 如果你刚开始在私人训练课程中让某人因在一组中错过了一次代表
而做上下动作，那么你看起来就像一名教官。 在群体环境中，你会得
到你所强调的内容。 如果您对每一次代表、一组和训练课程都要求高
度的完整性，那么您将获得更可预测的结果。因此，我们需要一种更加
自信的方法，以确保在与更大的群体打交道时取得这一结果。

背景对于规则来说非常重要。在时速 65 英里（105 公里/小时）的区
域以 70 英里/小时（113 公里/小时）的速度行驶，但随车流和速度行驶
是明显的违规行为，但不会被视为违规。 rules are meant to be broken 的
陈词滥调被误解了。 规则本身并不意味着要被打破，而是要在上下文
中理解和应用，并用逻辑指导是否遵守它们。 坚持不适用于当前情况
的规则是错误的。 我不需要惩罚我 75 岁的私人培训客户，因为他迟到
了 5 分钟并支付了我的课程费用。另外，如果教练不针对新人在球队训
练中迟到的情况采取行动，就会给那些被认为是容易被人欺负的教练带
来严重后果。如果你避免冲突，团队动力将取代你的权威并限制你指导
团队的能力。

When I was interviewed for the head S&C coach position at Army West
Point, I was asked what I would do on day one. My response was, “What do
we want going into our first game of the third year?” I was referencing the
fact that most staff get a three-year window to prove themselves, and if we do
not figure out how to have a winning program within that time, we lose our
jobs. My future boss answered, “I want a team that is tough, physical, and
trained!” My response was, “Then we are going to do everything on day one
to get us closer to that goal.” We went back and forth on whether to screen or
test athletes, and I agreed with all of it. But that was not what he was asking
for. In the opinion of my future boss, the best way to create a winning team
was to have tough, physical, and trained athletes. My job at the moment was
to go to work and form the strategy and logistics to execute making a team
that was tough, physical, and trained. A lot of that first year was raising the
standard by which we did things and establishing higher expectations for
ourselves as a team. That allowed us to do things down the road that were
more directly related to performance and injury reduction. For a strength
coach, understanding group dynamics is critical. Rules will be vulnerable to
not being upheld if you are not aware of how small decisions create a
concentric circle for everyone in the group.
The rules we will focus on in this section are biomechanics and
physiology. If you look at every decision we make with training, it comes
down to those two categories. The exercises we choose are based on the
movement potential we inherit and the movement capacity we hope to
develop. The way we manipulate variables (time under tension, reps, sets,
intensity, rest, frequency) is based on the physiological potential and the
physiological levels we hope to develop. We make all decisions with training
based on those two factors, so we need to establish rules for those two
categories.
With biomechanics, the question is, why do we choose a certain exercise
over another? This is an important thing to consider. The majority of us are
choosing exercises based on our environment, our social groups, our previous
experiences, our biases, and therefore, our agendas. Someone from a specific
background (powerlifting, weightlifting, track and field) will choose
exercises based on that criterion. The functional needs of that athlete are

当我接受陆军西点军校 S&C 主教练职位的面试时，有人问我第一天
会做什么。 My response was, “What do we want going into our first ga
me of the third year?” 我指的是这样一个事实：大多数员工都有三年
的时间来证明自己，如果我们不弄清楚如何在这段时间内制定一个成功
的计划，我们就会失去工作。 我未来的老板回答说：“我想要一支坚
韧、身体健康、训练有素的团队！”我的回答是：“那么我们将在第一
天尽一切努力让我们更接近这个目标。”我们在是否筛选或测试运动员
的问题上反复讨论，我全部同意。但这不是他所要求的。 在我未来的
老板看来，创建一支获胜团队的最佳方法是拥有坚韧、体格健壮且训练
有素的运动员。我目前的工作是上班并制定战略和后勤工作，以打造一
支坚韧、体力强、训练有素的团队。 第一年的大部分时间都是在提高
我们做事的标准，并为我们自己作为一个团队设定更高的期望。 这使
我们能够做一些与表现和减少伤害更直接相关的事情。 对于力量教练
来说，了解团队动态至关重要。 如果你不知道微小的决定如何为团队
中的每个人创造一个同心圆，那么规则就很容易不被遵守。

我们在本节中将重点关注的规则是生物力学和生理学。 如果你看看
我们在培训中做出的每一个决定，你会发现它都归结为这两类。 我们
选择的练习是基于我们继承的运动潜力和我们希望发展的运动能力。
我们操纵变量（紧张时间、次数、组数、强度、休息、频率）的方式是
基于我们希望发展的生理潜力和生理水平。我们根据这两个因素通过训
练做出所有决策，因此我们需要为这两个类别建立规则。

对于生物力学，问题是，为什么我们选择某种运动而不是另一种？
这是需要考虑的重要事情。 我们大多数人都根据我们的环境、我们的
社会群体、我们以前的经验、我们的偏见以及我们的议程来选择练习。
来自特定背景（举重、举重、田径）的人会根据该标准选择练习。 该
运动员的功能需求是

irrelevant to the agenda and bias of a coach. Sometimes we can get lucky,
and that person filters you out and chooses you based on your skill set. In that
case, you were what you said you were and a perfect match. In other cases,
we think we are inheriting athletes, but in fact, it is the other way around.
They are inheriting us coaches along with our previous experiences and
mentors who influenced us. Our decisions with exercise selection are now
our athletes’ inheritance, and that might not be congruent with their desired
outcome.
I ask again, why do you choose one exercise over another? A fundamental
aspect of biomechanical rules is having a screen. This is a taboo topic for
some coaches. Why would an agreed-upon movement screen or diagnostic of
what exercises may be best be met with opposition? A screen, by nature, can
be restrictive to certain things a coach may want to do. A screen is not
intended to discredit you as a coach. A screen creates tangible constraints for
your program. It provides context for what exercise will work best with our
principles of training. Rules are not restrictive; they are boundaries to help
you make effective programming decisions.
Why we do a certain exercise over another is at the heart of biomechanical
rules. Without rules built around exercise selection, we will have a bunch of
people driving on both sides of the road in all directions. We have to have
some diagnostics to choose one exercise over another. Subjectivity with
exercise selection is just a lack of discipline and forces irrational decisions.
Physiology helps us decide how long to stick with an exercise and how to
organize our training variables. Coaches who adhere to constant variation and
exercise novelty are not basing their decisions on objectivity. A common
thread is that since we play in chaos, our preparation should be chaotic. In a
small sample, you can get away with that logic. In a large sample, you
cannot. You can still have exercise variation along with more rapid changes
in training variables, but you at least need to decipher the impact of those
decisions. We create considerable noise when we have constant variations or
overly complicated exercise variations. It is tough to assess why something
was successful or not with so many variables to account for. Creating noisy
data for the sake of novelty is not a good exchange. A simple approach with
progression or progressive overload that did not work is more beneficial than

taking a randomized approach because it elicits a better understanding.
Simple things that fail teach us what is not true. Entropy is the outcome, but
we can reduce and delay that by avoiding added complexity. We can now
more definitively rule something out for the future and plan accordingly.
Choosing an exercise is about understanding what the athlete currently can
do. If the athlete has some underlying issue that prevents them from gaining
value from that exercise, that exercise is deemed obsolete. A screen has the
potential to alert us to things that we should be aware of not doing. It should
also create a clear road map for what we should do. Regardless of my
preferred method of training, a screen tells me what I need to do over what I
want to do. An exercise progression is a road map to take my athletes from
where they are to where they want to be. Biomechanical rules allow me to
find the fastest and safest route.
With physiology, we have to ask how much and how long for the exercise
we choose: How much and how long for time under tension, reps, sets,
intensity, rest, and frequency do we need? Again, we are the product of what
we have had success with. We tend to blame failure on circumstances. We
take too much credit for something going right. A program may not work
based on many factors we cannot control. A program may be wildly
successful based on many factors we had no control over whatsoever. We
cannot make future decisions based exclusively on previous successes. We
learn more from the mistakes we make. We know that does not work from a
hypothetical or application standpoint. We do not know the same for things
that did work, or as much as we think we do.
How much or how long we do any exercise is not a matter of what has
worked previously. How much or how long do decisions come from what
that person needs in that given period? Training age or fitness level has a
profoundly larger impact on training decisions than a program that another
school did or what worked for me as recently as last year. We meet the
athletes where they are based on a diagnostic screen of what they can do. We
progress based on where we want to be, combined with what they will benefit
from.

person needs. Long-term planning is just attempting to reverse engineer

Rules Reduce Noise
Rules are all about reducing noise (figure 8.2). We simply do not know what
we should do with someone until after we have done it. We know that
principles have to be in place; that is a given. That does not mean that writing
a program will be easy as a result. Specificity means we will repeat
something toward a preferred output. Individuality means we will respond
differently to the same things in a group. Rules allow us to bridge the gap
between these seemingly paradoxical principles.

Types of Rules
The rules we place with programming are foundational to ensuring the
consistency of an outcome. We will need rules for selecting appropriate
exercises based on biomechanics. We need rules for selecting appropriate
variables based on physiology.

Biomechanical Rules
We use biomechanical rules to select exercises to form a specific program to
meet the direct needs of the athlete. These rules base exercise selection on
where they are starting from and where they need to be. We have to think of
exercises as conduits for the qualities we are trying to develop. Do we have
the prerequisite biomechanics to go through the necessary volume, intensity,
and density to effectively develop the quality that most corresponds to
performance? We want the exercises we use to provide the value we intend
when we load redundantly to the threshold. Biomechanical rules ensure we
can do that consistently.

将对我们可以编程的内容产生更大的影响，从而使我们更接近我们最终
需要达到的目标。

Physiological Rules
We use physiological rules to leverage variables with those exercises to reach
the functional levels needed to perform at the highest level. The variables
associated with physiological rules are how we accommodate individuality.
Do we have the physiological capacity to recover from a training set, a
training session, and a training week? We want the variables we use during
training to facilitate the quality we are trying to develop. Physiological rules
ensure that we can do that consistently.
Creating rules around training gives us our best opportunity to handle
larger groups more effectively. We are trying to reduce noise and ensure a
positive outcome for the entire group. We match the demands placed on the

coach, who has to accommodate so many individuals at once, by having
simple, intuitive, and agreeable rules. We can still be creative, just within the
constraints of the rules. Rules are not meant to be broken. They are meant to
be understood and accepted, and then to find ways to push boundaries within
the constraints.

Take Home
Rules reduce noise. We want to increase our odds when we scale up with
training plans. We do not have the control we think we have, nor do we have
the ability to predict what we think will happen. Introducing rules ensures we
can control what we can control, from exercise selection (biomechanics) to
variable manipulation (physiology). It reduces noise and gives us a chance to
be successful with larger groups.

教练必须通过简单、直观且令人愉快的规则同时容纳这么多人。只要在
规则的限制内，我们仍然可以发挥创造力。规则并不意味着被打破。它
们旨在被理解和接受，然后找到在限制范围内突破界限的方法。

带回家
规则可以减少噪音。 当我们扩大培训计划时，我们希望增加成功的机
会。我们没有我们认为拥有的控制权，也没有能力预测我们认为会发生

择（生物力学）到变量操作（生理学）。它减少了噪音，让我们有机会
在更大的团队中取得成功。

BIOMECHANICAL RULES
Before we can establish rules, we need to understand what game we are
playing. Are we playing a game with someone who has no underlying
movement restrictions? Are we playing a game with someone who has an
extensive injury history? We know that the best predictor of future injury is
previous injury (Cook, 2011). The best way to assess what biomechanical
rules we need to have in place is to conduct a diagnostic to improve our
understanding of the potential future problems.

Testing
Training programs are at best an educated guess. We are shooting in the dark
based on an underlying hope that what we do will matter. Anne Duke (2018)
stated in her book Thinking in Bets that in life, we think we are playing chess
with the decisions we make. In reality, we are playing poker in life and with
training programs. What Duke meant by this is that we do not have the luxury
of predictable outcomes when we make decisions. Decisions are not simple;
they are complex. This creates unpredictable outcomes any time we make a
decision. Training decisions are more like playing poker; we know what
cards we have, and by process of elimination, we know what others may
have, and we can use probabilities to determine the outcome. A screen is an
appraisal of your odds. Rules allow us to count cards with programming.
We know the outcome is going to be unpredictable. How unpredictable is

9
生物力学规则
在制定规则之前，我们需要了解我们正在玩什么游戏。 我们是否正在
与没有潜在行动限制的人一起玩游戏？ 我们是在和一个有大量伤病史
的人一起比赛吗？ 我们知道，未来受伤的最佳预测因素是之前的受伤
情况（Cook，2011）。 评估我们需要制定哪些生物力学规则的最佳方
法是进行诊断，以提高我们对未来潜在问题的理解。

测试
培训计划充其量只是一种有根据的猜测。我们在黑暗中进行拍摄，是基
于一种潜在的希望，即我们所做的事情会发挥作用。 Anne Duke（2018
）在她的书Thinking in Bets中指出，在生活中，我们认为我们正在根据
自己所做的决定下棋。事实上，我们在生活中和训练计划中都在玩扑克
。杜克的意思是，我们在做出决策时没有可预测的结果。 决策并不简

对你的赔率的评估。规则允许我们通过编程来数牌。
我们知道结果将是不可预测的。多么不可预测

a matter of how well we can appraise what we are working with, or what our
hand is. We often think that if I just make someone stronger or faster, they
will have a better chance of winning. But this is only true if they do not get
hurt. The injury will make all increases in biomotor or bioenergetic changes
become obsolete. Appraising risk prioritizes exercises we can use with our
athletes. A screen is not restrictive to the things we want to do; it is
supportive of the things we can do. Framing a screen means we have a
baseline knowledge of what hurts, previous injury, asymmetry, and ROM
(range of motion). That knowledge is incredibly beneficial when selecting
exercises to train.
Before we discuss what a screen should look like, we need to consider
some factors. Reliability and validity are critical for any screen. Even more
important in working with groups is the concept of interrater reliability. We
need our tests to be all three to receive benefits toward making good
decisions with exercise selection. All these factors are incredibly important
when discussing an objective view of current functional abilities to truly
appraise risk:
Reliability in statistics is the overall consistency of a measure.
Validity is the extent to which a concept, conclusion, or measurement
is well-founded and likely corresponds accurately to the real world.
Interrater reliability is the degree of agreement among raters.

Reliability
Reliability is defined as the degree to which the result of a measurement,
calculation, or specification can be depended on to be accurate. Therefore,
our measurements need to be calibrated to ensure that each test is as reliable
as possible. Testing conditions, such as the day of the week, time of day,
segment within the training session, coach administering the test, and
methods used for testing, all need to be addressed before testing. Having a
standard operating procedure in place for testing is foundational to ensuring
the reliability of that testing.

Validity
Validity is defined as the quality of being logically or factually sound—

问题在于我们能否很好地评估我们正在使用的东西，或者我们的手是什
么。 我们常常认为，如果我让某人变得更强或更快，他们就会有更好
的获胜机会。 但这只有在他们不受伤的情况下才是正确的。 损伤将使
所有生物运动或生物能量变化的增加变得过时。 评估风险会优先考虑
我们可以与运动员一起使用的练习。 屏幕并不限制我们想做的事情；
它是我们想要做的事情的一部分。 它支持我们可以做的事情。 框架屏
幕意味着我们对疼痛、先前受伤、不对称和 ROM（运动范围）有基本
了解。 在选择要训练的练习时，这些知识非常有用。
在我们讨论屏幕应该是什么样子之前，我们需要考虑一些因素。 可
靠性和有效性对于任何屏幕都至关重要。 在与团队合作时，更重要的
是参与者间可靠性的概念。 我们需要进行全部三项测试，才能通过运
动选择做出正确的决定。 在讨论当前功能能力的客观观点以真正评估
风险时，所有这些因素都非常重要：
统计中的可靠性是指测量的整体一致性。有效性是指概念、结论
或测量有充分依据并且可能准确对应现实世界的程度。评估者间
的可靠性是指评估者之间的一致程度。

可靠性
Reliability定义为测量、计算或规格结果的准确程度。 因此，我们的测
量需要进行校准，以确保每次测试尽可能可靠。 测试条件，例如星期
几、一天中的时间、训练课程中的分段、管理测试的教练以及测试所使
用的方法，都需要在测试之前解决。 制定标准的测试操作程序是确保
测试可靠性的基础。

有效性
Validity被定义为逻辑上或事实上合理的质量——

soundness or cogency. Therefore, the tests we select need to be directly
related to the outcome we desire. Time is valuable. A simple inventory of
each test with two basic questions is paramount to success. Does the test
relate to the desired outcome? Does the test have an impact on training
decisions toward that outcome?

Interrater Reliability
Interrater reliability is defined as a measure of how consistent multiple raters
are in their ratings of the same item or phenomenon. Therefore, we need to
ensure our tests are consistent from one coach to the next. As mentioned
before, having a standard operating procedure is one way to combat changing
schedules, alternating environments, and staff turnover. The value of the test
is not based on how well we can test in perfect conditions. The real value is
how well the test can be consistently administered in an ever-changing
environment.
These factors are crucially important, and yet we often overlook them. We
also take for granted that our hypotheses about training are often biased. We
tend to make tests and screens that confirm our preexisting beliefs. Making
decisions about exercise selection outside of the objective is grounds for
disaster. Remember, we have to think at scale; we do not have the luxury of
making decisions for one or a couple. We have to think about whether we are
making decisions that serve a large number of people simultaneously.

Creating Biomechanical Rules
There are nine rules or factors to consider as part of a diagnostic to anticipate
potential future problems (figure 9.1).

健全性或说服力。 因此，我们选择的测试需要与我们想要的结果直接
相关。 时间很宝贵。 每个测试的简单清单以及两个基本问题对于成功
至关重要。 测试与预期结果相关吗？ 测试是否会对实现该结果的培训
决策产生影响？

评估者间的可靠性
Interrater reliability定义为衡量多个评估者对同一项目或现象的评级一致
性程度的指标。 因此，我们需要确保我们的测试从一位教练到另一位
教练都是一致的。 如前所述，制定标准操作程序是应对不断变化的时
间表、不断变化的环境和员工流动的一种方法。测试的价值并不取决于
我们在完美条件下测试的效果如何。真正的价值在于在不断变化的环境
中能够持续地管理测试。
这些因素至关重要，但我们却常常忽视它们。我们还理所当然地认为
我们对培训的假设常常是有偏见的。我们倾向于进行测试和筛选来证实
我们先前存在的信念。 在目标之外做出演习选择决策会导致灾难。请
记住，我们必须进行大规模思考；我们没有能力为一个人或几个人做决
定。我们必须考虑我们所做的决策是否能够同时为很多人服务。

创建生物力学规则
作为预测未来潜在问题的诊断的一部分，需要考虑九个规则或因素（图
9.1）。

FIGURE 9.1 Biomechanical rules.

Rule 1: Risk Appraisal
We need a risk appraisal, a screen, to assess
biomechanic potential.
We start by shifting our focus from trying to predict a very small list of
predetermined things we want to do. Instead, we shift to prepare for chaotic,
unpredictable environments. We can lower the potential risk of injury by
having a preparative focus on increasing our joint capacity, our force-length
capacity, and our control with an infinite number of potential movements
(Cook, 2011). An exercise’s use is only as good as the potential to develop
that pattern. If that exercise is contraindicated based on what we find on a
screen, it becomes less valuable. We can only leverage the development of

图 9.1 生物力学规则。

规则一：风险评估
我们需要风险评估、筛选来评估生物力学潜力。

我们首先将注意力从试图预测一小部分我们想做的预定事情开始。相反
，我们会为混乱、不可预测的环境做好准备。 我们可以通过专注于增
加我们的关节能力、我们的力量长度能力以及我们对无限数量的潜在运
动的控制来降低潜在的受伤风险（Cook，2011）。 练习的用途取决于
发展该模式的潜力。 如果根据我们在屏幕上发现的内容来看该练习是
禁忌的，那么它的价值就会降低。 我们只能利用发展

force, velocity, or work through certain exercises that are properly vetted.
Predetermined exercise selection makes us less aware of what we will get
from the time spent training. If that exercise hurts to do or cannot be done
correctly, it could have a negative impact.
All a screen is doing is giving a list of exercises we can do. Exercise
selection is based on the athlete’s biomechanical ability. An exercise is only
as good as its ability to be executed. If someone is experiencing pain or
restriction during certain motions, and that motion has a direct impact on
their ability to execute a movement pattern, they cannot do that movement
pattern. That reality does not make the exercise bad; it just makes that
exercise ineffective toward an end goal for that athlete in that context. The
ends have to justify the means. However, the means are only justified based
on enabling the end goal in the most efficient manner possible.

Rule 2: Validity and Reliability
Our screen needs to be both valid and interrater
reliable.
Validity establishes that what we are doing is accurate. For instance, if we
want to increase the odds of an exercise having a more direct impact on
performance training, we need to have a valid exercise selection appraisal.
This also suggests that we are creating criteria behind our hypothesis of
training. A hypothesis is simply a proposed explanation of what we think
might happen based on what we know. It is taking all the information we
have and creating an experiment around the information we know is true. If
we have valid information, we have a better chance of eliminating any noise.
Less noise means we have better odds of making decisions that will have a
positive impact on the environment; we cannot predict what will happen. The
validity of our screens is the most controllable aspect of exercise selection
when working within complex environments.
Any training program you write is a scientific experiment. If you are
reading this book, you are probably writing or have written programs for

通过某些经过适当审查的练习来锻炼力量、速度或功力。预定的运动选
择让我们不太清楚我们将从训练中得到什么。 如果这项练习做起来很
痛苦或者不能正确完成，它可能会产生负面影响。
屏幕所做的只是列出我们可以做的练习。 运动选择基于运动员的生
物力学能力。 一项练习的好坏取决于其执行能力。 如果某人在某些运
动中感到疼痛或受限，并且该运动对其执行运动模式的能力有直接影响
，则他们无法执行该运动模式。 现实并没有让这项练习变得糟糕；相
反，它是一种锻炼。 在这种情况下，这只会使该练习对于该运动员的
最终目标无效。 目的必须证明手段的合理性。 然而，只有以尽可能最
有效的方式实现最终目标，这些手段才是合理的。

规则 2：有效性和可靠性
我们的筛选需要既有效又可靠。

有效性证明我们所做的事情是准确的。 例如，如果我们想增加一项运
动对表现训练产生更直接影响的可能性，我们需要进行有效的运动选择
评估。这也表明我们正在为我们的训练假设制定标准。 假设只是根据
我们所知对我们认为可能发生的事情提出的解释。 它利用我们拥有的
所有信息，并围绕我们已知的真实信息进行实验。 如果我们有有效的
信息，我们就有更好的机会消除任何噪音。噪音减少意味着我们做出对
环境产生积极影响的决策的可能性更大；我们无法预测会发生什么。在
复杂环境中工作时，屏幕的有效性是运动选择最可控的方面。

你编写的任何训练计划都是一个科学实验。 如果您正在阅读本书，
您可能正在编写或已经编写过以下程序：

someone else. You collected relevant information, formed a hypothesis about
what to do, created an experiment or your training plan, calibrated your plan
based on your subjects’ compliance and motivation, and collected data on the
results. If you have compared baseline to posttesting based on a training plan
you implemented, you performed research. The big question we have to ask
is if you approached that training plan with the scientific precision necessary
to make any conclusions about your effect.
With any training plan, we have to accept that the part we do not know is
the foundation of the hypothesis. This is where it gets interesting. Because if
we go into the hypothesis with a bias without objectively looking at the needs
of the situation, the validity of our program and exercise selection becomes
tainted and deemed obsolete. If the hypothesis was correct, but the validity of
the screen did not assess what we needed it to, the training plan has to be
deemed irrelevant. Therefore, it is important to think critically about
everything we do. Sample sizes in research force our hypothesis to be more
objective, as with training programs with larger groups. Good science
explores the unknown, not what we want to be true.
We next have to consider the reliability of our screen. This is especially
important with large groups. We lose the ability to be as flexible with a plan
when things are not going the way we want with larger groups. Consistency
matters more when we amplify several things. If we increase training
sessions and the number of people in a session, the consistency with which
we do it will have a compounding effect on being reliable or unreliable if the
screen is not consistently administered. With screening, we need to have
reliability to prevent a negative compounding effect. Inconsistency is a major
driver of noise, which has a second-order effect of poor exercise selection
and program design.
Interrater reliability of the screen, or consistency among practitioners, is
more important with larger groups (which is the point of this book). If you
are the only one administering the screen, you do not need to worry about
this. Many coaches and physical therapists traditionally struggle with the
concept of standardized screens. The truth is that when you are working with
a single patient or athlete, you can get away with having a nonstandardized
screen. Working with larger groups makes having continuity among coaches

对于较大的群体，屏幕的评估者间可靠性或从业者之间的一致性更为
重要（这是本书的要点）。 如果您是唯一管理该屏幕的人，则无需担

到困惑。事实是，当您与单个患者或运动员一起工作时，您可以使用非

when administering a screen more important. It is again a compounding
problem, with unreliable screens leading to more noise when making
program decisions.
For better or worse, strength and conditioning professionals increasingly
need to screen not only for performance purposes but also for risk potential
(Minick et al., 2010). If you are one of many who will implement a screen,
quality controls need to be in place to ensure it is reliable when performed by
several coaches. We need to ensure the reliability and the interrater reliability
of all screening. We can bypass the need for interrater reliability by having
the same person do the screening over and over. This would be a short-term
and limited strategy. Working with hundreds of athletes creates a bottleneck
effect on the screen. It is certain that with larger groups, we need to scale
screening to several staff members. Even more of an issue with strength and
conditioning is that staff retention is really poor; chances are, someone else
will have to do a screen eventually.
Large groups + high staff turnover = scale the
screen
If the screen is not reliable, it is irrelevant.
If you are the only one who can administer the screen in a setting where
multiple people also need to administer the screen, then it is not a good
screen. In response to this, the concept of the human error element has
created a significant increase in the need for technology. In a setting where
we have a high volume of people with whom we are working and high
variance in the administrators of assessments, technology may be the only
asset we can leverage to ensure the highest interrater reliability. There are
inherent shortcomings with technology when analyzing things in three
dimensions or at the level of complexity required for processing a
multivariate movement system (Delp & Loan, 2000). However, relative to
poor screening standards and reliability scores, technology may be the best
option available.

The other major component to consider is the universal acceptance that
something is true among staff and athletes. We will have to rely on agreedupon objective assessments. A test or a screen should not be exclusive to a
specific audience. If we have a universally true screen, we have an objective
analysis that transcends human bias and gets to tangible data points we can
work from. There is a difference here between a performance test and a
movement screen. In a performance test, we are trying to narrow our focus by
pinpointing what we need for bimotor development. In a movement screen,
we are creating a platform that will help us handle high randomness and
variance. In preparing for chaos, the quality of the screen is in its ability to
appraise the probability of risk (Cook, 2011).

Modifying Lifts
Every program will have a part where a certain exercise will not
work. It is not a matter of if, but when, regarding having to modify
a lift.
Two questions that we want to ask when we face having to
modify an exercise. The first one is, why do we need to modify?
The second one is, to what can we modify?
The first question is almost entirely pain related. Contact
sports face this daily—noncontact sports not as much, but pain
will still be a recurring issue. Sometimes it is a motor issue, and
we have to find a variation of the exercise that we can be
successful with. In the event of pain, we will need to find an
exercise that does not hurt when performed.
The second question of what we can modify is based on doing
something that does not hurt. The issue is that we have a reason
behind the exercise we programmed, so what options does that
leave us with? We do want to mimic what we intended to do in
the first place as much as possible. We also want to not disrupt
the training session by having a coach displaced from their racks
or the athletes they are assigned to. Last, we want the coach to
have a contingency plan and the athlete to feel confident that the

另一个需要考虑的主要因素是工作人员和运动员普遍接受某些事情是
真实的。 我们必须依赖商定的客观评估。 测试或屏幕不应专属于特定
受众。如果我们有一个普遍真实的屏幕，我们就可以进行超越人类偏见
的客观分析，并获得我们可以利用的有形数据点。 性能测试和运动屏
幕之间存在差异。在性能测试中，我们试图通过查明双电机开发所需的
内容来缩小我们的关注范围。 在运动屏幕中，我们正在创建一个平台
，帮助我们处理高随机性和方差。 在为混乱做准备时，筛选的质量在
于其评估风险概率的能力（Cook，2011）。

改装电梯
每个程序都会有某个练习不起作用的部分。对于必须改造电梯，
这不是是否会发生的问题，而是何时发生的问题。
当我们面临必须修改练习时我们想问的两个问题。第一个是，
为什么我们需要修改？第二个是，我们可以修改什么？
第一个问题几乎完全与疼痛有关。 接触性运动每天都会面临这
样的问题——非接触性运动则没有那么多，但疼痛仍然是一个反
复出现的问题。有时这是一个运动问题，我们必须找到一种可以
成功的锻炼方式。 如果出现疼痛，我们需要找到一种执行时不会
疼痛的运动。
我们可以修改的第二个问题是基于做一些无害的事情。问题是
我们计划的练习背后有一个理由，那么这给我们留下了哪些选择
呢？ 我们确实想尽可能地模仿我们最初打算做的事情。 我们还
希望不要因为教练或他们所分配的运动员离开训练场而扰乱训练
。最后，我们希望教练有一个应急计划，并且运动员有信心

modification was thought out ahead of time.
The easiest thing to do here is to be aware. Programming
high-impact exercises or exercises that require the extremities to
have high ROM during the season is typically going to be met
with a lot of modifications. The second easiest thing to do is to
keep notes. If we know someone has an orthopedic issue, we
should have an account of that and make the changes before
they come to the weight room.
Regarding on-the-fly modifications, we want to stay as close
to the movement pattern as possible. We want to avoid random
changes. This can be confusing down the road, as well as lead
to structural imbalance if the modifications are redundant to other
exercises. Taking joints away from the lift by holding the weight
in a different position is pretty easy to do in a team setting.
Altering the position of the load is also easy.
Having a plan for potential modifications can be foundational
for continued progress in every athlete. It demonstrates that
training is always important. Regardless of circumstances, such
as injury or pain, there is always a means to getting better.
It is interesting to think about what a real key performance indicator (KPI)
is and what we latch onto regarding the training stimulus. We assume there is
a one-to-one relationship between increasing someone’s aptitude with a
specific exercise and leading seamlessly to increases in performance. With
that said, Parchmann and McBride (2011) found a weak correlation between
the functional movement screen (FMS) and sprinting, jumping, and agility
assessments. However, there was a strong correlation between the FMS and
one rep max squat. A screen’s job is not to predict performance. A screen is
not a KPI; it is an appraisal of risk that involves things we will do
redundantly in training and practice.

Rule 3: Rules and KPIs Differ

修改是提前考虑好的。
这里最简单的事情就是保持觉知。 在赛季中编写高影响力的练
习或要求四肢具有高活动度的练习通常需要进行大量修改。 第二
个最简单的事情是记笔记。 如果我们知道某人有骨科问题，我们
应该在他们来举重室之前对此进行说明并做出改变。

关于动态修改，我们希望尽可能接近运动模式。 我们希望避免
随机变化。 这可能会造成混乱，如果修改对其他练习来说是多余
的，还会导致结构不平衡。 在团队环境中，通过将重物保持在不
同的位置来将关节从举重机上移开是很容易做到的。改变负载的
位置也很容易。
制定潜在修改计划是每位运动员持续进步的基础。 这表明培训
始终很重要。 无论情况如何，例如受伤或疼痛，总有办法让病情
好转。

思考什么是真正的关键绩效指标 (KPI) 以及我们对培训刺激的关注点
是很有趣的。我们假设通过特定练习提高某人的能力与无缝地提高绩效
之间存在一对一的关系。 尽管如此，Parchmann 和 McBride (2011) 发现
功能运动筛查 (FMS) 与短跑、跳跃和敏捷性评估之间的相关性很弱。
然而，FMS 和一次最大深蹲次数之间存在很强的相关性。屏幕的作用不
是预测性能。屏幕不是 KPI；而是 KPI。 这是对风险的评估，涉及我们
在培训和实践中多余做的事情。

规则 3：规则和 KPI 不同

A screen is not a key performance indicator.
The idea that there is one screen to assess all possible risks is utterly
impossible (Bahr & Holme, 2003). It is such a multivariate problem we are
facing that predicting all possible risks from a single screen is not realistic.
Doing this at scale with a larger number of athletes, multiple coaches, and a
time-condensed schedule makes it even more implausible that a single screen
can accurately and consistently appraise risk. However, there is one obvious
point that is often overlooked, which is simply the acknowledgment that
previous injury is the best predictor of future injury (Bahr & Holmes, 2003).
No matter what screening tool you use, it will always be less accurate than
simply asking, “Have you been injured before?” After that, picking simple
heuristic-based screening procedures gives us a solid foundation for better
exercise selection.

Rule 4: Pain and Injury Affect Movement
Pain and previous injury are by far the simplest
and most important screen to appraise future risk.
We know the outcome is unpredictable. Screening, therefore, needs to
appraise our ability to handle chaos as adequately as possible.
A screen needs to be valid and reliable when
combined with larger groups to have a high
degree of interrater reliability and to be
universally accepted as true to reduce noise to
prepare for unpredictability.
We need to incorporate a screen that can be true in any setting and any
context. A good screen needs to give us tangible information that will help us

屏幕是not一个关键性能指标。
用一个屏幕来评估所有可能风险的想法是完全不可能的（Bahr & Holme
，2003）。 我们面临的是一个多变量问题，从单个屏幕预测所有可能
的风险是不现实的。大规模地进行这项工作，涉及大量运动员、多名教
练和时间紧迫的赛程，这使得单一屏幕能够准确、一致地评估风险变得
更加难以置信。 然而，有一个明显的点经常被忽视，那就是承认以前
的损伤是未来损伤的最佳预测因素（Bahr & Holmes，2003）。无论你
使用什么筛查工具，它总是不如简单地问“你以前受过伤吗？”准确。
之后，选择简单的启发式筛选程序为我们更好地选择运动项目奠定了坚
实的基础。

规则 4：疼痛和受伤影响运动
疼痛和既往伤害是迄今为止评估未来风险的最简单和最
重要的屏幕。
我们知道结果是不可预测的。 因此，筛选需要尽可能充分地评估我们
处理混乱的能力。
当与较大群体结合时，屏幕需要有效且可靠，以具有高
度的参与者间可靠性，并被普遍接受为真实的，以减少
噪音，为不可预测性做好准备。

我们需要整合一个在任何环境和任何环境下都可以真实存在的屏幕。
一个好的屏幕需要为我们提供有形的信息来帮助我们

make the best decisions possible for exercise selection. If we have a valid and
reliable metric, such as injury history, we can build off that. It will never be
perfect, but we can get closer with more information. We are aware of a
known risk factor. More importantly, injury risk is typically associated with
pain. Pain and injury histories are simple, easily understood, and accepted as
important and can be done across multiple coaches and athletes over any
length of time.

Injured Workouts
The team setting is filled with paradoxes. The more advanced
the athlete, the less you do. Injured athletes need more attention
but get less attention because of their injuries.
We have all been faced with an athlete who comes into a lift
with something broken, and we have to scramble to make a
workout that they can execute. Lower body injuries will be met
with upper body exercises. Upper body injury will be met with
lower body exercises. This will involve a quick description,
asking if they have any questions, and then sending them on
their way.
Sometimes we feel guilty and have a special time for them.
This is another paradox; your willingness to do one-on-one
injured workouts is contingent on whether it stays one-on-one.
The reason it is so paradoxical is that you do not want to make
this into a “thing.” Your time is valuable, and having a bunch of
athletes showing up to an injured workout makes it another
group. Essentially, you have added another group to your day.
You may safeguard yourself from turning this into another
group that you have to coach by choosing a time that only that
one person can come in, such as “See you Sunday at 5 a.m.”
You may make this hybrid, where you take them through the
complicated stuff and they do the less complicated stuff, such as
stationary pieces of cardio or machines. It may be working with
sports medicine, doing strength work around their rehab.

为运动选择做出尽可能最好的决定。如果我们有一个有效且可靠的指标
，例如伤病史，我们就可以以此为基础。 它永远不会是完美的，但我
们可以通过更多信息来接近完美。 我们知道一个已知的风险因素。 更
重要的是，受伤风险通常与疼痛相关。疼痛和受伤史简单、容易理解且
被认为很重要，并且可以在任意时间长度内由多名教练和运动员完成。

通过上半身锻炼来解决。 上半身受伤可通过下半身锻炼来解决。

前进。

您可以选择一个只有一个人可以进来的时间，例如“周日早上

康复期间进行力量训练。

The big reason you do not want this turning into another group
is that it represents a lot more people getting injured than you
want. It is unsettling to have many athletes in an injured group. It
is symbolic of a program getting off course. The antidote has
become a poison in some respects when you have an injured
group larger than your main group.
Having intratraining sessions is the easiest way to combat
this. You will need to give your undivided attention. As a head
strength coach, the responsibility will fall primarily on you. Rightly
so, it is outside of the purview of a day-to-day off-season plan for
most strength coaches. Chances are that the injured athlete was
injured while playing and is a contributor to the team’s success.
Making sure the injured athlete is staying on track and possibly
improving becomes critical and falls mainly on the higher-up
strength coaches on the staff.
Recall the concepts of top down, bottom up, whole part, and part whole.
What this refers to is starting with the movement pattern and breaking down
to joint assessments or starting with joint assessments and integrating them
into a movement pattern. There are two major questions to evaluate when
examining what direction a screen needs to go: How long do you have to
screen? How much detail is needed to get the information we need?
If we could simply ask, “Have you been injured before, and are you
currently in pain?” that would be all that’s needed to prepare for a chaotic
world, and we could stop there. Inventorying current pain and previous injury
only would be incredibly efficient. The only problem is that it wouldn’t give
us much direction, but it would be quick. Starting with movement patterns,
you get a 10,000 ft view of the problem. You know there is pain or potential
risk, but you just may not know where.
Alternatively, we could start with individual assessments of each joint’s
ROM and get a deeper understanding of how each joint is functioning. You
would have a good understanding of the limitations of each joint or pain in
specific directions at certain degrees of freedom. This would be incredibly
time-consuming, and you would not consider the total transfer to integrated

Rule 5: Joint ROM Is Movement Potential
Joint ROM dictates the potential for movement
patterns.
It is a chicken-or-egg kind of problem. If you have 100 people and you have
to screen them in an hour, you have to sacrifice detail. Let me rephrase that:
Sacrifice unnecessary detail. If you have one person with unlimited time, you
can add as much detail as possible. What is realistic is not the same as what is
ideal—you effectively have to make a choice. With all things considered,
having a screen that gives you a smaller amount of information rapidly will
have more value than one that gives a lot of information slowly. There is a
tradeoff between time and detail, but that does not necessarily mean you
cannot achieve effectiveness with a short screen. We can create a hierarchy of
necessary information to work through.
In terms of direction, using a movement pattern to assess joints requires a
known dichotomy. Meaning, if you do not need to know individual joint
actions because the movement patterns associated with those joints are
operating adequately, you have relevant information. If the sum of the parts is
performing, the parts are therefore adequate. An argument could be made that
you do not need to assess anymore; anything would be a waste. If you are
strapped for time, the need for extra information becomes less valuable. If we
unnecessarily add detail to the screen, knowing there is a tradeoff between
reliability, we make ourselves vulnerable to inconsistencies. The evaluation
of what movement we need to know versus what is nice to know is important.
It is especially important if validity is suffering due to low reliability or even
low interrater reliability.

A case could be made for starting with joint assessments and following up
with the movements. This premise is usually useful if someone is in pain and
