Rule 6: Pain Requires More Information
Pain requires more detail from your screen
through isolated joint ROM testing.
We have to look first at the point of a screen and then understand the context
in which we are doing the screening. If we want to prepare for as much as
possible, we need a screen that gets a lot of information rapidly that is both
valid and interrater reliable. At the same time, we need to gather more details
when more information is relevant. Pain creates a functional need to have
more information. Pain limits exercise selection more than joint ROM or
movement patterns, which makes us need to know where that pain occurs.
The only issue is that isolated joint ROM is less interrater reliable. A limited
number of people can assess joint ROM on any given staff. This creates a
bottleneck if we do not have systems for determining relevant information.

What should be done with everyone has to be fast, valid, and reliable
(figure 9.2). Here’s a practical example I’ve used and continue to use: First,
asking about pain and previous injury is the best predictor of future injury
(Bahr & Holme, 2003). Second is progress to countermovement jump (CMJ)
on a bilateral force plate. This serves two purposes. One, can they jump? If
they cannot, they are more than likely in pain, which would be an increased
risk (Cook, 2011). Two, do they jump with asymmetry? Asymmetry is a
known risk factor for injury and needs to be accounted for (Menzel et al.,
2013). A critical piece of this is the objectivity and higher level of interrater
reliability with bilateral force plates.
What is important to note on asymmetry is the perspective of risk
associated. Research associated with asymmetry is predictive within complex
environments. Athletes with asymmetries are more likely to be injured during
competition than those without (Cook, 2011). But that is only part of the

每个人应该做的事情必须是快速、有效和可靠的（图 9.2）。 这是我

未来伤害的最佳预测指标（Bahr＆Holme，2003）。其次是双边力板上
的反向运动跳跃（CMJ）的进展。 这有两个目的。 一、他们能跳吗？
如果他们不能，他们很可能会感到痛苦，这会增加风险（Cook，2011）
。 第二，它们的跳跃是否不对称？ 不对称是已知的受伤风险因素，需

patterns we will use during training. We leverage movement patterns with
certain amounts of external load, volume, and duration to create positive
adaptation. If those movement patterns are compromised, for example,
asymmetry during a controlled screen, the potential benefit from those
patterns is compromised as well.

Rule 7: Asymmetries Compromise Movement Ability
Asymmetries can potentially compromise benefits
from training.
Following a pain and injury appraisal along with CMJ, we potentially move
on to an FMS. Potentially because this takes time, which may not be a luxury
we have. Functional movement screening is a fantastic tool that can interpret
pain, asymmetry, and restricted ROM during movement patterns (Chimera &
Warren, 2015). Regardless of personal opinion, FMS, from the perspective of
validity in predicting injury risk and interrater reliability, is an extremely
effective diagnostic tool. Remember, the primary issue with the screen is
related to time. If we have something that can be done relatively quickly, is
considered valid in terms of risk appraisal, and has high interrater reliability,
it becomes necessary information after we determine that pain, injury, and
asymmetry are present.
Time is the factor that matters most in determining whether we proceed
within a screen. On the one hand, the FMS holds several key pieces of
information; on the other hand, we have to evaluate the opportunity cost.
Ideally, we run the screen on everyone, but this is not feasible. This is where
the screen takes on an if-then relationship. If there is asymmetry within the
CMJ, then we will need to assess further with the FMS. With the FMS, we
can dive into seven separate screens, five of which are asymmetrical. We can
assess further patterns that are asymmetrical within supine, quadruped,
standing, split stance, and single-leg stance positions. We can isolate the
ankle, shoulder, lumbar spine, and hip in terms of asymmetry, pain, and

如果这些运动模式受到损害，例如受控屏幕期间的不对称性，那么这些

Rule 8: Group Sizes Constrain Appraisal Time
With time constraints, we will need to be selective
with screening. The screens we choose will have
to give us the information we need and nothing
more.
If we find pain, this takes precedence over any time constraints. Pain will
have a more direct impact on any exercise we choose, more so than
asymmetries. Pain, therefore, needs more detail than any other factor related
to biomechanics. This will require a series of table tests to assess each joint’s
capacity (figure 9.3). Assessment is centered on the passive ROM (PROM)
compared to the active ROM (AROM). PROM is the potential for the joint.
PROM is centered on how many degrees of freedom a joint can demonstrate
without muscular contraction. AROM is the ability of the joint. AROM is
centered on how many degrees of freedom a joint can demonstrate with
muscular contraction. We need PROM before we can have AROM, but we
cannot have movement control without AROM.

规则 8：小组规模限制评估时间
由于时间有限，我们需要有选择性地进行筛选。 我们
选择的屏幕必须能够提供我们需要的信息，仅此而已。

如果我们发现疼痛，这优先于任何时间限制。 疼痛对我们选择的任何
运动都会产生比不对称更直接的影响。因此，与生物力学相关的任何其
他因素相比，疼痛需要更多的细节。这需要进行一系列的桌面测试来评
估每个接头的能力（图 9.3）。 评估的重点是被动 ROM (PROM) 与主
动 ROM (AROM) 的比较。 PROM 是关节的潜力。 PROM 的重点是在
没有肌肉收缩的情况下关节可以展示多少自由度。 AROM是关节的能
力。 AROM 的重点是肌肉收缩时关节可以表现出多少自由度。 在拥有
AROM之前我们需要PROM，但是没有AROM我们就无法进行运动控制
。

Rule 9: Pain Supersedes Time
Pain makes the time the screen takes irrelevant.
Screening takes time; the question is whether the information we get from the
screen makes training more effective. Can we filter out everything we do not
need while at the same time telling us what we will get the most value from?
Screening is not meant to just check a box but to give us context on what will
garner the most value from training. Screening can be a waste of time if it
does not have a direct impact on your programming decisions.

Take Home

FIGURE 9.3 Table test.

规则九：痛苦胜过时间
疼痛使得屏幕上花费的时间变得无关紧要。
筛查需要时间；问题是我们从屏幕上获得的信息是否能让训练更有效。
我们能否过滤掉不需要的所有内容，同时告诉我们将从中获得最大价值
？筛选不仅仅是勾选一个框，而是让我们了解什么可以从培训中获得最
大价值。 如果筛选不能对您的节目决策产生直接影响，那么它可能会
浪费时间。

带回家

Screening is about making better decisions with programming. It reduces
noise and gives us context on what to do versus what not to do. Time is an
extremely important factor in screening within a team setting. Taking time
from training is only beneficial if we get something of value from that time.
To do that, we need to have both valid and interrater reliable data.

筛选是为了通过编程做出更好的决策。 它减少了噪音，并为我们提供
了关于该做什么和不该做什么的背景信息。 时间是团队环境中筛选的
一个极其重要的因素。 只有当我们从培训中获得有价值的东西时，从
培训中抽出时间才是有益的。为此，我们需要拥有有效且可靠的数据。

10
APPLYING BIOMECHANICAL
RULES FOR STRUCTURAL
BALANCE
Following through on our baseline movement assessment is important to
ensure we are holding ourselves accountable to a higher level of thought with
our programming. The next and most important step is having an intuitive
and applicable system for programming. We need to have a convergence of
what we learned from our movement assessment with what we can
implement at scale. The movement assessment is the foundation of rules for
us to implement effective and safe training for large numbers over a longer
period.
Having valid and interrater reliable testing methods allows us to evaluate
the relative risk associated with each athlete within a group. We placed a
strong emphasis on movement potential. Do we have the ability to articulate
each joint to its full degree of excursion? If we cannot fully articulate a joint,
that becomes the rate-limiting step during a compound (multijoint) movement
pattern. Limited ROM (range of motion) of a joint is a compromised
movement pattern. This greatly diminishes the value we can obtain from the
program we implement.
This is important because the central aspect of training essentially comes
down to driving specific movement patterns to a threshold. The threshold is

10
应用生物力学规则实现结构平衡

遵循我们的基线运动评估对于确保我们在编程中对更高水平的思想负责
非常重要。 下一步也是最重要的一步是拥有一个直观且适用的编程系
统。 我们需要将从运动评估中学到的知识与我们可以大规模实施的知
识结合起来。 动作评估是我们长期、有效、安全地进行大批量训练的
规则基础。

拥有有效且在参与者之间可靠的测试方法使我们能够评估与组内每个
运动员相关的相对风险。 我们非常重视运动潜力。我们是否有能力将
每个关节连接到其最大程度的偏移？如果我们无法完全清晰地表达一个
关节，那么这将成为复合（多关节）运动模式中的速率限制步骤。 关
节的有限 ROM（运动范围）是一种受损的运动模式。这极大地减少了
我们从实施的计划中获得的价值。
这很重要，因为训练的核心本质上就是将特定的运动模式驱动到阈值
。 阈值是

the key to unlocking results in other areas, such as running faster or running
farther. To unlock the outcome we want, we will need to perform these
movement patterns that are redundantly pushed to a threshold. We will need a
certain volume, at a certain intensity, at a certain density, and with a certain
level of frequency to create adaptation. It is that redundancy, combined with
pushing to a threshold, that makes understanding the risk associated with
poor movement potential imperative for success.
We train these movement patterns, such as squats or hinges, constantly to
pursue something else, such as being able to jump higher or run faster. They
are simply a means to an end. If we do not have the prerequisite ROM of a
joint associated with that movement pattern, it lowers the potential from that
movement pattern. The patterns we use for development end up being the
product of our demise.
We want to build our program with the best exercises possible for each
athlete. If we lack the prerequisite ability before selecting an exercise, we will
lose value from that exercise. We do not want to limit our exercise’s
potential. Instead, we want to limit the number of exercises to provide the
most potential.

Structural Balance Rules
Rules are our constraints to ensuring we deliver the highest quality
experience and yield the best possible outcome. When you think about
biomechanical rules, think of exercise selection that maximizes structural
balance (figure 10.1). Remember that exercises are conduits of variables to
leverage an outcome. We want to be strategic with selecting exercises that we
can load redundantly to a threshold. The ability of that exercise to yield a
consistently better outcome is based on its foundational biomechanics.

解锁其他领域成果的关键，例如跑得更快或跑得更远。 为了解锁我们
想要的结果，我们需要执行这些被冗余推至阈值的运动模式。我们需要
一定的音量、一定的强度、一定的密度和一定的频率来创造适应。正是
这种冗余，加上达到阈值，使得了解与不良运动潜在相关的风险对于成
功至关重要。
我们不断训练这些运动模式，例如深蹲或铰链，以追求其他目标，例
如能够跳得更高或跑得更快。它们只是达到目的的一种手段。 如果我
们不具备与该运动模式相关的关节的必备 ROM，就会降低该运动模式
的潜力。 我们用于开发的模式最终会成为我们消亡的产物。
我们希望为每位运动员提供尽可能最好的练习来制定我们的计划。如
果我们在选择一项练习之前缺乏先决能力，我们就会失去该练习的价值
。 我们不想限制我们锻炼的潜力。 相反，我们希望限制练习的数量以
发挥最大的潜力。

结构平衡规则
规则是我们确保提供最高质量的体验并产生最佳结果的约束。 当您考
虑生物力学规则时，请考虑最大化结构平衡的运动选择（图 10.1）。
请记住，练习是利用变量来影响结果的渠道。我们希望战略性地选择可
以冗余加载到阈值的练习。 该练习能够持续产生更好的结果，这是基
于其基本的生物力学。

Ensure the potential of full articulation (range of
motion) of all movement patterns.

incredibly quickly (figure 10.2). The issue is that large groups with a poor
coach-to-athlete ratio compound with the redundancies and thresholds of
exercises we have to work with. Aberrant motion is a tiny hole in a dam. One
person working with a small dam can see more clearly what is wrong and

确保所有运动模式的充分关节（运动范围）的潜力。

我们需要将用于决策的量表与运动选择联系起来。 教练与运动员比例

。一个在小水坝工作的人可以更清楚地看到问题所在，并

FIGURE 10.2 Unmanageable versus manageable.
A very general concept that should feel intuitive, structural balance is a
commonly missed aspect of programming; forcing an exercise without
having the prerequisite ROM of the joints associated will lead to
compromised performance. We cannot add ROM to a joint during a
movement pattern. ROM has to be established before we integrate with other
joints during coordinated movement. If one joint is limited, another joint will
have to compensate for it. All movement patterns involve managing joints.
Joints provide the articulation to allow for that movement pattern to occur. If
we do not have the joint function, we will not have the movement pattern.
Forcing a pattern without evaluating the potential of that pattern is a mistake.
If ROM is the first step, then the next step is to have control of that ROM.

。 我们需要建立对运动模式进行编程的规则，以避免通过完全限制它
们而使小问题复杂化。

图 10.2 难以管理与易于管理。
一个非常普遍的概念，应该感觉直观，结构平衡是编程中经常被忽视
的一个方面； 在没有相关关节必要活动范围的情况下强行进行锻炼将
导致性能下降。 我们无法在运动模式期间将 ROM 添加到关节。在协调
运动期间，我们必须在与其他关节整合之前建立ROM。如果一个关节受
到限制，则另一个关节必须对其进行补偿。 所有运动模式都涉及关节
管理。关节提供关节以允许该运动模式发生。如果我们没有关节功能，
我们就不会有运动模式。在不评估该模式的潜力的情况下强行采用某种
模式是错误的。
如果 ROM 是第一步，那么下一步就是控制该 ROM。

It is one thing to be able to move a joint through full articulation. It is another
thing to control that articulation through that degree of ROM within an
integrated movement pattern. This is why we need a more holistic approach
to movement assessments. We cannot simply rely on isolated joint tests; we
need to see that pattern in action. If we lack the prerequisite ROM, we will
not be able to move without compensation. If we do not have control of a full
ROM, we will not be able to move without compensation. These two
variables, ROM and control, are interdependent movement patterns.

Rule 2: Joint Control
Ensure joint control during movement.
We have to appraise the interaction between joints during movement to
predict our ability to garner value from those movements. Movement
standards are a tricky subject because they largely depend on the context in
which that movement pattern is being used. There are definitive strategies
that alter the center of mass, length, tension, mechanical advantage, and
momentum. Any of these strategies affects the potential external load we can
use, the speed at which we move, or the duration for which we can move.
This creates a paradox with programming. We need something tangible
(force, velocity, work) to leverage the exercise’s potential value, but that
value is predicated on being able to move with control through a full ROM.
The point of an exercise is to correspond to something else, such as
running faster or farther. It is easy to associate success with an exercise as a
cause for success elsewhere. This is the classic causation-correlation paradox.
Is improvement in something from altering technique the cause of
performance improvement? We can easily improve performance with a
certain exercise by altering ROM, position, or momentum. The question then
becomes, if technique is subject to whatever facilitates more from that
exercise, will that exercise translate as much to performance? Will modifying
the technique to lift more weight transfer to performance? We justify things
because they are quantifiable, but is that a good thing? Being stronger and

能够通过完全关节活动来移动关节是一回事。在集成的运动模式中通过
一定程度的 ROM 来控制关节是另一回事。 这就是为什么我们需要一种
更全面的运动评估方法。 我们不能简单地依赖孤立的联合试验； 我们
需要看到这种模式的实际应用。 如果我们缺乏必备的ROM，我们将无
法在没有补偿的情况下移动。如果我们无法控制完整的 ROM，我们将
无法在没有补偿的情况下移动。 ROM 和控制这两个变量是相互依赖的
运动模式。

规则 2：联合控制
确保运动过程中的关节控制。
我们必须评估运动过程中关节之间的相互作用，以预测我们从这些运动
中获取价值的能力。 运动标准是一个棘手的主题，因为它们在很大程
度上取决于使用该运动模式的上下文。 有一些明确的策略可以改变质
心、长度、张力、机械优势和动量。这些策略中的任何一个都会影响我
们可以使用的潜在外部负载、我们移动的速度或我们可以移动的持续时
间。这造成了编程的悖论。 我们需要一些有形的东西（力、速度、功
）来利用练习的潜在价值，但该价值的前提是能够通过完整的活动范围
控制移动。
锻炼的目的是与其他事物相对应，例如跑得更快或更远。人们很容易
将成功与某项练习联系起来，认为这是其他地方成功的原因。这是经典
的因果相关悖论。改变技术带来的某些方面的改进是性能提高的原因吗
？ 我们可以通过改变活动范围、位置或动量来轻松提高某项练习的表
现。那么问题就变成了，如果技术受到任何有助于从该练习中获得更多
帮助的东西的影响，那么该练习是否会同样转化为表现？修改技术以举
起更多重量会影响表现吗？ 我们证明事物的合理性是因为它们是可以
量化的，但这是一件好事吗？ 变得更强并且

lifting more weight might not be correlated with each other.
A concept used in S&C is movements, not muscles. This means that we are
using compound movements, usually closed kinetic chain, and free-weight
exercises when training athletes, which is not the same as training individual
muscles. This was a departure from isolated movements, open kinetic chain,
and machine-based weights, which focus heavily on tension within a muscle
—a method that is not as transferable to the biomechanics of sport. The
extreme focus on outputs from compound, closed chain, free-weight
movements (i.e., external load) over the actual execution loses the connection
with the purpose of the exercise. We seemingly stopped training the
contractile and noncontractile tissues associated with a movement pattern
when we made this shift. Instead, we judge an exercise’s value almost
exclusively on what output it produces, regardless of how it was done.
Exercise selection involves taking the information we have from a
movement screen and then leveraging that information toward an outcome.
The exercise is a means to an end. The means is attempting to move within
certain parameters, such as joints involved, vectors used, or planes of motion
moved within. The results we get come from developing the movement
pattern along with the stress we place on the tissues associated with those
parameters. In a sense, we can augment the phrase to movements, not
muscles, but movements stress muscles.
How well we can do something should precede
how much we can do.
The pendulum swing of perceiving movements as detached from muscle
groups has made S&C professionals phobic against certain exercises. This is
further compounded by working in team or group settings. We criticize
certain tools for not having enough utility to match the needs of a large
group. Certain machines are now considered taboo for facility design due to
their limited use relative to the space they take up within a gym space. The
idea is based on the premise that we only need tools with unlimited utility
with a minimal footprint when working within a team setting. Although it

举更多的重量可能彼此不相关。
S&C 中使用的一个概念是movements, not muscles。这意味着我们在训
练运动员时使用的是复合动作，通常是闭合动力链，以及自由重量练习
，这与训练个体肌肉不同。这与孤立的运动、开放的动力链和基于机器
的重量不同，后者主要关注肌肉内的张力——这种方法不能转移到运动
的生物力学中。 在实际执行中过度关注复合、闭链、自由重量运动（
即外部负载）的输出会失去与练习目的的联系。 当我们进行这种转变
时，我们似乎停止了与运动模式相关的收缩和非收缩组织的训练。 相
反，我们判断一项活动的价值几乎完全取决于它产生的产出，而不管它
是如何完成的。

运动选择包括从运动屏幕中获取信息，然后利用该信息来获得结果。
练习是达到目的的一种手段。 means 尝试在某些参数内移动，例如涉
及的关节、使用的矢量或在其中移动的运动平面。 我们得到的结果来
自于开发运动模式以及我们对与这些参数相关的组织施加的压力。 从
某种意义上说，我们可以将短语扩充为 movements, not
muscles, but movements stress muscles。

我们能把某件事做得有多好，应该先于我们能做多少。

感觉运动与肌肉群分离的摇摆不定使得 S&C 专业人士对某些练习感
到恐惧。在团队或小组环境中工作会进一步加剧这种情况。 我们批评
某些工具没有足够的实用性来满足一大群人的需求。 某些机器现在被
认为是设施设计的禁忌，因为它们相对于它们在健身房空间内占用的空
间而言使用有限。 这个想法基于这样一个前提：在团队环境中工作时
，我们只需要具有无限实用性且占地面积最小的工具。 虽然它

may open compound, closed kinetic chain exercises, it will create a
bottleneck in adequately developing structural balance. We will delve into
this topic in facility design (chapter 14), but certain tools are more effective
than others for certain muscle groups. Movements, not muscles, can limit us
in exercise selection and adequate stressing of antagonist tissues uniformly.
We can overdevelop certain muscle groups and neglect others by simply not
having the right tools, which is the foundation for structural imbalance.
Think about it for a second; when doing a new exercise with an athlete,
their first question is “What does this work?” Your response probably will
not be “a knee dominant, horizontally vectored, sagittally oriented movement
pattern” when doing split squats. Chances are, out of convenience and
simplicity’s sake, you’ll say, “It works your quads.” Working quads is no
longer the reason we train split squats in training, but maybe it should be. The
foundation of structural balance is balancing stress between pushing- and
pulling-based exercises. How are we going to distribute stress between the
anterior and posterior aspects of our extremities? If we look at a split squat as
a quad exercise, does that change the way we do that exercise? Does that
change how much time we spend on that compared to a more hamstringoriented movement pattern? This creates another line of questioning: Can we
reach the same level of stress on the hamstring group, relative to the
quadriceps, if we do not have tools that adequately stress the hamstring group
as much as the quadriceps?
After ROM and control comes technique. The movement patterns we
choose to help us reach an outcome are only as good as our execution. If we
have poor execution, we will not effectively reach the outcome we want. Poor
execution could come from bad progression as easily as an extreme focus on
output. We have lost reliability in our training program because we have not
established good and bad techniques. When we lose reliability, we lose
validity. We cannot say something was valid or a cause of success if there
was no determined good or bad input. The output is only objective if the
input is standardized. We have to establish the execution of good technique
for every exercise before we can say it is beneficial to performance. The big
question is, how do we determine good versus bad?
ROM and control are prerequisites for technique. Technique is the

可能会打开复合的、封闭的动力链练习，这会给充分发展结构平衡造成
瓶颈。 我们将在设施设计中深入探讨这个主题（第 14 章），但对于某
些肌肉群来说，某些工具比其他工具更有效。运动，而不是肌肉，可以
限制我们的运动选择和对拮抗组织的均匀压力。由于没有合适的工具，
我们可能会过度发展某些肌肉群而忽视其他肌肉群，这是结构失衡的基
础。
想一想； 当与运动员一起进行新的练习时，他们的第一个问题是“
这有什么作用？” 在进行分腿深蹲时，你的反应可能不会是“膝盖主
导、水平矢量、矢状方向的运动模式”。 出于方便和简单的考虑，您
很可能会说，“它对您的股四头肌有用。” 股四头肌训练不再是我们
在训练中训练分腿深蹲的原因，但也许应该如此。结构平衡的基础是平
衡推拉练习之间的压力。 我们如何在四肢的前部和后部之间分配压力
？如果我们将分腿深蹲视为股四头肌练习，这会改变我们进行这项练习
的方式吗？ 与更注重腿筋的运动模式相比，这会改变我们花在这上面
的时间吗？这就产生了另一道疑问：如果我们没有足够的工具对腘绳肌
群施加与股四头肌一样大的压力，那么我们能否对腘绳肌群施加与股四
头肌相同的压力水平？

ROM 和控制之后是技术。 我们选择帮助我们取得成果的运动模式的
好坏取决于我们的执行力。如果执行力差，我们就无法有效地达到我们
想要的结果。执行力差可能源于糟糕的进展，也可能源于过度关注产出
。我们的训练计划失去了可靠性，因为我们没有确定好的和坏的技术。
当我们失去可靠性时，我们就失去了有效性。 如果没有确定的好的或
坏的输入，我们就不能说某件事是有效的或成功的原因。 只有输入标
准化，输出才是客观的。 我们必须为每项练习建立良好的技术执行力
，然后才能说它对表现有益。最大的问题是，我们如何确定好与坏？

ROM和控制是技术的先决条件。 技术是

standard by which we choose to move. The standard of movement, technique,
is assurance that we adequately stress the correct tissues at the correct time. It
is very simple; if we have a good technique throughout a training program
and we have good results, the intervention is good. If we have a bad
technique, the outcome is irrelevant because we cannot say that the input was
consistent. We lose the foundation of truth without establishing a good
technique. If we do not have a predetermined ROM, control, and position
during an exercise, we cannot determine what is good.
Having a standard of movement gives us an indication of where that loss
of control occurs. Loss of technique comes from one of two areas: poor
motor function or low capacity. To optimize the effect of an exercise, we
have to push the threshold limits of force, velocity, and work. Pushing to the
threshold requires us to have a hardwired motor pattern along with the tissue
capacity to sustain optimal technique. Progression from one block to the next
reinforces that motor pattern. Progressive overload reinforces that tissue
tolerance. If we lose that standard of movement, we lose the effectiveness of
both progression and progressive overload. From simple to more
complicated, combined with adapting to the stress imposed, is how we tease
out positive effects from training programs.
A key behind the technique is that we intentionally and objectively stress
something. We often downplay the idea of sensation during an exercise.
When someone feels targeted, intentional stress in a specific muscle group
based on the mechanics of an exercise, we are ensuring the technique is
adequate. Alternatively, if we feel tissues are not being targeted during an
exercise, we can, by default, say that the technique was less than adequate.
The standard of movement we use allows for accurate prediction of the
tissues we intend to stress. Execution creates a target of which muscles are to
be stressed. This is foundational to creating balance in stress and
subsequently, adaptation.

Rule 3: Tissue Tolerance
Develop tissue
patterns.

tolerance

during

movement

我们选择搬家的标准。运动和技术的标准是确保我们在正确的时间对正
确的组织施加足够的压力。很简单； 如果我们在整个训练计划中拥有
良好的技术并且取得良好的结果，那么干预就是好的。 如果我们的技
术不好，结果就无关紧要，因为我们不能说输入是一致的。 如果没有
建立良好的技术，我们就失去了真理的基础。 如果我们在锻炼过程中
没有预定的活动范围、控制力和位置，我们就无法确定什么是好的。
有了一个运动标准，我们就可以知道失控发生在哪里。 技术损失来
自两个方面之一：运动功能差或能力低。 为了优化锻炼效果，我们必
须突破力量、速度和功的阈值限制。达到阈值需要我们拥有硬连线的运
动模式以及维持最佳技术的组织能力。从一个区块到下一个区块的进展
强化了这种运动模式。 渐进性超负荷会增强组织耐受性。如果我们失
去了运动标准，我们就会失去渐进和渐进超负荷的有效性。 从简单到
复杂，再加上适应施加的压力，这就是我们从培训计划中梳理出积极效
果的方式。

该技术背后的关键是我们有意识地、客观地强调某件事。 我们经常
淡化锻炼过程中的感觉。当某人根据锻炼的原理对特定肌肉群感到有针
对性的、有意的压力时，我们就确保该技术是足够的。 或者，如果我
们感觉在锻炼过程中组织没有成为目标，默认情况下我们可以说该技术
不够充分。我们使用的运动标准可以准确预测我们想要施加压力的组织
。执行创造了一个肌肉要承受压力的目标。 这是创造压力平衡以及随
后的适应的基础。

规则 3：组织耐受性
在运动模式中培养组织耐受性。

A couple of key aspects are behind increasing tissue tolerance. One is the
direct correlation between increasing cross-sectional area (CSA; muscle
mass) and force output (Maughan et al., 1983). The other is that we can
institute progressive overload, progression, and critical drop-off with more
precision.
Regardless of the goal, increasing force is important to the overall
outcome. Force is not exclusively the result of external load. Increasing
external load based on technical proficiency is related to force. Altering
mechanical advantage, leverage, and center of mass allows for external load
but does not increase force in more organic game or gamelike environments.
Increasing external load within technical limits is correlated with force. When
we intentionally stress a muscle group where the athlete can feel the stress
directly, we have increased odds of improving CSA and subsequently
increasing force. The key is being intentional with stress.
The tissue connects to adaptation. The ability to maintain technique at the
threshold ultimately determines the amount of progressive overload, the rate
of progression, and the timing of critical drop-off. Altering the center of mass
during an exercise at the threshold of tissue tolerance will lead to changes in
mechanical advantage during the exercise, which can increase the momentum
of that movement. This altered pattern will lead to less direct stress in the
targeted area and a transfer of stress to other areas. A clear indicator of this is
delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in a completely unrelated area from
the target of the exercise and the proposed technique. DOMS is decreased
with exposure, so the more we train with a manipulated technique, the less
DOMS we have, which is a good indicator of isolated stress. We need to be
conscious of where we should feel something when we perform a certain
exercise.
Allocating stress equally between antagonist muscle groups is essentially
what structural balance is. The entire premise of structural balance is the
equal distribution of stress from training. If we have movement patterns that
stress targeted areas, this becomes easier to manage. If we have movement
patterns that are less predictable in a particular area, this becomes harder to
manage. For instance, if we have an equal distribution of pushing versus

提高组织耐受性背后有几个关键方面。 一是增加的横截面积（CSA；
肌肉质量）与力输出之间的直接相关性（Maughan 等，1983）。 另一
个是我们可以更精确地制定渐进式超负荷、进展和临界下降。
无论目标如何，增加力量对于整体结果都很重要。 力不仅仅是外部
载荷的结果。 根据技术熟练程度增加外部负载与力量有关。 改变机械
优势、杠杆和质心允许外部负载，但不会增加更有机的游戏或类似游戏
的环境中的力。在技术限制内增加外部负载与力相关。当我们有意地对
运动员可以直接感受到压力的肌肉群施加压力时，我们改善 CSA 并随
后增加力量的可能性就会增加。关键是有意识地应对压力。

该组织与适应有关。将技术维持在阈值的能力最终决定了渐进性超负
荷的量、进展的速度以及临界下降的时间。在运动过程中在组织耐受阈
值下改变质心将导致运动过程中机械优势的变化，这可以增加该运动的
动量。 这种改变的模式将导致目标区域的直接压力减少，并将压力转
移到其他区域。一个明显的指标是与锻炼目标和所提出的技术完全无关
的区域出现延迟性肌肉酸痛（DOMS）。 DOMS 会随着暴露程度的增
加而降低，因此我们使用操控技术进行的训练越多，我们的 DOMS 就
越少，这是孤立压力的一个很好的指标。 当我们进行某种练习时，我
们需要意识到我们应该在哪里感受到某种东西。

在拮抗肌群之间均匀分配压力本质上就是结构平衡。 结构平衡的整
个前提是训练压力的平均分配。如果我们有强调目标区域的运动模式，
这就会变得更容易管理。 如果我们在特定区域的运动模式难以预测，
那么管理就会变得更加困难。 例如，如果我们平均分配推动与

pulling exercises and our pushing exercises stress their antagonist muscle
group from poor technical standards, are we really moving nearer to
structural balance?

Rule 4: Balanced Pushing and Pulling Movements
Balance out pushing and pulling movements.
One area that Charles Poliquin established is a structural balance assessment
looking specifically at strength ratios. The central theme was built upon
injury prevention with the predictor lifts: biacromial bench press and back
squat. Strength ratios are centered on taking percentages from predictor lifts
to determine adequate loads for remedial exercises (Poliquin, 2013). For
example, the ratio of neutral grip pull-up one rep max should be 100% of
biacromial bench press. If you can do a pull-up with your body weight (200
lb [91 kg]), you should be able to bench press (200 lb [91 kg]). The idea is to
increase focus on exercises that receive less focus and to accentuate exercises
that receive more focus. It frames structural balance as a mechanism to
develop more correlated lifts, and it gives a reference point for someone who
is underdeveloped in certain lifts to develop those lifts.
The person who can squat and bench a lot but cannot do a pull-up or a
Nordic will have problems. It is a problem because they have altered the
length–tension relationships from front to back. They are at increased risk of
injury from the imbalance between antagonist muscle groups. The risk stems
from the breakdown of tissues around the joint due to uneven forces placed
on it. Overuse injuries, such as tendinopathies (tendonitis), are a clear
indication that poorly aligned stresses are placed on the connective tissue
around a joint. One key issue we face in training large groups is time. We can
save a significant amount of time by not doing extensive soft tissue work,
flexibility, mobility, corrective exercise, and remedial exercise by simply
balancing your pushing and pulling with a direct focus on technique.
Poliquin (2013) emphasizes this with his structural balance assessment.
Taking someone who is imbalanced means a focused effort on remedial

拉练习和我们的推练习由于技术标准不佳而对拮抗肌群施加压力，我们
真的更接近结构平衡吗？

规则 4：平衡的推拉动作
平衡推和拉的动作。
查尔斯·波利昆 (Charles Poliquin) 建立的一个领域是结构平衡评估，专门
关注强度比。 中心主题是建立在预测举重预防伤害的基础上的：双峰
卧推和后深蹲。 力量比的重点是从预测举重中获取百分比，以确定补
救练习的足够负荷（Poliquin，2013）。 例如，中立握引体向上一次最
大次数的比率应为双肩卧推的 100%。 如果您可以用自己的体重（200
磅 [91 公斤]）进行引体向上，那么您应该能够进行卧推（200 磅 [91 公
斤]）。这个想法是增加对注意力较少的练习的关注，并强调注意力较
多的练习。 它将结构平衡视为一种开发更多相关提升的机制，并为在
某些提升方面欠发达的人发展这些提升提供了参考点。

能做很多深蹲和卧推但不能做引体向上或北欧式的人就会有问题。
这是一个问题，因为它们从前到后改变了长度与张力的关系。他们因拮
抗肌群之间的不平衡而受伤的风险增加。这种风险源于关节周围的组织
由于施加在关节上的力不均匀而破裂。 过度使用损伤，例如肌腱病（
肌腱炎），清楚地表明关节周围的结缔组织受到了不对齐的压力。我们
在培训大型团体时面临的一个关键问题是时间。通过简单地平衡推拉和
直接关注技术，我们可以节省大量时间，无需进行大量的软组织训练、
灵活性、活动性、矫正运动和补救运动。

Poliquin（2013）通过他的结构平衡评估强调了这一点。接受不平衡
的人意味着集中精力进行补救

exercises. The result is a more conscious effort to increase external rotators
(supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and teres minor) and shoulder retractors
(middle and lower trapezius and rhomboids) to help restore balance within
the shoulder. He also advocates for training with dumbbells over barbells—
this creates more control in the frontal and transverse planes of motion, which
recruits more of the shoulder stabilizers. The same could be said for
developing frontal plane stabilizers of the knee, such as the vastus medialis
obliquus, or flexors of the knee, such as the hamstrings, to protect the knee
joint. Poliquin’s genius was to tap into a coach’s psyche of developing
predictor lifts through structurally balanced training. In Poliquin’s framework
for structural balance, he understood that coaches innately associate the
development of squatting and benching with overall development. Instead of
fighting for people to focus on nonpredictor lifts, he was able to meet them
where they were to accomplish structural balance.
Poliquin’s (2013) approach was intended to give a frame of reference for
what a trainee needs to focus on with future training. If there is a
prioritization of one exercise over another, specifically between pushing and
pulling, a structural imbalance will result. Programming inevitably is
funneled into something we can easily quantify; hence, exercises like
squatting and benching are low-hanging fruit. We can easily encourage
structural balance at the front by making it the foundation of our program. Or
we can find solutions for people who do not readily understand the
consequences of structural imbalance; this is the central aspect of Poliquin’s
approach.
Poliquin (2013) encourages using balanced pushing and pulling in
programming as well as variation to develop the joint and tissues around the
joint completely. The standard program of squat and bench leaves a lot on the
table for developing the motor pattern and supporting musculature and
connective tissue around the joint. This limits performance from the predictor
lift because it has a point of diminishing returns. Poliquin built his concept of
structural balance through strength ratios. Strength ratios are a quality control
mechanism to ensure you are hitting a balanced approach to lifting (figure
10.3).
Poliquin’s (2013) approach to programming for structural balance uses

练习。 其结果是更有意识地增加外旋肌（冈上肌、冈下肌和小圆肌）
和肩部牵拉器（中、下斜方肌和菱形肌），以帮助恢复肩部内部的平衡
。 他还主张用哑铃进行训练，而不是用杠铃进行训练——这样可以更
好地控制额部和横向运动平面，从而调动更多的肩部稳定肌。 同样的
道理也适用于发展膝盖的额面稳定肌，例如股内侧斜肌，或膝盖屈肌，
例如腿筋，以保护膝关节。 波利昆的天才在于利用教练的心理，通过
结构平衡的训练来发展预测举重。在波利昆的结构平衡框架中，他明白
教练天生会将深蹲和卧推的发展与整体发展联系起来。他没有努力让人
们专注于不可预测的提升，而是能够在他们需要的地方满足他们，以实
现结构平衡。

Poliquin（2013）的方法旨在为学员在未来的培训中需要关注的内容
提供一个参考框架。 如果一项练习优先于另一项练习，特别是在推和
拉之间，就会导致结构性失衡。 编程不可避免地会涉及到我们可以轻
松量化的东西； 因此，像深蹲和卧推这样的练习是唾手可得的。 通过
将其作为我们计划的基础，我们可以轻松地鼓励前端的结构平衡。或者
，我们可以为那些不太了解结构性失衡后果的人们找到解决方案； 这
是 Poliquin 方法的核心。

Poliquin (2013) 鼓励在编程中使用平衡的推和拉以及变化来完全发育
关节和关节周围的组织。深蹲和卧推的标准计划为发展运动模式以及支
撑关节周围的肌肉组织和结缔组织留下了很多空间。这限制了预测器提
升的性能，因为它有一个收益递减点。波利昆通过强度比建立了结构平
衡的概念。力量比是一种质量控制机制，可确保您采用平衡的举重方法
（图 10.3）。

Poliquin (2013) 的结构平衡用途编程方法

antagonist pairings. Structural balance occurs within the practical aspect of
training. The pitch was centered on the training economy. It takes a certain
amount of time to recover from higher-threshold exercises like squats or
bench presses. The recovery time needed for these exercises significantly
reduces the number of exercises and total density of sets you can do in a
session. You can increase density by using that time to pair them with an
antagonist exercise, like a leg curl or deadlift with a squat and pull-up or row
with a bench press instead of resting. The time spent doing nothing is now
spent performing an antagonist exercise. We get more done in the same
period while developing tissues on both sides of the joint completely. At the
same time, we ensure structural balance within training by pairing exercises
targeting the antagonist muscle group. Keeping track of things more readily
is another reason we need to consider the muscles associated with the
exercise.

需要考虑与锻炼相关的肌肉的另一个原因。

强度比。

Rule 5: Antagonist Pairings
Use antagonist pairings to ensure structural
balance.
The framework of training around the economy of time ensures structural
balance within a training session. It became an organic fail-safe to fight the
human psyche’s preference for one exercise over another. The psychological
component of programming for structural balance ensures that we maintain
optimal length–tension relationships around joints and antagonist muscle
groups. We will discuss this further later, but this approach affects the
component of the reflex arc from an overactive Golgi tendon organ and
muscle spindle, leading to reciprocal inhibition. The altered length–tension
relationship with antagonist muscle groups limits overall output.
Altered length–tension relationships manifest into altered stress–strain
relationships. Meaning we do not have the strain capacity to handle stress.
Imagine a cyclist who only bikes and does overspeed running. Their
chronically trained anterior musculature would cause an altered length–
tension relationship in their posterior musculature. This antagonist imbalance
would increase risk during other activities, like sprinting, due to the increased
stress. It would also lead to a decrease in running performance and,
potentially, their biking performance as well. Their constant redundant
activities create an imbalance of the musculature to a degree that increases
the risk to the antagonist musculature. The same could be true with
imbalanced exercise selection; we can alter length–tension relationships,
which negatively affect stress–strain relationships.

Antagonist Pairings
The easiest way to have structural balance is to superset
pushing and pulling exercises. This falls into microcycle design.
A total body program will have an upper push-based exercise
and a lower pull-based exercise. An upper-lower program will

规则 5：拮抗剂配对
使用拮抗配对来确保结构平衡。

围绕时间节约的培训框架确保培训课程内的结构平衡。 它成为一种有
机的自动防故障装置，可以对抗人类心理对一种运动的偏好。结构平衡
规划的心理部分确保我们在关节和拮抗肌群周围保持最佳的长度-张力
关系。 我们稍后将进一步讨论这一点，但这种方法会影响来自过度活
跃的高尔基腱器官和肌梭的反射弧成分，从而导致相互抑制。 与拮抗
肌群的长度-张力关系的改变限制了总体输出。

长度-张力关系的改变表现为应力-应变关系的改变。 这意味着我们
没有应对压力的应变能力。想象一下，一个骑自行车的人只骑自行车并
且超速跑步。 他们长期训练的前部肌肉组织会导致后部肌肉组织的长
度-张力关系发生改变。由于压力增加，这种拮抗剂的不平衡会增加其
他活动（如短跑）的风险。 它还会导致跑步成绩下降，甚至可能导致
骑行成绩下降。 他们持续的冗余活动造成肌肉组织的不平衡，从而增
加了拮抗肌肉组织的风险。 对于不平衡的运动选择也可能出现同样的
情况。 我们可以改变长度-张力关系，这会对应力-应变关系产生负面影
响。

拮抗剂配对
保持结构平衡的最简单方法是加强推和拉练习。 这属于微循环设
计。全身计划将包括上部推式练习和下部拉式练习。 上下程序将

have a training day with an upper push with an upper pull and
training day with a lower push with a lower pull.
Upper-lower splits can be somewhat polarizing for strength
coaches. The idea of pairing two primary exercises feels
contradictory. Having two primary exercises paired would make
one, potentially both, not primary. Primary represents being top
of the food chain of exercises in both value and correspondence.
Antagonist pairings of two primary exercises dilute the notion of
the most important, at least to a certain extent.
There is no such thing as extra; there is only necessary and
unnecessary.
If it is programmed, it is important. Programming an exercise
is based on the notion that exercise will help to accomplish
something greater than not programming an exercise.
Combining that with all exercises is a means to a greater end.
The exercise is not the point of training; the result we get from
that exercise is the point of training. Having an exercise paired
with another is not designed to diminish the value of that
exercise but to gain greater results from that training session.
Framing exercise organization and order should be based on
risk, not value. All exercises are valuable, but not all exercises
have the same risk. Total body, compound, closed chain
movements, such as Olympic lifts, carry more risk than isolated,
open chain movements. Total body movements do not need to
be paired with anything. Pushing and pulling exercises have
various degrees of potential for external load. Barbell
movements with reduced ROM or altered center of mass have a
higher potential for external load and carry a higher degree of
risk. They should be placed before the exercise with less
potential for external load.
Pushing and pulling are connected to the development of
muscle groups and particular biomechanical functions such as
extension or flexion. Pairing them together makes it easier to
organize over time and organically facilitates structural balance.

训练日进行上推和上拉，训练日进行下推和下拉。
对于力量教练来说，上下劈叉可能会有些两极分化。 将两个主
要练习配对的想法感觉很矛盾。 将两项主要练习配对后，其中一
项（甚至可能两项）都不再是主要练习。 Primary 代表在价值和
对应性方面处于锻炼食物链的顶端。两个主要练习的对抗配对至
少在一定程度上淡化了最重要练习的概念。
没有额外的东西； 只有必要和不必要。
如果它是编程的，那么它很重要。 制定练习的基础是这样的观
念：锻炼比不制定练习更有助于完成一些事情。将其与所有练习
相结合是实现更大目标的一种手段。训练的目的不是练习，而是
练习。 我们从练习中得到的结果就是训练的重点。 将一项练习
与另一项练习配对并不是为了降低该练习的价值，而是为了从该
训练课程中获得更好的结果。
制定演习的组织和顺序应基于风险，而不是价值。 所有练习都
是有价值的，但并非所有练习都有相同的风险。 全身、复合、闭
链运动（例如奥林匹克举重）比孤立的开链运动具有更大的风险
。 全身运动不需要与任何东西配对。 推和拉练习对外部负载有
不同程度的潜在影响。 活动范围减小或重心改变的杠铃运动承受
外部负载的可能性更大，风险也更高。 应将它们放置在练习之前
，以减少外部负载的可能性。

推和拉与肌肉群的发展和特定的生物力学功能（例如伸展或屈
曲）有关。 将它们配对在一起可以更轻松地随着时间的推移进行
组织，并有机地促进结构平衡。

Prioritize risk over subjective value when organizing what goes
first.
The reflex system is hypersensitive to stress when it is already at length,
which is reflected by the muscle spindle sending a premature response and
causing muscle contraction. Tension follows this contraction, causing the
Golgi tendon organ to activate and stop the agonist muscle group from
contracting (figure 10.4). This concept is known as reciprocal inhibition. It
decreases output, hence a decreased performance outcome. We can limit the
impact of reciprocal inhibition by promoting balanced stress and CSA of the
tissues on both sides of a joint.

FIGURE 10.4 Stretch versus tension.
The simple answer to this is to program based on antagonist pairings.
Antagonist pairings allow for continuity of training stress for both sides of
the joint. This creates a favorable ratio of CSA and force to optimize length–

在组织优先事项时，应将风险置于主观价值之上。

当压力已经达到极限时，反射系统对压力非常敏感，这通过肌梭发出
过早反应并导致肌肉收缩来反映。 这种收缩后会产生张力，导致高尔
基腱器官激活并阻止主动肌群收缩（图 10.4）。 这个概念被称为
reciprocal inhibition。 它会降低输出，从而降低性能结果。 我们可以
通过促进关节两侧组织的平衡压力和 CSA 来限制相互抑制的影响。

图 10.4 拉伸与张力。
对此的简单答案是根据拮抗配对进行编程。拮抗剂配对可以使关节两
侧的训练压力保持连续性。这创造了 CSA 和力的有利比率来优化长度

tension relationships (see figure 3.6 on page 49). The ratio of one exercise to
its antagonist pairing matters a great deal in overall function and safety. This
becomes increasingly important when we push things to the threshold
redundantly.

Rule 6: Prioritizing Pushing and Pulling Exercises
Place equal prioritization on both pushing and
pulling exercises.
On one end of the spectrum is Poliquin’s (2013) approach of pairing
antagonist muscle groups. On the other end, we can rotate exercises within a
program that ensures we have structural balance, such as the classic 5 by 5 (5
sets of 5 reps) program. Bill Starr (1999) wrote about prioritizing exercise
order in program design (figure 10.5). He broke down a microcycle into
heavy, moderate, and light versions of an exercise on each day. In this way,
the program equally prioritizes movement patterns and evenly distributes
stress based on the day within the microcycle. The program was not based on
antagonist pairings, as was Poliquin’s, but established that we need to stress
each movement pattern uniformly.
What we can learn from this is that certain movement patterns will affect
the movement pattern and the corresponding tissues differently. Depending
on the external load, in theory, we can place more or less load on the tissues
associated with that movement pattern. Strategy aside, this is why it is so
important to have the foundational rules of ROM, control, and technical
proficiency in place. This could easily lead to an altered center of mass and
shifts in mechanical advantage and momentum. The heavy, or the version of
an exercise with the greatest external load potential, could very likely become
an exercise that comes nowhere near stressing targeted tissues. Regardless of
the potential for the exercise to externally load, we need to have rules for
movement patterns to ensure we are optimizing training for structural
balance.

张力关系（参见第 49 页图 3.6）。一项运动与其拮抗运动配对的比例对
于整体功能和安全性至关重要。当我们多余地将事情推向门槛时，这一
点变得越来越重要。

规则 6：优先考虑推拉练习
对推和拉练习给予同等的重视。

一方面是 Poliquin (2013) 的拮抗肌群配对方法。另一方面，我们可以在
一个计划内轮换练习，以确保结构平衡，例如经典的 5 x 5（5 组，每组
5 次）计划。 Bill Starr (1999) 写过关于程序设计中练习顺序优先级的文
章（图 10.5）。 他把每天的一个微循环分解为大强度、中强度和轻强
度的锻炼。 通过这种方式，该程序会平等地优先考虑运动模式，并根
据微周期内的日期均匀分配压力。该计划并不像 Poliquin 那样基于对抗
配对，而是确定我们需要统一强调每种运动模式。

我们从中可以了解到的是，某些运动模式会对运动模式和相应的组织
产生不同的影响。 理论上，根据外部负荷，我们可以对与该运动模式
相关的组织施加或多或少的负荷。 抛开策略不谈，这就是为什么制定
ROM、控制和技术熟练程度的基本规则如此重要。 这很容易导致质心
改变以及机械优势和动量的变化。 heavy，或者具有最大外部负荷潜力
的运动版本，很可能会成为一种远未给目标组织带来压力的运动。无论
练习外部负荷的可能性如何，我们都需要制定运动模式规则，以确保我
们优化结构平衡训练。

FIGURE 10.5 Starr’s (1999) 5 x 5.
Boyle (2010) was one of the most important coaches in preaching the
benefits of having equal time allocated toward pushing and pulling exercises,
taking a step further by making categories of movement. Boyle, more so than
anyone in S&C, is the person we should model group-based training off
because that was his primary focus.

Capacity to External Load
Not all exercises are equal in propensity to external load. Basic
biomechanics gives us clues as to why a back squat is more
easily loaded than a front squat based on leverage and
mechanical advantage. Basic physiology gives us clues as to
why a bench is easier to load than an overhead press based on
muscle mass, muscle architecture, and muscle fiber type.
If an exercise can tolerate greater loads, does that make it
better? You can probably guess that my answer is no. But that
does not seem to be the consensus in the S&C community.
Regarding biomechanical rules and structural balance rules,
higher capacity to external load is fool’s gold, and we need to dig
up other reasons for one exercise over another.
Aside from body composition, progressive overload is the
easiest way to determine relative adaptation. Training age,
experience with a movement, environment, and the chosen
exercise will have a direct impact on the amount and rate at
which we can progressively overload. If someone is very
experienced with a particular exercise, it is hard to make
substantial changes, which makes it harder to determine
effectiveness.
This will be more obvious when you adopt a structurally
balanced approach to training. You will find that the antagonist
exercise can be progressively overloaded at a much different
rate and amount. If we can use the progressive overload rate
and amount as a proxy for programming effectiveness, it justifies
the logic of less loadable exercises.
Anyone who has worked with high-level football has
encountered a ready-made athlete. They squat and bench at
elite levels before even starting with you as their strength coach.

将分配给与所使用的运动类别相关的特定肌肉群。

外部负载能力
并非所有练习对外部负荷的倾向都相同。 基础生物力学为我们提
供了线索，解释为什么基于杠杆和机械优势，后深蹲比前深蹲更
容易负重。 基础生理学为我们提供了线索，根据肌肉质量、肌肉
结构和肌纤维类型，解释为什么卧推凳比过头推举更容易负重。
如果一项运动可以承受更大的负荷，它会变得更好吗？ 你可能
猜到我的答案是否定的。 但这似乎并不是 S&C 社区的共识。关
于生物力学规则和结构平衡规则，更高的外部负载能力是愚人金
，我们需要挖掘一种运动优于另一种运动的其他原因。
除了身体成分之外，渐进性超负荷是确定相对适应的最简单方
法。 训练年龄、运动经验、环境和选择的运动将直接影响我们逐
渐超负荷的数量和速度。 如果某人对某项练习非常有经验，就很
难做出实质性的改变，这使得确定有效性变得更加困难。

当您采用结构平衡的培训方法时，这一点会更加明显。 您会发
现拮抗运动可以以截然不同的速度和量逐渐超负荷。 如果我们可
以使用渐进超载率和数量作为编程有效性的代理，那么它就证明
了可加载练习较少的逻辑是合理的。
任何接触过高水平足球的人都遇到过现成的运动员。 在你开始
担任他们的力量教练之前，他们就已经达到了精英水平的深蹲和
卧推水平。

Whether that is innate or built, you have little room for
improvement. Chances are, you have come to the question:
What is strong enough? This question is only predicated on
having reached an apex with exercises and not exploring
untapped versions of that pattern or its antagonist.
The capacity to externally load organically pales in
comparison to the capacity to progressively overload. The
question should not be, what is strong enough? Instead, the
question should be, what can I make stronger? If we do an
inventory of an exercise and find that several have significant
untapped potential, we should go in that direction.
The framework is less about what amount an athlete can do
with one particular exercise and more about how much we can
affect an athlete’s potential by improving an exercise. It starts
with how we do something. That is followed by how much, how
fast, or how long we can do that thing. Your impact as an S&C
coach is predicated on how much you were able to affect
potential, not how much the athlete could already do.
This approach differs from Poliquin’s (2013) approach of prioritizing
structural balance to develop a primary movement pattern. This approach
prioritizes all patterns as the primary pattern. The idea is that if you are going
to do it, you might as well be as good as possible at it. A critical aspect of this
approach is to detach from the notion that one exercise is superior to another.
Dynamic correspondence is based on what will transfer to sports
performance; this is not exclusive to a particular list of exercises
(Verkhoshansky, 2011). Some exercises are more likely to correlate with a
specific sport or position. Those exercises are specific physical preparation,
which, ironically, is the product of the available general physical preparation
capacity. This correlation does not have to come at the expense of sacrificing
structural balance and length–tension relationships.

Rule 8: Movement Categories

无论是先天的还是后天的，你都没有什么改进的空间。 您很可能
会问这样一个问题：什么是足够强大的？ 这个问题只是基于通过
练习达到了顶点，而不是探索该模式或其对手的未开发版本。
与逐渐过载的能力相比，外部有机负载的能力显得苍白无力。
问题不应该是，什么足够强？ 相反，问题应该是，我能让什么变
得更强？ 如果我们对一项活动进行盘点，发现其中有一项活动具
有巨大的未开发潜力，那么我们应该朝这个方向前进。
该框架不是关于运动员在一项特定练习中可以做多少事情，而
是更多地关于我们可以通过改进一项练习来多大程度地影响运动
员的潜力。 它始于我们如何做某事。 接下来是我们能做多少、
多快或多长时间。 作为一名体能教练，你的影响力取决于你能够
在多大程度上影响潜力，而不是运动员已经可以做到多少。

这种方法不同于 Poliquin (2013) 优先考虑结构平衡以开发主要运动模
式的方法。 此方法将所有模式优先考虑为主要模式。这个想法是，如
果你要做这件事，你最好尽可能做好它。这种方法的一个关键方面是摆
脱一种练习优于另一种练习的观念。动态对应取决于将转化为运动表现
的内容； 这并不是特定练习列表所独有的（Verkhoshansky，2011）。
有些练习更有可能与特定的运动或位置相关。 这些练习是特定的身体
准备，讽刺的是，这是现有的一般身体准备能力的产物。这种相关性不
一定要以牺牲结构平衡和长度-张力关系为代价。

规则 8：动作类别

Use movement categories to ensure equal focus
on all movement patterns.
Boyle’s (2010) approach to movement categories occurs with a program split
(figure 10.6). Essentially, we break down programs into total body training
splits, pairing upper and lower body antagonist exercises, such as lower body
push with upper body pull exercises or lower body pull exercises with upper
body push exercises. The focus will shift from bilateral to unilateral, hip
dominant to knee dominant, and vertical to horizontal movement categories
based on the day.

FIGURE 10.6 Boyle’s (2010) 3 day.
Boyle’s (2010) approach focuses on prioritizing the balance of patterns
over performing any exercise. We can still layer in variations that allow for
higher external loads, but they will be prioritized equally between antagonist
muscle groups. The argument is that we will not reach as high a level without

使用运动类别来确保对所有运动模式的同等关注。

Boyle (2010) 的运动类别方法是通过程序分割来实现的（图 10.6）。 本
质上，我们将训练计划分解为全身训练，将上半身和下半身对抗性练习
配对，例如下半身推和上半身拉练习或下半身拉练习和上半身推练习。
根据当天的情况，重点将从双侧转向单侧，从髋部主导转向膝部主导，
从垂直运动类别转向水平运动类别。

图 10.6 Boyle (2010) 的 3 天。
Boyle（2010）的方法侧重于优先考虑模式的平衡而不是进行任何练
习。 我们仍然可以分层变化，以允许更高的外部负荷，但它们将在拮
抗肌群之间同等优先。争论的焦点是，如果没有

prioritizing one exercise, which is the point: to create programs that safeguard
against the logic that one exercise is superior to another. All exercises are a
means to an end. Some may be more correlated, but all matter. We should
never develop one exercise at the expense of structural balance.
Notably, we need to demonstrate the ability to move in multiple planes of
motion. Not just the sagittal, which dominates strength training. Most
correlated exercises fall within the sagittal plane, which is a clue to break into
the frontal and transverse planes more often. There are a couple of ways we
need to address this. One direct method is using more frontal and transverse
movement in training. Such as lateral or rotational versions of movement
patterns that we hit routinely. For instance, doing lateral squats over split
squats or cable rotational rows over a barbell row. This is the most logical
and seamlessly included in your already established program to ensure
balance in all planes. The other is using implements such as dumbbells and
kettlebells or positions of split stance or single-leg stance that require more
control in both frontal and transverse planes. This is where the capacity to
externally load gets amplified. We are less capable of using external loads
when we are in a split stance or single-leg stance or when we are using
asymmetric loading with kettlebells or dumbbells compared to a barbell. Less
capacity for external load creates more opportunities for progressive
overload. Chances are that multiplanar versions are untapped and potentially
more beneficial for the chaotic environments we see in the team setting.

Rule 9: Acyclic Sport Exercises
Acyclical sports need more exercise variety to
prepare for open-unpredictable environments.
We are simultaneously developing correlated movement patterns while
preparing for open, unpredictable environments. With acyclic sports, such as
football or basketball, there are an infinite number of movement possibilities
during practices or games. We need a program that can accommodate those
possibilities with as much variance as we can reasonably do. We can go

优先考虑一项练习，这就是要点：创建计划来防止一种练习优于另一种
练习的逻辑。 所有练习都是达到目的的手段。 有些可能更相关，但都
很重要。 我们决不应该以牺牲结构平衡为代价来开展一项工作。
值得注意的是，我们需要证明在多个运动平面上移动的能力。 不仅
仅是矢状面，它在力量训练中占主导地位。 大多数相关练习都位于矢
状面内，这是更频繁地进入额状面和横状面的线索。 我们需要通过几
种方法来解决这个问题。 一种直接的方法是在训练中使用更多的正面
和横向运动。 例如我们经常使用的横向或旋转运动模式。 例如，在分
腿深蹲上进行侧向深蹲，或者在杠铃划船上进行绳索旋转划船。 这是
最符合逻辑且无缝地包含在您已建立的计划中，以确保所有平面的平衡
。 另一种是使用哑铃和壶铃等工具，或者分叉站姿或单腿站姿，这些
都需要在正面和横向平面上有更多的控制。 这是外部负载能力被放大
的地方。 当我们处于分腿姿势或单腿姿势时，或者当我们使用壶铃或
哑铃与杠铃相比使用不对称负载时，我们使用外部负载的能力较差。外
部负载容量减少会产生更多渐进式过载的机会。多平面版本很可能尚未
开发，并且可能对我们在团队环境中看到的混乱环境更有利。

规则 9：非循环运动练习
非周期性运动需要更多的运动种类来为开放的不可预测
的环境做好准备。
我们同时开发相关的运动模式，同时为开放、不可预测的环境做好准备
。对于非循环运动，例如足球或篮球，在练习或比赛期间存在无限多种
运动可能性。 我们需要一个能够在合理范围内尽可能多地适应这些可
能性的程序。 我们可以走了

straight to chaos with randomized approaches to program design, but this
would abandon principles (progression, progressive overload). We can
sustain principles by using all planes of motion within all vectors with
exercise selection. We can keep our macrocycle and mesocycle structure and
simply alter the direction and orientation of an exercise we are already using.
We need to appreciate that an exclusive focus on sagittal plane, vertically and
horizontally based exercises will not adequately prepare team sport athletes
for their unpredictable environment. Their worlds are not that constrained.
This could come in the form of taking our lower body unilateral push in all
three planes of motion, such as a lateral or posterior lateral squat. It could be
loading our lower, hip dominant pull in the horizontal plane, such as a cable
single-leg Romanian deadlift. It could mean using an unstable load, such as a
sandbag or water bag, with any of the movement categories. The idea is that
we are stressing the contractile and noncontractile tissues associated with the
movement pattern in all planes and vectors to prepare for unpredictable
environments. We still progress from simple to complicated, and we still
progressively overload based on adaptation rates. The only difference is that
we are taking an approach that develops more corresponding patterns with a
higher capacity to improve.

Rule 10: Cyclic Sport Exercises
Cyclical sports need exercise variety to prevent
overuse.
With cyclic sports, like sprinting or cycling, we lean into highly correlated
exercises. Dynamic correspondence for cyclic-based motions is peaking with
the most correlated activities possible (Verkhoshansky, 2011). There is less
unpredictability in cyclic sports; however, there is a higher risk of overuse.
Overloading patterns to accentuate a skill or biomotor function has a purpose,
but it could come at a cost. We need to introduce variance in the form of
loading, stance, or certain parameters, such as sequence or order. Variance, in
this case, is a means to prevent negative outcomes from excessively

使用随机方法进行程序设计会直接陷入混乱，但这会放弃原则（渐进、
渐进超载）。 我们可以通过使用所有向量内的所有运动平面和练习选
择来维持原则。我们可以保持我们的大循环和中循环结构，并简单地改
变我们已经使用的练习的方向和方向。我们需要认识到，仅仅关注矢状
面、垂直和水平的练习并不能让团队运动运动员为不可预测的环境做好
充分的准备。他们的世界并没有那么受限。
这可以采取在所有三个运动平面上单侧推动下半身的形式，例如侧蹲
或后侧蹲。它可能会在水平面上加载我们下部、臀部主导的拉力，例如
绳索单腿罗马尼亚硬拉。这可能意味着在任何运动类别中使用不稳定的
负载，例如沙袋或水袋。我们的想法是，我们强调与所有平面和向量中
的运动模式相关的收缩和非收缩组织，为不可预测的环境做好准备。
我们仍然从简单到复杂，并且我们仍然根据适应率逐渐超载。唯一的区
别是，我们采取的方法是开发更多相应的模式，并具有更高的改进能力
。

规则 10：循环运动练习
周期性运动需要运动多样化，以防止过度使用。

对于短跑或骑自行车等循环运动，我们倾向于进行高度相关的运动。基
于循环的运动的动态对应随着尽可能相关的活动而达到顶峰（Verkhosh
ansky，2011）。 循环运动的不可预测性较少； 然而，过度使用的风
险较高。强调技能或生物运动功能的超负荷模式是有目的的，但可能会
付出代价。 我们需要以负载、姿态或某些参数（例如序列或顺序）的
形式引入方差。在这种情况下，方差是防止过度使用产生负面结果的一
种手段

overloading a limited number of movement patterns.
With cyclic sport exercise, variance can come in the form of asymmetrical
loading. Boyle (2010) coined the term bilateral deficit, which means the sum
of unilateral exercise strength on each leg is greater than the bilateral sum.
For example, if we take the sum of a barbell split squat load on each leg, that
would be greater than the weight used during a bilateral squat. We will more
than likely use bilateral exercises to peak with cyclic sports. The biomotor
abilities we develop from that focus should not have to come at the expense
of structural balance. Unilateral loading with split stance or single-leg
variations and single-arm or unilaterally loaded bilateral exercises (dumbbells
or kettlebells) can train the motion in all three planes by resisting motion in
the frontal or transverse planes. The synergistic and stabilizing muscles
associated with the movement pattern are more stressed due to the demands
of the exercise. It is not uncommon for a focus on variations of exercises to
lead to direct improvement with the more traditionally considered correlated
exercises.
Essentially, this chapter breaks down to training through a full ROM,
demonstrating control at that ROM, having an equal distribution of pushing
and pulling exercises, and considering all planes of motion and vectors.
Remember, rules are not true but need to be considered. There are plenty of
examples of programs or coaches that do not follow these rules and do not
incur injuries. The fundamental reason behind rules is whether these
examples would still be true if we took our sample to larger numbers. Our
regression to the mean would be, what if we did not have rules based on
hundreds of athletes training simultaneously? Rules ensure our regression to
the mean is favorable for preventing any issues with biomechanics during
redundant activities pushed to the threshold with large groups of people
training simultaneously.

Take Home
With structural balance, we need to have rules to hold us to a standard of
movement that we know will equate to high performance and reduction of
unnecessary injury. Rules around how we move, what we move, and when
we move are the foundation to ensuring we are addressing the largest group

使有限数量的运动模式超载。
在循环运动中，变化可能会以不对称负荷的形式出现。 Boyle（2010
）创造了术语bilateral deficit，即每条腿的单侧运动强度之和大于双侧运
动强度之和。例如，如果我们计算每条腿的杠铃分腿深蹲负荷的总和，
那么这将大于双边深蹲期间使用的重量。我们很可能会使用双边练习来
达到循环运动的顶峰。 我们从这一重点中发展的生物运动能力不应以
牺牲结构平衡为代价。 分腿站立或单腿变化的单侧负荷以及单臂或单
侧负荷双边练习（哑铃或壶铃）可以通过抵抗额状或横向平面中的运动
来训练所有三个平面中的运动。 由于运动的要求，与运动模式相关的
协同和稳定肌肉受到更大的压力。 关注练习的变化导致传统上认为的
相关练习的直接改进并不罕见。

本质上，本章分解为通过完整的 ROM 进行训练，展示对该 ROM 的
控制，均匀分布推和拉练习，并考虑所有运动平面和矢量。请记住，规
则并不真实，但需要考虑。 有很多不遵守这些规则并且没有造成伤害
的项目或教练的例子。 规则背后的根本原因是，如果我们将样本扩大
到更大的数字，这些例子是否仍然正确。 我们的均值回归是，如果我
们没有基于数百名运动员同时训练的规则怎么办？ 规则确保我们对均
值的回归有利于防止在大量人员同时训练的冗余活动中出现任何生物力
学问题。

带回家
对于结构平衡，我们需要制定规则来保持我们的运动标准，我们知道这
将等同于高性能和减少不必要的伤害。 关于我们如何移动、移动什么
以及何时移动的规则是确保我们面向最大群体的基础

possible. A good versus a bad program comes down to actually adhering to a
standard of principles and strategic rules to hold us accountable.

可能的。一个好的项目与一个坏的项目归结为实际遵守原则标准和战略
规则来让我们承担责任。

11
PHYSIOLOGICAL RULES
The term supercompensation means you are reaching a higher functioning
level than when you started. Selye (1950; creator of the general adaptation
syndrome) and Bannister (1975) (creator of the fitness–fatigue model) both
agreed that stress is not the end goal. The goal, rather, is a higher functioning
level relative to the predetermined objective. Zatsiorsky and colleagues
(2020) describe preparedness as the product of two major components: those
that are fast changing and those that are slow changing.
Fitness, or the targeted outcome, is slow
changing, while fatigue, the means to achieve the
targeted outcome, is fast changing.

Adaptation
There is such a delicate balance to manage here; on the one hand, we want to
achieve as much volume and intensity as possible to fast-track the targeted
outcome, or goal. On the other hand, we want to demonstrate patience
because there could rapidly be a point of diminishing returns through the
accumulation of stress. The biggest challenge to managing stress is not
understanding the relationship between fatigue and fitness but rather the
association that more fatigue is automatically correlated with more fitness

11
生理规则
supercompensation 一词表示您正在达到比开始时更高的功能水平。 Sel
ye（1950；一般适应综合症的创建者）和 Bannister（1975）（健身-疲
劳模型的创建者）都同意压力不是最终目标。相反，目标是相对于预定
目标而言更高的功能水平。 Zatsiorsky 及其同事（2020）将准备工作描
述为两个主要组成部分的产物：快速变化的部分和缓慢变化的部分。

健身（或目标结果）变化缓慢，而疲劳（实现目标结果
的手段）变化快速。

适应
这里需要保持一种微妙的平衡。一方面，我们希望达到尽可能多的数量
和强度，以快速实现目标成果或目标。 另一方面，我们希望表现出耐
心，因为压力的积累可能会很快达到收益递减点。 管理压力的最大挑
战不是理解疲劳和健康之间的关系，而是更多的疲劳与更好的健康自动
相关。

(figure 11.1).
The big question is, how do we find the point of equilibrium to optimize
training? Bannister created the fitness–fatigue model to answer that question
(figure 11.2) (MacDougal et al., 1990). Selye’s (1950) general adaptation
syndrome is the foundation of periodization, and fitness–fatigue is the
foundation of program design. What both models essentially boil down to is
at what point a certain amount of stress is enough to create a positive
adaptation or too much to recover from.

Fitness–Fatigue
If we overprescribe training stress, we will accumulate too much fatigue and
negatively affect adaptation. If we underprescribe, which is not the same as a
minimal effective dose, we will not create enough fatigue to positively affect
adaptation. There is a concept in Eastern medicine termed duality. All forces
acting on a system have a synchronous and balancing relationship referred to
as yin and yang. Balance between these forces, which can be referred to as
distress and eustress, is paramount to the system’s function. As strength
coaches working with athletes, our ultimate goal is fitness adaptation, and we
use fatigue to achieve a positive outcome.

（图 11.1）。
最大的问题是，我们如何找到优化训练的平衡点？ Bannister 创建了
健身-疲劳模型来回答这个问题（图 11.2）（MacDougal 等，1990）。
Selye（1950）的一般适应综合症是周期化的基础，健身-疲劳是计划设
计的基础。 这两种模型本质上都归结为什么时候一定量的压力足以产
生积极的适应，或者太大而无法恢复。

健身-疲劳
如果我们过度规定训练压力，我们就会积累过多的疲劳并对适应产生负
面影响。如果我们处方不足（这与最小有效剂量不同），我们就不会产
生足够的疲劳来对适应产生积极影响。东方医学中有一个概念叫做
duality。作用在系统上的所有力都具有同步和平衡关系，称为yin和yang
。 这些力（可称为 distress 和 eustress）之间的平衡对于系统的功能至
关重要。 作为与运动员一起工作的力量教练，我们的最终目标是体能
适应，我们利用疲劳来取得积极的成果。

Long-Term Planning
Periodization, or long-term planning, is about taking a macro view of stress
to achieve positive adaptation going into a certain period, such as in a season
or competition. Program design, or organization of training parameters and
variables, involves taking a more logistic approach to achieve positive
adaptation going into that same period. One is not better than the other; we
just need to be able to wear multiple hats when we approach working in
group settings. We need to have the ability to plan long term to give us a road
map. We understand that adaptation is complex and never goes according to
the script. However, our ability to better respond to setbacks or faster-thanexpected adaptation is enhanced by having a longer-term plan.

图 11.2 健身-疲劳模型。

长期规划
分期或长期规划是指从宏观角度看待压力，以在特定时期（例如赛季或
比赛）实现积极适应。 计划设计或训练参数和变量的组织涉及采取更
逻辑的方法来实现同一时期的积极适应。 一个并不比另一个更好； 当
我们在团队环境中工作时，我们只需要能够身兼数职。我们需要有能力
进行长期规划，为我们提供路线图。我们知道改编是复杂的，永远不会
按照剧本进行。 然而，制定长期计划可以增强我们更好地应对挫折或
比预期更快适应的能力。

FIGURE 11.3 Physiological rules.

Physiological Rules
Rules are our constraints (figure 11.3). We now need a system to select
training variables focused on volume, intensity, and rest. The organization of
variables allows us the predictability to develop a predefined quality. The
effectiveness of these variables toward the outcome is based on foundational
physiology. Do we have the capacity to respond to the training stress?

Rule 1: Understanding Training Stress
Training stress can only be a means to an end,
not the end itself.
We have to address a huge problem with larger groups and physiology, which

图 11.3 生理规则。

生理规则
规则是我们的约束（图 11.3）。 我们现在需要一个系统来选择专注于
训练量、强度和休息的训练变量。变量的组织使我们能够预测性地开发
预定义的质量。 这些变量对结果的有效性基于基础生理学。我们有能
力应对训练压力吗？

规则 1：了解训练压力
训练压力只能是达到目的的手段，而不是目的本身。

我们必须解决更大的群体和生理学的巨大问题，这

is accounting for individual differences and responses to stress. With
biomechanics, it was based on logistics—can we control the variables
associated with movement to better predict the outcome? With physiology,
we have to be able to detach ourselves from the psychological aspect. Social
dynamics, especially in highly competitive athletic environments, breed a
temperament that is hard to understand unless you have been in one or have
been working directly with large groups for a long time. To be perfectly
honest, it is this factor that makes this book necessary. When working with
groups, we are vulnerable to overly prescribing stress and garnering too much
fatigue to have more influence on the environment. This could be from a
multitude of reasons, such as overcompensation or pressure from superiors.
We are controlling the inputs for potentially hundreds of athletes in a day; it
is impossible to detach entirely from the ego and hierarchical structure of
high-level athletics.
This is why rules are so important. As Mike Tyson famously said,
“Everyone has a plan until you get punched in the mouth.” If we have no
criteria to control the stress we impose on athletes, the group dynamic will
take control and lead to potentially excessive amounts. This is the part that is
so difficult to understand for people who do not work in a team setting. The
group dynamics with highly competitive athletes are incredibly hard to
manage, let alone control. Things can easily get out of a coach’s ability to
manage if left to their own devices. Rules protect us from that. If we do
establish that training stress is only a means to accomplish something else, it
can easily become the focal point of training. Challenging social dynamics
pressure the coach to do more than is necessary and make training harder
than it has to be.

Rule 2: Fitness Over Fatigue
Fitness adaptations are more important than the
feeling of fatigue.
To appreciate the fitness–fatigue model, we need to understand why it exists.

正在考虑个体差异和对压力的反应。 对于生物力学来说，它是基于物
流的——我们可以控制与运动相关的变量来更好地预测结果吗？ 对于
生理学，我们必须能够脱离心理方面。社会动态，尤其是在竞争激烈的
运动环境中，会孕育出一种很难理解的气质，除非你曾在一个团体中或
长期直接与大型团体一起工作。 老实说，正是这个因素使得这本书变
得必要。 当与团队一起工作时，我们很容易承受过度的压力并产生过
多的疲劳，从而无法对环境产生更大的影响。 这可能有多种原因，例
如过度补偿或来自上级的压力。我们每天控制着数百名运动员的输入；
完全脱离高水平体育运动的自我和等级结构是不可能的。

这就是为什么规则如此重要。 正如迈克·泰森（Mike Tyson）的名言
：“每个人都有一个计划，直到你的嘴被打了一拳。” 如果我们没有
标准来控制施加给运动员的压力，群体动力就会控制并导致潜在的过量
压力。对于不在团队环境中工作的人来说，这是很难理解的部分。竞争
激烈的运动员的群体动态非常难以管理，更不用说控制了。 如果让教
练自行其是，事情很容易超出教练的管理能力。 规则可以保护我们免
受这种情况的影响。 如果我们确实确定训练压力只是完成其他任务的
一种手段，那么它很容易成为训练的焦点。 具有挑战性的社会动态迫
使教练做超出必要的事情，并使训练变得比必须的更加困难。

规则 2：健康胜于疲劳
Fitness adaptations are more important than the
feeling of fatigue.
To appreciate the fitness–fatigue model, we need to understand why it exists.

The concept of periodization is built on Hans Selye’s general adaptation
syndrome (GAS). Selye (1950) states, “Anything that causes stress endangers
life unless it is met by adequate adaptive responses; conversely, anything that
endangers life causes stress and adaptive responses.” This statement created a
dynamic that ultimately led to longer-term planning regarding training. The
concept led to training being an intentional stressor placed on a system to
trigger a sequence that manifests into a positive adaptation. The first iteration
was Matveyev’s (Kruger, 2016) classic linear periodization: an inverted
relationship of volume and intensity, with a peak of intensity closer to
competition (see chapter 12).
Fatigue creates a negative response, which is the
point of training!
What GAS and periodization are trying to state is that training is a simple
cause-and-effect dynamic that creates predictable outcomes. However, even
Selye (1950) said, “GAS never occurs in its pure form, but is always
complicated by superimposed specific actions of the eliciting stressors.”
Selye himself knew that nothing works in isolation; everything needs to be
looked at in a larger, integrated sequence of events. This is why we need a
more comprehensive model to leverage to fully appreciate the impact of
stress, such as the fitness–fatigue model.

Rule 3: Frequency Based on Fatigue
Frequency is based on fatigue from training.

More Fatigue Is Not Better
The residual impact of both fitness and fatigue needs to be
managed to garner positive adaptations. The often
misunderstood component is that more fatigue is synonymous

周期化的概念建立在 Hans Selye 的一般适应综合症 (GAS) 之上。 Selye
（1950）指出，“任何导致压力的事情都会危及生命，除非有足够的适
应性反应；相反，任何危及生命的事情都会引起压力和适应性反应。”
这一声明创造了一种动力，最终导致了有关培训的长期规划。 这个概
念导致训练成为一种有意施加在系统上的压力源，以触发一系列表现为
积极适应的序列。第一次迭代是 Matveyev（Kruger，2016）的经典线性
周期：音量和强度的倒置关系，强度峰值更接近竞争（见第 12 章）。

疲劳会产生负面反应，这就是训练的意义！

GAS 和周期化试图说明的是，训练是一种简单的因果动态，可以产
生可预测的结果。 然而，就连 Selye (1950) 也说，“GAS 从来不会以
纯粹的形式出现，而是总是因引发压力源的特定行为的叠加而变得复杂
。”塞利本人知道，没有什么是孤立的。 一切事情都需要从更大、更
完整的事件顺序来看待。 这就是为什么我们需要一个更全面的模型来
充分理解压力的影响，例如健身-疲劳模型。

规则 3：基于疲劳的频率
频率基于训练的疲劳程度。

疲劳并非越多越好
需要管理健身和疲劳的残余影响以获得积极的适应。 经常被误解
的部分是“更疲劳”是同义词

with increased results. What we at least understand from GAS is
the consequence that too much stress relative to what the
system can recover from leads to the exhaustion phase (Selye,
1950). The exhaustion phase is the point where the ratio of
fitness to fatigue drops from a factor of three to a possible factor
of two or even one. Said differently, fatigue accumulates to such
a high level that we do not achieve the fitness adaptations we
desire.
This incomplete recovery from excess fatigue from higher
volumes of higher-threshold activities, along with higher
frequencies, takes away from any intended positive adaptation.
The impact of Hans Selye’s (1950) GAS was immense. Without
GAS, there is no examination of how we can weigh and evaluate
the effects of stress on the body. To say that there needs to be
an evaluation of fitness along with fatigue does not diminish the
value of examining stress on the body. It is important to
understand that a balance and rhythm need to be in place to
consistently reach a targeted outcome. Performance training is
built on the premise that we need to improve to a predetermined
target. Performance training is not about how much fatigue we
accrue.
Zatsiorsky and colleagues (2020) state that there are slow-changing and fastchanging adaptations. Directly following a workout, there are two responses:
“a fitness response (slow) or a fatigue response (fast). So, there are two
different rates that we need to address when estimating the appropriate
stressors to place on an athlete.… For most crude estimations, it is assumed
that for one workout with an average age training load, the duration of the
fitness gain and the fatigue effect differ by a factor of three.” So if a fatigue
response lasts 24 hours after a workout, the residual fitness adaptation should
last 72 hours. This creates a working plan for managing stress within a
microcycle. We can only prescribe a certain number of training sessions
within a microcycle based on what we can recover from.
This also means that we need to appreciate that there is an interval of time

结果增加。我们至少从 GAS 中了解到，相对于系统可以恢复的压
力太大，会导致耗尽阶段（Selye，1950）。 疲惫阶段是指健康与
疲劳的比率从三倍下降到可能的两倍甚至一倍的阶段。换句话说
，疲劳累积到如此高的水平，以至于我们无法达到我们想要的健
身适应。

大量高阈值活动以及更高频率的过度疲劳导致的这种不完全恢
复会消除任何预期的积极适应。 Hans Selye (1950) 的《GAS》的
影响是巨大的。 如果没有 GAS，我们就无法衡量和评估压力对身
体的影响。 说需要对健康状况和疲劳进行评估并不会削弱检查身
体压力的价值。 重要的是要理解，需要保持平衡和节奏才能持续
达到目标结果。 绩效训练的前提是我们需要提高到预定的目标。
表现训练与我们累积了多少疲劳无关。

Zatsiorsky 及其同事（2020）指出，适应有缓慢变化和快速变化之分。
锻炼后，有两种反应：“健身反应（慢）或疲劳反应（快）。因此，在
估计对运动员施加的适当压力源时，我们需要考虑两种不同的速率……
对于大多数粗略估计，假设对于具有平均年龄训练负荷的一项锻炼，健
身增益和疲劳效应的持续时间相差三倍。” 因此，如果疲劳反应在锻
炼后持续 24 小时，则剩余的健身适应应持续 72 小时。 这创建了一个
在微周期内管理压力的工作计划。 我们只能根据我们可以恢复的情况
来规定一个微周期内一定数量的训练课程。

这也意味着我们需要意识到有一个时间间隔

between training sessions that we need to manage to ensure we achieve
positive results. We cannot consistently go as hard as possible in multiple
training sessions in a row without achieving some sort of negative outcome.
However, we need to accomplish quite a lot in the period we have to train
athletes, which is limited and restricted. When we plan a training program,
we need to ask how many higher-threshold training sessions can be included
within a microcycle. The answer to this question not only determines what
we will get from training but also how we manage higher-threshold training
session frequency.

Rule 4: Managing Frequency
Frequency needs to undulate intensity from one
training session to the next.
Undulating intensity with training sessions is an important rule for team-like
environments (figure 11.4). Accommodating many athletes’ schedules
simultaneously makes organizing training programs more complex than they
already are. Managing athletes’ training times, which are already jam-packed,
limits the times you can train. This has a profound impact on the recovery
rate from training sessions. For most cases, in the team setting, you are going
to have to work a Monday through Friday schedule (5-day microcycle + 2
rest days). Although this is a fairly common aspect of training, it does make
organizing more high-threshold, high-intensity training sessions within 5
days challenging. Not to mention that you have to work around class and
practice schedules, which further compounds the negative response to
training. Undulating higher-intensity training sessions with lower-intensity
training sessions are built around working within a 5-day microcycle at less
than favorable times (early morning or late night). Chances are, we will have
three to four opportunities to train a team during the off-season and two to
three opportunities during the season. This organically creates rest days from
training, not from stress, but from targeted training. If we are fortunate
enough to have four to five training opportunities, we have to be strategic

我们需要管理培训课程之间的时间，以确保我们取得积极的成果。 我
们不可能在连续多次训练中持续尽最大努力而不取得某种负面结果。然
而，我们在培养运动员的时期内需要完成的工作是相当多的，这是有限
的和受限制的。 当我们规划训练计划时，我们需要问一个微周期内可
以包含多少个更高阈值的训练课程。 这个问题的答案不仅决定了我们
将从培训中获得什么，还决定了我们如何管理更高阈值的培训课程频率
。

规则 4：管理频率
频率需要使一次训练到下一次训练的强度波动。

训练课程的强度波动是团队环境中的一条重要规则（图 11.4）。 同时
适应许多运动员的日程安排使得组织训练计划比现在更加复杂。管理运
动员的训练时间已经很拥挤，这限制了你可以训练的时间。 这对训练
的恢复率有着深远的影响。对于大多数情况，在团队环境中，您必须按
周一到周五的时间表工作（5 天微周期 + 2 个休息日）。尽管这是培训
中相当常见的一个方面，但它确实使得在 5 天内组织更多高门槛、高强
度的培训课程具有挑战性。 更不用说你必须围绕课堂和练习时间表进
行工作，这进一步加剧了对培训的负面反应。 波动的高强度训练课程
和低强度训练课程是围绕在不太有利的时间（清晨或深夜）的 5 天微周
期内进行的工作而建立的。我们有可能在休赛期有三到四次训练球队的
机会，在赛季期间有两到三次训练球队的机会。这有机地从训练中创造
了休息日，不是从压力中，而是从有针对性的训练中。 如果我们有幸
有四到五个培训机会，我们就必须有策略

with what we do on days following high-intensity work.
What this may look like is having an alternate sequence of day 1: high
intensity; day 2: low intensity; day 3: high intensity; day 4: low intensity; day
5: high intensity; and days 6 and 7: low intensity (rest days). As we discussed
with individuality, no two people respond the same to stress. On the one
hand, this undulation might be just right in terms of stress, and on the other
hand, it may be too much. For the more fast-twitch, advanced athletes, this
may sequence as day 1: high intensity; day 2: low intensity; day 3: low
intensity; day 4: high intensity; day 5: high intensity; and days 6 and 7: low
intensity (rest days). We have to consider rule 3, Fatigue, dictates frequency
as the means of adjusting high-intensity training sessions in a microcycle,
based on what the athlete can tolerate. This is also true for athletes who are
going through stressful periods, such as exams or extensive travel.

Rule 5: Types of Training Sessions and Frequency

规则 5：培训课程的类型和频率

In the situation where you have to do back-toback high-intensity training sessions, a greater
number of low-intensity training sessions is
needed in response.
The residual impact of both fitness and fatigue needs to be managed to garner
positive adaptations. The often misunderstood component is that more fatigue
is directly correlated with more results. What we at least understand from
GAS is the consequence that too much stress relative to what the system can
recover from leads to the exhaustion phase (Selye, 1950). The exhaustion
phase is the point where the ratio of fitness to fatigue inverts, with fatigue
being greater than fitness. Fatigue accumulates to such a high level that we
do not achieve the desired fitness adaptations. This incomplete recovery from
back-to-back training sessions creates excess fatigue, which detracts from any
intended positive adaptation. Residual fatigue is too great relative to the
fitness residual to create adaptation (figure 11.5).
Chiu and Barnes (2003) discuss the dynamics of volumes of higher
mechanical work, higher velocities, or general intensities requiring longer
recovery rates. They also state that increased volumes with increased
frequencies lead to a greater overall impact of fatigue and a reduced fitness
effect. As Selye (1950) references, the rationale for the stressor has to be
sufficient to create change, while at the same time, if the stress is too great,
the response will be counterproductive. This is an established concept in
medicine called hormesis: a biphasic dose response to an environmental
agent characterized by a low-dose stimulation or beneficial effect and a highdose inhibitory or toxic effect (Mattson, 2008). The phrase the difference
between the poison and the antidote is the dosage is appropriate and deserves
a closer look. We need to appreciate that there is a point of diminishing
returns, a principle that applies to activities or protocols that are too great to
recover from.

在必须进行连续高强度训练的情况下，就需要进行更多
的低强度训练来应对。

需要管理健身和疲劳的残余影响以获得积极的适应。经常被误解的一点
是，更多的疲劳与更多的结果直接相关。 我们至少从 GAS 中了解到，
相对于系统可以恢复的压力太大，会导致耗尽阶段（Selye，1950）。
疲惫阶段是健康与疲劳比率反转的点，疲劳大于健康。 疲劳累积到如
此高的水平，以至于我们无法达到预期的健身适应。连续训练的不完全
恢复会造成过度疲劳，从而影响任何预期的积极适应。 残余疲劳相对
于体能残余而言太大，无法产生适应（图 11.5）。

Chiu 和 Barnes (2003) 讨论了更高机械功、更高速度或需要更长恢复
率的一般强度的动态。 他们还指出，随着频率的增加而增加的训练量
会导致疲劳的整体影响更大，并降低健身效果。 正如 Selye (1950) 所提
到的，压力源的理由必须足以创造变化，而与此同时，如果压力太大，
反应就会适得其反。 这是医学上的一个既定概念，称为hormesis：对环
境因素的双相剂量反应，其特征是低剂量刺激或有益作用和高剂量抑制
或毒性作用（Mattson，2008）。 短语 the difference
between the poison and the antidote is the dosage 是合适的，值得仔细研究
。 我们需要认识到，存在收益递减点，这一原则适用于规模太大而无
法恢复的活动或协议。

Combine that with traditionally having to take Saturday and Sunday off,

inefficient. Aside from the awkwardness of the training program, the quality
of the second day on a back-to-back schedule would be less productive due to
the fatigue accumulated from day 1. The cost of doing back-to-back highintensity training days seems to be too much; however, there will be times
when you have to at least consider it as an option. In situations such as travel
