Rule 6: Neurologically Based Work
Neurological-based work requires more attention
to recovery than metabolic or muscular-based
work.
“The nervous system takes six times the length of the muscular system to
recover.” (Poliquin, 2016). As we evaluate the impact of training relative to
what we can do in the next training session, the hidden fatigue from the
neurologically based work is the hardest to understand, making it the most
challenging to amend. Muscle soreness from muscular work or general
fatigue from metabolic work makes it easy to rationalize rest days or reduce
volume. Soreness and fatigue are more inherently obvious and justifiable to
amend a training program. Neurological fatigue has a connotation of being
something we can readily overcome. We know that readiness from objective
measurements, such as resting heart rate or heart rate variability, will mean
diminished output of velocity, power, or absolute strength. Even with
knowledge of how performance will decrease following neurologically based
training, it is still hard to rationalize taking a deload week or rest day.
Chiu and Barnes (2003) discuss the fitness effect as primarily neural,
meaning that the response to the stimulus was displayed with catecholamine
response, specifically with beta and alpha receptors. Hormones such as
testosterone downregulate or decrease sensitivity based on the intensity or
frequency of the stressor placed on the subject. Interestingly, we see a shortterm drop in testosterone during high-volume workouts but an uptick in
testosterone with higher-intensity workouts. This reaction to training is
completely negated with high frequency; fatigue becomes greater than
fitness. Too much frequency means diminished recovery, especially with
higher receptor site sensitivity. The uptick of testosterone shifts to not
producing enough, and recovery gets compromised. Any benefit we receive

几周或化妆，了解将要发生的事情是我们唯一能做的事情。

规则 6：基于神经学的工作
基于神经的工作比基于代谢或肌肉的工作需要更多地关
注恢复。

“神经系统需要六倍于肌肉系统的时间才能恢复。” （波利昆，2016
）。 当我们评估训练相对于我们在下一次训练中可以做的事情的影响
时，基于神经学的工作所隐藏的疲劳是最难理解的，也使其成为最具挑
战性的修正。 肌肉工作引起的肌肉酸痛或新陈代谢工作引起的全身疲
劳，很容易合理安排休息日或减少训练量。 酸痛和疲劳本质上更明显
，并且有理由修改训练计划。 神经性疲劳意味着我们可以轻松克服。
我们知道，客观测量（例如静息心率或心率变异性）的准备状态将意味
着速度、功率或绝对力量输出的减少。 即使了解基于神经学的训练后
表现会如何下降，仍然很难合理地安排减负荷周或休息日。

Chiu 和 Barnes (2003) 讨论了健身效应主要是神经性的，这意味着对
刺激的反应是通过儿茶酚胺反应，特别是 β 和 α 受体来表现的。 睾
酮等激素会根据施加在受试者身上的压力源的强度或频率来下调或降低
敏感性。有趣的是，我们发现在高强度锻炼期间睾酮水平会出现短期下
降，但在高强度锻炼时睾酮水平会上升。 这种对训练的反应在高频率
下会被完全消除； 疲劳变得大于健身。 频率过高意味着恢复能力下降
，尤其是在受体位点敏感性较高的情况下。 睾丸激素的上升会导致产
生不足，并且恢复会受到影响。 我们收到的任何好处

from neurological work is offset by being impatient and doing too many
high-intensity, neurologically based training sessions with little rest between
them.
Managing the social pressure of being within a group relative to feeling
the impact of a nervous system not ready for training due to residual fatigue
is a hard thing to manage with a large group. Group dynamics amplify
everything good. We want more effort; we will get it, and the momentum of
the group will be there. In this case, if we are inadequately prepared for that
stress, we will respond negatively to it. The antidote has become a poison
based on the environment, which is why we need to understand that the
absence of soreness is not an excuse to keep pounding high neurological
work again. We can use high-level testing such as heart rate variability, but
anyone who has tried to make in-session adjustments with large groups based
on this information can attest that it is hard to do so consistently. It is safer to
make hard rules to manage this inevitable aspect of training.

Rule 7: Fitness of the Athlete and the Response to
Training
Relative fitness of the athlete determines the
fatigue response.
Chiu and Barnes (2003) discuss that the difference between stress as a poison
or antidote is the dosage relative to an athlete’s fitness level. The dosage
being too much is tied to the overall fitness or functioning capacity of the
athlete. The avoidance of exhaustion is as much related to the amount of
intensity, volume, and frequency as the overall fitness of the person going
through the program. If we are fitter, we can tolerate more. By fitness, we are
referring to the capacity of the oxidative system. This creates a paradox
because coaches need to develop adequate oxidative energy system levels to
train phosphagen energy systems effectively. The relative volume we can do
of high-intensity work is predicated on the capacity of that system. If we have
higher fitness levels, we can recover more efficiently intra- and intertraining

神经学工作中的疲劳被不耐烦和进行太多高强度、基于神经学的训练课
程所抵消，而训练课程之间几乎没有休息。
在一个大团体中，管理与感受因残余疲劳而未准备好训练的神经系统
的影响有关的群体内的社会压力是一件很难管理的事情。 团体动力会
放大一切美好事物。我们需要更多的努力；我们会得到它，并且团队的
动力将会存在。在这种情况下，如果我们没有充分准备好应对这种压力
，我们就会做出消极的反应。 解药已经成为基于环境的毒药，这就是
为什么我们需要明白，没有酸痛并不是再次继续进行高强度神经工作的
借口。 我们可以使用心率变异性等高级测试，但任何尝试根据此信息
对大型群体进行会话调整的人都可以证明，很难始终如一地做到这一点
。制定严格的规则来管理培训中不可避免的这一方面会更安全。

规则 7：运动员的体能和对训练的反应

Relative fitness of the athlete determines the
fatigue response.
Chiu 和 Barnes (2003) 讨论了压力作为毒药或解毒剂之间的区别在于相
对于运动员健康水平的剂量。 剂量过多与运动员的整体健康或功能能
力有关。 避免疲劳与强度、训练量和频率以及参加该计划的人的整体
健康状况息息相关。如果我们身体更健康，我们就能承受更多。通过健
身，我们指的是氧化系统的能力。 这就产生了一个悖论，因为教练需
要开发足够的氧化能量系统水平来有效地训练磷酸原能量系统。我们可
以完成的高强度工作的相对量取决于该系统的容量。如果我们有更高的
体能水平，我们就可以在训练中和训练间更有效地恢复

sessions. Having an athlete with poor fitness recover more slowly will affect
the volume of high-intensity work possible within a training session. This
will then affect how much work we can do overall in a training week, which
then limits how much high-intensity density we can have, lowering the
ceiling of performance we can achieve.
The impact of Hans Selye’s (1950) GAS was immense. Without GAS,
there is no examination of how we can weigh and evaluate the effects of
stress on the body. To say that there needs to be an evaluation of fitness along
with fatigue does not diminish the value of examining stress on the body. It is
important to understand that a balance and rhythm need to be in place to
consistently reach a targeted outcome. That rhythm is facilitated by the
system’s function, also known as the fitness of the system. Performance
training is built on the premise that we need to improve to a predetermined
target. The focus should be on what is needed over what is wanted.
Developing an oxidative energy system to serve a greater goal of running
faster or jumping higher is a need, and if we cannot recover adequately, it
becomes a necessary component of training. If we want someone to run
faster, they will have to be able to run longer to recover from the training that
makes them run faster.
It is during the process toward that target that we can lose sight of this
simple fact and overly romanticize fatigue as the purpose of training. In doing
so, we diminish the actual fitness adaptation we are seeking and accumulate
more and more fatigue. We can minimize the negative aspect of stress with
the logic that fatigue is part of the process. The struggle of working within a
group environment and the pressures that entail are given more buffering
when we are more oxidatively fit. We recover oxidatively from phosphagen
or glycolytic work (Plisk, 1991). What goes up must go down. There will
always be a centering force in what we do with training. The rate of that
centering is predicated on oxidative fitness. If we are fit, our ability to do
more is increased. The athlete with poor oxidative capacity, or low fitness,
will have the most difficult time recovering. At any given time, we can have
drastically different responses to training based on the relative capacity of the
athletes participating.

会议。体能较差的运动员恢复得更慢会影响训练中可能进行的高强度训
练量。 这将影响我们在训练周内可以完成的总体工作量，从而限制我
们可以拥有的高强度密度，从而降低我们可以达到的表现上限。
Hans Selye (1950) 的《GAS》的影响是巨大的。 如果没有 GAS，我
们就无法衡量和评估压力对身体的影响。说需要对健康状况和疲劳进行
评估并不会削弱检查身体压力的价值。重要的是要理解，需要保持平衡
和节奏才能持续达到目标结果。 这种节奏是由系统功能（也称为
fitness of the system）促进的。 绩效训练的前提是我们需要提高到预定
的目标。 重点应该放在需要什么而不是想要什么上。开发氧化能量系
统来实现跑得更快或跳得更高的更大目标是必要的，如果我们不能充分
恢复，它就成为训练的必要组成部分。 如果我们希望某人跑得更快，
他们就必须能够跑更长时间，以便从使他们跑得更快的训练中恢复过来
。

正是在实现这一目标的过程中，我们可能会忽视这个简单的事实，而
将疲劳过度浪漫化为训练的目的。在这样做的过程中，我们减少了我们
正在寻求的实际健身适应，并积累了越来越多的疲劳。 我们可以通过
疲劳是过程一部分的逻辑来最大限度地减少压力的负面影响。当我们的
氧化能力更强时，在团队环境中工作的挣扎和随之而来的压力就会得到
更多缓冲。 我们从磷酸原或糖酵解工作中进行氧化恢复（Plisk，1991
）。 上涨的必然下跌。 我们的训练过程中总会有一股中心力量。 这
种集中的速度取决于氧化适应性。 如果我们身体健康，我们做更多事
情的能力就会增强。 氧化能力差或体能低的运动员恢复起来最困难。
在任何特定时间，我们都可以根据参与运动员的相对能力对训练做出截
然不同的反应。

Rule 8: Advanced Versus Novice Athletes’ Response to
Training
More advanced athletes have a higher tolerance
compared to the same stress in novice athletes.
It would be ridiculous to give an infant the same dosage of medication as an
adult, even if they had the same disease. We can look at what the best
athlete’s training regimen is and assume it will work the same for a novice
athlete. What we often forget about is that a built tolerance through countless
cycles of imposed stress and recovery leads to an outcome of an incredibly
high capacity to handle imposed stress. We can classify this built-up
tolerance as the fitness of the individual, and as discussed, this built-up
fitness allows one to handle more stress than someone without that exposure.
The assumption that a particular program is the best because an elite athlete
uses it and therefore it will have the same result on a different person with
less capacity is the same as saying that a medication dosage that works for an
adult should work for an infant. We avoid looking at the fitness of a novice
athlete and overly glorify overwhelming fatigue as a badge of honor when we
overreach with greater than tolerable limits of recovery.
At the same time, advanced athletes may have increased tolerance to
training stress, but that is not their only source of stress. Advanced athletes
typically have their overall workloads outside of training, practice, and game
stress. They not only play more in games, but they also get more reps in
practice, and they are being demanded more of as a leader, which creates a
much higher overall level of stress. One important aspect of this chapter is
being deliberate about how we apply stress. We know that novice athletes
will respond more favorably to minimal doses of stress; we need to leverage
the same thought process for advanced athletes. We have to look at training
stress that is aggregated with overall stress. A large reason that novice
athletes respond favorably to training is due to the novelty combined with the
maintenance of fitness relative to fatigue. This is not the same for advanced

规则 8：高级运动员与新手运动员对训练的反应

与新手运动员相比，高级运动员具有更高的耐受力。

即使婴儿患有相同的疾病，但给婴儿服用与成人相同剂量的药物是荒谬
的。 我们可以看看最好的运动员的训练方案是什么，并假设它对新手
运动员也同样有效。我们经常忘记的是，通过无数次施加的压力和恢复
的循环而建立的耐受性会带来令人难以置信的高能力来处理施加的压力
。 我们可以将这种累积的耐受性归类为个人的适应性，正如所讨论的
，这种累积的适应性允许一个人比没有这种暴露的人承受更多的压力。
假设某个特定计划是最好的，因为精英运动员使用它，因此它对能力较
低的不同人会产生相同的结果，这与说适用于成人的药物剂量应该适用
于婴儿是一样的。 当我们超出了可容忍的恢复极限时，我们避免关注
新手运动员的健康状况，并过度美化压倒性的疲劳作为荣誉徽章。

与此同时，高级运动员对训练压力的耐受力可能有所提高，但这并不
是他们唯一的压力来源。 高级运动员通常有训练、练习和比赛压力之
外的总体工作量。 他们不仅在比赛中打得更多，而且在练习中也得到
了更多的代表，而且他们作为领导者的要求也更高，这造成了更高的整
体压力。 本章的一个重要方面是仔细考虑我们如何施加压力。 我们知
道，新手运动员会对最小程度的压力做出更有利的反应；我们需要为高
级运动员利用相同的思维过程。 我们必须考虑与总体压力相结合的训
练压力。 新手运动员对训练反应良好的一个重要原因是新颖性以及相
对于疲劳的健康维持。 这与高级的不一样

athletes; novelty is not a factor in adapting. Strategy with high stress followed
by adequate recovery is the only option we have with advanced athletes. For
advanced athletes, fatigue is much harder to manage due to the overall stress.
Less is not only more. This does not mean we should not leverage intensity
with advanced athletes; we just need to be more strategic with when and how
much.

Mood’s Effect on Rating of Perceived Exertion
Tracking wellness before the lift will be a chore over time. For the
athlete, it will feel as though this is pointless; for the coach, it will
feel as though it is more work and a waste of time. The problem
is that data collection takes time to tell us a story. We have to
collect and wait for a pattern to emerge. Wellness tracking is a
lot like watching a tree you planted grow.
One story we found was the correlation of mood to the training
rating of perceived exertion (RPE). On average, we found that
when athletes reported below 3 (ranging from 1, poor mood, to 5,
great mood), athletes reported significantly higher RPEs.
Average RPEs were an additional 1 point higher when mood
wellness was below 3. This brought on several other questions.
The first question was, where were bad moods coming from?
We tracked mood averages on each day. Mondays were, on
average, the best mood, and Wednesdays were the worst mood.
Next, we dove into the times of the year. The off-season mood
was significantly higher than the in-season mood. The results of
Mondays being good and Wednesdays being bad were universal
for the entire year but were amplified as worse in season.
What this meant for programming was fewer stressful things
on Wednesdays. We converted Wednesdays into an active
recovery day for the off-season and more upper body focus in
the season. The rationale was to prevent the average worst
mood day from negatively affecting recovery during the
microcycle. By isolating the worst mood day, we could better

们对高级运动员的唯一选择。对于高级运动员来说，由于整体压力，疲
劳更难控制。少不仅是多。 这并不意味着我们不应该利用高级运动员
的强度；我们只需要在时间和数量上更具战略性。

情绪对感知用力程度的影响
随着时间的推移，在电梯前追踪健康状况将成为一件苦差事。对
于运动员来说，会觉得这毫无意义；对于教练来说，这会感觉像
是更多的工作和浪费时间。问题是数据收集需要时间来告诉我们
一个故事。 我们必须收集并等待模式的出现。 健康追踪很像看
着你种下的一棵树长大。
我们发现的一个故事是情绪与感知劳累（RPE）训练评级的相
关性。 平均而言，我们发现，当运动员报告低于 3（范围从 1（
情绪不佳）到 5（心情好））时，运动员报告的 RPE 显着更高。
当情绪健康度低于 3 时，平均 RPE 会额外高出 1 个百分点。这带
来了其他几个问题。
第一个问题是，坏情绪从何而来？我们追踪每天的情绪平均值
。 平均而言，周一的情绪最好，周三的情绪最差。接下来，我们
深入了解一年中的各个时期。 淡季情绪明显高于旺季情绪。周一
好、周三差的结果在全年中都是普遍存在的，但在季节中会被放
大为更差。
这对于编程来说意味着周三的压力会减少。 我们将周三转变为
休赛期的积极恢复日，并在赛季中更多地关注上半身。 这样做的
理由是为了防止平均情绪最差的一天对微周期期间的恢复产生负
面影响。 通过隔离情绪最差的一天，我们可以更好

program for our athletes.
This is anecdotal, but it paints a clear picture of finding a
connection to your athlete’s well-being and fitness–fatigue ratio.
We tried to find correlations between sleep quality and RPE on
high-intensity days, between fatigue and RPE on high-workload
days, and between soreness and RPE on high-volume days.
Working to find correlations between wellness and RPE, or any
other metric, puts more value on the metric and demonstrates to
athletes and staff that it is worthwhile.

Rule 9: Intensity’s Relationship to Volume, Rest, and
Frequency
Intensity has an inverse relationship to volume,
density, and frequency.
We can adjust the stress we impose in multiple ways: intensity, volume,
density, or frequency. Each of these variables has a relationship with the
others. As coaches, we tend to compartmentalize these variables to better
leverage them in training. What can become lost is the fact that intensity is
inversely proportional to volume, density, and frequency as a function of the
training economy. As intensity increases, volume, density, and frequency all
must decrease. The only way we can accommodate any training focus is to
understand the relative relationships between these variables.
Periodization is made much simpler when we can default to this simple
and effective rule in training. Program design aligns these variables with
specific methods or exercises at certain points in the year, which is where
focused blocks take form. Having targeted stress through training is
contingent on how much stress we can maintain. When we increase either
volume, density, or frequency relative to a high intensity, we can reach
diminishing returns faster. Periodization is about avoiding diminishing
returns. Program design aligns these variables with methods and exercises to

为我们的运动员制定的计划。
这是轶事，但它清楚地描绘了如何找到与运动员的健康和健身
疲劳比之间的联系。我们试图找出高强度日的睡眠质量与 RPE 之
间的相关性、高工作负荷日的疲劳与 RPE 之间的相关性以及高工
作量日的酸痛与 RPE 之间的相关性。努力寻找健康与 RPE 或任何
其他指标之间的相关性，可以提高该指标的价值，并向运动员和
工作人员证明这是值得的。

规则 9：强度与训练量、休息和频率的关系

强度与体积、密度和频率成反比关系。

我们可以通过多种方式调整施加的压力：强度、体积、密度或频率。
这些变量中的每一个都与其他变量之间存在关系。 作为教练，我们倾
向于划分这些变量，以便在训练中更好地利用它们。 可能会丢失的事
实是，作为训练经济的函数，强度与训练量、密度和频率成反比。随着
强度的增加，体积、密度和频率都必须减少。 我们适应任何培训重点
的唯一方法是了解这些变量之间的相对关系。
当我们在训练中默认使用这个简单而有效的规则时，周期化就会变得
更加简单。 计划设计将这些变量与一年中某些时间点的特定方法或练
习相结合，这就是形成重点块的地方。 Having targeted stress through t
raining is contingent on how much stress we can maintain. 当我们相对
于高强度增加体积、密度或频率时，我们可以更快地达到收益递减。
分期是为了避免收益递减。程序设计将这些变量与方法和练习结合起来
，以

avoid diminishing returns.
We are trying to place constraints within our training program to preserve
the ability to progressively overload from one microcycle to the next. A
mismatched program design that tries to address multiple objectives
simultaneously ends up being counterproductive due to the excessive level of
fatigue it produces. Regardless of volume, density, or frequency, we will
produce fatigue when training at a higher intensity, pushed to threshold. The
ability to progressively overload allows us to evaluate whether we have too
much volume, not enough rest during a training session, or not enough
recovery between training sessions. The limited ability to increase intensity
means we did not adjust volume, density, or frequency enough to
accommodate adaptation. The residual fatigue is too much going into either
the next set within the workout or the next training session. The result is
diminished value from the time spent.
Chiu and Barnes (2003) discuss that the difference between low-volume,
high-intensity training and high-volume, low-intensity training yields a
difference in growth hormone levels. Where they saw a decrease in acute
testosterone during high-volume workouts, they saw a spike in growth
hormone as well. We are working within windows of opportunity; after
training, there are acute and chronic responses. It’s important to understand
that the relatively short-term impact can be augmented negatively with
decreased allowance for recovery. The acute response of increased growth
hormone can change for the worse if the frequency is higher than a person’s
fitness can tolerate. Remember that decreased recovery occurs frequently
within a microcycle. If we increase the occurrence of stress, we risk having
too much fatigue relative to fitness. We see this in all systems in the body;
there are feedback loops. The normal uptick in growth hormone could be
blunted by simply not being used, which directly results from the nervous
system going into survival mode and adjusting catecholamine production.
What an acute spike in testosterone from high-intensity exercise versus an
acute spike in growth hormone from high-volume exercise does is give a
framework for training. The term high-low refers to leveraging different
responses to different volumes and intensities for greater returns. Volume and
intensity are inversely proportional. Intensity and frequency or density are

避免收益递减。
我们正在尝试在我们的训练计划中施加限制，以保持从一个微周期到
下一个微周期逐渐超载的能力。 试图同时解决多个目标的不匹配的计
划设计最终会因为产生过度的疲劳而适得其反。 无论训练量、密度或
频率如何，当训练强度较高、达到阈值时，我们都会产生疲劳。逐渐超
负荷的能力使我们能够评估是否训练量过多、训练期间休息不足或训练
之间恢复不足。 增加强度的能力有限意味着我们没有调整足够的体积
、密度或频率来适应适应。 进入下一组训练或下一次训练时，残余疲
劳过多。 结果是所花费时间的价值减少。

Chiu 和 Barnes (2003) 讨论了低容量、高强度训练和高容量、低强度
训练之间的差异会导致生长激素水平的差异。 他们在大量锻炼期间发
现急性睾酮水平下降，同时生长激素水平也出现激增。 我们正在机会
之窗内开展工作； 训练后，有急性反应和慢性反应之分。 重要的是要
明白，相对短期的影响可能会随着恢复准备金的减少而增加。 如果频
率高于一个人的健康承受能力，生长激素增加的急性反应可能会变得更
糟。 请记住，恢复下降经常发生在一个微周期内。 如果我们增加压力
的发生，我们就会面临相对于健身而言过度疲劳的风险。 我们在身体
的所有系统中都看到了这一点；存在反馈循环。 生长激素的正常上升
可能会因不使用而减弱，这直接是由于神经系统进入生存模式并调整儿
茶酚胺的产生所致。

高强度运动引起的睾丸激素急剧上升与大容量运动引起的生长激素急
剧上升的作用是为训练提供一个框架。 术语 high-low 指的是利用对不
同数量和强度的不同响应来获得更大的回报。音量和强度成反比。 强
度和频率或密度是

inversely proportional at all times. We cannot have both. This is an organic
strategy to avoid being overly fatigued from high-frequency intensity or
volume focus. High-low, conjugate, or concurrent planning are all methods
that can be used to maintain high output without compromising fitness
adaptations.

Rule 10: Training Residuals
Length of training residuals are the product of
training stress spread over a longer period.
Clarke and Skiba (2013) said, “The goal of exercise prescription is to restore
or improve an individual’s functional capacity to a level commensurate with
healthy living or with his or her fitness or athletic performance goals.” This is
often a forgotten element in the training needs of individuals and deserves to
be addressed well before applying any level of stress. The term
supercompensation refers to reaching a higher functioning level than when
you started. With supercompensation, the drop precedes the rise. We
constantly look at these short-term drops as necessary but never appreciate
that longer drops are not the goal. To have longer residuals, we need a series
of drops. Drops in fitness with corresponding rises over lengthened periods
result in longer-term performance residuals (figure 11.6).
Clarke and Skiba (2013) showed that periods of detraining (or deloading)
result in a decay of physical abilities. This rate of decay reflects not only the
peak functional level but also the process of attaining that level (figure 11.7).
What we should see with the rest is a spike in adaptation. Alternatively, when
we see a drop, it reflects overreaching without recovery for far too long. The
key is to have a consistent rise in response to a drop. If we repeatedly reach a
higher functioning level, then overall, we will have longer residual effects.

任何时候都成反比。 我们不能两者兼得。 这是一种避免因高频强度或
音量集中而过度疲劳的有机策略。 高-低、共轭或并发规划都是可用于
在不影响适应性的情况下保持高输出的方法。

规则 10：训练残差
训练残差的长度是训练压力在较长时间内分布的产物。

Clarke 和 Skiba (2013) 说，“运动处方的目标是恢复或提高个人的功能
能力，使其达到与健康生活或他或她的健身或运动表现目标相称的水平
。”这通常是个人培训需求中被遗忘的因素，在施加任何程度的压力之
前都应该解决这一问题。 术语 supercompensation 指的是达到比开始时
更高的功能水平。 通过超补偿，下降先于上升。 我们不断地在必要时
考虑这些短期的下跌，但从来没有意识到长期的下跌并不是我们的目标
。为了获得更长的残差，我们需要一系列的下降。 随着时间的推移，
适应性的下降和相应的上升会导致长期表现残差（图 11.6）。

Clarke 和 Skiba (2013) 表明，一段时间的放松（或减负）会导致身体
能力衰退。这种衰减率不仅反映了峰值功能水平，还反映了达到该水平
的过程（图 11.7）。我们应该看到其余的事情是适应的激增。或者，当
我们看到下跌时，它反映了过度扩张而长期没有恢复。关键是要以持续
的上涨来应对下跌。如果我们不断地达到更高的功能水平，那么总的来
说，我们将产生更长的残留效应。

生理规则设置

Fitness–fatigue is a term that should be thought of as a progression from
GAS. In reality, it is a mechanism to hold us accountable for an overfascination with stress. Are we improving?—that’s the only question. Fitness
is taken for granted in the quest for the elite. It is viewed as a short-term
sacrifice for the greater good. But if we constantly prioritize fatigue as a
benchmark for success, we inevitably will net fewer adaptations. There needs
to be an appreciation that specific windows of fitness and fatigue close at
different rates. The sequence of fitness lasting longer than fatigue is part of
this larger harmonious dynamic that creates a sense of equilibrium toward
supercompensation. We are artificially creating a stress-adaptation response
in which we should demonstrate incredible restraint and patience. It is
tempting to think that if we can just incur more and more stress, we will
reach higher and higher levels. This may be the case for some, but not for all.
The majority will need to prioritize fitness over fatigue. Fatigue focus will
come up shorter than we want more times than we want. The relationship
between the two is easily one of the most important factors we manage with
training (figure 11.8).

Fitness–fatigue这个术语应该被认为是 GAS 的演变。 事实上，它是一种
让我们对压力过度迷恋负责的机制。我们有进步吗？——这是唯一的问
题。在追求精英的过程中，健康被认为是理所当然的。 它被视为为了
更大的利益而做出的短期牺牲。 但如果我们不断地将疲劳作为成功的
基准，我们不可避免地会减少适应。需要认识到特定的健康和疲劳窗口
以不同的速度关闭。 比疲劳持续时间更长的健身序列是这种更大的和
谐动态的一部分，它创造了一种朝向超级补偿的平衡感。 我们正在人
为地创造一种压力适应反应，在这种反应中我们应该表现出令人难以置
信的克制和耐心。 人们很容易认为，如果我们能够承受越来越大的压
力，我们就会达到越来越高的水平。对于某些人来说可能是这种情况，
但并非所有人都是如此。大多数人需要优先考虑健身而不是疲劳。 疲
劳焦点会比我们想要的时间短、次数比我们想要的多。 两者之间的关
系无疑是我们通过培训管理的最重要因素之一（图 11.8）。

FIGURE 11.8 Physiological rules setup (body comp screen).

Take Home
Training stress is a means to an end. Managing fatigue relative to fitness is
foundational to positively adapting to stress. As coaches, we need to use
simple and intuitive rules of physiology to consistently leverage stress
effectively. Adaptation should not be a difficult thing to accomplish,
regardless of group size, if we adhere to physiological rules of training.
Fatigue is not the goal; fitness adaptation is the goal with as many of our
athletes as possible. That may simply mean that less is more.

图 11.8 生理规则设置（身体补偿屏幕）。

带回家
训练压力是达到目的的一种手段。 管理与健身相关的疲劳是积极适应
压力的基础。 作为教练，我们需要使用简单直观的生理学规则来持续
有效地利用压力。 如果我们遵守训练的生理规则，无论团体规模如何
，适应都不应该是一件困难的事情。疲劳不是目标； 体能适应是我们
尽可能多的运动员的目标。这可能只是意味着少即是多。

APPLYING PHYSIOLOGICAL
RULES FOR PERIODIZATION
AND PROGRAM DESIGN
Periodization is an important concept for a strength coach; it means that you
have a plan. Not just a plan, you have an actual system in place to reach a
targeted outcome. A major component of training is focusing on a specific
target to optimize performance. The planning portion is the equivalent of
creating a map to reach that destination as quickly as possible. After the
initial plan is made, more decisions will always be required. Periodization is
the equivalent of deciding to take back roads knowing that it will be longer
based on mileage but quicker for avoiding traffic. Without periodization, we
cannot say whether an intervention we intend to use is an effective or
ineffective strategy.
As we learned in the last chapter, managing fatigue over developing
fitness is more of a determining factor in overall performance. To say that
planning is futile because unpredictable factors will emerge is a short-sighted
approach. The more complex something is, the more we need a solid plan.
Periodization is built on this idea. Good periodization is based not just on
what we want, but on what we do when a plan is not working the way we
want it to. We can look at planning as a means to prepare for inevitable
variance. Periodization gives us perspective. At the same time, periodization

12
应用生理规则进行周期化和程序
设计

对于力量教练来说，周期化是一个重要的概念。这意味着你有一个计划
。 不仅仅是一个计划，您还拥有一个实际的系统来实现目标结果。 培
训的一个主要组成部分是专注于优化绩效的特定目标。 规划部分相当
于创建地图以尽快到达目的地。 制定最初的计划后，总是需要更多的
决定。周期化相当于决定走回头路，因为知道根据里程数会更长，但为
了避开交通拥堵会更快。如果没有分期，我们就无法判断我们打算使用
的干预措施是有效还是无效的策略。

正如我们在上一章中了解到的那样，管理疲劳而不是增强体能更多地
是整体表现的决定性因素。 如果说计划是徒劳的，因为会出现不可预
测的因素，这是一种短视的做法。 事情越复杂，我们就越需要一个可
靠的计划。周期化就是建立在这个想法的基础上的。 良好的分期不仅
取决于我们想要什么，还取决于当计划没有按照我们希望的方式运作时
我们该怎么做。 我们可以将计划视为为不可避免的差异做好准备的一
种手段。分期为我们提供了视角。同时，分期

allows for contingencies to keep us moving toward the ultimate goal. Said
differently, periodization ensures we are working toward something
regardless of what happens during training.

History of Periodization
Periodization is our plan for any period extending past a day. If we plan a
week out, we are, in a sense, periodizing our training. When we want to
establish an objective and organize our exercises and variables, we are
periodizing our training. When we check our work and ensure we use
principles and rules, we are periodizing our training.
Think of periodization as an attempt to predict the future. The origin of
periodization comes from coaches and researchers attempting to achieve this.
The foundation was based on prediction. Like a stock market broker breaks
down patterns to find future investments, a strength coach breaks down
patterns to find future patterns toward systematically allocating stress.

Linear Periodization
Long-term planning emerged from a Russian scientist, Matveyev, to better
prepare USSR athletes for international competition. Matveyev combined the
seasonal calendar and the stress response cycle created by Hans Selye to
create a set sequence of events leading up to the competition (Krüger, 2016).
This simple structure was an incredibly novel concept in physical training.
Previously, there was a lot of trial and error combined with wishful thinking.
Matveyev’s method forced the coach to inventory the desired outcome and
the stimuli that would elicit it. Some athletes did not achieve optimal
performance using this model.
Matveyev’s original periodization model was classified as linear. The flow
of volume was higher earlier in the off-season and lower approaching the
competitive season. The volume change had an inverse relationship with
intensity; intensity went from low to high as the competition approached.
This form of periodization still holds value regarding athletes’ and coaches’
intuitive understanding that, as competition gets closer, training needs to
become more related to what is done on the field or court. Intuition aside, not
every athlete fits into the linear periodization model. It started the

允许突发事件让我们朝着最终目标前进。 换句话说，周期化可以确保
我们无论训练期间发生什么，都朝着某个目标努力。

分期的历史
周期化是我们针对超过一天的任何时期的计划。 如果我们计划一周，
从某种意义上说，我们就是在定期训练。 当我们想要建立一个目标并
组织我们的练习和变量时，我们正在将我们的训练分期进行。 当我们
检查我们的工作并确保我们使用原则和规则时，我们正在定期进行培训
。
将分期视为预测未来的尝试。 周期化的起源来自于试图实现这一目
标的教练和研究人员。该基础是基于预测的。 就像股市经纪人打破模
式来寻找未来的投资一样，力量教练也打破模式来寻找未来的模式，从
而系统地分配压力。

线性周期化
俄罗斯科学家马特维耶夫提出了长期规划，旨在更好地为苏联运动员参
加国际比赛做好准备。马特维耶夫将季节日历和 Hans Selye 创建的压力
反应周期结合起来，创建了一系列比赛前的事件序列（Krüger，2016）
。这种简单的结构在体育训练中是一个令人难以置信的新颖概念。此前
，有大量的尝试和错误以及一厢情愿的想法。马特维耶夫的方法迫使教
练盘点期望的结果以及引发该结果的刺激。 一些运动员使用该模型并
没有达到最佳表现。
马特维耶夫最初的周期模型被归类为线性模型。淡季初期的流量较高
，接近竞争季节的流量较低。 体积变化与强度呈反比关系； 随着比赛
的临近，强度由低到高。这种分期形式对于运动员和教练员的直观理解
仍然有价值，即随着比赛的临近，训练需要与球场或球场上的表现更加
相关。抛开直觉不谈，并不是每个运动员都适合线性周期模型。 它开
始了

conversation of finding more appropriate periodization models for the athlete
to train under.

Nonlinear Periodization
Periodization has evolved over the years into nonlinear forms such as
conjugate and concurrent. These forms focus on multiple qualities within a
microcycle or training session (Verkhoshansky, 2019). This plan undulates in
terms of volume and intensity but is still moving toward a peak performance.
Nonlinear periodization also includes block periodization developed by
Michael Yessis (2008). Block periodization focuses on the training quality
for an entire mesocycle.
Conjugate and concurrent periodization are mixed approaches. Block
periodization is similar to linear periodization but applies a different order of
volume and intensity from one mesocycle to the next. With conjugate
periodization, all biomotor functions of velocity, force, and work will be in
every training session. Concurrent periodization takes a microcycle approach,
spreading the biomotor functions through individual training sessions. Block
periodization takes an even more lengthened approach to biomotor functions
within a mesocycle. Think of it this way: Nonlinear periodization applies all
biomotor functions in each training session (conjugate), in each training week
(concurrent), or in each training block (block).
You will find that coaches demonstrate an extreme preference for one
form of periodization. This is a mistake. There is no benefit to casting one
form as superior to another; the only thing that matters is results. Treat
periodization like models of thinking. Some are useful, but never a universal
solution.

Applying Physiological Rules
Now we have to apply the rules we have built. This section is about you in
your everyday life having codes of conduct. Multiple groups of days, dozens
of athletes, meetings with coaches and administrators, and a plethora of other
things you are required to do will eventually lead to a poorly thought-out
decision. Think of the judge making unfair or poorly thought-out rulings
before lunch; you are human and will need rules to govern your decisions

寻找更适合运动员训练的周期模型的对话。

非线性周期化
多年来，周期化已演变为非线性形式，例如共轭和并发。 这些形式侧
重于微循环或培训课程中的多种品质（Verkhoshansky，2019）。该计划
在数量和强度方面有所波动，但仍在朝着峰值表现迈进。非线性周期化
还包括 Michael Yessis (2008) 开发的块周期化。 块周期化侧重于整个中
周期的训练质量。
共轭和并发周期化是混合方法。 块周期化与线性周期化类似，但从
一个中周期到下一个周期应用不同的音量和强度顺序。 通过共轭周期
化，速度、力量和做功的所有生物运动功能都将出现在每次训练中。并
行周期化采用微循环方法，通过个人训练课程传播生物运动功能。块周
期化对中周期内的生物运动功能采取了更长的方法。这样想：非线性周
期化在每个训练课程（共轭）、每个训练周（并发）或每个训练块（块
）中应用所有生物运动功能。

您会发现教练表现出对一种形式的周期划分的极端偏好。 这是一个
错误。 铸造一种形式优于另一种形式并没有什么好处； 唯一重要的是
结果。 将分期视为思维模型。有些是有用的，但不是通用的解决方案
。

准则。多组的日子、几十名运动员、与教练和管理人员的会议，以及你
需要做的大量其他事情最终会导致一个考虑不周的决定。 想想法官在
午餐前做出的不公平或考虑不周的裁决； 你是人类，需要规则来管理
你的决定

Rule 1: Peaking
Peaking for a predetermined biomotor ability is
the foundation of periodization.
Matveyev’s linear periodization model was to develop general capacity early
and finish with more specificity (figure 12.2). The early phase term is general
physical preparation (GPP), where training uses higher volumes with lower
intensities. The transition from general to specific is classified as specific
physical preparation (SPP), where training intensity is raised and the
corresponding volume dropped. The rationale was to peak for a biomotor

规则 1：峰值
预定生物运动能力的峰值是周期化的基础。

马特维耶夫的线性周期模型是尽早发展一般能力，并以更具体的方式完
成（图 12.2）。早期阶段术语是 general physical preparation (GPP)，其
中训练使用较高的训练量和较低的强度。 从一般到特定的转变被分类
为specific physical preparation（SPP），其中训练强度增加并且相应的
训练量下降。 基本原理是达到生物马达的峰值

or a combination with general movement patterns was intended to replicate
what was needed to perform during competition.

Rule 2: Specificity

The concept of sequencing sets, reps, time under tension (TUT), intensity,
and rest to garner a very specific result is how we create an outcome. This is
important because it gives credence to the fact that long-term planning makes
sense. This is the principle of specificity, and specificity directs periodization.
Developing a specific quality matters regarding performance, and we should

能力尽可能接近竞争。力量、速度、做功或与一般运动模式的组合的峰

规则 2：特异性
特异性指导分期，而个性控制分期。

为了获得非常具体的结果而对组数、次数、紧张时间 (TUT)、强度和休
息进行排序的概念就是我们创造结果的方式。这很重要，因为它证明了
长期规划是有意义的。这就是特异性原则，特异性指导分期。制定与绩
效有关的具体质量问题，我们应该

develop systems to reach that outcome consistently. What we will find, we
probably already know, is that what we want does not control what we get.
We all respond differently to the same stress based on the factors we have
discussed, which is why the principle of individuality controls periodization.
One major component of Matveyev’s model was to show that the
balancing act between work and recovery is the most crucial component of
adaptation. When you place a deadline on something, prioritizing rest feels
counterintuitive. Cunanan and colleagues (2018) state, “The scientific staging
for periodization was based on the thought that an athlete needs to receive an
optimal exercise or training stimulus balanced with appropriate unloading to
elicit favorable long-term training effects.” Taking time to promote recovery
by including designated rest weeks, or deload weeks, is central to
periodization to avoid the exhaustion phase to achieve adaptation (Cunanan
et al., 2018). Inter- and intrasession, microcycle, mesocycle, and macrocycle
rest are all based on the same rationale. Fatigue is what ultimately dictates the
outcome. The central piece of periodization is the constant management of
fitness based on accrued fatigue. We want to accomplish something specific,
but we all respond differently. Fatigue will happen; we just do not know how
much or when.

Overtraining Versus Undertraining
Can you train too much? Can you train too hard? Is too much or
too hard the product of not being adequately prepared for that
much stress at a given time?
The reality of the team setting is that all athletes have stressful
lives. The idea that an athlete’s life is controlled, almost sterile, is
a gross exaggeration. Athletes’ lives are jammed with stress
from competition, schoolwork, and personal life. Athletes are
great at compensating for all stress, but does that mean we
should compensate with the programming volume and intensity?
We can always take the approach of minimal effective dose
with volume or intensity. When in doubt, do less, but is that
enough? In a high-performance world, where the margins are

开发系统以持续实现该结果。 我们会发现，我们可能已经知道，我们
想要的并不能控制我们得到的。根据我们所讨论的因素，我们对相同压
力的反应不同，这就是个性原则控制周期的原因。
马特维耶夫模型的一个主要组成部分是表明工作和恢复之间的平衡行
为是适应的最关键组成部分。 当你为某件事设定最后期限时，优先考
虑休息感觉是违反直觉的。 Cunanan 及其同事（2018）指出，“周期化
的科学分期是基于这样的想法：运动员需要接受最佳的运动或训练刺激
，并与适当的卸载相平衡，以产生有利的长期训练效果。”通过指定休
息周或减负荷周来花时间促进恢复是周期化的核心，以避免疲劳阶段以
实现适应（Cunanan 等人，2018）。节间和节内、小周期、中周期和大
周期休息都基于相同的原理。疲劳最终决定了结果。 周期化的核心部
分是根据累积疲劳进行持续的健身管理。我们想要完成一些具体的事情
，但我们的反应各不相同。会发生疲劳；我们只是不知道有多少或何时
。

过度训练与训练不足
你能训练太多吗？你能训练得太刻苦吗？太多或太难是否是由于
在特定时间没有为如此大的压力做好充分准备而导致的？
球队环境的现实是所有运动员的生活都充满压力。认为运动员
的生活受到控制、几乎毫无生气的想法是一种严重的夸大其词。
运动员的生活充满了来自比赛、学业和个人生活的压力。 运动员
非常擅长补偿所有压力，但这是否意味着我们应该通过编程量和
强度来补偿？
我们总是可以采取体积或强度最小有效剂量的方法。 当有疑问
时，少做一点，但这就足够了吗？ 在一个高性能的世界里，利润
率很高

razor thin, can you risk not doing as much as possible? The
secret lies in the ability to make progress each week.
If we can make some progress from one microcycle to the
next, we are doing enough. The question then becomes, could
we have made more progress if we had done more? This is why
it is so important to track as much as possible. We are not just
trying to collect data to see outcomes but to determine norms.
One athlete’s antidote is another’s poison. We do not know
what is too much until after we learn what is too much. We do
not know what is too little until we establish norms and find
patterns. Too little stress is about finding statistical variances.
Understanding the line between overtraining and undertraining is
mostly gray and hard to define without information.
Leveraging as much volume and intensity as possible within a
training session, microcycle, and mesocycle is advantageous.
Overtraining is the product of understanding the upper limit of
stress while respecting the fact that the athletes will be in a good
place to handle that stress. The only way to know what is too
much or too little is to get as much information as possible.

Rule 3: Managing Fatigue
Since we do not know when someone will reach
fatigue, we need to organize variance with volume
and intensity ahead of time.
To plan for reduced volume or intensity is to understand the impact of stress
causing fatigue. One downside to a more linear approach is that we approach
fatigue more rapidly with more exposure to training over time. Another
approach is to oscillate volumes and intensities from one training block to
another (Poliquin, 1988)—the same concept, but a different cadence.
Undulating periodization is concentrated stress to create adaptation within

Do We Need Recovery Days?
One area we need to address with training is a recovery day.
The issue we run into is whether it is a huge waste of time. With
the athletes’ schedules being as full as they are, is it best to have
a day focused on recovery?
Recovery is a relative term to the state the athlete was in
before training. Each training session leaves a concentric circle
that makes the athlete different from before the training session.
The question then becomes, are we recovering from the training
session or trying to return to the state we were in before the
training session?
We will never be the person we were before the training
session. We probably won’t recover in time for the next training
session. The issue behind a recovery training session is that we
will never get what we want from it. The conquest of recovery is
a myth. What is not a myth is the value of time.
We tend to look at any time we have as sacred. Giving up a
day for rest is hard to do. But if all you were going to do on a day
was less volume, less intensity, and more recovery-based
modalities, then maybe it is better to give a rest day. The
emotional stress of having to go to the facility, get dressed, and
then foam roll and stretch is probably not worth it. Throw in a 6
a.m. group time, and you are eating into recovery.
A foundation of training is trust, which means that every day is
planned and orchestrated to the highest possible level. The
agreement between coach and athlete is that everything matters.
If you are programming, you have a responsibility to make every
day count. Taking an entire day dedicated to artificially creating
recovery is hoping to connect to a feeling experienced before
training, maybe is not as effective as taking the day off.
We should include methods such as soft tissue, flexibility,
mobility, and breathing work within training sessions. However,
having an entire session dedicated to recovery is a misuse of

我们需要恢复日吗？
我们需要通过培训解决的一个问题是恢复日。我们遇到的问题是
这是否是一种巨大的时间浪费。运动员的日程安排得这么满，是
不是最好有一天专注于恢复？
Recovery是与运动员训练前状态相对的术语。 每次训练都会
留下一个同心圆，让运动员与训练前有所不同。那么问题就变成
了，我们是从训练中恢复过来，还是试图回到训练前的状态？

我们永远不会是训练前的那个人。 我们可能无法及时恢复以参
加下一次训练。恢复训练背后的问题是我们永远无法从中得到我
们想要的东西。征服复苏是一个神话。时间的价值不是神话。
我们倾向于将任何时间视为神圣的。 放弃一天的休息是很难做
到的。但如果你一天要做的只是减少运动量、降低强度和更多基
于恢复的模式，那么也许最好休息一天。 必须去设施、穿好衣服
、然后进行泡沫轴滚压和伸展运动所带来的精神压力可能是不值
得的。 再加上早上 6 点的小组时间，你就开始恢复了。
培训的基础是信任，这意味着每一天都按照尽可能高的水平进
行计划和安排。 教练和运动员之间的共识是一切都很重要。如果
你正在编程，你就有责任让每一天都过得有意义。 花一整天的时
间来人为地进行恢复是希望与训练前的感觉联系起来，也许不如
休息一天那么有效。
我们应该在训练中纳入软组织、灵活性、活动性和呼吸等方法
。 然而，将整个会议专门用于恢复是一种滥用

time. It is better to manage workloads and instruct the athletes to
train as hard as possible. Managing stress is often more
productive than avoiding it over time. If you have a day when you
feel as though you cannot do something, give the athletes the
day off.
When we look at a macrocycle, we have to state the overall purpose of
training or the ultimate intended outcome. The macrocycle’s ultimate goal is
to peak in the quality that represents success in a particular sport. When we
set an ultimate goal, we are held to objectives that we must then meet to
accomplish that goal. We must break training into smaller increments to meet
the objective: a mesocycle. We can use the mesocycle to hit a particular
volume-to-intensity ratio that may not be the exact quality needed to be
successful but may position us to reach higher levels. A microcycle gives us
week-to-week periods to plan and subsequently adjust to stay on track to
meet the ultimate objective. The microcycle allows for microadjustments
such as a drop in volume, intensity, or frequency or an increase in rest. We
may need an early departure from a mesocycle focus to meet the timeline
predetermined before training.
The training session is what we have the most control over. The training
session is what determines the success of all the periods. A bad training
session is a concentric circle within the microcycle. A bad training session
comes down to either not being ready or doing too much for the athlete to
handle. Either scenario means one thing: excess fatigue. Managing this is
how we get the most out of the time we have. We manage what we can
control.

Rule 5: Training Integrity
Rep integrity, set integrity, and training session
integrity are the best means to controlling
complex systems outcomes.

时间。最好是管理工作量并指导运动员尽可能刻苦地训练。 随着
时间的推移，管理压力通常比避免压力更有效。如果有一天你觉
得自己做不了某件事，就给运动员放假。

当我们看待宏观周期时，我们必须说明培训的总体目的或最终预期结果
。宏观周期的最终目标是在特定运动中达到代表成功的质量顶峰。 当
我们设定最终目标时，我们就必须实现这些目标才能实现该目标。我们
必须将训练分成更小的增量来实现目标：中周期。 我们可以利用中循
环达到特定的体积与强度比率，这可能不是成功所需的确切质量，但可
能使我们达到更高的水平。微周期为我们提供了每周计划和随后调整的
时间，以保持正轨以实现最终目标。 微周期允许进行微调，例如降低
音量、强度或频率或增加休息时间。 我们可能需要尽早脱离中周期焦
点，以满足训练前预定的时间表。

培训课程是我们最能控制的。 训练课程决定了所有阶段的成功。 糟
糕的训练是微循环内的同心圆。 一次糟糕的训练归根结底是因为没有
做好准备，或者做得太多而让运动员无法应对。 这两种情况都意味着
一件事：过度疲劳。 管理这个是我们充分利用我们所拥有的时间的方
式。 我们管理我们能控制的事情。

规则 5：培训诚信
代表完整性、组数完整性和训练课程完整性是控制复杂
系统结果的最佳方法。

Training is a complex problem, not a complicated one. There is no way to
truly lay out an exact plan. Just because a problem is complex does not
change the intended outcome. A complicated plan has a lot of steps or
components with an actual pattern that we can replicate to get to an intended
outcome. In complex problems, a lack of patterns does not change the
outcome and thus the need for a logical plan. It means we need to rely more
on logic and reason to traverse an uncharted path. We need to rely on what
we can see as real. A good rep or set is our best means of handling a complex
system.
The macrocycle is the end of the marathon, the mesocycles are the
quarters, and the microcycle is the mile mark to assess pace. The unique thing
about this marathon is that we have no idea if we are running in the right
direction. So we need to break it up into miles to periodically assess if we are
running toward the destination. A good rep, set, and good training sessions
track the pace as we run this marathon. We do not know if we are making a
certain time without periodically assessing how fast we are running.
In reality, we do not know how imposing a specific stressor will manifest.
In response to that, we need to break up these intentional stressors to be able
to adjust accordingly toward a goal. Breaking up training sessions, sets, and
reps into smaller chunks does not change our ultimate goal. Having a plan
that is broken up into smaller, more manageable pieces means that the
outcome is still most important, but we are willing to adjust to meet that
purpose more efficiently. We do not know when our athletes will respond
poorly to a specific stress. A bad rep is our first indication of fatigue. A bad
set is a clearer picture of that fatigue. A bad training session is a problem in
ultimately reaching our training goal. Understanding the stress response
involves seeing the relatively short-term impact of something before making
a longer-term projection.

Rule 6: Periodization Versus Fatigue
Periodization matters more in advanced training
athletes, where fatigue is more of a determining
factor toward outcomes.

训练是一个复杂的问题，而不是一个复杂的问题。 没有办法真正制定
出准确的计划。 仅仅因为问题复杂并不会改变预期结果。 一个复杂的
计划有很多步骤或组件，具有实际的模式，我们可以复制它们以达到预
期的结果。 在复杂的问题中，缺乏模式不会改变结果，因此需要一个
逻辑计划。这意味着我们需要更多地依靠逻辑和理性来穿越未知的道路
。 我们需要依赖我们所看到的真实事物。良好的重复次数或组数是我
们处理复杂系统的最佳方法。
宏观周期是马拉松终点，中周期是四分之一，微周期是评估配速的里
程标记。这次马拉松的独特之处在于，我们不知道自己跑的方向是否正
确。因此，我们需要将其分解为里程，以定期评估我们是否正在朝着目
的地行驶。 当我们跑马拉松时，良好的代表、组数和良好的训练课程
可以跟踪我们的配速。如果不定期评估我们跑步的速度，我们不知道我
们是否达到了一定的时间。
事实上，我们不知道施加特定的压力源会如何表现。为了应对这一点
，我们需要打破这些有意的压力源，以便能够针对目标进行相应调整。
将训练课程、组数和重复次数分成更小的部分并不会改变我们的最终目
标。 将计划分解为更小、更易于管理的部分意味着结果仍然是最重要
的，但我们愿意进行调整以更有效地实现这一目标。 我们不知道我们
的运动员何时会对特定的压力反应不佳。不好的表现是我们疲劳的第一
个迹象。糟糕的组合更能清晰地体现出这种疲劳。糟糕的训练是最终达
到训练目标的一个问题。 了解压力反应包括在做出长期预测之前先了
解某件事的相对短期影响。

规则 6：分期与疲劳
周期对于高级训练运动员来说更为重要，因为疲劳更多
地是结果的决定因素。

Poliquin (1988) displayed that undulating sequences of volumes and
intensities for specific periods yield higher outcomes than a more linear
progression. Poliquin was referring to alternating these mesocycles to achieve
higher net outcomes and higher corresponding fitness–fatigue rates relative to
the specific application of volumes and intensities. This is more relevant to
athletes with higher training experience because fatigue is more manageable.
Novice athletes are developing biomechanics at a higher degree than
biomotor abilities and bioenergetic capacity, which are less regulated by
fatigue and motor learning. We can use a more linear approach with novice
athletes because it is less influenced by residual fatigue. Pretty much
anything works with younger athletes, so keeping it simple and allowing for
movement comprehension takes precedence.
With advanced athletes, we more genuinely try to peak for something
specific. At this point, we have established movement comprehension and
ability. The focal point shifts to leveraging those movements toward
something we want for their sport or position during competition. Classical
periodization uses the terms general and specific. With advanced athletes, for
periods of either higher volumes or intensities, the terms accumulation and
intensification are more appropriate. General is considered to focus on lower
intensities along with higher volumes and durations. This can create a
dichotomy in which higher volumes and longer durations are not specific to
anything. If the goal is more endurance, accumulation may be the SPP.
Conversely, specific is generally considered to focus on higher intensities and
lower volumes and durations. This can create an alternate dichotomy in
which higher intensities are always the specific outcome.
With advanced athletes, we are working in different contexts. They can
move, they understand, and we know more of what they need and less of
what they do not need. Adjusting the terminology to accumulation, where the
volumes are high, and intensification, where the intensities are high,
eliminates the dichotomy (figure 12.5). When we have the dichotomy of
specific always referencing intensity, we are, in a sense, trying to make a
complex problem complicated. The difference between the two is a clear
outcome; we create this preordained value on one quality over others, which

Poliquin (1988) 表明，特定时期的音量和强度的波动序列比更线性的进
展产生更高的结果。 Poliquin 指的是交替这些中周期，以实现更高的净
结果和相对于具体的训练量和强度应用而言更高的相应健身疲劳率。
这与训练经验较高的运动员更相关，因为疲劳更容易控制。新手运动员
正在比生物运动能力和生物能量能力发展更高程度的生物力学，而生物
运动能力和生物能量能力受疲劳和运动学习的调节较少。 我们可以对
新手运动员使用更线性的方法，因为它受残余疲劳的影响较小。 几乎
任何事情都适合年轻运动员，因此保持简单并考虑到动作理解是优先考
虑的。

对于高级运动员，我们会更真诚地尝试在特定的事情上达到顶峰。
至此，我们已经建立了动作理解和能力。 重点转移到利用这些动作来
实现我们想要的运动或比赛中的位置。 经典周期化使用术语 general 和
specific。对于高级运动员，对于较高训练量或强度的时期，术语
accumulation 和 intensification 更合适。 General 被认为专注于较低的强
度以及较高的训练量和持续时间。 这可能会造成一种二分法，即更高
的交易量和更长的持续时间并不特定于任何事物。 如果目标是更多的
耐力，积累可能就是SPP。相反，specific 通常被认为专注于更高的强度
和更低的训练量和持续时间。 这可以产生另一种二分法，其中更高的
强度始终是特定的结果。
对于高级运动员，我们在不同的环境下工作。 他们可以移动，他们
理解，我们更多地了解他们需要什么，更少了解他们不需要什么。将术
语调整为 accumulation（音量较高）和 intensification（强度较高），消
除了二分法（图 12.5）。 当我们有 specific 总是引用强度的二分法时，
从某种意义上说，我们试图使复杂的问题变得复杂。 两者之间的区别
是一个明显的结果；我们在一种品质上创造了这种注定的价值，而这种
品质超越了其他品质

is a mistake when dealing with complex problems. High intensity is not the
predetermined end for training programs. Training is not complicated; it is
complex, which is a large reason we need to shift from linear to undulating
periodization; for more advanced populations, what we end with matters.

Rule 7: Mesocycle Length
Mesocycle length is inversely proportional to
training age. Higher training age, shorter
mesocycles/lower
training
age,
longer
mesocycles.
The fatigue that corresponds to a specific stressor is not universal. We know
that focusing on intensification requires a longer recovery period.
Conversely, we know that focusing on accumulation requires fewer recovery
periods (Poliquin, 2013). As we explore how to most efficiently make it to a
targeted outcome, we need to acknowledge that the recovery process has a
significant impact on making it to point B as fast as we can. With the nervous
system being the relative focus in intensification blocks, we have to build in
periods where we can restore properly to reach a targeted outcome. With
advanced athletes, we will more than likely focus on nervous system
development, which will require more deload periods or rest. Or we can look
at the mesocycle length and regulate the stress we impose.
Traditionally, we control central nervous system fatigue by applying more
intramicrocycle recovery days, or low days, or dropping volume and
frequency for an entire microcycle. If we can layer in accumulation
mesocycles throughout a macrocycle, we can bypass or abbreviate the period
of recovery needed to reach the outcome. This is a central concept to shorter
mesocycles; we do not need to rest as much because lowering intensity is
rest. Instead of front-loading volume, we can use increased volume
concurrently, which organically lowers intensity to help someone who is on
an abbreviated timeline. The concept of undulating periodization looks at
qualities that we need to incorporate within a training cycle more effectively.

在处理复杂问题时是一个错误。 高强度并不是训练计划的预定目标。
训练并不复杂； 它很复杂，这是我们需要从线性周期转变为波动周期
的一个重要原因；对于更先进的人群来说，我们的结局很重要。

规则 7：中周期长度
Mesocycle length is inversely proportional to
training age. Higher training age, shorter
mesocycles/lower
training
age,
longer
mesocycles.
与特定压力源相对应的疲劳并不普遍。我们知道，专注于强化训练需要
更长的恢复期。相反，我们知道专注于积累需要更少的恢复期（Poliqui
n，2013）。当我们探索如何最有效地实现目标结果时，我们需要承认
恢复过程对于尽快到达 B 点具有重大影响。由于神经系统是强化训练中
的相对焦点，我们必须建立可以适当恢复的时期，以达到目标结果。
对于高级运动员，我们很可能会关注神经系统的发育，这将需要更多的
减负荷时间或休息。或者我们可以观察中循环长度并调节我们施加的压
力。

传统上，我们通过应用更多的微周期内恢复日或低日，或降低整个微
周期的训练量和频率来控制中枢神经系统疲劳。 如果我们能够在整个
宏观周期中分层积累中周期，我们就可以绕过或缩短达到结果所需的恢
复期。这是较短中周期的核心概念。 我们不需要那么多休息，因为降
低强度就是休息。 我们可以同时使用增加的音量，而不是预先加载音
量，这会自然地降低强度，以帮助时间较短的人。 波动周期的概念着
眼于我们需要更有效地融入训练周期的品质。

Accumulation is organically resting the central nervous system from
intensification. We can continuously train with high intensity with
intermittent breaks of high volumes for advanced athletes.
A deload week looks similar to what an accumulation microcycle may
look like. The only difference is that we are lowering volume or intensity to
peak within a mesocycle versus altering volume or intensity from one
mesocycle to the next. We can look at the overall distribution of qualities by
first examining which distributions garner the best overall outcome. For
instance, if someone wants to get faster, then higher volumes of faster
velocities must be used to reach that outcome. This is especially true if the
person is already developed in generating high amounts of force—the
distribution is shifted to a higher velocity. Before even looking at how we
will sequence training blocks to garner the highest peak in terms of velocity,
we need to accept that having a higher overall distribution of time allocated
to velocity, relatively speaking, compared to force or work, is necessary.

积累使中枢神经系统有机地休息，免于强化。 对于高级运动员，我们
可以持续进行高强度训练，并间歇性进行大量间歇性休息。
减载周看起来类似于积累微周期。唯一的区别是，我们在一个中周期
内将音量或强度降低到峰值，而不是从一个中周期到下一个周期改变音
量或强度。我们可以通过首先检查哪些分布获得最佳总体结果来查看质
量的总体分布。 例如，如果有人想要变得更快，那么必须使用更大的
量和更快的速度才能达到该结果。 如果人已经具备产生大量力量的能
力（分布会转移到更高的速度），则尤其如此。 在考虑如何对训练块
进行排序以获得速度方面的最高峰值之前，我们需要接受的是，相对而
言，与力或功相比，分配给速度的时间的总体分布更高是必要的。

FIGURE 12.5 Undulating adaptation response: intensification and
accumulation.
Organizing sets and reps in a training session is part of a larger, more
integrated framework. An approach of conjugate periodization, where we hit
all combinations of sets and reps in a training session, is a safe way to cover a
lot of bases. Alternatively, we can choose a concurrent approach, where we
prioritize a particular set and rep, specifically a quality, as a more aggressive
approach. This may play out in a year-round approach that garners a certain
level of performance in the training focus. A conjugate strategy that attempts
to hit higher intensities and higher volumes in every training session may
marginalize the level of results. A concurrent strategy may lead to increased
development in the qualities that were focused on in that training session.

FIGURE 12.6 Concurrent versus conjugate approaches.
By expanding these approaches in a nonlinear periodization model, we can

图 12.5 波动的适应反应：强化和积累。
在训练课程中组织组数和次数是更大、更综合框架的一部分。共轭周
期化方法是一种覆盖大量基础的安全方法，即我们在训练中进行所有组
数和次数的组合。 或者，我们可以选择一种并发方法，作为一种更积
极的方法，我们优先考虑特定的组数和次数，特别是质量。 这可能会
在全年的方法中发挥作用，在培训重点上获得一定水平的表现。尝试在
每次训练中达到更高强度和更高训练量的共轭策略可能会导致结果水平
边缘化。 并行策略可能会促进该培训课程中重点关注的素质的发展。

图 12.6 并发与共轭方法。
通过在非线性周期模型中扩展这些方法，我们可以

further examine the impact of either concurrent or conjugate (figure 12.6). A
conjugate approach is a year-round, daily nonlinear scheme. In the end, this
approach results in a general improvement in all aspects. A progression from
one training block to another will have little variance in their focuses other
than the exercises being used. The primary exercises will be either more
velocity or more force focused, and the secondary exercises will be more
work focused. With a concurrent approach, our task is block periodization
and timing of training blocks to create the highest functioning level of a
specific quality. If the desired quality is specifically velocity, force, or work,
it becomes a matter of determining which factors lead to the highest level of
that area.
We are typically working within a fixed timeline, which creates a paradox
in that we cannot simply focus on velocity; we need periods of restoration to
reach higher peaks. With a fixed timeline, spending time on recovery weeks
can feel counterproductive. Strategically using a lesser-intensity-oriented
block, accumulation within the macrocycle to elicit recovery is logistically
more efficient than front-loading volume and still having to use deload weeks
throughout the macrocycle. Using accumulation as a substitute for deload
microcycles is the most efficient use of time toward a goal with advanced
athletes.
With complex problems, there is no clear path, but with better indicators
of functioning levels at the onset, along with a clear vision of the future, we
can choose a better path. Undulating block periodization, in contrast with a
more linear model, creates better sequences of volume and intensity to reach
a designated outcome. We make a complex problem less complex by
understanding the endpoints. Starting with the end while appreciating that we
all start at different points means we can create a plan that is efficient and
adaptive. Undulating periodization allows us to leverage individual recovery
rates from similar stress to create the best overall sequence. For instance, if
we have a team of 50 people, we will have drastically different responses to
training. With undulating volume and intensity, we continuously focus on
developing advanced athletes by not having to back off in some way. We just
need to alter the mesocycle length to accommodate their rates of fatigue.
Accumulation–intensification–accumulation–intensification is also known

进一步检查并发或共轭的影响（图 12.6）。共轭方法是一种全年、每日
的非线性方案。 最终，这种方法导致各方面的普遍改善。从一个训练
块到另一个训练块的进展除了所使用的练习之外，其重点几乎没有变化
。 主要练习将更加注重速度或更加注重力量，而次要练习将更加注重
工作。 通过并发方法，我们的任务是训练块的块周期和计时，以创建
特定质量的最高功能水平。如果所需的质量具体是速度、力或功，那么
就需要确定哪些因素会导致该区域的最高水平。

我们通常在固定的时间范围内工作，这产生了一个悖论，因为我们不
能简单地关注速度；我们必须关注速度。我们需要恢复期才能达到更高
的顶峰。 在固定的时间表下，花时间在恢复周上可能会适得其反。 战
略上使用强度较低的区块，在宏观周期内进行积累以引发恢复在后勤上
比前期加载量更有效，并且在整个宏观周期中仍然需要使用减载周。
对于高级运动员来说，使用积累作为减负荷微循环的替代品是实现目标
的最有效的时间利用方式。
对于复杂的问题，没有明确的路径，但在开始时有更好的功能水平指
标，加上对未来的清晰愿景，我们可以选择更好的路径。 与更线性的
模型相比，波动块周期化可以创建更好的音量和强度序列以达到指定的
结果。 通过理解端点，我们可以使复杂的问题变得不那么复杂。从最
终开始，同时认识到我们都从不同的点开始意味着我们可以制定一个高
效且适应性强的计划。 波动的周期使我们能够利用相似压力下的个体
恢复率来创建最佳的整体序列。 例如，如果我们有一个 50 人的团队，
我们对培训的反应将会截然不同。 随着训练量和强度的变化，我们不
断专注于培养高级运动员，不必以某种方式退缩。我们只需要改变中循
环长度以适应它们的疲劳率。
积累-强化-积累-强化也称为

as working functional hypertrophy for 2 weeks, relative strength for 8 weeks,
hypertrophy for 2 weeks, followed by speed and strength for 4 weeks. By
lowering the mesocycle length and undulating the volume and intensity, we
can create higher outputs. That is the key behind periodization and rules.
While we understand that humans will respond uniquely to stress, we can still
create consistent progress toward a specific outcome. We can use a linear
model with a novice at the same time as an undulating model with an
advanced athlete. We can alter the mesocycle length for the advanced athlete
while maintaining a longer mesocycle length with a novice (figure 12.7). We
can accommodate various levels by making subtle adjustments to the
variables to create a periodization scheme that produces amazing results.
Programming becomes simply adjusting variables: frequency, rest, sets, reps,
TUT, velocity, and intensity for each individual.
In the team setting, a coach has very little autonomy in selecting the
frequency of training. In most situations, the decision of how many training
sessions a week is not in the hands of the strength coach. In the team setting,
we are better served by understanding how to leverage the frequency we have
and trying to get more by doing a good job.

工作功能性肥大持续 2 周，相对力量持续 8 周，肥大持续 2 周，然后是
速度和力量持续 4 周。 通过降低中循环长度并波动体积和强度，我们
可以创造更高的输出。 这是分期和规则背后的关键。虽然我们知道人
类会对压力做出独特的反应，但我们仍然可以朝着特定结果取得持续的
进展。 我们可以对新手使用线性模型，同时对高级运动员使用波动模
型。我们可以改变高级运动员的中周期长度，同时保持新手运动员更长
的中周期长度（图 12.7）。我们可以通过对变量进行微妙的调整来适应
不同的水平，以创建一个产生惊人结果的周期方案。编程变得简单地调
整变量：每个人的频率、休息、组数、次数、TUT、速度和强度。

在团队环境中，教练在选择训练频率方面几乎没有自主权。 在大多
数情况下，每周训练多少次的决定权不在力量教练手中。在团队环境中
，通过了解如何利用我们现有的频率并努力通过做好工作来获得更多，
我们会得到更好的服务。

Rule 8: Frequency and Recovery
Frequency is determined by what an athlete can
recover from.
The most important factor in deciding frequency is what the athlete can
recover from. The rate of decay of fitness relative to fatigue accumulation
determines adaptations. On average, the fitness effect from training lasts 3
days, while the fatigue effect lasts 1 day. As training frequency increases, the
residual impact of fatigue increases, leading to shorter fitness residuals.
Alternatively, if the frequency is too low, the residual impact of fitness is not
long enough to cause adaptation. This occurs because there are no additional
stressors to continuously drive adaptations; therefore, there is most certainly a
sweet spot for training frequency.

图 12.7 中周期长度。

规则 8：频率和恢复
频率取决于运动员可以从中恢复的程度。

决定频率的最重要因素是运动员可以从中恢复什么。 体能相对于疲劳
累积的衰减率决定了适应性。 平均而言，训练的健身效果持续3天，疲
劳效果持续1天。随着训练频率的增加，疲劳的残余影响也会增加，从
而导致体能残差缩短。或者，如果频率太低，适应性的残余影响就不足
以引起适应。发生这种情况是因为没有额外的压力源来持续推动适应；
因此，训练频率肯定有一个最佳点。

Understanding the end goal and what is going on holistically makes a huge
difference in how many training sessions can occur. We have some models to
leverage in evaluating optimal frequency with different strength events. With
bodybuilding, there are two ends of the spectrum. On one end is highintensity training, which trains a body part once every 7 to 10 days. On the
other end is a split routine, which trains a body part a day, leading to that
muscle being stressed once every 3 to 5 days. Schoenfield and colleagues
(2016) demonstrated that increased frequency led to increases in crosssectional area relative to low frequency.
We want to use various stressors within the body that will drive
adaptation. Training may be perceived as a stressor, but as discussed in other
sections and the concept of hormesis, the difference between an antidote and
a poison lies in the dosage. The minimum effective dose (MED) is the least
amount of something required to elicit the desired change. In terms of
frequency, MED is an important concept to understand before determining
whether something is too much or too little.
To determine the MED, we need to know what change we desire. Dosage
being too much or too little is easily seen by adverse effects from the
proposed intervention. However, we can determine if something was a
necessary undertaking only if we fully understand what we are trying to
accomplish. If we can accomplish a goal with less overall time or work, why
would we not take that option? MED is only a good concept if it reaches the
targeted outcome. If the frequency is too low, there is a risk of too little
stress, and MED becomes insufficient.
One variable that must be evaluated is the construct of increasing
frequency: Why is it necessary in the first place? Schoenfield and colleagues
(2015) state, “Well-trained individuals benefit from including periods of
training muscle groups 3 days per week when the goal is to maximize muscle
hypertrophy.” They also note that increasing frequency did not have the same
positive effect on increased hypertrophy with novice or less experienced
lifters. We need to evaluate how we can make a greater impact on lifters of
various training ages. If we can accomplish similar results with fewer total
training sessions, we should take that option. It is worth noting that
Schoenfield and colleagues’ results indicate increased cross-sectional muscle

了解最终目标以及整体上正在发生的事情对于可以进行多少次培训课
程有着巨大的影响。我们有一些模型可以用来评估不同强度事件的最佳
频率。对于健美运动来说，有两个极端。 一方面是高强度训练，每 7
到 10 天训练一次身体部位。 另一端是分次训练，每天训练身体的一个
部位，导致该肌肉每 3 到 5 天受到一次压力。 Schoenfield 及其同事（2
016）证明，相对于低频，频率的增加会导致横截面积的增加。

我们希望利用体内的各种压力源来推动适应。训练可能被视为一种压
力源，但正如其他部分和毒物兴奋效应概念中所讨论的那样，解毒剂和
毒药之间的区别在于剂量。 最小有效剂量 (MED) 是引起所需变化所需
的最小剂量。 就频率而言，MED 是在确定某物是否过多或过少之前需
要了解的一个重要概念。
为了确定 MED，我们需要知道我们想要什么改变。剂量过多或过少
很容易通过所提出的干预措施的不利影响看出。 然而，只有当我们完
全理解我们想要完成的任务时，我们才能确定某件事是否是一项必要的
任务。如果我们可以用更少的总时间或工作来实现一个目标，为什么我
们不采取这个选择呢？ MED 只有达到目标结果才是一个好概念。 如果
频率太低，则存在压力太小的风险，并且 MED 变得不足。
必须评估的一个变量是增加频率的结构：为什么它首先是必要的？ S
choenfield 及其同事（2015）指出，“当目标是最大限度地增加肌肉肥
大时，训练有素的人会受益于每周 3 天的肌肉群训练。”他们还指出，
对于新手或经验不足的举重运动员来说，增加频率对于增加肌肥大并没
有同样的积极作用。 我们需要评估如何对不同训练年龄的举重运动员
产生更大的影响。 如果我们可以用更少的总训练次数来实现类似的结
果，我们应该采取这种选择。 值得注意的是，Schoenfield 及其同事的
结果表明横截面肌肉增加

area and are not specific to increased speed and power, which may need less
frequency (de Villarreal et al., 2008).
We have to evaluate the relative intensity with which we train before we
can determine an ideal frequency. It may seem obvious, but increased
training frequency results in a greater fatigue effect. The relative fatigue
impact is greater when you combine increased frequency with higher
intensities (Busso et al., 2002). There are innumerable methods to assess
intensity, but in this context, acute-to-chronic ratios fit best. Gabbett (2016)
developed acute-to-chronic ratios to create a metric to assess relative
workloads for the athlete. The primary reason this was created was to prevent
injury and to optimize workload progressions from week to week.
Workload is assessed by assessing the rating of perceived exertion on a
modified Borg Scale (1-10) multiplied by minutes of activity (Gabbett, 2016;
see figure 4.8 on page 64). The acute workload is heavily weighted by the
overall perceived intensity and then multiplied by minutes of work. It is even
more weighted by increased frequency. An intense individual workout
performed every 72 to 96 hours would pale in comparison to a moderate
workout performed daily in terms of acute workloads. The ratio of acute to
chronic creates an optimal ratio to work within to achieve optimal
adaptations. The optimal ratio discussed by Gabbett was 0.8 to 1.3. When we
have a significant spike in acute workload because of increased frequency,
we risk overfatiguing the athlete and subsequent injury. And there is the
trade-off. Increased frequency may be a more efficient path to results, but at
the same time, it may increase relative risk.
The final component to discuss with frequency is what increasing it does
to the potential output. Timothy Noakes and colleagues (2001) created the
central governor model, which evaluates intensity relative to an athlete’s
training frequency. As the duration of an activity increases, the potential
intensity drops. The same can be said with frequency. With increased
frequency, residual fatigue builds up and lowers the potential output in future
workouts. The central governor model becomes lowered in response to
increased fatigue to protect itself. At a certain point, increasing frequency
becomes impossible. The drop in intensity to accommodate the fatigue
buildup becomes the only means to make it through a microcycle. The focus

面积，并且不特定于增加速度和功率，这可能需要更少的频率（de Villa
rreal 等，2008）。
在确定理想的频率之前，我们必须评估训练的相对强度。 这似乎是
显而易见的，但增加训练频率会导致更大的疲劳效应。 当您将增加的
频率与较高的强度结合起来时，相对疲劳的影响会更大（Busso et al., 20
02）。 评估强度的方法有无数种，但在这种情况下，急性与慢性比率
最适合。 Gabbett（2016）开发了急性与慢性比率来创建评估运动员相
对工作量的指标。这样做的主要原因是为了防止受伤并优化每周的工作
量进展。
工作量的评估方法是评估改良博格量表 (1-10) 的感知劳累等级乘以活
动分钟数（Gabbett，2016 年；参见第 64 页的图 4.8）。 剧烈的工作量
很大程度上取决于总体感知强度，然后乘以工作时间。随着频率的增加
，它的权重甚至更大。 就剧烈工作负荷而言，每 72 至 96 小时进行一
次高强度的个人锻炼与每天进行的中等锻炼相比显得苍白无力。 急性
与慢性的比例创造了一个最佳的工作比例，以实现最佳的适应。 Gabbet
t 讨论的最佳比率是 0.8 至 1.3。当我们因频率增加而导致急性工作量大
幅增加时，我们就有可能使运动员过度疲劳并随后受伤。 这是需要权
衡的。增加频率可能是获得结果的更有效途径，但同时，它可能会增加
相对风险。
讨论频率的最后一个因素是增加频率对潜在输出的影响。 Timothy N
oakes 及其同事（2001）创建了中央调节器模型，该模型评估相对于运
动员训练频率的强度。 随着活动持续时间的增加，电位强度会下降。
频率也是如此。 随着频率的增加，残余疲劳会累积并降低未来锻炼的
潜在输出。 为了应对保护自身的疲劳增加，中央调速模型会降低。 在
某一点上，增加频率就变得不可能了。 为了适应疲劳累积而降低强度
成为度过微循环的唯一方法。焦点

transitions from adapting to surviving.
Training frequency has a sweet spot. It is not a matter of doing too much
or too little; it is a matter of whether we made the mark. Above all else,
training is meant to accomplish something. Too many concepts, like
frequency, become more a part of the objective than the actual outcome. The
variables that affect frequency are more important than the number itself.
There is a rationale for training with more or less frequency, but it is
predicated on the variables associated with the athlete. Making the athlete
better is the goal. From there, you reverse engineer the optimal frequency to
best meet that outcome. That frequency is ultimately determined by what the
athlete can recover from.
To appreciate frequency, we must first understand the outliers and the
rationale behind that frequency when choosing to subject our athletes to it. If
you calculate the number of sessions in a week, you can get a raw score of
frequency. This is important because it leads to increased acute workload
scores. Abadjiev (Kraemer, Fry, Zatsiorsky, 2020) with the Bulgarian
national team reached a frequency of 28 to 30, which is an example of the
upper limit or an outlier in terms of frequency. The acute load behind that
frequency is significantly above what is normal, which raises the question of
why a frequency like this would be used.

从适应到生存的转变。
训练频率有一个最佳点。这不是做得太多或太少的问题；而是做得太
多或做得太少的问题。 问题在于我们是否取得了成功。 最重要的是，
培训是为了完成某些事情。 太多的概念，比如频率，更多地成为目标
的一部分，而不是实际结果。影响频率的变量比数字本身更重要。或多
或少的训练频率是有道理的，但它取决于与运动员相关的变量。 让运
动员变得更好是我们的目标。从那里，您可以对最佳频率进行逆向工程
，以最好地满足该结果。该频率最终取决于运动员可以从中恢复的情况
。
要了解频率，我们在选择让运动员接受该频率时，必须首先了解异常
值和该频率背后的基本原理。如果计算一周内的会话次数，您可以获得
频率的原始分数。 这很重要，因为它会导致急性工作负荷分数增加。
保加利亚国家队的阿巴德吉耶夫（Kraemer、Fry、Zatsiorsky，2020）达
到了 28 到 30 次的频率，这是频率上限或异常值的一个例子。 该频率
背后的急性负载明显高于正常负载，这就提出了为什么要使用这样的频
率的问题。

FIGURE 12.8 Adaptation window.
The rationale behind this logic is that sessions that maximize anabolic
hormones need to be brief (under 45 min) but intense (figure 12.8) (Komi,
2008). Poliquin (2013) seconded that notion by stating that training sessions
should not surpass 60 min to support anabolic pathways. This creates a
criterion to investigate. If we do 1 h training sessions daily, what is the
systemic impact compared to 2 h sessions?
This is why it is important to investigate acute-to-chronic workloads.
There needs to be a way to quantify the workload with a broader perspective.
Considering the workloads compared to the performance of each session
through metrics like tonnage or velocity can help assess the quality of
increased frequency versus duration. Understanding the point of training
gives some credence to the decision to go longer per session or shorter with
an increased frequency of training sessions. It becomes rather simple: If
acute-to-chronic workloads fall outside the range of 0.8 to 1.3 week-to-week
changes, it is either too much or too little. Additionally, if week-to-week
progress is not being made in terms of progressive overload, it could be that
the stimulus was simply too much.
When looking at training outcomes, an unavoidable truth is that we need
to accumulate a certain amount of stimulus to reach a specific outcome.
Standards regarding tonnage must be hit to be an international-level lifter
(Verkhoshansky, 2019). The aggregate total of all the weight lifted over a
career manifests in better performances during competitions. This is not an
uncommon thought process; we often see it in distance events, such as
swimming or running. In a way, it is a similar mindset to the 10,000-hour rule
(Gladwell, 2011). It is a tempting thought that anyone can be great at
something as long as they commit a certain number of hours and persevere.
The 10,000-hour rule, or any focus on reaching incredible tonnages or
mileages, is an example of causation and correlation. The concept that
becoming the best in the world in anything is the product of just reaching a
certain number of hours is not entirely true. Some patterns and sequences are
simply superior to others. Range (Epstein, 2019) made an argument against
early specialization. In a sense, you can look at early specialization as a

图 12.8

适应窗口。

这一逻辑背后的基本原理是，最大化合成代谢激素的疗程需要简短（
45 分钟以下）但强度大（图 12.8）（Komi，2008）。 Poliquin (2013)
支持这一观点，指出训练时间不应超过 60 分钟以支持合成代谢途径。
这创建了一个调查标准。 如果我们每天进行 1 小时的训练，与 2 小时
的训练相比，系统性影响如何？
这就是为什么研究急性到慢性工作负载很重要。需要有一种方法以更
广泛的视角来量化工作量。通过吨位或速度等指标将工作负载与每个会
话的性能进行比较，有助于评估增加的频率与持续时间的质量。 了解
训练的要点可以为每次训练时间更长或随着训练频率增加而缩短训练时
间的决定提供一定的可信度。 事情变得相当简单：如果急性到慢性工
作负载的每周变化超出 0.8 到 1.3 的范围，则要么太多，要么太少。 此
外，如果在渐进式超负荷方面每周都没有取得进展，则可能是刺激措施
太多了。

在审视训练结果时，一个不可避免的事实是，我们需要积累一定量的
刺激才能达到特定的结果。要成为国际水平的举重运动员，必须达到吨
位标准（Verkhoshansky，2019）。 职业生涯中举起的所有重量的总和
体现在比赛中更好的表现。 这并不是一个罕见的思维过程。 我们经常
在游泳或跑步等长距离比赛中看到它。在某种程度上，它与 10,000 小时
规则类似（Gladwell，2011）。 这是一个诱人的想法，只要投入一定的
时间并坚持不懈，任何人都可以在某件事上取得出色的成绩。
10,000 小时规则，或者任何关注达到令人难以置信的吨位或里程的规
则，都是因果关系和相关性的一个例子。 认为在任何事情上成为世界
上最好的人都是达到一定时间的结果的想法并不完全正确。有些模式和
序列比其他模式和序列更优越。 Range（Epstein，2019）提出了反对早
期专业化的论点。 从某种意义上说，您可以将早期专业化视为

means to begin the ascent to achieve the levels described. Epstein showed
that it is less a matter of what amounts someone reaches and more a matter of
how and when they did what they did.
The principle of critical drop-off states that every training session has a
point at which it is no longer effective. What Abadjiev (Kraemer, Fry,
Zatsiorsky, 2020) and Poliquin (2013) were trying to say is that a session has
a certain length of time before critical drop-off takes effect. An interesting
perspective in weightlifting is Prilepin’s chart (figure 12.9), which was an
attempt to find the most effective volume in each intensity bracket
(Verkhoshansky, 2019). Epstein suggests that certain events in training can
have a more significant impact and can fast-track progress toward a goal. The
concept in Range and Sports Gene was based on “chunking” an activity that
promotes accelerated learning and development (Epstein, 2019). Critical
drop-off ensures we stay in the zone of accelerated development longer,
which was the point of Prilepin’s chart.
What we understand from critical drop-off is that teaching must be based
on the fitness of an individual and their level of fatigue. This matters because
when attempting to reach more intense levels to expedite the process, low
levels of fitness and high levels of fatigue make the drop-off occur faster.
Staying within the zone with the highest yield is about being conscious of the
current function level. The relative effects of a longer workout or a shorter
workout broken up into a higher frequency need to be considered. The
question becomes not how many training sessions someone should do, but
how many quality sessions they can do.
There is no one frequency for everyone. There are so many different
variables to account for, which makes a one-size-fits-all approach impossible.
The optimal frequency is the one at which the athlete can sustain the highest
output possible throughout the entire workout. When the athlete recovers,
that is the appropriate time to train again. This is not an easy thing to figure
out; it takes time to get to know the acute-to-chronic workloads, wellness,
internal and external markers of performance, outcomes, and motivation of
the athlete. The bottom line is that when deciding how many times to train
someone, you have to understand the relative impact frequency may have on
the individual. Fighting every urge to say that more sessions will be better,

意味着开始上升以达到所描述的水平。 爱泼斯坦表明，问题不在于某
人达到了多少，而在于他们如何以及何时做他们所做的事情。
临界下降原则指出，每次训练都有一个不再有效的点。 Abadjiev (Kr
aemer, Fry, Zatsiorsky, 2020) 和 Poliquin (2013) 试图说的是，在关键下降
生效之前，会话有一定的时间长度。 举重运动中一个有趣的观点是 Pril
epin 的图表（图 12.9），该图表试图找到每个强度等级中最有效的训练
量（Verkhoshansky，2019）。 爱泼斯坦认为，训练中的某些事件可以
产生更重大的影响，并且可以快速实现目标。 Range 和 Sports Gene 中
的概念基于“分块”一项促进加速学习和发展的活动（Epstein，2019）
。 关键的下降确保我们在加速发展区域停留的时间更长，这就是普里
莱平图表的要点。

我们从临界下降中了解到，教学必须基于个人的健康状况和疲劳程度
。这很重要，因为当试图达到更高强度的水平以加快这一过程时，低体
能水平和高疲劳水平会使下降速度更快。 Staying within the zone with the
highest yield is about being conscious of the current function level. 需要考
虑较长时间锻炼或较短时间锻炼分解为较高频率的相对影响。 问题不
是一个人应该参加多少次培训课程，而是他们可以参加多少次高质量的
培训课程。
没有一种频率适合每个人。 有太多不同的变量需要考虑，这使得一
刀切的方法不可能实现。最佳频率是运动员在整个锻炼过程中能够维持
尽可能最高输出的频率。 当运动员康复时，就是再次训练的适当时机
。 这并不是一件容易弄清楚的事情； 了解运动员从急性到慢性的工作
负荷、健康状况、表现、结果和动机的内部和外部标记需要时间。 最
重要的是，在决定培训某人多少次时，您必须了解频率可能对个人产生
的相对影响。 抵制每一次说更多的会议会更好的冲动，

we need to focus on what is important: the constraints on your program
combined with the functional needs of the athlete.
The easiest way to describe the relationship between sets and reps is that
they are inversely proportional to each other. The more repetitions we ask of
a single set, the fewer total sets we can perform. Alternatively, the fewer
repetitions, which automatically raise the intensity, the greater the number of
sets that can be performed. As we will explore, there are numerous reasons
more sets may be performed versus more repetitions.

The important question to ask is, why would we need more repetitions or
increased intensity and, subsequently, more sets? Selecting a target makes a

描述组数和次数之间关系的最简单方法是它们彼此成反比。我们要求
单组重复的次数越多，我们能完成的总组数就越少。 或者，重复次数
越少（会自动提高强度），可以执行的组数就越多。 正如我们将探讨
