要问的重要问题是，为什么我们需要更多的重复或增加强度，以及随后
的更多组数？ 选择一个目标可以使

significant difference in the allocation we give to volume and intensity
dispersed through a prescribed set and rep scheme. Tonnage, the aggregate of
volume and intensity in a training session, is a meaningless number unless we
know how we got there. If we squatted 1 lb every 30 s for 12 h every day,
every week, every month, every year, every decade, it would be meaningless.
It would not be intense enough and would take too long to achieve results.
The allocation of sets and reps is the way to optimize the distribution of
tonnage. If we want to increase someone’s force-generating capability, we
want increased intensity—fewer reps and increased sets. If we want to
increase work capacity, we want increased duration or repetitions—lower
intensity and fewer sets. Leveraging a certain number of sets or reps garners a
targeted outcome that gets to the desired outcome faster.
A threshold needs to be reached with intensity to make changes. That
threshold is different based on training experience. Kraemer (2020) noted that
80% of a subject’s one rep maximum is needed to reach any neural
adaptations. Alternatively, novice lifters can reach positive neural adaptations
with much less intensity, such as 60% of a subject’s one rep max. We know
that a percentage leads to a different repetition amount that we can
theoretically accomplish. Advanced trainees need higher intensities, so they
will need more sets to accomplish change. Conversely, novice trainees who
don’t need as high an intensity will require increased reps to accomplish
change.
Another component to consider when allocating sets and reps is the
number of exercises in a training session. There is a finite amount of time a
training session should last. The addition of sets in one exercise by default
means there will be either fewer exercises or fewer sets of other exercises.
This is a paradox with athletics. On the one hand, athletes need more exercise
to meet the complex demands of their sport (Poliquin, 2013). On the other
hand, athletes need more sets to make both neural and tissue adaptations
(Kreiger, 2010). The irony is that anyone who has ever worked in athletics
knows that time is extremely limited.
There is an obvious benefit to increasing sets of anything. Kreiger (2010)
showed that increasing sets, from three to six, was effective for both trained
and untrained lifters. Kraemer (2020) further supports increasing sets as a

我们通过规定的组数和次数方案分配的训练量和强度存在显着差异。吨
位是训练中训练量和强度的总和，除非我们知道我们是如何达到目标的
，否则它是一个毫无意义的数字。 如果我们每天、每周、每月、每年
、每十年每30秒深蹲1磅，持续12小时，那就毫无意义了。它的强度不
够，而且需要很长时间才能取得成果。组数和次数的分配是优化吨位分
配的方法。 如果我们想提高某人的力量产生能力，我们需要增加强度
——更少的次数和更多的组数。 如果我们想提高工作能力，我们需要
增加持续时间或重复次数——降低强度和减少组数。利用一定数量的组
数或重复次数可以获得有针对性的结果，从而更快地达到预期结果。

需要达到一个阈值，强度才能做出改变。 该阈值根据训练经验而不
同。 Kraemer (2020) 指出，受试者需要完成一次最大重复次数的 80% 才
能达到任何神经适应。或者，新手举重运动员可以以低得多的强度达到
积极的神经适应，例如受试者一次最大重复次数的 60%。我们知道，百
分比会导致我们理论上可以完成的不同重复次数。 高级学员需要更高
的强度，因此他们需要更多组数来完成改变。 相反，不需要那么高强
度的新手学员将需要增加次数来完成改变。

分配组数和次数时要考虑的另一个因素是训练中的练习数量。 培训
课程的持续时间是有限的。 默认情况下，在一项练习中添加组数意味
着练习数量会减少，或者其他练习的组数也会减少。这是田径运动的一
个悖论。一方面，运动员需要更多的锻炼来满足运动的复杂需求（Poliq
uin，2013）。 另一方面，运动员需要更多组数来进行神经和组织适应
（Kreiger，2010）。 具有讽刺意味的是，任何从事过田径运动的人都
知道时间极其有限。
增加任何东西的数量都有明显的好处。 Kreiger（2010）表明，将组
数从三组增加到六组，对于受过训练和未经训练的举重运动员来说都是
有效的。 Kraemer（2020）进一步支持增加集合作为

superior strategy for increasing strength when comparing two to three sets
with both novice and experienced trainees. There is a functional need to work
with athletes to increase the number of sets, but that may come at the expense
of accomplishing all the exercises needed. This creates a question of which is
more important.
Again, it comes down to the goal. We know that increasing strength
requires more total sets. The same is true for increasing speed and power.
However, increases in muscular size are the product of increased work, the
outcome of increased repetitions (Kramer, 2020). As with strength and
power, an increased number of sets for higher work rep schemes garners
better results (Craig & Kang, 1994). The need is based on how significant
increasing muscular size is to the overall outcome. We can achieve increases
in muscular size with fewer sets as long as the repetitions are increased.
There will always be a necessary trade-off between how many sets and the
number of repetitions or amount of exercises one can do. The answer to the
question is simply, what is more important?
Ostrowski and colleagues (1997) showed that higher set routines were
more effective for lower body exercises, showing a 7.5% strength increase in
lower set routines and an 11.9% strength increase in higher set routines. The
same was not true for upper body exercises, where lower set routines resulted
in a 4% strength increase versus a 1.9% strength increase for higher set
routines. The difference in necessary sets for the lower body is a more
important consideration than for upper body exercises; this helps
tremendously with the organization of a workout. The trade-off for the
number of exercises we can do is offset by prioritizing higher sets for lower
body exercises and fewer sets for upper body exercises. In this, we can reach
the necessary vectors, planes, and structural balance needed for a sound
program and the necessary volume for each.
The inverse relationship between sets and reps is a naturally occurring
aspect of all programs. It has a wrinkle: We need to account for the number
of exercises we need to accomplish. By understanding the inverse nature of
increasing mechanical stress through increased work versus more neural
impact through increased intensity, the program organically falls into either
increased sets or increased reps. The outcome dictates the intervention, the

当与新手和经验丰富的受训者进行两到三组比较时，这是增加力量的优
越策略。与运动员合作增加组数是一种功能上的需要，但这可能是以完
成所有所需练习为代价的。这就产生了一个问题，哪个更重要。
再说一次，这取决于目标。 我们知道，增加力量需要更多的总组数
。 提高速度和功率也是如此。然而，肌肉尺寸的增加是工作量增加的
结果，是重复次数增加的结果（Kramer，2020）。 与力量和力量一样
，增加组数以实现更高的工作次数计划可以获得更好的结果（Craig & K
ang，1994）。 需求取决于增加肌肉尺寸对整体结果的显着程度。只要
增加重复次数，我们就可以用更少的组数来增加肌肉的大小。一个人可
以做的组数和重复次数或练习量之间总是存在必要的权衡。 这个问题
的答案很简单，什么更重要？

Ostrowski 及其同事 (1997) 表明，较高组数的训练对下半身锻炼更有
效，较低组数的训练强度增加了 7.5%，较高组数的训练强度增加了 11.
9%。对于上半身训练来说情况并非如此，较低组数的训练可以增加 4%
的力量，而较高组数的训练则可以增加 1.9% 的力量。 与上半身练习相
比，下半身所需组数的差异是更重要的考虑因素； 这对锻炼的组织有
很大帮助。 我们可以进行的练习数量的权衡可以通过优先进行下半身
练习的较高组数和上半身练习的较少组数来抵消。在此，我们可以达到
声音程序所需的必要矢量、平面和结构平衡以及每个必要的音量。

组数和次数之间的反比关系是所有计划中自然发生的一个方面。 它
有一个问题：我们需要考虑需要完成的练习数量。 通过了解通过增加
运动来增加机械压力与通过增加强度来增加神经影响的相反性质，该计
划有机地分为增加组数或增加次数。 结果决定了干预措施

driving force behind selecting any set and rep scheme.
What if you knew that the number on a roulette wheel would win? Would
you put all your money on that exact number, or would you hedge your bets
and attempt to increase your odds of winning? In truth, we take the approach
of hedging our bets in training all the time. We match uncertainty with an
approach of distributing time over several exercises or even diverse sets and
rep schemes. We may know exactly what that person needs to reach a goal,
but we struggle with committing to that based on the fear of not doing
enough.
With team sports, we need to address a variety of different planes and
vectors in training. We do this with a wide range of exercises in those planes
and vectors. By default, with more exercises, we cannot commit to more sets
of any particular exercise within a single training session. The commitment to
a large array of exercises in a single training session becomes the focus. This
does not have to be at the expense of performance in any of those exercises.
Less saturation of volume or intensity with a particular exercise will lead to
diminished ability in that exercise. The relative impact of acumen in a
specific exercise is less than having adequate stress in a proprioceptive-rich
environment. The strategy of how we load more diverse exercises needs to be
carefully considered to accommodate less time allocated to each exercise.
A really important factor for team setting training is the inclusion of
power, speed, and change of direction work. Stress is stress. We need to
appreciate that we cannot just lock in on training in the weight room. If we
are adding, doing so only in the weight room will do a great disservice to our
athletes. Evaluating the overall stress from training is important. We need to
look at workloads from sprinting, change of direction, plyometrics, and work
in the weight room as an aggregate. If we accumulate too much, whether it is
inside or outside, it’s too much.
Increasing sets has the same potential to improve quality as it does with
tonnage. What becomes apparent is that we want to increase stress through
intensity, reps, TUT, or rest, but there is a point of diminishing returns over
time. We can increase reps and TUT, or we can decrease rest when we want
to increase volume within an accumulation block. As we manage this
increase in volume or density, it becomes harder to manage if we are

在团队运动中，我们需要在训练中处理各种不同的平面和向量。我们

团队训练的一个真正重要的因素是包括力量、速度和改变方向的工作
。 压力就是压力。 我们需要认识到，我们不能只专注于举重室的训练

的伤害。评估训练的总体压力很重要。我们需要将短跑、变向、增强式
训练和举重室训练的工作量作为一个整体来看待。如果我们积累太多，
无论是内在还是外在，那就太多了。
增加组数与增加吨位具有相同的提高质量的潜力。 显而易见的是，
我们希望通过强度、次数、TUT 或休息来增加压力，但随着时间的推移
，效果会出现递减点。我们可以增加次数和 TUT，或者当我们想要增加
累积块内的训练量时，我们可以减少休息。 当我们管理体积或密度的
增加时，如果我们

allocating stress within a limited number of sets. The longer the individual set
is, the harder it is to manage. To get the most from accumulation blocks,
increasing the number of sets is superior to increasing the length of each set.
Breaking down the total volume, or TUT, within a session, if we accrue
the same amount in a session, does it matter if it is in fewer or more sets? Is it
a question of how we can increase sets in a fixed session length? The best
way to accomplish this is with antagonist pairings, supersetting a push with a
pull in the form of a lower-lower pairing or an upper-lower pairing. We
cannot add more time, but we can make the most of the time we have. We
need a certain amount of time to recover from a specific exercise. To increase
the volume or density of work, we pair exercises that do not impede the
quality of each set.
A 1 h training session typically allows for 20 total sets. If the intensity
goes up, the volume will go down, but the rest needed will increase. If the
intensity goes down, the volume will go up, but the rest needed will decrease.
Greater intensity results in more nervous system stress, which makes the time
allocated in a training session greater for recovery between sets. Greater
volume results in more mechanical stress, which makes the total time
allocated in a training session greater for work. Twenty sets is the median
between higher intensity, higher volume, or moderate volume, moderate
intensity training sessions.
Knowing the winner and betting all your chips on a single number is the
same thing as saying, I know what will have the biggest net impact, and I can
allocate all my training toward a specific focus. Hedging bets when you are
uncertain is the same as saying we are going to do a little bit of everything.
There will be situations where you can zero in on an objective; in that case,
put all focus on a particular area without hesitation. Alternatively, there are
situations where there are so many possible ways to go that it is best to just
distribute training time toward intensity and volume. The rationale that one is
better is misleading; one is just not as impactful relative to the goal.
Organizing training by overall outcome makes programming sets and reps
a matter of prioritization. The trade-off between the amount of volume we
can achieve by increasing the number of sets or vice versa is rationalized by
what we want to achieve and how much we understand what is correlated. A

可以将目标归零； 在这种情况下，请毫不犹豫地将所有注意力集中在
某个特定领域。 或者，在某些情况下，有多种可能的方法，因此最好
将训练时间分配给强度和训练量。认为一个人更好的理由是一种误导；
一个只是相对于目标而言没有那么有影响力。
按总体结果组织培训使编程组和重复次数成为优先事项。 我们可以
通过增加组数来实现的训练量之间的权衡，反之亦然，这取决于我们想
要实现的目标以及我们对相关内容的理解程度。一个

training session that spends more time performing work, increasing sets with
higher intensity, or using more or fewer exercises all have an impact on the
end goal. An inventory of what is needed, along with what is correlated,
gives direction in selecting the appropriate distribution of sets and reps within
a training session and subsequent training block.

Rule 10: Randomness and Training Predictability
The more random the environment, the more
diversity we need with our training program.
In an Olympic-style sport, where there is a narrow and focused requirement,
we can shrink the exercise inventory down. For an Olympic athlete or a
strength sports athlete, the events they need to prepare for are limited in
number. They are extremely focused. This focus limits the diversity of
exercises needed because of the reduced variety or randomness of their sport.
The drop in the number of exercises needed can lead to an increased number
of sets for those exercises. This leads to developing more correlated
exercises, more associated with performance. Committing as much time as
possible to one exercise leads to increased performance in that exercise,
which makes evaluating whether it is valuable extremely important.
Developing the wrong quality relative to performance with increased sets can
be as counterproductive as productive if it is the correct exercise.
We are driving adaptation in 1 h increments. We cannot add time, but we
can manage the time we have better. If we know we need less variation of
exercises for cyclic sports, we can spend more time with fewer exercises.
Alternatively, we also need to appreciate that we cannot spend as much time
with certain exercises for acyclic sports. Sets are the primary means we can
manage stress, but we cannot change the total number of sets within a
workout due to time constraints. There is an upper limit of time and overall
sets we can do in a training session; the average is 20 plus or minus four sets.

Take Home

花更多时间进行训练、增加更高强度的组数或使用更多或更少练习的训
练课程都会对最终目标产生影响。 所需内容以及相关内容的清单为在
训练课程和后续训练块中选择适当的组数和次数分布提供了指导。

规则 10：随机性和训练可预测性
环境越随机，我们的训练计划就越需要多样性。

在奥林匹克运动中，要求范围窄且集中，我们可以减少练习量。 对于
奥运会运动员或力量运动运动员来说，他们需要准备的赛事数量是有限
的。 他们非常专注。 由于运动的多样性或随机性减少，这种关注限制
了所需练习的多样性。所需练习数量的减少可能会导致这些练习的组数
增加。 这导致开发更多相关的练习，与表现更相关。 在一项练习上投
入尽可能多的时间可以提高该练习的表现，这使得评估它是否有价值变
得极其重要。如果是正确的练习，那么通过增加组数来发展与表现相关
的错误质量可能会适得其反，就像富有成效一样。

我们以 1 小时为增量推动适应。我们无法增加时间，但我们可以更好
地管理我们拥有的时间。 如果我们知道循环运动需要较少的练习变化
，我们就可以花更多的时间进行更少的练习。另外，我们还需要认识到
，我们不能花那么多时间进行非循环运动的某些练习。 组数是我们管
理压力的主要手段，但由于时间限制，我们无法改变锻炼中的总组数。
一次训练的时间和总组数是有上限的；平均是20正负四组。

带回家

There could be a feeling that long-term planning is futile with a team. There
are simply too many things to consider with complex adaptive systems and
large groups. However, if we can systematically create adaptations that are
net positive for the entire team, we are more effective as strength coaches.
Periodization rules are really about understanding that the ability to recover
dictates the overall outcome. Programming variables come down to
managing quality through volume. If we can understand and leverage
training, we can accomplish consistently positive results with large groups.

可能会有一种感觉，团队的长期规划是徒劳的。对于复杂的自适应系统
和大型群体来说，需要考虑的事情太多了。 然而，如果我们能够系统
地制定对整个团队产生积极影响的调整，那么我们作为力量教练的效率
会更高。分期规则实际上是为了理解恢复能力决定总体结果。 编程变
量归结为通过数量来管理质量。 如果我们能够理解并利用培训，我们
就能在大型团体中取得持续的积极成果。

LOGISTICS
What is the goal of having an S&C department or a weight room? Have you
ever thought about that? It is an important question, one that we should
consider when building a weight room, organizing it, hiring staff, and
planning how to educate, train, and organize them. What are we trying to
create with our staff and weight room, and how do we optimize it? You are
probably not thinking of this to the extent you should. You are probably
concerned with more obvious things, like programming, accountability, and
technique, which is first-order thinking. Second-order thinking will have you
concerned about whether you have the right setup so you are not fighting
yourself all the time.
The goal is simple: to increase performance. It may seem obvious, but that
does not change the fact that we need to establish that truth before anything
else. We are going to talk about weight room design, sports science, and
coaching in this section, but understanding a common goal makes this topic
simpler: increasing performance. Whatever training, analytics, coaching, or
organizational decisions we make will be based on the premise that the intent
is to increase performance (figure 13.1).
The goal of a team setting is to win more games. The goal of a commercial
business is to make more money. This should be obvious, but we can easily
lose sight of the goal in our day-to-day. From there, it is a matter of finding a
couple of key factors to achieve increased performance. First, find out what
you can change versus what you cannot change. Second, inventory what you

performance. For the most part, this is about reducing injuries. Someone who
is faster, stronger, or has greater endurance comes secondary to resilience. If
they are injured, they cannot help win more games.

For appraisal, we need to establish a standard, which is a very hard thing
to do. There is a lot to consider when determining what is considered good
versus bad. We could purely rely on outcome measures to determine what is
good. We can look at predetermined criteria of good execution during a rep, a
set, and a training session. We could create a checklist for each segment of a
training session for athletes to check to determine whether that session was
good or bad. The appraisal is a combination of objective, good execution, and
tangible items to complete that will allow us to determine what is good.
A good thought experiment is to ask how good this team would be without
S&C. Not working with another staff, but without it entirely. This is a serious
question because S&C is not cheap for athletic departments. Think of the cost
of the staff, the weight room, and the upkeep for that weight room. Have you
ever wondered why Olympic sports athletes typically do not stay for summer
training? It is ridiculously expensive. So if we are going to evaluate anything,
how good our teams would be without S&C is a good place to start. From the
standpoint of expense, S&C is something that athletic departments are always
thinking of ways to eliminate or reduce the cost of.
How do we determine the return on investment? Let us say that your
athletic director decided to make budget cuts; how would we justify keeping
S&C? There is only one way to answer this. You have to be so indispensable
that the teams you work with and the athletic department cannot be
successful without you. Whatever the cost to the athletic department is, it
becomes justified by the relative value you bring compared to not having
S&C at all. The only way we can objectively determine this is by
understanding what we have control over, what we have versus what we do
not, and how well we do what we do.
We have indicators of this when we compare ourselves to our competitors.
Often, this depends on whether they have more talent or better resources. All
things being equal, good S&C will play itself out in two ways. One is
resiliency and the avoidance of noncontact injuries. A good proxy of this is
learning the number of athletic department surgeries from your program
relative to another program or previous staff. The other is performance. Is our

做我们所做的事情有多好。
当我们将自己与竞争对手进行比较时，我们就有了这一点的指标。通
常，这取决于他们是否拥有更多人才或更好的资源。在所有条件相同的
情况下，良好的 S&C 会以两种方式发挥作用。 一是弹性和避免非接触
式伤害。 一个很好的指标是了解您的项目相对于另一个项目或以前的
员工进行的运动部门手术的数量。另一个是性能。是我们的

team running faster, jumping higher, and throwing further?
If we can improve resiliency, we can save money for athletic departments.
Surgery and all that comes with it are expensive for athletic departments:
surgery, physical therapy, return-to-play redshirt years, and potentially
medical dismissal from the team. Reduce injuries, specifically noncontact
injuries, and you save money for the athletic department. To quote an athletic
director when I asked how to evaluate S&C, “I don’t know what you guys do,
but I do know we spend less on surgeries with some strength staffs compared
to other staffs we have had.”
The other factor is to improve performance. We can go any way we want
with this, so we need to establish two frameworks for appraising
performance. The first one is key performance indicators (KPIs), which are
preselected metrics that we feel strongly correspond to performance in
competition. The second way to appraise performance is through objectives
and key results (OKRs). Objectives are what we want to achieve with the
training. Key results are the metrics that ensure we are achieving our
objective. Both KPIs and OKRs are valuable tools in appraising performance,
but the most important part to consider is that we are evaluating our
achievement of performance targets.
What you may find when genuinely trying to appraise your performance
through OKRs or KPIs is that you will miss the mark. Whenever we miss the
mark in terms of outcome, we have to ask two fundamental questions. First,
was my rationale for training correct? In reality, we could miss the mark
considerably with our interventions, which negates the actual way in which
we trained. Second, did we execute our training plan? If we have the correct
rationale for training with poor execution, we miss the mark (figure 13.2).
Both are valuable proxies for reaching an OKR or KPI. When our back is
against the wall, we should have an exact understanding of our ability to raise
performance or not. We can only fix something that we know is broken. If we
do not assess our achievement of benchmarks, we will fail to justify what we
have.
OKRs or KPIs force us to preselect an outcome that we evaluate our
program against. We want our rationale to be sound so we can focus on
execution. When we know what we are trying to achieve, we can focus on

当你真正尝试通过 OKR 或 KPI 评估你的绩效时，你可能会发现你会

计划执行了吗？如果我们有正确的理由进行训练，但执行力不佳，我们
就达不到目标（图 13.2）。两者都是实现 OKR 或 KPI 的宝贵指标。 当
我们陷入困境时，我们应该准确地了解自己是否有能力提高绩效。我们
只能修复已知损坏的东西。如果我们不评估基准的实现情况，我们就无
法证明我们所拥有的一切是合理的。

OKR 或 KPI 迫使我们预先选择一个结果来评估我们的计划。 我们希
望我们的理由是合理的，这样我们就可以专注于执行。 当我们知道自
己想要实现什么目标时，我们就可以专注于

how we can do it better. As strength coaches, we want to marry ourselves to
outcomes, not solutions. Running faster, jumping higher, or throwing
something farther are the outcomes we want. What gets us there is largely
predicated on what our athletes can do biomechanically and recover from
physiologically. Outcome focus allows us to look at the bigger picture of
training and ask ourselves whether it helps performance. Is the team I am
working with good because of or despite my help?

Coaches are evaluated on wins and losses, and strength coaches are
evaluated on correlated performance metrics. Running faster, jumping higher,
or throwing an implement farther are general performance markers. They are
hard to cheat and are readily understood as corresponding to performance.
Specific aspects can connect these general performance markers to certain
sports, but the takeaway is that if we want to be considered valuable, we must
establish that we bring value.

performance. We are the product of what we repeatedly do. If we have

the product of how well we do something and how much of that we do. If we
have limitations to the ability to do something well, such as poor equipment
or lack of space, then we have to expect a lesser outcome.
What preselected outcomes eventually do is align our thoughts and actions
toward something bigger. Outcomes force us to remove limitations or find
ways to manage them. Outcomes force us to find better solutions. Outcomes
create a common theme for coaches, athletes, and strength coaches. It
answers the question of how much we are contributing and, therefore, how
much value we bring.

Coordinating With Support Staff
What becomes apparent as a strength coach is that the ability to
communicate is central to being successful. In the team setting,
you have counterparts such as sports medicine and sports
nutrition. You will need to communicate with them, and your
ability to do so creates a positive asset in the quest for
performance.
Job descriptions are a tricky thing within athletic departments.
Most strength coaches are incredibly resourceful and find
solutions to problems regardless of whether it is within a job
description. At the beginning of a strength coach’s career, there
is no job too small. There will always be a will, and therefore, a
way.
As we progress through our careers, we get more resources,
and the diversity of jobs decreases. You have people who are
more capable than we are at the jobs we had to do previously.
This is obvious but not easy to appreciate. It comes down to
timelines and communication of timelines to optimize
relationships.
Communication is always a bidirectional path. People need to
listen to each other. At the same time, people need to speak with

表现。 我们是我们反复做事的产物。 如果我们的工作效率低下，我们
的产品就会减少。结果是我们做某事的好坏以及我们做了多少的结果。
如果我们在做好某件事的能力上受到限制，例如设备较差或缺乏空间，
那么我们就只能期待较小的结果。
预先选定的结果最终会促使我们的思想和行动朝着更大的方向发展。
结果迫使我们消除限制或找到管理它们的方法。结果迫使我们寻找更好
的解决方案。结果为教练、运动员和力量教练创造了一个共同的主题。
它回答了我们贡献了多少以及我们带来了多少价值的问题。

与支持人员协调
作为一名力量教练，显而易见的是，沟通能力是成功的关键。 在
团队环境中，有运动医学和运动营养学等同行。 您需要与他们沟
通，而您这样做的能力将为追求绩效创造积极的资产。

在体育部门中，职位描述是一件棘手的事情。大多数力量教练
都非常足智多谋，无论问题是否在工作描述范围内，都能找到解
决方案。 在力量教练职业生涯的初期，没有什么工作是太小的。
总会有一个意志，因此也会有一个方法。
随着我们职业生涯的进步，我们获得了更多的资源，而工作的
多样性却在减少。 在我们以前必须做的工作上，你们有比我们更
有能力的人。这是显而易见的，但并不容易理解。 归根结底是时
间表和时间表的沟通，以优化关系。
沟通始终是双向路径。人们需要互相倾听。与此同时，人们需
要与

confidence and clarity about what is needed. Detaching ego from
any conversation in a high-stakes, competitive environment is
not easy. As a strength coach, it can be challenging to defer to
others when you have had to find solutions without them for so
long.
The tricky part is that you were going at your own pace and
figuring out solutions on your timeline. When you have
competent sports medicine and sports nutritionists to work with
you, you have to become adept at coordinating schedules. This
will feel like a bureaucratic waste of time, but it’s the cost of
doing business in high-performance environments. Getting on
the same page is critical for success.
Being prepared ahead of time for what your job description
describes is the most crucial step. The best sign of respect for a
colleague is taking care of your responsibilities. Get lined up on
the same vision. Make the process collaborative. Get on their
timelines when needed. Agree on meeting dates. Compromise
when needed. When in doubt, understand the job you have to do
and the job they have to do, then work hard coordinating to
provide the best training possible.

Control
There are two ends of the continuum when it comes to control: what you can
and what you cannot control. We are constantly facing decisions with our
program. The truth is, the only way to handle the constant decisions is to
reduce the number we have to make. Eliminating decisions we have no
control over is the first step. The second step is to reduce the number of
decisions we have control over that have little impact.

What We Can Control
One of the best lessons I can give you from this book is to understand what
you can control. This is what you should worry about. Throughout your
career, you will face many problems that are beyond your control. You can

对需要什么充满信心和清晰。在高风险、竞争激烈的环境中，将
自我从任何谈话中剥离出来并不容易。 作为一名力量教练，当你
必须在长时间没有他人帮助的情况下寻找解决方案时，遵从他人
的意见可能会很困难。
棘手的部分是你要按照自己的节奏前进并在你的时间表上找出
解决方案。 当您有称职的运动医学和运动营养师与您合作时，您
必须善于协调时间表。 这感觉像是官僚主义浪费时间，但这是在
高性能环境中开展业务的成本。 达成共识对于成功至关重要。

提前为您的职位描述做好准备是最关键的一步。尊重同事的最
好标志就是履行自己的职责。 为同一个愿景而排队。 使流程具

需要时妥协。如有疑问，请了解您必须完成的工作以及他们必须
完成的工作，然后努力协调以提供尽可能最好的培训。

控制
当谈到控制时，连续体有两端：你能控制什么和你不能控制什么。 我
们的计划不断面临决策。 事实是，处理不断变化的决策的唯一方法就
是减少我们必须做出的决策数量。 第一步是消除我们无法控制的决定
。 第二步是减少我们可以控制的影响不大的决策数量。

我们可以控制什么
我可以从这本书中给你的最好的教训之一就是了解你可以控制什么。
这是你应该担心的。 在你的职业生涯中，你会遇到许多你无法控制的
问题。 你可以

stress all you want about things you have no control over, but this is wasted
energy that you cannot overcome unless you figure out a system to manage it.
Focusing on what you can control is important. You will inherit a weight
room that you disagree with in terms of the layout or equipment selection. A
fundamental question for facility design is whether you are programming for
the weight room or designing your weight room based on your program
(figure 13.3). Chances are, you are designing your program based on the
weight room.
Every weight room has its nuances. Traffic patterns within the weight
room are largely based on an architectural plan that may or may not include
the strength staff working in that space. In the event an architect asks a
strength coach what the preferred layout is, is there a good answer? Think
about that for a moment: Is there an optimal organizational layout for a
weight room for efficiency?
A couple of models we can think about here are assembly line or station
based. An assembly line is based on Taylorism and Fordism philosophy
(McChrystal, 2015), creating a sequence of events from start to finish for a
coach and athletes to follow one group at a time. A station-based model
divides the room into separate stations, with the entire group following the
workout in the same order simultaneously.

对你无法控制的事情施加你想要的一切，但这是你无法克服的浪费精力
，除非你找到一个系统来管理它。
专注于你可以控制的事情很重要。您将继承一个您在布局或设备选择
方面不同意的举重室。设施设计的一个基本问题是您是在为举重室编程
还是根据您的程序设计举重室（图 13.3）。 您很可能正在根据举重室
设计您的计划。
每个举重室都有其细微差别。 举重室内的交通模式很大程度上取决
于建筑规划，该规划可能包括也可能不包括在该空间工作的力量人员。
如果建筑师询问力量教练首选布局是什么，有好的答案吗？ 想一想：
举重房是否有一个最佳的组织布局以提高效率？
我们在这里可以考虑的几个模型是基于装配线或工作站的。 装配线
基于泰勒主义和福特主义哲学（McChrystal，2015），从开始到结束创
建一系列事件，让教练和运动员一次跟随一组。 基于站点的模型将房
间划分为单独的站点，整个小组同时按照相同的顺序进行锻炼。

FIGURE 13.3 Weight room driven versus program driven.
The assembly line model of training is an efficient way to organize
training. Each station is allocated a certain amount of time before
transitioning to the next station. A lot of times, this can be confused with
circuit training, where people may have a different order of exercises or focal
points. Circuit training takes an entire group of athletes, flowing them from
station to station. The assembly line is where everyone starts at a certain
station, for instance, movement prep, and then everyone proceeds to power,
speed, agility, quickness, strength training, conditioning, and recovery.
Circuit training would just have those stations set up, and people would have
completely different starts and ends.
The pros of the assembly line model are that we can take many people

图 13.3 举重室驱动与程序驱动。
流水线培训模式是一种有效的组织培训方式。 每个站点在转换到下
一个站点之前都会分配一定的时间。 很多时候，这可能与循环训练相
混淆，循环训练中人们可能有不同的练习顺序或焦点。 巡回训练需要
一整组运动员，让他们从一个站到另一个站。 装配线是每个人从某个
站开始的地方，例如，动作准备，然后每个人都进行力量、速度、敏捷
性、速度、力量训练、体能训练和恢复。巡回训练只会设置这些站点，
人们会有完全不同的开始和结束。

流水线模式的优点是可以带很多人

through a training program without sacrificing order or quality based on that
order. We can toggle a better coach-to-athlete ratio. We can organize training
to prioritize higher-value but riskier things early in the workout. We ensure
that everyone across the entire team has the same experience. The cons of
assembly lines are that we can only train a certain number of people at a
specific time. Working in a team setting is built around small windows of
training, such as before classes, before practice, or after practice. If you have
to train a team of 100 athletes and only 6 to 12 at a time can perform the task
based on the assembly function, you are going to have a hard time
accommodating an entire team’s limited schedule, not to mention the
inevitable curveball in terms of oversleeping, study hall, practice running
long, punishments, or general schedule changes, which make the assembly
line back up considerably.
The station model’s pros accommodate a broader range of schedules but
are limited to how many stations one may have. If we have a team of 100
people and six racks, we will have a hard time training the entire team at
once. Unless you create circuits at each rack, there is going to be a lot of
standing around. The station model is completely contingent upon how many
stations you have to work with. That has a direct impact on the coach-toathlete ratio and how you organize your training. The primary con of stationbased training is that it is limited to potential tools you may use for certain
situations, such as isolated open kinetic chain machines. You will find that
the station-based model is centered on the utility of equipment over
everything else. The more versatility the station has, the more value it will
have. For example, a rack and barbell will have more utility than a leg press.
A general rule of thumb for facility setup or design is to break everything
down into three (figure 13.4). Three to a rack is a manageable number for
spacing and organization. Isolated exercises, supersets, or trisets all work
well with three people working together. Someone to spot, someone resting,
and someone working is typically the flow. The ability to execute the
program will be based on fitness, the complexity of the setup, and the
environment created by the coach. We want the athlete to be able to
definitively execute each rep and set through the entire training session. Their
execution will be based on the individuality of the athlete, combined with

车站模型的优点是可以适应更广泛的时刻表，但受到车站数量的限制
。 如果我们有一个100人的团队和6个机架，我们很难一次性训练整个
团队。 除非你在每个机架上建立电路，否则将会有很多人站在那里。
车站模型完全取决于您必须使用的车站数量。 这对教练与运动员的比
例以及你组织训练的方式有直接影响。基于站的培训的主要缺点是它仅
限于您在某些情况下可能使用的潜在工具，例如隔离的开放式动力链机
器。 您会发现基于站点的模型以设备的实用性为中心，而不是其他一
切。 车站的多功能性越多，它的价值就越大。例如，架子和杠铃比腿
举更实用。

设施设置或设计的一般经验法则是将所有内容分解为三部分（图 13.4
）。 对于空间和组织来说，三个机架是一个易于管理的数字。 单独练
习、超级组或三组都适合三个人一起训练。 通常情况下，有人去发现
、有人休息、有人工作。 执行该计划的能力将取决于身体状况、设置
的复杂性以及教练创造的环境。 我们希望运动员能够在整个训练过程
中明确执行每一次重复和设定。他们的执行将基于运动员的个性，并结
合

how well we coach and the overall environment we create with the weight
room.
Three racks per coach is a manageable workload. A lot of this depends on
the setup. Do you record for your athletes, or do they record their weights
themselves? Do you have a lot of setup, or is it a minimal setup? Is there a
complicated exercise that you will need a lot of precision for versus a simple
exercise that requires less precision? The workload for a coach is an
important aspect of rep, set, and training session integrity. As the person
programming many people at once, you will need to consider how many
things a coach can manage.
One supplemental piece of equipment per three racks works well for flow
and limiting the bottleneck. Most supplemental pieces will fit into the tertiary
part of the workout. Traditionally, these will come as a triset or potentially
have a staggered flow from the A series to the B and C series. Machines,
functional trainers, dumbbells, kettlebells, medicine balls, and
cardiorespiratory pieces are all necessary if you can fit them in your space
and they are accessible to athletes. If you have 12 stations in a weight room
and one piece of equipment, such as one glute-ham raise, you will have a
bottleneck if you program that within the workout. You will need at least four
glute-ham raises to include them in a workout. There is a tradeoff between
having too many things and having space to use, not to mention having to
keep them organized.

我们的教练水平以及我们在举重室创造的整体环境如何。
每节车厢三个行李架是一个可管理的工作量。这很大程度上取决于设
置。 您为运动员记录体重，还是他们自己记录体重？ 您有很多设置，
还是最少的设置？ 是否有一项复杂的练习需要很高的精度，而一项简

课程完整性的一个重要方面。 作为同时为多人编程的人，您需要考虑
教练可以管理多少事情。
每三个机架添加一台补充设备可以很好地缓解流量和限制瓶颈。大多
数补充部分都适合锻炼的第三部分。 传统上，这些将作为三组出现，
或者可能从 A 系列到 B 和 C 系列交错流动。 如果您能将机器、功能训
练器、哑铃、壶铃、健身球和心肺器械放在您的空间内并且运动员可以

太多东西和有空间使用之间需要权衡，更不用说必须保持它们井井有条
了。

FIGURE 13.4 Facility rule of threes.
A couple of hard-and-fast rules to live by with what we can control: If it
has dust, get rid of it. You are not using it. There is a reason you are not using
it. Either it is deemed ineffective or does not fit with the system you are using
to train your athletes. The second rule is that before you buy anything, ask if
you would be willing to pay your own money for it. Too often, we are
playing with other people’s money when equipping a weight room. We make
careless decisions when we do not have any skin in the game. The piece that
we bought, which was not thought out, creates a lasting impression of being
wasteful. It creates a stereotype that you are careless with everything you do.
The best way to combat that mistake is to be willing to front the money
yourself or give the impression it matters that much to you that you would be
willing to pay for it. If you hesitate at all based on not being sure if you need
it or not, you should not buy that piece of equipment. The third rule, and this
is an important one, is that not knowing how to use a piece of equipment
should not be the limiting factor to having that piece of equipment. Valuable
tools in the weight room should not be limited by people coaching them. If
that piece of equipment can bring value, you should have it regardless of
whether a coach knows how to use it.

设施三人规则。

对于我们可以控制的事物，必须遵守一些严格的规则：如果有灰尘，
请将其清除。你没有使用它。您不使用它是有原因的。它要么被认为无
效，要么不适合您用来训练运动员的系统。第二条规则是，在购买任何
东西之前，询问您是否愿意自己掏钱购买。 很多时候，我们在装备健
身房时都是在花别人的钱。当我们没有参与其中时，我们就会做出粗心
的决定。我们购买的这件作品未经深思熟虑，给人留下了一种浪费的印
象。它会造成一种刻板印象，即你对所做的一切都粗心大意。克服这种
错误的最好方法是愿意自己掏钱，或者给人一种印象，这对你来说很重
要，你愿意为此付费。如果您因不确定是否需要而犹豫不决，那么您不
应该购买该设备。第三条规则，也是一条重要的规则，是不知道如何使
用一件设备不应该成为拥有该设备的限制因素。举重室中的宝贵工具不
应受到指导人员的限制。 如果那件装备能带来价值，你就应该拥有它
，不管教练是否会使用它。

What We Cannot Control
Being optimistic differs from being realistic. There is an endless list of things
we have no control over that dominate our thoughts. Instead of focusing on
things we can change, our thoughts can be consumed with things we cannot
change. Our judgment becomes clouded by the distraction. Making good
choices within your training plan involves strategically removing
unproductive thoughts as much as possible.
Anyone who says space is king, on the pretense of more movement, has
probably not designed a weight room. Yes, movement is important, but there
is nothing tangible we can say we get from open space relative to a piece of
equipment we put there. Chances are that either you have an indoor practice
field where you can run, or you do not have a big enough facility to support
all your athletes. Space is a luxury, not a necessity. Think about what your
job is and what tools you need to get it done. Chances are that you will be
better served by having something occupying that space, not the space itself.
The most important part of setting up your weight room and workspace is
finding how to optimize time. If you were to go with an assembly line
approach, make sure your weight room flows to accommodate that order. If
you were to go with a station-based approach, make sure that you have a
natural progression from entering the door, going through the training
session, and leaving. You will sometimes need to get rid of stuff, move stuff,
organize stuff, clean stuff, and buy more stuff. If you cannot get a new weight
room or buy new things, you will be forced to organize what you have in a
better way. Think of a weight room as a living, breathing ecosystem. We are
introducing a bunch of organisms to that ecosystem that have a direct impact
on its natural state. You and that weight room need to adapt to meet the
forever-changing needs of the individuals who enter that ecosystem daily.
A couple of hard-and-fast rules to live by regarding what we cannot
control: If you cannot get rid of something, you have to organize it so it
doesn’t interrupt the flow of a training session. Move a piece of equipment
out of a sightline or to a spot that does not limit efficiency. If you cannot buy
something new, you need to get more from what you have. The other
alternative is to find solutions that close the gap between what you do not
have. In the spirit of reducing decisions, if you had a choice, getting rid of

Inventory
We will break the program inventory down into two sections. What we have
versus what we need. What we have are the tools, the ability, and the
motivation. What we need is based on inventorying what we have and
determining the gaps in the program to achieve higher performance.

What We Have
Do you have an idea of the years you performed extremely well versus the
years you did not perform as well? Chances are, you probably do not know
how to answer this. Transition is a natural part of S&C; your ability to
replicate success will be the determinant of long-term tenure. When we
discuss the inventory of what we need, it all comes down to replicating
success over a longer period (figure 13.5).
Can success be replicated within the weight room? My answer is yes, but
that means having a dialed-in inventory of what we do and have at a high
level. This will eventually boil down to a list of questions you need to ask
about your facility and your staff that are essential to long-term, repeatable
success.
It is important to discuss the idea that a facility and its staff are
interconnected. We cannot have one without the other. We can say that an
S&C staff without a weight room could be successful, but that would be a lie.
We could say that a weight room could be successful without an S&C staff,
but that would also be a lie. We cannot have one without the other if we want
to be successful. Both the staff and the rooms in which they work are
interdependent. It is the equivalent of a pianist and a piano or an artist with a
brush and canvas. I think we should test this theory a little bit more.
Let’s look at facilities that are open and available to the public without
supervision. A question we should ask is, what is the injury risk, and what is
the actual performance gained without supervision or guidance? We know
that commercial gyms have extremely low adherence on average and very

输入导致输出。 我们的产出最终取决于我们的投入内容和投入程度

appropriate tools to do the job.
Case in point, return to play is built upon a tangible adaptive response to
rehabilitation. Atrophy from surgery and underuse is met with targeted
hypertrophy in a localized area. Joint range of motion, joint function, and
joint articulation strength are all diagnostics of rehabilitation progress. There
is a transition from sports medicine to S&C, and we continue that progress.
There is an expectation that we focus on what we do best concerning
developing biomotor ability with closed kinetic, compound movement
patterns and that we build upon the progress made postoperatively and in
rehabilitation.
Anyone who has worked with a return-to-play athlete recovering from
surgery will understand that there is a tradeoff between reeducating
movement pattern function and direct stress in a given area. Unless we have a
specific tool to create tension in a specific muscle group, reacclimating
integrated movement patterns will come at the expense of targeted
hypertrophy. The point is that, unless we have isolated machines that can
target a muscle group, we may not have the requisite tools to execute the
athlete’s return to play in as short a period as possible. But remember, we
have to decide between assembly line or station-driven programs, which
could limit options for isolated machines due to a lack of functionality.
Returning to play or any other specific activity requires a specific tool. Do
you have the appropriate tools to do the job?

What We Need
Your philosophy will determine a large part of the tools and equipment you
will have. For instance, if you have a closed kinetic, compound movement,
pattern-based program, you will have an abundance of free-weight options.
Racks, barbells, dumbbells, and possibly kettlebells and medicine balls will
be the primary equipment options. With that list comes an ability to develop
core movement patterns such as total body Olympic lifts, squatting, hinging,
pushing, and pulling. With that list might come some weak spots in terms of
developing other movement patterns, such as vertical pulling for larger body
masses or weaker athletes, as well as knee-dominant posterior chain
movements.

完成这项工作的适当工具。
举个例子，重返比赛是建立在对康复的切实适应性反应的基础上的。
手术和使用不足导致的萎缩会在局部区域出现有针对性的肥大。 关节
活动范围、关节功能和关节强度都是康复进度的诊断指标。从运动医学
到 S&C 的转变，我们将继续这一进展。人们期望我们专注于通过封闭
动力学、复合运动模式发展生物运动能力方面最擅长的事情，并以术后
和康复方面取得的进展为基础。

任何与从手术中恢复的运动员一起工作过的人都会明白，重新训练运
动模式功能和给定区域的直接压力之间存在权衡。除非我们有特定的工
具来在特定的肌肉群中产生张力，否则重新适应综合运动模式将以牺牲
目标肥大为代价。 关键是，除非我们拥有可以针对某个肌肉群的孤立
机器，否则我们可能没有必要的工具来让运动员在尽可能短的时间内恢
复比赛。 但请记住，我们必须在装配线或工作站驱动程序之间做出选
择，这可能会由于缺乏功能而限制孤立机器的选择。重返比赛或任何其
他特定活动都需要特定的工具。 您有合适的工具来完成这项工作吗？

我们需要什么
您的理念将决定您将拥有的大部分工具和设备。 例如，如果您有一个
封闭的动态、复合运动、基于模式的计划，您将有大量的自由重量选择
。架子、杠铃、哑铃，可能还有壶铃和健身球将是主要的装备选择。有
了这个清单，就有了发展核心运动模式的能力，例如全身奥林匹克举重
、下蹲、铰链、推和拉。这份清单可能会出现一些在发展其他运动模式
方面的弱点，例如针对较大体重或较弱运动员的垂直拉动，以及以膝盖
为主的后链运动。

Alternatively, if you have a machine-based program, your weight room
will be filled with isolated joint and muscle machines. You will come up
short if there is a need to develop a closed kinetic, compound movement
pattern due to a lack of space or direct equipment. If you have a functional
movement focus with wide open space, you will lack the necessary tools to
externally load movement patterns, such as physical weights. Every
philosophical decision will have some collateral cost associated with
supporting the diverse needs of your athletes.
Your philosophy and the tools that coincide with that philosophy will
accentuate certain aspects of development. At the same time, they will create
bottlenecks that will limit development in other areas. The question becomes,
how much of a detriment will that weak spot in your programming be toward
building performance and resiliency? Objectively inventorying your primary
tools’ strengths and weaknesses relative to the primary output of training is
important to critically evaluate your program.

Become a Minimalist Strength Coach
Our lives are filled with clutter in boxes, phones, schedules, and
weight rooms. Clutter is synonymous with distraction; the more
clutter we have, the more distractions we have.
The biggest distraction we have in programming is
unnecessary equipment. There are pieces of equipment that are
glorified dust collectors. The comparison is with at-home
equipment that people use as clothing racks when they stop
exercising. The burden of having clutter from unnecessary
equipment is immense.
Unnecessary is a metaphor for how you are possibly
operating daily. It represents a cluttered life. Overrun desks or
boxes are representative of chaos winning. The opportunity to be
more efficient is worth removing excess clutter.
Unnecessary equipment makes logistics more complicated.
Ingress and egress become more challenging when there are
obstructions. Having to plan around clutter means more

您的理念以及与该理念相一致的工具将强调开发的某些方面。同时，
它们也会造成限制其他领域发展的瓶颈。问题是，您的编程中的弱点会
对构建性能和弹性产生多大的损害？ 客观地盘点主要工具相对于培训
主要输出的优势和劣势对于批判性地评估您的计划非常重要。

成为一名极简力量教练
我们的生活充满了盒子、电话、日程表和举重房等杂乱的东西。
混乱是分散注意力的代名词。 我们的杂物越多，我们的干扰就越
多。
编程中最大的干扰是不必要的设备。有些设备被称为除尘器。
比较的是人们在停止锻炼时用作衣架的家用设备。 不必要的设备
造成的混乱造成的负担是巨大的。

不必要是对你每天可能如何运作的隐喻。 它代表着混乱的生活
。 超支的桌子或盒子代表混乱获胜。为了提高效率，消除多余的
混乱是值得的。
不必要的设备使物流变得更加复杂。当有障碍物时，入口和出
口变得更加困难。 必须围绕杂乱进行计划意味着更多

decisions you have to make in a given day. More decisions are
distractions from the primary objective of putting together the
best program imaginable.
The best strategy is to remove things you are not using. One
of the best systems for evaluating equipment use is the cleaning
system. One of the most valuable pieces of feedback is talking to
staff about what they hate cleaning. Staff will grow to hate things
they do not understand and are asked to do repeatedly. Cleaning
dust off weight room relics is a clear sign of unnecessary clutter.
Just get rid of it. It is a distraction from the objective.
Like clothes that you do not wear, unnecessary equipment is
making your life more stressful. Your jobs are stressful enough.
Having to program around unnecessary equipment makes a very
challenging job impossible. Extrapolate from removing unused
equipment to emails, meetings, and unnecessary engagements.
Focus on what is important and remove what is unimportant.
A good strength coach understands what they do well but is obsessed with
what they do not do well. Creating a comprehensive program is about
constantly inventorying what we do not do well and finding solutions to those
weaknesses. A good movement screen and physiological screen allow you to
objectively evaluate your strengths and weaknesses. What is the trend of
performance, what are patterns of injuries, and what are the areas in which
you feel you are constantly coming up short? This is the only way to evaluate
what you will need to do your job effectively. If you lack the prerequisite
tools to do your job, you will not have the opportunity to do your job.
Once we have the tools, the next question is, do we know how to use those
tools? We need to understand what we want, then we need to get what we
need, and then we need to understand how to execute with what we now have
to be successful. Skill as a coach in demonstrating, explaining, correcting,
cueing, modifying, or pivoting is equally important as having the tool itself.
The symbiotic relationship between having the tools to do our job and being
able to use those tools effectively is inescapable.
This comes down to training versus education. Education is understanding

您在某一天必须做出的决定。 更多的决定会分散人们对制定可想
象的最佳计划这一主要目标的注意力。
最好的策略是删除不使用的东西。 评估设备使用情况的最佳系
统之一是清洁系统。最有价值的反馈之一是与员工谈论他们讨厌
清洁的事情。员工会逐渐讨厌他们不理解并被反复要求做的事情
。清理举重室遗物上的灰尘是不必要的混乱的明显标志。只要摆
脱它即可。这是对目标的干扰。
就像你不穿的衣服一样，不必要的设备会让你的生活更有压力
。 你的工作压力已经够大了。必须围绕不必要的设备进行编程使
得一项非常具有挑战性的工作变得不可能。 从移除未使用的设备
到电子邮件、会议和不必要的活动进行推断。专注于重要的事情
，删除不重要的事情。
一名优秀的力量教练了解他们擅长什么，但又关注他们做得不好的方
面。 创建一个全面的计划就是不断盘点我们做得不好的地方，并找到
针对这些弱点的解决方案。良好的运动筛选和生理筛选可以让您客观地
评估自己的优势和劣势。 表现的趋势是什么，受伤的模式是什么，以
及您觉得自己在哪些方面不断落后？这是评估有效完成工作所需条件的
唯一方法。 如果您缺乏完成工作所需的必备工具，您将没有机会完成
您的工作。
一旦我们有了工具，下一个问题是，我们知道如何使用这些工具吗？
我们需要了解我们想要什么，然后我们需要得到我们需要的东西，然后
我们需要了解如何执行我们现在必须获得的成功。 作为教练，演示、
解释、纠正、提示、修改或转变的技能与拥有工具本身同样重要。拥有
完成工作的工具和能够有效地使用这些工具之间的共生关系是不可避免
的。
这归结为培训与教育。教育就是理解

what we do not yet know. Training is doing what we do or should know
better. We start with education for all staff. The first thing to do with
everyone is assume they do not know what you are talking about. Think of
John Wooden teaching his team how to put on socks and then shoes. The
concept is built upon the idea that if our strength coaches do not know, our
athletes definitely will not know. Once we educate, we train.
Training is based on standards. Do you have a definable criterion for what
is good versus bad? Rep integrity is your standard. There has to be an
objective difference between a good and a bad rep. Standards serve as the
basis for training. If a coach cannot uphold standards themselves or get others
to execute them, they will need some training to hold the standard.
Philosophy dictates much of what is necessary as education and then
training. More nuance in programming from exercise selection, diversity, and
variables (time under tension, reps, sets, intensity, rest) will dictate how much
education you will need and, subsequently, how much training you will need.
If you are benefiting from large resources and a large staff, you can
effectively do more intricate programming. If you are on the other end, with
low resources and a small staff, you are forced to do a less intricate program.
It all comes down to how you get everyone to execute the standards you
create.
If you are not motivated to find better solutions or uphold standards, the
program will suffer. The simple answer is to quit. Being unmotivated in this
industry is of no value to the coaches you work with and the athletes you
serve. The simple question of how motivated you are to do your job is a
critical aspect of a program. Too often, we tolerate coaches who are not
intrinsically motivated to uphold a standard, which compromises everything.
We discuss this in the coaching chapter (chapter 16), but the harsh reality is
that this industry is not for the faint of heart. You have to be motivated to do
your job at the highest level possible every day, no matter what. Many people
want what you have, which means you are replaceable. If you are not excited
about what you are doing, you should find another role, workplace, or career.
As a leader, you can decrease motivation among your staff by having poor
organizational skills. Inventorying yourself as a leader with clarity,
consistency, and objectivity is critical. If you have a staff that was once

with you. You have to be the example that you want your staff to be.
Therefore, it is important to inventory yourself because you are likely to be
the problem.

Appraise
What we do well matters; we can accentuate a positive to enhance the impact
of our program. However, if we are not aware of what we do not do well, we
will have clear limitations in our program. Insight into strengths and
weaknesses creates a clear direction for improvement in your program.

What We Do Well
We have to appraise what we will need to be successful. Different from
understanding what we can control and taking inventory of what we need,
appraising is about what we have and asking how we can do better with it.
Appraising is arguably more important than asking what we cannot control or
what we do not have because it forces us to focus on being simply better
(figure 13.6).
Why not just place appraisal first on the list and be done with it? It is
important to appreciate what we cannot control and what we need before we
can truly accept what we can control and what we have. Working through the
list of what we have and what we can control is often taken for granted.
What do we need to appraise? There are three fundamental questions we
need to ask when evaluating our program’s potential. Are we making our
athletes better? Is what we ask of our athletes replicable? Can we hold our
athletes to a standard? Your facility, your staff, and your program are all
predicated on being able to execute certain things, but that is only valuable if
it leads to improvement.
Are we making our athletes better relative to the decisions we make
regarding their training? We all have ideas of what training is or what we
think good training is. We all have aspirations of helping our athletes to the
best of our abilities. What becomes challenging is matching good intentions
with actual outcomes from our training. We can explore an infinite number of

积极性很高，但他们的积极性逐渐下降，作为领导者向内看是一个很好
的起点。如果您是一名首席力量教练，那就从您开始。 您必须成为您
希望员工成为的榜样。因此，盘点一下自己很重要，因为你很可能就是
问题所在。

评价
我们做得好很重要；我们可以强调积极的一面，以增强我们计划的影响
。然而，如果我们不知道自己哪些方面做得不好，我们的计划就会有明
显的局限性。 深入了解优势和劣势可为您的计划改进制定明确的方向
。

我们擅长什么
我们必须评估我们需要什么才能获得成功。 与了解我们可以控制的东
西和盘点我们需要的东西不同，评估是关于我们拥有的东西并询问我们
如何能够利用它做得更好。评估可以说比询问我们无法控制什么或我们
没有什么更重要，因为它迫使我们专注于变得更好（图 13.6）。
为什么不直接将评估放在清单上并完成它呢？ 在我们真正接受我们
可以控制的东西和我们拥有的东西之前，重要的是要了解我们无法控制
的东西和我们需要的东西。列出我们拥有的和我们可以控制的东西通常
被认为是理所当然的。
我们需要评估什么？ 在评估我们项目的潜力时，我们需要问三个基
本问题。 我们是否让我们的运动员变得更好？ 我们对运动员的要求可
以复制吗？ 我们能否让我们的运动员达到标准？ 你的设施、你的员工
和你的计划都是以能够执行某些事情为基础的，但这只有在能够带来改
进的情况下才有价值。
相对于我们针对训练做出的决定，我们是否让我们的运动员变得更好
？ 对于什么是培训或者什么是好的培训，我们都有自己的想法。 我们
都希望尽我们所能帮助我们的运动员。 具有挑战性的是如何将良好的
意图与我们培训的实际结果相匹配。我们可以探索无数个

options with programming, but we have to appraise whether they are good
ideas.
In truth, we cannot appraise whether deciding to use one method or
another is good until we evaluate whether it was executed properly and held
to a high standard over time. We have to know if our rationale for deciding to
do any exercise or for organizing any training variable was sound judgment.
For us to truly evaluate the efficacy of our programming, we need to establish
that training was consistently executed over the entire period.

Let’s start with our technique being replicable. There should be some
uniformity from coach to athlete, and that should be replicated over an
extended period. A coach should have an impact, but determining that impact
can be challenging if we rely on an athlete’s genetic potential. Outcomes
from training will vary widely based on many factors, but the technique in
which that athlete moves should not. In some ways, the only thing we can
control is the way we do something.
An outsider evaluating a program can be misled by certain outcome
measurements. The truest evaluation of a strength coach’s ability is integrity
with reps, sets, and training sessions. How each rep, set, and training session
is executed determines the effectiveness of the strength staff. The only thing

件事

we can effectively control is the technique we use in each aspect of a training
session.
An argument could be made that there is no one way to do an exercise.
Another could be made that no rep is the same as the last. All true, but some
aspects can, and should, be consistent. Where an athlete puts their hands, feet,
or eyes when they lift is controllable and reflective of what a coach does. The
range of motion an athlete is asked to move with is controllable. How heavily
or quickly someone moves is controllable. If we have no impact on how an
athlete moves from direct coaching, there is no point in having a coach.
Having someone execute something at a high level over time determines
the outcome. Intermittent high-level execution pales in comparison to
continuous, lasting high-level execution in reaching objectives. One good rep
does not make a good coach or a good program. A good coach can hold a
standard of execution over an extended period. A coach understands the
outcome and, therefore, the consequences of not holding a standard. The
primary responsibility of a coach is to hold athletes accountable to that
standard. Technique, therefore, is not a matter of subjectively saying
something is good or bad but a prerequisite for a coach to execute in their
job.
An athlete must execute each rep with precision based on the
predetermined criteria for the set and training session to be effective. A coach
will need to have the fortitude to uphold that standard for the entirety of a set,
training session, microcycle, and beyond. We all have a job to do. Training is
a collection of individuals who agree on what is effective and then work
relentlessly to achieve a desired outcome.
If we can lift with high standards and continue to do so throughout the
training program, we can evaluate the program’s effectiveness. Improvement
without the context of where that improvement came from is a poor
evaluation. Without continuity of execution, we cannot effectively evaluate
our program year to year. Execution and improvement are the foundation of
being able to say with confidence that we are good at what we do.
If we have consistent execution, then we begin to unpack the question of
what is good. Good technique is the foundation that determines the program’s
effectiveness. If we miss the mark for KPIs, we can discern that our rationale

。运动员举重时手、脚或眼睛的放置位置是可控的，并且反映了教练的

后坚持不懈地努力以达到预期的结果。
如果我们能够以高标准举重，并在整个培训计划中继续这样做，我们

评估我们的计划。 执行和改进是我们能够自信地说我们擅长我们所做
的事情的基础。
如果我们有一致的执行力，那么我们就开始解开什么是好的问题。好
的技术是决定方案有效性的基础。如果我们没有达到 KPI 的标准，我们
可以看出我们的理由

for training decisions, such as exercise selection and variables, was the
reason.

What We Do Not Do Well
This is the critical aspect of program evaluation. If we can execute properly
and come up short, we will have to rethink the program. We will have to
rethink the tools we have versus the tools we need. We will have to rethink
the education and training of our staff. We will have to rethink what we do
not have. We will have to evolve into a better version of ourselves as
coaches.
Appraising our program is about finding ways to be objective with what
we are doing daily. We can justify any lack of outcome, but that is not what
elite-level S&C is or should be. Hiding behind excuses for why something
did not happen is not what elite-level strength coaches do. Limited resources
or less-than-ideal working conditions are too common to use as a valid
excuse. We have to be resourceful and demonstrate high utility in any
situation. In the end, we can only get more resources based on the
demonstration that we can produce with limited resources.
Finding out what we can and cannot control is only part of the equation.
Inventory of what we have versus what we need is another part of the
equation. But the biggest part of the equation, in which all other parts take
form, is appraising our program. Whether our program is good is only
accurate if the way we executed that program was good as well. Setting up a
staff or organizing a weight room comes secondary to understanding what is
good in the first place.
If we are going to say we truly make a difference, it needs to come from
objectivity. The pretense of getting hired or a misleading indicator of not
getting fired is the validation of one’s ability. It’s an achievement, but that
does not substitute for true indicators such as tangibly improving. Approval is
not the same as accomplishment. If you are worth a damn as a strength coach,
you will receive accolades, but that is not the goal of an S&C program. Your
athletes depend on you to put them in a place to be successful, more
successful than they would be without your being there. You hold the key to
success.

训练决策（例如练习选择和变量）就是原因。

我们做得不好的地方
这是计划评估的关键方面。 如果我们能够正确执行但出现问题，我们
将不得不重新考虑该计划。 我们将不得不重新考虑我们拥有的工具与
我们需要的工具。 我们将不得不重新考虑员工的教育和培训。 我们将
不得不重新思考我们所没有的东西。 作为教练，我们必须发展成为更
好的自己。
评估我们的计划是为了找到客观地对待我们每天所做的事情的方法。
我们可以为任何缺乏结果的情况辩护，但这不是精英级别的 S&C 的样
子或应该是的。 为没有发生的事情找借口并不是精英级力量教练所做
的事情。有限的资源或不太理想的工作条件太常见，不能作为有效的借
口。 我们必须足智多谋，在任何情况下都表现出高实用性。 最终我们
只能基于用有限的资源可以生产的示范来获得更多的资源。
找出我们能控制什么和不能控制什么只是等式的一部分。我们拥有的
库存与我们需要的库存是等式的另一部分。 但这个等式中最重要的部
分（所有其他部分都在其中形成）是评估我们的计划。 只有当我们执
行该程序的方式也很好时，我们的程序是否好才是准确的。相比了解什
么是好的，设置员工或组织举重室是次要的。
如果我们要说我们真正有所作为，那么它需要来自客观性。 假装被
录用或没有被解雇的误导性指标是对一个人能力的验证。 这是一项成
就，但这并不能取代诸如明显改善之类的真实指标。认可并不等于成就
。如果你值得作为一名力量教练，你将会获得赞誉，但这不是 S&C 计
划的目标。你的运动员依靠你来帮助他们取得成功，比没有你的情况下
他们会更成功。您掌握着成功的关键。

Take Home
What is our purpose? Training, development, and improvement are
important, but they have to come from somewhere or something. How are
you going to substantiate your purpose from the effort and whatever outcome
may emerge? Determining what is in our control, what we have, and how we
do something is the foundation for understanding our impact. Our purpose is
to provide an environment that improves those around us. Before we can
decide what is needed in a weight room or how staff should navigate it, we
need to become truly objective with what we do.

带回家
我们的目的是什么？ 培训、发展和改进很重要，但它们必须来自某个
地方或某个地方。 您将如何通过努力以及可能出现的结果来证实您的
目标？确定我们能控制什么、我们拥有什么以及我们如何做某事是了解
我们影响力的基础。我们的目的是提供一个改善我们周围的人的环境。
在我们决定举重室需要什么或工作人员应如何进行操作之前，我们需要
对我们所做的事情变得真正客观。

WEIGHT ROOM DESIGN
We again start with whether we are building our weight room based on our
program or building our program based on our weight room. It is an
important question. It will shape everything you do at a particular school or
organization where you are working. It is often overlooked and taken for
granted, but it should not be.
A common aspect of S&C is that we inherit our weight rooms. We have
organized our training around someone else’s decisions made long before we
had the opportunity to work in that weight room. You could have a
philosophy, but it might be compromised or require amendment if you don’t
have the correct tools or proper layout. For example, imagine you have a
weightlifting focus, and the person before you had a powerlifting focus. You
would have to figure out how to accommodate bars that do not spin, plates
that do not bounce, and racks that take up entire platforms. We have to be
malleable to the environment because it will not adjust to us easily.
You have two choices when moving into an existing weight room. You
can force your philosophy into a weight room that does not support your
methodology, or you can adapt your philosophy to the existing weight room.
Which is correct? The answer is neither. Having an entrenched belief that one
philosophy is superior to another is a fragile approach to training. You will
face a weight room that does not support your preferred methods and will be
forced to adapt. You will inherit weight rooms that do not support your
methodology, and you will have to adjust. There is a 100% certainty that you

14
举重室设计
我们再次开始考虑是根据我们的计划建立我们的举重室还是根据我们的
举重室建立我们的计划。 这是一个重要的问题。 它将影响您在您工作
的特定学校或组织中所做的一切。 它经常被忽视并被视为理所当然，
但事实不应该如此。
施恩禧的一个共同点是我们继承了举重房。 我们的训练是围绕其他
人早在我们有机会在举重室工作之前就做出的决定来组织的。 您可以
有一个哲学，但如果您没有正确的工具或适当的布局，它可能会受到损
害或需要修改。 例如，假设您专注于举重，而您之前的人也专注于举
重。您必须弄清楚如何容纳不旋转的杆、不弹跳的板以及占据整个平台
的架子。 我们必须适应环境，因为环境不会轻易适应我们。

搬入现有举重室时，您有两种选择。 您可以将您的理念强行带入不
支持您的方法的举重室，或者您可以使您的理念适应现有的举重室。哪
个是正确的？答案是否定的。坚信一种哲学优于另一种哲学是一种脆弱
的培训方法。 您将面临一个不支持您首选方法的举重室，并且将被迫
适应。 您将继承不支持您的方法的举重室，并且您必须进行调整。 100
% 确定您

will be in situations that will force you to adapt your methods, reorganize
your training, and adjust the weight room to accommodate your needs.
Your philosophy needs to be based on what is true without context:
principles. Your philosophy needs to transcend a weight room with a
particular layout or specific pieces of equipment. Regardless of whether you
are using a barbell or a dumbbell, you will need to accommodate specificity,
individuality, progressive overload, progression, reversibility, and
diminishing returns. There is no situation where those principles will not be
appropriate. Principles allow you to walk into any weight room and create an
effective program.
The comparison would be a chef only being able to cook in Michelin-rated
kitchens. A great chef can take any list of ingredients in any setting and
create an enjoyable meal that will not make you sick. Imagine if they had
perishable food without refrigeration; they would not serve it. Imagine if they
had a particular ingredient that needed to be prepared a certain way but they
lacked the appliance to do so; they would not serve it. It is nice when they
have everything, but it is not a prerequisite. Like a chef, a strength coach
makes their decisions on what is true and what they can control.
Once you have established that principles are foundational, you have to
create rules. Rules are context dependent; your weight room and the
conditions it creates determine the rules. This could be as simple as having a
certain number of athletes at a given time due to a lack of equipment or
coaches. It could be as complex as adapting training intensity based on
readiness determined by workloads, wellness, or jump performance. Rules
allow you to optimize what you have. We can adjust how complicated our
program is or how many people we work with at once, but we cannot adjust
principles.
Rules are determined by the worst possible scenario. An obvious example
is having too many athletes in a weight room, leading to unnecessary injury.
But you can invert that to establish the highest number of athletes you want
to train and still be effective as the benchmark for determining rules. Risk
versus performance appraisals will determine how you do everything. The
bigger question is, what will be more detrimental to an outcome: diminished
output or avoidable injury?

将面临迫使您调整方法、重新组织训练并调整举重房以满足您的需求的
情况。
你的哲学需要基于没有背景的真实事物：原则。 您的理念需要超越
具有特定布局或特定设备的举重室。无论您使用杠铃还是哑铃，您都需
要适应特异性、个性、渐进性超负荷、渐进性、可逆性和收益递减。
这些原则在任何情况下都不适用。原则允许您走进任何举重室并制定有
效的计划。

比较而言，厨师只能在米其林评级的厨房里做饭。 一位优秀的厨师
可以在任何环境下使用任何食材清单，创造出一顿不会让你生病的令人
愉快的饭菜。 想象一下，如果他们的食物没有冷藏就容易腐烂；会怎
样？他们不会提供服务。想象一下，如果他们有某种特定的原料需要以
某种方式准备，但他们缺乏这样做的设备；那会怎样？ 他们不会提供
服务。 当他们拥有一切时很好，但这不是先决条件。 就像厨师一样，
力量教练根据什么是真实的以及他们可以控制的来做出决定。
一旦确定原则是基础，就必须制定规则。 规则取决于上下文； 您的
举重房及其创造的条件决定了规则。这可能很简单，就像由于缺乏设备
或教练而在特定时间拥有一定数量的运动员一样。 它可能像根据工作
量、健康状况或跳跃表现确定的准备情况调整训练强度一样复杂。 规
则可以让你优化你所拥有的。 我们可以调整项目的复杂程度或同时合
作的人数，但我们无法调整原则。

规则是根据最坏的情况确定的。一个明显的例子是举重室里有太多运
动员，导致不必要的伤害。但你可以颠倒过来，确定你想要训练的运动
员的最大数量，并且仍然可以作为确定规则的基准。 风险与绩效评估
将决定你如何做每件事。 更大的问题是，什么对结果更不利：产出减
少还是可以避免的伤害？

and architects in your life, you can easily get overwhelmed with jargon and
get lost. I apologize for the overly simplistic explanations, but you will see
that these concepts will add up as we go and can become very complicated.

fewer athletes can train at once. Smaller spaces also mean fewer pieces of

paradox. It can mean more athletes and more equipment. That is true only if
you have the coaches to accommodate more athletes working over a larger
area with a greater variety of equipment. Space determines a lot of what you
can do and, subsequently, how you manage your time.

residential and commercial areas reside within a city. Try to visualize the
travel routes that citizens use, including roads and sidewalks, as they
commute from their homes to work and back. Try to imagine the modes of
transportation, from public buses and trains to private cars. Try to imagine
the heights of the buildings and their proximity to one another. Picture where
people congregate in public parks, stadiums, and shopping areas. Ask where
public services such as police, fire, hospital, sanitation, and upkeep are
located. Now think about all the things that piss you off: random one-way
streets, no parking, high traffic, poor upkeep, and unsupervised dangerous
areas. Think about historical cities that are restricted in terms of
modifications compared to newer cities that are more open to change. Now
apply that same line of thought to your weight room. Imagine where your
athletes train and coaches work daily. Does the weight room allow for
optimal efficiency? Or is the weight room a poorly designed city that makes
its inhabitants’ lives hell?
It starts with foundational pieces. What and where is the epicenter? What
does everything orbit? Typically, a weight room is built from the rack
outward. Currently, most weight rooms are designed to support ground-based
functional movement. Much of that philosophy is built upon using a barbell.
Regardless of your beliefs, most S&C facilities are built around how many
racks (rack + barbell + bench) the space can accommodate.
Think about commercial gyms; what is the epicenter? Traditionally, it is
cardiorespiratory equipment. The primary difference is centered on not what
will bring the most value to the athlete but the most return on investment to
the business. For a commercial business, its primary investment is money.
That investment of financial resources necessitates a financial return. For a
performance-based facility, the investment is time. How well we optimize the
time we have with athletes determines the value we provide. Instead of
attracting as many clients as possible, as a commercial gym does,
performance-oriented weight rooms are forced to think about how to
maximize time.
Racks serve a plethora of options. These options traditionally center on
barbell-based exercises such as squatting, hinging, pushing, and pulling. It
serves another purpose, as a central hub for a group (traditionally two to four

You have to think about how many square feet you have and compare that
to the square footage of your hub. If your rack and platform for Olympic
weightlifting take up 224 ft² (21 m2), that dictates how many stations you can
have in a specific space. Instead of fighting the notion that a certain number
of racks will be necessary, ask how big the space is and how many stations
that space can allow for.
Of note, you will not have a perfectly symmetrical room where you can
simply place a uniform number of stations. You will have to accommodate
nooks and crannies in your weight room. It may mean being creative with
how you organize where the racks are located. It may mean having a smaller
number of stations to accommodate a layout that is small or oddly shaped. If
you are basing your program on movements in the rack, the number of racks
will be the rate-limiting factor in how many athletes you can serve at a given
time. If you can be creative with how you orient or place your racks, you may
be able to serve a greater number of athletes at once.

图 14.3 机架平台站。
您必须考虑您拥有多少平方英尺，并将其与您的中心的平方英尺进行
比较。 如果您的奥运会举重架和平台占地 224 英尺² (21 m2)，这决定了
在特定空间内可以有多少个站。不要与需要一定数量的机架的想法作斗
争，而是询问空间有多大以及该空间可以容纳多少个站。
值得注意的是，您不会拥有一个完全对称的房间，您可以在其中简单
地放置统一数量的站点。 您必须在举重室中容纳角落和缝隙。 这可能
意味着在如何组织机架的位置上发挥创意。这可能意味着要减少车站数
量以适应较小或形状奇怪的布局。如果您的计划基于架子上的运动，则
架子的数量将成为您在给定时间可以服务的运动员数量的限制因素。如
果您能够在调整架的方向或放置方式上发挥创意，您也许能够同时为更
多数量的运动员提供服务。

The number of racks should be a certain percentage of your room. You
can exchange racks for anything you consider a hub for your programming.
Before we give a number, we have to create conditions for how much that
percentage should be. If you demand space without equipment to make more
room for movement, the percentage of the weight room area occupied by the
racks will decrease. If you require more machines for your programming,
racks will again take up less space. Remember, you will need certain tools to
execute your job. There is a trade-off between having more central hubs and
the potential ability to execute very specific tasks.
There is also dead space to consider. Clearance is needed for the barbell or
loading plates on or off the weight trees. People need a place to stand in
between sets or when spotting for multiple people. It will be taken for
granted, but a drop zone for misses is necessary. Roughly 50 ft² (5 m2) of
dead space per station is needed. This dead space will have to be attributed to
each station on top of the space needed. This is traditionally the most
overlooked aspect in weight room design.
You can start with 50% of the allocated space for racks or central hubs,
with the other half of the room preserved for space or other equipment.
Increase that number to 75% for racks and reserve even less space and room
for equipment. When the space in your room becomes 75% racks, you limit
your options. Alternatively, if you reduce that number below 50%, you take
away a central hub to work from. There are a couple of things to consider
when determining a percentage. One is a missed opportunity; the other is
choosing racks with higher utility.
If you can design or redo your weight room, you will have a small window
of opportunity to get what you need. There will be no asking for more
afterward. You could be accommodating with space to allow for more
movement. You could be conservative and hope to grow in the space as you
learn more about your environment. Experience is a double-edged sword in
this situation. You won’t make the mistake of not getting something you
know you need when you have the chance. If you overspend, you have the
downside of an overcrowded room that is hard to navigate. Not to mention,
having too much equipment is a nightmare to organize. There is no correct
answer here; my advice is that whatever would be more difficult to overcome

机架的数量应占房间的一定比例。 您可以将机架更换为任何您认为
是编程中心的东西。在给出一个数字之前，我们必须为这个百分比应该
是多少创造条件。如果您需要没有设备的空间来留出更多的移动空间，
则举重室中机架所占面积的百分比将会减少。 如果您需要更多机器进
行编程，机架将再次占用更少的空间。请记住，您将需要某些工具来执
行您的工作。在拥有更多的中心枢纽和执行非常具体的任务的潜在能力
之间存在权衡。
还需要考虑死区。举重树上或下的杠铃或负重板需要留有间隙。 人
们需要在组间休息或为多人寻找位置时有一个站立的地方。 这将被认
为是理所当然的，但是一个用于失误的下降区是必要的。 每个站点需
要大约 50 ft² (5 m2) 的死区。这个死区必须归因于每个站顶部所需的空
间。 传统上，这是举重室设计中最容易被忽视的方面。
您可以从 50% 的分配空间开始用于机架或中央集线器，而另一半空
间则保留用于空间或其他设备。将机架数量增加到 75%，并为设备预留
更少的空间和空间。 当你房间里的空间变成了 75% 的机架时，你的选
择就受到了限制。 或者，如果您将该数字减少到 50% 以下，您就会失
去一个工作的中心枢纽。 确定百分比时需要考虑几件事。 一是错失良
机；二是错失良机。 二是选择实用性较高的货架。
如果您可以设计或重做您的举重室，您将有一小段时间获得您所需要
的东西。 以后就不会再要求更多了。 您可以提供空间以允许更多的活
动。您可能会比较保守，并希望随着您对环境的了解越来越多，在这个
领域中不断成长。 在这种情况下，经验是一把双刃剑。 当你有机会时
，你不会犯没有得到你知道你需要的东西的错误。 如果你超支，你就
会面临一个缺点：房间过于拥挤，难以通行。 更不用说，拥有太多的
设备对于组织来说是一场噩梦。 这里没有正确答案；我的建议是，任
何更难克服的事情

should guide the decision.
The other aspect is that stations are of higher utility than they have ever
been. The options at an individual rack have created a lessened need for
isolated machines. Racks have an incredible array of options for isolated
exercises that were previously unavailable. The need for a large dumbbell set
that takes up a lot of space is diminished by the availability of adjustable
dumbbells. Reserving space for machines or dumbbell stands is becoming
less necessary with each passing year. There will always be a trade-off
between utility and the quality that tools engineered for a specific function
bring. This trade-off could create a massive swing in outcomes and force a
decision to be made. The answer again falls on what will be harder to
overcome, which will ultimately decide the outcome.
How you arrange your racks makes a huge difference in flow and sight
lines for the coach. You have a couple of options with rack arrangement,
from the perimeter facing in or the middle facing out. There is a lot to
consider with where you place your racks; we need to review station-based
and assembly line models.

Station-Based Model
With a station-based model, you can either split the room with racks or have
them against a wall and have athletes fan out from the perimeter. There are
pluses and minuses to both. If you have them against the wall and facing
toward the rack, there will be a transition from the rack to auxiliary
equipment. There will also be an ingress of the next group and an egress of
the current group to consider. If you were to have them facing out, you would
place your auxiliary equipment against the wall, and the athletes could
transition from the station to their side of the room. But that setup requires
having a mirrored image of the equipment that both sides can access.

Assembly Line Model
With an assembly line model, you are locked into where the racks fit into the
workout (figure 14.4). For example, if you are transitioning from station to
station and the racks are third, following movement prep and speed with
plyometrics stations, the racks are landlocked in a specific location. They will

应指导决策。
另一方面是车站的效用比以往任何时候都高。 单个机架上的选项减
少了对隔离机器的需求。 训练架为孤立练习提供了一系列令人难以置
信的选项，这是以前无法实现的。可调节哑铃的出现减少了对占用大量
空间的大型哑铃组的需求。 为机器或哑铃架预留空间的必要性逐年下
降。 为特定功能设计的工具带来的实用性和质量之间总是存在权衡。
这种权衡可能会造成结果的巨大波动并迫使做出决定。 答案再次落在
更难克服的问题上，这将最终决定结果。

行李架的布置方式会对客车的流动和视线产生巨大影响。 您有多种
机架排列方式可供选择，从周边朝内或中间朝外。 放置机架的位置需
要考虑很多因素； 我们需要审查基于工作站和装配线的模型。

基于站的模型
使用基于站的模型，您可以用架子分隔房间，也可以将它们靠在墙上，
让运动员从周边散开。 两者都有优点和缺点。 如果将它们靠墙放置并
面向机架，则会出现从机架到辅助设备的过渡。 还需要考虑下一组的
入口和当前组的出口。如果你让他们面朝外，你可以将辅助设备靠墙放
置，运动员可以从站转移到房间的一侧。 但这种设置需要有双方都可
以访问的设备的镜像。

对于装配线模型，您被锁定在机架适合锻炼的位置（图 14.4）。 例如
，如果您要从一个站点过渡到另一个站点，并且架子位于第三位，在增
强式训练站的运动准备和速度之后，则架子会固定在特定位置。他们会

more than likely be at a wall facing in. You will need fewer racks and less
equipment, but you will also be able to support fewer athletes within a shorter
time frame. The racks need to be facing the previous station to be easily
accessible.

have options and that any decision comes with both advantages and
disadvantages. You will always sacrifice something for the design. The
deciding factor will be how you minimize inefficiencies and maximize the
output of increasing performance. Other variables to consider are the amount
and distribution of equipment relative to the rack or workstation. You will not
know this is a problem until you encounter it. The two biggest factors that
determine if you set your room properly are training session organization and
athlete compliance during training.
