For station-based setups, we have a couple of options: racks facing out
versus racks facing in. The primary deciding factor is how many teams are
training at once. Ingress and egress will have a huge impact here, but
ultimately, deciding where to face racks or having multiple teams will
determine the outcome. If you have one team using the space, having them
clustered together facing the same direction has advantages for the coach
(figure 14.5). Facing out and together allows for easier organizing of the
room; the team can move as a unit through the workout and leverage
residuals from one rack’s energy and effort to another. If you have multiple
teams at once, having racks isolated in a specific area facing each other has
considerable advantages. Facing racks in and separated allows coaches not to
coach over each other and avoids having teams overlap.
Sam Walton used to sit in the breakrooms of his Walmarts to hear the staff
complain about their jobs. He used that as foundational knowledge to
understand what was either poorly explained or poorly set up. The same
applies to your weight room. If setting up your equipment takes nearly double
the time it does to train, you will have unrest with your staff. Having to move
pieces of equipment across the room for the workout and then back to clean
up probably means you need to move those pieces closer together. For
example, if you have sleds in a storage closet, it’s probably easier to keep
them on the turf than to move them each time you use them, if you are using
them enough. Your staff will do what you tell them to; your best indicator is
doing this yourself. If you hate setting up, chances are your room needs to be
better organized.
The other issue is that athletes either take forever to get back to the station
or go missing entirely. Athletes taking forever to come back could be a
bottleneck issue due to not having enough equipment. It could be a proximity
issue from the station being too far. Athletes going missing in a workout is
not uncommon. They may not go missing for you, the person reading this,
but they could and probably do for your intern or coach who does not have a
lot of confidence. You can fix that by either not pairing things outside the
rack or giving your coach the ability to leave the rack by having exercises
that are easier to execute. The simplest answer is that a bigger decrement in
your program will determine where you put something and how you organize

A couple more notes on how we should adjust based on the size of the
room, coaching position, and subsequent angles are really important. You
have to think of blind spots in your room. Can you see everything as the
director? Can you see what you need to see as a coach at the rack? If you
have no good sight line or spot to orient yourself, you will constantly feel as
though you are in the way. You have to consider angles for coaches and how
you will position yourself (figure 14.6).
The last consideration is traffic patterns and how you want athletes to
enter and exit. It’s pretty simple to start: Where’s the door? Then, how you
want your session to flow will determine how it transitions: central meeting
place, movement prep, speed, plyometrics, turf or track, rack, supplemental
work, postwork, nutrition, and leave. Where you place everything determines
traffic. Think again about city planning. Where are the traffic jams, the
accidents, or the areas that cause inefficiencies? If it is structural, you can’t
control that. If it is not structural and causing problems, you probably need to
move it.

How Many Athletes Do You Have in Total?
The next question we need to answer is how many athletes are required to
train in total and at a given time. We do not control this number, at least we
don’t think we do. But this will have a tremendous impact on how we lay out
our weight room.

Athletes Per Session
There are a couple of situations to break down regarding athlete numbers
compared to the athletic department setup. The team setting has some
wrinkles to consider with the total number of athletes. We have departments
broken up into football and Olympic, which could have a drastic effect on
athletes relative to weight room size. Another aspect is that Olympic sports
are broken into court and field sports. These classifications potentially mean

每场比赛的运动员
与体育部门的设置相比，关于运动员数量，有几种情况需要细分。 球

If we look at top-line numbers, we may need a huge weight room. There is
a psychological strategy in describing gross numbers versus how they are
broken down into training session groups throughout the day. Certain groups
hold different weight when leveraging for more. Imagine asking for a 30,000
ft2 (2,787 m2) weight room on the pretext of training 100-plus football
athletes versus 15 basketball athletes. Aside from what we put in the weight
room or where we place something, we have to understand the concentric
circle that describes how a certain number of people or certain subgroups
have a variable level of influence. The number matters a great deal in getting
more.
Regarding your weight room, consider the number of athletes you serve
and how that number breaks down into groups. If you have 1,000 athletes to
train, you must figure out how to get them through your weight room on
average three to four times a week in the off-season and one to three times a
week in the season. If you want to simplify the number, multiply the total
number of athletes by three (the average number of sessions per week
throughout the entire year). Take that number and divide by five (the typical
scheduling window you will have to work within). That is the total number of
athletes per day you will need to support.

athletes per hour. As we talked about with the weight room size, we will not

constraints with practice and games; and we have different perspectives on
training time, pre- or postpractice, or lifting after a game or before a game. It
will be a lot messier than the breakdown presented here.

Athletes Per Day
We will talk about windows in which we can train, but we have limited
hours. We don’t have a 24 h window to accommodate the number. We are
likely working within a 6 to 8 h window. So we have to figure out how to
squeeze that number into the limited time we have. You are not trying to train
600 athletes in 24 h, you more likely have 6 h. That means you are probably
training 100 athletes per hour if you have 1,000 total athletes. Going back to
our rack rule of three, that means you will need 34 racks. If each rack
requires 150 ft2 (14 m2), your weight room will need to be at least 5,100 ft2
(474 m2).
If you have an assembly line, you will have to consider staging and the
number of coaches. You can segment stations and have athletes trickle
through the training session from station 1 to station 4. You can organize this
in one of two ways: fixed time or variable time. The fixed time would be 15
min per station, and the variable time would be 10 to 20 min. With fixed
time, you can roll groups through every 15 min. With variable time, you
would have to delay the next groups to accommodate the elongated time at
one station versus another.

Open Hours
Before you get all excited about the fact that we have athletes
without direct S&C guidance, let’s understand the dynamics of
college athletic departments. Athletes coming into the weight
room on their own time is a gift and a curse for a strength coach.
On the one hand, you have athletes who are willing to put in
extra work. On the other hand, they are typically wasting time,

线。在保持相同数量的情况下，我们必须弄清楚如何每小时挤入 100 名
运动员。正如我们谈到举重室的大小时，我们不会有一个完美的时间表
。我们有不同的团队规模；我们的训练和比赛有不同的时间限制； 我
们对训练时间、训练前或训练后、赛后或赛前的举重有不同的看法。它
会比这里介绍的细分要混乱得多。

每天的运动员
我们将讨论可以训练的窗口，但我们的时间有限。 我们没有 24 小时窗
口来容纳该号码。 我们可能会在 6 到 8 小时的时间内工作。 所以我们
必须弄清楚如何在我们有限的时间内压缩这个数字。您并不是想在 24
小时内训练 600 名运动员，您更有可能有 6 小时。这意味着如果您总共
有 1,000 名运动员，您可能每小时训练 100 名运动员。回到我们的三机

14 米v1})，那么您的举重室将需要至少 5,100 英尺2 (474 米2)。
如果你有一条装配线，你将不得不考虑舞台和教练的数量。 您可以
对训练站进行分段，让运动员从训练站 1 到训练站 4 逐步进行训练。您
可以通过以下两种方式之一进行组织：固定时间或可变时间。每站固定
时间为15分钟，可变时间为10至20分钟。 在固定时间下，您可以每 15
分钟滚动一次。 如果时间可变，您将不得不延迟下一组，以适应一个
站点相对于另一个站点延长的时间。

开放时间
在你对我们的运动员没有直接接受 S&C 指导这一事实感到兴奋之
前，让我们先了解一下大学体育部门的动态。 对于力量教练来说
，运动员在自己的时间进入举重室是一种礼物，也是一种诅咒。
一方面，运动员愿意付出额外的努力。 另一方面，他们通常会浪
费时间，

leaving a mess, doing contraindicated things, and are very much
a distraction.
There is no such thing as extra work. If it needs to be done, it
is no longer extra but necessary. I have worked at every level of
the team and private sector; open hours are easily one of the
most difficult aspects of your job. Most S&C coaches are in the
weight room by 5 a.m., coaching until 9 a.m., and get a break for
a couple of hours, then back to coaching the rest of the
afternoon. Most S&C coaches are putting 100% into every
session and are fighting to recover between sessions. Athletes
coming in between groups is nice, but it essentially creates more
work for the coaches. It is a complete Catch-22. If we don’t
coach these athletes, we appear lazy. If we choose to recover
between lifts, we run the risk of the athletes doing unnecessary,
potentially dangerous things.
Athletes may think they are doing a good thing by coming in
on their own time, but they are more than likely not. If athletes
have the energy to do a workout outside of training and practice,
chances are they are not working hard enough there. They are
probably doing things that are unrelated to performing at a higher
level and practicing productive procrastination. Focusing more
on the time allocated to training and practice is underrated.
Performance is not the product of overall time spent but time
spent wisely.
Another aspect is that the extra work is typically not congruent
with the training program and not in line with the weight room
design. Scratching the itch of doing things like extra speed work,
plyometrics, circuits, and so on that a high school coach had
them do is not beneficial. It is just building fatigue. At one point,
that was a beneficial edge, but then it became less valuable. Not
to mention the elaborate setups needed for some programs are
a nightmare for the coach, who either has to coach around them
or clean up after them.
There is an absolute case to be made regarding gaps in a

留下一团糟，做禁忌的事情，这些都会让人分心。
不存在额外工作之类的事情。如果需要做的话，它就不再是多
余的，而是必要的。我曾在团队和私营部门的各个层面工作过；
开放时间很容易成为您工作中最困难的方面之一。 大多数 S&C
教练早上 5 点就到举重室，训练到上午 9 点，休息几个小时，然
后下午剩下的时间继续训练。 大多数 S&C 教练在每次训练中都
投入 100% 的精力，并在训练之间努力恢复。 运动员在小组之间
插队固然很好，但这本质上给教练带来了更多的工作。 这是一个
完整的第 22 条军规。 如果我们不指导这些运动员，我们就会显
得懒惰。 如果我们选择在两次举重之间恢复，我们就会面临运动
员做不必要的、潜在危险的事情的风险。
运动员可能认为他们在自己的时间参加比赛是在做一件好事，
但事实很可能并非如此。 如果运动员有精力在训练和练习之外进
行锻炼，那么他们很可能在训练和练习之外还不够努力。 他们可
能正在做一些与更高水平的表现和有效拖延无关的事情。 更多地
关注分配给培训和实践的时间被低估了。绩效不是总花费时间的
结果，而是明智地花费时间的结果。

另一方面是额外的训练通常与训练计划不相符，也不符合举重
室的设计。仅仅做一些高中教练要求他们做的事情，比如超速训
练、增强式训练、循环训练等，是没有好处的。 这只会造成疲劳
。 在某一时刻，这是一种有利的优势，但后来它的价值就变得不
那么高了。更不用说某些项目所需的复杂设置对于教练来说是一
场噩梦，他要么必须在这些项目周围进行指导，要么在它们之后
进行清理工作。
关于差距，绝对有必要提出

program and a direct need for the athlete. For example, most
time spent with S&C is developing velocity, power, and force
and, rarely, work capacity. If the athlete has poor fitness and
needs to invest more time there, yes, absolutely, come in during
open hours. If the athlete has limited flexibility and needs to do
soft tissue and targeted flexibility work, yes, absolutely, come in
during open hours. Having an honest conversation about the
limitations of schedules and fostering an environment of
individual responsibility for development is necessary and
important.
There will be situations where athletes form a group within the
team. This can be social, but it could also be training. I have
been in several situations where athletes come in with their
teammates and do extra upper body workouts. If this is
happening frequently and with a large number of athletes, it may
be to your advantage. One thing is that the upper body exercises
are not that hard to execute and do not rely on coaching. You
may consider not programming that in the team workouts,
because it has already been accomplished. The other thing is
that athletes are demonstrating leadership by coordinating with
their teammates. Leaders are not born; they are developed. If a
player can convince their teammates to come in and get an extra
workout, it may be necessary due to the rapport created.
Open hours are not the easiest thing to manage. You have
every right to a break. You have every right to protect athletes
from sabotaging their development. You have every right to limit
extra work for yourself outside the basic description of your job.
But you can also find creative ways to capitalize on it. It is
ultimately up to you, the coach, to decide how you want to
manage it. My advice is to protect yourself and your program, but
if it is inevitable, find ways to get something from it.

开放时间并不是最容易管理的事情。 你完全有权利休息一下。
您完全有权保护运动员免遭破坏他们的发展。您完全有权限制自
己在工作基本描述之外的额外工作。但您也可以找到创造性的方
法来利用它。 最终由你（教练）决定如何管理它。我的建议是保
护你自己和你的程序，但如果这是不可避免的，想办法从中得到
一些东西。

The final aspect to consider is whether to train as a team or in groups.
Football is the focal point here, but there are smaller groups or even one-onone training sessions to consider. Training a large group is a challenge, but so
is small group training. There are pros and cons for each. Time slots will
always affect group size and training dynamics. There is no good answer to
this issue. A large part is the discretion of the sports coach, the availability of
equipment in the weight room racks, and the size of the weight room. If you
are required to train a large group or an entire team, you will need to have a
larger weight room. You will also need a larger staff.

When Are We Allowed to Train Our
Athletes?
Your windows to train athletes are going to be very small most of the time. In
the off-season, you will have more flexibility with scheduling. In-season, you
will have less scheduling flexibility. You have to find creative ways to get
most of your athletes before or after classes or before or after practice. This
probably means you will have a lot of early morning groups and late
afternoon groups. No one said S&C was easy.
You have to think of other models to truly understand how to solve the
problem of getting all your athletes within limited windows of time.
Restaurants have very similar structures to those of working with a team in
S&C. How does a restaurant make money? The costs of food, preparing the
food and serving it, and the combined overhead (rent) make it difficult to be
profitable. This is evident in how many restaurants go out of business every
year. They also have limited windows for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. They
are filled with logistic bottlenecks in optimizing their space every day while
still producing high-quality output.
How do they address the issue of accommodating more people or
potentially getting more from fewer people? Those are the two ways a

当涉及多个举重室时。 我们可以容纳更多的运动员和更多的后勤问题
。 然而，我们需要考虑质量控制和运动员分享的一致经验。
最后要考虑的一个方面是是以团队形式还是分组形式进行训练。足球
是这里的焦点，但也可以考虑进行小团体甚至一对一的训练课程。大团
体训练是一项挑战，小团体训练也是如此。 每个都有优点和缺点。 时
间段总是会影响团体规模和训练动态。 这个问题没有好的答案。很大
程度上取决于体育教练的判断力、举重室架上设备的可用性以及举重室
的大小。如果您需要训练一大群或整个团队，您将需要更大的举重室。
您还需要更多的员工。

我们什么时候可以训练我们的运动
员？
大多数时候，你训练运动员的窗口会非常小。在淡季，您的日程安排将
更加灵活。在旺季，您的日程安排灵活性会降低。 你必须找到创造性
的方法来让你的大多数运动员在课前或课后或练习前后都得到锻炼。
这可能意味着您将有很多清晨团体和下午晚些时候团体。没有人说施恩
禧是一件容易的事。
您必须考虑其他模型才能真正理解如何解决在有限的时间内让所有运
动员都参加的问题。餐厅的结构与施恩禧团队的工作结构非常相似。
餐厅如何赚钱？ 食物、准备食物和提供食物的成本以及综合管理费用
（租金）使得盈利变得困难。 从每年有多少餐馆倒闭就可以看出这一
点。他们的早餐、午餐和晚餐时段也有限。他们每天在优化空间的同时
仍然生产高质量的产品，充满了物流瓶颈。

他们如何解决容纳更多人或从更少人身上获得更多利益的问题？ 这
是两种方法

restaurant can make money. They can figure out how to get more people to
buy their food, or they can figure out how to charge more for their food. The
cafeteria-style restaurant is the ultimate means of getting more people
through the door. You can cycle more people through by having a lot more
food created in advance and having them cycle through from start to finish.
Serving more people means you can charge less. À la carte is a way to charge
more per person by getting customers to pay for more options as they dine.
You make less food, but you have to serve fewer people. With fewer people,
you have to charge more.

Efficiency Versus Value
The restaurant model applies to us by helping us find ways to be more
efficient. We can do that by trying to get bigger weight rooms, more weight
rooms, or optimizing efficiency with training. Because changing the weight
room size or number is not that controllable, we will focus on efficiency. We
have to find ways to be more organized with everything we do. Getting more
done by simply moving things in the weight room or sequencing exercises a
certain way can be the difference between getting a complete workout and
not. We can train more athletes with larger weight rooms and more coaches,
but this may not be the optimal way to bring value. Being more organized
allows us to work with more people in a given day. This may not mean more
value, but at least we can be accessible to more people. We can increase the
efficiency of training by having larger weight rooms, more coaches, or being
more organized with our plans (figure 14.7).
We can increase the value we offer when we have the athletes, which is a
much tougher dynamic to unpack. How do we bring more value? Coaching is
one way to bring more value. More skilled coaches with higher amounts of
certifications and tenure can bring more value. Experience and knowledge do
not always mean more value, but they create the potential for it. We can
improve the coach-to-athlete ratio by decreasing the group size. Again, this
does not guarantee that we improve value, but the potential is increased. We
can increase value by altering the ratio of coaches to athletes, combined with
having more skilled coaches.

餐厅可以赚钱。 他们可以想出如何让更多的人购买他们的食物，或者
他们可以想出如何对他们的食物收取更高的费用。自助餐厅式餐厅是吸
引更多人进店的终极手段。 你可以通过提前制作更多食物并让他们从
头到尾循环来循环更多的人。为更多的人服务意味着您可以收取更少的
费用。点菜是一种提高每人收费的方式，让顾客在用餐时为更多选择付
费。你生产的食物减少了，但你必须服务的人也减少了。人少了，就要
多收费。

效率与价值
餐厅模式适用于我们，帮助我们找到提高效率的方法。 我们可以通过
尝试获得更大的举重室、更多的举重室或通过训练优化效率来做到这一
点。 因为改变举重室的大小或数量不是那么可控，所以我们将关注效
率。我们必须找到让我们所做的一切更有条理的方法。通过简单地在举
重室移动物体或以某种方式排序练习来完成更多的工作可能是获得完整
锻炼与否的区别。我们可以用更大的举重室和更多的教练来训练更多的
运动员，但这可能不是带来价值的最佳方式。 更有条理可以让我们在
一天内与更多的人一起工作。这可能并不意味着更多的价值，但至少可
以让更多的人接触到我们。我们可以通过拥有更大的举重室、更多的教
练或更有条理的计划来提高训练效率（图 14.7）。
当我们拥有运动员时，我们可以增加我们提供的价值，这是一个更难
解开的动态。我们如何带来更多价值？辅导是带来更多价值的一种方式
。 拥有更高数量的认证和终身教职的更熟练的教练可以带来更多的价
值。经验和知识并不总是意味着更多价值，但它们创造了更多价值。
我们可以通过减少团体规模来提高教练与运动员的比例。 同样，这并
不能保证我们提高价值，但潜力会增加。我们可以通过改变教练与运动
员的比例以及拥有更熟练的教练来增加价值。

Evaluating When Is Best to Train
The biggest thing within your control is your philosophy and your approach
to training. You have to efficiently accommodate all your athletes through
their training while still providing them with high value. If you are stuck on a
philosophy or system that does not allow creating an equal experience for all
athletes over the entirety of their careers, you will have to switch.
How do we evaluate if we are not efficient? A pretty simple way would be
to assess when everyone starts and finishes. If you have people finish at
different times, you will have to identify which part of the workout is slowing
certain groups down. Is there a part of the session that is moving slowly?
That delay could be the setup or the application. You have to assess if one
group can finish promptly and another cannot and what the differences are. If
the setup is good for one but not for another, it will need to become uniform.
If the application is inconsistent, staff training will need to take place.

图 14.7 效率与价值。

评估最佳训练时间
您可以控制的最重要的事情是您的理念和培训方法。 您必须有效地适
应所有运动员的训练，同时仍然为他们提供高价值。如果你坚持的理念
或体系不允许为所有运动员在整个职业生涯中创造平等的体验，你将不
得不改变。
如果我们没有效率，我们如何评价？一个非常简单的方法是评估每个
人何时开始和完成。 如果你让人们在不同的时间完成训练，你就必须
确定锻炼的哪一部分拖慢了某些群体的速度。 会议的某个部分是否进
展缓慢？该延迟可能是设置或应用程序造成的。 你必须评估一组是否
可以迅速完成而另一组则不能，以及差异是什么。如果设置对一个人有
利但对另一个人不利，则需要变得统一。如果申请不一致，则需要对员
工进行培训。

Before- or After-Practice Training
Training before or after practice is an inevitable conversation in
the team sector. What do we do if our only option is to lift after
practice? Circumstances make this a reality, and we can make
the most of the situation by becoming as efficient as possible.
Ideally, we get to train before practice. This is not uncommon,
but it is even more appreciated when you have to train after
practice for a while. When we have to train after practice, we
have to focus on what will bring the most value in the least
amount of time.
Stripping away the unnecessary elements in a training session
is important here. Focusing on what is needed, based on a larger
goal, is the most important aspect of after-practice training. This
will mean dropping a movement prep because they just practiced
for 1 to 2 h, focusing on high return on investment movements,
having modifications from injuries sustained during practice, and
adopting the most linear path to getting a good training session
after practice.
If your weight room setup is station based, it may be worth
looking into an assembly line approach. The biggest gripe with
after-practice training is staggered starts. It’s jarring to have
athletes trickle in postpractice, but if you inventory their time from
the end of practice to getting into the weight room, you can see
why an assembly line system is worth it. The coach talking to
them will delay the start time. Good players have interviews with
the media, which will delay the start time. Sustaining an injury
and having to talk to sports medicine will delay the start time.
Having the ability to come in and knock out a lift based on not
having a lot of after-practice tasks is always appreciated.
We want quality, but we want efficiency more. Playing the long
game and meeting the athletes where they are during the
season is most important. Program exercises and variables that
can be successful within a time-constrained period. Think to

练习前或练习后培训
训练之前或之后的训练是球队部门不可避免的话题。 如果我们唯
一的选择就是练习后举重，我们该怎么办？ 环境使这成为现实，
我们可以通过尽可能提高效率来充分利用这种情况。
理想情况下，我们在练习之前先进行训练。这并不罕见，但当
你必须在练习一段时间后进行训练时，这就更值得赞赏了。 当我
们必须在练习后进行训练时，我们必须专注于在最短的时间内带
来最大价值的事情。
去除培训课程中不必要的元素在这里很重要。基于更大的目标
，专注于需要的东西，是练习后训练最重要的方面。 这意味着放
弃动作准备，因为他们只练习了 1 到 2 小时，专注于投资回报率
高的动作，对练习期间受伤的情况进行修改，并在练习后采用最
线性的路径来获得良好的训练。

如果您的举重室设置是基于工作站的，那么可能值得考虑采用
装配线方法。 训练后训练最大的问题是错开开始。 运动员在训
练后缓慢地进行训练是很不舒服的，但如果你盘点一下他们从训
练结束到进入举重室的时间，你就会明白为什么装配线系统是值
得的。 教练与他们交谈将推迟开始时间。好的球员接受媒体采访
，会推迟开赛时间。 受伤并需要与运动医学人员交谈会延迟开始
时间。在没有大量练习后任务的情况下，有能力进来并完成电梯
总是值得赞赏的。

我们要品质，但更要效率。打持久战并在赛季中与运动员见面
是最重要的。 制定可以在有限时间内成功的练习和变量。 想

stimulate, not annihilate. Make the most of a less-than-perfect
situation. Your sports coaches notice you handling these things
well. Over time, they value your contribution more and will ask if
you want to start lifting before practice.
How do we evaluate if we are not bringing value? It is a fight to find
objectivity. We need to revisit our appraisal: improvement, standards, and
accountability. Finding objectivity with those criteria is the best way to
determine the relative value we bring. We will not be perfect every day. We
are looking for an understanding of the level we need to achieve to ensure we
are bringing value each day. If our coaches do not understand, we need to
educate them. If they are not executing on something they do understand, we
need to train them. Education and training based on objective criteria are the
best tools to determine value daily.
The lowered ceiling of adaptation from reduced efficiency and diminished
value based on the philosophy you have means you will have to change your
philosophy. More specifically, evolve your philosophy. When evaluating
anything, ask yourself if this is something we can fix. If we cannot fix the
issue, we need to reconsider the reasons behind our initial choice. If we
cannot do Olympic lifts because we do not have enough platforms, we have
to develop power in other ways. If we cannot do speed work due to not
having enough space to run, we have to develop speed in other ways.
A restaurant will have to change its menu to accommodate what it can
prepare at a high level at a high frequency. What we do determines how well
we can do it and how quickly we can do it. If we have a large group of
athletes, a low number of coaches, and a small weight room, we will have to
distill what we do to focus on what brings value as efficiently as possible.
The evolution of a program is necessary for survival.

How Many Coaches Do You Have in Total?
The number of coaches working in the weight room is probably the most
important thing you will have to consider. It is the most important because
they represent what you can do regarding programming.

我们所做的事情决定了我们能做得多好以及我们能做多快。 如果我们

你们一共有多少位教练？
在举重室工作的教练数量可能是您必须考虑的最重要的事情。 这是最
重要的，因为它们代表了您可以在编程方面做什么。

More than any other factor, the number of
coaches you have will most affect the level of
detail your program can have.

Value of Coaches
Think of the value and efficiency with which you run your program. Value is
single-handedly the most important aspect of having a certain number of
coaches. You can simply do more when you have more coaches. The detail
you can bring to your program is amplified based on the number of coaches
you have.
Another model is car manufacturing. We are familiar with the Fordism
model and assembly line manufacturing. Developing a system of highvolume output is foundational to the car industry. Compare that to cars that
focus more on craftsmanship. What is the difference between the two from a
process standpoint? The assembly line model finds ways to automate or
simplify very repeatable processes to increase efficiency. The craftsmanshipbased system focuses not on efficiency but on quality. The output is more
about craftsmanship, which requires more craftsmen.
A program is always filtered through the coaches who are coaching it. We
can only implement programs that we can coach. If we are limited by the
number of coaches we have, we are limited by the program we can do. There
is a linear correlation between the details of a program and the number of
coaches we have. The potential value we bring is based on the number of
coaches.
There is absolutely a skill component to the coaches we have regarding
value. Coaches with limited experience, lesser skill, and limited knowledge
bring less value than experienced, more skilled, and more knowledgeable
coaches. Yes, we want coaches with as much experience, skill, and
knowledge as possible, but that should not come at the expense of the number
of coaches. The number of coaches we have relative to the number of athletes
we have will have the most impact on value.
Coaching is redundant; experience is gained quickly. A person coaching

详细程度影响最大。

想想您运行程序的价值和效率。价值是拥有一定数量的教练最重要的方
面。 当你有更多教练时，你可以做得更多。 您可以为计划提供的细节
会根据您拥有的教练数量而放大。
另一种模式是汽车制造。 我们熟悉福特主义模式和流水线制造。 开
发大批量输出系统是汽车工业的基础。 与更注重工艺的汽车相比。从
流程的角度来看，两者有什么区别？ 装配线模型找到了自动化或简化
重复性极高的流程的方法，以提高效率。以工匠精神为基础的体系不注
重效率，而注重质量。 产出更多的是工艺，这就需要更多的工匠。

一个项目总是要经过指导该项目的教练的筛选。我们只能实施我们可
以指导的计划。 如果我们受到教练数量的限制，那么我们能做的项目
也会受到限制。项目的细节和我们拥有的教练数量之间存在线性相关性
。 我们带来的潜在价值取决于教练的数量。
我们的教练的价值绝对是有技能成分的。 经验有限、技能较差、知
识有限的教练所带来的价值低于经验丰富、技术更高、知识更丰富的教

应以牺牲教练的数量为代价。我们拥有的教练数量相对于我们拥有的运
动员数量将对价值产生最大的影响。
辅导是多余的； 经验获得得很快。 一个人辅导

multiple athletes who play several different sports will develop coaching
skills. There is too much information that is easily obtained not to gain
knowledge rapidly. My point is that the ability of the coaches we have can be
improved, but the number of coaches may not. Focus on getting as many
coaches as you can to amplify the value you can bring.

Coach-to-Athlete Ratio
What is the appropriate athlete-to-coach ratio? This is not an easy question to
answer. You poll 100 different coaches, and you will get 100 different
answers. Often, you will not have much control over how many coaches you
have. But you will have control over the number of athletes you can train at a
given time. If you want to have a high-value program and you have a limited
number of coaches, you will have to increase the number of sessions to keep
the number of athletes per session down. But there is a limit to how many
groups you can run. If you still have a poor athlete-to-coach ratio after adding
as many groups as you can, you will have to either add more coaches or
lower the details of your program.
A good number to work from is how many rack stations you have.
Keeping with the theme of three, we can use that number for how many
coaches we need. If we have three athletes per rack, a coach can be effective
with three racks. You then take the total number of racks and divide by three
to get the necessary number of coaches. For example, if we have twelve
racks, we will need four coaches.
That ratio would be poor if you were attempting to implement a very
complicated protocol. It would be overkill if you were implementing a very
simple program. A one-to-nine athlete-to-coach ratio is not a perfect answer
for every program. It is a start to asking more questions about how many staff
members you need to fully optimize your weight room or write a program
that you think will bring high value.
If you were to run assembly line fashion, you would need to break down
the number of coaches based on the number of stations you will run during a
session. The number of stations represents how many coaches you will need
during a training session. In theory, you may only need that many coaches,
but you will have to consider breaks, setup, and breakdown. Instead of

参加多种不同运动项目的多名运动员将培养教练技能。 有太多容易获
得的信息，无法快速获取知识。我的观点是，我们教练的能力可以提高
，但教练的数量却不一定。 专注于获得尽可能多的教练，以放大你可
以带来的价值。

教练与运动员比率
适当的运动员与教练的比例是多少？这不是一个容易回答的问题。 你

多少教练没有太多控制权。但您可以控制在给定时间可以训练的运动员
数量。如果你想要一个高价值的项目，而你的教练数量有限，你就必须
增加训练次数，以减少每次训练的运动员人数。 但您可以运行的组数
量是有限的。如果在添加尽可能多的团体后，运动员与教练的比例仍然
很差，那么您将不得不添加更多教练或降低计划的细节。

例如您需要多少员工来全面优化举重室或编写您认为会带来高价值的计

论上，你可能只需要那么多教练，但你必须考虑休息、准备和故障。

A high-quality car manufactured with high-quality craftsmanship takes
time and puts a limit on how many cars can be manufactured in a year. In
S&C, we need to evaluate the craftsmanship of our programs. We need as
many coaches as we can get to write the programs that will bring the most
value.

What Equipment Will You Need?
You may be wondering why I would save what equipment we will need for
last. It comes down to understanding what we can control, what we will need,
and how well we can do something.
The continuum goes from having a large weight room, a small number of
athletes who can train when you want them to, and an abundance of coaches
to the opposite (figures 14.8 and 14.9). Having small weight rooms, a large
number of athletes, limited times to train, and a small number of coaches is
more often our reality. Therefore, we need to close any gaps we may have
with equipment.

Fact Versus Fiction
The reality we have has a huge influence on the programming we can do and
how we design our weight room. Such conditions force us to simplify our
program, find simpler tools to execute our program, or combine both
approaches to bring value through higher execution. Think of a protocol of
three sets of 10 reps on a leg press versus doing 6, 4, 2, 6, 4, 2 with a 5/0/x/0
tempo on a heels elevated cambered bar squat—which will be easier to
execute? If we have a small number of coaches with a large number of
athletes, the compromise will be to what the athlete can understand, not what
the coach can do.

仅考虑会话长度，添加 30 到 60 分钟以适应整个会话所需的时间。 如
果 60 分钟内有四个站，则需要四辆教练车，再加上两辆用于休息，使
教练车总数达到六辆。
一辆采用高品质工艺制造的高品质汽车需要时间，并且一年可以生产
的汽车数量受到限制。 在施恩禧，我们需要评估我们程序的工艺。 我
们需要尽可能多的教练来编写能够带来最大价值的程序。

解我们可以控制什么、我们需要什么以及我们能把某件事做得有多好。
这个连续体从拥有一个大的举重室、少数可以在你想要的时候训练的
运动员、以及大量的教练到相反的情况（图 14.8 和 14.9）。 举重室狭

。 因此，我们需要弥补设备方面可能存在的任何差距。

事实与虚构
我们所面临的现实对我们可以进行的编程以及我们如何设计举重室有着
巨大的影响。 这种情况迫使我们简化程序，找到更简单的工具来执行
程序，或者结合这两种方法通过更高的执行带来价值。 想象一下腿举
三组，每组 10 次，与脚后跟抬高弧形杠深蹲以 5/0/x/0 节奏做 6、4、2
、6、4、2 次相比，哪个更容易执行？ 如果我们的教练人数较少而运动
员人数较多，那么妥协的重点就是运动员能理解什么，而不是教练能做
什么。

The number of periods we can train is a factor to consider as well. The

What You Will Actually Need
We start with the rack and build out from there. That is the hub from which
everything, and subsequently everyone (coaches and athletes), works. With
the rack, we can accommodate four primary movements: push, pull, hinge,
and squat. Traditionally, this is done through a barbell, which means we
would need a barbell and plates (metal or bumper, or both) for each rack.
Additionally, we would need a vertical pull with a pull-up bar, a dip
attachment, and a roller pad for glute-ham exercises (figure 14.10).
This setup leads to difficulties with relative strength exercise. It is harder

to scale bodyweight exercises with large groups based on two big

Having machines or pieces of equipment that are focused on an isolated
joint action is a departure from having high-utility pieces like a rack. The
higher the utility of something, the less direct a function it can have. We trade
a wide variety of exercises for the specific development of all exercises.
Understanding gaps in programming choices is a foundation for equipment
selection. Equipment is the equivalent of tools for a contractor. There are so
many jobs that need to be done, but only so many tools that can be used. We
need the right equipment to do the job.
Having an assortment of tools such as dumbbells, medicine balls,
kettlebells, clubs, or maces is always valuable (figure 14.11 and figure
14.12). You will run into bottlenecks with these tools, which is inevitable

when you have a fixed load option, which would lead to exploring adjustable

There are definite specialty options we can consider, such as machines;

question is, can all my coaches coach these specialty items?
The options to load patterns of joints are endless now. A better question is,
what will bring the most value? We can explore these options, but will they
bring value relative to doubling down on what you may already have?
Finding gaps in your program justifies exploring options that help address
those gaps. There are unique problems we face every day as strength coaches,
and there is a tool that can help us with that. The secret is objectively
evaluating what you do not do well and then finding the right tool for the job.
Last is the durability component. The unspoken aspect of buying
equipment is that it does not need to be durable; chances are, you will not last

difficult to care about. As a business owner, it matters; as a college strength

Your weight room is your workshop! You can develop the athletes you’ve

the athletes who enter. There is a symbiotic relationship between the weight

before you make any decisions on what to buy.

TESTING
This book would not be complete without a discussion on sports science or
the integration of testing hardware and software, interpretation, and
implementation within an athletic department. The reality is that anything I
write will likely be obsolete or even irrelevant in a very short period due to
the constant change occurring in sports science. With that said, this chapter
will serve a greater purpose regarding how to integrate and leverage testing
and interpretation in your setting. Instead of deciding what hardware to use or
what software to integrate, we will look at why, how, and when we should
test and then decide what to do with that information. This chapter is divided
into three parts: testing rationale, testing logistics, and testing interpretation.

Testing Rationale
We are biased and easily persuaded by our personal preferences or social
group. With that said, we have logic and reason. This makes both humans
and technology necessary. We cannot be eliminated by technology, and
technology cannot function without us.
In my second book, How to Become a Strength Coach, I presented the
case that there is a 30% to 40% chance machine learning will replace what
we know but not what we do. The rationale for this is based on our not using
logic and reasoning to make choices but preference and bias. We are making
absolute decisions based on incomplete knowledge of what we are working

测试
如果没有对运动科学或测试硬件和软件的集成、解释以及在运动部门内
的实施的讨论，本书就不完整。 现实情况是，由于运动科学不断发生
变化，我写的任何东西都可能在很短的时间内过时甚至无关紧要。 话
虽如此，本章将服务于如何在您的环境中集成和利用测试和解释的更大
目的。我们不会决定使用什么硬件或集成什么软件，而是研究为什么、
如何以及何时应该测试，然后决定如何处理这些信息。本章分为三个部
分：测试原理、测试逻辑和测试解释。

测试原理
我们有偏见，很容易被个人偏好或社会群体说服。 话虽如此，我们有
逻辑和理由。 这使得人类和技术都变得必要。 我们不能被技术消灭，
技术没有我们也无法发挥作用。
在我的第二本书 How to Become a Strength Coach 中，我提出了这样
一个案例：机器学习有 30% 到 40% 的机会取代我们所知道的，但不会
取代我们所做的。这样做的理由是我们不使用逻辑和推理来做出选择，
而是使用偏好和偏见。我们基于对我们正在工作的不完全了解而做出绝
对决定

with. We need an unbiased third party that can be set to specific parameters
to make the most informed decisions possible. We test to add objectivity to
decision-making.
What machine learning cannot do is replace our ability to apply context
and connect with and coach our athletes. Machines provide information,
whether you agree with it or not; they probably provide the most logical
description of what is happening and therefore what we should do. The
ability to discern between what is necessary and what is wanted is too
important to rely solely on human intuition. As things stand today, we can get
away with relying on human intuition with programming, but that will cease
to be the case the more machine learning understands what is needed.

Appraisal of the Best Program
So what does testing give us that we cannot get from our general
observations? One thing is a clear indication of what we are good at versus
what we are bad at. We have talked about what training is supposed to be, but
we have not talked about how it should be structured. We can focus on
developing weaknesses to increase general ability, starting at the beginning
with our screens and using that as the foundation for our programming. We
can focus on reverse engineering from a predetermined peaking perspective
of what we want through training, starting at the end, and structuring training
to meet that goal. Both can be right; testing allows us to choose correctly.
We need testing to be objective and clear about what path to take. I prefer
to have a general athletic profile to establish that athletes have a better skills
foundation. If someone can run faster, jump higher or further, and project an
implement higher or further, that athlete is more capable within their sport.
Training should correspond with the sport it is associated with. We cannot
say we have the athlete’s best performance unless we commit to testing that
corresponds to the sport they play.
However, there are two perspectives on testing. One perspective is to
consider the baseline conditions and limitations of the athlete and write a
program based on developing weaknesses. Another perspective is that testing
serves as a determinant of the relative difference between the beginning and
end ability to write a program to a specific target. We can say that one

和。 我们需要一个公正的第三方，可以设置特定的参数，以做出最明
智的决策。 我们尝试增加决策的客观性。
机器学习无法取代我们应用情境以及与运动员联系和指导的能力。
机器提供信息，无论你是否同意； 它们可能对正在发生的事情以及我
们应该做什么提供了最合乎逻辑的描述。 区分什么是必要的和什么是
想要的的能力太重要了，不能仅仅依靠人类的直觉。就目前的情况来看
，我们可以摆脱依赖人类直觉进行编程的情况，但随着机器学习对需求
的了解越多，这种情况就不再是这样了。

最佳节目评选
那么，测试给了我们什么是我们无法从一般观察中得到的呢？ 一件事
是清楚地表明我们擅长什么和不擅长什么。我们已经讨论了培训应该是
什么，但我们还没有讨论培训应该如何构建。 我们可以专注于开发弱
点以提高综合能力，从我们的屏幕开始，并将其作为我们编程的基础。
我们可以通过培训从预定的峰值角度专注于逆向工程，从最后开始，并
构建培训来实现该目标。两者都可能是正确的；测试使我们能够做出正
确的选择。
我们需要进行客观且明确的测试，以明确要采取的路径。我更喜欢有
一个一般的运动概况，以确定运动员有更好的技能基础。如果某人跑得
更快，跳得更高或更远，并将器械投射得更高或更远，那么该运动员在
其运动中的能力就更强。训练应与其相关的运动相对应。 除非我们致
力于与他们所从事的运动相对应的测试，否则我们不能说我们拥有运动
员的最佳表现。
然而，对于测试有两种观点。 一种观点是考虑运动员的基线条件和
限制，并根据发展的弱点编写计划。另一种观点是，测试是针对特定目
标编写程序的开始能力和最终能力之间的相对差异的决定因素。 我们
可以说，一个

method is running away from the beginning, whereas the other method is
running toward the end.

Evaluation of Your Program’s Execution
We want to approach every day as if it was a testing day to instill the effort it
takes to achieve high performance. However, no two athletes will respond to
training the same. This will mean that all athletes will develop at different
rates. What is important is that we are executing with standard technique. We
are instilling the value of approaching each day with the requisite effort it
takes, but that is relative to the standard required to determine that effort was
actually productive. You are constantly working forward and backward.
Adaptation does not operate on a linear timescale, and therefore,
programming does not either. The only thing that we can actually control is
the effort and execution of technique each day.
If we are demanding a high standard with training every day, then we need
to expect the same from actual testing. Testing execution needs to be intact so
we can determine if our approach was appropriate. The fundamental aspect
for testing is understanding whether you had a positive impact on the athlete.
The premise that we should expect positive outcomes and that there is no
need to test is false. If that were the case, then everyone, including your
opponents, would expect positive outcomes. We reframe the logic of being
simply better with how much more something could have been better. It’s all
net positive; the difference is how much net positive it is relative to the
baseline. The better program is not the one that improves without context.
The better program is the one that improves relative to the baseline or
objective and by how much.

Progress Review
Testing is a predetermined proxy to determine the amount and rate of change.
The extent to which we can change something that we have predetermined as
valuable is important. Being better at your job has a direct influence on the
teams and athletes you work with. How fast you get your testing results
matters. Being able to produce faster has a tremendous impact on overall
outcomes. You test to determine how much and how long it takes to achieve

要。 能够更快地生产会对整体结果产生巨大影响。您进行测试以确定
实现目标需要多少时间和时间

Every Day Is Testing Day
The most improbable thing in strength and conditioning is every
athlete peaking in competition at the same time. We build a large
part of our program from a certain peak in the weight room, but
that is potentially a huge missed opportunity for the approach to
training.
Building up to a peak in the weight room for all athletes at a
specific time is a fool’s errand. It prioritizes the means as the
ends, or the methods over the goals. The only peak that matters
is competition. This mindset should not diminish the value of
maximal effort and the importance of leveraging it within training.
We have such limited training windows that we cannot afford
not to maximize each session. Arbitrarily saying one day of
training is more important than another based on its position on a
calendar is a significant missed opportunity. The better approach
is to treat every day as a testing day but alter the upper limit an
athlete can train with.
Imagine a scenario where every training session was treated
with the same level of focus and intensity as a testing day. If the
training session is the same intensity as a testing day, the risk
outweighs the reward. If the intensity is lowered, the reward
outweighs the risk. The trick of it all is to focus on training
intention each day you have the opportunity to train. Never turn
the switch off; just dim the light from time to time.
Putting governors on each day is the key to allowing for
maximal intent with training. Choosing exercises and methods
that limit absolute intensity is the means of governing training.
When an athlete hits a personal record, that is their testing day.
It will happen on a day you did not plan for. That should not
count against the athlete.
The mentality of approaching each day as a testing day is how

the desired amount: Your “better” is better than theirs.

每一天都是测试日
体能训练中最不可能的事情是每位运动员同时在比赛中达到巅峰
。我们计划的很大一部分是从举重室的某个峰值开始制定的，但
这对于训练方法来说可能是一个巨大的错失机会。
对于所有运动员来说，在特定时间在举重室达到顶峰是一件愚
蠢的事。 它优先考虑手段作为目的，或者优先考虑方法优先于目
标。唯一重要的高峰是竞争。 这种心态不应削弱最大努力的价值
以及在训练中利用最大努力的重要性。
我们的培训窗口非常有限，我们不能不最大化每次训练。 根据
日历上的位置武断地说某一天的训练比另一天的训练更重要是一
个重大的错失机会。更好的方法是将每一天都视为测试日，但改
变运动员可以训练的上限。
想象一下这样一个场景，每次训练课程都受到与测试日相同水
平的关注和强度。如果训练课程的强度与测试日的强度相同，则
风险大于回报。 如果强度降低，回报将超过风险。 这一切的秘
诀是每天有机会训练时都专注于训练意图。 切勿关闭开关；只是
时不时调暗灯光。
每天安排调速者是实现训练最大意图的关键。 选择限制绝对强
度的练习和方法是控制训练的手段。当一名运动员打破个人纪录
时，那就是他们的考验日。它会在你没有计划的一天发生。 这不
应该对运动员不利。
把每一天都当作考验日来对待的心态是怎样的

you capitalize on limited training frequency. Periodically, you
have good and bad days. Both are treated the same way,
training with the utmost intent. The most important thing you can
do is approach each day with a clear objective, keep training
intent as high as possible, and adjust the intensity to be able to
train as if each day were a testing day.
Training with maximal intent is training to peak during
competition. Competition, being the most important aspect of
peaking, will require a general approach of treating every day as
a testing day. We train to peak during competition by attempting
to peak every day.
As with exercise technique, testing execution matters. To do that, we need
to have processes to ensure tests are executed properly. We need to talk about
what, when, where, and how to work out the testing logistics. We then need
to ensure we are using the data to improve our programming. Believing in
testing is not enough to get value from testing.
Once we have established that the testing was executed properly, we need
to review its efficacy. Making progress is the goal, and if we are executing
our plan, the only thing left is to evaluate our programming decisions. The
process of making decisions on exercises and corresponding variables needs
to be assessed and compared to the progress our athletes make. Not making
progress or not making enough progress reflects poor decisions. We want to
make progress because of our contribution, not despite it. Taking on the
responsibility of achieving a great outcome is the pressure you need to place
on yourself as a coach.
We want to see not only the amount of progress but also the rate. You will
find that all athletes adapt at different rates. We want to make an impact on
all, not some, and we have the means to determine when an athlete’s peak
was, which is a metric that is as important as the outcome. Keeping pre- and
posttest results and daily, weekly, and monthly changes is necessary to
evaluate the level of progress your athletes make.

您可以利用有限的培训频率。 每隔一段时间，你就会有好日子和
坏日子。 两者都受到同样的对待，都以最大的意图进行训练。你
能做的最重要的事情就是每天都有一个明确的目标，尽可能保持
高强度的训练意图，并调整强度，以便能够像每天都是测试日一
样进行训练。
最大意图的训练是在比赛中达到巅峰的训练。 竞争是达到顶峰
最重要的方面，需要采取一种将每一天都视为测试日的通用方法
。我们每天都尝试达到峰值，从而在比赛期间进行训练。

与锻炼技巧一样，测试执行力也很重要。为此，我们需要有流程来确
保测试正确执行。我们需要讨论测试的内容、时间、地点以及如何制定
测试流程。 然后我们需要确保我们正在使用这些数据来改进我们的编
程。 相信测试并不足以从测试中获得价值。
一旦我们确定测试执行正确，我们就需要审查其有效性。 取得进展
是我们的目标，如果我们正在执行我们的计划，那么剩下的唯一事情就
是评估我们的编程决策。 需要评估练习和相应变量的决策过程，并将
其与运动员取得的进步进行比较。 没有取得进展或没有取得足够的进
展反映了错误的决策。 我们希望因为我们的贡献而取得进步，而不是
尽管有贡献。 作为教练，承担取得伟大成果的责任是你需要给自己施
加的压力。
我们不仅希望看到进展的数量，还希望看到进展的速度。你会发现所
有运动员的适应速度都不同。 我们希望对所有人而不是某些人产生影
响，并且我们有办法确定运动员的巅峰时间，这是一个与结果同样重要
的指标。保留测试前和测试后的结果以及每日、每周和每月的变化对于
评估运动员的进步水平是必要的。

Testing Logistics
What testing should accomplish matters a great deal to what and how we test.
Most of us will find ourselves in situations where we are understaffed and
overworked. Therefore, we need testing to be an asset, not a liability. We
have to use testing to make ourselves more effective at our jobs. At the same
time, testing needs to be efficient and reliable so it can make us better at our
jobs without making our jobs harder.
Here is what we should hope for from testing:
Training session
– Give some level of readiness for training
– Give some feedback during training on what is too much or too fast
– Give some idea of how hard a training session was to help
determine what to do next
Microcycle
– Give some indication of the week-to-week impact of training
Mesocycle
– Give context on how much and how fast something has changed
Macrocycle
– Determine how effective the training was
We want to think of testing within different time intervals. Things that
happen daily have a completely different set of logistics compared to those
that happen weekly, monthly, or annually. Think of this as brushing your
teeth multiple times a day, every day, versus going to the dentist. Brushing
your teeth requires toothpaste, a toothbrush, and a ritual around brushing to
ensure you do it. Going to the dentist is a completely different process that
involves insurance, scheduling, travel, and working with an actual dentist.
We have training sessions for testing, microcycle testing, mesocycle testing,
baseline testing, and posttesting (figure 15.1).

检测物流
测试应该完成什么对于我们测试什么以及如何测试非常重要。我们大多
数人都会发现自己处于人手不足和工作过度的境地。 因此，我们需要
将测试变成一种资产，而不是一种负债。 我们必须使用测试来提高自
己的工作效率。同时，测试需要高效、可靠，这样才能让我们更好地完
成工作，而不会让我们的工作变得更加困难。
这是我们希望从测试中得到的结果：
培训课程 – 为培训做好一定程度的准备 – 在培训期间就什么太
多或太快提供一些反馈 – 说明培训课程的难度如何，以帮助确定
下一个做什么 微周期 – 说明培训中周周期的影响 – 给出有关事
物变化的程度和速度的背景信息 宏观周期 – 确定培训的有效性

我们想要考虑在不同的时间间隔内进行测试。 与每周、每月或每年
发生的事情相比，每天发生的事情有一套完全不同的物流。 可以将其
视为每天多次刷牙，而不是去看牙医。 刷牙需要牙膏、牙刷和刷牙仪
式来确保你刷牙。 去看牙医是一个完全不同的过程，涉及保险、日程
安排、旅行以及与真正的牙医一起工作。我们有测试、微循环测试、中
循环测试、基线测试和后测试的培训课程（图15.1）。

FIGURE 15.1 Training session testing.

Training Session
The shortest interval is the training session. Within that training session, we
need to know the athlete’s readiness to train, determine if the volume,
duration, intensity, and density are accomplishing their intended goals, and
evaluate the session’s difficulty. This will break into pre-, intra-, and
posttraining. Understanding why we are testing and what we are trying to
achieve gives us a chance to be successful.
With testing, think of the bottleneck first. When will this become too
much work relative to the value of the information? Think less about yourself
and more about the coaches who will administer the tests and the athletes
who will do the tests. It could simply be their understanding of why they are
doing the tests. It could be that they see the test results periodically. It could
be having a setup that makes it easy on everyone. It is important that
everyone involved understands why they are testing and what the tests are
saying and that it is as easy as possible to set up and test.
We will break up the training session testing into three phases:

图 15.1 训练课程测试。

培训课程
最短的间隔是训练课程。 在训练中，我们需要了解运动员的训练准备
情况，确定训练量、持续时间、强度和密度是否达到预期目标，并评估
训练的难度。 这将分为训练前、训练中和训练后。 了解我们为什么要
进行测试以及我们想要实现的目标让我们有机会取得成功。
通过测试，首先考虑瓶颈。 相对于信息的价值来说，什么时候这会
变得太多的工作？少考虑自己，多考虑负责测试的教练和进行测试的运
动员。这可能只是他们对为什么要做测试的理解。他们可能会定期查看
测试结果。可能有一个让每个人都能轻松完成的设置。 重要的是，每
个参与人员都了解他们为什么要进行测试以及测试的内容，并且设置和
测试要尽可能简单。
我们将培训课程测试分为三个阶段：

preworkout, intraworkout, and postworkout. For preworkout, we want to
know what their potential is for that workout. For intraworkout, we want to
know how well training is going. For postworkout, we want to know the sum
of what we did. Essentially, we want to make each day as valuable as
possible. Testing is a key to bridging the gap from simply training to treating
every opportunity to train as a test.
Preworkout, we want to understand the athlete’s potential for the day by
determining their readiness. Readiness is an idea of what that athlete is
capable of on that day. We break down readiness into subjective wellness and
CNS (central nervous system) readiness. The idea is that we understand how
the athlete is feeling and their potential on that given day (figure 15.2).
Wellness gives us something to work from regarding how the athlete is
feeling about the upcoming training session. We are looking for trends and
deviations from those trends. We often view training as a completely
physiological entity, but it is not. Having a proxy for how the athlete feels
before we start is important. We want to establish that it is expected to be
sore or tired from training. We can better explain the need for something like
a deload week, low days, or critical drop-off during the session. Wellness has
a sweet spot based on the training week within the block. The total score
should be lowered following continuous loading. If it was not, we could have
gone harder.
Central nervous system readiness is an important thing to understand, but
there are some logistics to consider. A common CNS readiness assessment is
CMJ (countermovement jump). A question that often comes with CMJ
pretraining sessions is how effective jump testing is without a warm-up. It is
a fair point, but it does not take into account the ability to be reliable and
consistent with testing over the entire training block. If the best time to test
CMJ is when the athlete enters the facility, and it doubles to track attendance
and body mass, then that is the best time. The result might not be their best,
but the process is the most realistic for our setup and staff.

锻炼前、锻炼中和锻炼后。 对于训练前，我们想知道他们在训练中的
潜力。 对于训练内，我们想知道训练进行得如何。对于锻炼后，我们
想知道我们做了什么。 本质上，我们希望让每一天都尽可能有价值。
测试是弥合从简单培训到将每一次培训机会都视为测试之间差距的关键
。
训练前，我们希望通过确定运动员的准备情况来了解他们当天的潜力
。 准备状态是指运动员当天的能力。我们将准备度分为主观健康度和
CNS（中枢神经系统）准备度。我们的想法是，我们了解运动员在那一
天的感受和潜力（图 15.2）。
健康为我们提供了一些帮助我们了解运动员对即将到来的训练的感受
的东西。 我们正在寻找趋势以及与这些趋势的偏差。 我们经常将训练
视为一个完全生理的实体，但事实并非如此。 在开始之前了解运动员
的感受非常重要。 我们想要确定它会因训练而感到疼痛或疲劳。我们
可以更好地解释诸如减负荷周、低潮日或训练期间严重下降之类的需求
。根据街区内的训练周，健康有一个最佳点。 连续加载后总分应降低
。如果不是，我们可能会更加努力。

中枢神经系统的准备情况是需要了解的重要事项，但也需要考虑一些
后勤工作。常见的中枢神经系统准备状态评估是 CMJ（反向运动跳跃）
。 CMJ 预训练课程中经常出现的一个问题是，在没有热身的情况下，
跳跃测试的效果如何。这是一个公平的观点，但它没有考虑到整个训练
块测试的可靠性和一致性的能力。 如果测试 CMJ 的最佳时间是运动员
进入设施时，并且加倍跟踪出勤率和体重，那么那就是最佳时间。结果
可能不是他们最好的，但过程对于我们的设置和员工来说是最现实的。

FIGURE 15.2 Subjective wellness.
What we want is to see the residual impact of training, practice, and
competition on the nervous system. Most acute drops in performance will be
attributed to the CNS being in a heightened state for extended periods. We
can attempt to predict what the athlete can do based on prior acute workloads,
but there is considerable uncertainty with that. It is better to assess CNS
readiness with a weekly jump or a less invasive test, such as grip strength.
The next phase is intratraining, where we want to determine how well the
session is going. We want to focus on what we can control, from the rep out
to the set for each training session. Here is the catch: The intensity or load
being used needs to reach a certain threshold to create adaptation. We want to
lift with the predetermined technique, full range of motion, and a certain body

图 15.2 主观健康。
我们想要的是看到训练、练习和比赛对神经系统的残余影响。大多数
表现急剧下降是由于中枢神经系统长时间处于高度紧张状态。 我们可
以尝试根据之前的急性负荷来预测运动员可以做什么，但这存在相当大
的不确定性。 最好通过每周跳跃或侵入性较小的测试（例如握力）来
评估中枢神经系统的准备情况。
下一阶段是内部培训，我们想要确定课程的进展情况。我们希望专注
于我们可以控制的事情，从每次训练的代表到组数。 问题是：所使用
的强度或负荷需要达到一定的阈值才能产生适应。我们希望以预定的技
术、全方位的动作和一定的身体来举重

position. But that standard of technique is of value if the challenge from the
intensity is enough to stimulate adaptation.
We discussed relative intensity to determine progressive overload (see
figure 4.7 on page 61). The other half of relative intensity is reps in reserve,
which is based on the principle that the higher the relative intensity, the fewer
reps you will have in reserve. A relative intensity above 90% is a threshold
weight, which means the athlete should not be able to complete more than
four reps. Maintaining technique is determined at an intensity greater than
90%.
We want to use a method relatable to what an athlete understands. Reps in
reserve are easier to communicate than working from a relative intensity. One
of the first things to assess is whether the athlete is using adequate intensity
based on the stage of the training block. Asking the athlete in week four of
four, “How many reps could you have hit that for?” can rapidly determine if
the weight was adequate or not. That is built upon the foundation of good
technique. If the athlete’s technique has declined during a set, the weight is
too heavy.

FIGURE 15.3 Rep brackets.
The second means to assess the execution of a set is staying within a rep
bracket (figure 15.3). When we use threshold weight, we need to make a
target of the number of reps we programmed. The intensity represents the

位置。 但如果强度的挑战足以刺激适应，那么这种技术标准就有价值
。
我们讨论了相对强度以确定渐进性超负荷（参见第 61 页的图 4.7）。
相对强度的另一半是备用次数，其原理是相对强度越高，备用次数越少
。 高于 90% 的相对强度是阈值重量，这意味着运动员不能完成超过四
次。 维持技术是在强度大于90%时确定的。

我们希望使用一种与运动员理解相关的方法。后备代表比相对强度的
工作更容易沟通。首先要评估的事情之一是运动员是否根据训练阶段使
用了足够的强度。 在第四周的第四周询问运动员：“你能打多少次？
”可以快速判断重量是否足够。 这是建立在良好技术的基础上的。 如
果运动员的技术在一组中有所下降，则说明重量过重。

图 15.3 代表括号。
评估一组表现的第二种方法是保持在次数范围内（图 15.3）。 当我
们使用阈值重量时，我们需要为我们编程的重复次数设定一个目标。
强度代表

potential adaptation. Volume is the vehicle for that adaptation to occur. If we
miss the rep number, the intensity we use becomes irrelevant. If we miss the
rep bracket by not being able to hit the prescribed number, the set is
unsuccessful. We can also lump being able to hit more reps than the rep
bracket as unsuccessful.
Time under tension (TUT) is the time it takes to finish the set. A rep is not
just concentric, isometric, and eccentric contractions. It is a representation of
time. If we prescribe a certain number of reps, that should correspond to a
certain amount of time. Changing the concentric velocity can make a higher
rep set move faster, which decreases the total TUT. That will mean the same
amount of work from a displacement perspective, but less metabolic stress. If
we are trying to create a certain outcome of hypertrophy or increased
capacity, the duration matters. Time under tension multiplied by the rep
bracket is another means to determine set success.
The next intraworkout metric to track is velocity (figure 15.4). You can
look at velocity zones to target a specific quality, such as velocity or force,
which is the intended use. There is a means to look at loading and create
brackets for the athlete to work within. If it is too slow, it is too heavy. If it is
too fast, it is too light. That is true for all velocity zones.

潜在的适应。容量是这种适应发生的载体。如果我们错过了重复次数，
我们使用的强度就变得无关紧要。如果我们因未能达到规定的次数而错
过代表组，则该组比赛不成功。 我们也可以将能够达到比代表范围更
多的次数视为不成功。
Time under tension(TUT) 是完成该组所需的时间。一次代表不仅仅是
同心、等长和离心收缩。它是时间的表示。 如果我们规定了一定的重
复次数，那么它应该对应于一定的时间。 改变同心速度可以使更高次
数组移动得更快，从而减少总 TUT。从位移的角度来看，这意味着相同
的工作量，但代谢压力更少。如果我们试图创造某种肥大或容量增加的
结果，那么持续时间很重要。 紧张时间乘以次数范围是确定一组成功
的另一种方法。
下一个要跟踪的锻炼内指标是速度（图 15.4）。 您可以查看速度区
域来定位特定的质量，例如速度或力，这是预期用途。 有一种方法可
以查看负载并为运动员创建一个可以在其中工作的支架。如果太慢，则
太重。如果太快，则太轻。对于所有速度区都是如此。

FIGURE 15.4 Velocity brackets.
Reps in reserve and rep brackets are both a judgment call. The athlete has
a say in how heavy something feels with reps in reserve. The coach has a say
in whether the athlete maintains technique within rep brackets. It is supposed
to be as objective as possible, and both have some element of objectivity but
not completely, which can be a strain on both the coach and the athlete.
Remember, we will be working with large groups and a small number of
coaches in a team setting. We need to build trust and allow for autonomy for
both the athletes and all coaches. But that comes with a chance of
discrepancy from one training session to the next.
Velocity-based training is the one true objective rep-based parameter we
have, which can be a relief for the staff implementing a program. Telling an
