后备代表和代表括号中的代表都是一个判断。运动员对备用次数的感
觉有发言权。教练对运动员是否在次数范围内保持技术有发言权。它应
该尽可能客观，两者都具有一定的客观性，但不完全客观，这可能会给
教练和运动员带来压力。请记住，我们将在团队环境中与大型团体和少
数教练合作。我们需要建立信任并允许运动员和所有教练拥有自主权。
但这可能会导致一次训练与下一次训练之间存在差异。

基于速度的培训是我们拥有的一个真正客观的基于代表的参数，这可
以让实施计划的员工松一口气。讲述一个

athlete their technique was suboptimal is important. Telling an athlete their
technique was suboptimal due to poor weight selection is challenging.
Athletes are competitors, so they will perceive the cause-and-effect
relationship between hard work and results. Telling an athlete who may have
completed a lift but with reduced range of motion or altered position to go
lighter is very difficult. It feels counterintuitive for the athlete to be told not
to train as hard, or what they perceive as hard, as they can.
We could apply the same set of parameters to maximal sprinting based on
a top speed recorded. Timing gates are optimal here to be as objective as
possible. Finding the athlete’s top speed and recording speed per individual
rep allows for creating a ratio for speed training. Similar to velocity-based
training, we can establish a targeted zone based on max sprint ability for
maximal sprinting (>90%), tempo work (60%-80%), and work capacity
(40%-60%). Of course, timing gates are not accessible to everyone, but a
stopwatch can suffice at a very low cost.
An important aspect of running a staff is accepting that there will be a
discrepancy between the skill and the motivation to do a job over a longer
period. If you are writing the program or leading a staff, you will need to be
strategic about when and where you place complicated and challenging
components. Remember, the athletes are the ones going through the program,
but the coaches are the ones implementing it. Having rigorous standards
makes the difference in truly appraising whether your program is effective
and at what cost.
All of this is to give coaches a mechanism to do their jobs better. To
uphold the standards while minimizing conflict. Young coaches who are
trying to process a large amount of information at once will struggle with
conflict from athletes. Veteran coaches who are trying to maintain their
motivation to uphold a standard will also struggle with conflict from athletes.
In both scenarios, you want to place systems to safeguard standards and
unload them from the responsibilities of constantly scrutinizing every rep and
every set. Reps in reserve place the onus on the athlete; they are responsible
for their development and choosing an adequate weight. Velocity brackets
place the onus on the velocity-based training tool; the coach or athlete did not
say it was bad, but the unit did. Rep (TUT) brackets are the responsibility of

运动员的技术欠佳很重要。 告诉运动员由于体重选择不当而导致他们
的技术不理想是一项挑战。运动员是竞争对手，所以他们会感知努力与
结果之间的因果关系。告诉一个已经完成举重但运动范围缩小或改变位
置的运动员减轻是非常困难的。 对于运动员来说，被告知不要尽可能
努力地训练，或者他们认为很难的事情，感觉是违反直觉的。
我们可以根据记录的最高速度将同一组参数应用于最大冲刺。 时间
门在这里是最佳的，尽可能客观。 找到运动员的最高速度并记录每次
重复的速度可以为速度训练创建一个比率。 与基于速度的训练类似，
我们可以根据最大冲刺能力（>90%）、节奏工作（60%-80%）和工作
能力（40%-60%）建立目标区域。 当然，计时门并不是每个人都能使
用，但秒表就足够了，而且成本非常低。
管理员工的一个重要方面是要接受这样的事实：在较长一段时间内，
技能与工作动机之间会存在差异。如果您正在编写程序或领导员工，则
需要对何时何地放置复杂且具有挑战性的组件有策略。请记住，运动员
是执行该计划的人，但教练是实施该计划的人。 拥有严格的标准可以
真正评估您的计划是否有效以及成本如何。

所有这一切都是为了给教练一个更好地完成工作的机制。 维护标准
，同时尽量减少冲突。 试图同时处理大量信息的年轻教练将难以应对
运动员的冲突。 试图保持动力以维持标准的经验丰富的教练也会与运
动员的冲突作斗争。在这两种情况下，您都希望建立系统来维护标准，
并使它们摆脱不断审查每个代表和每组动作的责任。替补代表将责任归
于运动员；他们对自己的发育负责并选择适当的重量。 速度括号将责
任置于基于速度的训练工具上；教练或运动员没有说不好，但单位却说
不好。代表 (TUT) 括号内的人员负责

both the athlete and the coach. This is where coaches should assist by
counting reps or tempo. Another option is to have athletes count each other’s
tempo or reps.
Heart rate during training is another mechanism to control both intensity
and rest periods. Allocating recovery interset is always a challenge. We
usually compensate for this by adding a ton of supersets and pairings to
facilitate being productive while resting. This is not an awful strategy and
works well without the use of a heart rate monitor. But the higher the stakes,
meaning higher thresholds of speed or intensity, the greater the risk. Using
heart rate as an indicator to rest more or less becomes a valuable asset in
controlling density, overall tonnage, and training impulse.

Hardware Management
Here is a problem you are not thinking about when you purchase
a piece of testing hardware: Where are you going to put it?
Bigger picture thoughts, like when are you going to test, how are
you going to train staff, and how are you going to use that data to
improve your test, are all top of mind when purchasing a testing
system, but that should not be your first thought.
What any testing tool represents is potential. Potential to
understand more. Potential to do more. Potential to be more. But
all that potential is wasted if there is no logistics conversation on
where something will be placed and possibly stored when that
testing tool arrives. We have to have some idea, or that tool may
never come out of the box.
Before making any purchase and deciding why you are going
to use a piece of equipment, you should have a conversation
about where it will go. Can we leave it in a particular spot in the
weight room at all times? Do we need to make a testing area? Is
it hard to break down and reassemble if we have to store it each
day or week? Does it take up a lot of space? Is it heavy? Are
there a lot of pieces? You will not ask this before making the
purchase, but you will wish you had after the purchase.

无论是运动员还是教练。 这是教练应该通过计算次数或节奏来提供帮
助的地方。另一种选择是让运动员计算彼此的节奏或次数。
训练期间的心率是控制强度和休息时间的另一种机制。 分配恢复兴
趣始终是一个挑战。 我们通常会通过增加大量的超级组和配对来弥补
这一点，以促进在休息时提高工作效率。 这不是一个糟糕的策略，并
且在不使用心率监测器的情况下也能很好地发挥作用。但赌注越高，意
味着速度或强度的阈值越高，风险就越大。 使用心率作为休息指标或
多或少成为控制密度、总吨位和训练冲动的宝贵资产。

硬件管理
当您购买测试硬件时，有一个您没有考虑的问题：您要把它放在
哪里？购买测试系统时，最重要的是考虑更大的想法，例如您何
时进行测试、如何培训员工以及如何使用这些数据来改进测试，
但这不应该是您的第一个想法。
任何测试工具都代表着潜力。 有可能了解更多。有潜力做更多
事情。潜力更大。但是，如果没有就测试工具到达时将放置和可
能存储的东西进行后勤对话，那么所有的潜力都会被浪费。我们
必须有一些想法，否则该工具可能永远不会现成的。
在进行任何购买并决定为什么要使用一件设备之前，您应该讨
论一下它将去往何处。我们可以一直把它放在举重室的特定位置
吗？我们需要建立一个测试区吗？如果我们每天或每周都必须存
放它，那么分解和重新组装是否会很困难？ 它占用很多空间吗？
重吗？ 有很多碎片吗？ 您在购买前不会询问此问题，但您会希
望在购买后询问。

My advice to all strength coaches is to request a demo before
purchasing. You get a firsthand experience with potential
logistics. Like books, if someone has incurred this problem
before, you can find answers to your new questions. Ask the
vendor where they would put the testing tool. Ask other coaches
who have what you are getting where they have placed it. Make
everyone on staff chime in. Make everyone’s staff go through
testing, setting up, and breaking down if you are going to move it
every time.
Your weight room is an ecosystem. It has a flow and symbiotic
relationship with the people there and the equipment being used.
Adding a piece that has no specific placement alters that
ecosystem. Adding a system of moving each time alters that
ecosystem. Just as you have to declare all items when traveling
internationally to protect the ecosystem you are entering, the
same applies to all testing equipment. How would the symphony
of a training session be altered if I added a new instrument? The
same applies to any testing tool we may want to add.
A quick note on GPS tracking. It is phenomenal, but it is mainly reserved
for games and practice, at least in my opinion. You will not achieve the
running distance or workloads to necessitate using GPS during training. One
could argue it can track max velocity sprinting and total time, but a timing
gate or stopwatch can capture top speeds. You can take that top speed or
maximal sprinting and quantify how many total yards and rest you need. GPS
is a fine tool; you can easily justify using it if you have the resources. I find it
overkill in a training setting.
We can extrapolate how hard a set was from reps in reserve. The more
reps in reserve, the easier the set, which leads to less actual recovery time.
We can use an RPE (rating of perceived exertion) posttraining to see how
hard something was. Lower RPE would require less recovery time between
sets. Or we can look at the time it takes for the heart rate to return to a
baseline; a typical drop of 25 to 50 beats per minute following phosphagen
power work is the ideal recovery amount to perform anaerobic work again.

我对所有力量教练的建议是在购买之前请求演示。 您将获得潜
在物流的第一手经验。 就像书籍一样，如果有人以前遇到过这个
问题，您可以找到新问题的答案。 询问供应商他们会将测试工具
放在哪里。询问其他教练，他们在他们放置的地方有你所得到的
东西。让每个员工都参与进来。如果你每次都要移动它，那么让
每个员工都经历测试、设置和分解。

你的举重室是一个生态系统。它与那里的人和所使用的设备具
有流动和共生关系。添加没有特定位置的部分会改变该生态系统
。 每次添加移动系统都会改变该生态系统。正如您在国际旅行时
必须申报所有物品以保护您所进入的生态系统一样，这同样适用
于所有测试设备。如果我添加一种新乐器，培训课程的交响乐会
如何改变？这同样适用于我们可能想要添加的任何测试工具。

关于 GPS 跟踪的快速说明。它是惊人的，但它主要保留用于游戏和
练习，至少在我看来。 在训练期间，您将无法达到需要使用 GPS 的跑
步距离或工作量。有人可能会说它可以跟踪最大速度冲刺和总时间，但
计时门或秒表可以捕获最高速度。 您可以采用最高速度或最大冲刺，
并量化您需要的总码数和休息量。 GPS是一个很好的工具；如果您有资
源，您可以轻松证明使用它的合理性。我发现它在训练环境中太过分了
。
我们可以从预备队的代表中推断出一组的难度。 预留的次数越多，
组数就越容易，从而导致实际恢复时间更少。我们可以使用训练后的 R
PE（感知劳累等级）来了解某件事有多难。 较低的 RPE 需要较少的组
间恢复时间。 或者我们可以查看心率恢复到基线所需的时间； 磷酸原
动力工作后，每分钟典型下降 25 至 50 次，是再次进行无氧工作的理想
恢复量。

Whether we are resting too long or too short is often hard to determine on the
fly. The discrepancy with rest intervals based on anxiousness or not
perceiving something as taxing can affect the density or time of a training
session.
Intratraining session testing is followed by an aggregate assessment of the
training session. How much was the tonnage (volume × intensity) for the
primaries in a training session? Save yourself the hassle and only count your
primary training intensity and volume. How much was the acute workload
(RPE × minutes) from the entire training session? How much was the training
impulse (average heart rate × minutes) from the entire training session? How
hard something was matters a great deal from one training session to the next.

Microcycles, Mesocycles, and Macrocycles
Something that we can consider very difficult should be countered with
something less difficult. Microcycles would alter the sequence of high
intensity and short duration, followed by low intensity and longer duration.
Mesocycles should have some response from one week to the next regarding
rates of progressive overload. If something is perceived as difficult, it would
have a direct impact on next week’s training by requiring a smaller jump in
intensity. If something is incredibly easy, the jump goes up substantially.
Putting the responsibility on the athlete to assess their performance is
important here. They will need to be able to decide on what weight to use
from one week to the next. We can rely exclusively on prescribed intensity,
but that is hitting the middle of the distribution curve and not accounting for
fast-twitch or slow-twitch athletes. Athletes should have a reference for how
hard something was to give input on their following week’s intensity. “How
hard was last week’s training session?” is a powerful conversation about what
weight to use the following week. See figure 4.8 on page 64 for how
perceived exertion can influence weekly progression.
We can also build that into acute-to-chronic scores, training tonnage, and
overall workload week to week. How much an athlete can tolerate within one
training session and its residual fatigue is something you learn over time with
your team. Some teams practice incredibly long, which will have a direct
impact on what you need to do and what you can do. Some teams rely on

我们通常很难即时确定我们休息的时间是太长还是太短。 由于焦虑或
不认为某事繁重而导致的休息间隔差异可能会影响训练的密度或时间。
培训课程测试之后是对培训课程的总体评估。 训练中初选的吨位（
体积 × 强度）是多少？省去麻烦，只计算您的主要训练强度和训练量。
整个训练课程的急性工作负荷（RPE × 分钟）是多少？整个训练课程的
训练冲动（平均心率×分钟）是多少？从一次训练到下一次训练，事情
的难度有多重要。

微循环、中循环和大循环
我们认为非常困难的事情应该用不太困难的事情来应对。 微循环会改
变高强度和短持续时间的顺序，然后是低强度和较长持续时间。中周期
应该从一周到下一周对渐进超载率有一些反应。如果某件事被认为是困
难的，那么它会要求较小的强度跳跃，从而对下周的训练产生直接影响
。如果某件事非常简单，那么跳跃就会大幅上升。
让运动员有责任评估他们的表现在这里很重要。 他们需要能够决定
从一周到下一周使用什么重量。 我们可以完全依赖规定的强度，但这
只是达到分布曲线的中间，而不考虑快肌动或慢肌动的运动员。运动员
应该对某件事有多难有一个参考，以便为他们接下来一周的强度提供信
息。 “上周的训练有多难？”是关于下周使用什么重量的强有力的对
话。 请参阅第 64 页上的图 4.8，了解感知运动如何影响每周进度。

我们还可以将其纳入急性到慢性分数、训练量和每周的总体工作量中
。一名运动员在一次训练中可以忍受多少以及其残余疲劳程度是您随着
时间的推移与您的团队一起了解的。 有些团队练习的时间非常长，这
将直接影响你需要做什么和你能做什么。 有些团队依靠

strength and conditioning to build fitness; you will need to build up as much
capacity through training as possible. Having an idea of what constitutes a
high or low total workload becomes increasingly important for a strength
coach.
The most important aspect of testing around the training session is that it
is reliable. Coaches are human and will make mistakes. In situations where
we have to rely on athletes to input their information, they will make more
mistakes. The best way to combat that is to rely on low human error hardware
to collect data. When in doubt, use tools that do not rely on human testing or
human data entry. The collection and input can make a valid test obsolete.
Tools that are intuitive and rely on the hardware to dictate input are superior
to those that rely on humans alone. Software that auto-populates results and
hopefully transfers them to a storage platform is superior to those that rely on
humans to do so.
This is a valuable indication of how well-constructed a sports science
department is in handling staff turnover. Processes and systems that are too
complicated or difficult to execute will only last for so long with certain staff
members. Having a plan that is transferable from one coach to the next is the
true test of how well thought out your plan is. Staff members need to be
interchangeable with testing due to the importance of the information. If one
staff member were to leave and testing ceased, a large amount of time and
resources would be wasted. You have more rapid indicators of this when a
coach has been pulled away for something else. Can another coach step in
and gather data that will determine its long-term value?
Start small and start with what you understand. The more you understand
something, the easier it will be to justify when it becomes challenging to
collect. Tools that do a lot of the heavy lifting for you are key. Hours of data
collection followed by hours of data entry are not a good use of your time.
This is especially true if you have a poor athlete-to-coach ratio and need that
time to work with athletes.

Testing Interpretation
The final element of sports science is interpreting the data. We need to use

力量和体能训练以增强体质；您需要通过培训来建立尽可能多的能力。
对于力量教练来说，了解什么构成了总工作量的高或低变得越来越重要
。
培训课程测试最重要的一点是它的可靠性。 教练也是人，也会犯错
误。 在我们必须依赖运动员输入信息的情况下，他们会犯更多的错误
。解决这个问题的最佳方法是依靠低人为错误的硬件来收集数据。如有
疑问，请使用不依赖人工测试或人工数据输入的工具。 收集和输入可
能会使有效的测试变得过时。直观且依赖硬件来指示输入的工具优于那
些仅依赖人类的工具。 自动填充结果并希望将其传输到存储平台的软
件优于那些依赖人类这样做的软件。

这是一个有价值的指标，表明体育科学部门在处理员工流动方面的结
构如何。 过于复杂或难以执行的流程和系统对于某些员工来说只能持
续很长时间。制定一个可以从一位教练转移到另一位教练的计划才是对
您的计划是否经过深思熟虑的真正考验。 由于信息的重要性，工作人
员需要与测试互换。如果一名工作人员离开并且测试停止，就会浪费大
量的时间和资源。 当教练因为其他事情而被解雇时，你会更快速地发
现这一点。 另一位教练能否介入并收集决定其长期价值的数据？

从小事做起，从你所理解的开始。你对某件事了解得越多，当收集起
来变得困难时，就越容易证明其合理性。为您完成大量繁重工作的工具
是关键。数小时的数据收集和数小时的数据输入并不能很好地利用您的
时间。如果你的运动员与教练的比例很差并且需要时间与运动员一起工
作，则尤其如此。

测试解释
运动科学的最后一个要素是解释数据。 我们需要使用

the data to make objectively good decisions; otherwise, staff and athletes will
lose interest. What you will find, if you have not already, is that data are
incredibly overwhelming. It is daunting to look at the endless possibilities of
numbers and how they interact with each other to draw a conclusion about
whether your program was successful. What you also find is that data are
malleable; we can tell whatever story we want to tell. Let us discuss how to
interpret data.
First, we want to make sure the transfer from the test to the dataset was
input correctly. Manual transfer is a nightmare and should be avoided. At
times, we will have to resort to manual transfer, but if it can be avoided, it
should be. Data entry mistakes are a multiple of the number of athletes and
the number of entries. The more athletes, the more inputs, and the more
coaches inputting data will amplify all mistakes and reduce the value of the
data you are trying to interpret.
Inputting data has value regarding intimacy with the numbers and their
connection to athletes’ progress. You need to have familiarity with the
numbers that demonstrate your program’s success. Sports coaches are intense
and will expect you to answer anything they are thinking of at any given
time. A sure way to be prepared for random questions is to input data daily. I
hold fond memories of inputting body weights or jumps every week for the
entire football team with my coworkers. Finishing a session, grabbing the
clipboards, getting a coffee, setting up a chair for myself and another staff
member, pulling up the file, and seeing how fast I could input data is
surprisingly a very good memory. Inadvertently, I was more prepared for outof-nowhere questions because of the intimacy I had with the data.
Nostalgia and preparing for random questions are not enough to keep an
antiquated data entry system. Good hardware should have a connection to
datasets through direct transfer or cloud-based transfer. Your process of
evaluating what tools to use should consider whether they have direct
connectivity to either a dashboard or a dataset. We should use the time we
have gained to understand the information ourselves and explain it to others.
A large reason a coach asks random questions is that they feel uninformed.
Bringing them a report daily on training or practice creates a line of
communication that decreases the likelihood of random questions.

用于做出客观正确决策的数据；否则，工作人员和运动员就会失去兴趣
。 如果您还没有发现的话，您会发现数据是令人难以置信的压倒性。
查看数字的无限可能性以及它们如何相互作用来得出关于您的程序是否
成功的结论是令人畏惧的。 您还会发现数据是可塑的； 我们可以讲任
何我们想讲的故事。 让我们讨论如何解释数据。
首先，我们要确保从测试到数据集的传输输入正确。 手动传输是一
场噩梦，应该避免。 有时，我们不得不诉诸手动传输，但如果可以避
免，那就应该避免。 数据输入错误是运动员人数和条目数的倍数。 运
动员越多，输入越多，输入数据的教练越多，就会放大所有错误并降低
你试图解释的数据的价值。
输入数据对于与数字的亲密程度及其与运动员进步的联系具有价值。
您需要熟悉证明您的计划成功的数字。体育教练很热情，希望你在任何
特定时间都能回答他们想到的任何问题。为随机问题做好准备的一个可
靠方法是每天输入数据。我对每周与同事一起为整个橄榄球队输入体重
或跳跃数据有着美好的回忆。 完成一个会议，抓起剪贴板，喝杯咖啡
，为自己和另一位工作人员摆好椅子，调出文件，看看我输入数据的速
度有多快，令人惊讶的是，这是一个非常好的记忆。无意中，由于我与
数据的亲密关系，我对突然出现的问题有了更充分的准备。

怀旧和准备随机问题不足以保留过时的数据输入系统。 好的硬件应
该通过直接传输或基于云的传输来连接到数据集。 您评估要使用哪些
工具的过程应考虑它们是否可以直接连接到仪表板或数据集。 我们应
该利用获得的时间来自己理解信息并向他人解释。教练随机提出问题的
一个重要原因是他们感觉自己不了解情况。每天给他们提供有关培训或
练习的报告，建立了一条沟通渠道，减少了随机问题的可能性。

What are we looking for with data? We should have this question
answered before we start testing. We are looking for signs that training is
moving in the correct direction toward our predetermined goal of increasing
performance. Objectives and key results best describe this. The objective is
our intended outcome. Key results are indicators that we are reaching that
outcome. We want to determine key results on a microscale, such as a
training session or microcycle, to track progress toward an objective.
As a field, we often commit to philosophies or trains of thought that are
hardwired. We see this with the way we set up our weight rooms, our staff,
and our programs. Whatever the rationale is for programming anything, we
should be able to test whether the rationale was well thought out and well
executed. Key results are related to the objective, not the justification of the
training philosophy. Speed or resiliency are universally important but can
easily be dismissed based on what we use to substantiate our program.
Correspondence from training to competition is pretty straightforward.
Did we win more games or have a positive impact on performance? In
football, if our game one starters were able to practice every practice and play
every game, resiliency was created. If our team increased speed measured by
a pre- and posttest of the same distance of a 10, 20, or 40 yd (9, 18, or 37 m)
dash, speed was created—bottom line: Objectives matter.
We can manipulate that to our advantage. We are all on the chopping
block when it comes to not producing. We have to choose things we know we
can be successful with. A large part of our job is built on the idea that the
things we are good at changing do matter. We can easily prioritize that at the
expense of what we may need or something entirely unrelated. There could
be a small sample of athletes that benefited, but the majority matters more.
What the difference was systematically is the real measure. We should have a
positive impact on what is related to performance.
We can break this down into weaknesses and develop them into strengths
or push toward a predetermined peak. We are fixing problems or working
toward an outcome. There is no right or wrong here, just what makes more
sense to you, the coach. If you opt to address weaknesses, what is the
progress of those areas relative to the primary objective? If you decide to
work toward a peak, how fast and how much progress is being made? Shown

我们要通过数据寻找什么？ 在开始测试之前我们应该回答这个问题
。 我们正在寻找迹象表明培训正在朝着我们预定的提高绩效的目标朝
着正确的方向发展。 目标和关键结果最好地描述了这一点。 目标是我
们预期的结果。 关键结果是我们正在实现这一成果的指标。 我们希望
确定微观层面的关键结果，例如培训课程或微周期，以跟踪目标的进展
情况。
作为一个领域，我们经常致力于遵循根深蒂固的哲学或思路。 我们
通过设置举重室、员工和项目的方式看到了这一点。 无论编程的基本
原理是什么，我们都应该能够测试该基本原理是否经过深思熟虑并得到
良好执行。 关键结果与目标相关，而不是与培训理念的合理性相关。
速度或弹性普遍重要，但根据我们用来证实我们计划的内容，很容易被
忽视。
从训练到比赛的对应关系非常简单。我们赢得了更多比赛还是对表现
产生了积极影响？ 在足球比赛中，如果我们的第一场首发球员能够练
习每一次训练并参加每场比赛，那么就会产生弹性。如果我们的团队通
过 10、20 或 40 码（9、18 或 37 m）冲刺相同距离的前后测试来提高速
度，那么速度就被创造出来了——底线：目标很重要。
我们可以利用它来发挥我们的优势。 当谈到不生产时，我们都处于
砧板上。我们必须选择我们知道可以成功的事情。 我们工作的很大一
部分建立在这样的理念之上：我们擅长改变的事情确实很重要。我们可
以轻松地优先考虑这一点，但会牺牲我们可能需要的东西或完全不相关
的东西。 可能会有一小部分运动员受益，但大多数人更重要。系统性
的差异才是真正的衡量标准。我们应该对与绩效相关的事情产生积极的
影响。
我们可以将其分解为弱点，并将其发展为优势或推动达到预定的峰值
。 我们正在解决问题或努力取得成果。 这里没有对错之分，只有什么
对你（教练）更有意义。 如果您选择解决弱点，那么这些领域相对于
主要目标的进展如何？ 如果您决定向顶峰努力，进步的速度和程度如
何？如图所示

in figure 15.5 is a spider chart that gives relative ability based on normative
data. Normative data can be from a current roster, which is the same as
standard distribution, and where someone falls on a bell curve for certain
metrics. Normative data can be from multiple teams over an extended period.
The spider chart demonstrates that an athlete is weak relative to the norm.

Athlete Objectives
What gets measured, gets managed. We know that testing leads to reactions.
We want to move toward an objective, and testing will have a direct
psychological impact on that (figure 15.5). The more frequently we test
something, the more influence that testing will have. If we want something to
be taken seriously by both the coach and the athlete, we test as much as we
can get away with. This is why having direct data transfer is so important.
We always want to toe the line of testing frequency because we want to push
for as much change as possible.

图 15.5 是一个蜘蛛图，给出了基于规范数据的相对能力。 规范数据可
以来自当前名单，这与标准分布相同，并且某人在某些指标上落在钟形
曲线上。规范数据可以来自多个团队在很长一段时间内的数据。蜘蛛图
表明运动员相对于正常水平较弱。

运动员目标
衡量什么，就管理什么。我们知道测试会导致反应。我们希望朝着一个
目标前进，而测试将对此产生直接的心理影响（图 15.5）。 我们测试
某件事的频率越高，测试的影响力就越大。如果我们希望教练和运动员
都认真对待某件事，我们会尽可能多地进行测试。 这就是为什么直接
数据传输如此重要。我们总是希望遵守测试频率，因为我们希望推动尽
可能多的改变。

FIGURE 15.5 Athlete objectives.
You will find layers of testing data that you did not know existed. You can
analyze that data and create a bottomless abyss of information that you can
get lost in. Metrics within datasets can be potentially counterproductive if
you do not have the direct key results you are looking for. For instance, if you
are jumping on force plates, you will find several metrics from one jump test.
What matters is simply, did you jump higher, yes or no? What you can
unpack from performance gain or loss is what metrics were out of range.
Once you find your key result metric and jump height, we bolster that result
with supporting or negating evidence. As the numbers pile up, having triggers
to dig deeper will make data dives more appropriate.

to objectives and key results, these would be examples of key results. Key
results are the mechanisms of how we reach an objective. The point of
training is to be a means to initiate and encourage change. If it does not, it
should be evaluated as too much, too little, or the wrong thing altogether.
Key results give insights into the relative rate and amount of change we are
making.
It will be bad before it is good. Training creates negative adaptation before
it makes a positive adaptation. This is where the faith in your programming
comes in. Training will hurt testing for an undetermined amount of time. We
can use deloads or tapers, but there is no guarantee of enough time to elicit
positive outcomes. We will also see massive discrepancies between how
much and when an athlete adapts. You will have to be sure that things such as
the level of execution and supporting metrics are moving in a positive
direction. Get ahead on this before you discuss it with coaches and athletes.
Without context about adaptive responses to stress, they will react in a way
that can be counterproductive.
When cutting a program and pivoting in another direction, it is difficult to
navigate. The sunk cost of training affects both the coach and the athlete.
Committing time and energy to something makes abandoning it harder. Faith
in something that is not working is a hard thing to argue. This is why it is so
important to rely on year-over-year results and commit to testing for an
extended period. You get better at understanding if something is a good plan
or not based on being in situations where you learned it was bad.

同时影响教练和运动员。将时间和精力投入到某件事上会让放弃它变得

，你会更好地理解它是否是一个好计划。

Key Performance Indicators
The final aspect is creating dashboards for athletes and position groups. They
could come in a spider chart or a simple progress of key performance
indicators (figure 15.6). What matters is what makes sense for you
logistically and in communication with coaches and athletes. If only one
person understands the chart or report, it is not a good representation of the
success of a program. The other aspect is how challenging a dashboard is to
create. It may be time to find something more repeatable if it is too timeconsuming.
Considering all available data and what it means is never easy. In reality,
at a certain point, someone will read this and wonder why there is a
discussion on coaches breaking down data in the first place. Eventually,
machine learning will replace humans in breaking down data. Change will
come in this direction and will prove that humans, just as we have found with
tests and manual entry, are proving less and less capable. This is not to

考虑所有可用数据及其含义绝非易事。事实上，在某个时候，有人会

replace our jobs; it reinforces what we do. We need to be excellent coaches
and program writers. If we can do that, we can take whatever objective
information is available and create substantial change.

Take Home
Adaptation is a tough thing to figure out; it is even tougher with large groups
and limited people interpreting what adaptations were made. Focus should be
on why you are testing, how to test efficiently, and what to interpret. Simple
execution and easy-to-understand metrics are far superior to difficult
execution and hard-to-understand metrics. Create a plan that is sustainable
and interchangeable from one coach to the next. The more well thought out
your rationale, testing, and interpretation, the more that data will assist you in
your programming.

取代我们的工作； 它强化了我们所做的事情。 我们需要成为优秀的教
练和节目编写者。 如果我们能做到这一点，我们就可以利用任何可用
的客观信息并创造实质性的改变。

带回家
适应是一件很难弄清楚的事情；对于大团体和有限的人来说，解释所做
的调整就更加困难了。重点应该放在为什么要测试、如何有效地测试以
及解释什么上。简单的执行和易于理解的指标远远优于困难的执行和难
以理解的指标。 制定一个可持续的、可以从一位教练到另一位教练互
换的计划。 您的基本原理、测试和解释越深思熟虑，数据就越能帮助
您进行编程。

COACHING A SESSION
Can we replicate good coaching? It is a really important question because if
we cannot replicate good coaching, we will be at the mercy of variables
beyond our control that determine outcomes from training. Models of
coaching are a great place to start. Do we have a plan for how we are going to
coach? This is an important question to start with.
Diversity in the staff is the best way to approach complex problems.
Diversity of experience, backgrounds, and personalities makes your staff
more complete, and thus, more capable of supporting your athletes. Your
athletes will be broad in how they respond to coaching and motivational
tactics, which is why your staff also needs to be broad. The more diverse
your staff is, the more capable they are of handling variance in athlete
responses. But that does not mean coaching is completely random based on
the diversity within the staff.
A more diverse staff will need a structure to provide consistent training
output. Having a plan for how we want to execute a training session or a drill
matters. A staff with a range of experiences will be more or less capable,
which is expected. But if the coach is responsible for something, they will
need to have a baseline competency to execute it. Baseline execution is the
standard operating procedure (SOP) of coaching.
We build repeatable high-level coaching with SOPs through models. The
two models we will use are Newell’s model and Ericsson’s model. We will
need to design a session not only for the athlete but also for the coaches

辅导课程

要广泛。 您的员工越多元化，他们处理运动员反应差异的能力就越强
。 但这并不意味着教练是完全随机的，基于员工内部的多样性。

Newell’s Model
An important model to leverage here is Newell’s model of coaching (figure
16.1). Newell’s (Newell, et al, 2001) model describes components of an
environment, tasks, and individual constraints for an athlete and the coach’s
relationship in prescribing and coaching the athlete. One thing that becomes
incredibly important to discuss is that we are primarily working with larger
groups, and the need to replicate what we do among all our athletes over an
extended period is largely predicated upon how we leverage constraints.

操作每个会话。 我们的能力不仅取决于运动员的能力，还取决于教练
的指导能力。 SOP 基于每个教练的能力。 有时，我们必须根据每个教
练的最低共同标准来制定计划才能取得成功。 我们还需要在物流限制
范围内进行编程。 爱立信的模型和纽厄尔的模型都将帮助我们建立标
准操作程序，使我们员工中的每位教练都能取得成功。

纽厄尔模型
这里可以利用的一个重要模型是纽厄尔的教练模型（图 16.1）。 纽厄
尔（Newell，et al，2001）模型描述了运动员的环境、任务和个人约束
的组成部分以及教练在规定和指导运动员时的关系。 需要讨论的一件
非常重要的事情是，我们主要是与更大的群体合作，并且需要在很长一
段时间内在所有运动员中复制我们所做的事情，这在很大程度上取决于
我们如何利用限制。

FIGURE 16.1 Newell’s model.
With Newell’s model, we titrate up or down the level of constraint to
remove complexity from the situation. Reducing complexity positively
affects our ability to reproduce certain things. An extreme example of this is
comparing the ability to replicate throwing a ball at a target that is 5 ft (1.5
m) away with that of a professional baseball player and a toddler throwing a
90 mph (145 km/h) slider. That same example may or may not occur in your
training program daily. Your coaches could be coaching in a way that is not
relevant or appropriate for the task or the environment.

Individual
For us to leverage Newell’s model, we have to start with the individual. We
discussed individual differences in chapter 2. Before we program anything,
we should know the training age, biological age, gender, and muscle fiber

复杂性。 降低复杂性会对我们复制某些事物的能力产生积极影响。一
个极端的例子是将向 5 英尺（1.5 m）外的目标投掷球的能力与职业棒
球运动员和幼儿投掷 90 英里/小时（145 公里/小时）滑块的能力进行比
较。同样的例子可能会也可能不会出现在您的日常训练计划中。您的教
练的指导方式可能与任务或环境无关或不合适。

个人
为了利用纽厄尔模型，我们必须从个人开始。 我们在第 2 章中讨论了
个体差异。在进行任何编程之前，我们应该了解训练年龄、生物年龄、
性别和肌纤维

type. You cannot predict how each person will respond to training, but you
can better understand patterns by inventorying the answers to individual
archetypes. When we understand baseline parameters, we can program more
appropriately to the organism’s needs.
In the case of extremes, we are not going to program the same thing for a
freshman in high school as we would a 5-year National Football League
veteran. It seems obvious to say, but for the novice coach who will associate
more with better, it is not. You will need to have a rationale for why that is
not always true through principles and logic. With that freshman, we will be
starting with basic-level unloaded patterns because that gives the best start to
progression and progressive overload. We do not know how they will
respond, so we have to simplify the task and the environment. Alternatively,
we fast-track training decisions for more advanced athletes. We have a better
working knowledge of what they can do and get right along with what is
needed.
The environment should be the next consideration in setting up your
training program and how you coach it. Much like individual differences, you
will have little control over the environment. You are more than likely
programming to accommodate your facility, not the other way around. We
have to adapt to what we have and omit what we do not. We have to associate
the difference in training with low stakes and only positive upside scenarios
to eventually having training translate to being in competition where there is
a higher chance of failure.
High-stakes competition, such as team sports, where there is a definitive
winner and loser, is something to consider in training environments.
Competition reveals everything. Bad mechanics, bad posture, poor fitness,
and limited power, velocity, force, and work capacity will be revealed when
the stakes increase. If we tap into intense environments, we amplify
everything. You can titrate up the level immediately by increasing the stakes;
the question is, when should you do this?
Environmental conditions that pit athletes against each other will increase
the level of effort but will expose poor foundations. A top-down approach to
teaching can work in exposing deficiencies. A bottom-up approach will have
to revisit foundational biomechanical, biomotor, and bioenergetic levels. The

类型。 您无法预测每个人对培训的反应，但您可以通过盘点个人原型
的答案来更好地理解模式。当我们了解基线参数时，我们可以更适合生
物体的需求进行编程。
在极端情况下，我们不会为高中一年级新生设计与在国家橄榄球联盟
效力 5 年的老兵相同的东西。说起来似乎理所当然，但对于将更多与更
好联系在一起的新手教练来说，事实并非如此。 你需要通过原则和逻
辑来解释为什么这并不总是正确的。对于这位新生，我们将从基本级别
的卸载模式开始，因为这为进步和渐进超负荷提供了最好的开始。 我
们不知道他们会如何反应，所以我们必须简化任务和环境。或者，我们
可以快速跟踪更高级运动员的训练决策。我们对他们能做什么以及如何
满足需要有更好的工作了解。

在设置训练计划以及如何指导训练时，环境应该是下一个考虑因素。
就像个体差异一样，你对环境几乎无法控制。 您很可能会根据您的设
施进行编程，而不是相反。 我们必须适应我们拥有的，并忽略我们没
有的。我们必须将训练的差异与低风险和只有积极的上行场景联系起来
，最终将训练转化为失败机会更高的竞争。

在训练环境中需要考虑高风险的比赛，例如团队运动，其中有明确的
赢家和输家。竞争揭示了一切。 当风险增加时，不良的力学、不良的
姿势、较差的体能以及有限的力量、速度、力量和工作能力都会暴露出
来。 如果我们进入激烈的环境，我们就会放大一切。您可以通过增加
赌注来立即提升等级；问题是，你应该什么时候这样做？
运动员相互竞争的环境条件会增加运动员的努力程度，但也会暴露出
较差的基础。自上而下的教学方法可以暴露缺陷。自下而上的方法必须
重新审视基础的生物力学、生物运动和生物能量水平。这

truth is that you can use a competitive environment whenever you want, but
it’s better to be strategic with how and when. You can frame the competition
as athlete versus athlete or athletes against their previous best. Competition is
the primary environmental consideration; as your training moves closer to
competition, you should increase the frequency and intensity of training to
match the upcoming demands. There should be a correspondence between
how we increase environmental demands and seasonal periods.

Task
The second aspect of Newell’s model is the task, which we have the most
control over. The foundation of training is understanding what the athlete will
need to elicit the best outcome but also what they can perform successfully
and still recover from. We do this organically with progressions in
biomechanics, biomotor abilities, and bioenergetics.
With tasks, or the selection of a drill or exercise, we are either increasing
or decreasing the constraints placed to achieve immediate success or facilitate
more implicit learning. The individual and the environment have the most
impact on how we want to approach the task. Novices with poor
biomechanics will likely mean high-constraint tasks. Something that novices
will be successful with immediately is most appropriate. Advanced athletes
with solid biomechanics will more than likely mean low-constraint tasks,
something they will more than likely not be successful with and that requires
increased focus. With both novice and advanced athletes, the task needs to
facilitate something that we can build from our progressions. The tasks and
environments will increase in intensity and demands, and having a plan that
works in concert with their organism’s ability to adapt is the primary focus.

Environment
We are detaching from the psychological aspect of training, which is not fair
to you, the reader. We know of advanced athletes who have fixed mindsets
and hate to fail. We know of novice athletes who have a growth mindset and
love to fail. We know of intrinsically motivated athletes who want more
challenging environments. We know of extrinsically motivated athletes who
will need incentives to perform their best. We also know that this is never

事实是，您可以随时使用竞争环境，但最好对如何以及何时使用有策略
。您可以将比赛定义为运动员与运动员之间的竞争，或者运动员与他们
以前的最佳成绩之间的竞争。竞争是首要的环境考虑因素； 当你的训
练越来越接近比赛时，你应该增加训练的频率和强度，以满足即将到来
的需求。 我们如何增加环境需求和季节周期之间应该存在对应关系。

任务
纽厄尔模型的第二个方面是任务，这是我们最能控制的。训练的基础是
了解运动员需要什么才能获得最佳结果，以及他们可以成功表现并仍然
可以恢复的内容。 我们通过生物力学、生物运动能力和生物能量学的
进步有机地做到这一点。
通过任务或练习或练习的选择，我们要么增加或减少为立即取得成功
或促进更隐性学习而设置的限制。 个人和环境对我们如何完成任务影
响最大。 生物力学较差的新手可能意味着高限制的任务。新手能立即
成功的东西是最合适的。 具有扎实生物力学的高级运动员很可能意味
着低约束任务，他们很可能无法成功完成这些任务，并且需要更加集中
注意力。 对于新手和高级运动员来说，这项任务都需要促进我们可以
从我们的进步中建立一些东西。 任务和环境的强度和要求将会增加，
制定一个与有机体适应能力相一致的计划是首要重点。

环境
我们脱离了训练的心理层面，这对读者来说不公平。 我们知道有些先
进的运动员有着固定型思维并且讨厌失败。我们知道有些新手运动员具
有成长心态并且喜欢失败。 我们知道有些具有内在动机的运动员想要
更具挑战性的环境。 我们知道有外在激励的运动员需要激励才能发挥
最佳水平。 我们也知道这从来都不是

fixed and fluctuates from day to day or even minute to minute. What is true
for one task and a particular environment will differ from another task in a
particular environment for each individual.
Newell’s model, or some version of it, is something we should leverage to
give our coaches the tools they need to execute the program. If we all know
that the task is designed for unpredictable, complex environments, the coach
can react to the situation more effectively. In that situation, the coach can
give feedback on aspects such as effort or level of focus. If there is a concrete
or definitive means of performing an exercise and the athlete does not
execute it, the coach can respond more effectively by holding them to a
standard.

Coach-Led Versus Athlete-Led Model
Does a strength coach have control? The dynamic of a team
environment is built on the premise of hierarchy: Someone is in
charge, and others follow. A coach leads each session, and the
athletes follow, or do they?
High performance is a model that blends sports science,
strength and conditioning, sports medicine, sports nutrition, and
sports psychology into a cohesive unit. The center of the highperformance model is the athlete. This utopia of high
performance is not useful unless there is a direct focus on what
the athletes need.
There is no better resource on what the athlete needs than the
athlete. A simple but important message here is that the athlete
is in charge. How they feel or desire to do something governs the
program. When we talk about who’s in charge, it is always the
athlete.
How does this revelation affect the hierarchy? Nothing
changes. A coach is an expert in their domain. The athlete relies
on the coach to create and guide the best path possible. Guiding
is coaching. Just because there is a perceived hierarchy, the
coach’s responsibilities don’t change. There will be times when

每天甚至每分钟都是固定的和波动的。 对于每个人来说，一项任务和
特定环境中的真实情况将不同于特定环境中的另一项任务。
我们应该利用纽厄尔模型或其某些版本来为我们的教练提供执行计划
所需的工具。 如果我们都知道任务是针对不可预测的复杂环境而设计
的，那么教练就可以更有效地对情况做出反应。 在这种情况下，教练
可以就努力程度或专注程度等方面提供反馈。如果有具体或明确的方法
来进行练习，而运动员没有执行，教练可以通过让他们遵守标准来更有
效地做出反应。

教练主导模式与运动员主导模式
力量教练有控制力吗？ 团队环境的动态性是建立在等级制度的前
提下的：有人负责，其他人跟随。 每次训练都有教练带领，运动
员跟随，或者他们这样做吗？
高性能是一种将运动科学、力量与体能、运动医学、运动营养
和运动心理学融为一体的模型。 高绩效模型的中心是运动员。
除非直接关注运动员的需求，否则这种高性能的乌托邦是没有用
的。
对于运动员的需求，没有比运动员更好的资源了。 这里的一个
简单但重要的信息是运动员负责。他们对做某事的感受或愿望决
定了该计划。 当我们谈论谁负责时，总是运动员。
这一启示如何影响等级制度？ 没有任何改变。教练是其领域的
专家。运动员依靠教练来创造和指导尽可能的最佳路径。指导就
是辅导。 仅仅因为存在明显的等级制度，教练的职责就不会改变
。 会有这样的时候

we have to take a rougher route. There will be times when we
will have to take an easier route.
The only way an athlete will choose to do something is based
on faith in their coach, faith that the coach has the athlete’s best
interest in mind and will do their best to support the athlete’s
journey.
Simply stating to the people you are working with the context they are
working within and how the drill or exercise is based on those variables
relative to a goal or objective makes a world of difference. We only have its
execution as a means to determine whether our program was effective. We do
not want to be hamstrung by limiting our options to highly constrained, lowcompetitive contexts. We want our ceiling to be high so we can facilitate
constant development.

Ericsson’s Deliberate Practice Model
The next model to break down is Ericsson’s deliberate practice model (figure
16.2). Different from Newell’s, Ericsson’s approach offers more control over
variables. It still boils down to the same central theme: Why are we doing
what we are doing, and how are we going to optimize that particular drill or
exercise?
Ericsson’s (Ericsson, 2003) model is broken down into goals, challenges,
focus, and feedback. Each one has a continuum or even a quadrant to break
things down. It can get confusing if we get too deep, but it is also worthwhile
because the human psyche is very complex, and we need a model that is
malleable and not fixed. The key is to know where your program stands on
any given day with each of these attributes to give context to the staff on
what we are trying to accomplish.

我们必须走一条更崎岖的路。 有时我们将不得不采取更容易的路
线。
运动员选择做某事的唯一方式是基于对教练的信任，相信教练
会考虑到运动员的最大利益，并将尽最大努力支持运动员的旅程
。

简单地向正在工作的人说明他们正在工作的环境，以及演习或练习如
何基于与目标或目标相关的这些变量，就会产生很大的不同。我们仅将
其执行作为确定我们的计划是否有效的一种手段。我们不想因为将我们
的选择限制在高度受限、低竞争的环境中而受到束缚。 我们希望我们
的上限很高，这样我们才能促进不断发展。

爱立信的刻意练习模型
下一个要打破的模型是爱立信的刻意练习模型（图 16.2）。与纽厄尔的
方法不同，爱立信的方法提供了对变量的更多控制。 它仍然归结为同
一个中心主题：我们为什么要做我们正在做的事情，以及我们将如何优
化特定的训练或练习？
爱立信（Ericsson，2003）模型分为目标、挑战、焦点和反馈。 每个
人都有一个连续体，甚至一个象限来分解事物。如果我们研究得太深，
可能会让人感到困惑，但这也是值得的，因为人类的心理非常复杂，我
们需要一个可塑的而不是固定的模型。 关键是要了解您的计划在任何
一天的情况以及每个属性，以便为员工提供我们正在努力实现的目标的
背景信息。

FIGURE 16.2 Ericsson’s model (overview).

Goal
It should go without saying, but we should understand the goal of what we
are doing. By combining Newell’s model with Ericsson’s model, we can
reduce constraints, and the goal may become something very temporal, such
as how fast or how heavy it is. A low-constrained drill or exercise could
become more spatial by how it feels. The same could be true for a highconstraint environment with a more spatial goal during tempo runs, where the
point of emphasis is to feel front-side mechanics and run with fluidity.
Having a temporal goal of crossing a line in a certain time or maintaining a
certain velocity is less important in this circumstance. There will be situations
with both novice and experienced coaches who will struggle to be malleable

图 16.2 爱立信的模型（概述）。

目标
这是不言而喻的，但我们应该了解我们正在做的事情的目标。 通过将
纽厄尔模型与爱立信模型相结合，我们可以减少约束，目标可能会变得
非常暂时，比如有多快或多重。 低约束的训练或练习可能会因感觉而
变得更加空间化。 对于在节奏跑期间具有更多空间目标的高约束环境
也可能如此，其中重点是感受前端力学并流畅地运行。在这种情况下，
在一定时间内越过一条线或保持一定速度的时间目标就不那么重要了。
在某些情况下，新手和经验丰富的教练都很难保持可塑性

to the environment and lose focus on the primary goal.
The goal can be the paradox of programming. We want to marry ourselves
to outcomes, but the process of how we get there is what dictates that.
Outcomes can monopolize thought processes to exclusively focus on
temporal aspects, such as training variables (time under tension, reps, sets,
intensity, velocity, rest). We can lose connection to the spatial aspects of
training. What is important here is not that we pick one over the other. What
is important is that we discuss the goal before we start a program with our
coaches. The paradox comes from detaching from outcomes to focus on what
is in front of us, the process.

Challenge
What the challenge should be is another thing we need to discuss. Things like
low days or deload weeks are always difficult to understand for the athlete.
The fact that we get better when we are recovered feels counterintuitive. The
same is true for strength coaches, who could easily feel that an opportunity is
squandered when the athletes are not giving absolute effort. Intentionally
lowering the challenge can directly oppose what athletes and coaches are
accustomed to. Therefore, it is better to communicate the targeted level of
challenge and its intent with both staff and athletes.
An argument absolutely can be made that fatigue is a relative concept to
the individual, and the challenge is very much context dependent. This is
undoubtedly true, but it reflects a reaction to unknown variables. We should
know if something is intentionally challenging based on the pretense that it is
time to go for it. Alternatively, a low day or deload week can still be
perceived as challenging based on physiological or psychological levels. The
point is to have a clearly defined level of challenge that we want to have
before the session to facilitate something relative to the goal, both temporally
and spatially.

Focus
The level of focus is the next component to discuss, from both the coach’s
and the athlete’s perspective. One way to look at this is that early in a
mesocycle, an explanation of the program’s objectives or implicit

环境而失去对主要目标的关注。
目标可能是编程的悖论。我们希望将自己与结果结合起来，但我们实
现这一目标的过程却决定了这一点。结果可以垄断思维过程，只关注时
间方面，例如训练变量（紧张时间、次数、组数、强度、速度、休息）
。 我们可能会失去与训练的空间方面的联系。这里重要的不是我们选
择其中之一。重要的是我们在与教练开始计划之前讨论目标。悖论来自
于脱离结果而关注我们面前的事情，即过程。

挑战
挑战应该是什么是我们需要讨论的另一件事。对于运动员来说，诸如低
潮日或减负荷周之类的事情总是难以理解。当我们康复时，我们会变得
更好，这一事实感觉违反直觉。对于力量教练来说也是如此，当运动员
没有付出绝对的努力时，他们很容易觉得机会被浪费了。 故意降低挑
战可能直接违背运动员和教练的习惯。 因此，最好与工作人员和运动
员沟通挑战的目标级别及其意图。
完全可以认为，疲劳对于个人来说是一个相对的概念，而挑战在很大
程度上取决于具体情况。 这无疑是事实，但它反映了对未知变量的反
应。 我们应该知道某件事是否是基于假装是时候去做而故意具有挑战
性。 或者，根据生理或心理水平，低负荷日或减负荷周仍可能被视为
具有挑战性。关键是在会议之前有一个明确定义的挑战级别，以便在时
间和空间上促进与目标相关的事情。

重点
从教练和运动员的角度来看，关注程度是下一个要讨论的部分。 看待
这个问题的一种方法是，在中周期的早期，对计划目标或隐含的目标进
行解释

expectations is important. It may feel obvious to us, but having lower reps
may not mean a heavier or faster focus for our athletes. We should not expect
our athletes to intuitively understand what we are trying to do with each
program we write. We should, however, expect them to perceive and
understand what we are saying differently. The same could be said toward the
end of the mesocycle when we evaluate the explanation of the implicit
expectations of the program. Did we or did we not improve relative to the
predetermined focus? That improvement is relative to the individual going
through the program.
How we accomplish implicit outcomes is through explicit focus. We get
what we get from the level of execution we have. If we have a 4-week
mesocycle, we should have an explicit focus on technique. Having cues based
on the level of training age or exposure to something is the first
consideration. External or internal, toward or away, analogies or metaphors,
and the ability to demonstrate are the primary tools for having an explicit
focus (Winkleman, 2020). We want improvement, and we have to consider
how we do something as the primary driver to accomplish it.

The Benefit of Open Drills
Open drills are unscripted drills in which the athlete needs to
figure out a solution to an undetermined problem. For a coach,
this is the ultimate test of your program. The solutions your
program represents are on display in an open environment more
so than anything else you use to evaluate the effectiveness of a
program.
All training programs are a reduction of what will happen
during competition. After that reduction, we repeat certain
elements over and over with increased load, speed, or duration.
This approach of repeating with emphasis is intended to
correspond to performing at a higher level in unpredictable
environments.
How do we know if what we are doing is making a difference?
Doing drills based on broken-down running mechanisms should

期望很重要。 这对我们来说可能是显而易见的，但较低的次数可能并
不意味着我们的运动员需要更重或更快的注意力。我们不应该期望我们
的运动员直观地理解我们编写的每个程序想要做什么。 然而，我们应
该期望他们以不同的方式感知和理解我们所说的内容。当我们评估对计
划隐含期望的解释时，可以在中周期结束时说同样的话。 相对于预定
的重点，我们是否有所改进？ 这种改善与参加该计划的个人有关。

我们如何实现隐性结果是通过明确的关注。 我们从我们所拥有的执
行水平中得到我们所得到的。 如果我们有一个为期 4 周的中周期，我
们应该明确关注技术。首先要考虑的是根据训练年龄或接触某物的水平
提供线索。 外部或内部、朝向或远离、类比或隐喻以及演示能力是获
得明确焦点的主要工具（Winkleman，2020）。 我们想要改进，并且我
们必须考虑如何作为完成它的主要驱动力。

开放式练习的好处
开放式训练是无脚本的训练，运动员需要找出解决未确定问题的
方法。 对于教练来说，这是对你的计划的终极考验。 您的程序
所代表的解决方案比您用来评估程序有效性的任何其他东西都更
能在开放的环境中展示。
所有训练计划都是为了减少比赛期间发生的事情。 减少之后，
我们会一遍又一遍地重复某些元素，并增加负载、速度或持续时
间。这种强调重复的方法旨在对应于在不可预测的环境中以更高
水平执行。
我们如何知道我们正在做的事情是否有所作为？进行基于故障
运行机制的演练应

translate into increased running speed. Getting stronger should
increase power. We prove this through testing. We assessed the
problem, created a solution, and tested to see if that solution was
effective.
But jumping higher or running faster is not the real test;
performing in an unpredictable environment is. An open drill is a
proxy for how getting stronger or faster applies to performance.
The entire premise of reduction and repetition is to make the
system more efficient. We have a greater reserve to move, and
that should increase the odds of being successful when we
cannot predict what will happen.
As a coach, let go of the situation and accept that you cannot
control everything. A key to open drills within a training program
is that you are relinquishing the illusion of control that a coach is
perceived to have. We enhance smaller, more reproducible
parts, but that is not the purpose of programming. We enhance
parts to serve as a platform to reveal limiting factors. An athlete
who loses a game that you constructed to demonstrate skill at a
certain point during the off-season paints a clear picture of what
is needed.
Open games give credence to redundancies. If an athlete is
not performing well during a game, it does not mean their
training was wrong. It means the focus was on the wrong thing.
The ultimate benefit of open drills and games is creating a clear
depiction of what is needed. That will guide training and reinforce
the coach’s responsibility as a guide to increased performance.

Feedback
Last is feedback. We can say a couple of things after a set or the completion
of a drill. Completing objectives based on predetermined standards is referred
to as task-intrinsic feedback. Task-intrinsic feedback is simply whether the
athlete does what was asked of them. At this point, you should do a selfinventory: What is your primary form of feedback? Is it exclusively task

转化为跑步速度的提高。 变得更强应该增加力量。我们通过测试
证明了这一点。我们评估了问题，创建了解决方案，并进行了测
试以查看该解决方案是否有效。
但跳得更高或跑得更快并不是真正的考验；真正的考验是考验

或更快对表现的影响。减少和重复的整个前提是让系统更加高效
。 我们有更大的行动储备，当我们无法预测会发生什么时，这应
该会增加成功的几率。
作为一名教练，放下现状并接受你无法控制一切的事实。 在训
练计划中开展训练的关键是你要放弃教练所拥有的控制幻觉。 我
们增强了更小、更可复制的部件，但这不是编程的目的。 我们增

开放的游戏让裁员变得可信。 如果运动员在比赛中表现不佳，

事情上。公开训练和游戏的最终好处是清楚地描述需要什么。这
将指导训练并强化教练作为提高表现指导的责任。

反馈
最后是反馈。在一组或完成训练后我们可以说几件事。根据预定标准完
成目标称为task-intrinsic feedback。 任务内在反馈就是运动员是否按照
要求去做。 此时，您应该进行自我盘点：您的反馈的主要形式是什么
？ 是专门的任务吗

intrinsic? This is not an awful thing, but you can see that it applies more to
temporal goals and implicit focus.
However, we can give feedback during the drill or set. Augmented
feedback comes in the form of the athlete knowing they are performing
something well or reaching the benchmarks, such as rep integrity or velocity
during the set or drill. The spatial focus of how well someone is performing
dictates the level of feedback. Bad positioning or poor range of motion
should be met with immediate feedback, such as “Get your depth,” “Keep
your chest up,” or “Rack it and lighten the weight.” If the athlete is not
performing adequately by missing reps or target bar speed, they should be
met with some intervention, such as cueing, correction, or interruption. We
can further break that down into knowledge of results or performance. As an
example of results, did they make the rep, did they maintain position, or
would range of motion be the actual performance?

constantly in your mind as you are coaching. A good program will take into
account these components based on the principles and rules you have created.
Common sense means doing something that has a high constraint, clearly
determined outcome goal, low challenge, clear focus, and direct feedback
with novice athletes. Experience teaches us that we need to frame the
necessary amount of constraint with more spatial goals, challenge, explicit
focus, and augmented feedback with more advanced athletes (figure 16.3).
Here’s the rub: Everything and nothing can work. You will not know until
you at least try. You have to write programs, you have to determine the
targeted outcome of those programs, and then you have to inventory where
the results came from. If you did not reach an outcome, you should have
some knowledge of what was emphasized regarding coaching the program.
Let’s break down the cadence of coaching meetings to best set this up.

Meetings
I can say this with confidence: If you meet too much, you will burn your staff
out. I can also say with confidence: If you do not meet enough, you will risk
having an underinformed staff. I am sure that is not helpful right now, but it
is important to understand that we, as strength coaches, are typically
amplified in how we operate. If we commit to not meeting, we never meet,
and our coaches are uninformed. If we commit to a meeting, we probably
meet too much and are disenfranchised with coaching.

Daily Plan
Instead of saying we should not do something too much or too little, a better
means to evaluate this is by asking what determines good coaching. We have
situations with extremely inexperienced staff who need a lot of structure and
context. We also have situations with extremely experienced staff who need a
lot of freedom and less context. You have to ascertain which meetings are
necessary for your entire staff.
There are two vectors we need to consider with the frequency of meetings:
staff education and staff training. Education is based on the pretense that we
are not informed or not exposed to something before. We need a foundation
of information before sorting through nomenclature, program structure,

当你在训练的时候，不断地在你的脑海里。一个好的程序将根据您创建
的原则和规则考虑这些组件。常识意味着做一些具有高约束、明确确定
的结果目标、低挑战、明确的重点以及与新手运动员直接反馈的事情。
经验告诉我们，我们需要通过更多的空间目标、挑战、明确的焦点和更
高级的运动员的增强反馈来制定必要的约束（图16.3）。
问题是：一切都行不通，但什么都行不通。至少在你尝试之前你不会
知道。 您必须编写程序，必须确定这些程序的目标结果，然后必须清
点结果的来源。 如果您没有取得成果，您应该对指导该计划所强调的
内容有所了解。让我们分解一下辅导会议的节奏，以最好地进行设置。

会议
我可以自信地说：如果你见面太多，你的员工就会精疲力竭。我也可以
自信地说：如果你见面不够，你就会面临员工信息不足的风险。我确信
这现在没有帮助，但重要的是要了解，我们作为力量教练，通常会在我
们的运作方式上被放大。 如果我们承诺不见面，我们就永远不会见面
，我们的教练也不会知情。 如果我们承诺参加一次会议，我们可能会
见得太多，并且被剥夺了接受辅导的权利。

每日计划
与其说我们不应该做太多或太少的事情，更好的评估方法是询问什么决
定了良好的指导。我们遇到过员工经验极其缺乏的情况，他们需要大量
的结构和背景。我们也遇到过经验丰富的员工需要大量自由和较少背景
的情况。 您必须确定哪些会议对于您的全体员工来说是必要的。
关于会议频率，我们需要考虑两个因素：员工教育和员工培训。教育
是建立在我们之前不了解或未接触过某些事物的假装之上的。 在对术
语、程序结构进行排序之前，我们需要一个信息基础，

exercise technique and standards, leveraging hardware and software, and
accountability with athletes. Education is designed to give the uninformed a
baseline level of knowledge. However, there is training that is based on the
pretense that staff are informed and have been exposed to something prior
(figure 16.4). Experience refines things but also dulls things and creates bad
habits by doubling down on false information that erodes coaching ability.
Training is designed to eliminate bad habits and fix bad practices.
Daily meetings are based on training and reviewing things the staff should
know. We do this to either reinforce the mission or remind us of important
aspects of the program. What a daily meeting provides is a means to prevent
problems from happening. Training is, at its core, a reaction to problems. The
staff has demonstrated an understanding of what to do, but they are just not
doing it. It could be that they have forgotten or lost interest. We address this
by reminding and reinforcing with a daily meeting.

Weekly Plan
The vector of education is prospective, and the vector of training is
retrospective. With education, we have to assume they do not know, and we
need to review everything. Education is definitely when someone is starting a
new job but also typically at the beginning of an off-season. With training,
we do not want to assume they know everything, but we have to have some
standard to evaluate whether they are executing their job. Intertraining
sessions or posttraining day debriefs on mistakes made are the foundation;
acknowledging the problem and addressing it immediately is a prerequisite to
fixing something rapidly. Recurring problems could be problems with
education, and revisiting onboarding and annual meeting points of emphasis
or structure could solve the problem. It could mean something systemic that
you will need to address with staff meetings.

情况并接触过某些内容（图 16.4）。 经验可以使事情变得精炼，但也
会通过加倍削弱教练能力的错误信息来使事情变得迟钝并养成坏习惯。
培训旨在消除不良习惯并纠正不良做法。
每日会议以培训和审查员工应了解的内容为基础。 我们这样做是为
了强化使命或提醒我们该计划的重要方面。每日会议提供的是防止问题

我们通过每日会议提醒和强化来解决这个问题。

每周计划
教育的载体是前瞻性的，培训的载体是回顾性的。对于教育，我们必须

Weekly meetings are based on education by having a forum to discuss
new and interesting topics. We break up education into things we need to
learn and things we want to learn. Having an objective with education is
important. Having accountability with a weekly meeting makes education
valuable. Each week, having a planned topic that allows the staff to
collaborate and connect is powerful for performance.
Your staff will need three things to be successful: knowledge of how to do
their job, the tools to do their job, and the motivation to do their job.
Knowledge comes from educating your staff; knowledge of how to use the
tools at their disposal comes from education, and motivation comes from
training. Your job as a head coach is to educate your staff on what and how to
do their job, along with training your staff to want to do their job effectively
over time.
Your best bet to facilitate the appropriate amount of education and training
is to understand how to leverage meetings. Timing education at the onset of
employment or the beginning of the year is your best bet for success. You

Education
Education starts with job requirements. When you hire or promote someone,
you should have some objective tasks for them. Something as simple as a job
title can be the clearest description of what someone is required to do. A
strength and conditioning coach will be required to coach strength and
conditioning. But we all know that there can very easily be a significant
amount of nuance associated with one strength coach versus another.

What Do They Need to Know?
We need clearly defined responsibilities for each coach to determine
education. There are universal responsibilities and specific responsibilities.
Coaching athletes is a universal responsibility. How that is done and what is
objective determines whether a strength coach is good or bad. Start with rep
integrity, work to set integrity, then training session integrity. What is a good
rep, a good set, and a good training session? The integrity of each rep, set,
and training session will be the responsibility of each coach. Finding ways to
evaluate a coach from the smallest aspects of training to the largest is the
premise of education for a strength coach.
Understanding the basic aspects of the program and the nomenclature of
drills and exercises is a prerequisite for strength coaches. Being able to
demonstrate drills and exercises is a prerequisite for strength coaches. Being
able to coach, cue, and give feedback is paramount for all strength coaches.
This is not the responsibility of some, but of all strength coaches. The ability
to execute this is what you base your education on for each strength coach.
Next are the specific responsibilities of the strength coach. A strength
coach responsible for nutrition will need to know things like body
composition testing, supplementation, nutrition guidance, and nutritional
coaching. A strength coach responsible for sports science will need to know
things like using testing hardware SOPs, how to teach and instruct coaches
and athletes to maintain SOPs, and how to interpret and communicate results.
A strength coach responsible for returning to play after an injury will need to
create an open line of communication with sports medicine, be able to

训练结束后，可能每周一次。节奏很重要。

教育
教育始于工作要求。当你雇用或晋升某人时，你应该为他们设定一些目
标任务。像职位名称这样简单的东西就可以最清楚地描述某人需要做什
么。 需要体能教练来指导体能训练。 但我们都知道，一位力量教练与
另一位力量教练之间很容易存在大量细微差别。

他们需要知道什么？
我们需要明确规定每位教练的职责来确定教育。 有普遍责任和特殊责
任。指导运动员是一项普遍的责任。如何做到这一点以及目标是什么决
定了力量教练的好坏。从代表诚信开始，努力设定诚信，然后是培训课
程诚信。什么是好的代表、好的组数和好的训练课程？ 每一次代表、
每组训练和训练课程的完整性将是每位教练的责任。找到从训练中最小
的方面到最大的方面来评价教练的方法，是力量教练教育的前提。

了解该计划的基本方面以及训练和练习的术语是力量教练的先决条件
。 能够演示训练和练习是力量教练的先决条件。对于所有力量教练来
说，能够指导、提示和提供反馈是至关重要的。这不是某些人的责任，
而是所有力量教练的责任。执行此操作的能力是每个力量教练接受教育
的基础。
接下来是力量教练的具体职责。 负责营养的力量教练需要了解身体
成分测试、补充、营养指导和营养指导等知识。 负责运动科学的力量
教练需要了解诸如使用测试硬件标准操作程序、如何教导和指导教练和
运动员维护标准操作程序以及如何解释和传达结果等知识。负责受伤后
重返赛场的力量教练需要与运动医学建立开放的沟通渠道，能够

implement and interpret table tests and functional movement screens, and
program progressions, regressions, and lateralizations based on the level and
rate of rehabilitation. Other responsibilities will be needed, but these are the
foundation of each position.
The flow for education is to evaluate what is needed for that strength
coach and their job title and reverse engineer a curriculum to execute it.
Ideally, you have qualified and trained coaches who have a working
knowledge of their responsibilities and can fast-track the process. You should
not assume they know; it could be something as simple as the terminology
used previously, and they may need to be educated on the appropriate terms
to use.
Hiring people based on their familiarity with what you do helps.
Promoting interns, grad assistants, and part-time employees makes education
a lot faster and easier than hiring externally. In the event you hire externally
from your organization, you will need to determine their aptitude to learn a
new system and terminology. Hiring smart, intuitive, and resourceful coaches
always has tremendous value when they are learning to assimilate into a new
staff and program.

What Do They Know?
The length of time it takes to educate is entirely dependent on familiarity or
intelligence. You are trying to create basic aptitude based on a clearly defined
set of responsibilities. Ensuring each of your coaches knows how to do their
job and leverages the tools to do their job is an essential piece of having a
cohesive and competent staff. Having tests or benchmarks to determine their
level of learning dictates how long education needs to be. We are always
working against the clock and need as many hands as possible to ensure we
are providing the best experience for our athletes, but that should not come at
the expense of the quality with which you do something.
Create benchmarks and milestones for each new coach:
Not allowed to take athletes through a movement prep until vetted and
graded by an existing coach
Not allowed to break down the lift until vetted and graded by an

教育流程是评估力量教练及其职位所需的内容，并对课程进行逆向工

教育所需的时间长短完全取决于熟悉程度或智力。您正在尝试根据一组
明确定义的职责来培养基本能力。确保每位教练都知道如何完成自己的
工作并利用工具来完成自己的工作，这是拥有一支有凝聚力、有能力的
员工队伍的重要组成部分。通过测试或基准来确定他们的学习水平决定
了教育需要多长时间。 我们总是争分夺秒地工作，需要尽可能多的人
手来确保为运动员提供最好的体验，但这不应以牺牲工作质量为代价。

为每位新教练创建基准和里程碑：
在现有教练审查和评分之前，不允许带运动员进行动作准备 在现

Not allowed to perform a test or screen until vetted and graded by an
existing coach
The trick is to make the vetting process a universal responsibility of every
strength coach. Peer-to-peer evaluation is much more effective than top-down
evaluation. Top-down evaluations create a bottleneck if only one person can
take others through a benchmark assessment. The other aspect is that the
teacher learns best. Having coaches instruct and take others through
assessments means they will need to understand the responsibilities of their
job that much more. Once they are properly vetted and graded, they will
move on to the next phase or be integrated into the program.
What you will find is that the resources you allocate to hiring will expose
a length of time to educate new staff. More vetting during interviewing will
lead to less time spent educating staff. This is the time and money equation.
Your cost of interviewing is substantially less than your cost during
onboarding and education. If you have a coach who cannot contribute for
months on end because of not having a dialed-in hiring process, you will pay
for that mistake for your entire tenure.

Training
The assumption is that each coach understands their primary responsibility as
a coach. Education is all about understanding what is not yet known, whereas
training is improving or refining that which is known. This is an important
distinction because the act of correcting actions by a coach is drastically
different if the person does not understand versus if they are not maintaining
the standard.

What Can They Do?
The last thing the strength coach should need is motivation to constantly
deliver. Details matter a great deal in coaching and programming. Strength
and conditioning mean constantly doing small things well over time. It is
asking someone to do something correctly with more external load, higher
speeds, longer durations, or generally more intensity than they did previously.
It is demanding something of someone who inherently does not want to do it.

在经过现有教练的审查和评分之前，不允许进行测试或筛选
诀窍是让审查过程成为每个力量教练的普遍责任。同行评价比自上而
下的评价有效得多。如果只有一个人可以带领其他人进行基准评估，那
么自上而下的评估就会产生瓶颈。 另一方面是老师学得最好。 让教练
指导并带领其他人进行评估意味着他们需要更多地了解自己的工作职责
。 一旦经过适当的审查和评分，他们将进入下一阶段或整合到该计划
中。
您会发现，您分配给招聘的资源将暴露出培训新员工的时间长度。
在面试过程中进行更多审查将减少培训员工的时间。 这就是时间和金
钱的等式。您的面试成本大大低于入职和教育期间的成本。 如果你的
教练因为没有拨入的招聘流程而连续几个月无法做出贡献，那么你将在
整个任期内为这个错误付出代价。

训练
假设每个教练都了解他们作为教练的主要责任。教育的目的是了解未知
的事物，而培训则是改进或完善已知的事物。 这是一个重要的区别，
因为如果教练不理解和不保持标准，教练纠正行为的行为是截然不同的
。

他们能做什么？
力量教练最不需要的就是不断交付的动力。 细节在辅导和编程中非常
重要。 力量和体能训练意味着随着时间的推移，不断地做好小事。 它
要求某人以比以前更大的外部负荷、更高的速度、更长的持续时间或通
常更高的强度来正确地做某件事。它要求一个本来不想做的人做某事。

In reality, we exist to provide structure to working hard and doing things
correctly.
What is the concentric circle of good coaching? How you do one thing is
how you do everything; messaging is important. Strength coaches are the
conduits for improved performance. We can take a slow, weak, small, or
poorly conditioned athlete to a stratosphere of performance they could never
dream of. We produce that outcome by coaching to a standard. It is an
awesome responsibility, and it is a privilege to have it.

What Do They Need to Do?
There are two components of training to consider here: new hires and veteran
coaches. New hires need to be held to a standard of doing something based
on the pedestal you put responsibilities on during the education period. It is
catastrophic when a coach has to go to great lengths to coach a movement
prep, and then it is wildly inconsistent with every other coach. The other end
of this continuum is the veteran coaches, who must uphold the standard over
time.
Having a conversation about performance with a veteran coach without
standards is impossible. If there were SOPs and a coach has been doing
something incorrectly for years, that is now the SOP for that particular thing.
Saying to do it correctly would be against the way that the coach has always
done it. It starts with everyone being held to the same standards, with no
exceptions. If there are standards and that coach is doing them incorrectly,
you have a platform to correct that action.
With training, there is prospecting and reacting. Prospecting information
based on common knowledge that certain things will deteriorate without
emphasis is easily the best strategy with training. Daily huddles that go over
daily objectives, schedules, individual responsibilities, current events, and
updates are the simplest and most effective way to train staff (figure 16.5). A
good leader anticipates problems and finds solutions beforehand. Veteran
coaches need to understand their expectations every day. The difference is
that novice coaches are centered on how you communicate. Daily huddles
that tell a novice coach where to stand, what to do, what to say, when to say
something, and what to do afterward are direct and clear. Daily huddles that

An important aspect of the daily huddle is allowing for collaboration.
Dictation will be met with deaf ears over time. Having a component of that
meeting asking if there is anything I am missing or if there is anything that
could go wrong is an open invitation to collaborate. Some coaches like to
hear themselves speak and will chime in no matter what. Often, it will be
repeating back what you just said as a means to demonstrate they agree with
you. Sometimes, it will be unrelated aspects that you will need to steer away
from to stay focused on the task at hand. In either scenario, you have your
staff talking, and that is a good thing.
A weekly plan (figure 16.6) is optional and could be argued to be overkill
based on having daily huddles, but a weekly layout can be very helpful.
Weekly plans can be either prospective or retrospective. Having a recap of
the week is valuable for feedback and training needs. Having a plan for the
week can be illuminating for the coach for that given week. The right answer
here is based on what works best for you. One aspect is that if daily huddles
are prospective, then weekly plans can be retrospective. Your litmus is based
on what your staff responds to and performs best with. You do not make your
decision based on what you prefer, but on what your staff executes best.

The other aspect of this is weekly staff meetings or seasonal workshops.
There is a definite need for communication, and if you can leverage meetings,
you have a great resource to connect with your staff and athletes. But at the
same time, you can crush morale with over meeting. Having a longer format
meeting focused on a topic can be transformational for your staff if you know
how to leverage meetings.
Meetings can be a huge aspect of training if you are organized and make
the most of the time. Get comfortable talking in front of your peers. Be
careful about being too preachy or getting on a pedestal. Your staff is not
paid to pay attention to you. Be careful of being too loose or too group
focused. Socratic questioning, asking why, is good but can be inefficient if
not well structured. Have segments where you lead and segments where staff
are involved (figure 16.7). Give your staff a heads-up on what they will be
responsible for during the meeting.

Evaluation
Schedule staff evaluations and use them to determine the need for ongoing
training. Evaluations are a great proxy to determine the level of execution
and, therefore, the need to revisit some things. What you will find is that
there are systemic problems and isolated issues. Systemic problems mean
revisiting education and scheduling training. Isolated issues mean a one-onone meeting to address and correct.

Peer Evaluation
One-on-one conversations can be used as a debriefing after the session on
areas that need direct discussion. Addressing a performance problem
immediately is always a good strategy. There are situations where there might
not be time, or it could be a delicate situation. Scheduling a time to talk is the
next step. It’s better to be direct in these situations. Be careful to correct not
the person but the action if it is the action that was executed poorly.
Reinforcing performance by having planned peer evaluations can be a
powerful driver of performance. When a coach critiques another coach, it

视教育和安排培训。 孤立的问题意味着需要召开一对一的会议来解决
和纠正。

同行评价
一对一的对话可以用作会议结束后需要直接讨论的领域的汇报。 立即

are not living up to their potential.

Top-Down Evaluation
If an issue involves a person, it relates to their motivation or motives.
Motivation to do one’s job is never a certainty. You, as a leader, have to take
ownership of the situation if the staff is constantly losing interest in doing a
good job; it is you, the leader, who is at fault. If one coach has dropped in
motivation, addressing the issue head-on is imperative. Results will come
down to effort, execution, and consistency over time. It’s the consistency of
effort and execution that will determine the outcome, and that starts with
coaches.

The supervisor still needs to conduct a performance review. As a boss, you

Take Home
Coaching is a skill. We can develop coaches with a solid plan. Coaching each
session to the highest attainable level is our best chance to ensure outcomes
from training. Giving the correct parameters for each session for a coach to
be successful is the direct responsibility of the head coach. Having great
education and training plans makes a world of difference in the performance
of each coach.

TRAINING SESSION DESIGN
We are finally here! I can only write so much before you start to wonder what
an actual program looks like. Before we do that, let’s review some things.
Good programming matters, and we have spent much time trying to
explain that. But a good program needs two things: principles (see figure 1.3
on page 7) and rules (figure 17.1). The principles are set; they do not need
context to be applied. The absence of principles means your program needs to
be improved by things we know are true. Rules, however, need context. Your
facility, your staff, your athletes, and all the other nuances of your program
require your unique rules.
It is your program, with your rules. Remember that we want to have a
foundation of biomechanics and physiology for our rules. The sport or
position, the training age, the biological age, the sex, and all the individual
aspects of your athletes determine the biomechanical and physiological rules.
You can maintain a period with increased focus on certain elements in
situations with time constraints and a particular quality, but not forever.
What is a training program? It is simple when you break it down into
segmented periods. A training session is a cluster of exercises broken up into
clusters of sets. Breaking it down even further, all sets are a cluster of reps.
All reps are in a sequence of eccentric to isometric to concentric to isometric
contractions. If we are going to break down the quality of a session (figure
17.2), we simply need to evaluate the quality of each rep, set, sets for each
exercise, and each exercise.

17
培训课程设计
我们终于来了！在你开始想知道实际的程序是什么样子之前，我只能写
这么多。在我们这样做之前，让我们回顾一些事情。
良好的编程很重要，我们花了很多时间试图解释这一点。但一个好的
程序需要两件事：原则（参见第 7 页的图 1.3）和规则（图 17.1）。 原
则已定； 他们不需要应用上下文。缺乏原则意味着您的计划需要通过
我们已知的事实来改进。然而，规则需要背景。您的设施、员工、运动
员以及项目的所有其他细微差别都需要您独特的规则。
这是你的程序，有你的规则。 请记住，我们希望为我们的规则奠定
生物力学和生理学的基础。 运动或位置、训练年龄、生物年龄、性别
以及运动员的所有个人方面决定了生物力学和生理规则。在时间有限和
特定质量的情况下，您可以在一段时间内更加关注某些元素，但不能永
远如此。
什么是培训计划？ 当你把它分成几个分段的时期时，事情就很简单
了。训练课程是一组分为几组的练习。 进一步细分，所有组数都是一
组重复次数。所有次数均按偏心收缩、等长收缩、同心收缩、等长收缩
的顺序进行。 如果我们要分解训练的质量（图 17.2），我们只需要评
估每个次数、每组、每组练习以及每项练习的质量。

The workout needs to be relevant to the coaches and athletes going
through the program. With Newell’s model, do we have an account for the
organism and the tasks we are asking of it within its environments? With
Ericsson’s model, do we have an account for the goal of the training session,
the necessary level of challenge and focus, and the feedback you will have to
give?
A training session has two primary components: movement preparation
and the training session. Each segment has its own approach and needs a
separate discussion. Both fall to the principles and rules. The difference is
how we focus on certain rules based on the segment we are working within.

Movement Prep
The movement prep should prepare the athlete for the session. Having
context for the goal, the challenge, the level of focus, and the feedback
needed to create an appropriate movement prep is essential. There needs to be
cohesion between what we do during the training session and what we do
during the movement prep.
The movement prep can have a large concentric circle within the training
session. The potential for movement during training sessions is seen long
before the movement prep. If we do not have the prerequisite movement
ability when we are warming up, the likelihood that we will have it when we
are training is lessened, which makes movement prep a potential proxy of
training session potential.
We established that the movement screen is the foundation of our
biomechanical rules (see figure 9.1 on page 153) and thus the exercises we

图 17.2 培训课程。

以及创建适当的运动准备所需的反馈是至关重要的。我们在训练期间所
做的事情和我们在运动准备期间所做的事情之间需要保持一致。
运动准备可以在训练过程中有一个大的同心圆。 训练期间的运动潜
力早在运动准备之前就已显现。 如果我们在热身时不具备必要的运动
能力，那么我们在训练时拥有这种能力的可能性就会降低，这使得运动
准备成为训练课程潜力的潜在指标。

select. By process of elimination, we can say that if we have pain, lack of

运动准备期的目标是为个人训练做好准备。 运动范围和控制是准备
