We then increase the coordination of the associated motor units that
correspond to that movement pattern. Then we increase the temperature or
tolerance of the tissues that will be used during the training session based on
the goal.
A big piece of the movement prep is ruling out limiting factors. An
argument could be made that focusing on flexibility, which is classified as
passive ROM (PROM), is counterproductive to high-velocity or high-force
movements. The logic associated with static stretching is not conducive to
performing well with higher-threshold activities, but it is fundamentally
sound. With that said, there is an acute response from static stretching. If we
were to static stretch and then ask someone to immediately sprint or jump,
performance would be lessened. But that is never the case, and static
stretching is a precursor to more activities later that will need that potential
for ROM.
Taking a step back and focusing on tissue quality with soft tissue
modalities, such as self-myofascial release, can be met with resistance. It is
the same with conversations about occupying a weight room with isolated
pieces of equipment; you will regret not having it. In the case of tissue
quality, you will regret not spending more time on it if an injury has
occurred. The same is true of conversations about flexibility; it is a priority
we need to address. If we find during our movement screen that all athletes
lack requisite ROM, we will need to focus on releasing and lengthening
tissues associated with the patterns we are going to use. Time spent or a drop
in performance is a moot conversation if we lack the necessary ROM before
we start. Any drill or performance of that drill during a session will be
compromised; thus, we are obligated to commit a portion of the movement
prep to improving tissue quality and flexibility.

Tissue Extensibility
Strategy is centered on the goal of the training session. If we are looking to
improve linear speed, we need to create the length of the tissues associated
with those motor patterns. Front and side mechanics of ankle, knee, and hip
flexion, along with back and side mechanics of ankle, knee, and hip
extension, need to be vetted for potential. Having a small but focused period

然后，我们增加与该运动模式相对应的相关运动单位的协调性。 然后
，我们根据目标提高训练期间使用的组织的温度或耐受性。
运动准备的一个重要部分是排除限制因素。 有人可能会认为，专注
于灵活性（被归类为被动 ROM (PROM)）对于高速或高力量运动会适得
其反。 与静态拉伸相关的逻辑不利于在较高阈值的活动中表现良好，
但从根本上来说是合理的。话虽如此，静态拉伸会产生敏锐的反应。如
果我们进行静态拉伸，然后要求某人立即冲刺或跳跃，那么表现就会下
降。 但事实并非如此，静态拉伸是以后更多活动的先兆，这些活动需
要 ROM 的潜力。

退一步并通过软组织方式（例如自我肌筋膜释放）关注组织质量可能
会遇到阻力。 这与关于用孤立的设备占据举重室的对话是一样的； 你
会后悔没有它。 就组织质量而言，如果发生损伤，您会后悔没有花更
多时间在上面。 关于灵活性的对话也是如此。 这是我们需要解决的一
个优先事项。 如果我们在运动筛查中发现所有运动员都缺乏必要的活
动度，我们将需要专注于释放和延长与我们将要使用的模式相关的组织
。如果我们在开始之前缺乏必要的 ROM，那么花费时间或性能下降都
是没有意义的话题。 训练期间的任何练习或该练习的表现都会受到影
响； 因此，我们有义务投入一部分运动准备来提高组织质量和灵活性
。

组织延伸性
策略以培训课程的目标为中心。 如果我们希望提高线速度，我们需要
创建与这些运动模式相关的组织长度。 踝关节、膝关节和髋关节屈曲
的正面和侧面力学，以及踝关节、膝关节和髋关节伸展的背侧和侧面力
学，都需要进行潜力审查。有一个短暂但专注的时期

of specific static stretches looking to increase either extension or flexion
gives insight into potential mechanics during sprinting. There is no cue to
compensate for the lack of PROM in the ankle, knee, and hip joints during
sprinting.
But with that said, this does not have to take considerable time or be
completely passive. Using strategies of proprioceptive neuromuscular
facilitation or isometrics at length, we leverage this period to increase PROM
and potentiate motor units. Passive range of motion is not exclusive to
passive stretching. It focuses on increasing the noncontractile range of the
tissues. Understanding the PROM potential, combined with strategies to
cover multiple bases simultaneously, has far too much value not to be
included.
Next is mobility, or active ROM (AROM). This is an area that we are
probably most comfortable with before a training session. It is the action of
moving into a ROM that feels most appropriate before the session. The issue
with exclusively focusing on mobility is that we are only capable of moving
to the limits of our PROM. We can rarely move past our PROM limitations,
which means that mobility never increases the potential for ROM, which
limits the potential for mechanics and return on investment from the exercises
we use during training.
We are also ramping up during the dynamic portion of the sessions. The
ability to take a slow start and progress with control to higher-rate
movements is an approach that deserves some discussion. Not every coach is
comfortable with a slow ramp of soft tissue, flexibility, and then mobility.
Working with younger athletes who have low attention spans makes a slow
start a nightmare. As the coach, you are in a constant battle with having
command and doing best practices. It is not a 100% compromise, but it places
a strain on the coach. The response to this is that you are good at what you
emphasize, and if you are not directly coaching it, it will not be as valued.
However, developing trust and rapport with your athletes to allow them
autonomy with performing soft tissue and flexibility on their own is a
valuable coaching method. No matter what you choose, a ramp that is guided
or unguided, having a plan for establishing ROM passively and actively will
make a big difference.

旨在增加伸展或屈曲的特定静态伸展可以深入了解冲刺期间的潜在力学
。 在短跑期间，没有任何提示可以补偿踝关节、膝关节和髋关节的 PR
OM 缺乏。
但话虽如此，这并不需要花费大量时间或完全被动。 使用本体感觉
神经肌肉促进或等长训练策略，我们利用这一时期来增加 PROM 并增
强运动单位。 被动运动范围并不只限于被动伸展。 它的重点是增加组
织的非收缩范围。 了解 PROM 的潜力，结合同时覆盖多个基地的策略
，具有太多的价值，不容忽视。

接下来是移动性，或主动 ROM (AROM)。 这是我们在训练前最熟悉
的区域。 在训练之前，感觉最合适的就是进入 ROM 的动作。只关注移
动性的问题是我们只能移动到 PROM 的极限。我们很少能够超越 PRO
M 的限制，这意味着流动性永远不会增加 ROM 的潜力，这限制了我们
在训练期间使用的练习的机械潜力和投资回报。

我们也在会议的动态部分加大力度。 缓慢启动并控制较高速率运动
的能力是一种值得讨论的方法。并不是每个教练都能适应缓慢的软组织
、灵活性和灵活性的提升。与注意力不集中的年轻运动员一起工作会让
缓慢的开始成为一场噩梦。 作为教练，你要不断地与指挥和最佳实践
作斗争。这不是100%的妥协，但它给教练带来了压力。 对此的回应是
，你擅长你所强调的事情，如果你不直接指导它，它就不会受到重视。
然而，与运动员建立信任和融洽关系，让他们能够自主地执行软组织和
灵活性，是一种有价值的教练方法。无论你选择什么，有引导或无引导
的坡道，制定被动和主动建立 ROM 的计划都会产生很大的不同。

The most overlooked aspect of movement prep in a group environment is
the organization. How we orient our team at the onset of training affects the
organization of the training session. Soft tissue and flexibility will be looser
than a structured line-to-line-based mobility and dynamic warm-up segment.
When working with younger athletes or a larger group, consider that the
strategy you have for organization, or lack thereof, may need to take
precedence. Not having control at the onset of the group will decrease the
likelihood of having control later.
With mobility, we want to continue what we started with tissue quality
and length. Taking this enhanced ROM and applying AROM is an important
transition for the rest of the workout. We are capitalizing on the newfound
ROM to make plastic changes to the tissues and to access them during
integrated movements and drills. In the linear speed session, we can use ankle
dorsiflexion and plantar flexion, knee flexion (extension is rarely a problem),
and hip flexion and extension mobility drills. We can do this in place or
locomoting from one spot to the next (line to line).

Movement Coordination
Potential is useless if we do not figure out how to integrate it. We have
established that tissue quality, PROM, and AROM are more prepared states;
now we have to do something with them. Just because we go through a
greater degree of excursion than we could 5 to 10 min before, does not mean
that ROM will be used during dynamic high-threshold activities. We now
need to coordinate movement better and apply it to the training session.
First, we need to control movement. Balance is an underrated aspect when
working with athletes. We take for granted that they are excellent
compensators and may have severe deficiencies with proprioception and
control. The movement screen may reveal we have asymmetries, and that is
as much a control issue as it is a ROM issue. Asymmetries are multivariate
but typically result from a previous injury, redundant patterns, or body
structure.
We cannot control body structure, but it is worth talking about. We are
naturally asymmetrical. We have different internal environments with
locations of internal organs and subsequent flow of fluids within the body

在团体环境中，运动准备中最容易被忽视的方面是组织。我们在培训
开始时如何引导团队会影响培训课程的组织。 软组织和灵活性将比结
构化的基于线到线的移动性和动态热身部分更宽松。当与年轻运动员或
更大的团体一起工作时，请考虑您可能需要优先考虑您的组织策略或缺
乏组织策略。 在小组开始时没有控制权会降低以后获得控制权的可能
性。
就移动性而言，我们希望继续我们从组织质量和长度开始的努力。采
用这种增强的 ROM 并应用 AROM 是其余训练的重要过渡。 我们正在
利用新发现的 ROM 对组织进行塑性改变，并在综合运动和训练中访问
它们。在线性速度训练中，我们可以使用踝关节背屈和跖屈、膝关节屈
曲（伸展很少成为问题）以及髋关节屈伸活动训练。 我们可以就地执
行此操作，也可以从一个地点移动到下一个地点（从线到线）。

动作协调
如果我们不弄清楚如何整合潜力，那么潜力就毫无用处。 我们已经确
定组织质量、PROM 和 AROM 是更准备好的状态；现在我们必须对他
们做点什么。 仅仅因为我们经历了比之前 5 到 10 分钟更大程度的偏移
，并不意味着在动态高阈值活动期间会使用 ROM。 我们现在需要更好
地协调动作并将其应用到训练中。
首先，我们需要控制运动。与运动员合作时，平衡是一个被低估的方
面。 我们理所当然地认为它们是优秀的补偿器，但在本体感觉和控制
方面可能存在严重缺陷。 运动屏幕可能会显示出不对称性，这既是控
制问题，也是 ROM 问题。 不对称是多因素造成的，但通常是由先前的
损伤、多余的模式或身体结构造成的。
我们无法控制身体结构，但值得一谈。 我们天生不对称。 我们有不
同的内部环境，包括内部器官的位置以及随后体内液体的流动

that give rise to organic asymmetries in our skeletal and muscular systems.
This is out of our control, but we can learn to manage certain aspects of this
by having a dialed-in plan to account for it. Most of our movements will be
constrained in some manner. Stances and posture will be accounted for when
we perform an action intended to generate velocity, force, or work. This
usually comes with a bilateral stance and a bilateral loaded external load. If
we are naturally asymmetrical and working to organize bilateral orientations
both top down and bottom up, we will create a natural torque in the structures
that are asymmetrically oriented in between. Will this break us? No, but we
do need to account for this with our nonloaded movements.

Athlete-Led Tracking
We have our training session planned, our coaches in place, and
we’re ready to go! The last thing on our minds is tracking data,
more specifically, how to track data.
The logistics of testing is the most overlooked aspect of a
training session. It does not have to be a burden; you have
assets that you can leverage to collect data. No one cares about
data more than the person you are collecting data from. Athleteled tracking is the best chance to get quality data while
minimizing workload.
There will be some front-end education about what and why
you are tracking each athlete. This is a good thing; one of the
more common criticisms of tracking is a lack of understanding
behind testing. Next, you will have to train your athletes on how
to track. The trick is to make it simple and easy to replicate.
Having athletes track their data is a system. We want to have
a system where athletes have a clear understanding of what they
are doing every day in everything we do. We often forget that no
one is more interested in the process than the athlete. Asking for
help from your athletes is a crucial step in a training program’s
success.
Here are some tips for having athletes track their data:

导致我们的骨骼和肌肉系统有机不对称。这是我们无法控制的，但我们
可以通过制定计划来管理它的某些方面。 我们的大部分行动都会受到
某种方式的限制。当我们执行旨在产生速度、力或功的动作时，将考虑
站姿和姿势。 这通常伴随着双边立场和双边加载的外部负载。 如果我

我们确实需要通过空载运动来解决这一问题。

测试的后勤工作是培训课程中最容易被忽视的方面。 它不一定

据的人更关心数据。运动员主导的跟踪是获得高质量数据同时最

让运动员跟踪他们的数据是一个系统。我们希望有一个系统，

员寻求帮助是训练计划成功的关键一步。
以下是让运动员跟踪数据的一些技巧：

Make it seamless. Include these on a training card or sheet
when possible: wellness, sleep quantity, training volume and
intensity, and rating of perceived exertion.
Use training software. Continuity of training cards is important
when you ask athletes to track their data. The more important
play here is syncing with cloud-based storage. Having
automatic migration of training data adds so much value; it
makes training software worth having.
Focus on missed data. Not tracking comes down to it being
confusing or complicated. Simplify and streamline. Clearly
understood questions and data entry are better than
complicated data collection. Missed entries are a sign that the
tracking system needs improvement.
Many of the mobility drills we may use will be in a half-kneeling, split
stance, or single-leg stance. We get a lot of value from this approach. We
develop balance and coordination while working to improve mobility. But we
also get a reprieve from constant bilateral actions. Chances are that we are
using these less stable positions because of the intuition that we need them.
My point is, do not fight that notion. Learn to double up aspects of mobility
and balance as much as possible. We get so many more benefits when we can
get multiple benefits simultaneously, as well as increase the function for the
next step.
The sequence of movement is about understanding the locomotion of
being a bipedal animal (moving on two feet). If we can coordinate our gait at
slow and controlled speeds, we can coordinate at faster speeds. The easiest
way to control ourselves is to increase the base of support surface area
relative to the ground. Controlling two points of contact in a standing position
is a lot harder to do than controlling four points of contact in a quadruped
position. When in doubt with control, increase surface area contact with the
ground, and chances are, control will improve dramatically.
The same logic applies with PROM being in place before AROM, as with
control and points of contact with the ground. Ruling out our ability to do a

健康状况、睡眠量、训练量和强度以及感知锻炼程度的评级。
Use training software.当您要求运动员跟踪他们的数据时，训练

我们可能使用的许多灵活性训练都是半跪、分腿或单腿站立。 我们

和平衡性。当我们能够同时获得多种好处时，我们会获得更多的好处，
并为下一步增加功能。
运动顺序是为了理解双足动物的运动（用两只脚移动）。如果我们能
够以缓慢且受控的速度协调我们的步态，我们就可以以更快的速度进行
协调。 控制自己的最简单方法是增加相对于地面的支撑表面积。在站
立位置控制两个接触点比在四足位置控制四个接触点要困难得多。 当
对控制有疑问时，增加与地面的接触面积，很可能控制力会显着提高。

同样的逻辑也适用于 PROM 在 AROM 之前就位，就像控制点和与地
面的接触点一样。 排除我们做某事的能力

pattern in a prone or supine position before a single-leg stance position is
more efficient. If we find out we can do something after the fact because we
are in an advanced position, we do not know what the limiting factor is. If we
open with the regressed position where more surface area is in contact with
the ground, we can rule out faster whether it is a control or ROM issue. If we
cannot execute a motor pattern with as balanced a position as possible in
either a prone or supine position, chances are it is a ROM issue.
The progression we should think about is as follows:
1. Prone, supine, side lying
2. Quadruped, tall kneeling, half kneeling
3. Bilateral stance, split stance, single-leg stance
We can incorporate all those stances within all different planes of motion
by adjusting the body segment in contact with the ground. Turning the knee
or foot out would be a transverse adjustment, having the knee or foot wide or
narrow would be a frontal plane adjustment, and having the knee or foot
forward or backward would be a sagittal plane adjustment.
Then we can combine that with orientation, where our arms are moving in
various vectors. By reaching our arms up and down, we have a vertical vector
movement. By reaching our arms across and crossing the midline, we have a
rotational movement. By reaching our arms laterally or medially, we have a
horizontal movement. We can combine any of these stances and reach
patterns to create a sequence of control in all planes and vectors.
We are challenging our athletes’ level of proprioceptive ability by
enriching their movement profile during the movement prep. By altering the
stance, the orientation of that stance, and integrating various vectors of
movement, we create a proprioceptive-rich environment that prepares our
athletes for all activities in the training session and the chaotic environment
of sport. Most muscular and connective tissue orientations are in an oblique
or transverse direction, the same as our fascial systems. We are organizing
tissue based on concepts of tensegrity: the interplay of tension and
compression. We want certain joints and tissues to be static and others to be
dynamic. This is how we can sustain extremely high forces internally.

。

我们通过在运动准备期间丰富运动员的运动概况来挑战运动员的本体

们创造了一个丰富的本体感受环境，让运动员为训练课程中的所有活动
和混乱的运动环境做好准备。 大多数肌肉和结缔组织的方向都是倾斜
或横向的，与我们的筋膜系统相同。 我们根据 tensegrity 的概念来组织
组织：张力和压力的相互作用。我们希望某些关节和组织是静态的，而
其他关节和组织是动态的。这就是我们如何能够在内部维持极高的力量
。
最后，我们要关注增强作用。增强作用给我们带来了什么

training session? It results in a greater output from whatever we are trying to
do. Potentiation can easily be replaced with intent. The idea is centered on
being intentional about how you do an activity so you can reap more benefit
from it. This can come in several forms, such as extensive plyometric work,
functional isometrics, irradiation techniques, or centration techniques.
For extensive plyometric work, we are looking at light rhythmic
movement. On paper, something like jumping rope is a great idea. That is,
until you realize the skill to get value from it is simply not there. Having lowamplitude jumps (two feet to two feet), hops (one foot to ipsilateral one foot),
bounds (one foot to contralateral one foot), and skips (hop to a bound) are
incredible for coordination and potentiation. We can progress them from in
place to transitional or integrate them into locomotive patterns. The
locomotor patterns include walking, jogging, running, shuffling, and carioca.
Again, we can integrate multiplanar foot positions and multivector arm
reaches.
Functional isometrics are an amazing tool to drive intent with athletes. We
have two categories: overcoming and yielding. Overcoming is a concentric
action away from the pull of gravity. Yielding is an eccentric action, also
away from gravity. Even without equipment, isometrics can become very
cumbersome if you let them. Keep it simple, understand the assignment, and
focus on the goal of the session. Overcoming isometrics is a great way to
drive intent with something, which may be beneficial to things like
acceleration or concentric force activities. Yielding isometrics are a great way
to create force at length, which may be beneficial for deceleration or
eccentric force activities. The trick is to get value without being bogged down
by equipment and lengthy explanations.
Irradiation and centration techniques are about creating compression
within joints, combined with the contraction of muscular tissues for stability.
No matter what, we will need to demonstrate control of the thorax and pelvis
during locomotion. We want our legs to be force generators and our arms to
be force suppliers. In between, we want to control the transfer of energy from
distal to proximal and then distal again. Centration, or packing of a joint, is a
powerful technique to control the thorax and pelvis during movement.
Packing a joint that is more suited for stability, such as the lumbar spine, can

很容易地被意图取代。 这个想法的核心是有意识地了解你如何进行一
项活动，这样你就可以从中获得更多的好处。 这可以有多种形式，例
如广泛的增强式训练、功能等长训练、照射技术或集中技术。
对于广泛的增强式训练，我们正在研究轻快的节奏运动。 从理论上
讲，跳绳之类的事情是个好主意。 也就是说，直到您意识到根本不存

功能等距是激发运动员意图的神奇工具。我们有两类：克服和屈服。
克服是一种远离重力的同心动作。 屈服是一种离心行为，也远离重力
。 即使没有设备，如果您允许的话，等轴测图也会变得非常麻烦。保
持简单，理解任务，并专注于会议的目标。 克服等距是驱动某些事物
意图的好方法，这可能有益于加速或同心力活动等。屈服等距是产生长

冗长的解释所困扰的情况下获得价值。

辐射和对中技术是在关节内产生压缩，并结合肌肉组织的收缩以保持
稳定性。无论如何，我们都需要证明在运动过程中对胸部和骨盆的控制
。我们希望我们的腿成为力量的发生器，我们的手臂成为力量的供应者
。在这之间，我们想要控制能量从远端到近端的传输，然后再到远端的
传输。 Centration（或称关节收缩）是一种在运动过程中控制胸部和骨
盆的强大技术。包扎更适合稳定的关节，例如腰椎，可以

make an incredible difference in output. Irradiation, or the intentional
contraction of static muscular groups during movements, is another strategy
for exhibiting control during locomotion. We can use external tools, such as
holding onto an implement while we are moving dynamically in the opposite
quadrant (lower or upper). We can focus on internal strategies of bracing and
contracting our legs versus our arms or our arms versus our legs.

Tolerance
The bottom line of the entire movement prep period is to prepare for the goal
and the tasks we have on that given day. A large part of that is reducing the
risk associated with doing the tasks that are designed to reach the goal. We
have covered a lot on movement prep already, but the truth is that the only
thing that matters is whether we are prepared to do what is being asked of us
and reduce associated risk as much as possible.
A large part of that is circulation and blood flow. We are essentially just
water bags moving through space. Contractile tissue (muscle and fascia)
moves noncontractile tissue (connective tissue and bone), and fluids circulate
through the body. Fluid creates momentum, and we are responsible for
controlling that fluid as much as we are responsible for controlling our arms
and legs. Blood is one of those fluids, and if we have adequate circulation, we
have increased delivery of energy in the form of glucose, ATP, and
eventually heat.
Movement is based on the conversion of energy into heat. We generate
heat when we move. The more we move, the more heat we generate. The
tissues that are most susceptible to trauma are the ones that are not adequately
prepared for proper temperature increase. The highest amount of energy
expenditure will occur during the training session. We want to gradually
increase heat through increased energy expenditure closest to the training
session. This increases performance and lowers the risk associated with high
energy expenditure.
This means that our movement needs to be faster and go longer. We need
to increase the amplitude of the movements we have been doing during the
movement prep. We need to increase the duration or the distance to expend
more energy. We do this by progressing to more direct practice of the drills

使输出产生令人难以置信的差异。 Irradiation，或运动过程中静态肌肉
群的有意收缩，是在运动过程中表现出控制力的另一种策略。 我们可
以使用外部工具，例如在相反象限（下或上）动态移动时握住工具。我
们可以专注于支撑和收缩我们的腿与手臂或手臂与腿的内部策略。

宽容
整个运动准备期的底线是为当天的目标和任务做好准备。其中很大一部
分是降低与执行旨在实现目标的任务相关的风险。 我们已经介绍了很
多关于运动准备的内容，但事实是，唯一重要的是我们是否准备好按照
要求去做并尽可能降低相关风险。
其中很大一部分是循环和血液流动。 我们本质上只是在太空中移动
的水袋。 收缩组织（肌肉和筋膜）移动非收缩组织（结缔组织和骨骼
），并且液体在体内循环。 流体产生动量，我们有责任控制流体，就
像我们有责任控制我们的手臂和腿一样。血液就是其中一种液体，如果
我们有足够的循环，我们就会以葡萄糖、ATP 和最终热量的形式增加能
量的输送。
运动基于能量转化为热能。 当我们移动时，我们会产生热量。 我们
移动得越多，产生的热量就越多。 最容易受到创伤的组织是那些没有
为适当的温度升高做好充分准备的组织。 最高的能量消耗将出现在训
练期间。 我们希望通过增加最接近训练时的能量消耗来逐渐增加热量
。这可以提高性能并降低与高能量消耗相关的风险。

这意味着我们的运动需要更快、走得更远。我们需要增加我们在运动
准备期间所做的运动的幅度。 我们需要增加持续时间或距离来消耗更
多的能量。 我们通过更直接的练习来做到这一点

we will be doing within the session. We are doing these drills in a
submaximal environment but faster or harder than the preceding drills and
exercises we have been doing. Since we are not doing them as fast or as
heavily, we will need to do them over a longer duration or distance to build
the prerequisite temperature and blood flow before going to the maximal
threshold.
Rehearsal is classified as warm-up sets. We have laid the foundation for
tissue quality, flexibility, mobility, control, sequence, potentiation, and
increased temperature and blood flow. We now have to transition to the
primary task. This applies to everything we do with training, both inside and
outside. If we are sprinting, we will need to do buildup runs. If we are
changing direction, we will need to build up deceleration reps. If we are
lifting, we will need warm-up sets. We need to rehearse the action in a lowerthreshold environment before doing the action in a higher-threshold
environment.
Rehearsal means practice. Practice means we have an opportunity to coach
and give feedback. The chances of changing something at full speed during
the rep are a lot less than at submaximal speed during the rep. If someone is
running at 50% of their speed, cueing front-side or backside mechanics can
make a difference. You will lose that ability during the actual session when
the stakes are higher. If you want to change a technical component, you will
have a much greater opportunity to do so during the movement prep (figure
17.4).
The last consideration on movement prep is whether we need to have a
high-energy start or a review of the session. Honestly, it is up to you. My
advice is that the shorter your team’s attention span, the faster or more
enthusiastic the start to your session. For professional athletes, athletes
preparing for a combine, or individual sports athletes, you will want to give a
breakdown. It comes down to their intrinsic motivation. You have to work
with your athletes. Team sports are not devoid of intrinsic motivation; they
are just much more of a group dynamic. You can empathize with the fact that
being part of a team is about managing a group and the variance in
motivation. People who are being paid or isolated in the competition have a
more direct responsibility for their development.

我们将在会议期间进行。 我们在次最大环境中进行这些训练，但比我
们之前所做的训练和练习更快或更难。 由于我们没有那么快或那么剧
烈地进行这些运动，因此我们需要在更长的时间内或更长的距离上进行
这些运动，以在达到最大阈值之前建立必要的温度和血流量。
排练被归类为热身活动。 我们为组织质量、灵活性、移动性、控制
、顺序、增强以及增加温度和血流量奠定了基础。 我们现在必须过渡
到主要任务。这适用于我们在训练中所做的一切，无论是内部还是外部
。 如果我们进行短跑，我们需要进行积累跑。 如果我们要改变方向，
我们将需要建立减速次数。 如果我们举重，我们需要热身组。我们需
要先在较低阈值的环境中排练该动作，然后再在较高阈值的环境中执行
该动作。
排练意味着练习。实践意味着我们有机会进行指导和提供反馈。 在
代表期间全速改变某些东西的机会比在代表期间以次最大速度改变东西
的机会要少得多。如果某人以 50% 的速度跑步，提示前侧或后侧机制
可能会产生影响。 当赌注更高时，您将在实际会话中失去这种能力。
如果您想更改技术组件，在运动准备期间您将有更大的机会这样做（图
17.4）。
关于动作准备的最后一个考虑因素是我们是否需要有一个高能量的开
始或对训练进行回顾。 老实说，这取决于你。 我的建议是，你的团队
的注意力持续时间越短，你的会议开始得越快或越热情。 对于职业运
动员、准备联合训练的运动员或个人运动员，您需要提供详细信息。
这取决于他们的内在动机。 你必须与你的运动员一起工作。 团队运动
并不缺乏内在动力； 他们只是更具团队活力。您可以理解这样一个事
实：成为团队的一员就是管理一个团队以及动机的差异。 在竞争中获
得报酬或孤立的人对自己的发展负有更直接的责任。

Refer to the goal of the session and the environment to determine what
you think is the best starting point. If the goal is to have 100 football players
running with technical precision and great effort, your biggest limiting factor
is not information but momentum. A fast start with energy and enthusiasm is
a fantastic tool in that situation. If you have a professional group of track
athletes who represent a country, they understand their relative roles. A 100
m sprinter and a shot-putter know they have to give great effort because they
will be competing in front of millions of people with the potential to make
generational wealth in the not-too-distant future. Clapping it up and running
out to stations is not necessary.

Training Session
The movement prep’s purpose is to prepare for the training session. This is
important because if the movement prep does not have a connection to the
training session, you have effectively wasted your time. This then makes it
important to reinforce the goal, the prospective challenge, the needed focus,
and the feedback you will need to give.
The training session is composed of key components. If we can learn to
leverage those components, we can create high-level training sessions. The
components of an effective training session include selecting exercises and
the variables we use for those exercises. Exercise selection is the foundation
of facilitating biomechanical aspects of training. The variables are how we
facilitate the biomotor and bioenergetic aspects of training. The interplay of
the exercises we select and the volume, intensity, and rest are means of
making tangible changes with athletes.
Remember, the training session is only as good as the quality of the reps
we have, the sets we finish, and the exercises we complete with rep and set
integrity. We need to remind ourselves to complete each rep with the
prescribed TUT (time under tension), the prescribed ROM, the prescribed
position, and a threshold load or velocity. Each rep needs to be executed
based on the accomplishment of defined criteria. We then apply that pattern
to the entire set.
Each set needs to have a target rep bracket, a total TUT, and a target
external load or velocity. Accomplishing each rep in a set within the targeted
rep bracket determines the success of the set and also means you reached the
total TUT for the set. The last piece is using an external load or targeted
velocity that we can maintain for the entire set. We want this for each
exercise within a training session.
The last point is that both rep and set integrity for every exercise are
critical for each training session. Structural balance is the foundation of
reducing the rate of injuries during competition. The prioritization of one
exercise over another based on exercise order or point of emphasis can lead

FIGURE 17.4 Movement prep.

培训课程
动作准备的目的是为训练课程做准备。 这很重要，因为如果运动准备
与训练没有联系，那么你实际上是在浪费时间。 因此，强化目标、未
来的挑战、所需的重点以及您需要提供的反馈就变得很重要。
培训课程由关键部分组成。 如果我们能够学会利用这些组件，我们
就可以创建高水平的培训课程。 有效的培训课程的组成部分包括选择
练习以及我们用于这些练习的变量。运动选择是促进生物力学方面训练
的基础。 这些变量是我们如何促进训练的生物运动和生物能量方面。
我们选择的练习以及训练量、强度和休息的相互作用是为运动员带来切
实改变的手段。
请记住，训练课程的好坏取决于我们的次数质量、完成的组数以及我
们以重复次数和组数完整性完成的练习。 我们需要提醒自己按照规定
的 TUT（紧张时间）、规定的 ROM、规定的位置以及阈值负荷或速度
完成每次重复。 每个代表都需要根据定义的标准的完成情况来执行。
然后我们将该模式应用到整个集合。
每组都需要有一个目标次数范围、总 TUT 以及目标外部负载或速度
。在目标代表范围内完成一组中的每个代表决定了该组的成功，也意味
着您达到了该组的总 TUT。 最后一部分是使用外部负载或目标速度，
我们可以在整个组中维持它。 我们希望训练课程中的每项练习都如此
。
最后一点是，每次练习的重复次数和设定完整性对于每次训练都至关
重要。 结构平衡是降低比赛受伤率的基础。 根据练习顺序或重点，将
一项练习优先于另一项练习可能会导致

to muscular imbalances. Having equal stress applied to antagonist muscle
groups or motor patterns is the simplest means of reducing injuries. Having
each exercise executed with both rep and set integrity becomes the central
piece of bringing value as a strength coach.
“Amateurs talk about tactics, but professionals
study logistics.”
—General Robert H. Barrow, United States Marine
Corps
It is worth mentioning that a poorly written program executed well will
outperform a well-written program executed poorly. Good coaches think
about logistics as much as tactics. Having a plan of attack for how we will
execute our well-thought-out program is foundational to overall performance.
Placing our coaches and athletes in a particular spot to execute the aspects of
the program being asked of them is easily the most important factor in
working in a large group. Having the right tools, the correct amount of
knowledge, and the requisite motivation to do a job makes a coach effective
and able to benefit larger numbers of athletes at a given time.

Exercise Selection and Order
A common line you will hear is, there is no such thing as a bad exercise;
there is only poor execution. That is a nice thought, but there are bad
exercises based on the context in which a good exercise was placed. We have
the burden of knowledge when we screen and appraise; we cannot rely on
anecdotes from other strength coaches. We are governed by principles and
rules. The standard has increased.
Modifications
If it hurts, don’t do it. It’s pretty simple logic. Before we explore what that
means, we need to understand the concept of pain. Pain is a relative feeling.
One person’s pain is another’s pleasure. Pain experienced from the novelty of
a stimulus in the form of targeted stress is real. Pain experienced from an

导致肌肉失衡。 对拮抗肌群或运动模式施加相同的压力是减少伤害的
最简单方法。 作为力量教练，以重复次数和组数完整性执行每项练习
成为带来价值的核心部分。

“业余者讲战术，专业者研究后勤。”
——罗伯特·H·巴罗将军，美国海军陆战队

值得一提的是，编写得不好但执行得好的程序会比编写得好的执行得
不好的程序表现更好。 优秀的教练不仅会考虑战术，还会考虑后勤保
障。 制定一个关于如何执行深思熟虑的计划的攻击计划是整体绩效的
基础。将我们的教练和运动员安排在特定的位置来执行要求他们完成的
计划的各个方面，这无疑是在大团队中工作的最重要因素。 拥有正确
的工具、正确的知识以及完成工作所需的动力可以使教练变得高效并能
够在特定时间使更多的运动员受益。

练习选择和顺序
你会听到的一句常见说法是，没有什么是糟糕的锻炼；只有锻炼才是最
好的。只是执行力很差。 这是一个很好的想法，但是根据好的练习的
背景，也有一些不好的练习。我们在筛选、评价时有知识的负担； 我
们不能依赖其他力量教练的轶事。 我们受原则和规则约束。标准提高
了。
Modifications
如果很痛，就不要这样做。 这是非常简单的逻辑。 在我们探讨这意味
着什么之前，我们需要了解疼痛的概念。疼痛是一种相对的感觉。一个
人的痛苦就是另一个人的快乐。以有针对性的压力形式出现的新奇刺激
所带来的疼痛是真实存在的。 经历过的疼痛

injury and attempting to execute a movement that exaggerates that pain is
also real. Being able to dissociate between the two is foundational to exercise
selection.
Do not guess when it comes to pain. Use your screen. If someone has an
orthopedic issue, such as a break or fracture, the obvious answer is to avoid
directly loading that injury. We are not medical doctors and cannot use
Wolff’s law, which refers to the application of stress to create an adaptive
response in built-up tissue that aims to heal the injury. We cannot diagnose or
prescribe a treatment. We can, however, work around injuries without further
damage.
Here, the principle of progression returns. Progression is an
omnidirectional concept. We can go forward to more direct stress and
progression. We can go backward with less direct stress and regression.
Finally, we can go laterally and apply the same stress with a different
exercise and lateralization. We want to train patterns that stress muscles and
connective tissue within a specific plane or vector, or both, to reach a certain
outcome. Understanding the intent of that exercise will allow us to progress,
regress, or lateralize.
Pain is your guide here. Standard operating procedures for dealing with
pain to have a unified response are the key aspect behind working within a
group. We lose the luxury of making organic decisions when we expand the
size of the group and the number of coaches. The vector of the exercise
becomes an if this, then that, based system. We want to rehearse this with the
staff and explain to the athletes why it is necessary to safeguard the intent of
the exercise toward the goals (figure 17.5).
Variations
Most of the exercises will be broken down into four primary patterns: squat,
hinge, push, and pull. We have variations within each exercise of bilateral or
unilateral for squat or hinge and vertical or horizontal for push or pull. We
further break down our patterns and their constraints into multiple planes of
motion, vectors, types of loading, and positions of loading.
The more constraints we place on that exercise, the more we can
exaggerate things like external load or velocity. For example, a squat pattern
in a fixed plane of motion, such as a leg press, will have a higher external

当谈到疼痛时，不要猜测。 使用你的屏幕。 如果某人有骨科问题，
例如骨折或骨折，显而易见的答案是避免直接承受伤害。 我们不是医

我们可以在不造成进一步损害的情况下解决伤害问题。
在这里，渐进原则又回来了。 进步是一个全方位的概念。 我们可以
继续承受更直接的压力和进步。 我们可以以更少的直接压力和回归来

疼痛是你的向导。 处理疼痛并做出统一反应的标准操作程序是团队

做出有机决策的奢侈。 练习的向量变成了一个基于“如果这样，那么
那样”的系统。我们希望与工作人员一起排练并向运动员解释为什么有

We need to select an exercise that corresponds to the goal. Certain
exercises are more conducive to a specific quality, such as power, relative

general rule, the more focus on the specific quality, the more constrained the
exercise needs to be. Conversely, the more general the focus, the less

Combining these patterns can make this even more complicated. We can
combine certain movements, such as a squat and a press or a hinge and a pull.
This can be further broken down into planes, vectors, loading, and load
placement. For the sake of simplicity, we consider these isolated exercises
within a program and do not generally count them toward structural balance,
with balancing pushing and pulling. However, if you substitute a total body
exercise for a direct pattern-based exercise, you need to account for the
differential in potential load. For instance, if we are counting a squat to a
press as the squat exercise in that training session and we have a targeted
hinge pattern, there will be a differential loading between the musculature
and connective tissue in the anterior and posterior aspects of the legs. We will
need to account for that in another workout or substitute the total body
exercise with a more directly loadable exercise. Or we can replace the more
loadable exercises with less loadable exercises, such as unilateral variations.
The next piece, outside of direct patterns, is functional isolated joint
exercises, primarily focusing on knee flexion and hip extension. The
distinction between primary patterns that are more compound in nature and
use multiple joints while still targeting a specific joint is important to note.
With a squatting pattern, we primarily target the quadriceps through the knee
joint. With a hinge pattern, we primarily target the hamstring group through
the hip joint. When we have isolated joint exercises, like a glute-ham raise or

组合这些模式会使事情变得更加复杂。 我们可以将某些动作结合起

量、载荷和载荷放置。 为了简单起见，我们在一个程序中考虑这些孤

下一部分是直接模式之外的功能性孤立关节练习，主要侧重于膝关节
弯曲和髋关节伸展。 需要注意的是，本质上更复合的主要模式和使用
多个关节但仍针对特定关节的主要模式之间的区别很重要。在深蹲模式
中，我们主要通过膝关节来瞄准股四头肌。 通过铰链模式，我们主要
通过髋关节瞄准腿筋群。当我们进行孤立的关节练习时，例如臀腿抬高
或

hip bridge, we still target the same muscle group as a hinge joint, but through
an isolated joint movement pattern. There are layers to this that we need to
understand.
We can focus on our four primary patterns, but that would leave structural
imbalances over time, specifically in the hips and knees. We have biarticular
and monoarticular muscle groups. Monoarticular muscle groups and
biarticular muscle groups have different functions during compound lifts. The
hamstring group is a particularly interesting muscle group from the
perspective that its primary function is to decelerate knee extension by being
a flexor of the knee and an extensor of the hip. The biarticular muscle groups
act as a stabilizer as much as a primary mover. This causes problems if we do
not target them as primary movers. Another aspect is that the body tends to
lay down sarcomeres in a localized area if we do not have both distal and
proximal loading of joints. We can further break down hinge patterns into
isolated actions, such as knee dominant and hip dominant, that target all
muscle actions and sections of the muscle group.
The second component of choosing exercises from our movement screen
is the ROM we have. If you think about it, we cannot have a movement
pattern that requires a certain degree of freedom if we do not have the
prerequisite ROM we found on our screen. ROM is a one-way street; we may
not have the pattern if we have the ROM, but we do not have the pattern if
we do not have the ROM. We need to select exercises based on the potential
we can gain from them.
How and where we load the movement make huge differences in the
potential ROM we can get. Using anterior loading will allow for better
organization of the thorax and pelvis during a squatting pattern. We can see a
similar effect by changing the stance using a slant board. Elevating the heels
also leads to better organization of the thorax and pelvis during a squat,
leading to increased ROM.
The idea is to start with the exercise standard we established before the
onset of the exercise regarding ROM and position. Then we select the stance,
the position of the load, and how we load to facilitate that standard. You have
to select exercises that each athlete can be successful with based on the setup
we work with. A good coach can correct, modify, and cue an athlete to reach

我们可以专注于我们的四种主要模式，但这会随着时间的推移而导致

是，如果我们没有关节的远端和近端负载，身体往往会在局部区域放置
肌节。 我们可以进一步将铰链模式分解为单独的动作，例如膝关节主
导和髋关节主导，这些动作针对所有肌肉动作和肌群的各个部分。

从运动屏幕中选择练习的第二个组成部分是我们拥有的 ROM。 如果
你想一想，如果我们没有在屏幕上找到的必备 ROM，我们就无法拥有
需要一定自由度的运动模式。 ROM是一条单行道；有ROM就可能没有
图案，但是没有ROM就没有图案。我们需要根据我们可以从中获得的潜
力来选择练习。
我们加载机芯的方式和位置会对我们可以获得的潜在 ROM 产生巨大
的影响。 使用前路负重可以在蹲姿过程中更好地组织胸部和骨盆。通
过使用斜板改变姿势，我们可以看到类似的效果。在深蹲过程中，抬高
脚后跟还可以更好地组织胸部和骨盆，从而增加活动范围。
这个想法是从我们在练习开始之前建立的关于活动范围和位置的练习
标准开始。然后我们选择姿势、负重位置以及负重方式来促进该标准。
您必须根据我们使用的设置来选择每个运动员都能成功的练习。一个好
的教练可以纠正、修改和提示运动员达到目标

the standard. But that is not feasible at scale. A better approach is to rely on
the rules we created to select exercises that facilitate success with the largest
possible value overall.
The last layer of exercise selection is exercise order. I will keep this one
brief. Do not overthink this; whatever exercise simultaneously has the most
value and risk needs to be placed first. There is no need to get fancy here; we
have to prioritize higher-value movements earlier in the workout because that
is our best chance to get a return on the investment of time. We also have to
prioritize the exercise with the most inherent risk, which, ironically, has the
most value, earlier in the workout. The premise is the same; we have more
available energy and focus to leverage an exercise’s potential earlier in the
workout.
We will discuss this more with microcycle design, but we need to discuss
pairing certain exercises as antagonist exercises. Antagonist pairings can
come as lower + lower-upper + upper or lower + upper-upper + lower. Same
quadrant pairings, such as lower + lower, will have a profound impact on
exercise selection. A general dynamic will be at play with large systemic
loads. We are loading two large muscle groups with a high capacity for
external load, such as a squat and deadlift, being paired together. The solution
is to pair one with a high external load capacity with one with a lower
external load capacity. We should prioritize the one with the higher external
load first.
With lower + upper pairings, the biggest consideration is equipment and
use of the rack. For instance, if you have half racks, it will be difficult to pair
a barbell-loaded squat pattern with a vertical pulling exercise using the pullup bar. The proximity of equipment has a considerable impact on the
potential density you are trying to accomplish. Pairing a movement at the
rack with an exercise far away from the rack can aid with adding rest or slow
the training session to a fault (figure 17.7).

标准。但这在规模上是不可行的。更好的方法是依靠我们创建的规则来
选择有助于成功并获得最大可能整体价值的练习。
练习选择的最后一层是练习顺序。 我将简要介绍这一点。 不要想太
多； 任何同时具有最大价值和风险的活动都需要放在首位。这里没有
必要花哨；我们必须在锻炼的早期优先考虑更高价值的动作，因为这是
我们获得时间投资回报的最佳机会。我们还必须优先考虑具有最大固有
风险的锻炼，具有讽刺意味的是，在锻炼的早期，这种锻炼具有最大的
价值。 前提是一样的； 我们有更多的可用能量和注意力，可以在锻炼
的早期发挥锻炼的潜力。
我们将通过微循环设计对此进行更多讨论，但我们需要讨论将某些练
习与拮抗练习配对。 拮抗剂配对可以是下+下上+上或下+上上+下。相
同象限配对，例如较低的+较低，将对运动选择产生深远的影响。 总体
动态将在巨大的系统负载下发挥作用。 我们正在对两个具有高外部负
荷能力的大肌肉群进行负荷，例如深蹲和硬拉，并配对在一起。解决方
案是将具有高外部负载能力的一台与具有较低外部负载能力的一台配对
。 我们应该优先考虑外部负载较高的。

对于较低的+上部配对，最大的考虑因素是机架的设备和使用。例如
，如果您有半架，则很难将杠铃负重深蹲模式与使用引体向上杆的垂直
拉动练习配对。 设备的接近程度对您想要达到的潜在密度有相当大的
影响。 将架子上的动作与远离架子的练习配对可以帮助增加休息或减
慢训练进度（图 17.7）。

Variables
The variables we use in training are under the pretense of what quality they
represent. A certain number of reps or TUT is a meaningless number unless it
corresponds to a certain quality we are trying to develop. The same can be
said for intensity and rest. The question of how much, how long, how heavy,
or how frequently we do something within a training session completely
depends on what we are trying to accomplish.
The qualities we are trying to develop are the foundation for selecting any
combination of reps, TUT, sets, intensity, and rest (figure 17.8). Reaching a
goal is based on how well we organize these training qualities, combined
with how well we execute each variable that coincides with that quality. We
can work forward or backward with progressions of training qualities. We
can address weaknesses early with training qualities. We can reverse engineer
from a peak with training qualities. The point is that once we establish what
quality we are going to focus on and then organize our training variables to

图 17.7 练习顺序 101。

变量
我们在训练中使用的变量是假装它们代表什么质量。一定数量的重复次
数或 TUT 是毫无意义的数字，除非它对应于我们试图培养的某种质量
。 对于强度和休息也可以这样说。我们在训练中做某件事的量、时间
、重量或频率完全取决于我们想要完成的目标。
我们试图培养的品质是选择次数、TUT、组数、强度和休息的任意组
合的基础（图 17.8）。 目标的实现取决于我们组织这些培训质量的程
度，以及我们执行与该质量相符的每个变量的程度。我们可以随着训练
质量的进步向前或向后努力。 我们可以通过培训质量尽早解决弱点。
我们可以通过训练质量从巅峰进行逆向工程。关键是，一旦我们确定了
我们要关注的质量，然后组织我们的训练变量

best leverage that quality, we are developing.
Volume
Another factor with all variables is that they are inversely proportional. Sets
and reps work in tandem but with an inverse relationship. If sets are high,
reps are low. If sets are low, reps are high. Time under tension and rest are
inversely proportional. If TUT is long, the rest is short. If TUT is short, the
rest is long. Reps and intensity are also inversely proportional. If reps are
high, the intensity is low. If reps are low, the intensity is high.

FIGURE 17.8 Training qualities.
To say it another way, anything with a low rep number and low TUT will
have a large number of sets, high intensity, and long rest. What a low rep and
high intensity represent is global and nervous system-based fatigue, which is
more taxing and requires a short total TUT per set. Since we have fewer reps
and shorter TUT per set, we will need more sets to accrue the necessary
amount of stress for adaptation. With the greater impact on the nervous
system, we will need more rest to recover. The general idea is that we will
need a different approach with more nervous system qualities than muscular
system qualities.

最好地利用这种品质，我们正在发展。
Volume
所有变量的另一个因素是它们成反比。 组数和次数是协同工作的，但
呈反比关系。 如果组数较高，则重复次数较低。 如果组数少，次数就
高。 紧张的时间和休息的时间成反比。 如果 TUT 较长，则其余部分
较短。 如果 TUT 短，则其余部分长。 次数和强度也成反比。 如果重
复次数较高，则强度较低。如果重复次数较低，则强度较高。

图 17.8 培训质量。
换句话说，任何低重复次数和低 TUT 的动作都会有大量的组数、高
强度和长时间的休息。低次数和高强度代表的是全身性和基于神经系统
的疲劳，这更费力，并且每组需要较短的总 TUT。由于我们每组的次数
较少且 TUT 较短，因此我们需要更多组数来积累适应所需的压力。 由
于对神经系统的影响更大，我们需要更多的休息来恢复。 总的想法是
，我们需要一种不同的方法，神经系统质量多于肌肉系统质量。

Power and relative strength have more neural qualities. This approach uses
shorter TUT per set, fewer reps per set, more sets per exercise, higher
intensity per set, and longer rest between sets. Most of the changes we are
looking for will be centered on how we increase voluntary muscular
contractions via the nervous system over the direct contribution of more
contractile units of the muscle, increasing the rate and amount of impulses
coming from the central nervous system to the motor unit, and synchronizing
and coordinating the motor units to express more force, a faster rate, or a
combination of more force at a faster rate.
Functional hypertrophy and hypertrophy will occur within the
musculature. This approach uses longer TUT per set, more reps per set, fewer
sets per exercise, lower intensity per set, and shorter rest between sets. Most
of the change here is to increase the number of contractile units within the
muscle, both cross-sectionally and longitudinally. We want to break down
existing muscle fibers to regenerate and build more sarcomeres within the
muscle cell. Functional hypertrophy will use a higher intensity and create
more muscular damage. Another mechanism is to create metabolic stress that
leads to cellular swelling and initiates a healing process, which creates more
sarcomeres. Hypertrophy will use longer TUT, more reps, or shorter rest and
create more metabolic stress to create more sarcomeres.
Muscular endurance is an often overlooked aspect of training in the team
setting. We neglect this due to the time constraints and limited options with a
large group. Having extended TUT can lead to a lot of time with insignificant
TUT. Having a lot of reps can lead to a lot of poor reps. Having a minimal
number of sets limits the potential for motor learning due to a lack of
debriefing and correction between sets. Or it could be completely the
opposite if it is needed and we have equipment such as machines or
stationary cardiorespiratory pieces to facilitate longer bouts of continuous
work. Muscular endurance is necessary, and it comes with risk in both time
and execution, but it is a necessary aspect of organizing training qualities.
Once we have a goal, the quality we work on, and the underlying
mechanism that creates adaptation, we can layer in whatever variables make
sense. Often, we select the sets and reps before we even know the quality we
want to work with. There is also the element of exercise selection and

肌肉耐力是团队训练中经常被忽视的一个方面。由于时间限制和一大
群人的选择有限，我们忽略了这一点。延长 TUT 可能会导致大量 TUT
时间微不足道。 重复次数太多可能会导致重复次数很多。 由于缺乏组
间汇报和纠正，最少组数限制了运动学习的潜力。 或者，如果需要的
话，情况也可能完全相反，我们有机器或固定心肺呼吸器等设备来促进
更长时间的连续工作。 肌肉耐力是必要的，它在时间和执行上都存在
风险，但它是组织训练质量的必要方面。

一旦我们有了目标、我们努力的质量以及创造适应的潜在机制，我们
就可以分层添加任何有意义的变量。通常，我们在知道我们想要的质量
之前就选择了组数和次数。 还有运动选择的因素

exercise order. Highly constrained compound lifts will have a higher
potential for external load, which could be more congruent with more neural
qualities, such as power or relative strength. Less constrained compound lifts
will have a lower potential for external load but will be challenged by
proprioception and balance. We may be better served by working with a more
moderate quality in terms of volume and intensity, such as functional
hypertrophy.
Reps are numbers, and numbers are symbols. Of all the variables, reps are
the most symbolic of what we are trying to accomplish in the training
session. A set of three will always be associated with power or relative
strength. A set of five will more than likely be associated with functional
hypertrophy. A set of 10 will more than likely be associated with
hypertrophy. The power of that symbol is important for understanding the
meaning behind the program for both the athlete and the coach.
The issue with this symbolism is that it may not be congruent with the
quality we are trying to develop. Time under tension represents the
connection between what we are doing and what we are trying to accomplish.
We can do a set of 10 with a 1/0/x/0 pattern that is 10 s, which would be
classified as either power or relative strength. The length of time, not the
amount of movement, is what creates a desired outcome. But that may run
directly opposite to the rep count we are trying to leverage.
A protocol you may want to use for functional hypertrophy might be three
reps with an 8/0/x/0 TUT. An 8 s rep for reps would be functional
hypertrophy but perceived as something different. An athlete may go too
heavy, overestimate a training load, and miss reps. There are ways to
navigate with this relative intensity, reps in reserve, a target rating of
perceived exertion, or a target bar velocity. The issue is that there are more
systems you have to put in place that your staff or your athletes may not be
ready for.
It is not immediately obvious to an athlete that when reps are low, the
weight is heavy, or when reps are high, the weight is light. It takes time and
effort to convey this as a strength coach. This is not a universal truth, but it is
important to build logic with your athletes. In a group setting, your athletes
will be responsible for grasping simple concepts. In the event a coach is

与更多的神经品质（例如力量或相对力量）更加一致。限制较少的复合
举升机承受外部负载的可能性较低，但会受到本体感觉和平衡的挑战。
在训练量和强度方面采取更适中的质量（例如功能性肥大）可能会更好
。
代表是数字，数字是符号。在所有变量中，次数是我们在训练中试图
实现的目标中最具象征意义的。 一组三个总是与权力或相对强度相关
。 一组五个很可能与功能性肥大有关。 一组 10 个很可能与肥大有关
。 该符号的力量对于运动员和教练理解该计划背后的意义非常重要。

这种象征意义的问题在于，它可能与我们试图发展的品质不一致。
紧张的时间代表了我们正在做的事情和我们想要完成的事情之间的联系
。我们可以用 1/0/x/0 模式（即 10 秒）做一组 10 次，这将被分类为功率
或相对强度。 创造期望结果的是时间的长度，而不是运动的量。 但这
可能与我们试图利用的代表数正好相反。
您可能想要用于功能性肥大的方案可能是 3 次，每次 8/0/x/0 TUT。
8 秒的重复次数可能是功能性肥大，但感觉却有所不同。 运动员可能会
举重过重、高估训练负荷并错过重复次数。 有多种方法可以根据相对
强度、储备次数、感知用力的目标等级或目标杆速度进行导航。 问题
是，您必须安装更多的系统，而您的员工或运动员可能还没有准备好。

对于运动员来说，当次数少时，重量就重，或者当次数多时，重量就
轻，这并不是立即显而易见的。作为力量教练需要花费时间和精力来传
达这一点。这不是普遍真理，但与运动员建立逻辑很重要。 在小组环
境中，您的运动员将负责掌握简单的概念。 如果教练是

working with a large group of athletes, the best chance of success lies in the
athletes who can make logical decisions with their training. Keeping rep
schemes the focus, more so than the TUT, is a strategy we will need to
employ.
Time under tension is still important, just due to a different pretense. The
time variants we use will need to work within individual pieces. It is better to
break down the individual aspects of TUT to better understand contraction
types. We are stronger eccentrically than we are concentrically, and we are
stronger isometrically than we are concentrically, which is not immediately
obvious to athletes. We can establish how to teach that through structured
TUT.
An athlete will be stronger eccentrically and isometrically than they are
concentrically. We are governed by what we can do concentrically. This
means that the weight an athlete can lift during an exercise is based on what
they can do concentrically. When we tell an athlete to select a weight for a
particular rep number, their concentric strength is the determining factor. The
issue is that there is a huge reserve of strength and ability eccentrically and
isometrically that exceeds the weight we choose. We are trying to
supercompensate collectively among the group, and we are using consistently
submaximal external loads.
If anyone has ever tried to overload eccentrics with weight release hooks,
they can attest that it is difficult to execute. It is a tool that can bring a lot of
value, but it brings some logistic issues. I say this because we have to
consider that overloading eccentrically, relative to concentrically, is not the
easiest thing to execute. With that said, we have a variable we can leverage
with eccentric or isometric contractions: time.
We can view time through a similar lens as a rep: The more reps, or time,
we have, the greater the stress. By focusing the stress in the form of time on
the stronger contraction types, eccentric and isometric, we essentially
overload the stronger contractions. The message to athletes is we are stronger
eccentrically and isometrically, so we will spend more time during an
individual rep where we are stronger. Each rep, therefore, should have a
longer period in either the eccentric or isometric contraction to create
appropriate adaptive stress.

与一大群运动员一起工作，成功的最佳机会在于那些能够在训练中做出
逻辑决定的运动员。 保持代表计划比 TUT 更重要，是我们需要采用的
策略。
紧张的时间仍然很重要，只是由于不同的借口。我们使用的时间变量
需要在各个片段中工作。最好分解 TUT 的各个方面，以便更好地了解
收缩类型。 我们的离心力比同心力更强，而等长力比同心力更强，这
对运动员来说并不是立即显而易见的。 我们可以通过结构化 TUT 确定
如何教授这一点。
运动员的离心力和等长力会比同心力更强。 我们受制于我们能够同
心协力做的事情。 这意味着运动员在锻炼过程中可以举起的重量取决
于他们可以同心做的事情。 当我们告诉运动员为特定次数选择重量时
，他们的同心力量是决定因素。问题是，在离心和等距方面有巨大的力
量和能力储备，超出了我们选择的重量。 我们正在尝试在团队中集体
进行超级补偿，并且我们始终使用次最大外部负载。

如果有人尝试过用重量释放钩使偏心轮超载，他们可以证明这很难执
行。它是一个可以带来很多价值的工具，但它也带来了一些后勤问题。
我这样说是因为我们必须考虑到，相对于同心重载，偏心重载并不是最
容易执行的事情。 话虽如此，我们有一个可以利用偏心或等长收缩的
变量：时间。
我们可以通过与代表类似的视角来看待时间：代表次数或时间越多，
压力就越大。通过将时间形式的压力集中在较强的收缩类型（偏心和等
长）上，我们基本上使较强的收缩超载。向运动员传达的信息是，我们
在离心力和等长力方面都更强，因此我们会在个人训练中花更多的时间
来增强我们的力量。 因此，每次重复应该有更长的离心或等长收缩时
间，以产生适当的适应性压力。

Sets, as we discussed, have an inverse relationship with either TUT or
reps. More sets with fewer reps or shorter TUT have a significant impact on
the training session. We have, on average, 20 sets within a 1 h workout. For
neural focus, that number will drop to 16 total sets. For muscular focus, that
number will jump to 24 total sets. If we are doing four primary patterns,
possibly a total body pattern, we have to divide the 16 to 24 range by four to
five. If we are doing a lower number of reps with less TUT, we are going to
do more sets. That will eat into the time spent on each pattern.
This is significant because we can inadvertently distribute stress unevenly.
Uneven stress will lead to structural imbalance. Doing 6 to 10 sets on one
exercise in a workout where we are only doing 16 to 20 sets creates a
disproportionate amount of stress on a certain pattern, certain connective
tissue, and certain muscular tissue. A particular pattern may be more relevant
to a sport or an event. Although this can be the case, you risk injury or issues
associated with reciprocal inhibition.
The easiest means to address this is the rotation of the pattern that is taking
place with a larger number of sets. The frequency will have an impact on this.
In a 4-day program, it is easy to evenly align the four primary patterns. Two
and three days are trickier. It could mean sacrificing a movement pattern that
can be trained more in other periods, like during the season. It may mean
cutting exercises on a given workout to focus on two primary patterns.
Regardless of the split, we will need to rotate the first exercise in a training
session, which is where we allocate most of our focus and time.
Intensity
Intensity is the final intraset variable to review. The most important aspect of
intensity is reaching the threshold during a set. What becomes lost is the
distinction between intent and threshold intensity. Threshold intensity
happens when the set is reaching its completion. The final few reps we have
within a set are considered threshold intensities. If we were going to do a rep
max at 80%, the final two reps, or 4 s, would be the threshold reps, or TUT.
These reps are where adaptation occurs (figure 17.9).
The primary issue is that the reps that precede the threshold still have
value from a bioenergetic perspective, but more importantly, from an intent
perspective. What is easily misunderstood is how to do subthreshold reps and

正如我们所讨论的，组数与 TUT 或次数呈反比关系。更少次数的更
多组数或更短的 TUT 对训练课程有重大影响。我们平均 1 小时锻炼 20
组。对于神经焦点，这个数字将下降到 16 组。对于肌肉集中训练，这
个数字将跃升至 24 组。 如果我们正在做四种主要模式，可能是全身模
式，我们必须将 16 到 24 的范围除以 4 到 5。如果我们用更少的 TUT 做
更少的次数，我们就会做更多的组数。这将消耗在每个模式上花费的时
间。
这很重要，因为我们可能会无意中不均匀地分配压力。压力不均匀会
导致结构失衡。 在一次训练中，一项练习要做 6 到 10 组，而我们只做
16 到 20 组，这会对特定模式、特定结缔组织和特定肌肉组织产生不成
比例的压力。特定模式可能与运动或赛事更相关。尽管情况可能如此，
但您可能会受伤或出现与相互抑制相关的问题。
解决这个问题最简单的方法是轮换更多组数的模式。频率会对此产生
影响。在为期 4 天的计划中，很容易均匀地调整四种主要模式。两天和
三天比较棘手。这可能意味着牺牲一种可以在其他时期（例如赛季期间
）进行更多训练的运动模式。 这可能意味着在给定的锻炼中减少练习
，以专注于两种主要模式。无论如何划分，我们都需要在训练课程中轮
流进行第一个练习，这是我们分配大部分注意力和时间的地方。

Intensity
强度是要审查的最终组内变量。强度最重要的方面是在一组中达到阈值
。 失去的是意图和阈值强度之间的区别。 当该组即将完成时，就会出
现阈值强度。我们在一组中的最后几次代表被认为是阈值强度。如果我
们要以 80% 进行最大次数，最后两次或 4 秒将是阈值次数或 TUT。这
些代表是适应发生的地方（图 17.9）。
主要问题是，从生物能量的角度来看，阈值之前的代表仍然有价值，
但更重要的是，从意图的角度来看。容易被误解的是如何进行阈下次数
和

threshold reps. Under threshold intensity, the probability of success with that
threshold is predicated on rehearsed motor patterns that are hardwired. The
intent with which we do submaximal reps has tremendous carryover to
maximal reps.
This is where the value of TUT comes in within a team setting. The
simplest way to encourage intent is to prescribe x for concentric. Regardless
of the time spent within the eccentric or isometric portions of the lift, intent
should be the primary focus. Intent is most lost when we are intentional with
the concentric portion of the lift. Feeling the rep is best served at scale during
the eccentric and isometric portion, we slow down to understand and interpret
more of what is going on. Alternatively, unless we are trying to push through
the concentric position of the lift with violent intent, chances are we lose the
potential value.
Having velocity-based training to encourage intent is extremely valuable
in a group setting (figure 17.10). Getting objective feedback on how fast or
slow something was is valuable when you cannot give direct feedback on
every set for each athlete. As a coach, you have an assistant coach at each
rack for every barbell movement. The external load has a profound effect on
the rate of force development and potential tension. However, external load is
not a guarantee that the athlete will use high intent during the set, which is
why the coach is so valuable. Strength coaches are the conduits to the
execution of not just the weight on the bar, but the intent behind weighting
the bar.

阈值代表。在阈值强度下，达到该阈值的成功概率取决于预先排练的硬
连线运动模式。 我们做次最大次数的意图对最大次数有着巨大的影响
。
这就是 TUT 在团队环境中的价值所在。 鼓励意图的最简单方法是为
同心指定 x。 无论在升降机的偏心或等长部分花费的时间如何，意图都
应该是主要关注点。当我们有意识地使用升降机的同心部分时，意图是
最容易丧失的。感觉代表在偏心和等距部分得到最好的服务，我们放慢
速度来理解和解释更多正在发生的事情。或者，除非我们试图以暴力的
意图推动电梯的同心位置，否则我们很可能会失去潜在的价值。

在团体环境中进行基于速度的训练来鼓励意图非常有价值（图 17.10
）。 当您无法对每位运动员的每组动作提供直接反馈时，获得关于某
件事的快慢程度的客观反馈是很有价值的。 作为教练，每个杠铃架上
都有一名助理教练负责每个杠铃动作。外部载荷对力的发展速度和潜在
张力有深远的影响。然而，外部负荷并不能保证运动员在比赛中表现出
高度的意图，这就是教练如此有价值的原因。 力量教练不仅是执行杠
铃重量的渠道，也是执行杠铃重量背后意图的渠道。

FIGURE 17.9 Rep max threshold %.
The heavier and slower the concentric contraction is, the more mechanical
tension is required. We are still moving with absolute intent; we’re just using
contractile unit tissue to complete the concentric position. When we reach the
threshold reps or TUT, mechanical tension is created. Alternatively, when the
weight is lighter and therefore faster, it is more neuromuscular than
contractile. The momentum of fluids and reflex systems is more at play when
we are moving at a faster rate.
This is significant because we can tie the quality we are trying to develop
to the intensity, the velocity, and the rep or TUT number. We commit to
putting x as the concentric TUT and getting maximal intent on each rep. If it
is heavier, we will be slower and rely on more contractile tissue, which is
connected to hypertrophy or functional hypertrophy. We will have slow

重复最大阈值 %。

同心收缩越重、越慢，需要的机械张力就越大。我们仍然带着绝对的
意图前进；我们只是使用收缩单位组织来完成同心位置。当我们达到阈
值次数或 TUT 时，就会产生机械张力。或者，当重量较轻并因此速度
较快时，其神经肌肉作用大于收缩作用。当我们以更快的速度移动时，
液体和反射系统的动量会发挥更大的作用。
这很重要，因为我们可以将我们试图提高的质量与强度、速度和次数
或 TUT 数量联系起来。 我们致力于将 x 作为同心 TUT，并在每个代表
上获得最大的意图。如果它更重，我们就会变慢并依赖更多的收缩组织
，这与肥大或功能性肥大有关。 我们会有缓慢的

concentric contractions with relative strength, but the total TUT is less, so we
will not break down as many muscle fibers.
Prescribing intensity is a tactic you may want to employ in training a team.
Using the rep max chart (figure 4.5, page 59) is a good place to start. We
know that faster-twitch fiber athletes will be less capable at certain intensities
of hitting as many reps as slow-twitch athletes. We also know that the
recovery rate will differ for fast-twitch athletes and men than for slow-twitch
athletes or women (see figure 2.5, page 29). Using intensity can be tricky
within a group setting. A tactic is always to work submaximally to ensure
that you do not overshoot with athletes. Yes, you will run the risk of having
reps and, subsequently, sets that will not be stimulating enough for
adaptation. However, you will have better rep integrity from a manageable
external load, which will empower the athlete. You cannot go wrong
prioritizing rep integrity, but eventually, you will have to increase intensity to
create adequate stimulus.

You have a few tactics to employ: rep brackets, reps in reserve, and
velocity zones. Your choice is going to be based on what the lowest common

denominator in the room can understand. The youngest coach with the least
experience—can they explain a loading tactic better than another? The
freshman who has never lifted a weight—what concept will they understand
faster? Your choice is not based on what you prefer as a coach, but what will
have the most impact on the team?
With intensity, we need to build on execution. With submaximal intensity,
it is easier to execute rep integrity than with maximal intensity. Having
multiple sets within a training session gives more opportunities to reach
stimulating loads with plenty of rehearsal. Having multiple weeks within a
mesocycle gives multiple exposures to progressively overload and reach
threshold intensity adequately. You have more time than you think; the rush
to max out the first week is a novice mistake. It is like baking; you can
always add, but you can never subtract once an ingredient is mixed in.
Rest
The only interesting variable is rest. The time spent between sets or exercises
is often overlooked. We can look at rest in two ways: quality or density. The
shorter, faster, or heavier set means we will need more rest. You will see up
to 5 min for highly neurological drills like sprinting, advanced plyometrics,
Olympic lifts, or neurologically based protocols in the weight room. These
are examples of rest based on what we are doing during the set. The set, more
often than not, determines the rest.
However, density is a stressor in itself and needs to be part of the
conversation regarding rest. When the point is to accrue more density,
decreasing rest time is the progressive overload. If we are using expanding
density, we are adding more volume in a fixed time, which means less rest
from one training session to the next. If we are compressing density, we are
doing the same work in less time, which also means less rest. Rest is
autoregulated by the ability to perform the preceding set and expectation; we
can go again. If a density approach best serves the quality we are trying to
work with, we need to review the logic that sets variables to determine the
rest.
With rest, use common sense and logic. We probably do not need to rest
for a full 5 min between submaximal work. Even if it is neurological in focus,
it is overkill and a session killer with a large group to have a rest period that

分母在房间里就能明白。 最年轻、经验最少的教练——他们能比其他
教练更好地解释装载战术吗？ 对于从未举重的新生来说，他们会更快
地理解什么概念？你的选择不是基于你作为教练的偏好，而是基于什么
对球队影响最大？
在强度方面，我们需要以执行力为基础。使用次最大强度时，比使用
最大强度时更容易执行重复完整性。 在一次训练中进行多组训练可以
让您有更多机会通过大量排练来达到刺激负荷。 在中周期内有数周的
时间可以进行多次暴露，以逐渐超负荷并充分达到阈值强度。 你拥有
的时间比你想象的要多； 急于在第一周就达到最大是一个新手错误。
这就像烘焙一样； 您可以随时添加，但一旦混合了某种成分，就永远
无法减少。
Rest
唯一有趣的变量是休息。组次或练习之间花费的时间常常被忽视。我们
可以从两个方面来看待休息：质量或密度。 The shorter, faster, or heavier
set means we will need more rest.您将看到长达 5 分钟的高度神经学训练
，例如短跑、高级增强式训练、奥林匹克举重或举重室中基于神经学的
方案。 这些是基于我们在训练期间所做的事情的休息示例。集合往往
决定其余部分。
然而，密度本身就是一种压力源，需要成为有关休息的对话的一部分
。 当重点是增加密度时，减少休息时间就是渐进式超负荷。 如果我们
使用扩展密度，我们会在固定时间内增加更多的训练量，这意味着从一
个训练到下一个训练的休息时间会减少。 如果我们压缩密度，我们就
能用更少的时间完成同样的工作，这也意味着更少的休息。 休息是根
据执行前一组的能力和期望来自动调节的；我们可以再去一次。 如果
密度方法最能满足我们想要达到的质量，我们需要检查设置变量的逻辑
来确定其余部分。
休息时，运用常识和逻辑。 我们可能不需要在次最大强度工作之间
休息整整 5 分钟。即使它是神经学的重点，它也是矫枉过正的，是一个
会议杀手，一大群人有一个休息时间

long. Exercise order and antagonist pairings facilitate rest from one
movement to the next. Having racks with three to four people facilitates rest
between sets organically. Having stations with a certain group working or
resting facilitates rest. Employing intuitive coaching by giving longer
explanations or providing exaggerated demonstrations has a significant
impact.

Tracking and Organizing
How are we going to track all of this? The strength coach is the driver. The
weight room is the vehicle. The program is the direction. For us to get where
we want to go, we need to establish the program as the most linear path to
getting there. The question then is, how do we deliver and document our
program at scale?
This topic can be pretty polarizing, but the way you deliver your program
is incredibly important. Traditionally, strength coaches become masters of
Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets and print off hundreds of training cards
each week. There is a certain level of personal touch with a training card that
is hard to replicate. You can put your creative design and overall touch on
something by designing and administering training cards. But the bigger
questions are, can you replicate that through other coaches, and does it cost
you a lot of unnecessary time?
There is a lot to be said about building systems and restricting creativity.
We have talked a lot about creating standard operating procedures and
repeatable practices to facilitate consistent output. When we face the reality
of using a software program, we limit creative expression. As strength
coaches, we pay very little attention to our level of skill and creativity.
Taking away an outlet for the sake of scalability or efficiency is potentially a
lot to ask. But we have to be realistic; reducing a bottleneck of training cards
is necessary.
The biggest added value for programming software is cloud-based storage
of training data. The fact that it saves countless hours of data transfer is worth
abandoning the preference for training cards. With training cards, we risk
losing a card or illegible handwriting, forcing us to consider programming

长的。 锻炼顺序和对抗配对有助于从一个动作到下一个动作的休息。
拥有三到四个人的架子可以有机地促进组间休息。 拥有特定组工作或
休息的站点有助于休息。 通过提供更长的解释或提供夸张的演示来采
用直观指导会产生重大影响。

跟踪和组织
我们如何追踪这一切？ 力量教练就是司机。 举重室就是车辆。纲领就
是方向。为了到达我们想去的地方，我们需要将计划建立为到达那里的
最线性路径。 那么问题是，我们如何大规模交付和记录我们的计划？
这个话题可能非常两极分化，但交付程序的方式非常重要。 传统上
，力量教练成为 Microsoft Excel 或 Google Sheets 的大师，每周打印数百
张训练卡。训练卡具有一定程度的个人风格，这是难以复制的。 您可
以通过设计和管理培训卡来将您的创意设计和整体风格融入到某些事物
中。 但更大的问题是，你能通过其他教练复制这一点吗？这是否会花
费你很多不必要的时间？
关于构建系统和限制创造力有很多话要说。我们已经讨论了很多关于
创建标准操作程序和可重复实践以促进一致输出的内容。 当我们面对
使用软件程序的现实时，我们限制了创造性表达。 作为力量教练，我
们很少关注我们的技能和创造力水平。为了可扩展性或效率而取消出口
可能是一个很大的要求。但我们必须现实一点；减少训练卡的瓶颈是必
要的。
编程软件的最大附加值是基于云的训练数据存储。事实上，它节省了
无数小时的数据传输时间，值得放弃对培训卡的偏好。 使用训练卡，
我们可能会面临丢失卡片或字迹难以辨认的风险，迫使我们考虑编程

software. That data represents a breadcrumb trail to retrace our steps in case
we get lost. Backtracking to training inputs that we deviated from is
important for evaluating program efficacy.
An extremely important piece of data entry is who enters the training data.
Having the perspective that you, as a coach, are a facilitator and the athlete is
the purpose of the program shapes who should record the data. We want to
provide the best experience possible. It is natural to try to do more, like
recording weights for our athletes. In a group setting, you have to prioritize
safety and execution over recording weights. We still need that data; hence,
we need athletes to record it themselves.

Start and Finish as a Team
An important consideration of working in a team setting is the
pageantry of a training session. It matters how the session looks
to the outsider or a colleague. You may not want to hear this, but
the appearance of the session will have a big influence on how
people perceive you as a strength coach.
The easiest way to do this is to have a session that looks
organized and even well-choreographed. Making a point of
emphasis at the start is strategically important. It kick-starts a
large group, which is hard to do. Momentum with one person is a
lot easier to generate than with many. Having an emphatic start
is intentional for psychological inertia. Getting an emphatic start
is critical to managing large groups because it demonstrates
there is someone in charge and tasked with managing the group.
Certain coaches have a certain presence that comes
naturally. Others may struggle with this aspect. Find what works.
Leveraging your team as a means to offload the work is a
strategy if you struggle in this area. Collaboration with the team
and staff on something that feels natural and aligns with the
team’s identity can be extremely beneficial.
However, the finish is something that can go multiple ways.
Breaking down the lift and having a definitive finish is tough.

软件。这些数据代表了一条面包屑路径，可以在我们迷路时追溯我们的
脚步。 回溯我们偏离的培训输入对于评估计划效果非常重要。
数据输入的一个极其重要的部分是由谁输入训练数据。作为一名教练
，你是一名促进者，而运动员是该计划的目的，目的是确定谁应该记录

以团队形式开始和结束
在团队环境中工作的一个重要考虑因素是培训课程的盛况。会议
在局外人或同事看来如何很重要。您可能不想听到这个，但是课
程的外观将对人们如何看待您作为力量教练产生很大影响。
要做到这一点，最简单的方法就是让会议看起来井井有条，甚
至精心设计。 从一开始就明确重点具有战略意义。 它启动了一
个大团体，这是很难做到的。与一个人一起比与多人一起更容易
产生动力。 强烈的开始是为了心理惰性。 强有力的开始对于管
理大型团体至关重要，因为它表明有人负责并负责管理团体。

某些教练有一种自然而然的存在感。其他人可能会在这方面遇
到困难。找到有效的方法。如果您在这方面遇到困难，那么利用
您的团队作为减轻工作负担的方法是一种策略。 与团队和员工在
感觉自然且符合团队身份的事情上进行合作可能非常有益。
然而，最终的结局可以有多种方式。打破电梯并最终完成任务
是很困难的。

Having a definitive stop means that we have a uniform training
program. We become hampered by what we can do in a training
session because we have to finish at the same time. If we
choose to have multiple programs occurring simultaneously, it
will involve different sets, reps, intensities, and rest periods.
We could have everyone stay around and have a breakdown
as a team. There are many necessary things following a
program: sports science, postworkout nutrition, cleaning, and
setting up for the next group. Having closure for that group with a
breakdown can be completely overshadowed by the endless list
of tasks that still need to be completed.
Athletes respond well to routine. Indicators of what is next, or
a benchmark, are important. The rituals create organization.
Having rituals around starting a training session is important
because they trigger the approach to certain segments of the
day. We need great execution and great effort; we can leverage
the power of ritual to get them. We can also leverage the power
of ritual to engage and connect with athletes.
Giving autonomy and showing vulnerability that you need your athlete’s
help and support during a session is a valuable message. An athlete recording
their weight demonstrates trust and the value of taking responsibility for their
development. Being a helicopter coach and doing everything and protecting
the athletes from anything leads to sheltered, limited experiences. Taking
ownership of each responsibility is a critical dynamic in a team setting. The
tools we have should be intuitive and user friendly, so we do not make our
lives harder. Chances are that your athletes are more capable with technology
and present themselves as untapped assets we have yet to leverage.
You will want to organize your racks by ability to optimize training
session efficiency. Changing weight takes time. Time has a cost, and if we
spend it on poorly organized workouts, we lose potential value. There is a
human element to assigning racks. Some people work better together than
others. Some people elevate others around them. Understanding the human
element matters. Rack assignments represent a commitment to the

明确的停止意味着我们有统一的训练计划。我们在训练中能做的
事情会受到阻碍，因为我们必须同时完成。 如果我们选择同时进
行多个项目，它将涉及不同的组数、次数、强度和休息时间。
我们可以让每个人都留下来，作为一个团队进行崩溃。 计划结
束后有很多必要的事情：运动科学、锻炼后营养、清洁以及为下

创造组织。在开始训练时进行仪式很重要，因为它们会触发一天
中某些部分的开始。我们需要强大的执行力和巨大的努力；我们
可以利用仪式的力量来获得它们。我们还可以利用仪式的力量来
与运动员互动和联系。

给予自主权并表现出你在训练期间需要运动员的帮助和支持的脆弱性
是一个有价值的信息。运动员记录体重表明了信任以及对自己的发展承
担责任的价值。 作为一名直升机教练，尽一切努力保护运动员免受任
何伤害，这会带来受庇护的、有限的经历。 承担每项责任是团队环境
中的关键动力。 我们拥有的工具应该直观且用户友好，这样我们才不
会让我们的生活变得更加困难。您的运动员很可能拥有更强的技术能力
，并将自己呈现为我们尚未利用的未开发资产。
您需要根据能力来组织训练架，以优化训练效率。 改变体重需要时
间。 时间是有成本的，如果我们把时间花在组织不好的锻炼上，我们
就会失去潜在的价值。 分配机架存在人为因素。 有些人比其他人更好
地合作。 有些人会提升周围的人。 了解人的因素很重要。 机架分配
代表了对

organization in each training session. Programming exercises and variables
represent your professionalism and understanding. Thinking about athletes
and which pair best with one another represents your awareness and
connectedness.

Coaching
Coaching assignments matter too. An obvious hierarchy is created when you
place a coach in a certain spot. Athletes and coaches are aware of the
difficulty in doing something. Placing a coach in a position that involves
something more difficult, carries higher risk, or has greater relative impact
makes them appear more significant. A coach placed at a rack with the team’s
best players will be perceived as more important. The coaches are aware of
this, and you can use this as an incentive.
When you have assistants, you probably are not as aware as you should be
of their jockeying for standing as much as they are. Your gestures and
mannerisms as a supervisor have a profound impact on their performance.
Your consistency and messaging can derail motivation or inspire others to be
better than they imagined. Similar to assigning racks based on efficiency or
group dynamics, assigning coaches should also be given high regard.
Understanding the dynamics of placing a coach in a particular spot is the
director’s responsibility in programming and interacting with athletes.
It all starts with a single rep. If we can program and coach each rep
effectively, our odds of making a difference increase. From there, it is about
doing that consistently. Athletes will get stronger, their motivation will
change, they will get hurt, they will be in a bad mood, and they will have
something that you cannot control. All that matters, but you have no control
over any of that. What you do have control over is the next rep, and making
that most important is all you can do. If you have a plan, you are organized,
and you are committed to each training session, it will be great.

Take Home
Training session design is about finding the biggest limiting factor to rep
integrity and removing it. In a team setting, the most creative session design

每期培训的组织。 编程练习和变量代表了你的专业水平和理解力。 思
考运动员以及他们之间的最佳搭配代表了你的意识和联系。

辅导
辅导任务也很重要。当你把教练放在某个位置时，就会产生明显的等级
制度。 运动员和教练员都意识到做某事的困难。 将教练置于涉及更困
难、风险更高或相对影响更大的职位会让他们显得更重要。与球队最好
的球员并肩作战的教练会被认为更重要。 教练们都知道这一点，你可
以以此作为激励。
当你有助手时，你可能不会像你应该意识到的那样，意识到他们为了
站得尽可能多而争先恐后。 作为主管，你的手势和举止会对他们的表
现产生深远的影响。你的一致性和信息传递可能会破坏动力或激励他人
比他们想象的更好。 与根据效率或团队动态分配机架类似，分配教练
也应受到高度重视。了解将教练安排在特定位置的动态是导演在规划和
与运动员互动时的责任。
这一切都始于一次代表。 如果我们能够有效地规划和指导每个代表
，我们做出改变的可能性就会增加。从那时起，就是要始终如一地这样
做。 运动员会变得更强，他们的动力会改变，他们会受伤，他们会心
情不好，他们会有一些你无法控制的事情。所有这些都很重要，但你无
法控制其中的任何一个。你能控制的是下一次代表，而你能做的就是让
这件事变得最重要。如果你有计划、有组织、并且全身心地投入到每一
次训练中，那就太好了。

带回家
培训课程设计的目的是找到代表完整性的最大限制因素并消除它。在团
队环境中，最具创意的会议设计

pales in comparison to the most organized and efficient. Understand the
assignment as a strength coach working with a large group. We have to
prioritize that the group has great training each day over everything else.

与最有组织、最高效的组织相比，就相形见绌了。 了解作为一名力量
教练与一大群人一起工作的任务。 我们必须优先考虑让团队每天进行
良好的训练，而不是其他一切。
