MICROCYCLE DESIGN
A microcycle is a collection of training sessions. An important distinction is
that a microcycle’s length does not have to be tied to a calendar week. A
microcycle is the length of time it takes to get back to the original session
within the microcycle. Establishing the length of the microcycle as not
exclusive to 7-day periods allows for creativity and openness to solutions to
problems we do not know exist.
Microcycles’ central point is to organize movement patterns within a set
period. Think of a microcycle as the organizational chart of when and where
we program movement patterns, which directly affect the variables we
choose to use with those patterns. How we structure microcycles speaks
volumes about what movement patterns are prioritized and when. Choosing a
certain training split is a clear demonstration of which movement patterns
hold the most weight in a training program. Just as reps have symbolic
gestures, exercise placement holds a symbolic gesture of their relative
importance.
The length of the microcycle has a huge impact on the placement of those
exercises. We know that we will primarily fall into a 7-day microcycle,
working traditionally Monday through Friday with our training days. This is
the realistic setup of most of the work within strength and conditioning. This
is not a bad thing, but it does restrict certain training splits. Taking into
consideration many factors, such as recovery rates, mesocycle focus,
macrocycle period, and pure logistics, has a tremendous impact on how we

18
微循环设计
微周期是训练课程的集合。 一个重要的区别是，微周期的长度不必与
日历周挂钩。 微周期是指在微周期内返回到原始会话所需的时间长度
。 将微周期的长度确定为不限于 7 天，可以发挥创造力并以开放的态
度解决我们不知道存在的问题。
微循环的中心点是在设定的时间内组织运动模式。将微循环视为我们
在何时何地编程运动模式的组织图，它直接影响我们选择与这些模式一
起使用的变量。 我们如何构建微循环充分说明了哪些运动模式需要优
先考虑以及何时优先考虑。选择特定的训练分组可以清楚地表明哪些运
动模式在训练计划中最重要。 正如代表有象征性手势一样，练习位置
也有其相对重要性的象征性手势。

微周期的长度对这些练习的安排有巨大的影响。 我们知道，我们主
要会陷入 7 天的微周期，传统上周一到周五的训练日都是工作的。这是
力量和体能训练中大部分工作的现实设置。这并不是一件坏事，但它确
实限制了某些训练分组。 考虑到许多因素，例如回收率、中周期焦点
、宏观周期和纯物流，对我们如何

design our microcycles.

Microcycle Length
The microcycle length is determined by how long it takes us to get back to
the original training session, which is significant because it is the foundation
of progressive overload. We have to repeat a training session to progressively
overload an exercise in some manner. This is the premise behind determining
the rate and quantity of adaptation. We can increase intensity, volume, and
density. But that is only the case if we repeat the same training session from
one microcycle to the next.
In a sense, we need to think about the length of the microcycle in terms of
how long it will take us to recover to allow for progressive overload
consistently. Training splits, or specific durations, are predicated on what it
takes to adapt to facilitate consistent increases in volume, intensity, or
density. We choose to use a pattern or a drill on certain days for logistic
purposes and personal preference. Have you ever stopped and asked if that is
the best organization to facilitate consistent progressive overload? If we
change the order, can we get faster and greater recovery?
Looking back at the history of this and early team-setting programs, a
large portion of them were 3-day total body splits within a 5-day window and
a 7-day microcycle. A 3-day total body program hitting a variation of a
primary pattern one time per week was the focal point early in strength and
conditioning. A large part of that was predicated on Olympic lifting programs
for amateur athletes who held jobs on top of their training. Three-day total
body programs were designed to provide enough stimulus to increase
strength and simultaneously facilitate recovery from day-to-day jobs. This
scenario is not uncommon in the arrangement our current athletes face.
That training split evolved into models like Boyd Epley’s Husker Power
(Shurley, 2012) or Arthur Jones’ HIT (Smith, 2009). Both were essentially
the same total body programs that were repeated three times over the same 5day window within a 7-day microcycle. This is interesting because instead of
a 7-day gap between stressing a pattern, it became a 2-day gap. Progressive
overload was still a focal point, just not as much as before. The idea was

设计我们的微循环。

微循环长度
微周期的长度取决于我们回到原来的训练需要多长时间，这很重要，因
为它是渐进式超负荷的基础。我们必须重复训练，以某种方式逐渐超负
荷练习。这是确定适应速度和数量的前提。 我们可以增加强度、体积
和密度。但只有当我们从一个微周期到下一个微周期重复相同的训练课
程时才会出现这种情况。
从某种意义上说，我们需要考虑微周期的长度，即我们需要多长时间
才能恢复到持续不断的渐进超负荷。 训练分段或特定持续时间取决于
如何适应以促进训练量、强度或密度的持续增加。 出于后勤目的和个
人喜好，我们选择在某些日子使用图案或钻头。您是否曾经停下来问过
这是否是促进持续渐进超负荷的最佳组织？ 如果我们改变顺序，是否
可以得到更快、更大的恢复？
回顾这个项目和早期团队设置项目的历史，其中很大一部分是在 5 天
的窗口和 7 天的微周期内进行 3 天的全身训练。 每周一次、为期 3 天
的全身训练计划，针对主要模式进行一次变体训练，这是早期力量和体
能训练的重点。其中很大一部分是针对业余运动员的奥林匹克举重项目
，他们在训练之外还从事工作。 为期三天的全身计划旨在提供足够的
刺激来增强力量，同时促进日常工作的恢复。 这种情况在我们目前运
动员面临的安排中并不罕见。
这种训练划分演变成了博伊德·埃普利 (Boyd Epley) 的 Husker Power (
Shurley, 2012) 或阿瑟·琼斯 (Arthur Jones) 的 HIT (Smith, 2009) 等模型。
两者本质上是相同的全身计划，在 7 天的微周期内的同一个 5 天窗口内
重复 3 次。这很有趣，因为强调模式之间的间隔不是 7 天，而是 2 天。
渐进性超负荷仍然是一个焦点，只是没有以前那么严重。 这个想法是

based on the idea that if it is important, do it every day. Husker Power was
ahead of its time and fostered a huge competitive advantage. HIT evolved
into machines and targeting a muscle or muscle group once in a 7-to-10-day
period.
Taking a step further, a more aesthetically focused training split emerged
with a 5-day split routine. The focus transitioned from movement patterns to
muscles or muscle groups. The central idea was to stress an individual muscle
more on a given day or increase the frequency of training that muscle within
a training window and microcycle. The focus on stressing a muscle more was
centered on increasing pure volume in a given training session. This approach
was set up by not having to stress that muscle within a 7-to-10-day gap.
Before you chastise me for this being nonfunctional or not a good use of
time, remember it is a model that has had a profound effect on performance.
Think of what you would do with someone who could travel 5 to 6 days
within a microcycle. What would you do differently?
Body part splits did have an impact in a program more oriented to muscle
groups. This provided a greater frequency of hitting patterns or muscles,
focusing on clusters of muscle groups such as upper and lower, or chest and
triceps, back and biceps, and quadriceps and hamstrings. Volume was shifted
from a concentrated training session to a spread-out frequency. Stress was
spread, but the recovery gap was shortened. A muscle group was trained
every 2 to 3 days instead of every 7 days. Frequency within a microcycle
became a really important part of microcycle design.
This then led to a 4-day training split that focused on either upper and
lower or push and pull. The central idea is that stress allocation is best
through increased frequency. Similar to training splits oriented to muscle
groups, having more stress within a given microcycle in a movement pattern
was the focal point. The general idea was built upon the notion that more
total training inputs in a microcycle, and subsequently a mesocycle, were
most important.
Finally, the cyclic nature of life brought us back to a 3-day total body
program, incorporating more functional, nonpattern variations of squat,
hinge, push, and pull in all three planes of motion programming. Speed
training, focusing on linear acceleration and top-end speed, or

基于这样的想法：如果重要，那就每天都做。 Husker Power 领先于时
代并形成了巨大的竞争优势。 HIT 演变成机器，每 7 到 10 天针对一个
肌肉或肌肉群进行一次。
更进一步，更注重美观的训练计划出现了，为期 5 天的训练计划。焦
点从运动模式转移到肌肉或肌肉群。中心思想是在某一天对单个肌肉施
加更大的压力，或者在训练窗口和微周期内增加训练该肌肉的频率。对

身体部位的分割确实对更针对肌肉群的计划产生了影响。 这提供了
更高的击打模式或肌肉频率，重点关注肌肉群群，例如上肌群和下肌群
，或胸部和三头肌、背部和二头肌、四头肌和腿筋。训练量从集中训练
转变为分散频率训练。 压力分散了，但恢复差距缩短了。 每 2 至 3 天
而不是每 7 天训练一次肌肉群。 微循环内的频率成为微循环设计中非
常重要的一部分。
随后进行了为期 4 天的训练，重点是上、下或推和拉。 中心思想是
通过增加频率来最好地分配压力。 与针对肌肉群的训练分割类似，在
运动模式的给定微周期内承受更大的压力是焦点。 总的想法是建立在
这样的观念之上的：微循环以及随后的中循环中更多的总训练输入是最
重要的。
最后，生命的循环性质让我们回到了为期 3 天的全身计划，在所有三
个运动平面中融入了更多功能性、非模式变化的深蹲、铰链、推拉和拉
动计划。 速度训练，重点是线性加速和最高速度，或者

multidirectional power cutting and speed cutting, became a huge focal point
of training. Adding plyometric exercises, like jumping, hopping, bounding,
medicine ball throwing, and tossing, became another focal point of training.
Last, Olympic weightlifting and its variations using barbells and dumbbells
led to the use of kettlebells, sandbags, water bags, and various other
implements. These nonpattern entities did not fit neatly into a normal
program and forced an evolution of programming. If you were to evaluate in
hindsight, going back to a 3-day total program to start from was smart.

Adaptation Rate
All this history is only as important as one thing: Can we get better using a
certain organization within a microcycle? The rate and quantity of adaptation
are critical aspects of the microcycle. Regardless of the preference for
training split or microcycle length, if we are positively adapting, we have
selected the correct amount of stimulus. The question is, could we have had
more adaptation at a faster rate by choosing a different training split and
mesocycle length? Outcomes, not solutions, are what govern everything.

FIGURE 18.1 Weekly rate of progressive overload.
We are targeting a 2% to 5% amount of progressive overload within, at
most, 7 days (figure 18.1). That number is an average of 4 weeks, the typical

多向力量切割和速度切割，成为训练的巨大焦点。 增加增强式训练，
如跳跃、弹跳、弹跳、投掷药球和投掷，成为训练的另一个重点。最后
，奥运会举重及其使用杠铃和哑铃的变式运动导致了壶铃、沙袋、水袋
和各种其他工具的使用。 这些非模式实体并不完全适合正常程序，并
迫使编程发生演变。如果您要事后评估，那么回到从 3 天的总体计划开
始是明智的。

适应率
所有这些历史只与一件事一样重要：我们能否在微循环内更好地利用某
个组织？适应的速度和数量是微循环的关键方面。 无论对训练分段或
微周期长度的偏好如何，如果我们积极适应，我们就选择了正确的刺激
量。 问题是，通过选择不同的训练分割和中周期长度，我们能否以更
快的速度获得更多的适应？决定一切的是结果，而不是解决方案。

图 18.1 每周渐进性超负荷率。
我们的目标是在最多 7 天内实现 2% 至 5% 的渐进超载（图 18.1）。
这个数字平均为 4 周，典型的

length of a mesocycle. It will be front-loaded early in a mesocycle, around
7% to 10%, and then trail off to the end of the mesocycle for a 1% to 2%
amount of progressive overload. The 7 days is something that allows for a
reduction in delayed onset muscle soreness, glycogen repletion, potential
protein synthesis, and neurological recovery. If we can make a jump of 5%
each microcycle within a mesocycle, we will get as much out of that
mesocycle as possible.
A lot of microcycle design is not up to us. We are building our program
around what we inherit and what our teams allow us to do. For many of us,
that is a 2-day to 3-day per week training allotment in a weight room that is
built upon compound lifts. More than likely, we are locked into a training
split and microcycle length based on circumstances. A significant aspect that
we have to explore, regardless of circumstances, is centered on what allows
for the most rapid and extensive levels of adaptation.

Weekly Training Windows
There is a difference between microcycle length and training windows, which
is most obvious with a 7-day microcycle (figure 18.2). We only have a 5-day
window to train within that microcycle. It is 7 days between one training
session and the next, but 2 days are guaranteed to have no training sessions.
We have to localize and concentrate training stress into a 5-day window. The
relative rate of recovery from a movement pattern focus, a muscle or muscle
group focus, or even a quality being trained can easily be compromised by
the shrunken training window.

中周期的长度。 它将在中周期早期提前加载，大约 7% 到 10%，然后
逐渐减弱到中周期结束时，逐渐过载 1% 到 2%。 7 天可以减少迟发性
肌肉酸痛、糖原补充、潜在的蛋白质合成和神经恢复。 如果我们能够
在中周期内每个微周期跳跃 5%，我们就能从中周期中获得尽可能多的
收益。
很多微循环的设计并不取决于我们。 我们正在围绕我们继承的东西
和我们的团队允许我们做的事情来制定我们的计划。 对于我们许多人
来说，这是每周在复合举重室进行 2 天到 3 天的训练。 很有可能，我
们会根据具体情况来限制训练的分割和微周期的长度。无论情况如何，
我们必须探索的一个重要方面是如何实现最快速和最广泛的适应。

每周训练窗口
微周期长度和训练窗口之间存在差异，这在 7 天的微周期中最为明显（
图 18.2）。我们只有 5 天的时间在这个微周期内进行训练。 一场训练
与下一场训练之间相隔 7 天，但保证 2 天没有训练。我们必须将训练压
力本地化并集中到5天的时间窗口内。运动模式焦点、肌肉或肌肉群焦
点、甚至正在训练的质量的相对恢复率很容易因训练窗口的缩小而受到
影响。

FIGURE 18.2 Microcycle length versus window.
This problem is handled by various training split rationales. A reduced
window needs to be matched with overreaching within that window. We can
then capitalize on the guaranteed closed window to train for recovery. The
central aspect of this is keeping a positive relationship between fitness and
fatigue. Back-to-back training days, to compensate for restricted days for
training, lead to accruing excess fatigue. Training the same pattern, muscles
and muscle group, or quality, more and more days in a row builds a level of
fatigue that may not facilitate recovery during the closed window. But with
that comes a compromise of the total stress we can tolerate in a given
microcycle.
We need to be creative with how we arrange a microcycle and its length.
Having enough time to facilitate progressive overload is the most important
factor. If we can get that within 48 hours, we should explore it. If we can
train a pattern or quality within 12 hours but with a focus on a different
quality, we should explore that as well. If we lengthen a microcycle to 10
days but have a higher frequency within those 10 days with many pattern
variations and target muscles and muscle groups in unique formats, we
should explore that too.
We know fast-twitch athletes will respond to the same stress more than
slow-twitch athletes. This is especially true if we are using compound lifts

图 18.2 微循环长度与窗口的关系。
这个问题是通过各种训练分割原理来处理的。 缩小的窗口需要与该
窗口内的过度扩张相匹配。然后我们可以利用保证关闭的窗口来进行恢

数的限制，连续训练几天会导致过度疲劳。 连续越来越多的天训练相

在关闭窗口期间恢复。 但随之而来的是我们在给定微循环中可以承受
的总压力的妥协。

That does not necessarily mean the opposite for a slow-twitch athlete. The
nature of strength and conditioning focuses on anaerobic development, such
as velocity, power, and force. We will push this neurological and muscular
stimulus on our athletes to make them more explosive, more efficient, and

found the right length and window to work within. Most things will work for
novice athletes. Most things do not work with advanced athletes. Find the
right length over time because you know the athlete better.

Training Splits
We will need to pick a microcycle organization to build an anchor point for
our program. Ensuring we have structural balance by hitting all pushing and
pulling exercises for the upper and lower body is paramount to success.
Training splits are our means to seamlessly transition from the off-season to
the in-season without missing a step. We simply toggle the exercises and
their order based on the level of frequency we train within a microcycle.

What You Can Control
The training split is how we plan to organize exercises within a microcycle.
Where and when we do something has a dual impact and symbolism behind
it. When you open the week with a certain pattern, you are saying this is the
most important exercise that will have the biggest impact. We then need to
use that exercise as the keystone piece behind our microcycle. The bottom
line is, once you commit to the exercise that is first or last, you need to
commit to it and make the best microcycle you can to facilitate constant
progressive overload.

训练分批是我们从休赛期无缝过渡到赛季内、不遗漏任何一步的手段。
我们只需根据微周期内训练的频率水平来切换练习及其顺序即可。

Organizing Exercises
Where training splits get hung up is the organization of the other components
we are responsible for as strength coaches. Squatting, hinging, pushing, and
pulling patterns are central to organizing training splits. When we have to
include components that are not patterns, it throws our programming
equilibrium off, which means we will have to orient ourselves differently.
One thing about speed, plyometrics, and weightlifting is that they are all
highly neurological in stimulus, which will have a greater impact on fatigue
and recovery. Doing linear or multidirectional speed has huge logistic
considerations as well.

Combining Speed, Plyometrics, and Resistance Training
One thing to consider with high neurologically based stimuli is to concentrate
the stress to increase recovery time within a microcycle; for example, doing
speed, plyometrics, Olympic weightlifting, and compound lower body lifts on
the same training day, which allows us to get more rest than trying to space
that over multiple days. Concentrated high neurological loads are best served
in one dose as opposed to spread-out dosages, which allows for more
intramicrocycle recovery. A huge consideration is doing microtraining
sessions before practice and games. A 15 to 30 min training session focusing
on the rate of force development to potentiate is a stressor and needs to be
considered within the larger microcycle organization.
Which patterns match better with high neurological days? The key is
aligning with which high-threshold motor units will be recruited. By stacking
all activities that access high-threshold motor units, we can facilitate recovery
intramicrocycle by not having to recruit those motor units multiple days in a
row. We can get upward of 48 to 72 hours by having isolated high-threshold
days rather than 12 to 24 hours. That extra recovery can do wonders for
increasing the rates and quantity of adaptation.
Our training split now has to be based on how many days we get, along
with more than just the primary patterns we have to develop. Keeping it
simple, again, is the best strategy. Stack your high neurological activities
together, hit your patterns, and facilitate recovery between sessions. A 2-day
program is easy: Stack all the exercises within 2 days and allow for as much
recovery time as possible between sessions; the same applies to a 3-day
program. A 4-day program gets interesting and is worth spending some time
on.
A 4-day program is interesting because we work within a 7-day
microcycle, traditionally with a 5-day window. We can get 2 to 3 high
neurological days. We can hit major patterns multiple times per week without
compromising recovery. We stack speed, plyometrics, and weightlifting,

习的机会。 我们可以通过更好的微循环安排，在我们的计划中通过非
模式和模式练习来分层更好的进展。

along with big patterns that recruit a large number of motor units on two of
the days and lower nervous system, elongated work, and patterns that recruit

A 4-day program, whether it is push and pull or lower and upper, has to
consider that we will activate high-threshold motor units each day. The
concept to explore is whether regional motor unit recruitment leads to more
fatigue compared to general motor unit recruitment. Based on other models,
such as body part splits, this may be too much. The model focuses on overall
training volume and density, which is more metabolic stress as opposed to
neurological stress. The mechanism for regional-based frequency is not
hitting motor units each day, but rather the length of time delayed onset
muscle soreness lasts in order to repeat a training session. For high-threshold
motor unit training, you will need to test and see a residual impact from one
training session to the next. This can have a second-order impact on
mesocycle length.
The last point for the organization is that simultaneous programs are going
on. If we are in a situation where different microcycles occur, we have to
resort to the logistics of weight room setup and coaching organization. Where
and when we can be successful is just as important as the premise behind the
program. Something as simple as explaining the workouts to different groups
can be a nightmare if not prepared. The most important consideration is that
you have the weight room set up to accommodate multiple programs
simultaneously. Accessibility to the equipment matters most; if we have
bottlenecks and lose efficiency, we lose the ability to execute the training
session effectively. Next, do we have enough coaches, and do they have the
bandwidth to handle this? A good microcycle is like a good training session:
Can we execute this with a larger number of athletes as our top priority?

品质安排
微循环难题的最后一块是力量、相对力量、功能性肥大、肌肉肥大和肌
肉耐力等品质的排列。 这方面与中循环密切相关。 我们正在根据更大
、综合的宏观周期图景来开发质量。这

microcycle and the training session are the pieces of the mesocycle that
facilitate the development of quality.
The larger picture dictates the smaller picture. If we are in a more
traditional periodization, like linear, our microcycle will be based on where
we are in the macrocycle. If we are following a block periodization, the
microcycle will also be based on where we are in the macrocycle. However,
if we are working on a conjugate or concurrent periodization model, we are
working on all the qualities simultaneously.

Conjugate Periodization
Conjugate periodization is a method that focuses on all the qualities we have
discussed each day. A conjugate-based training session will feature a period
focused on velocity or power, a period focused on force, and then a period
focused on work. Conjugate periodization is a grenade approach that tries to
address each quality in each training session. It spreads the rate and amount
of force to ensure hitting each quality on each day. Training session design is
based on neurologically demanding movements early and more muscular
movements later; the microcycle is no different. So that would mean opening
with velocity and power, transitioning to relative strength, and finishing with
hypertrophy or muscular endurance. With conjugate periodization, we
traditionally see a 4-day upper and lower training split. This allows for the
arrangement of qualities with certain patterns being stressed and adequate
recovery.

Concurrent Periodization
Concurrent periodization is a method that focuses on a specific quality for an
entire training session. The quality rotates within the microcycle depending
on the focus of the mesocycle. The organization of qualities within a training
session is established, but within the microcycle requires some planning. It
comes mostly down to the training split. Keeping training session rules in
place for microcycle rules is helpful here. The same applies to a training
session; we want to focus on neurological movements earlier in the
microcycle and muscular movements later in the microcycle. If we were to
focus on velocity or power during a training session, that would have to come

较大的图景决定较小的图景。 如果我们处于更传统的周期（例如线

循块周期，微周期也将基于我们在宏观周期中的位置。然而，如果我们
正在研究共轭或并发周期模型，我们就会同时研究所有质量。

共轭周期化
共轭分期是一种关注我们每天讨论的所有品质的方法。 基于共轭的训
练课程将包括一个专注于速度或力量的时期，一个专注于力量的时期，
然后一个专注于工作的时期。共轭周期化是一种手榴弹方法，试图解决
每次训练中的每个质量问题。 它分散了力量的速度和大小，以确保每
天击中每个质量。训练课程的设计是基于早期对神经系统要求较高的运
动和随后更多肌肉运动；微循环也不例外。因此，这意味着以速度和力
量开始，过渡到相对力量，最后以肌肉肥大或肌肉耐力结束。 对于共
轭周期，我们传统上会看到 4 天的上限和下限训练。 这允许对某些模
式进行强调和充分恢复的品质安排。

并发分期
并发周期化是一种专注于整个训练课程的特定质量的方法。 质量在微
循环内旋转取决于中循环的焦点。培训课程中的质量组织已经建立，但
在微周期内需要一些规划。 这主要取决于训练的划分。 保持微循环规
则的训练课程规则在这里很有帮助。 这同样适用于培训课程； 我们希
望关注微周期早期的神经运动和微周期后期的肌肉运动。 如果我们要
在训练期间关注速度或力量，那就必须

earlier in a microcycle, which would mean relative strength and hypertrophy
later in a microcycle.
The trickiest part of this is tied into organizing it with speed, plyometrics,
and Olympic weightlifting, with it being velocity or power. If you are going
to include these entities in your training sessions, they will determine how
your microcycle is arranged. Since they are going to be high in neurological
impact, they will need to take priority regarding available energy and
facilitating recovery. If you are using them within a conjugate-based
program, you will have to place them earlier in the training session as well as
early in the microcycle. The same can be said for concurrent-based programs.
We need to consider the transition from rest days to training days here as
well.
A good question to have is, what is the residual impact on the rest of the
week of placing the most neurally demanding training session first in a
microcycle? Another question is, do we have to place the highest
neurological impact early in a microcycle? What is apparent when coming off
a weekend or multiple days off is that athletes’ ability to transition to intense
work is not a given. The residual fatigue from the previous microcycle may
linger and negatively affect the next microcycle. The lack of recent exposure
to the high threshold may negatively affect performance within highthreshold activities in the next microcycle. We all know that multiple days off
will open up athletes to enjoying their free time, and that will negatively
impact performance. This may leave us open to starting the week with a
lower-intensity training session and saving higher-threshold training sessions
for later in the microcycle.
This is not bad logic, but not at the expense of squeezing more highthreshold training sessions within a microcycle. If we have the chance to get
one more high-threshold training session in a microcycle, we have to take it.
This only comes if we open with a high-threshold training session first. If we
have a 2-day or a 3-day microcycle, we have little choice but to open with a
high-threshold training session first. If we have a 4-day or even a 5-day
microcycle, we can potentially get an additional higher-threshold training
session if we do it first within the microcycle.
The best way to determine this is by performance later in the week.

在一个微周期的早期，这意味着在一个微周期的后期相对力量和肥大。
其中最棘手的部分是用速度、增强式训练和奥林匹克举重来组织它，
即速度或力量。 如果您打算将这些实体纳入您的培训课程，它们将决
定您的微周期的安排方式。 由于它们对神经系统的影响很大，因此需
要优先考虑可用能量和促进恢复。 如果您在基于缀合物的计划中使用
它们，则必须将它们放在训练课程的早期以及微周期的早期。对于基于
并发的程序也是如此。我们还需要考虑从休息日到训练日的过渡。

一个好问题是，将神经要求最高的训练课程放在微周期的第一位，对
本周剩余时间的残余影响是什么？ 另一个问题是，我们是否必须将最
高的神经影响放在微周期的早期？当周末或多天休息时，显而易见的是
，运动员过渡到高强度工作的能力并不是一定的。 前一个微周期的残
余疲劳可能会持续存在，并对下一个微周期产生负面影响。最近缺乏对
高阈值的接触可能会对下一个微周期中高阈值活动的表现产生负面影响
。我们都知道，多天休息会让运动员享受空闲时间，但这会对表现产生
负面影响。 这可能会让我们在本周开始时进行较低强度的训练，并将
较高阈值的训练留到微周期的后期。

这逻辑不错，但并不以在一个微周期内压缩更多高门槛训练为代价。
如果我们有机会在一个微周期内再进行一次高门槛的训练，我们就必须
接受。只有当我们首先开始高门槛的培训课程时，才会出现这种情况。
如果我们有一个 2 天或 3 天的微周期，我们别无选择，只能先以高阈值
的训练开始。 如果我们有一个 4 天甚至 5 天的微周期，如果我们首先
在微周期内进行，我们可能会获得额外的更高阈值的训练课程。
确定这一点的最佳方法是根据本周晚些时候的表现。

Testing pretraining wellness and looking at metrics like mood and stress are
connected to neurological fatigue. We can look at posttraining rating of
perceived exertion and the residual impact over the following days in the
training sessions by looking at total wellness. Last, we can see the rate of
critical drop-off by assessing reps in reserve, rep brackets, and bar velocity.

Take Home
The length of the microcycle matters a great deal. If we learn anything from
this chapter, it is that we have to be creative with how we organize our
microcycles. We have to develop plans that build on the training session’s
organization and execution. We want our microcycle to be the right length
and organization to facilitate consistent progressive overload.

带回家
微周期的长度非常重要。如果说我们从本章学到了什么的话，那就是我

织和执行为基础的计划。 我们希望我们的微周期具有合适的长度和组
织，以促进持续的渐进式超负荷。

MESOCYCLE DESIGN
Keeping the theme going, a mesocycle is a collection of microcycles. As a
planet orbits a star and the moons orbit planets, the training session revolves
around microcycles, and the microcycle revolves around mesocycles. The
star provides heat, light, and, subsequently, energy to the planets. The
mesocycle provides the quality that gives meaning and direction to our
macrocycles.
The mesocycle is designed and governed by the quality we are trying to
develop. The qualities include power, relative strength, functional
hypertrophy, hypertrophy, and muscular endurance (see figure 17.8 on page
310). Each of these qualities represents something relative to the greater goal.
It is worth mentioning that the goal is not the qualities individually. These
qualities are the foundation of accomplishing the goal.
From a general physical preparation perspective, each of these qualities
develops a greater general capacity. The capacities lead into one another and
become the gatekeepers to unlocking more returns from time invested in each
quality. For instance, if we have greater muscular endurance from a
mesocycle focused on work capacity, we will be able to perform higher
density within the power or relative strength mesocycles. If we develop
greater tensile strength of connective tissue from a hypertrophy mesocycle,
we can sustain higher loads during power and relative strength. If we develop
greater strength during a relative strength mesocycle, we can use a higher
external load during hypertrophy and muscular endurance mesocycles. Each

19
中循环设计
继续主题，中循环是微循环的集合。 当行星绕恒星运行、卫星绕行星
运行时，训练课程围绕微周期进行，而微周期又围绕中周期进行。 恒
星为行星提供热量、光和能量。 中观循环提供了赋予我们的大循环意
义和方向的品质。
中循环是由我们正在努力开发的质量设计和控制的。 这些品质包括
力量、相对力量、功能性肥大、肌肉肥大和肌肉耐力（参见第 310 页的
图 17.8）。这些品质中的每一个都代表着与更大目标相关的东西。值得
一提的是，目标并不是个人的素质。 这些品质是实现目标的基础。
从一般身体准备的角度来看，这些品质中的每一个都会发展出更大的
综合能力。这些能力相互关联，成为从在每项品质上投入的时间中释放
更多回报的把关人。 例如，如果我们在专注于工作能力的中循环中具
有更大的肌肉耐力，我们将能够在功率或相对强度中循环中执行更高的
密度。 如果我们从肥大的中周期中发展出更大的结缔组织拉伸强度，
我们就可以在功率和相对强度期间承受更高的负荷。如果我们在相对力
量中周期期间发展出更大的力量，我们就可以在肥大和肌肉耐力中周期
期间使用更高的外部负荷。 每个

quality is interconnected with the others, and understanding that is key to
developing them.
There is an art to layering one quality on top of another. Having a
seamless transition of mesocycles takes a working knowledge of what that
quality gives us and its relevance to a larger goal. It takes the experience of
knowing that to have something larger, we need to develop things we do not
yet have. It requires the perspective that we have to build a foundation of
corresponding qualities to get to a goal. Also present is the aspect of having a
gradual change from one mesocycle to the next to allow for continuous
development.
We need to demonstrate creativity by progressing from one mesocycle to
the next, but at the same time, we need structure and discipline. The transition
from one mesocycle to the next is a metamorphosis of the athlete into having
a greater physical capacity. That physical change creates a new platform to
leverage the focal point of the next training block. Matveyev (Kruger, 2016)
created this framework with the traditional linear form of periodization (see
figure 12.2 on page 200). The term building a base is represented by
alternating high volume and low intensity with low volume and high
intensity. The entire construct of periodization is built on the premise that
there needs to be a foundational ability before we can accomplish something
else. This stems from Selye’s general adaptation syndrome (Seyle, 1950).
Developing a quality is contingent upon the body’s ability to positively
respond to stress.
The essence of periodization is planning. We are forging a path that we
hope is the most linear direction toward our goal. We develop qualities along
this path. Each one of those qualities has a positive impact on the next, if
planned properly. With each quality developed, we increase our potential to
reach that goal. Quality development is a benchmark for our progress.
Planning can be based on developing weaknesses into strengths or reverse
engineering the best possible outcome. In either case, we develop qualities
sequentially. We organize our mesocycles to develop our weaknesses or
move closer to our peak.
The mesocycle represents that quality and, therefore, the plan. The time it
takes to develop the quality that is relevant to the goal is contingent upon

质量与其他因素相互关联，理解这一点是发展质量的关键。
将一种品质叠加在另一种品质之上是一门艺术。 实现中周期的无缝
过渡需要了解这种质量给我们带来了什么及其与更大目标的相关性。
我们需要经验，知道要拥有更大的东西，我们需要开发我们还没有的东
西。 它要求我们必须建立相应素质的基础才能实现目标。还存在从一
个中周期到下一个中周期逐渐变化的方面，以允许持续发展。

我们需要通过从一个中周期进展到下一个中周期来展示创造力，但同
时，我们需要结构和纪律。从一个中周期到下一个中周期的转变是运动
员身体能力的转变。 这种身体变化创造了一个新的平台来利用下一个
训练块的焦点。 Matveyev (Kruger, 2016) 使用传统的线性形式的周期化
创建了这个框架（参见第 200 页的图 12.2）。 项building a base由高音
量和低强度与低音量和高强度交替表示。 整个周期结构的前提是，我
们需要具备基础能力才能完成其他事情。 这源于 Selye 的一般适应综合
症（Seyle，1950）。发展一种品质取决于身体积极应对压力的能力。

分期的本质是计划。 我们正在开辟一条道路，希望它是实现我们目
标的最线性方向。我们沿着这条道路培养品质。 如果计划得当，这些
品质中的每一个都会对下一个品质产生积极的影响。 随着每一项品质
的发展，我们都增加了实现这一目标的潜力。 质量发展是我们进步的
标杆。规划可以基于将弱点转化为优势，或者通过逆向工程获得最佳结
果。 无论哪种情况，我们都会按顺序培养品质。 我们组织中周期来发
展我们的弱点或接近我们的巅峰。
中周期代表了这种质量，因此也代表了计划。开发与目标相关的质量
所需的时间取决于

how long it takes to develop. How much it matters relative to the goal is also
significant. If the goal was to run faster, then we should have more
mesocycles that focus on developing power and velocity. We should have
mesocycles that are longer and more frequent based on their importance.
Another aspect of mesocycles is that they give physical boundaries to
progressive overload. The length of the mesocycle gives the window during
which we can progressively overload. If it is a 2-week mesocycle, we have 2
weeks to progressively overload. The length of the mesocycle dictates the
rate and amount of progressive overload. This is significant because people
going through the program may or may not be able to handle faster rates of
progressive overload. We want to squeeze as much from each mesocycle as
possible, but not at the expense of being able to recover from a fast rate or
high quantity of change. We need to be strategic with how long and how we
load each block to maximize the development of each quality.
Above all else, remember that a mesocycle is a collection of microcycles,
which is a collection of training sessions, which is a collection of exercises,
sets, and reps. It may feel overwhelming to plan the perfect sequence of
mesocycles, but remember, they are just simple, repeatable parts. The
organization of mesocycle order and focus pales in comparison to the
execution of each training session. We can have a bad program and execute it
well and be successful. We cannot have a good program executed poorly and
do well.

Mesocycle Length
One thing we know is that a mesocycle will take at least 2 weeks to
accommodate progressive overload. That part is a given; the other end of the
length of a mesocycle is a bit more nuanced. We have to consider many
variables and factors that make the length of a mesocycle a complex subject.

Training Age
The first factor to consider is training age. Less experienced athletes will
need longer mesocycles. At the top of the list of reasons is that they are
inexperienced and less aware of what will happen. We discussed with novice
trainees that most of their adaptation will be neurological, which can lead to a

开发需要多长时间。它相对于目标的重要性也很重要。 如果目标是跑
得更快，那么我们应该有更多专注于发展力量和速度的中循环。 根据
其重要性，我们应该有更长、更频繁的中周期。
中周期的另一个方面是它们为渐进式超负荷提供了物理界限。 中周
期的长度给了我们可以逐渐超载的窗口。如果是两周的中周期，我们有
两周的时间逐渐超负荷。 中周期的长度决定了渐进超负荷的速率和量
。 这很重要，因为参加该计划的人可能能够也可能无法处理更快的渐
进超负荷率。 我们希望从每个中周期中榨取尽可能多的资源，但不能
以从快速或大量变化中恢复为代价。我们需要对加载每个块的时间和方
式进行战略规划，以最大限度地提高每种质量的发展。

最重要的是，请记住，中循环是微循环的集合，微循环是训练课程的
集合，是练习、组数和次数的集合。 计划完美的中周期序列可能会让
人感到不知所措，但请记住，它们只是简单、可重复的部分。 与每次
训练课程的执行相比，中周期顺序和重点的组织相形见绌。我们可以有
一个糟糕的计划，但执行得很好并会取得成功。我们不可能让一个好的
计划执行得不好却做得很好。

介观周期长度
我们知道的一件事是，中周期至少需要两周的时间来适应逐渐超负荷。
这部分是给定的；中周期长度的另一端有点微妙。 我们必须考虑许多
变量和因素，使中周期的长度成为一个复杂的主题。

训练年龄
首先要考虑的因素是训练年龄。 经验不足的运动员将需要更长的中周
期。 首要原因是他们缺乏经验并且不太了解将会发生什么。我们与新
手学员讨论，他们的大部分适应将是神经方面的，这可能会导致

rapid ramp in terms of progressive overload; this is not a good strategy with
longer mesocycles. A huge spike in training loads from the previous week
might not take into consideration the motor learning aspect. The pattern is not
ingrained with such minimal exposure, and we are using a pretense of
adaptation. A psychological bump from having multiple weeks of
improvement can lead to a long-term appreciation of strength training. A
freshman stacking up wins every week for multiple weeks is incredibly
underrated for developing confidence.
We see massive changes in novice athletes with a new training program.
This can lead to fast rates and high amounts of progressive overload,
resulting in a shorter mesocycle. If we look at mesocycles of 2 to 8 weeks, we
have a median of 4 weeks. So anything less than 4 weeks is short, and
anything above 4 weeks is long. A general rule to abide by is that the less
exposure an athlete has, the longer the mesocycle. This means we need to
temper huge spikes in training loads with novices to make it past 4 weeks. If
we do not discourage huge spikes in training load, we may not reach past 4
weeks, which is why we need to control week-to-week progressive overload.
We are looking for a 1% to 10% progressive overload from microcycle to
microcycle. The median progressive overload is 5%, so anything below 5% is
a small change, and anything above 5% is a large change. For longer
mesocycles, greater than 4 weeks, we need a smaller progressive overload,
less than 5%. For shorter mesocycles, less than 4 weeks, we need larger
progressive overload, greater than 5% (figure 19.1).

逐渐超载方面的快速斜坡；对于较长的中周期，这不是一个好的策略。
前一周训练负荷的大幅增加可能没有考虑到运动学习方面。这种模式并
没有在如此少的曝光下根深蒂固，我们正在假装适应。 数周的进步所
带来的心理冲击可以导致对力量训练的长期欣赏。 一个连续几周每周
都取得胜利的新生对于培养信心来说是被严重低估的。

我们看到新手运动员在新的训练计划中发生了巨大的变化。这可能导
致速率加快和大量渐进式超负荷，从而导致中周期缩短。如果我们观察
2 至 8 周的中周期，则中位数为 4 周。 因此，少于 4 周的时间为短时间
，超过 4 周的时间为长时间。 需要遵守的一般规则是，运动员接触的
暴露越少，中周期就越长。 这意味着我们需要缓和新手训练负荷的巨
大峰值，以使其能够度过 4 周。如果我们不阻止训练负荷大幅增加，我
们可能无法达到过去 4 周，这就是为什么我们需要控制每周的渐进式超
负荷。我们正在寻找从一个微周期到另一个微周期 1% 到 10% 的渐进超
载。渐进超载的中位数为 5%，因此低于 5% 的任何内容都是小变化，
高于 5% 的任何内容都是大变化。 对于较长的中周期（超过 4 周），
我们需要较小的渐进超负荷（小于 5%）。 对于较短的中周期（少于 4
周），我们需要更大的渐进超负荷，大于 5%（图 19.1）。

FIGURE 19.1 Mesocycle loading.
If we have short mesocycles regardless of training experience, we can only
allow for larger jumps. This also has to be considered. We need to start
heavier in the earlier weeks because we have little time. Having 2-week
mesocycles means we only have 2 weeks to attain the adaptation from that
period. We typically reserve shorter mesocycles for more advanced athletes,
who will have a greater familiarity with exercises and adequate training
loads. What this means is we can get right to the point by loading up week 1
heavier than if we were going with a 4-week mesocycle.
Does this mean that we only use shorter training blocks with advanced
athletes and longer ones with novices? The answer to that is no. We can make
a general rule, such as athletes with less than 1 year of experience need 6 to 8
week mesocycles; those with less than 2 years, 4 to 6 week mesocycles; and
those with greater than 2 years, 2 to 4 week mesocycles (see figure 12.7 on
page 210). But there will always be exceptions, such as schedules or
amplification in terms of volume, intensity, or density training blocks that
don’t allow for longer mesocycles.

图 19.1 中循环加载。
如果无论训练经验如何，我们的中周期都很短，我们只能允许更大的
跳跃。 这也必须考虑。 我们需要在前几周开始增加重量，因为我们的
时间很少。 有两周的中周期意味着我们只有两周的时间来适应该时期
。 我们通常为更高级的运动员保留较短的中周期，他们将更熟悉练习
和足够的训练负荷。这意味着我们可以通过在第一周增加比 4 周中周期
更重的负载来切入主题。
这是否意味着我们只对高级运动员使用较短的训练块，对新手使用较
长的训练块？答案是否定的。我们可以制定一个通用的规则，比如经验
不足1年的运动员需要6到8周的中周期；中周期少于 2 年、4 至 6 周的；
以及中周期超过 2 年、2 至 4 周的那些（参见第 210 页的图 12.7）。 但
总会有例外，例如在容量、强度或密度训练块方面的日程安排或放大，
不允许更长的中周期。

Muscle Fiber Type
We also need to consider muscle fiber type when discussing mesocycle
length. A faster-twitch muscle fiber type will respond at a higher degree than
a slower-twitch muscle fiber type, which means that our mesocycles will be
shorter for fast-twitch fibers because of their more rapid adaptation, but more
importantly, their rate of fatigue. We can view more frequent mesocycle
changes as a means to respond to faster adaptation rates, or we can view them
as a means to get a more frequent drop in intensity, volume, or density.
Regardless of how long a mesocycle is, week 1 will always be the lightest of
the new mesocycle. This is a period of supercompensation.
More frequent mesocycle change allows for more exercise variation
within a macrocycle. By changing the mesocycle more often, we change the
exercises we use more often. We can stack more variations within an offseason period by changing the mesocycle more frequently. There is a catch
here; we run the risk of limiting adaptation by changing too quickly. If we are
choosing between variation and adaptation, it is always adaptation.

Concentrated Volume or Intensity
The last piece for mesocycle length is amplified volume, intensity, and
density. We respond to a huge spike in training load by shortening the period
during which it occurs. We talked about the optimal range of 0.8 to 1.3, with
a workload based on the rating of perceived exertion. That window of
workload is a good rule of thumb for training intensity, volume, or density.
We should not see a spike above 15% in any of the variables without some
amendment to mesocycle length. The larger the spike, the shorter the
mesocycle length.
The other consideration is that we may have athletes on different
mesocycles from different timelines. This is a potential problem if we do not
address it. We could have a deload week the same week as a performance
week. The simultaneous peaking and adapting create a paradoxical
environment. As a coach, you need to anticipate and address the potential
pressure associated with an athlete in an environment that is not congruent
with the timing of their mesocycle.

肌纤维类型
在讨论中周期长度时，我们还需要考虑肌纤维类型。快肌纤维类型的反
应程度高于慢肌纤维类型，这意味着快肌纤维的中周期会更短，因为它
们的适应速度更快，但更重要的是它们的疲劳率。 我们可以将更频繁
的中周期变化视为响应更快适应速率的一种手段，或者我们可以将它们
视为获得更频繁的强度、体积或密度下降的手段。无论中周期有多长，
第一周始终是新中周期中最轻的一周。这是一个超补偿期。

更频繁的中周期变化允许在宏观周期内有更多的运动变化。通过更频
繁地改变中周期，我们改变了更经常使用的练习。 我们可以通过更频
繁地改变中周期来在淡季期间叠加更多的变化。 这里有一个问题；我
们面临着改变太快而限制适应的风险。如果我们在变异和适应之间做出
选择，那么它总是适应。

集中训练量或强度
中周期长度的最后一部分是放大的体积、强度和密度。我们通过缩短训
练负荷发生的时间来应对训练负荷的大幅增加。我们讨论了 0.8 到 1.3
的最佳范围，工作量基于感知努力程度的评级。 该工作量窗口是训练
强度、训练量或密度的良好经验法则。如果不对中周期长度进行一些修
改，我们不应该看到任何变量的峰值超过 15%。 尖峰越大，介观周期
长度越短。
另一个考虑因素是，我们可能有来自不同时间线的不同中周期的运动
员。如果我们不解决这个问题，这将是一个潜在的问题。 我们可以在
表演周的同一周安排一个减载周。 峰值和适应的同时发生创造了一个
矛盾的环境。 作为教练，您需要预测并解决运动员在与中周期时间不
一致的环境中所面临的潜在压力。

The weight room organization matters a great deal in this potential
situation. Isolating certain athletes on a specific program can hold significant
value for coordinating multiple programs, which can work against you at the
same time. The social impact of having a team working together in a singular
program can be empowering. Dividing the group can potentially mean
diluting the enthusiasm and energy. You have to be equally skilled in
organizing your training program as you are in programming it.
The simplest solution is to empower your coaches to control their energy.
They are the catalysts of energy. At the same time, they are the gateway to
controlling the amount of energy we emit. Coaches have the power to limit
the rate and amount of entropy in a weight room. Empower them to do so.
Give them the reins on the particular program with a specified group. You
want to have multiple programs running simultaneously to accommodate
individual differences; to do so, you need to allow facilitators to facilitate.

Mesocycle Organization
Once we determine the length of the mesocycle, we have to determine how to
organize the block. There is a concept of deloading to allow for adaptation. A
reduction in volume, intensity, or density is necessary to allow the quality we
are overreaching to manifest. When and where we place that deload can
greatly affect performance.

Deloading
First, we have an organic deload at the beginning of each new mesocycle. We
progress each week from that first week. This serves multiple purposes. The
first is to recover the previous mesocycle, and the second is to acclimate to
the new mesocycle. We are simultaneously adapting and assimilating. We are
recovering from a previous stimulus and responding to a new stimulus.
This onset of a mesocycle does not vary. The question of how quickly we
need to deload again is much more difficult to answer. The length of the
mesocycle will be anywhere from 2 to 8 weeks, with shorter mesocycles for
more advanced, faster-twitch athletes and longer mesocycles for novice,
slower-twitch athletes. So we will deload more frequently for advanced,
faster-twitch athletes.

在这种潜在情况下，举重室的组织非常重要。将某些运动员隔离在特
定项目上对于协调多个项目具有重要价值，但同时也会对您产生不利影
响。让一个团队在一个单一的项目中一起工作可以产生强大的社会影响
。 分裂团队可能意味着削弱热情和精力。 您必须像编程一样熟练地组
织培训计划。
最简单的解决方案是让你的教练能够控制他们的精力。它们是能量的
催化剂。 同时，它们也是控制我们排放的能量的门户。 教练有权限制
举重室中熵的速率和数量。 授权他们这样做。让他们对特定组的特定
程序进行控制。 您希望多个程序同时运行以适应个体差异；为此，您
需要让协调人提供协助。

中循环组织
一旦我们确定了中周期的长度，我们就必须确定如何组织块。有一个卸
载的概念以允许适应。体积、强度或密度的减少对于让我们过度追求的
质量得以体现是必要的。 我们何时何地进行卸载会极大地影响性能。

卸货
首先，我们在每个新的中周期开始时都有一个有机的减载。从第一周开
始，我们每周都在进步。这有多种目的。一是恢复之前的中周期，二是
适应新的中周期。我们同时在适应和同化。我们正在从之前的刺激中恢
复过来，并对新的刺激做出反应。
中周期的开始没有变化。我们需要多快再次卸载的问题更加难以回答
。 中周期的长度为 2 至 8 周，对于更高级、快速肌动的运动员来说，
中周期较短，而对于新手、慢速肌动的运动员来说，中周期较长。 因
此，对于高级、抽搐更快的运动员，我们会更频繁地进行减重。

With longer mesocycles, we may need to deload within that period to
facilitate constant development. If we are conducting 8 weeks of
uninterrupted training without a change in methods or protocols, we may
require a period of reduction. You could argue we should change mesocycles
at this period, but this could come at the expense of quality or the exercise we
are trying to develop. Using a strategic deload instead of changing the
mesocycle can potentially lead to a greater level of adaptation. Figure 19.2
provides an example of an in-season mesocycle.
We have two formats for a mesocycle: traditional and performance (Kenn,
2003). Each week is categorized as a specific development feature. We have
the deload week, during which we decrease one variable by 5% to 30%.
Next, we have a base week, during which we introduce the exercises, sets,
reps, intensity, and density of a new mesocycle to build upon. Next, we have
a load week or weeks to build up from a base or deload week through some
form of progressive overload. Last, we have a performance week, during
which we are at our peak in terms of the selected methods and protocols we
have chosen.

随着中周期的延长，我们可能需要在这段时间内进行减载以促进持续
发展。 如果我们进行 8 周不间断的训练而不改变方法或方案，我们可
能需要一段时间的减少。你可能会说我们应该在这个时期改变中周期，
但这可能会以牺牲质量或我们正在尝试开发的练习为代价。 使用战略
性减载而不是改变中周期可能会导致更高水平的适应。 图 19.2 提供了
季节性中周期的示例。
我们有两种中循环形式：传统形式和性能形式（Kenn，2003）。每
周都被归类为特定的开发功能。我们有减载周，在此期间我们将一个变
量减少 5% 到 30%。接下来，我们有一个基础周，在此期间我们介绍了
新中周期的练习、组数、次数、强度和密度。接下来，我们有一个或数
周的负荷周，从基础周或减负荷周开始，通过某种形式的渐进超负荷进
行积累。 最后，我们有一个绩效周，在此期间，我们在所选方法和协
议方面处于巅峰状态。

Traditional Mesocycle
One progression is what Kenn (2003) would refer to as a traditional
mesocycle. With a traditional mesocycle, we progress from a base microcycle
(relative to 70%, 10-12 reps in reserve), load microcycle (relative to 80%,

The thing about traditional mesocycles (figure 19.4) is that they are
intuitive for novice trainees. Each week, you are going to progressively
overload, which makes sense. Showing a gradual arc throughout a 4-to-8week period is a clear visual for everyone to follow. Explaining throughout
the mesocycle that it will get gradually heavier, longer, or more difficult is
easier to process. Your lightest week, which will serve as your deload week,
is easier to convey. Your best chance to be successful is to have something
your athletes can figure out on their own. From there, you focus on
encouraging them to execute and perform at their best.

传统中循环（图 19.4）的特点是它们对于新手来说很直观。 每个星
期，你都会逐渐超负荷，这是有道理的。 在 4 到 8 周的时间内呈现出
渐进的弧线，是每个人都可以遵循的清晰视觉效果。 在整个中周期中
解释它会逐渐变得更重、更长或更困难更容易处理。你最轻松的一周，
将作为你的减负周，更容易传达。 获得成功的最佳机会是拥有运动员
可以自己解决的问题。 从那里开始，您专注于鼓励他们执行并发挥最
佳水平。

Performance Mesocycle
The primary difference between a traditional cycle and a performance cycle
is the placement of the deload week (figure 19.5). With the traditional cycle,
we use a base week as a deload. With the performance cycle, we drop the
base week and put in a deload week later in the mesocycle. We want to be
careful not to have too steep a drop-off after the first two loading weeks. The
idea is to have a week of recovery to facilitate better recovery for the
performance week. This style of mesocycle is better for more advanced
athletes with more familiarity with a method or protocol and who can start
with a load week. That familiarity allows for heavier loading earlier, which
can increase the rate of fatigue.
The deload week is an art as much as it is a science. It will feel
counterintuitive for an athlete to reduce weight, which is why you will need
to focus on volume or density. This works in our favor because we want to
focus on restoring the nervous system or muscular system but not sabotage
the performance of the rest of the mesocycle. We can easily accomplish this
by maintaining intensity and dropping volume. We can drop volume by
cutting sets or resting more between sets. (For a visual example, see figure
11.7 on page 195). This approach will accommodate the feeling of training
hard and competing with their teammates while recovering from the loadingbased microcycles.

性能中循环
传统周期和性能周期之间的主要区别在于卸载周的安排（图 19.5）。对
于传统周期，我们使用基准周作为减载。 在性能周期中，我们放弃了
基准周，并在中周期稍后加入了减载周。 我们要小心，不要在前两周
装载周后出现急剧下降。我们的想法是有一周的恢复时间，以促进表现
周更好的恢复。 这种中周期风格更适合更熟悉方法或方案并且可以从
负荷周开始的更高级运动员。 这种熟悉感允许更早地承受更大的负荷
，这会增加疲劳率。

减负周既是一门艺术，也是一门科学。 对于运动员来说，减轻体重
会感觉违反直觉，这就是为什么你需要关注体积或密度。 这对我们有
利，因为我们希望专注于恢复神经系统或肌肉系统，但不破坏中周期其
余部分的表现。我们可以通过保持强度和降低训练量来轻松实现这一点
。 我们可以通过减少组数或在组间休息更多来减少训练量。 （有关视
觉示例，请参见第 195 页的图 11.7）。 这种方法将适应刻苦训练和与
队友竞争的感觉，同时从基于负荷的微循环中恢复。

The last consideration is the calendar for the team you are working with.
An argument can be made that we do not need deload weeks, given the many
stoppages in the training schedule already. Discretionary weeks, spring break,
the 4th of July, winter break, or long weekends are all things we cannot
avoid. If it’s the part of the year where we never have 4 weeks consecutively,
we should avoid using a deload or base microcycle. However, if we have 8
weeks or more, as with spring sports in the fall, we should consider
traditional or performance cycles with deload and base weeks.

Mesocycle Progression
The last piece of the mesocycle puzzle is how we progress from one
mesocycle to the next. What is the appropriate transition of exercises along
with the ideal change in our variables from one mesocycle to the next?

Exercise Progression
Starting with exercises, we should have an idea of what to do based on the
principle of progression. The trajectory should progress from the off-season,
moving closer to preseason and competition with the completion of each
training session. As we get closer to competition, we should have exercises
more specific to the competition. These can be specific exercise selections in
which we are trying to mirror the actions in competition. You can choose
exercises that facilitate training-specific qualities that we are looking to peak
for competition. They can be exercises that come from trying to develop a
weakness into a strength over the off-season.
Specific exercises are interesting. There is an optimal technique for certain
actions within sports. Optimal is based on the outcome; the better player has
the better technique. Optimal technique also has an element of efficiency and
repeatability under pressure or challenging circumstances. We can break this
down into isolated actions of the joints associated with the specific movement
pattern. We load a specific joint action, for instance, external rotation of the
shoulder with throwing. Or we can load the pattern, for instance, a split
stance rotational chop and lift, by swinging a bat. What exercises are best is
largely based on a conversation with the athlete, the position coach, athletic
trainers, and the physical therapist on staff.

最后要考虑的是与您合作的团队的日历。可以说，鉴于训练计划中已
经出现了多次停顿，我们不需要减负周。自由周、春假、7 月 4 日、寒
假或长周末都是我们无法避免的事情。如果一年中我们从来没有连续 4
周的时间，我们应该避免使用减载或基础微循环。 然而，如果我们有 8
周或更长的时间，就像秋季的春季运动一样，我们应该考虑传统的或具
有减负荷和基础周的表现周期。

中周期进展
中周期难题的最后一块是我们如何从一个中周期进展到下一个中周期。
练习的适当过渡以及变量从一个中周期到下一个周期的理想变化是什么
？

运动进展
从练习开始，我们应该按照循序渐进的原则知道该怎么做。 随着每次
训练课程的完成，轨迹应该从休赛期开始，逐渐接近季前赛和比赛。
随着比赛的临近，我们应该进行更有针对性的练习。这些可以是特定的
练习选择，我们试图在其中反映比赛中的动作。 您可以选择有助于促
进我们希望在比赛中达到峰值的训练特定素质的练习。 它们可以是在
休赛期尝试将弱点变成优势的练习。

具体的练习很有趣。体育运动中的某些动作有一个最佳技术。最佳是
基于结果；更好的球员有更好的技术。最佳技术还具有在压力或挑战性
环境下的效率和可重复性的要素。我们可以将其分解为与特定运动模式
相关的关节的孤立动作。 我们加载特定的联合动作，例如投掷时肩部
的外旋。 或者我们可以加载模式，例如，通过挥动球棒来进行分步旋
转劈砍和举起。 哪种练习最好，很大程度上取决于与运动员、位置教
练、运动训练师和工作人员的物理治疗师的对话。

Alternatively, we can consider choosing exercises that peak for qualities
relative to competition. Certain exercises allow for greater expression of
qualities than others. If we are trying to peak in terms of force through
relative strength, we will need to use exercises that are more stable and
familiar. A front squat with a barbell in this situation would be better served
than a split stance holding on to a water bag. Understanding the assignment
and then choosing exercises based on their connection to the quality we are
trying to develop is the goal here.

或者，我们可以考虑选择相对于比赛而言质量达到最高水平的练习。
某些练习比其他练习更能表达品质。 如果我们试图通过相对力量达到
力量峰值，我们将需要使用更稳定和熟悉的练习。在这种情况下，用杠
铃进行前蹲比握着水袋的分体站姿效果更好。 理解作业，然后根据它
们与我们试图培养的质量的联系来选择练习是这里的目标。

FIGURE 19.6 Example of an off-season mesocycle.
With exercise selection, if we need to accrue many variations, we can
leverage shorter mesocycles. Team sports that are played within open
environments with low-constraint tasks need a wide range of exercise
variation. Performing more mesocycles during the off-season can allow for
more variety and the ability to get more specific. We can leverage that to

图 19.6 淡季中周期的示例。
通过运动选择，如果我们需要积累多种变化，我们可以利用较短的中
周期。 在开放环境中进行低约束任务的团队运动需要广泛的运动变化
。 在淡季进行更多的中循环可以允许更多的多样性和变得更具体的能
力。 我们可以利用它来

develop a broad range of qualities as well. The caveat is that this is for more
advanced athletes who are more familiar with foundational movements and
can adapt to more frequent changes. A novice can limit their development
from too much variety.

Variable Progression
Progressing variables is another important consideration. We are looking to
have a gradual transition of volume, intensity, and density to capitalize on the
previous mesocycle. Too much of a change can limit the ability in the next
mesocycle. If we have a huge spike or drop in volume, we cannot use as
much intensity from either fatigue or lack of exposure to higher intensity. The
same can be said for high spikes or drops in intensity. A gradual change is
somewhere in the range of 5% to 15% change for volume, intensity, or
density.
Implementing this progression with volume, we must look at the peak and
average volume used. For instance, we can use a high-volume program like
10 sets × 10 reps (100 reps). A raised intensity is natural in the next block,
but going to a protocol of wave loading (3, 2, 1, 3, 2, 1) would be a drop in
volume of 94 reps. You are setting the athlete up to fail by not having a more
gradual transition. The peak of 100 to 6 is too much of a drop. The average of
10 to 2 is also too much of a drop. We need a much higher volume following
the 10 sets × 10 reps mesocycle, or if we planned on doing 3, 2, 1, 3, 2, 1, do
a different mesocycle beforehand.
For intensity, 10 reps would be 75% RM (rep max), which would
transition to potentially 95% RM for one rep. The peak intensity is too much
relative to the next block. There is an art to going from one mesocycle to the
next in terms of building a crescendo of volume, intensity, and exercise
selection. Programming is about seeing the full picture. We want to increase
the variables that most correlate to our sport. Understanding when and how
much requires seeing the entire picture relative to what we can execute. A
better progression would be doing 85% RM for six reps for no less than six
sets. We can titrate up the time under tension to close the gap from 100 reps
to 36 reps, increasing the total volume by increasing the time of each rep and
set.

还培养广泛的素质。需要注意的是，这适用于更熟悉基础动作并且能够
适应更频繁变化的更高级运动员。 太多的多样性可能会限制新手的发
展。

可变进展
进展变量是另一个重要的考虑因素。 我们希望利用之前的中周期，实
现体积、强度和密度的逐渐转变。 太多的变化会限制下一个中周期的
能力。 如果我们的训练量大幅上升或下降，我们就无法使用尽可能多
的强度，因为疲劳或缺乏较高强度的暴露。对于强度的高峰值或下降也
是如此。 渐进变化是指体积、强度或密度发生 5% 到 15% 的变化。

通过音量实现这种级数，我们必须查看所使用的峰值和平均音量。
例如，我们可以使用大容量计划，例如 10 组 × 10 次（100 次）。 在下
一个区块中，强度的提高是很自然的，但如果采用波浪加载协议（3、2
、1、3、2、1），则训练量会下降 94 次。如果你没有进行更渐进的过
渡，你就会让运动员失败。 100到6的峰值，下降幅度太大了。平均10比
2也降幅太大了。在 10 组 × 10 次中观循环之后，我们需要更高的训练
量，或者如果我们计划进行 3、2、1、3、2、1，请提前进行不同的中观
循环。
对于强度，10 次重复将是 75% RM（最大重复次数），这将过渡到 1
次重复的潜在 95% RM。峰值强度相对于下一个块太多。从一个中周期
过渡到下一个中周期是一门艺术，需要逐渐增加训练量、强度和运动选
择。编程就是要看到全局。我们希望增加与我们的运动最相关的变量。
了解何时以及多少需要了解与我们可以执行的内容相关的整个情况。
更好的进展是在不少于六组的六次重复中完成 85% RM。我们可以滴定
紧张状态下的时间，将差距从 100 次缩短到 36 次，通过增加每次重复
和组数的时间来增加总训练量。

We need to consider the previous mesocycle and future mesocycle length.
The longer the mesocycle, the less the overall change. Shorter mesocycles
require more drastic changes. If we have an 8-week-long mesocycle, it will
have a smaller change in volume, intensity, or density than the next
mesocycle. The development of the quality we focused on in the preceding
mesocycle still needs time to settle. Keeping the total change under 5%
allows for a more gradual progression of quality that was just recently
obtained.
Moderate mesocycles of 4 weeks can tolerate upward of 10% change.
Short mesocycles of 2 weeks can tolerate upward of 15% change. The
athletes who are using short to moderate mesocycles are more developed in
the exercise motor pattern and the quality being developed. A more
pronounced change from one mesocycle to the next is better tolerated (figure
19.7).
The biggest and most important aspect of a mesocycle is whether it can
facilitate constant development toward our overall goal. If we have too long a
mesocycle, we may not be able to have enough variation with qualities and
exercise selection. If we have too short a mesocycle, we may not be able to
develop the quality in the way we want to. In mesocycles both too long and
too short, the burden then is placed on the progression of mesocycles.
Mesocycles that are longer than they have to be will require a sharp change in
loading to the next one to compensate for the lack of change previously. The
opposite is true for mesocycles that are shorter than needed; the change is too
gradual to compensate. You will not know whether your mesocycle is too
short or too long until you are well into the next mesocycle because you will
not be able to progressively overload.
The answer to all this is to start with the rep and work out from there. Can
we execute each rep with the prescribed technique and the loading parameters
we set to reach our overall goal? If we can, we have found the right
mesocycle length, organization, and progression. You are not an oracle, and
you cannot predict the future, but you can see what is in front of you as good
or not good and work from there.

我们需要考虑之前的中周期和未来的中周期长度。中周期越长，总体
变化越小。 较短的中周期需要更剧烈的变化。 如果我们有一个为期 8
周的中周期，那么它的体积、强度或密度变化将比下一个中周期小。
上一个中周期我们重点关注的质量发展还需要时间沉淀。 将总变化保
持在 5% 以下，可以实现最近获得的质量的更渐进的进步。

4 周的中等中周期可以承受 10% 以上的变化。 2 周的短中周期可以承
受 15% 以上的变化。 使用短至中周期的运动员在运动运动模式和质量
方面更加发达。 从一个中周期到下一个中周期的更明显的变化更容易
被容忍（图 19.7）。
中周期最大、最重要的一个方面是能否促进我们的总体目标不断发展
。如果我们的中周期太长，我们可能无法在素质和运动选择上有足够的
变化。 如果我们的中周期太短，我们可能无法按照我们想要的方式发
展质量。 在中周期太长和太短的情况下，负担就会落在中周期的进展
上。比实际长度更长的中循环将需要对下一个中循环的负载进行急剧变
化，以补偿之前变化的不足。对于短于所需的中周期来说，情况正好相
反。这种变化太渐进，无法弥补。 在进入下一个中周期之前，您不会
知道中周期是否太短或太长，因为您将无法逐渐超载。

所有这一切的答案是从代表开始，然后从那里开始解决。我们可以使
用规定的技术和我们设置的负载参数来执行每个代表以达到我们的总体
目标吗？ 如果可以的话，我们就已经找到了正确的中周期长度、组织
和进程。 你不是神谕，你无法预测未来，但你可以看到你面前的事情
是好是坏，并从那里开始工作。

FIGURE 19.7 Mesocycle progression.

Take Home
The mesocycle is the time representation of the quality we are trying to
develop. If we plan our mesocycles correctly in terms of the length,
organization, and progression, we should be able to develop any quality we
set out to develop. Featuring a quality we are trying to develop is a piece of
the overall puzzle. If we can execute each microcycle and training session
within that mesocycle, we can develop the quality. It requires dual planning
and coaching; we need to be good at both.

图 19.7 中周期进程。

带回家
中周期是我们正在努力开发的质量的时间表示。 如果我们在长度、组
织和进展方面正确规划中周期，我们应该能够发展我们想要发展的任何
品质。 我们正在努力开发的品质是整个难题的一部分。 如果我们能够
在中周期内执行每个微周期和培训课程，我们就可以提高质量。 它需
要双重规划和指导；我们需要两方面都擅长。

MACROCYCLE DESIGN
We are here, finally! Now we can put all this together into a cohesive plan
that will empower us to get the result of increased performance along with a
decreased rate of injury. I must warn you that everything discussed will be a
review. We have gone through periodization with our physiology rules; this
will be periodization in practice. This chapter is about how to approach
planning and organizing your macrocycle.
We are going to arrange some workflows to organize your annual
calendar. Think of each step in this process as your map for getting through
the year. Your periodization template serves as your guide in traversing
through your off-season, into preseason, into competition, and finally into
postseason. Each step will bring its own set of problems and setbacks. Think
of your periodization calendar as a tool to keep you on track.
Above all, think of how you are going to execute each training session.
That is the bottom line. We can say some clichéd things, such as “every
journey begins with the first step” or “we are the product of what we
repeatedly do, so excellence is a habit.” But the truth is that these are clichés
because they are true. We cannot have the outcome without engaging in the
process that produces the outcome. We need to be able to see the long-term
plan combined with being present and accountable for the short-term
executable actions. Figure 20.1 provides a blank macrocycle template to start
from.

大循环设计
我们终于来了！ 现在我们可以将所有这些整合到一个有凝聚力的计划
中，这将使我们能够提高表现并降低受伤率。我必须警告您，讨论的所
有内容都将是回顾。 我们已经按照生理规则经历了分期； 这将是实践
中的分期。 本章介绍如何规划和组织宏观周期。
我们将安排一些工作流程来组织您的年度日历。 将此过程中的每一
步视为您度过这一年的地图。 您的分期模板可作为您穿越休赛期、季
前赛、比赛、最后进入季后赛的指南。每一步都会带来一系列问题和挫
折。将分期日历视为让您步入正轨的工具。
最重要的是，考虑一下您将如何执行每次培训课程。这是底线。 我
们可以说一些陈词滥调，比如“每一段旅程都从第一步开始”或者“我
们是反复做事的产物，所以卓越是一种习惯”。但事实是，这些都是陈
词滥调，因为它们是真实的。 如果不参与产生结果的过程，我们就无
法获得结果。 我们需要能够看到长期计划，同时对短期可执行行动负
责。图 20.1 提供了一个空白的宏循环模板作为起点。

Step 1: Working Forward or Backward?
This step is critical for a periodization plan. You need to determine whether
you are going to work forward or backward. Working forward means
developing weaknesses, either physiologically or biomechanically, into
strengths. Working backward means building your entire plan around
developing qualities or movement patterns that are specific to the athlete’s
sport or position.
There is no right or wrong way to go about this. My advice is to be
flexible with how you approach this. Regardless of your choice here, you
need to start with a baseline assessment. Determining your biomechanical
limitations will determine your exercises and how you progress, either to the
end or from the beginning. If you find a lot of range of motion restrictions,
movement asymmetries, or structural imbalances, chances are you will need
to work forward. You have a lowered ceiling from a smaller exercise
inventory that you will need to address. Your exercise selection will be
regressed to what the athlete can do based on their limitations. The restricted
exercise list will have a direct impact on your ability to program certain
methods and protocols.

FIGURE 20.1 Blank macrocycle.

第一步：向前还是向后？
此步骤对于分期计划至关重要。 您需要确定是要向前还是向后工作。
向前努力意味着将生理上或生物力学上的弱点转化为优势。 逆向工作
意味着围绕发展针对运动员的运动或位置的素质或运动模式制定整个计
划。
解决这个问题的方法没有正确或错误之分。 我的建议是灵活处理这
个问题。 无论您在这里做出什么选择，您都需要从基线评估开始。 确
定您的生物力学限制将决定您的练习以及您的进展方式，无论是到最后
还是从头开始。 如果您发现很多运动范围受限、运动不对称或结构不
平衡，您很可能需要继续努力。 您需要解决的锻炼清单较小，因此您
的上限较低。 您的运动选择将根据运动员的限制回归到他们可以做的
事情。限制练习列表将直接影响您对某些方法和协议进行编程的能力。

图 20.1 空白宏周期。

If you find that the athlete is a blank canvas of movement and has no
obvious limitations, you will need to understand their physiology. Their
current functional level, from a biological and training age, affects how long
we need to stay with a current mesocycle and structure our microcycles. We
need to compare their relative biomotor ability (velocity, power, force, work)
and their bioenergetic ability (phosphagen, glycolytic, oxidative systems). If
the athlete has a poor ability in any of the biomotor or bioenergetic aspects of
performance unrelated to their sport or position, you will more than likely
have to work forward. The athlete’s inability to recover from training will be
the limiting factor to peaking for specific qualities. That diminished capacity
to recover takes precedence over everything else.
If you find they have a high training age and are predominantly fast-twitch
athletes, you will need shorter mesocycles. This will affect exercise
progressions and variable selection. If you find biomechanical constraints do
not limit them and they can move through a full range of motion without
asymmetry, you have a wide array of exercises you can use and progress
more rapidly. In this case, you will want to work backward from a specific
peak. Without biomechanical or physiological restrictions, you shift focus to
the end, from the beginning not being as limited.

Reverse Engineering an Outcome
You can think of it this way: If you are working forward, you are going from
GPP (general physical preparation) to SPP (specific physical preparation).
Working forward pushes SPP to the forms of preseason and competition.
Preseason is coming; there is no changing that. The only difference for you is
how you align your training to best prepare for it by reducing limiting factors.
If you have to fix a lot of things, you have to spend time during the offseason addressing them. Alternatively, if you are working backward, you are
going from SPP to GPP. Specific physical preparation starts earlier than
preseason when you are working backward because you do not have as many
limiting factors. You will still develop general qualities but with less time
allocated to them.

如果您发现运动员的运动是一张空白的画布并且没有明显的限制，那
么您将需要了解他们的生理机能。 从生物和训练年龄来看，它们当前
的功能水平会影响我们需要保持当前中循环和构建微循环的时间。我们
需要比较它们的相对生物运动能力（速度、功率、力量、做功）和生物
能量能力（磷酸原、糖酵解、氧化系统）。 如果运动员在与他们的运
动或位置无关的任何生物运动或生物能量方面的能力较差，那么你很可
能必须继续努力。运动员无法从训练中恢复将成为达到特定素质巅峰的
限制因素。恢复能力的下降比其他一切都更重要。

如果您发现他们的训练年龄很高并且主要是快肌运动员，那么您将需
要较短的中周期。 这将影响锻炼进度和变量选择。如果您发现生物力
学约束并不限制它们，并且它们可以在没有不对称的情况下进行全方位
的运动，那么您可以使用多种练习并更快地进步。 在这种情况下，您
需要从特定峰值开始向后推算。没有生物力学或生理学的限制，你可以
将注意力转移到最后，从一开始就不再受到限制。

逆向工程结果
你可以这样想：如果你正在前进，你就是从GPP（一般身体准备）转向
SPP（特定身体准备）。向前推进将 SPP 推向季前赛和比赛的形式。季
前赛即将到来；这是没有改变的。对您而言，唯一的区别在于如何通过
减少限制因素来调整您的训练，以便为训练做好最佳准备。如果你必须
解决很多问题，你就必须在休赛期花时间来解决它们。或者，如果你逆
向工作，你就会从 SPP 转向 GPP。 当你向后训练时，特定的身体准备
会比季前赛更早开始，因为你没有那么多限制因素。 你仍然会发展一
般素质，但分配给他们的时间会减少。

Premortem
One key aspect of program design is having an objective. There
is an exercise to develop a plan called a premortem. A
premortem represents a vision of what you hope to accomplish.
We have talked a lot about planning, but we have not talked
about the real meaning of a plan.
A plan is a hope for change. Things change when we are tired
of where we are, and we are good enough to do something
about it. The beginning of every off-season is the dawn of a new
hope. It is a feeling that we do not have to accept what has
happened in the past; we can shape our future however we feel
fit.
The first step is having a vision; the second step is laying out
what is needed. A premortem is about having action items that
will help us fulfill our expectations for the next season. More
important than the action items is listing the limiting factors. The
limiting factors serve as speed bumps toward training. They slow
us down, and we need to bulldoze them before we can proceed.
The bulldozer is the way we overcome our limiting factors and
execute the action item.
Example Premortem: Goal: Beat Rival
Action Item: Get Faster
Limiting factor: injury
– Limiting factor bulldozer: prep foam roll, stretch,
hydration
Limiting factor: lifestyle
– Limiting factor bulldozer: sleep, hydration, nutrition
Action item: be conditioned for four quarters
Limiting factor: effort
– Limiting factor bulldozer: competition
Limiting factor: recovery

事前剖析
程序设计的一个关键方面是有一个目标。有一个制定计划的练习
称为 premortem。 事前剖析代表了您希望实现的目标的愿景。我
们谈论了很多关于计划的事情，但是我们没有谈论计划的真正含
义。
计划是改变的希望。当我们厌倦了现状时，事情就会发生变化
，而我们有能力对此做点什么。每一个休赛期的开始都是新希望
的曙光。 这是一种我们不必接受过去发生的事情的感觉；我们可
以以自己认为合适的方式塑造我们的未来。
第一步是有愿景；第二步是列出需要什么。 事前剖析是指制定
行动项目，帮助我们实现对下一赛季的期望。 比行动项目更重要
的是列出限制因素。 这些限制因素成为训练的减速带。它们拖慢
了我们的速度，我们需要用推土机推平它们才能继续前进。推土
机是我们克服限制因素并执行行动项目的方式。

These items will look no different to the athlete, by the way. Their job is
what is in front of them with each rep, each set, each exercise, each training
session, each microcycle, and each mesocycle. Your job is to see the bigger
picture with the entire macrocycle. As a coach, you understand the power of
execution, but that is understood by both coach and athlete relative to the
larger, grander plan. Are you moving closer to the ultimate goal of better
performance with reduced risk for the collective? Is each athlete on that team
performing better with you as their strength coach?
Once you determine if you are working forward or backward, you lay out
your mesocycles. Each mesocycle represents a quality moving from the start
or from the end. If you are working forward, you will want to organize your
qualities to develop your athlete’s deficiencies. Focusing on muscular
endurance to increase capacity to handle higher stresses is a common baseline
for athletes who are physiologically deficient in oxidative capacity. Focusing
on tissue quality, range of motion, motor control, or increasing connective
tissue tensile strength is a common starting point for athletes with
biomechanical deficiencies. This format will look like a classic linear
periodization model of high volume and low intensity to low volume and
high intensity (see figure 12.2 on page 200).

Fixing Weaknesses
If you find that the athlete is not deficient or limited biomechanically or
physiologically, you will have fewer traditional vectors. For example, you
may work with an athlete who needs high work capacity going into
preseason. Mixed sports such as lacrosse, soccer, or basketball may benefit

顺便说一句，这些物品对于运动员来说看起来没有什么不同。 他们
的工作就是摆在他们面前的每一次代表、每组、每一次练习、每一次训
练、每一个微周期和每一个中周期。 你的工作是看到整个宏观周期的
大局。作为一名教练，你了解执行力的力量，但教练和运动员都了解相
对于更大、更宏伟的计划。 您是否正在朝着提高绩效并降低集体风险
的最终目标迈进？在你作为力量教练的帮助下，该队的每位运动员是否

一旦你确定了你是向前还是向后工作，你就可以安排你的中周期。每
个中周期代表从开始或从结束移动的质量。如果你正在努力前进，你会
想要组织你的素质来弥补运动员的不足。 对于生理上氧化能力不足的
运动员来说，关注肌肉耐力以提高应对更高压力的能力是一个共同的基
线。对于存在生物力学缺陷的运动员来说，关注组织质量、运动范围、
运动控制或增加结缔组织拉伸强度是一个常见的起点。 这种格式看起
来像高容量和低强度到低容量和高强度的经典线性周期模型（参见第 20
0 页的图 12.2）。

修复弱点
如果你发现运动员在生物力学或生理学上没有缺陷或限制，那么你的传
统向量就会减少。 例如，您可能与一位需要高工作能力进入季前赛的
运动员一起工作。 长曲棍球、足球或篮球等混合运动可能会受益

from finishing with a block that focuses on oxidative capacity in a
macrocycle. With the same group, you may find that the limiting factor from
the previous season was maintaining lean muscle mass, and finishing with a
hypertrophy block going into preseason makes the most sense. You are not
limited by what they need from the start. Without limitations, you are free to
determine what they will need at the end of the off-season. This will take on
an undulating form of periodization where qualities are arranged to garner the
most specific outcome possible (see figure 12.3 on 202). We organize our
mesocycles to attain something that highly corresponds to their sport or
position.
Don’t get too caught up in working forward or backward. It has to make
sense to you, your coaches, and your athletes. If you all collectively feel more
comfortable with a certain vector, chances are that is the right choice. It will
come down to execution, no matter what.

macrocycle.

Step 2: Annual Calendar
The annual calendar likely has fixed dates to work around. We cannot train
on certain days and certain weeks, so we might as well pull them from the
schedule. Using college football as an example, because I am most familiar
with it, let’s break down the year.
January: Martin Luther King Jr. Day: 3-day weekend
February: Presidents’ Day: 3-day weekend
March: spring break: 1 week off
April: Easter weekend: 3-day weekend
May: finals or no school: 4 weeks off
June: no holidays
July: 4th of July: 3-day weekend or 1 week off
August: preseason
September: in-season
October: in-season

With college football, we need 8 weeks of discretionary period, which is 8
weeks of no direct coaching. Athletes can still train, but not under direct
supervision from the coach. We have 5 weeks between spring break and May
break. The other 3 weeks are a matter of preference and circumstances. The
timing of spring practice significantly affects this.

When You Can Train
Our best chance to make any changes is to have the longest, most
uninterrupted period of training we can get. If we have spring practice pushed
back to the end of March or the beginning of April, we can get January,
February, and March for the winter off-season. This matters a lot. First, we
are setting the foundation for summer. Second, we are trying to time end-ofseason surgeries and return to play through rehab and strength and
conditioning. Third, we can manage short weeks and weeks off better.
Fourth, we can get 1 to 2 weeks of discretionary period done in January. The
8th week of discretionary time comes after spring practice at the end of April.

When You Cannot Train
This is a discretionary trick, but you can have workouts, just unsupervised.
You can also run screens and set up meetings to review goals and plan the

you did not win it all; your athletes are most motivated at that point. From my
perspective, we can tap into that motivation by having the team run training
sessions. Trust me, they will work extremely hard no matter what. We can
build in general qualities such as work capacity or hypertrophy here, which is
less coaching intensive. You know your athletes will crush this period. You
can reserve the more technical stuff with more inherent risk for
nondiscretionary periods with you. If you have March or April spring

possible. Your best hope is to organize your training to get as much work in
before spring practice and then follow up spring practice with whatever will
have the best residual impact going into summer (figure 20.3).
Within the Time You Are Training
The point is that you will have aspects of your schedule that you will have no
control over. If you work with Olympic sports, your schedule is even more
restricted. Chances are, you will not have them during the summer. Chances
are, they will practice during the off-season. Chances are that the first thing to
go in the season will be training. What you have to learn to do is organize
your schedule and program around when you do have them. How do you
maximize the time you have?

What Else Is Occurring?
Start with holidays—just remove them from the calendar for training

potential 4-day microcycle and makes it a 3-day or a potential 3-day
microcycle and makes it a 2-day. You will have to adjust your mesocycles if

week. A drop in volume does not have to come from training sessions; it can
come from intramicrocycle design.
Next, find out when and where the team intends to practice. Do not fight
this. Your best chance to earn more training time is to demonstrate value with
the time you do have. If you can get great results from 2 days a week for 6

will need to adjust your microcycle and subsequent training sessions around
practices and individual training sessions. Develop empathy for your athletes.
Would you want to max out on squats the day after getting buried in practice?
Learn to communicate with your coaches and assistant coaches. Develop a

Step 3: Organizing the Mesocycles
Mesocycles represent qualities. You should be thinking of the quality you are
trying to develop when organizing your mesocycles. What is the best possible
outcome from that training block relative to both long- and short-term goals?
There is a science to sequencing one mesocycle to the next; we want to
leverage that to achieve the desired outcome.

Organizational Logic
We are now in a spot where we can organize our mesocycles. This is where
we take the qualities we are either working forward or backward in our
mesocycle and format them individually. The trick here is to structure the
mesocycle to have the best possible outcome by sequencing each one to get
the most from that quality at the end of the macrocycle.
We will have locked-in training periods that we will need to account for
first. We cannot make a period longer or shorter; we have to make do with
what we get. We then need to figure out how long each mesocycle needs to
be and how we want to load it.
The length of the mesocycle will be based on the quality we are training,
the age, the training age, and the muscle fiber type. The rules we established
within our periodization chapter (chapter 12) dictate this. Refer to their
physiology as a basis for determining mesocycle length. We want to consider
simultaneously what will garner the best outcome from loading and what we
can recover from (figure 20.4).
We have to go back to the standard distribution of training effects now.
We will have high and low responders, and most will fall around the mean. It
is a statistical phenomenon that most things will regress to the mean over
time. We can choose a length for a mesocycle as low as 2 weeks and as long
as 8 weeks. Those lengths are for the high and low responders to the loading
and recovery response. Most of our athletes will fall into a 3-to-5-week
mesocycle.
One abundantly clear element is that the monotony of programming will
affect coaches far more than athletes. If you are running several groups a day,
5 days a week, and running a program for 8 weeks, you will see the life

中循环代表品质。在组织你的中周期时，你应该考虑你想要发展的品质
。相对于长期和短期目标，该训练模块的最佳可能结果是什么？将一个
中周期排序到下一个中周期是一门科学。 我们希望利用这一点来实现
预期的结果。

组织逻辑
我们现在处于可以组织中循环的位置。 这就是我们在中观周期中向前
或向后工作的品质，并单独格式化它们的地方。 这里的技巧是通过对
每个循环进行排序来构建中循环，以在大循环结束时充分利用该质量，
从而获得最佳结果。
我们将有锁定的训练期，我们需要首先考虑这一点。 我们不能延长
或缩短一个时期； 我们必须凑合着用我们得到的东西。 然后我们需要
弄清楚每个中周期需要多长时间以及我们希望如何加载它。
中周期的长度将取决于我们训练的质量、年龄、训练年龄和肌纤维类
型。我们在分期章节（第 12 章）中建立的规则规定了这一点。 参考它
们的生理学作为确定中周期长度的基础。我们要同时考虑什么可以从加
载中获得最佳结果以及我们可以从中恢复什么（图 20.4）。
现在我们必须回到训练效果的标准分布。我们会有高反应者和低反应
者，大多数人都会落在平均值附近。这是一种统计现象，随着时间的推
移，大多数事情都会回归到平均值。我们可以选择中周期的长度，短至
2 周，长至 8 周。这些长度适用于对负载和恢复响应的高响应者和低响
应者。 我们大多数运动员都会陷入 3 到 5 周的中周期。
一个非常明确的因素是，单调的编程对教练的影响远远大于对运动员
的影响。如果你每天跑几个组，每周跑 5 天，并且跑一个程序 8 周，你
就会看到生活

pulled from your coaches in front of your eyes. We have spent a lot of time
talking about how athletes will respond to mesocycle length, but very little
about the coaches who are coaching the mesocycle. You may want to have a
6-to-8-week mesocycle, but that could come at the expense of your coach’s
morale.

FIGURE 20.4 Macrocycle and mesocycle arrangement.
A way to combat monotony for coaches is to facilitate autonomy. If the
coaches can amend the plan, as long as they are staying within the parameters
of the programming rules, you will see a much more enthusiastic staff. Have
them bring their perspective on changes to the training session format and
organization. Have them bring value outside of the direct session with
motivational tactics. The mesocycle is merely the quality we are trying to
develop. The people who are going through the program and those coaching
it need to be connected with the mind, body, and spirit of the program.
We do have to talk about a mesocycle periodization structure called block
periodization and how it may be beneficial to consider it from a
psychological perspective. Block periodization focuses a block on a specific
quality for the entire mesocycle (figure 20.5-20.8). The broad categories are
broken up into accumulation, stress through volume and intensification, and
stress through intensity (see figure 12.5a and figure 12.5b on page 207). The

对教练来说，消除单调的一种方法是促进自主性。 如果教练可以修

以及通过强度产生的压力（参见第 207 页的图 12.5a 和图 12.5b）。这

premise is to saturate that mesocycle, based on the quality being developed,
with either a higher volume focus or a higher intensity focus.
From a physiological perspective, the body prefers continuity. Remember,
everything works for novices, and less works for advanced athletes. Over
time, we have to evolve our program to work with adapted physiology and
have more controls to test our hypothesis regarding training. Mixed training
methods that touch everything are poorly controlled research designs. We
have little idea where adaptation is coming from when we complete a
program and therefore cannot assess the quality of the program. We may or
may not be running faster, jumping higher, and throwing something further
from a mixed or block approach; the difference can be assessed more directly
with a more saturated block focus. In the event of knowing or not knowing, I
choose to know.

循环饱和。
从生理角度来看，身体更喜欢连续性。请记住，一切都适合新手，但
对于高级运动员来说则不太有效。 随着时间的推移，我们必须改进我
们的计划，以适应适应的生理学，并有更多的控制来检验我们关于训练
的假设。 触及一切的混合训练方法是控制不善的研究设计。 当我们完
成一个项目时，我们几乎不知道适应是从哪里来的，因此无法评估该项
目的质量。 我们可能会或可能不会跑得更快、跳得更高、从混合或块
状方法中扔得更远；通过更饱和的块焦点可以更直接地评估差异。在知
道或不知道的情况下，我选择知道。
